video_title: 💰 Lily Learns about Wants and Needs

summaries.summary: Lily asks her dad for a new bike, but Dad explains that a bike is something she wants, not something she needs. Lily can exercise by riding her old bike or doing other active things. When her raincoat is too small, Dad helps her find an inexpensive coat that will keep her dry. Lily also learns that visiting the dentist is a need, while bowling, mini golf, and ice cream are wants. At the grocery store, Lily helps choose milk, vegetables, and toilet paper. She learns that root beer is a want, even though Dad enjoys it. After picking up Mom at the hospital, Lily learns that doctors, medicine, and care are needs, while television is something patients may want. Dad explains that after a family buys everything it needs, it may use leftover money for wants. Lily and Dad decide to ride to the park and buy ice cream the next day.

video_title: 🦃 Stories for Kids Read Aloud 🦃 I Am Thankful A Thanksgiving Book For Kids [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: A child travels to visit family for Thanksgiving. The child helps clean, cooks, shops for an apron, visits a pumpkin patch, makes a turkey craft, looks at family pictures, and works on a puzzle with a big brother. The family hikes through golden trees, watches a parade and football, gives treats to dogs, and takes cans of food to the pantry. The child also talks with Dad on the phone. At last, everyone helps prepare a large Thanksgiving meal. Guests arrive, and the family serves them plates piled with food. When everyone is full, the child gives out hugs. Family and friends gather together, and Thanksgiving is here. Throughout the day, the child feels thankful, with love filling their heart from head to toes.

video_title: good night little blue truck kids book read along

summaries.summary: Little Blue Truck and Toad are driving home when a loud storm begins. They hurry into the warm garage. Soon, Goat, Hen, Goose, Cow, Duck, and Pig come inside because they are wet, cold, or scared of the thunder. Everyone stays close together while rain falls outside. The friends notice that the thunder is only a noisy sound. The rain also gives the thirsty plants a drink to help them grow. After a while, the clouds move away and the storm ends. The animals feel brave because they are together with Little Blue. They all climb into Little Blue Truck for a bedtime ride. The moon shines in the starry sky as Little Blue takes each friend home. At last, Toad gets into his small bed, says good night, and Little Blue Truck falls fast asleep.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑇ℎ𝑒 𝐻𝑒𝑟𝑜 𝑇𝑤𝑜 𝐷𝑜𝑜𝑟𝑠 𝐷𝑜𝑤𝑛 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: In 1959, twenty-year-old Steve Satlow learns that his father is seriously ill. Steve races to get help, but his father dies. While mourning, Steve finds a box of childhood treasures and a letter his father wrote two years earlier. The letter reminds Steve that his father loved him deeply and that family, faith, and friendship can help people through difficult times. A ticket from the 1948 Dodgers home opener brings back happy memories. The story then returns to 1948, when eight-year-old Steve eagerly follows the Brooklyn Dodgers and admires Jackie Robinson, the first African-American player in modern Major League Baseball. Steve worries about Jackie’s weight and Pete Reiser’s injury, while also hoping to attend opening day. However, Steve keeps getting into trouble at school. After he and his friend Senna push their teacher, Miss Malakin, into a hedge, Steve is suspended for ten days and loses his chance to attend the Dodgers’ opening game.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: CONCLUSION to Disney's MOANA Folk Tale The Story of Moana the Wayfinder

summaries.summary: Long ago, people sailed across the ocean and knew how to find their way by the stars, clouds, and wind. Then the heart of Te Fiti was stolen, and darkness spread. The people stayed safely on their island and forgot how to sail. Many years later, Moana was born. The ocean chose her to return Te Fiti’s heart. Moana crossed the reef and found Maui, a demigod. Together, they traveled to the realm of monsters and found Maui’s magical fishhook. Maui taught Moana the old ways of finding a path across the sea, and Moana helped Maui become strong again. At Te Fiti’s island, they met the fire monster, Te Kā. Moana saw that Te Kā had lost her heart. She returned the heart, and Te Kā became Te Fiti again. Darkness turned to light. Moana went home, and her people celebrated. Then Moana taught them to sail once more. Together, they became voyagers again.

video_title: The Runaway Iceberg | Story Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Gasper and Rossy are penguin explorers when a chunk of ice breaks away, carrying them out to sea on a runaway iceberg. Rossy stays hopeful, but Gasper is frightened because he cannot swim and soon they can no longer see land. A snow petrel shows them which way home lies, while Antarctic silverfish push the iceberg through the water. When the iceberg becomes trapped, a blue whale smashes through the ice and clears a path. As the penguins travel onward, the iceberg begins to melt quickly. Rossy tells Gasper that he must swim, reminding him that he is the captain. Encouraged by Rossy and their new friends, Gasper bravely jumps into the freezing water and follows her. They finally reach home and reunite with their families. Gasper feels proud, but says he could not have completed the dangerous adventure without his trusty first mate, Rossy.

video_title: Planes Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Planes - Dusty to the Rescue

summaries.summary: Dusty is a little racing plane who cannot race because his engine is damaged. While his friends look for parts, Dusty trains to become a firefighter at Piston Peak National Park. He learns to scoop water and drop fire retardant, but he makes mistakes because he does not listen and is afraid to use his broken engine. During a dangerous fire, Dusty admits that he may never race again. Blade tells him that giving up could mean not saving lives. Dusty decides to help. He flies through smoke and falling rocks, fills his pontoons, and drops water on a burning bridge to save two vehicles. His engine breaks, but Maru repairs it with spare parts and gives Dusty a new engine. Dusty earns his firefighter certification. He learns that racing is not everything and becomes a hero both as a racer and as a firefighter.

video_title: Oh No, George! | Read Aloud Story for Kids 📚 | Storytime with K G Merlo

summaries.summary: George is a little dog who promises Harris he will be good while Harris goes out. But George sees a cake, a cat, and some lovely soil. He wants to eat the cake, play with the cat, and dig in the soil, and he does all three. When Harris comes home, he sees the mess and asks George what happened. George feels sorry and gives Harris his favorite toy. Harris thanks him and takes George for a walk. Outside, George sees another cake and walks past it. He sees some soil but does not dig. He does not chase the cat either. George is doing well. Then he smells something very interesting near a rubbish bin, which is something George loves. The story stops just as George must decide what to do.

video_title: The Name Jar Read Aloud | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: Yunhai moves from Korea to America and feels nervous about starting a new school. Some children tease her because they have trouble saying her Korean name, so she wonders whether to choose an American name. Her classmates make a jar filled with names for her, and she considers names such as Daisy, Stella, and Avery. Yunhai’s grandmother sends a letter reminding her that she will always be Yunhai, no matter how far away they are. Yunhai then shows Joey the beautiful wooden name stamp her grandmother gave her. Joey begins to understand and say her name correctly. When the name jar disappears, Yunhai tells the class that she has chosen her own name because Yunhai means grace. The children practice saying it, and they accept her choice. Joey returns the jar and explains that he took it because he wanted Yunhai to keep her own name. He gives her a Korean nickname, Chinu, which means friend.

video_title: Beauty and the Beast Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, The Enchantment

summaries.summary: A selfish prince turns into a Beast after he refuses shelter to an enchantress. His castle servants become household objects, and everyone forgets the castle. Later, Belle comes to the castle to rescue her father, Maurice, and takes his place as the Beast’s prisoner. At first, Belle is frightened, but she discovers that the Beast can be kind. They read together, play in the snow, and share a special dance. Belle learns to see the goodness beneath his frightening appearance, and the Beast learns to love and care for her. When Maurice is in danger, the Beast gives Belle a magic mirror and lets her go help him. Gaston attacks the castle and badly injures the Beast. Belle tells the Beast that she loves him just before the last rose petal falls. The spell breaks, and the Beast and his servants become human again. The prince and Belle recognize each other’s inner beauty and live happily together.

video_title: 🖍️📚The Color Monster by Anna Llenas, kids story read aloud with sound effects

summaries.summary: The Color Monster wakes up feeling confused because all his emotions are mixed together. A helper tells him to separate each feeling and put it in its own jar. Happiness is yellow, and it makes him laugh, jump, dance, play, and share. Sadness is blue and lonely, and it may make him hide, be alone, or cry. Anger is red and hot like fire, and life can feel unfair when he is angry. Fear makes him feel tiny and makes him want to run away from gray shadows. The helper says they can find a way through fear. Calm is green, quiet, and peaceful. It helps the Color Monster breathe slowly and deeply. After each feeling is put in the right place, the Color Monster can rest and feels much better. Then the helper notices that he is feeling something new and asks how he feels now.

video_title: Thelma the Unicorn, kids book read along

summaries.summary: Thelma wishes she could be a unicorn, but her friend Otis tells her she is perfect just as she is. One day, Thelma finds a carrot and ties it to her nose. A truck spills pink paint and glitter on her, making her look like a unicorn. Soon, everyone knows Thelma, and she becomes famous. At first, she loves being a superstar. But crowds chase her everywhere, asking for autographs, and some people are unkind. Thelma becomes lonely and realizes that fame is not making her happy. She cleans off the glitter, removes the carrot horn, and returns to Otis. When he asks about her trip, she says she would rather just be herself. Thelma tells others that they are special and should keep being who they are.

video_title: Wonders Grade 5 Where the Mountain Meets the Moon

summaries.summary: Minli asks the King of Bright Moonlight for the borrowed line she needs to take to the Old Man of the Moon. The king shows her a precious page torn from the Book of Fortune. Its mysterious words say, “You only lose what you cling to.” The king realizes that his family has protected the page for generations even though it represents his ancestor’s greed and anger. He decides that giving it away means he is no longer clinging to it, so he places the page in Minli’s hands. While Minli is inside the city, Dragon waits outside and meets the stone guardian lions. They explain that the Old Man of the Moon once gave them a red thread of destiny to protect the city from a dangerous crack. After the city became peaceful, the thread was never used. The lions give it to Dragon. In the morning, Minli and Dragon compare their treasures and realize they still need the Old Man of the Moon to decide which is the true borrowed line.

video_title: Giraffes Can’t Dance

summaries.summary: Gerald is a tall giraffe with a long neck, thin legs, and crooked knees. He is good at standing and eating tree shoots, but he cannot dance well. At the jungle dance, the animals waltz, rock, roll, and reel. When Gerald tries to join, they laugh and say giraffes cannot dance. Gerald feels sad and walks away. In a quiet clearing, a cricket tells him to listen to the grass, trees, and moon. The cricket plays the violin, and Gerald begins to move. His hooves shuffle, his neck sways, and his tail swishes. He leaps and dances happily. The other animals see him and call him the best dancer. Gerald says that everyone can dance when they find music they love.

video_title: Luca - Friends Are Forever 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Luca and Alberto are two sea monsters who are friends. They build a scooter and have an exciting time together. In the seaside town of Portorosso, they meet Julia, a human girl. Julia is brave and protects Luca and Alberto from a bully named Aircolay. Luca wants to learn new things, so he learns how to ride a bicycle. Riding is hard at first, but his friends cheer for him. Julia also shows Luca a train going to her school and tells him that he can go to school too. Later, Alberto becomes trapped, and Luca is ready to rescue him. When Julia gets hurt, Luca and Alberto go back to help her. Together, the three friends become the Portorosso Cup champions. At the end, the friends must part ways and may not see each other often, but they remain friends forever. Luca can always count on Julia and Alberto.

Luca and Alberto are sea monsters and very good friends. They build and ride a scooter before having an exciting adventure in the beautiful seaside town of Portorosso. There, they meet Julia, a human girl. Julia is different from them, but she becomes their friend. She stands up for Luca and Alberto when a bully named Aircolay troubles them. Luca also tries to learn how to ride a bicycle. It is difficult at first, but his friends encourage him. Julia points to a train traveling to her school and tells Luca that he can go to school as well. When Alberto is trapped, Luca goes to rescue him. Later, Julia is hurt, so Luca and Alberto return for her. The three friends help one another and become Portorosso Cup champions. Even though they later go separate ways and may not meet often, their friendship remains strong forever.

Luca and Alberto enjoy being friends and share exciting adventures. They are sea monsters who build a scooter and ride it together. Their adventure takes them to Portorosso, a beautiful seaside town. They meet Julia, a human girl who is brave and helpful. Julia protects them from a bully named Aircolay. She also helps Luca imagine going to school by pointing out a train headed to her school. Luca learns to ride a bicycle, although it is not easy at first. His friends cheer him on and help him keep trying. When Alberto is trapped, Luca is ready to rescue him. When Julia gets hurt, Luca and Alberto go back to help her. The three friends work as a team and become Portorosso Cup champions. Later, they have to part ways and may not see one another often. Still, Luca, Alberto, and Julia remain friends forever, and Luca can count on them.

video_title: The Berenstain Bears and the SPOOKY OLD TREE | Read-Aloud

summaries.summary: Three little bears go to a spooky old tree. One carries a light, one carries a stick, and one carries a rope. They dare to go inside. First, they climb a twisty old stair. Then they find a giant key and a moving wall. They dare to go through the wall and enter a spooky old hall. In the hall, they see Great Sleeping Bear. The bears are brave enough to go over Great Sleeping Bear, even though they have many shivers. Soon they are in the tree without their light, stick, or rope. They need to find a way out. The three bears go up a ladder, through the floor, and down a slide. At last, they run out a door. The three little bears get home again, safe at last.

Three little bears begin an adventure in a spooky old tree. One has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They climb a twisty old stair and keep going. They find a giant key and a moving wall. The bears dare to pass through the wall and enter a spooky old hall. There they meet Great Sleeping Bear. The bears go over Great Sleeping Bear, even though they are very shivery. Now they are inside the tree without the light, the stick, or the rope. They must get out. They climb up a ladder, go through the floor, and slide down a slide. Then they run fast and go out a door. The three little bears make it home. They are safe at last after their spooky trip.

A group of three little bears visits a spooky old tree. They bring useful things: a light, a stick, and a rope. The bears go inside and climb a twisty old stair. Next, they find a giant key and a wall that moves. They go through the moving wall and enter a spooky old hall. Great Sleeping Bear is there. The bears dare to go over Great Sleeping Bear, although they all have the shivers. After that, they are left without a light, without a stick, and without a rope. They need to escape from the tree. The bears travel up a ladder, through the floor, and down a slide. Finally, they run out through a door and go home. Their adventure in the spooky old tree ends with the three little bears safe at last.

video_title: Danny and the Dinosaur🦕 , by Syd Hoff. Read Aloud kids book. Storytime

summaries.summary: One day, Danny visits a museum and sees many things, including dinosaurs. Danny loves dinosaurs and wishes he had one. Then a dinosaur named Benny speaks to him. Danny climbs onto Benny, and they travel around town. Benny is so tall that people think he is a car, and he must be careful around buildings and houses. He helps a lady carry her bundles, watches a ball game, swims, and almost eats grass before Danny stops him. At the zoo, everyone runs to see Benny instead of the animals. Children ask to ride him and play games. Benny tries hide-and-seek, but the children find him each time. At the end of the day, Benny returns to the museum because he is needed there. Danny goes home alone, happy about their wonderful day.

Danny goes to a museum because he wants to see dinosaurs. He is surprised when a dinosaur named Benny comes alive and talks to him. Danny rides on Benny’s head, and they have an exciting day in town. Benny makes car noises, looks at tall buildings, helps a lady with her bundles, and watches a ball game. He wants to eat some grass, but Danny sees a sign telling them to keep off it, so they eat ice cream instead. At the zoo, the people and animals pay more attention to Benny than to the lions, elephants, monkeys, seals, giraffes, and hippos. Some children ride Benny, teach him tricks, and play hide-and-seek with him. When evening comes, Benny says goodbye and goes back to the museum. Danny walks home, remembering their special day.

Danny loves dinosaurs, so he is very happy when Benny, a real dinosaur, speaks to him at the museum. Danny rides Benny through town. Benny is very tall and has to be careful not to knock over buildings, stores, or houses with his long tail. Together they help a lady, watch a home run, swim, and see grass that Benny wants to eat. They choose ice cream instead. At the zoo, everyone comes running to see Benny, so the zoo man asks them to leave so the animals can be watched. Soon, children find Danny and Benny. The children take turns riding Benny, teaching him to shake hands and roll over, and playing hide-and-seek. Benny cannot find a hiding place, but the children pretend not to find him. Later, Benny returns to the museum. Danny says goodbye and goes home, glad they had a wonderful day.

video_title: 🐱🐈 Kids Read Aloud Books : Dreamworks Gabby’s Dollhouse : Merry Christmas Gabby Cats!

summaries.summary: It is Christmas time at the dollhouse. Gabby and Pandy decorate the tree, hang stockings, and put a kitty topper on top. Pandy leaves a Christmas pickle for Santa Kitty because he loves pickles. Then Figgy the elf calls from the North Pole. Santa Kitty needs help making gifts for kittens on the nice list. Gabby and Pandy travel there in Baby Box’s magical cardboard kitty sleigh. At the workshop, Pandy makes a scuba kitty, Figgy makes a robot, and Gabby makes a doll. Together, they put the toys in boxes, add bows, and load the gifts into Santa Kitty’s sleigh. Santa Kitty recognizes Pandy and invites both friends to ride with him. They fly with Candy Cane and the reindeer kitties to the dollhouse. Gabby and Pandy toss presents to their friends. Santa Kitty gives Pandy a Christmas pickle and gives Gabby a gift. Then snow begins to fall.

Gabby and Pandy are excited for Christmas at the dollhouse. They decorate the tree and prepare a snack for Santa Kitty. Pandy hopes to meet him one day. Figgy the elf calls from the North Pole and asks Gabby for help because many presents are not ready. Gabby and Pandy fly to the North Pole with Baby Box in a magical cardboard sleigh. There, they help Figgy make three toys: a doll, a robot, and a scuba kitty. The friends work together to choose boxes, place the toys inside, and add colorful bows. When the presents are finished, they hurry to Santa Kitty’s sleigh. Santa Kitty thanks them and lets them ride along while he delivers gifts. They fly over the night sky to the dollhouse. Gabby and Pandy give presents to their friends. Santa Kitty gives Pandy a Christmas pickle, and snow falls as everyone celebrates a magical Christmas night.

On Christmas Eve, Gabby and Pandy make the dollhouse ready for Christmas. They hang stockings, decorate the tree, and place a kitty topper on it. Pandy leaves a Christmas pickle for Santa Kitty. Then Figgy the elf telephones from the North Pole. She says Santa Kitty needs help preparing presents. Gabby, Pandy, and Baby Box travel to the North Pole in a magical cardboard kitty sleigh. Pandy builds a scuba kitty, Figgy builds a robot, and Gabby builds a doll. They finish the toys and work together to put each one in the right box with a bow. Santa Kitty is happy when they bring the gifts. He knows Pandy and invites Gabby and Pandy to ride in his sleigh. Candy Cane leads the reindeer kitties through the sky. At the dollhouse, the friends deliver the presents. Santa Kitty gives Pandy a pickle, and Gabby sees snow falling. Everyone enjoys the wonderful Christmas night.

video_title: Pete the Cat Easter bandit kids book read along

summaries.summary: One Easter morning, Pete the Cat cannot find his Easter basket. He looks everywhere and discovers a trail of colorful jelly beans. The trail leads him to Callie’s house. Callie has not seen the basket, but she finds a trail of candy eggs. Pete and Callie follow it to Alligator’s house, then follow marshmallow chicks to Gus’s house. Lollipops lead them to Turtle’s house, and chocolate bunnies lead everyone to a little house in the garden. The Easter Bunny is inside with Pete’s basket. He explains that he borrowed it because he delivers baskets every year but never receives one. Pete understands and shares his candy. His friends add candy from their baskets, too. Soon, they make a wonderful basket for the Easter Bunny. Pete gives it to him, and everyone is happy. They promise to make him a basket every Easter. Sharing is the sweetest gift.

Pete the Cat wakes up on Easter morning and finds that his Easter basket is gone. While searching, he sees jelly beans on the floor. Pete follows the jelly bean trail to Callie. Together, they find candy eggs and follow them to Alligator. A trail of marshmallow chicks takes Pete, Callie, and Alligator to Gus. Then lollipops lead them to Turtle. At Turtle’s house, chocolate bunnies point toward a colorful little house by the playground. The friends follow the trail and meet the Easter Bunny. He has Pete’s basket because he borrowed it. The Easter Bunny says he feels sad because he gives baskets to everyone but never gets one himself. Pete hugs him and decides to help. Pete shares his candy, and Callie, Alligator, Gus, and Turtle share theirs. They fill a new basket with treats and give it to the Easter Bunny. He is delighted, and the friends promise to remember him every year.

When Pete discovers his Easter basket is missing, he follows a trail of treats to find it. First, colorful jelly beans lead Pete to Callie. Candy eggs lead Pete and Callie to Alligator, and marshmallow chicks lead them to Gus. Gus has not seen the basket, but lollipops point the way to Turtle. Turtle finds chocolate bunnies, so all the friends follow the trail to a small house in the garden. The Easter Bunny opens the door. He has Pete’s basket and says he borrowed it because he never gets an Easter basket of his own. Pete is not angry. He hugs the Easter Bunny and fills an empty basket with some of his candy. Callie, Alligator, Gus, and Turtle add treats from their baskets. The new basket becomes full and colorful. Pete gives it to the Easter Bunny, who happily eats a jelly bean. From then on, Pete and his friends make him a basket every Easter.

video_title: With My Mummy | Read Aloud Children Stories

summaries.summary: A child has a happy day with Mommy. In the morning, Mommy helps the child get ready and they look for Teddy. Then they go shopping. Mommy carries the bags and lifts the child when the walk home feels too long. In the park, Mommy helps a little ladybird turn over. The child plays on the roundabout, falls off, and cries, but Mommy gives kisses, rubs the sore place, and hugs the child. At home, they bake together, make a messy cake, and fix broken toys. They hang washing outside and pretend the bedsheets are capes while they fly. Mommy makes dinner when the child is hungry. After a fun bath, she wraps the child in a towel. At bedtime, Mommy cuddles, reads adventures, kisses the child’s hand, and sings a tune. The child falls asleep, happy to have Mommy’s love and fun.

The child says that days with Mommy are full of laughter and play. They begin by getting up quickly and searching for a teddy. Then they zoom around the shops while Mommy carries many bags. In the park, they find a ladybird stuck on its back, and Mommy gently helps it. The child spins on the roundabout, falls, and cries. Mommy kisses and hugs the child until the hurt goes away. Later, they bake and decorate a cake together. Mommy can also mend and sort toys very quickly. When the washing is dry, the child and Mommy pretend the bedsheets are flying capes. Mommy makes dinner for the hungry child and Teddy. They splash and laugh in the bath. Finally, Mommy wraps the child warmly, cuddles close, reads adventures, waves to the moon, and sings while the child goes to sleep.

Mommy makes ordinary parts of the day special. She helps the child in the morning and searches for Teddy. While shopping, Mommy carries the bags and carries the child when the walk is long. During a park walk, she notices a little ladybird on its back and puts it safely right. The child has fun on the roundabout but falls off. Mommy comforts the child with a kiss, a rub, and a hug. At home, Mommy joins the child in baking, even after sprinkles make a big mess. She fixes toys, hangs the washing, and plays pretend flying with the bedsheets. When the child’s tummy rumbles, Mommy serves dinner. Bath time brings more tickles and laughter. At night, she gives a warm towel, cuddles the child in bed, reads adventures, and sings a tune. The child looks forward to another fun day together.

video_title: Kermit the Hermit

summaries.summary: Kermit was an old crab who lived alone in a rocky castle in Monterey Bay. Because food was scarce, he became selfish and grumpy. He collected everything he found, even things he could never use, until his cave was packed. One day, a shiny tin can tricked Kermit into leaving the bay. A dog grabbed him and tried to bury him, but a boy stopped the dog and carried Kermit safely back to the sea. Kermit wanted to thank the boy, so he tried to help him catch a fish. Instead, a huge fish pulled Kermit far into the ocean. There, Kermit escaped a shark by hiding inside an old treasure chest filled with gold. He carried the gold to his cave, then asked a pelican to help him find the boy. The pelican delivered gold to the boy’s poor family, who used it for toys, bicycles, and a television.

Kermit the crab had always been greedy because finding food in the bay was difficult. His cave became full of useless objects, and he thought only about keeping things for himself. His life changed when a dog caught him near a shiny tin can and tried to bury him. A kind boy rescued Kermit and returned him to the sea. Kermit decided to repay the boy with a bicycle, but he had no money. While trying to help the boy catch a fish, Kermit was pulled into deep water by a powerful fish. He landed near a sunken pirate ship and hid from a giant shark inside a chest. The chest contained many gold coins. Kermit carried two coins at a time back to his cave for three months. When he could not find the boy, a friendly pelican helped him. Together, they dropped gold into the boy’s chimney, bringing his family toys, bicycles, and other useful things.

After a boy saved Kermit from being buried by a dog, the crab wanted to give him a reward. Kermit first planned to help the boy catch a large fish, but the fish escaped with Kermit attached to the line. Kermit was carried far across the waves and sank to the ocean floor. A shark chased him, so Kermit squeezed under the lid of an old chest. The shark could not open it and eventually left. Kermit discovered that the chest held gold. Instead of keeping every coin for himself, Kermit carried the treasure back to his cave and searched for the boy. The boy was not at the dock, so Kermit told a pelican what had happened. The pelican knew where the boy lived and carried Kermit over the bay. They dropped two gold coins down the family’s chimney. The family found the gold and soon had bicycles, toys, and a television.

video_title: COOL CARS (Amazing Machines) by Tony Mitton & Ant Parker - Read Aloud Story

summaries.summary: Cars help people travel on busy roads. Cars come in many shapes and sizes, from tiny cars to big, shiny cars. A driver uses traffic lights, signs, a steering wheel, mirrors, and pedals to control a car. Cars need care, too, so people check the oil, fill the tires with air, add fuel, and wash the car. Some cars have soft tops for sunny days, while four-wheel-drive cars travel over rough ground. Racing cars go fast, police cars help at crashes, limousines carry special people, and taxis carry passengers. Sometimes many cars make a traffic jam. On a clear day, a family can pack a picnic, buckle their safety belts, and enjoy a drive in the country. The car’s engine gives power, wheels help it move, and the boot holds bags.

A car needs a driver to start and move. The driver watches traffic lights, road markings, and signs. The steering wheel turns the car, mirrors show nearby traffic, and pedals help the driver stop or speed up. To keep a car working well, people check the oil, pump the tires, fill the tank, wash the car, and use the wipers to clean the windscreen. Different cars have different jobs. A convertible is fun in the sun, and a strong four-wheel-drive car is useful on rough roads. Racing cars zoom quickly. Police cars use flashing lights and sirens. Limousines carry movie stars, presidents, and queens, while taxis carry people around town. Cars can get stuck in traffic, but a sunny country drive can be happy. A family packs a picnic, buckles up, and travels safely.

Cars take people from place to place. They can be little or large, and every car needs a driver. Drivers follow signs and lights, turn the steering wheel, look in mirrors, and press pedals to stop or go. Cars also need care: their oil, tires, fuel, windows, and wipers must be looked after. There are many kinds of cars. A convertible opens its top for sunny driving. A four-wheel-drive car has thick tires for bumpy ground. Racing cars roar past very fast. Police cars flash lights and sound sirens when they help people or chase criminals. Fancy limousines carry important passengers, and taxis give people rides. Too many cars can make a traffic jam. When roads are clear and the weather is bright, people can drive into the country. They pack a picnic, fasten their safety belts, and enjoy the journey.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Flounder Loves Ariel

summaries.summary: Ariel and Flounder swim together and look for something wonderful. Flounder worries that sharks may be nearby, but Ariel tells him not to be afraid. They find a strange object and decide to ask about it. Then a shark appears and frightens Flounder. Ariel catches the shark, and Flounder feels relieved. Flounder says that he wishes he were more like Ariel because she is not afraid of anything. Ariel says she is not sure about that. Flounder explains that Ariel loves excitement and adventures, wants to learn about everything, and is the best singer under the sea. Ariel thanks Flounder for saying these kind things. She tells him that he is the best at being her friend. Flounder asks Ariel what she loves. Ariel says that she loves being part of Flounder’s world, too. The two friends are happy to be together.

Flounder asks Ariel to wait for him while they swim. He wonders if there might be sharks in the water. Ariel tells him not to be such a guppy, and then she sees something wonderful. Flounder asks what it is, but Ariel does not know, so they decide to ask. Soon, a shark appears. Ariel catches the shark, and Flounder is relieved. Flounder wishes he could be brave like Ariel. He says that Ariel is not afraid of anything and that she loves excitement and adventures. Flounder also says that Ariel always wants to know everything and that she is the best singer under the sea. Ariel thanks her friend. She tells Flounder that he is the best at being her friend. Flounder asks what Ariel loves. Ariel answers that she loves being part of his world, too.

Ariel and Flounder are swimming and exploring under the sea. Flounder is nervous because he thinks there could be sharks. Ariel tells him not to worry so much. Together, they notice something they have never seen before. They do not know what it is, so they go to ask. A shark then appears, but Ariel catches it. Flounder feels safe again. He tells Ariel that he wishes he could be like her. Flounder thinks Ariel is brave, enjoys excitement and adventures, and wants to learn about everything. He also praises her singing. Ariel thanks Flounder for his kind words. She says that Flounder is the best at being her friend. Flounder asks Ariel what she loves. Ariel says she loves being part of his world. The friends show that they enjoy exploring together and being part of each other’s worlds.

video_title: Unicorn Thinks He’s Pretty Great by Bob Shea

summaries.summary: A goat thinks he is pretty cool until a unicorn moves nearby and does everything better. The unicorn flies past the goat’s bike, makes it rain cupcakes instead of making marshmallow squares, and wins the talent show with wonderful prancing. The goat feels left out and thinks the unicorn is showing off. Then the goat discovers that being a goat has special good things too. He can eat goat cheese pizza, while the unicorn can eat only glitter and rainbows because of his sensitive stomach. The unicorn notices the goat’s split hooves. The goat explains that they help him stand on steep hills and climb mountains. The goat feels unhappy about his horn, but the unicorn says it could be perfect for soccer. Soon, they imagine working together as an unstoppable team. At last, the goat tells the unicorn that he feels they could be friends, and the unicorn agrees.

The goat feels jealous when the unicorn arrives. The goat rides a bike, makes marshmallow squares, performs a special dance, and tries a magic trick with a quarter. Each time, the unicorn does something more amazing: he flies, makes cupcakes rain from the sky, wins first prize for prancing, and turns things into gold. The goat says nobody could be friends with such a showoff. Then the unicorn and goat talk about their differences. The goat enjoys goat cheese pizza and can spread cheese on a tin can or sprinkle it on garbage. The unicorn can eat glitter and rainbows, but his stomach is sensitive. The unicorn asks about the goat’s hooves, and the goat explains that his split hooves help him climb steep hills and mountains. The goat dislikes his horn, but the unicorn thinks it would help with soccer. Together, they imagine being an unstoppable team and decide they can be friends.

When the unicorn moves in, the goat thinks his own talents are not good enough. The goat’s bike ride is passed by the flying unicorn. His almost-right marshmallow squares are outdone by cupcakes falling from the sky. At the talent show, the goat dances, but the unicorn prances and wins first prize. Even the goat’s magic trick with a quarter seems small when the unicorn turns things into gold. The goat complains that the unicorn thinks he is great. But the two friends begin noticing that they each have special abilities. The goat has goat cheese pizza and can eat cheese on a tin can or garbage, while the unicorn must eat glitter and rainbows. The goat’s split hooves help him stand on steep hills and climb mountains. His horn might be useful for soccer, too. The unicorn and goat imagine joining their skills, then the goat realizes they could be friends.

video_title: 🪹 The Perfect Nest

summaries.summary: Jack the cat builds a dry, cozy nest that is just the right size. He hopes a chicken will use it, lay an egg, and give him an omelette. A chicken comes first, but then a duck pushes her away, and a goose pushes the duck away. The birds argue and squish together in the nest. Jack tells them about an empty nest nearby, so they all leave. Jack finds three eggs and plans small breakfast, medium lunch, and large dinner. But the eggs hatch. A chick, a duckling, and a gosling all think Jack is their mother. They follow him everywhere and ask for food, play, and sleep. At last, Jack puts the three babies in the nest and climbs in with them. When they fall asleep, Jack understands that the nest is perfect after all.

Jack wants to make three omelettes, so he builds a perfect nest for a chicken. A chicken lays a small egg, a duck takes the nest and lays a medium egg, and a goose takes it and lays a large egg. The birds keep climbing on one another and refuse to leave. Jack tries shouting fire and wolf, but nothing helps. Finally, he tells them about an empty nest on the next farm. The chicken, duck, and goose each have a reason for leaving, and they flap away. Jack returns to his nest and sees the three eggs. Before he can cook them, they crack open. A baby chick, baby duck, and baby goose call Jack Mama. The babies follow Jack wherever he hides. They need food, play, and sleep. Jack cares for them, and the nest becomes perfect.

Jack the cat gathers materials and makes a warm nest. He expects a chicken to come, lay a perfect egg, and provide an omelette. Instead, a chicken, a duck, and a goose each claim the nest. One after another, they push each other aside and leave their eggs behind. The birds argue for days while Jack tries to make them move. He finally points them toward a better empty nest, and they all fly away. Jack arranges the eggs in a row and imagines breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Then the eggs hatch into a chick, a duckling, and a gosling. Each baby believes Jack is its mother. They find him in the barn, woods, and under a tractor. Jack brings them back to the nest. The babies ask for warmth and sleep, so Jack lies down with them. Soon everyone is asleep, and Jack discovers the true perfect nest.

video_title: Lilo & Stitch 📖 Read Along Storybook | Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Lilo and Stitch are excited because it is Pet Day at school. Nani reminds Stitch to behave, and Stitch agrees. At school, children show many pets, including the class frog, Mr. Fibs. When Stitch tries to look at the frog, Mr. Fibs escapes. Stitch chases him through classrooms, a science room, the hallway, and the cafeteria. Stitch even makes a stink bomb while experimenting, and it sends everyone running. Mr. Fibs causes a food fight when he jumps onto a lunch tray. Stitch keeps following the frog, but he is distracted by all the interesting school activities. Finally, in the gym, Stitch dodges balls and catches Mr. Fibs. He returns just in time for Lilo’s presentation. Lilo explains that Stitch is not only her pet but also her best friend and part of her family. After school, Nani gives them ice cream because Pet Day was great.

On Pet Day, Lilo brings Stitch to school so he can be introduced to the class. Nani asks Stitch to be on his best behavior, and he is eager to see everything. The class has many unusual pets and a frog named Mr. Fibs. When the frog jumps out of his habitat, Stitch runs after him. The chase leads through an experiment room, where Stitch makes a stink bomb, and into the cafeteria, where Mr. Fibs jumps onto a tray and starts a food fight. Stitch follows the frog from room to room, but school keeps distracting him. He remembers Nani’s words and hurries back. In the gym, Stitch catches Mr. Fibs while avoiding flying red balls. He gets back to class just as Lilo’s turn begins. Lilo says Stitch is her best friend and part of her Ohana, which means family.

Lilo and Stitch go to school for a special Pet Day. The children bring pets of many sizes and kinds, while the classroom’s pet is Mr. Fibs, a little frog. Stitch becomes curious and accidentally lets the frog escape. He follows Mr. Fibs through the school. In a science classroom, Stitch remembers Jumba’s lab and makes a stink bomb. Later, Mr. Fibs hops into the cafeteria and lands on a food tray, causing food to spill and a food fight to begin. The frog keeps escaping, and Stitch keeps chasing him. Although he enjoys the interesting rooms and activities, Stitch remembers that he promised to behave and needs to return to Lilo. At last, he catches Mr. Fibs in the gym after jumping and cartwheeling around flying balls. Stitch returns in time for Lilo’s presentation. She proudly says he is her best friend and part of her family. Nani celebrates with ice cream.

video_title: 👁 The Doctor with an Eye to Eyes: : The Story of Dr. Patricia Bath (Amazing Scientists, 2)

summaries.summary: Patricia Bath grew up in Harlem, New York, loving science and learning from her family. Her mother gave her a chemistry set, and Patricia decided she wanted to become a doctor and help sick and poor people. Many people believed doctors should be men, and the nearby high school was only for white children with money. Patricia traveled by train, finished high school in three years, and continued to college and medical school. She noticed that Black patients were blind twice as often as white patients, especially in places where money was scarce. Patricia taught students about eyes and started an eye-doctor training program. She then studied lasers in Europe and invented a laser probe that helped patients see again for many more years. She also created a place that believed healthy vision was everyone’s right. Patricia wanted to help people more than she wanted fame.

Patricia Bath loved copying her older brother and believed that anything boys could do, girls could do too. Her chemistry set made her excited about science, and a family friend inspired her to become a doctor. Patricia’s parents encouraged her and taught her that education could open many doors. Even when her high school was far away and her medical school treated girls unfairly, she kept going. While studying eyes and caring for hospital patients, Patricia discovered that Black patients were blind twice as often as white patients. She worked to make eye care more important for people with less money. Patricia taught hundreds of students, fought for a better workplace, and led the first eye-doctor training program. Later, she studied lasers in Europe and developed a laser probe that restored sight to many patients. She also created a place to bring hope and insisted that healthy vision belonged to everyone.

Patricia Bath was a clever girl from New York who dreamed of helping people through medicine. She faced unfair rules because she was a girl and because some schools were only for white children with money, but she worked hard and finished high school early. At medical school, she chose to focus on eyes. Her hospital work showed her that Black patients were blind twice as often as white patients, so she planned ways to improve eye care in communities with little money. Patricia taught students, began an eye-doctor training program, and became the first woman to achieve that accomplishment. She traveled to Europe to learn more about lasers. After practicing for months, she invented a laser probe that helped patients who had been unable to see. She later created a place whose message was that healthy vision is important for rich and poor people of every color. Her greatest wish was to heal.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Prince Charming is not one person. Long ago, bards called many princes “Prince Charming” when they rescued princesses, fought dragons, broke curses, or simply danced well. Princes Liam, Duncan, Gustav, and Frederick all disliked being given the same name. In one adventure, Prince Gustav rides to a farm where a troll is eating freshly picked beets. Rosilda, the farmer, tells her children to go inside, but then grabs a shovel and orders the troll to stop. Gustav charges in, thinking the troll has eaten a child. The troll quickly defeats Gustav and throws him around the garden. Rosilda hits the troll with her shovel and makes it leave. Gustav discovers that the red liquid on the troll’s mouth was beet juice, not blood. The children are safe, but the fight has ruined the farm. Rosilda asks Gustav to pay for the damage and jokes about the famous story of how a girl saved his life. Gustav is embarrassed and blames the bards for telling that story.

The story explains that “Prince Charming” is an adjective, not a real name. Bards and minstrels used the name for many different princes because they did not care about details. Prince Liam truly fought a dangerous monster, Prince Duncan woke a princess because dwarves told him what to do, Prince Gustav fell from a tower while helping Rapunzel, and Prince Frederick impressed Cinderella by dancing. None of them liked the name. Later, Gustav finds a troll in a farmer’s beet garden. Rosilda Stiffenkrauss bravely protects her vegetables with a shovel while her children watch. Gustav attacks the troll with an axe, believing the beet juice around its mouth is blood from a child. The troll knocks Gustav down and nearly throws him onto the farmhouse. Rosilda strikes the troll and sends it away. Gustav learns that every child is safe, but his battle destroyed the garden. Rosilda asks him to pay for the repairs and teases him about his old story.

A group of princes has been given the same storybook name, even though their adventures are very different. Prince Gustav wants to be known as a mighty warrior, but he feels embarrassed because Rapunzel once saved him. While visiting a farm, Gustav sees a large troll eating beets. Rosilda, the farmer, is angry because the troll is ruining her crops. She raises her shovel and orders it to leave. Gustav arrives on horseback and attacks. He knocks the troll down, but the troll soon catches him, takes his axe, and tosses him through fences and crates. Gustav thinks the red beet juice on the troll’s face means it has eaten a child. Rosilda knows the children are safe and hits the troll from behind. The troll drops Gustav and leaves. The children cheer, but the farm is badly damaged. Rosilda asks Gustav to pay for everything. She also jokes about his famous rescue by Rapunzel, which makes him even more upset.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Danny Day says he has a strange secret: he lives every day twice. His first day is called a discard day. It is like a practice day, because everything resets when he sleeps, except his memory. On discard days, Danny can skip school, play video games, eat lots of candy, pull pranks, and try wild stunts without lasting consequences. He even broke his leg while testing a bed-sheet parachute. His second day is a sticky day. That day works like a normal day for everyone else, so his choices and their results remain. Sticky Danny goes to school on time, does chores, avoids trouble, and eats less junk food. The power is not always fun. Moving to a new home means Danny must spend four days behind a truck instead of two. When he was younger, his parents thought he was strange, but a therapist helped them understand. Danny does not know why this happens, though he wonders if his birthday has a clue.

Eleven-and-a-half-year-old Danny Day has perfect attendance, even though he has skipped school hundreds of times. He can do this because every day happens twice. During a discard day, Danny practices life. At night, the day resets, so only his memory remains. He uses these days to play video games, fake being sick, pull pranks, eat seventeen candy bars, borrow his parents’ car, and test a parachute made from a bed sheet. The broken leg from that stunt disappears by the next day. During a sticky day, Danny must face normal results. He goes to school, does chores, stays out of trouble, and plays carefully. A move from Houston to Idaho shows the hard side of his power because a long trip takes twice as many days for him. Danny’s parents once worried that he was imagining things, but Dr. Donaldson helped him. Danny still does not know how his power began, although his birthday happened on February 22 at 2:22 a.m.

Danny explains that he is about eleven and a half years old, but he has experienced about twice that much time. Every day begins as a discard day and is followed by a sticky day. On the discard day, Danny can experiment because his words and actions vanish when the day resets. He remembers what happened, though. He usually plays games or pretends to be sick, but he also performs pranks and dangerous stunts. On the sticky day, life is permanent, so Danny behaves responsibly. He arrives at school on time, completes chores, avoids attention, and does not repeat his risky tricks. The unusual power can help him, but it can also make difficult events last longer. Danny remembers having the stomach flu twice and traveling four days during a move. His parents were confused when he remembered conversations they forgot. A therapist helped them accept that Danny was not crazy. Danny has investigated superhero explanations but has found no answer. He only knows that he lives every day twice.

video_title: Gorilla by Anthony Browne 🦍 | Kids Book Read Aloud | Storytime with K G Merlo

summaries.summary: Hannah loved gorillas, but her busy father never had time to take her to the zoo. For her birthday, she asked for a gorilla. At night, a little toy gorilla came alive. Hannah was frightened at first, but the gorilla smiled and asked her to visit the zoo. Hannah put on her coat, and the gorilla wore her father’s hat and coat. They swung through the trees and reached the zoo, even though it was closed. They climbed over the wall and saw many gorillas, an orangutang, and a chimpanzee. Then Hannah and the gorilla went to the cinema, walked together, and ate. At home, they danced on the lawn. Hannah was very happy. In the morning, the gorilla was only a toy again. Hannah told her father about the night. Her father asked if she wanted to go to the zoo, and Hannah was very happy.

Hannah liked reading about gorillas, watching them on television, and drawing them. She wanted to see a real gorilla, but her father was always busy or tired. On the night before her birthday, Hannah received a small toy gorilla. During the night, the toy became a real, talking gorilla. He asked Hannah to go with him to the zoo. They put on warm clothes and swung through the trees. The zoo was closed, so they climbed over the wall. Hannah saw many gorillas and also saw an orangutang and a chimpanzee. After that, she chose to go to the cinema. They walked, ate, and returned home. Before bed, Hannah and the gorilla danced on the lawn. He said he would see her tomorrow. In the morning, he was a toy again. Hannah told her father everything. This time, her father asked to take her to the zoo.

Hannah loved gorillas more than anything. She read books, watched television, and drew pictures of them. Her father worked all day and evening, so he kept saying, “Not now” or “Maybe tomorrow.” Hannah wanted a gorilla for her birthday, and a little toy gorilla appeared beside her bed. At night, it spoke to her and invited her to the zoo. Hannah was scared for a moment, then happily went along. The gorilla wore her father’s hat and coat, and they traveled through the trees. The zoo was closed, but they climbed over the wall and looked at the animals. Hannah saw gorillas, an orangutang, and a chimpanzee. Later, she and the gorilla went to the cinema, walked down the street, ate, and danced on the lawn. Hannah felt very happy. In the morning, the gorilla was a toy again. Her father then offered to take Hannah to the zoo.

video_title: Aladdin Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Aladdin - Runaway Rajah

summaries.summary: Aladdin, Jasmine, Rajah, and Abu saw a wonderful parade with snake charmers, fire-eaters, peacocks, elephants, and tigers. Jasmine showed that Rajah could balance and slice fruit with his claws. Aladdin suggested that Abu and Rajah join the parade while he and Jasmine went back to the palace. When they returned, Rajah was missing. Abu showed them that the parade people had taken him. Aladdin and Jasmine flew after the parade on the magic carpet. The carpet crashed into clotheslines, so Abu stayed to help it while Aladdin and Jasmine ran across rooftops. They found Rajah being put into a cage. Jasmine hugged him and removed his collar, but the parade master stopped her. Jasmine proved Rajah was hers by tossing him a melon. Rajah sliced it perfectly. The parade master apologized and invited Jasmine and Rajah to be the stars of a special show. Jasmine was happy to have her friend back.

A big parade passed by Aladdin and Jasmine. They watched a snake charmer, a fire-eater, peacocks, elephants, and a group of tigers. Jasmine showed everyone how clever Rajah was. He balanced a melon, an apple, and a fig, then tossed the fruit and cut it into pieces with his claws. Aladdin saw monkeys in the parade and told Abu and Rajah to walk with the performers. Later, Abu came back alone and acted out what had happened. Jasmine understood that the parade had taken Rajah. She and Aladdin followed the parade on the magic carpet. Abu fell from the carpet, but Jasmine caught him. Then the carpet became tangled in clotheslines. Aladdin and Jasmine hurried over rooftops and found Rajah near a cage. The parade master did not know he belonged to Jasmine. Rajah showed his special fruit trick, so the parade master understood his mistake. Rajah was free, and he and Jasmine became parade stars.

Jasmine loved watching the tigers in the city parade, but she also knew that her tiger, Rajah, was very special. She gave him fruit, and Rajah balanced it on his nose and cut it into pieces with his claws. Aladdin asked Abu and Rajah to join the parade. When Aladdin and Jasmine returned to the palace, Rajah was gone. Abu showed them that the parade people had taken him. They chased the parade on the magic carpet. The carpet crashed into clotheslines, so Aladdin and Jasmine continued across the rooftops while Abu helped the carpet. At last, they saw Rajah being put into a cage. Jasmine ran to him, but the parade master said Rajah was not hers because he wore no royal collar. Jasmine tossed a melon to Rajah. He sliced it quickly, proving that he was her tiger. The parade master apologized and invited them to perform together. Jasmine was glad her friend was safe.

video_title: The Three Questions

summaries.summary: Nikolai wants to be a good person, but he has three questions: When is the best time to act? Who is most important? What is the right thing to do? His friends give different answers, so Nikolai visits Leo, an old turtle, in the mountains. Leo is digging a garden. Nikolai helps him, and while they work, a storm begins. Nikolai hears a panda calling for help. He carries the injured panda to Leo’s house and makes a splint for her leg. Then he finds her cold, frightened baby and brings the little panda inside. The next morning, the mother and baby are safe. Leo explains that Nikolai’s questions were answered by what he did. The best time is now. The most important person is the one with you. The right thing is to help the person beside you.

Nikolai asks his friends how to always do the right thing. Sonia the heron says people should plan ahead. Gole the monkey says they should watch carefully. Pushkin the dog says they need friends to help them decide. The friends also give different answers about who matters most and what people should do. Nikolai thinks their answers are not quite right, so he visits Leo, a very old turtle. Leo does not answer. Instead, he gives Nikolai a shovel and lets him help dig the garden. When a storm comes, Nikolai hears a panda crying. He carries her inside, fixes her injured leg, and searches for her baby. He finds the little panda cold and wet, then brings her to safety. Leo tells Nikolai that helping the panda, the baby, and Leo showed the answers: now is important, the person nearby matters, and kindness is the right action.

A boy named Nikolai wants to understand how to be good. He asks about the best time to do things, the most important person, and the right thing to do. His friends try to answer, but each gives a different idea. Nikolai then climbs to the mountains to ask Leo the turtle. Leo is digging, so Nikolai helps him instead of insisting on an answer. During a loud storm, Nikolai discovers a panda hurt by a fallen tree. He brings her to shelter and makes a bamboo splint. The panda asks about her baby, so Nikolai runs into the storm and finds the little panda shivering on the ground. He brings the baby inside and reunites it with its mother. When Nikolai still asks for answers, Leo says his actions have already shown them. The important time is now, the important person is the one nearby, and the right thing is to do good for that person.

video_title: Fly Guy Meets Fly Girl! Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, and Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day, Buzz and Fly Guy were bored, so they went for a walk. They played chase and cooled off in a fountain. Then they saw a girl running while a fly chased her. Buzz said flies could be pets, and the girl explained that the fly was her pet, Fly Girl. Buzz showed that Fly Guy could do tricks, eat gross things, and say his name. The girl said Fly Girl could do those things too. Her name was Liz, and she invited Buzz to play on the swings. Fly Guy and Fly Girl sat together and talked in Flytalk. They told each other they were nice. Then they both said “wuzzle,” which meant “let’s be friends.” Buzz and Liz said goodbye, and everyone had fun.

Buzz and his pet Fly Guy needed something fun to do. They walked outside, played chase, and rested in a fountain. During their walk, they met Liz, a girl with a pet fly named Fly Girl. At first, Buzz and Liz compared their pets. Buzz said Fly Guy could do tricks, eat gross food, and say “Buzz.” Liz answered that Fly Girl could do the same things, and she showed that Fly Girl could say “Liz.” Then Buzz asked Liz to play on the swings, and she agreed. Fly Guy and Fly Girl sat beside each other. They used their special Flytalk words to say that they were nice. They talked for a long time, making many Flytalk sounds. Finally, both flies said “wuzzle,” meaning “let’s be friends.” Buzz and Liz said they would see each other soon.

Fly Guy was Buzz’s pet fly, and the two friends enjoyed spending time together. When they became bored, they took a walk, played chase, and cooled themselves in a fountain. They met Liz when her pet fly, Fly Girl, chased her. Liz explained that Fly Girl was not a pest but a pet. Buzz and Liz proudly told each other about their flies. summaries.summary: Derick, a longtime newspaper photo librarian, is sorting old pictures before retirement. In the background stands a tall figure dressed completely in black, staring toward the photographer. He begins to believe the photographs show a supernatural killer who has returned across time. When Derick checks the evening diary, he discovers that Nick, a young photographer, has gone to the same park to take landscape pictures. Terrified that Nick is in danger, Derick rushes from the office. However, he is killed when a truck crashes into his car, sending it into a railway cutting where an express train destroys it. At the park, Nick discovers that the black figure is actually an old, rusted Boer War statue. Before he can investigate further, someone grabs him by the neck.

summaries.summary: Pete was a predictable, practical, uncomplicated pig who liked quiet plans. During a storm, an escaped elephant named Pickles came to his house for help. Pete hid her from the circus man, and Pickles left him a dandelion. The next day, Pete found Pickles at the circus, chained in a dark tent, so he unlocked her and helped her escape. Pickles stayed at Pete’s house, where her size and unusual habits made life noisy and surprising. Soon they traveled together, imagining adventures in Switzerland, Tahiti, Paris, Venice, Moscow, and other places. Pete became tired of the changes and told Pickles she should leave. Then a pipe broke, and water flooded the house. Pete reached the last open window, but Pickles could not climb out. Pete realized he could not live without her. He stayed with Pickles through the night, sharing every breath. Firefighters rescued them, and the friends later continued their adventures together.

Together, they went on many wonderful journeys, including sledding near the Matterhorn, visiting Tahiti and Venice, and singing Italian songs. summaries.summary: A lonely old woman and old man bake a gingerbread girl after losing their gingerbread boy. They decorate her with candy and licorice hair. When the oven door opens, she jumps out and runs away. Farmers, a pig, an artist, a cow and calf, dogs, children, and teachers chase her, but she runs faster than everyone. At the river, the same fox who tricked her brother offers to help her cross. The Gingerbread Girl asks for a promise, then climbs onto his tail. The fox dives into the water and tells her to move to his head. She jumps there, ties his snout with her licorice hair, and makes him turn around. Everyone follows her back home. She and the old couple bake more gingerbread. Their house is happy and full, so they are never lonely again. The Gingerbread Girl also teaches the fox good manners.

The old woman and old man miss their gingerbread boy, so they bake a clever gingerbread girl. She escapes from the oven and sings that nobody can catch her. At last, she reaches the river where the fox is waiting. He says he was her brother’s friend and offers her a ride across. The Gingerbread Girl is careful and asks if he will keep her safe. When the fox tries to eat her, she uses a licorice strand from her hair to tie his mouth. Then she rides him back to the old couple’s house. She helps bake more cookies, and the house becomes happy and busy. The fox learns manners too.

The Gingerbread Girl is made by a lonely old woman and old man who hope she will stay safe. She hears them talk about how her brother trusted a fox, so she decides to be wiser. The fox cannot bite her and must carry her back. The crowd follows them to the house. The Gingerbread Girl mixes dough and bakes more cookies with the old couple. Their home is no longer lonely. Later, she teaches the fox manners with gingerbread crumbs.

summaries.summary: On a moonlit night, three thieves examine jewels stolen from Carlotta Grimstone. The treasures include famous cursed gems: an emerald brooch, the Crack in the Sky turquoise, and the Makepeace Diamond. One thief also takes a necklace of moonstones. When the necklace breaks, the stones form a glowing circle and show each thief a frightening vision. One thief will be caught, another will die by water, and the first sees that two people born together will die together. A helicopter arrives, forcing the thieves to run. Two thieves escape with the moonstones, but one slips into a waterfall. Years later, March McQuinn is helping his father, Alfie, complete another jewel theft in Amsterdam. March steals a bicycle and waits outside a hotel. Alfie throws him a strange blue-white stone, then falls from the roof and dies. March escapes with the stone, grieving his father and remembering his advice. Soon, he realizes someone is following him.

The story begins with three thieves celebrating a successful robbery on a dark lakeshore. Their stolen jewels are valuable but rumored to be cursed. One thief argues about keeping a necklace containing seven moonstones. When the clasp breaks, the stones glow and create a perfect circle. The thieves become unable to look away and experience visions of terrible futures. A helicopter interrupts them. Two thieves grab the moonstones and flee through the woods, across a cliff, and into an icy cave. They try to convince each other that the prophecy will not affect them. While escaping beside a waterfall, one thief slips and is swept away. In Amsterdam, March McQuinn steals a bicycle so he can help his cat-burglar father, Alfie. Alfie throws March a mysterious stone from a hotel roof, but then falls to his death. March runs away with the stone, following his father’s final instructions to find Jewels. He soon discovers that someone is following him.

March McQuinn is a young thief working with his famous father, Alfie. One night, March steals a bicycle and rides to a hotel where Alfie is stealing diamonds. March has prepared carefully, carrying food and using a false identity in case a police officer stops him. Alfie appears on the roof, but instead of climbing down, he throws March a small, bright blue-white object. March catches it in his paper bag. When he looks up again, Alfie is falling. Alfie lands badly and dies, though he manages to tell March to find Jewels. Police and medics arrive, and diamonds spill from Alfie’s pockets. March remembers his father’s rule to run when he sees a uniform, so he escapes through Amsterdam’s confusing streets. He grieves over the things they will never do together. Then the mysterious stone rolls from his bag. March believes Alfie gave it to him for a reason and promises not to let his father down. After moving only one block, March realizes someone is following him.

video_title: A Cat for Santa

summaries.summary: One day in the Enchanted Forest, a white kitten chased a blue butterfly. The butterfly was really the dark fairy, who led the kitten to a well and fell inside when the kitten startled her. The kitten was left wet, scared, and unable to remember where she lived. The Sugar Plum Fairies heard her cries and lifted her from the well. Because the kitten had no home, the orange fairy asked if she would like to live at the North Pole. The kitten agreed. Mrs. Claus saw her and asked to care for her, and the kitten said yes. Santa named her Iris because her eyes looked like iris flowers. Iris became friends with Santa’s dog, Fudge. She helped Mrs. Claus and Santa, although she once slept while Jack Frost hid the brownie ingredients. Iris found them in the cabinets. Later, she helped load Santa’s sleigh and guarded the presents from Christmas goblins.

A little white kitten became lost after chasing a blue butterfly. The butterfly changed back into the dark fairy, and the kitten fell into a deep well. The Sugar Plum Fairies heard the kitten crying and used magic to bring her out. The kitten did not remember her home, so the orange fairy invited her to live at the North Pole. Mrs. Claus wanted to take care of the kitten, and the kitten agreed. Santa was happy to meet her and named her Iris because of her green eyes. Iris and Santa’s dog, Fudge, soon became best friends. Iris helped around the house and watched for Jack Frost, but she sometimes took naps. Jack Frost once hid the brownie ingredients, and Iris helped find them in the cabinets. Iris also helped Santa on Christmas Eve. She loaded presents, helped with the sleigh, and used her snowball cannon to stop goblins from stealing gifts before Santa’s Christmas journey.

Iris began as a lost kitten in the Enchanted Forest. She chased what looked like a blue butterfly, but it was the dark fairy in disguise. The kitten fell into a well and cried until the Sugar Plum Fairies rescued her. Since Iris could not remember where she lived, the fairies took her to the North Pole. Mrs. Claus asked to keep her, and Iris happily agreed. Santa loved cats, so he was delighted to meet her. He called her Iris because her eyes were the color of iris flowers. Iris became a good friend to Fudge, Santa’s dog. She helped Mrs. Claus bake, though she slept through one trick by Jack Frost. When Jack hid the ingredients, Iris figured out that they were in the cabinets. On Christmas Eve, Iris helped Santa load his sleigh and shoot presents into his bag. She then guarded the gifts with her snowball cannon while Santa prepared to deliver them.

video_title: Gravity Falls Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Mabel, Dipper, and Wendy are working at the Mystery Shack when Wendy invites the twins to join her friends. They drive to an abandoned convenience store that is rumored to be haunted. Inside, the teenagers play with the store’s food, games, and television. When Dipper sits on a chalk outline, the lights go out and the haunted store traps the group in different objects. Dipper notices that each person was taken while doing something teenagers often do, such as texting, playing games, or acting sarcastically. He realizes the ghosts dislike teenagers. Dipper admits that he is twelve, not thirteen, and two old ghosts explain that teenagers once annoyed them with rude behavior and loud rap music. To free his friends, Dipper performs the embarrassing Lamby Dance in a lamb costume. The ghosts enjoy the dance and release everyone. Dipper hides the truth about his dance, while his friends praise him as Dr. Fun Times.

At the Mystery Shack, Mabel persuades Dipper to go with Wendy and her friends to a condemned convenience store. The building is supposed to be haunted, but the group enters anyway and starts a food fight. They soon find chalk outlines on the floor. Dipper steps onto one, and strange magic begins. Tambri is pulled into the television, Thompson is trapped inside a dancing game, and Lee is placed on a cereal box. Mabel becomes possessed and warns the trespassers that the store will be their eternal home. Dipper and Wendy hide while Dipper studies what happened. He discovers that everyone was captured while behaving like a teenager. Dipper tells the ghost he is twelve. Two ghosts appear and explain that they hate teenagers because rude teens once caused their deaths with shocking music. They demand a funny dance. Dipper wears a lamb costume and performs the Lamby Dance, freeing his friends and restoring the store.

Wendy takes Mabel and Dipper to meet her friends at an abandoned dusk-to-dawn convenience store. The friends joke about the building, enter through the roof, and play among the old snacks and machines. The fun ends when Dipper lies on a chalk outline. The store’s lights flicker, and the group is attacked by its supernatural powers. Tambri disappears into a television, Thompson is swallowed by a video game, and Lee is trapped on a cereal box. Mabel is possessed, and the room turns upside down. Dipper searches for a pattern and sees that each victim was doing a typical teenage activity. He calls out to the ghost and explains that he is only twelve. The ghosts reveal that they banished teenagers after their own deaths, caused by teens’ irritating behavior and loud rap music. Dipper agrees to dance in a lamb costume. His ridiculous performance satisfies the ghosts, who release everyone. The friends leave and plan to meet at the Mystery Shack next time.

summaries.summary: Mike sat in Boo’s bedroom and acted silly to make her laugh. He wanted to help power Monstropolis. Boo was happy to see Mike, but she did not laugh as much as usual. She pointed to pictures of school and children showing vacation photos. Boo said school would start soon, and she wanted a fun story and pictures about her vacation. Mike took Boo through her closet door to Monsters, Inc. He found an old camera. Boo’s big laugh made it work. Mike surprised Sully, and the monsters showed Boo their tricks. Boo took many photos around Monsters, Inc. and Monstropolis. Sully learned that Boo wanted to show a picture at school. He said the monster world had to stay secret. Boo became sad, so Sully let her take one picture. At school, Boo showed it to her class. Everyone thought it was Bigfoot, but Boo said it was Kitty.

Boo wanted to tell her class about her summer vacation, but she needed a fun story and some pictures. Mike understood and took her to Monsters, Inc. through her closet door. He borrowed an old camera and made a silly sound. Boo laughed so hard that the lights flickered, so Mike knew the camera worked. Then Mike brought Boo to the laugh floor and surprised Sully. The monsters were excited to see Boo and showed her their new tricks. Mike and Boo hurried all around Monsters, Inc. and Monstropolis. Boo took many photos. Sully was worried because humans were not supposed to know about the monster world. He saw that Boo was disappointed. Finally, Sully said Boo could take one picture, and he would choose it. The next day, Boo showed the picture at school. Her teacher thought it was Bigfoot, but Boo happily said it was Kitty.

Boo had pictures of school and children with vacation photos. She wanted to have a special vacation story for her class. Mike invited her to Monsters, Inc. and helped her borrow an old camera. Boo laughed when Mike made a funny sound, and the camera worked. Mike then called for Sully. Sully hugged Boo, and many monsters showed her their tricks. They visited places all over Monsters, Inc. and Monstropolis, taking lots of photos before school began. Mike explained that Boo wanted to share the photos with her class. Sully said the monster world must remain a secret from the human world. Boo looked sad, and Sully wanted to help her. He allowed her to take one photo, but he chose which one. At school, Boo told the class about her adventure. Nobody believed her until she showed the picture. The teacher thought the picture showed Bigfoot. Boo giggled and said it showed Kitty.

The friends must leave the van and look for a warm place. Scooby finds a large, empty house. They climb inside and discover two robbers hiding in the cellar with money from a bank. The friends are frightened, but they make a plan. They move furniture against the cellar door so the robbers cannot get upstairs. Scooby carries a flashlight in his mouth and runs into the road. He catches the attention of a police car. The police come to the house and arrest the robbers. The friends explain what happened. They say Scooby is their real hero because he brought help. They promise to buy him the biggest, juiciest steak ever.

After shopping, Scooby-Doo and the gang drive through a heavy snowstorm. They do not recognize the road, and the Mystery Machine stops even though it still has gas. Fred discovers that the battery is the problem. The friends leave the van and follow Scooby to an old house. The house has no lights and is boarded up, but Scooby finds a loose window. Inside, they hear two crooks counting money from a bank robbery. The friends hide upstairs. They know the crooks have guns, so they push desks, tables, and chairs against the cellar door. When the crooks try to get upstairs, the friends hold the door shut. Then Scooby runs outside with a flashlight and signals a passing police car. The police arrest the robbers. The friends thank Scooby and call him a hero.

A snowstorm makes it hard for Scooby-Doo and his friends to drive home. Their van breaks down, so they search for shelter. Scooby leads them to a dark, empty house. The friends enter through a loose window and hear robbers downstairs. The robbers have guns and money from a bank. The friends want to stay quiet until morning, but they also need help. They block the cellar door with old furniture. One chair falls and makes a loud sound, so the robbers try to force the door open. The friends push back and wait for Scooby. Outside, Scooby runs with a flashlight in his mouth. A police car sees him and stops. The police enter the house and take charge. The friends tell the officer about the robbers. The officer arrests them, and everyone agrees that Scooby saved them by bringing help.

summaries.summary: It was a lovely summer morning, but little Roo felt grumpy. He did not know why, and he did not want to play. Roo still would not smile. His mother tossed dry leaves into the air, and the leaves landed on Roo. He looked funny, but he still said he was not smiling. Then it was time for breakfast.
