summaries.summary: Ben Ripley is a twelve-year-old who thinks his life is ordinary. He goes to school, struggles with bullies, and secretly dreams of becoming a spy. One day, CIA agent Alexander Hale appears in Ben’s house and explains that the agency has been watching him. Ben is a brilliant student with unusual mathematical and testing abilities, so the CIA accepts him into its secret Academy of Espionage. Ben leaves home immediately, even though he must pretend to attend a normal science academy. At the school, Alexander suddenly tells him to run because armed attackers are shooting at them. Ben reaches a dormitory and is tackled by a mysterious girl named Erica. She gives him a taser and explains that enemies have taken students and teachers hostage. Erica escaped because she skipped the assembly where everyone else was captured. Ben learns that dozens of dangerous commandos are inside the school. Although he has only just arrived, he must help face the crisis.

Ben Ripley’s life changes when Alexander Hale, a CIA agent, visits his home. Alexander says the agency knows Ben is a straight-A student, speaks three languages, has excellent mathematics skills, and shows talent for espionage. Ben is offered a place at the secret CIA school, where students train to become spies. He is excited by the chance to become like Alexander, so he agrees without fully considering the dangers. Ben’s parents believe he is attending an ordinary science academy. When Ben arrives at the hidden campus, it looks like an old private school surrounded by walls and snow. Then Alexander notices that the grounds are strangely empty. He orders Ben to run while shooting breaks out. Ben escapes into a dormitory, where a skilled older girl attacks him before discovering that he is new. She introduces herself through her actions rather than her name, equips him with a taser, and leads him through the building. She explains that armed enemies have surrounded the assembly hall and captured everyone inside.

Ben Ripley has always imagined that spies are confident, athletic, and exciting, so he is thrilled when Alexander Hale tells him he has been chosen for spy school. The CIA selected Ben because of his remarkable test results, mathematical talent, electronics ability, and interest in the agency. Ben worries that he is too awkward and ordinary, but he accepts the offer because he wants adventure and hopes to impress Elizabeth Pasternak. At the academy, however, the adventure becomes frightening immediately. The campus appears deserted, and Alexander discovers that something is wrong. He gives Ben a chance to run, and gunfire follows Ben across the snowy path. Inside the dormitory, a girl in black pins him down. She is calm, strong, and armed, and she soon realizes Ben is a new student. She hands him a taser and explains that a security breach has allowed heavily armed enemies to take the school’s students and faculty hostage. With communications blocked and forty-one attackers counted, Ben receives a terrifying welcome to spy school.

video_title: Wiggle | A fun story for those who can’t stop moving!

summaries.summary: Wiggle is a playful story about moving in many funny ways. It begins by asking if you wake up with a wiggle and wiggle out of bed. If you wiggle while eating breakfast, your food might land on your head. You can wiggle where your tail would be, wiggle all your hair, and wiggle in your underwear. You can wiggle with your shadow and your toys. Gorillas may make a wiggle noise when they wiggle. In the water, you can wiggle one fin on each side or open wide and wiggle like a crocodile. Wiggles can fill the sky where wings would be. You can wiggle slowly with shy polar bears. A snake is one big wiggle, with no wings, tails, or feet. Some wiggles are worth waiting for. At the end, everyone wiggles, even on the moon.

This story invites everyone to wiggle. First, it asks about waking up with a wiggle and wiggling out of it. Wiggling with breakfast can make breakfast end up on your head. The story then shows many more wiggles: wiggling where a tail would be, wiggling your hair, and wiggling in your underwear. You can wiggle with your shadow or your toys. Gorillas might make a wiggle noise. In water, wiggle one fin on each side, or wiggle like a crocodile with its mouth open wide. If you wiggle where wings would be, wiggles fill the sky. With polar bears, wiggle slowly because they are very wiggle shy. Snakes are one big wiggle, with no wings, tails, or feet. Some wiggles are worth waiting for. The story ends by asking you to wiggle on the moon and saying that everyone is wiggling.

Wiggle can happen at breakfast, in your hair, with your shadow, and with your toys. The story begins with questions about waking up with a wiggle and wiggling out of it. A breakfast wiggle may send food onto your head. Then the story asks you to wiggle where your tail would be and to wiggle all your hair while feeling extra silly. You can wiggle in your underwear, with your shadow, or with toys. You can wiggle with gorillas and hear a wiggle noise. In water, wiggle one fin on each side or move like a crocodile, open big and wide. Wiggles can fill the sky where wings would be. Polar bears need a slow wiggle because they are wiggle shy. Snakes are one big wiggle, with no wings, tails, or feet. Some wiggles are worth waiting for. Soon, everyone wiggles, even on the moon.

summaries.summary: Marcus Jackson loves drawing comics about Toothpick, a skinny superhero who becomes powerful when Marcus gets scared or angry. One day, Marcus imagines Toothpick defeating the villain Dead Eye and his henchmen. His friend JR visits, but Marcus agrees to play a zombie video game instead of finishing his drawing. They play for three hours, so Marcus’s father takes away the game. Marcus’s father also learns that Tyrell may have chased Marcus home from school and warns him not to bring violent drawings to school. Because study lab is full and Marcus dislikes sports, his father signs him up for filmmaking. In film class, Marcus meets Jasmine, Khalid, Amari, and Sierra. When the teacher suggests making a superhero movie, Marcus realizes he could make a Toothpick movie and star in it. However, the class must create Sierra’s screenplay, Phone Zombies, for the school arts showcase. Marcus promises to bring his own screenplay the next day.

The story begins with Marcus imagining his superhero, Toothpick, fighting Dead Eye in a deli. Toothpick is actually Marcus’s alter ego. When Marcus becomes frightened or angry, he changes into a taller, stronger hero with sharp finger spears. Marcus’s friend JR interrupts his drawing and persuades him to play Army of the Undead 3. Their game lasts until Marcus’s father comes home, and Marcus loses the game system for breaking the rule about gaming on school days. His father then makes him choose an after-school activity. Marcus rejects sports, study lab, martial arts, chess, and musical theater before choosing filmmaking. In the class, Marcus argues with Sierra, a girl he dislikes, and learns that she has written a screenplay called Phone Zombies. The teachers ask the students to use Sierra’s script for their group film. Marcus wants to make Toothpick’s movie instead, so he decides to turn his comics into a screenplay.

Marcus is excited about his imaginary hero Toothpick, who defeats Dead Eye and protects people. While Marcus draws this adventure, JR comes over and talks about a real bully named Tyrell, who may have chased Marcus from the bus stop. JR then convinces Marcus to play a zombie game. Their three-hour gaming session makes Marcus’s father angry, and the game system is taken away. Marcus must also join an after-school program. Since art class has rules Marcus dislikes and every other activity seems wrong for him, he chooses filmmaking. The first film class includes Jasmine, who wants to make beauty videos; Khalid, who likes monster movies; Amari, who makes music; and Sierra, who wants to become a filmmaker and actor. Marcus and Sierra insult each other until the teachers calm them down. When Marcus imagines making and starring in a Toothpick movie, he becomes determined. But the class has already chosen Sierra’s screenplay, Phone Zombies. Marcus insists that his own movie will be better and plans to bring in his Toothpick comics as a screenplay.

video_title: HOW TO CATCH THE EASTER BUNNY Read Aloud ~ Easter Stories for Kids ~ Kids Read Along Books

summaries.summary: The Easter Bunny works with his peeps and crew to make eggs and bring them to children. He keeps his real name secret, and his friends call him EB. He comes to homes where there is Easter spirit. People make traps for him with carrots, rugs, a dance floor, and clever machines. The Bunny is very fast. He uses his burrowing skills, dances away, listens with his super sonic ears, and hops over flying fish and cherry yogurt pops. He can even change from two feet tall into something small and gray, but strong Easter spirit helps people see him. He delivers many treats, then escapes the Bunny Tumbler 2.0 with his lucky rabbit’s feet. After taking treats to children big and small, he makes one special stop for his favorite kid. He says Easter is here and no one can catch him because he is too fast.

The Easter Bunny says he has worked hard with his peeps and crew to make Easter eggs. He brings the eggs and treats to children, but he hides his true identity. People try to catch him. First, they put carrots on a plate, but the Bunny is too fast. Then they cover a hole with a rug, but burrowing is part of his life. A bright dance floor does not stop him either. He dances and runs behind a door. Clever engineers make another trap, but the Bunny has super sonic ears. He dodges flying fish and cherry yogurt pops, hops away, and changes his size to something small and gray. His Easter spirit is still easy to see. He leaves treats for children, escapes the Bunny Tumbler 2.0, and wins with his lucky rabbit’s feet. Then he delivers the treats and visits his favorite kid.

EB is the Easter Bunny, and he is coming to homes with Easter spirit. He has made eggs with his peeps and crew and carries treats in a magic basket. Many traps try to catch him. Carrots do not work, and a rug over a hole cannot stop him because he likes burrowing. A fully lit dance floor only gives him a place to do hip-hop before he dashes away. A trap made by brilliant engineers also fails because the Bunny has super sonic ears. He hops over flying fish and cherry yogurt pops. Then he changes from two feet tall into something small and gray, although the Easter spirit helps people see him. He leaves treats so children will not be sad. The Bunny Tumbler 2.0 spins him around, but his lucky rabbit’s feet help him win. He delivers treats to children and makes one special stop before saying he is too fast to catch.

video_title: 💤 Goodnight Ganesha

summaries.summary: Vikram and the narrator spend a gentle bedtime evening with Nana and Tata. They begin by saying good night to the window, the frame, and Ganesha, who watches their game. In Nana’s grand room, they see marigolds, the moon, and planes outside. A breeze moves through the open curtains, and a little gecko hides. They notice the golden figures of Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu on the mantle. Tata says it is bedtime, so everyone goes upstairs to brush their teeth. Tata tells stories, gives kisses, and soon falls asleep. The children prepare a tray in the Puja room, light the deepam, smell flowers, and whisper while Tata snores. Nana tells one more tale about how peacocks got their blue plumes. Then Nana hums, drinks chai, and turns off the light. Vikram, the narrator, Nana, and a bear snuggle together. They say good night to Ganesha, their family, love, and the stars.

At bedtime, Vikram and the narrator say good night to many things around their home. Ganesha sits by the window with wisdom in hand and watches them play. The children see marigolds, a bright moon, and planes zooming in the sky. A cool breeze comes through the curtains, and a shy baby gecko scurries away. On the marble mantle, golden idols of Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu gleam. Tata’s face becomes red as a beet, and Nana says it is time for bed. After brushing their teeth, Tata kisses their hands, tickles their feet, and tells stories before falling asleep. The children gather in the Puja room, light the deepam, smell perfume and flowers, and whisper while Tata snores. Nana tells them one more story about peacocks. At last, Nana sings softly, turns out the light, and strokes their hair as they fall asleep.

The bedtime story follows two children, Vikram and the narrator, as they settle down with Nana and Tata. They greet Ganesha by the window and say good night to the room, the moon, planes, curtains, and a hiding gecko. They look at Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu on the shining mantle. Tata announces bedtime, and the children brush their teeth. Tata shares familiar stories, kisses their hands, tickles their feet, and then becomes tired and sleeps. In the dim Puja room, the children arrange a round tray, light the deepam, and enjoy the smell of perfume and flowers. They whisper and wiggle, but Tata’s loud snore scares sleep away. After closing the door, they sit on the floor and ask Nana for one more tale about peacocks and their blue plumes. Nana hums while drinking spicy chai. Finally, she turns off the light, and everyone snuggles together beneath the stars.

video_title: Pete the Cat Out of This World (Adventure & Exploration)#toddlers #kindergarten #educational #school

summaries.summary: Pete the Cat goes to space camp and meets his bunkmate, Glenn. Pete and Glenn put on space uniforms and learn about astronauts. They practice in a zero-gravity chamber, ride rovers, and build rockets. Pete’s rocket flies very far. Then Pete learns that a moon mission is leaving that day, and there is room for him to join. Pete climbs into the space capsule with Tom and Sally. After the countdown, their ship flies past a satellite and a comet. On the moon, the astronauts collect rocks and make maps. Pete puts on a jetpack and flies toward Mars to take pictures. Then Pete notices that he has lost track of time. The moon is far away, and he must return before the ship leaves. Pete makes it back just in time. The astronauts fly home, and Pete plays more music. He is happy to be back on solid ground after his amazing trip to outer space.

Pete the Cat is excited to attend space camp. He meets Glenn, puts on a uniform, and hurries to class. The campers learn about space trips and try many activities. They float in a zero-gravity chamber, ride rovers, and build rockets. Pete builds a rocket that flies very, very far. Soon, Tom tells the campers that a flight to the moon is leaving that day. Sally asks Pete to come along, and Pete happily agrees. During the trip, the ship passes a satellite and a comet. Tom and Sally surprise Pete with his guitar, so Pete plays a song in space. On the moon, they collect rocks and map the ground. Pete uses a jetpack to take pictures near Mars, but he stays away too long. He races back and reaches the ship before it takes off. Then everyone returns home, with time for more tunes.

At space camp, Pete the Cat discovers many exciting things about astronauts. He and Glenn dress in uniforms and go to class. Pete floats, rides in a rover, and builds a rocket. His rocket travels very far, which makes Glenn cheer. Then Pete is invited to join a moon flight with Tom and Sally. The spacecraft lifts off and zooms through space. The travelers see a satellite and a comet. Pete receives his guitar and plays a groovy song while mission control listens. When they reach the moon, the astronauts explore, gather rocks, and draw maps of the surface. Pete has another job, so he puts on a jetpack and flies toward Mars to take pictures. He loses track of time and must hurry back because the moon is far from the ship. Pete returns just in time. The astronauts go home, and Pete enjoys playing music before standing safely on solid ground again.

video_title: Kindness is My Superpower | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Lucas is an ordinary boy who loves his toy Teddy, candy, jelly, and cakes. One day, he teases his friend Lisa about her glasses, and she cries. At home, Lucas’s mother tells him that what he did was wrong and explains that kindness means using gentle words, respecting people, and helping others. Lucas thinks about her words and decides to be kind. The next morning, he thanks his mother, cleans up his toys, and makes his bed. He welcomes a new boy on the bus, helps him find his classroom, greets his friends, and shares his crayons and pens. Lucas apologizes to Lisa, and she says it is okay. He waits patiently for the slide, helps a boy find a ball, and picks up trash. Later, he helps people in his neighborhood and cares for his family. Lucas stops teasing, shouting, and being selfish. He learns that kindness can make his heart shine and that kindness can come back to you.

Lucas does something unkind when he teases Lisa about her glasses and makes her cry. His mother holds his hand and explains that kindness means saying gentle words, respecting older and younger people, and helping anyone in need. Lucas wants to change, so he decides to become kind. The next day, he says thank you to his mother, puts away his toys, and makes his bed. He invites a new boy to sit beside him on the bus and helps him find his classroom. Lucas says hello to his friends and shares his crayons and pens. When he sees Lisa, he apologizes, and Lisa smiles and says it is okay. Lucas is kind at school and outside school too. He waits for the slide, helps find a lost ball, picks up trash, holds a door for a lady with a stroller, and helps an old lady cross the street. At home, he helps his family and his neighbor. Lucas learns that being kind is not hard.

Lucas begins as a boy who sometimes makes mistakes. After teasing Lisa and making her cry, he learns from his mother that kindness is shown through gentle words, respect, and good deeds. Lucas thinks about this all night and chooses to change. In the morning, he thanks his mother and takes care of his room. He is friendly to a new boy on the bus, helps him find his classroom, greets his friends, and shares his things. Lucas tells Lisa he is sorry, and she forgives him. He then practices kindness in many places. He waits patiently for his turn, helps a little boy find a lost ball, picks up trash, holds open a door, and helps an old lady cross the street. At home, he covers his sleeping father, kisses his forehead, helps his little sister tie her shoe, and shares cake with his lonely neighbor. Lucas also helps water the flowers. He stops teasing, slamming doors, shouting, and acting selfishly. He learns that kindness brings joy.

video_title: The Curious Garden by Peter Brown

summaries.summary: Liam lived in a city with no gardens, trees, or greenery, but he loved being outdoors. One day, he explored an old railway and found a small patch of wild flowers and plants. The plants were dying, so Liam came back every day to care for them. He learned how to water and prune them, and soon the little patch became a real garden. The garden began to grow along the railway. Weeds and mosses moved first, and then the more delicate plants followed. Liam explored the railway with the curious garden through spring, summer, and autumn. In winter, snow kept him away, so he prepared tools and plans for spring. When the snow melted, the sun and Liam’s help woke the plants. The garden spread into the city. Many years later, the whole city was filled with gardens, but Liam’s favorite garden was still the one where everything began.

In a dreary city without trees or gardens, Liam enjoyed splashing outside while other people stayed indoors. During one walk near the old railway, he discovered stairs leading to the tracks. There he found dying wild flowers and plants. Liam knew he could help, so he returned the next day and became their gardener. At first, he made mistakes with watering and pruning, but he found better ways to care for the plants. Soon, the plants formed a garden. The garden was not content to stay in one place. Weeds and mosses spread down the railway, and delicate plants followed them. Winter brought snow, so Liam could not visit, but he prepared for spring. After the snow melted, he brought new gardening tools, and the sun helped the plants wake up. The garden spread through the city, and new gardeners appeared. Years later, the city had blossomed.

Liam was the only boy in a gray city who loved spending time outdoors. While exploring an old railway, he found a lonely patch of flowers and plants. They were dying and needed a gardener. Liam began caring for them, even though he had to learn how to water and prune correctly. As the weeks passed, Liam became a real gardener, and the plants became a real garden. The garden grew curious and traveled along the railway. Tough weeds and mosses spread first, followed by delicate plants. After three seasons, winter covered the city with snow, and Liam stayed away from the garden. Instead, he prepared for spring. When the snow melted, Liam returned with gardening gear and tools. The sun and his careful planning helped the plants wake up. The garden then spread beyond the railway, growing in forgotten places across the city. Many years later, the city was full of gardens, and Liam loved the garden where it all began.

video_title: The Diary of a Spider 🕷️ Kids & Family Together Picture Story Book | Read Aloud English

summaries.summary: A young spider writes about school, family, and her best friend, Fly. Grandpa visits school and teaches that spiders are not insects, that insects have six legs, and that spiders help keep insects from taking over the world. The spider learns to travel on the wind and practices climbing, releasing silk, and flying. She and her sister make a web on a water fountain. At school, she learns to run from dangerous vacuums. She visits Worm’s house, molts her skin, and brings the old skin for show-and-tell. When Fly feels sad after Daddy Longlegs teases her, the spider shares her lunch with him. Fly’s treehouse and Grandpa are later blown away, but Grandpa returns from Paris. The spider and Fly have a few funny accidents together. At the end, the spider writes that spiders and people might get along if they took time to know each other.

The spider’s diary tells about her busy life with her family and friends. On Grandparents Day, Grandpa teaches her about spiders and insects. At gym class, she learns how to catch the wind and makes flash cards to practice flying. She and her sister try playground equipment, but their sticky web works best on the water fountain. The spider learns that vacuums are dangerous and is frightened during a vacuum drill. She sleeps at Worm’s house, molts her skin, and takes the old skin to school. When Daddy Longlegs makes fun of Fly, the spider finds him and gives him some lunch instead of being unkind. Fly’s treehouse blows away, and Grandpa travels to Paris before coming home. Later, Fly gets stuck in the spider’s web, so they play at Fly’s house. The spider ends by saying that spiders should not all be judged by the few that bite.

A little spider records important days from March through August. Grandpa teaches her that spiders are different from insects and tells her that spiders and flies once did not get along. The spider learns how to catch the wind and notices that Fly can fly. She plays with her sister, practices safety at school, and learns to stop, drop, and run when she hears a vacuum. She visits Worm, grows too big for her skin, and brings her old skin to show-and-tell. The spider tries to help Fly after Daddy Longlegs teases her, and she gives him part of her lunch. Wind carries away Fly’s treehouse and Grandpa, but Grandpa later returns from Paris with stories about French bugs. Fly gets stuck in the spider’s web, and Grandpa laughs. The spider learns never to fall asleep in a shoe. Finally, she writes that spiders and people could get along if they took time to know one another.

video_title: 🚓💨 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Pixar Cars 3 : Taken By Storm

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen is a famous race car. One day, a new racer named Jackson Storm beats him. Storm is very fast, but he is unkind. He ignores a young fan and makes fun of Lightning. Lightning goes to Thomasville to train with Smokey and Cruz Ramirez. Cruz helps Lightning practice driving around tractors and learning new skills. Storm keeps training alone and thinks he will always win. At the Florida 500, Lightning begins the race and moves ahead. Then some cars crash, and a yellow flag stops the race. Lightning asks Cruz to finish for him. Cruz feels nervous, but Lightning reminds her of their training. Cruz catches Storm. Storm pushes Cruz toward the wall, but Cruz drives up the wall and flips over him. Cruz wins the race. Everyone cheers, and Cruz says she learned from the best: Lightning McQueen.

Jackson Storm is a new racing car who wins many races against Lightning McQueen. People admire Storm because he is fast, but Storm is not kind. He does not stop for a child who wants an autograph, and he laughs at Lightning. Lightning travels to Doc Hudson’s hometown to get ready for another race. Smokey and Cruz Ramirez help him train. Cruz is learning to be a racer, too. At the big Florida 500 race, Lightning starts racing against Storm. After a crash, Lightning sends Cruz onto the track to finish the race. Cruz remembers her training and races hard. She catches Storm. Storm pushes her toward the wall, but Cruz uses her skills to drive along the wall and pass him. Cruz crosses the finish line first. Storm is shocked, and Lightning celebrates with Cruz. When a reporter asks how she won, Cruz says she learned from Lightning.

The racing season is busy, and Lightning McQueen meets a speedy rookie called Jackson Storm. Storm beats Lightning and believes he is better than everyone. He will not talk kindly to fans, and he spends many hours training on a simulator. Lightning prepares for a rematch with help from Smokey and Cruz Ramirez. Cruz practices difficult driving while tractors chase her. At the Florida 500, Storm expects an easy victory. Lightning races well, but a crash brings out the yellow flag. Lightning chooses Cruz to take his place. Cruz is nervous, so Lightning reminds her about what they practiced. She races after Storm and catches him. Storm tries to push Cruz into the wall. Cruz keeps control, drives up the wall, and flips over Storm. She lands safely and finishes first. The crowd cheers for Cruz and Lightning. Reporters ask Cruz how she beat Storm, and Cruz smiles and says she learned from the best.

video_title: The Ugly Pumpkin

summaries.summary: An ugly pumpkin waits all through October to be picked, but each time things seem hopeful, he is tricked. One bright, crispy day, a skeleton comes for pumpkins. The pumpkin asks for a ride, but the skeleton laughs and says no. When the pumpkin says it is getting late and he has no home, the skeleton rolls his eye, says goodbye, and leaves him alone. The pumpkin walks into November and finds some trees. He politely asks to stay. The trees smile, and one tells him to take off his boots and spread his roots. The pumpkin realizes this is another cruel joke. He shouts that he is ugly, and rain begins to fall, so he cries. Then he finds shelter in a garden full of squash. He notices something odd and discovers that he is a squash too. At Thanksgiving, he finds where he fits in, and the feast can begin.

The pumpkin says that none of the many pumpkins are quite like him. He has waited since early October to be picked, but every chance ends badly. A skeleton visits one day, and the pumpkin asks to ride along. The skeleton says no and leaves the pumpkin alone when he explains that he has no home. In November, the pumpkin walks until he comes to some trees. He asks if he may stay, and he says please. The trees smile, but one tells him to take off his boots and spread his roots. This is another cruel joke for the pumpkin. He shouts at the sky, and then rain makes him cry. He hides in a garden covered with squash. There, he notices something very strange. He realizes, “I’m a squash at last.” It is Thanksgiving, and the pumpkin finally finds where he fits in. His story ends as the feast begins.

A pumpkin feels different from the other pumpkins and calls himself ugly. He waits in October to be picked, but he keeps getting tricked. A skeleton comes for pumpkins, yet he will not give the pumpkin a ride. The pumpkin says it is late and that he has no home, but the skeleton rolls his eye and leaves. The pumpkin keeps walking into November. He meets trees and asks to stay for a while. The trees smile, then one says, “Take off your boots and spread your roots.” The pumpkin knows this is another cruel joke. He cries out to the sky, and rain starts falling. He takes shelter in a garden filled with squash. Then he notices something odd and discovers that he is a squash after all. On Thanksgiving, he finds the place where he belongs. After being alone and turned away, the pumpkin finally joins the feast.

video_title: The Eleventh Hour: A Curious Mystery By Graeme Base

summaries.summary: When Horus the elephant turns eleven, he plans a grand fancy-dress birthday party for his friends. He writes invitations, chooses eleven kinds of food, prepares eleven games, and cooks a huge feast. Guests arrive in wonderful costumes, including an admiral, a punk, an astronaut, a princess, a musketeer, Cleopatra, a judge, and angels. They play many funny games, such as sack racing, musical chairs, cards, snakes and ladders, cricket, pool, blind man's buff, tennis, hide-and-seek, chess, and tug-of-war. Everyone is too excited to eat until the eleventh hour. When the time finally comes, the guests rush to the dining hall, but the feast has vanished. They accuse one another, yet nobody admits taking it. Horus cheers everyone up by making healthier sandwiches. Then he reveals that he saved the birthday cake in the kitchen. The friends enjoy a picnic on the lawn, but they never discover who stole the feast.

Horus is excited because he has turned eleven for the first time. He invites his friends to a fancy-dress party and carefully prepares food, games, and decorations. The guests come dressed as colorful characters, and Horus welcomes them in a grand hall. A magnificent feast is displayed, but Horus tells everyone they must wait until the eleventh hour before eating. During the wait, the friends enjoy a series of unusual games. They race, play cards, cricket, pool, tennis, hide-and-seek, chess, and tug-of-war. At last, the special hour arrives, and everyone runs toward the feast. However, all the food has disappeared, leaving only crumbs. Each guest denies being the thief, even though some have large appetites. Horus decides that being sad will not help, so he makes wholemeal sandwiches. Finally, he brings out the birthday cake, which he had hidden in the kitchen. The party ends happily with a picnic, but the mystery remains unsolved.

Horus the elephant wants his eleventh birthday to be unforgettable, so he organizes a party with eleven games and a large homemade feast. His animal friends arrive in clever costumes, and they admire the beautifully decorated hall and table. Horus will not let them eat until the eleventh hour, so the guests spend the day playing games. Some games end in ties, some are won by lucky players, and some are stopped by accidents. After tug-of-war, the guests hurry upstairs to eat. They are shocked to find that the cakes, cream, chocolate mousse, and other food are gone. The animals question one another. The zebra, tiger, giraffes, mouse, pig, rhinos, cat, and crocodile all deny stealing the feast, but no one can prove who is innocent. Horus brings sandwiches from the kitchen and tells them they are healthier than the original food. Then he surprises everyone with the birthday cake, which he had kept safely away. The guests enjoy the rest of the celebration, although the thief is never identified.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse 📖 Read Along Storybook | Minnie's Summer Vacation

summaries.summary: Minnie is happy because it is summer. Her friends want to do different things. Mickey wants to swim, Goofy wants to fish, Daisy wants to swing, Pluto wants to dig, and Donald wants to hike. Minnie wants to take pictures. Minnie knows they can go to Star Lake. Goofy can fish there, and Mickey can swim. Daisy needs help to swing, so Minnie calls Toodles. Toodles helps Daisy swing. Pluto wants to dig for a bone, but he needs help too. Minnie calls Toodles, and Toodles brings a map. Then Pluto can dig. Donald can hike up a hill. Pluto finds a bone. Daisy swings, Goofy fishes, Mickey swims, and Minnie takes pictures. Everyone has a happy summer.

It is summer, and Minnie is happy. She asks what her friends want to do. Mickey wants to swim. Goofy wants to fish. Daisy wants to swing. Pluto wants to dig. Donald wants to hike. Minnie wants to take pictures. Minnie says they can go to Star Lake. Goofy fishes, and Mickey swims. Daisy cannot swing until Minnie calls Toodles. Toodles helps Daisy swing. Pluto wants to dig for a bone, but he cannot do it at first. Minnie calls Toodles again, and Toodles brings a map. Pluto can dig and finds a bone. Donald can hike up a hill. At Star Lake, Daisy swings, Goofy fishes, Mickey swims, and Minnie takes pictures. The friends have a happy summer.

Minnie and her friends enjoy a summer day at Star Lake. Each friend has a plan. Mickey wants to swim, Goofy wants to fish, Daisy wants to swing, Pluto wants to dig, and Donald wants to hike. Minnie wants to take pictures. Minnie calls Toodles when Daisy needs help, and Toodles helps Daisy swing. Pluto wants to dig for a bone, but he needs help. Minnie calls Toodles, and Toodles brings a map. Pluto can then dig, and he finds a bone. Donald hikes up a hill. Goofy fishes, Mickey swims, Daisy swings, and Minnie takes pictures. Minnie is happy, and the friends have a happy summer together.

video_title: I Am Anne Frank (With Highlighted Words) Cd Audio: Read Along

summaries.summary: Anne Frank was a Jewish girl who loved playing, watching movies, collecting autographs, and writing stories. She lived in Germany when Adolf Hitler and the Nazis began treating Jewish people cruelly. Anne’s family moved to Amsterdam, but the Nazis soon took over there too. Jewish people lost many freedoms, and Anne’s sister received a notice that meant she might be sent to a concentration camp. Anne’s family went into hiding in a secret space behind a bookcase. Seven people lived there quietly for more than two years. Helpful friends brought them food, books, and news. Anne studied, wrote in her diary, and found hope by looking at the sky and a chestnut tree. The people in hiding were eventually found, and Anne died during the Holocaust. Her diary was saved and became famous. Anne’s story reminds us to help people, speak up against unfairness, and look for hope even in dark times.

Anne Frank grew up enjoying ordinary childhood activities and dreamed of becoming a writer. Because Anne and her family were Jewish, the Nazis made unfair rules against them. They could not visit many public places, attend their old school, or move freely. When Anne’s sister received a call-up notice, the family decided to hide. They entered a secret annex behind a bookcase in Anne’s father’s office. Another family and a dentist hid with them, so eight people had to share a very small space. They whispered during the day, wore socks to make less noise, and used the toilet carefully. Brave helpers risked their lives to bring food and books. Anne wrote to her diary, Kitty, and stayed hopeful by watching the sky and tree outside the attic window. After the war, Anne’s diary was published. Her words still encourage people to choose goodness and help others.

Anne Frank’s life changed when the Nazis began persecuting Jewish people. Her family escaped Germany and settled in Amsterdam, but the Nazis later occupied the Netherlands. Anne had to wear a yellow star, and Jewish children were separated from other students. When danger came to Anne’s sister, the family hid in the Secret Annex. They lived there for two years and one month with the Van Pels family and Fritz Pfeffer. They studied, listened to the radio, decorated the rooms, and tried to make life feel normal. Non-Jewish helpers secretly brought food, books, and other supplies. Anne wrote about her fears, dreams, and belief that people were good at heart. The people in the annex were eventually discovered, and Anne died in a concentration camp. Her diary survived and became one of the world’s most read books. Anne’s story teaches people to help others and never stay silent when something is unfair.

video_title: 👻🎃 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Spooky Collection

summaries.summary: On All Hallows’ Eve, Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket hear a story about the Witch of Wal Dunkle Way. People say she lives in a dark cave and comes to town to find an animal friend. When Pinocchio and Jiminy return home, Geppetto and Figaro are missing. Pinocchio worries that the witch took Figaro, but Jiminy says the witch is only a story. Then Jiminy wonders if Pinocchio is right, so they go to the witch’s cave. On the twisted trail, a deer and an owl frighten them. At the cave, many bats fly at them, but they do not see the witch or Figaro. When they return home, they find Geppetto and Figaro beside the cottage. Figaro is safe. Pinocchio says he thought the witch had taken him, and Jiminy reminds him that the witch is just a story. Everyone goes inside because the night is spooky.

Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket go shopping on All Hallows’ Eve. In town, Pinocchio hears about a witch who lives in a dark cave and searches for a new animal friend. When the friends get home, Geppetto and Figaro are gone. Pinocchio thinks the witch may have taken Figaro. Jiminy first says that the witch is only part of a story, but then he becomes worried too. They follow a twisted trail toward the cave. A deer leaps out, an owl flies above them, and many bats fly from the cave. Pinocchio asks where the witch and Figaro are, but they find nothing. The friends go back home. There they see Geppetto beside the cottage, with Figaro next to him. Figaro is safe, so Pinocchio and Jiminy are relieved. They explain that they thought the witch had taken Figaro, and then everyone hurries inside.

A spooky story makes Pinocchio wonder if the Witch of Wal Dunkle Way has taken Figaro. The story says the witch lives in a dark cave and looks for an animal friend on All Hallows’ Eve. Pinocchio and Jiminy go to the cave to look for her. The trail is frightening. A deer jumps in front of them, an owl flies over them, and bats rush out of the cave. Jiminy is scared, but the friends keep looking. They cannot find the witch or Figaro, so they return home. At the cottage, Geppetto is waiting, and Figaro is right beside him. Pinocchio and Jiminy cry that Figaro is safe. Pinocchio says he thought the witch had taken him. Jiminy says he had already explained that the witch was only a story. Because the night is still spooky, everyone hurries inside.

video_title: 👻🎃 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Spooky Collection

summaries.summary: Wendy, John, and Michael are practicing flying when Wendy gets scared. She explains that All Hallows’ Eve is a holiday with ghosts and spooky things. Peter Pan learns that people hollow out turnips, give them faces, play tricks, and tell spooky stories. Peter decides to trick Captain Hook with the ghost of Old Sea Dog. He puts on an old white sheet and a pirate hat, while Tinker Bell sprinkles Pixie Dust on the children. They fly to Captain Hook’s ship. Hook says he hates All Hallows’ Eve. Peter taps him, then pretends to be Old Sea Dog. Hook becomes scared and runs away, while Wendy and her brothers laugh. On the way home, they see a spooky glow in the woods. Peter floats out of the shadows and scares Wendy with a floating turnip. Wendy says Peter really scared her, and Peter says that was the idea.

Wendy, John, and Michael are learning to fly when Wendy becomes frightened. She tells Peter Pan about All Hallows’ Eve, a holiday filled with ghosts, spooky things, tricks, and stories. Peter wants to play a trick on Captain Hook. He uses an old white sheet and a pirate hat to look like Old Sea Dog, a ghost from a pirate story. Tinker Bell gives the children Pixie Dust, and they fly over to Hook’s ship. Hook does not like All Hallows’ Eve. Something taps him, and he jumps. Peter softly says that he is Old Sea Dog, then flies straight at Hook. The captain runs away, and Wendy, John, and Michael laugh. Wendy says it is time to go home. Then they see a spooky glow in the woods. Peter floats out of the shadows with a floating turnip and scares Wendy again. He tells her that scaring her was the idea.

On All Hallows’ Eve, Wendy tells Peter Pan about ghosts, turnips with faces, tricks, and spooky stories. Peter thinks of a trick for Captain Hook. He puts on a sheet and pirate hat and pretends to be Old Sea Dog, a ghost pirates fear. Tinker Bell sprinkles Wendy, John, and Michael with Pixie Dust, so they can fly to Hook’s ship. Hook is already saying that he hates the holiday when something taps his shoulder. Peter says, “It is I, the old sea dog,” and flies at him. The frightened captain runs away. Wendy and her brothers laugh, then decide to go home. In the woods, they see a glowing object. It is a floating turnip. Peter comes out of the shadows and scares Wendy. She tells him he really frightened her. Peter says that was exactly what he wanted to do.

video_title: 👻🎃 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Spooky Collection

summaries.summary: Mickey puts up spooky decorations and gets yummy snacks ready for a Halloween party. He hears something outside, but he decides he is being silly. In the dark attic, thunder and lightning begin. Mickey sees something move, but it is only a coat rack covered with a sheet. Then a plastic skeleton pops out of his trunk. Mickey carries the decorations downstairs and gets dressed in his pirate costume. Outside, Pluto runs under a clothesline, and a sheet covers him. Rain makes the sheet stick to Pluto, so he cannot see. Donald, Goofy, Minnie, and Daisy arrive at Mickey’s house, but no one answers. The lights go out, and strange noises come from upstairs. Mickey’s friends think a ghost or monster is coming. The lights return, and Mickey appears. They learn the noises were caused by Mickey. Then Pluto runs in like a ghost, and Mickey says Halloween is good for a scare, but friends are good for a laugh.

Mickey is preparing a Halloween party when the house begins to seem spooky. He goes into the dark attic to find his old pirate costume. During a storm, he thinks a coat rack is something moving. When he opens his old trunk, a plastic skeleton pops out, but Mickey knows it is only a decoration. Outside, Pluto gets covered by a sheet, and rain makes it stick to him. Mickey’s friends arrive at the house. The lights go out, and they hear strange sounds upstairs. They see something run past a window, hear footsteps, and hear rattling bones. They think a horrible monster is coming. Suddenly, the lights come back on, and Mickey says hello. Minnie and Donald explain that they thought he was a monster. Then Pluto runs through the doggy door covered by the sheet. Minnie thinks the ghost has returned, but it is only Pluto. Mickey says Halloween is good for a scare and friends are good for a laugh.

Mickey plans a Halloween party with decorations and snacks. He searches the attic for his pirate costume while thunder and lightning fill the night. A covered coat rack and a plastic skeleton give him little surprises. Pluto has a surprise too: a sheet falls over him, and rain makes it cling to his body. When Donald, Goofy, Minnie, and Daisy arrive, the house is dark and quiet. Then the lights go out. Strange noises, a moving shape, footsteps, and rattling bones make Mickey’s friends believe a ghost or monster is nearby. The lights suddenly come back on, and Mickey is standing there. He explains that the scary noises came from him while he was dealing with spider webs upstairs. His friends say he frightened them. Then Pluto runs in wearing the wet sheet, making Minnie think the ghost is back. Mickey ends by saying that Halloween scares are fun, and friends bring laughter.

video_title: 🚛🚚🚒 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Pixar Cars : Mater's Junkyard Jamboree

summaries.summary: Mater the tow truck builds a jukebox in his junkyard. He wants to show it to his friends, but everyone is busy because little tractors are causing trouble in Radiator Springs. The tractors knock over Luigi’s tires and ruin Red’s flowers. Mater tries to tell Lightning McQueen, Luigi, and Sheriff about his jukebox, but they are all too busy catching the tractors. Then Mater plays his jukebox and sings. One little tractor follows him, and soon many tractors follow the music. Mater discovers that the tractors like listening to his jukebox. He takes the jukebox back to his junkyard, and the tractors dance inside. His friends see what happened and cheer for Mater. The music keeps the tractors from causing trouble. Everyone enjoys the jukebox, and the little tractors come back whenever Mater plays it.

Mater has been making a junkyard jukebox all week. It is almost finished, but one favorite tire is missing. Mater decides to add it later and takes the jukebox to show his friends. Ramone is busy catching little tractors. Lightning McQueen is also rounding them up, and Luigi does not have time to listen. The tractors have knocked over Luigi’s tires and ruined Red’s flowers. Sheriff is busy too, because the tractors are everywhere. Radiator Springs is messy. Mater returns to his junkyard and turns on the jukebox. He sings with the music. A little tractor follows him, and then more tractors follow. Mater learns that the tractors want to hear the music. He takes the jukebox inside, and the tractors dance. His friends cheer because Mater helped stop the trouble. After that, the tractors return whenever Mater plays his jukebox.

Mater wants to share his new junkyard jukebox with Ramone, Lightning McQueen, and Luigi. But his friends are busy because little tractors are running around town. Luigi’s pile of tires falls over, Red’s flowers are ruined, and Sheriff must chase the tractors. Mater sees that Radiator Springs is a mess. He says he needs to put away his jukebox so he can help. While Mater goes back to his junkyard, he starts the jukebox and sings. A shy tractor follows the music. Soon, many little tractors follow too. Mater understands that they like his music. He turns the jukebox louder and brings it into the junkyard. The tractors dance inside. Mater’s friends see the tractors gathered there and cheer for him. The tractors are no longer getting into trouble, so everyone can enjoy the music. Mater smiles because his jukebox saved the day, and the little tractors come back for more music.

video_title: Little Quack Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Mama Duck has five little ducklings named Whittle, Waddle, Paddle, Puddle, and Little Quack. They live together in a soft nest. One day, Mama says it is time to leave the nest and paddle on the water. The ducklings are scared. Whittle jumps into the pond first. Then Waddle joins her. Paddle becomes brave and wiggles into the water. Puddle leaps in too. Little Quack is the last duckling in the nest. He looks at the water, sniffs it, and touches it with his foot. Mama, Whittle, Waddle, Paddle, and Puddle tell him, “You can do it.” Little Quack closes his eyes and jumps into the pond. He says, “I did it!” Mama says she always knew he could. Then all five ducklings paddle together in the pond. Little Quack is brave, and the five ducklings are proud.

summaries.summary: Judy Hopes and Nick Wild chase a stolen catering van through Zootopia, causing a lot of damage. Their boss sends them to a class because Judy cares too much and Nick does not care enough. At a big anniversary gala, Judy notices vans like the stolen one. She discovers Gary D. Snake taking Milton and an important journal. Gary says the journal can prove that snakes were not bad. Judy and Nick help Gary escape, so the police think they are working with him. With help from Nibbles, they follow Gary and learn that Ebenezer Lynxley stole Angus D. Snake’s plans for Zootopia. Pubert tries to destroy the proof, but Gary saves Judy, and Nick helps stop Pubert. Judy, Nick, Nibbles, and Gary find Angus’s home and discover proof that she truly created Zootopia. Angus finally receives credit, and the case is closed. Judy and Nick learn that working together makes them great partners.

Judy and Nick are police partners, but they are very different. Judy worries a lot, while Nick does not worry enough. After a wild chase, they are sent to a partners-in-crisis class. Judy later sees a stolen catering van at a city gala and follows her hunch. Gary D. Snake is there with an old journal. He says the journal will show that snakes were not bad. Judy chooses to keep the journal and help Gary, even when this makes the police chase her and Nick. Nibbles helps them search for Gary. They learn that Gary’s great-grandmother, Angus, made the first plans for Zootopia, but Ebenezer Lynxley stole them. Pubert wants to destroy the proof. In the cold weather wall, Gary saves Judy with antivenom, and Judy and Gary rescue Nick. The friends reach Reptile Raven and find Angus’s home. The journal and other evidence show that Angus was the true founder of Zootopia.

A stolen van chase begins a big adventure for Judy Hopes and Nick Wild. Their chase damages the city, and they must learn to work better together. At Zootopia’s anniversary gala, Judy sees the stolen vans again. Gary D. Snake takes Milton and a journal that holds secrets about the city’s past. Judy and Nick help Gary run away, but the police think they are criminals. Their friend Fufu gives them Nibbles Maple Stick’s card. Nibbles helps them follow clues through Marsh Market and toward a cold place. Gary shows that the journal’s cover has a hidden map. The map leads to Reptile Raven, where Angus D. Snake once lived. Pubert lies and poisons Judy because he wants to destroy the truth. Gary uses his antivenom to save her, while Nick escapes the police and helps stop Pubert. The group finds Angus’s home and proof that she created Zootopia. Angus finally gets credit, and Judy and Nick solve the case together.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑊ℎ𝑒𝑛 𝑌𝑜𝑢 𝑅𝑒𝑎𝑐ℎ 𝑀𝑒 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Miranda’s mother has finally earned a chance to compete on The $20,000 Pyramid, so Miranda helps her practice. Miranda keeps the practice words on index cards and notices the date, April 27, written on the game-show postcard. She also thinks about her missing friend, who once asked her to write a letter explaining everything that happened during the fall and winter. Miranda describes her life in New York City, her mother’s boyfriend Richard, the apartment’s problems, and her friendship with Sal. She remembers how she and Sal met as babies and how they used to walk home together past the frightening Laughing Man. One October day, a boy in a green army coat suddenly punches Sal and hits him in the face. The other boys are strangely silent. Sal cries, bleeds, and runs home after the Laughing Man approaches them. At their building, Sal shuts Miranda out. Miranda realizes that this attack began the story she was asked to tell and ended her friendship with Sal.

Miranda begins thinking about the story behind several mysterious notes. Her mother is preparing for a television contest called The $20,000 Pyramid, and Miranda helps by making word cards for practice. The contest date is April 27, which is also Richard’s birthday. Miranda explains that she lives with her mother, who works in a small law office, and Richard, a lawyer who loves sailing and teaching her knots. She also recalls waiting at Belle’s Market, where she tells Belle about her favorite book, and she explains why her mother named her Miranda. Miranda and her mother hide a spare apartment key in an old fire hose. While tying knots, Miranda wonders where her story should begin. She finally chooses the day Sal was punched. As they walk home, a boy in a green army coat attacks Sal without explanation. Sal becomes frightened and hurt, then runs home and refuses to let Miranda into his apartment. Miranda sees this as the beginning of the mystery and the end of their friendship.

Miranda’s mother is excited because she will appear on The $20,000 Pyramid after trying for three years. Miranda helps her prepare while keeping a box of notes connected to someone who is no longer there. She describes the people and places around her: Richard, her mother’s boyfriend; Louisa, Sal’s mother; Belle’s grocery store; and the Laughing Man, a troubled man who stays near their corner. Miranda remembers that she and Sal were once inseparable and always walked home together. She also remembers the day their friendship changed. A boy wearing a green army coat leaves a group near a garage, blocks Miranda and Sal, and punches Sal in the stomach. He then strikes Sal’s face and walks away as if nothing happened. Sal cries, bleeds from the nose, and becomes sick with fear. The Laughing Man’s approach frightens him even more, so Sal runs home. After Miranda follows him to the building, Sal closes his apartment door and will not let her in. Miranda decides this is the beginning of the story she must tell.

video_title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears-by: Jan Brett. #storytime #readingaloud ​@Children-12j #reels

summaries.summary: Three bears lived together in a little house in the woods. They had three bowls of porridge, three chairs, and three beds. One day, while the bears walked in the woods, Goldilocks went into their house. She tasted the porridge and ate the little bear’s because it was just right. She sat in the little bear’s chair, but it broke. Then she tried the beds and fell asleep in the little bear’s bed. The bears came home and saw that someone had used their things. The little bear found Goldilocks sleeping in his bed. His sharp voice woke her. Goldilocks jumped from the bed, ran out the window, and hurried away. The bears never saw her again.

A great huge bear, a middlesized bear, and a little small wee bear lived in a house in the woods. One morning, they made porridge and went outside while it cooled. Goldilocks came into the empty house. She tried all three bowls. The great huge bear’s porridge was too hot, the middlesized bear’s was too cold, and the little bear’s was just right. She ate it all. She tried the chairs, too, and the little bear’s chair broke. Upstairs, she found the little bear’s bed just right and fell asleep. When the bears returned, they noticed their porridge, chairs, and beds had been used. They found Goldilocks in the little bear’s bed. His voice woke her, and she ran away. The three bears never saw her again.

In a house in the wood lived three bears: one great huge bear, one middlesized bear, and one little small wee bear. They each had a bowl, a chair, and a bed. While the bears were away, Goldilocks entered their house. She tasted the three porridges and liked the little bear’s best, so she ate it all up. Then she sat in the three chairs. The little bear’s chair felt just right, but it broke beneath her. Goldilocks went upstairs and slept in the little bear’s bed. The bears came home and discovered that someone had eaten the little bear’s breakfast, sat in their chairs, and slept in their beds. They found Goldilocks asleep. When the little bear cried out, Goldilocks woke up. She saw the bears, jumped out of the bed, and ran away through the window. The bears never saw her again.

video_title: Clap Your Hands - Read Aloud Flip-Along Picture Book | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: First, clap your hands and stomp your feet. Shake your arms, then sit down. Rub your tummy and pat your head. Find something yellow and something red. Reach for the sky and wiggle your toes. Stick out your tongue and touch your nose. Next, roar like a lion and growl like a bear. Give a kiss, wiggle your fingers, and slap your knee. Tickle each other. Find something big and something small. Spin around, close your eyes, count to four, and do a somersault. Then spread your feet, look upside down, and make a silly clown face. Hop like a bunny, flap like a bird, and be quiet like a mouse. Say your name, tell your age, and share a secret. Purr, bark, crawl, jump, count fingers and toes, and wiggle your eyebrows and nose. Smile, frown, balance, jump, fly, and wave goodbye.

A lively game begins with many movements. Clap hands, stomp feet, shake arms, and sit down. Rub a tummy and pat a head. Look for something yellow and something red. Reach high, wiggle toes, stick out a tongue, and touch a nose. Make a lion roar and a bear growl. Give a kiss, wiggle fingers, and slap a knee. There is a tickle game, too. Find something big and something small, spin in a circle, and try not to fall. Close your eyes, count to four, and roll in a somersault. Make a silly face like a clown. Hop like a bunny, flap like a bird, and stay quiet like a mouse. Tell a name, an age, and a secret. Then purr, bark, crawl, jump, count fingers and toes, wiggle, smile, frown, balance, jump, fly like an airplane, and wave bye-bye.

The song asks for one action after another. Start by clapping, stomping, shaking, and sitting. Rub your tummy and pat your head. Find yellow and red things. Reach for the sky, wiggle your toes, stick out your tongue, and touch your nose. Roar like a lion, growl like a bear, and give a kiss. Wiggle your fingers and slap your knee, with a tickle if the other person tickles. Find big and small things. Spin, close your eyes, count to four, and do a somersault. Spread your feet, look upside down, and act like a clown. Hop like a bunny, flap like a bird, and say nothing like a mouse. Tell your name, age, and secret. Purr, bark, crawl, jump like a frog, count fingers and toes, wiggle eyebrows and nose, smile, frown, stand on one foot, jump, fly high, and wave goodbye.

video_title: Pig the Pug Read Aloud 🐶 | Funny & Mischievous Storytime for Kids [English] 2025

summaries.summary: Pig was a pug who lived with a wiener dog named Trevor. Pig had many toys, but he was greedy and selfish. When Trevor asked to play, Pig said the toys were his and told Trevor to go away. Pig gathered all the toys into one big pile. Then he climbed to the top and shouted that Trevor could not have them. Trevor saw that the pile was wobbling and warned Pig to watch out. But pugs cannot fly. Later, things became different. Pig began sharing his toys, and Trevor became his friend. Now they play together. The story shows Pig changing from keeping everything for himself to sharing and playing with Trevor.

A pug named Pig lived in a house with Trevor, a wiener dog. Trevor noticed Pig’s wonderful toys and asked if they could play together. Pig did not want to share. He grumbled, told Trevor to go away, and said the toys were his again and again. Pig made a tall pile with all his things. He climbed on top and felt happy because Trevor could not get the toys. Then Trevor saw the pile wobble. He called out a warning, but Pig was a pug, and pugs cannot fly. The story later says that Pig changed. He shares his toys now, and Trevor is his friend. They play together. Pig and Trevor are no longer kept apart by Pig’s selfishness.

Pig the pug was not nice to Trevor, the wiener dog who lived with him. Pig owned many toys, but he would not let Trevor touch them. Trevor suggested that playing together might be more fun. Pig became upset and said, “They’re mine,” and “Only mine.” He gathered his toys into a big pile and climbed to the top. Pig shouted that Trevor would not get his things. Just then, Trevor noticed that the pile was wobbling. He warned Pig to watch out. The story says that pugs cannot fly. After this, Pig’s life became different. Pig now shares his toys. Trevor is his friend, and they play together. The ending shows that Pig no longer keeps all his toys only for himself.

video_title: Cinderella (With Highlighted Words) Read Along: Cd Audio

summaries.summary: Cinderella lives with her cruel stepmother and two selfish stepsisters. She dreams of going to the palace ball, but her family makes her work and tears her dress. Cinderella feels sad, but her Fairy Godmother comes to help. Magic turns a pumpkin into a coach, mice into horses, and Cinderella’s rags into a beautiful gown with glass slippers. At the ball, Prince Charming dances with Cinderella and thinks she is the girl of his dreams. When midnight comes, Cinderella runs away and loses one glass slipper. The prince searches the kingdom for the girl whose foot fits it. Cinderella is locked away, but her mouse friends help free her. The slipper fits Cinderella perfectly. She marries the prince, and she learns that if she keeps believing, her dreams can come true.

Cinderella wants to attend the royal ball for the prince, but her stepmother says she may go only after finishing her work and finding a dress. Cinderella’s mice and birds make her a lovely gown. Her stepsisters become jealous and rip the dress apart. Then Cinderella’s Fairy Godmother appears. With magic, she makes a coach, horses, a shining dress, and glass slippers. Cinderella dances with the prince until the clock begins to strike twelve. She hurries home and leaves one slipper behind. The prince asks every maiden to try on the slipper. Cinderella’s stepmother locks her in the attic, but her mouse friends bring her the key. The slipper is broken, yet Cinderella has the matching one. It fits her foot perfectly. Wedding bells ring, and Cinderella and the prince ride away happily.

A royal ball is announced, and Cinderella hopes she can go. Her stepmother keeps her busy, while Anastasia and Drizella laugh at her. Cinderella’s animal friends help sew a dress, but the stepsisters tear it to pieces. Cinderella cries in the garden until her Fairy Godmother arrives. The Fairy Godmother uses her wand to make a coach from a pumpkin and horses from mice. She also gives Cinderella a sparkling gown and glass slippers, but the magic will end at midnight. Cinderella dances with Prince Charming, then races away when the clock chimes. She loses a slipper. The prince searches for its owner. Cinderella’s stepmother hides her in the attic, but the mice rescue her. The glass slipper breaks, and Cinderella shows the other one. It fits, so she marries the prince and lives happily ever after.

video_title: Max the Brave By Ed Vere

summaries.summary: Max is a sweet kitten who sometimes wears bows, but he does not like them. Max wants to be brave because he chases mice. First, he needs to learn what a mouse looks like. He looks around and asks a fly, a fish, and some birds if they are Mouse. Each one says no, but each has seen Mouse nearby. Max then asks an elephant, who also points him along. At last, Max asks a monster. The monster says Mouse is sleeping close by. Max sees the monster’s big head and thinks it must be Mouse. He asks Mouse to wake up and proudly says he will chase and eat him. Then Max notices the very big teeth. He feels worried and decides that chasing mice is not as wonderful as he thought. Max learns he does not need to be brave all the time, except when he is chasing monsters.

Max is a fearless kitten, and he wants to chase mice. But Max does not know what a mouse looks like, so he begins searching. He looks in a can and asks a fly, “Are you Mouse?” The fly says no and tells Max that a mouse went by. Max asks a fish, some birds, and an elephant the same question. They all say they are not Mouse, but they each help Max follow the mouse’s path. Then Max meets a monster. The monster says Mouse is sleeping nearby and that Max might catch him if he is quick. Max sees the huge sleeping monster and thinks it is Mouse. He bounces on the monster’s head and says he will chase and eat him. When Max sees the monster’s enormous teeth, he changes his mind. Chasing mice is not all it is cracked up to be.

Max looks sweet, and people sometimes dress him in bows. Max would rather be a brave kitten who chases mice. One day, he sets out to find a mouse. He asks many creatures for help. A fly, a fish, birds, and an elephant all say, “I am not Mouse,” but they tell Max where Mouse went. Finally, a monster says that Mouse is sleeping over there. Max hurries to the sleeping creature. The monster is so large that Max thinks it must be Mouse. Max wakes him by jumping on his head. He announces that he is Max the Brave and that he chases mice. He even says he might eat Mouse. Then Max sees the monster’s very large teeth and says, “Yuck!” Max decides that chasing mice is not so good after all. He does not need to be Max the Brave every moment, unless he is outside chasing monsters.

video_title: We Will Rock Our Classmates Read Aloud 🎸 | Penelope Rex's Talent Show Adventure

summaries.summary: Penelope was the only T-Rex at her school, so sometimes her classmates saw only a dinosaur. She loved playing, reading, drawing, singing, and playing guitar. When her teacher announced a talent show, Penelope bravely signed up to rock and roll. She planned a colorful outfit, but during rehearsal she froze and could not sing or play. She began to think dinosaurs could not rock. Penelope stopped playing with friends and crossed her name off the list. Her father showed her family pictures and reminded her that being a T-Rex was only one part of who she was. Penelope was also kind, caring, creative, and adventurous. At school, her classmates asked to join her band. On show night, Penelope and the Mustard Seeds performed. They came in second place, and Penelope was happy. She learned that being yourself takes courage.

Penelope Rex loved music more than anything. She sang, played guitar, and dreamed of rocking her classmates at the school talent show. Although she was excited, she felt nervous when she signed up. At rehearsal, Penelope froze on stage. She could not sing or play guitar, and she worried that a dinosaur could not be a rock star. The next day, she sat alone, refused to play games, and removed her name from the talent-show list. Daddy Rex helped her by showing pictures of family members who had done different things. He told Penelope that being a T-Rex was only part of her. She was also kind, caring, creative, and adventurous. Penelope returned to the signup sheet. Her classmates joined her band, giving her courage. At the show, Penelope and the Mustard Seeds performed and came in second place. She was proud and happy.

Penelope was different from her classmates because she was the only T-Rex in school. Sometimes children treated her only as a dinosaur, but Penelope enjoyed playing, reading, drawing, and making music. When the school talent show was announced, she signed up to perform rock and roll. Penelope felt brave at first, but she became frightened during rehearsal and froze. She stopped joining games and decided to leave the show. Her father helped her understand that she was much more than a T-Rex. She was kind, caring, creative, and adventurous, and she could choose what she wanted to be. Then Penelope’s classmates asked to play in her band. With their help, she went on stage with the Mustard Seeds. Other children performed first, and then Penelope’s band played. video_title: 👧🏻 The Girl with a Mind for Math: The Story of Raye Montague

summaries.summary: Rey Montagu grew up in Arkansas and became interested in engineering when her grandfather took her to see a submarine. She wanted to design ships, but people laughed because she was a Black girl. Her mother told her to stay strong and use her brains. Schools were segregated, and Black students received fewer opportunities, but Rey studied hard and learned mathematics. When an engineering school would not admit Black students, she studied business instead. Later, she moved to Washington, D.C., and worked as a Navy clerk typist. Rey watched engineers, studied computers, and learned their work. When the staff became sick, she completed everyone’s work from memory and was promoted. When the Navy urgently needed ship plans, Rey created a computer system that finished the calculations in eighteen hours. Although she faced unfair treatment, she became the Navy’s first woman to lead ship design and achieved her dream.

As a child, Rey Montagu was bright, determined, and curious. Seeing a submarine made her dream of becoming an engineer. Her mother encouraged her even though people often said girls and Black students could not succeed in engineering. Rey attended segregated schools, worked hard, and taught herself mathematics. An engineering program refused to accept Black students, so she earned a business degree and continued learning. She found a job with the Navy, where she typed documents for people who designed submarines. Rey studied their work and learned computers at night. During an illness, she completed the engineers’ work and impressed her boss by remembering the needed information. Later, the Navy needed ship plans quickly. Rey designed a computer program and completed the plans in eighteen hours and twenty-six minutes. Even after being excluded from the ship’s launch, she kept working. Her skills were recognized, and she became the first woman to lead ship design for the Navy.

Rey Montagu dreamed of designing ships after visiting a submarine when she was seven. She faced racism and unfair rules throughout her education and career. People laughed at her dream, and an engineering school would not accept Black students. Rey did not give up. She studied business, learned mathematics, watched engineers at work, and studied computers at night. At the Navy, she began as a clerk typist, but she learned how ship design worked. When the engineers became ill, she finished their tasks from memory and earned a promotion. Later, the president ordered a ship to be designed quickly. Rey explained that her computer system could complete the calculations much faster. She worked with determination and finished the first computer-designed ship in just over eighteen hours. Some people still treated her unfairly and expected a man when they heard about her work. Rey answered difficult moments with skill and humor. In time, she became the Navy’s first woman to lead ship design and received important honors.

video_title: Baby Farm Animals@Readingtimewithnana

On the farm, many baby animals have special names. A baby sheep is a lamb, and it runs in the grass. Baby cats are kittens, and they play and sleep in the barn. Chicks cannot swim, so they look for worms with their mother. Piglets dig with their snouts and sleep on straw. Puppies bark near the horses. Goat kids play by bumping heads. Swan babies will grow white feathers, and a young goose will become a big gray goose. A foal grows from walking to galloping. A small pony carries friends. The baby cow says “Moo” when lunch is ready.

The farm is full of baby animals. The lamb runs in the meadow, and the kittens play together in the barn at night. The rabbit lives in a tiny hutch and is friends with kittens and puppies. A guinea pig notices the rabbit’s mischief. A tired donkey sees a carrot on a stick and knows someone is trying to make him move. Ducklings invite chicks to swim, but the chicks stay out of the water and search for worms. Piglets sleep in clean straw and cry for their mother when they are chased. Puppies bark at strangers and play pretend with a shoe. Goat kids bump heads. Young swans grow feathers, and a goose searches under the water for food. A foal grows into a horse, and a pony gives rides. Then the calf says it is lunchtime.

video_title: Appa Reads: Kindness Makes Us Strong by Sophie Beer

Kindness begins with saying hello and being patient. It continues with helping, cheering, trading treats, giving a boost, taking turns, and sharing. Kindness also means offering comfort, visiting, and reaching out. These kind actions make us strong.

video_title: Bearsentain bears God Bless our country kids book read along

summaries.summary: It was early summer in Bear Country, and Brother, Sister, and Honeybear were preparing for the Fourth of July parade. Brother, Sister, and Honeybear were excited for the Bear Country Fourth of July parade. They decorated their bicycles with red, white, and blue ribbons and streamers. Papa prepared to march in his old army uniform, and Mama made flags for the parade route. While eating milk and honeybread, the cubs asked why the Fourth of July was special. A war followed because the faraway king wanted his country back, but the settlers won. On parade day, the cubs rode with other children, and Papa marched with army bears. Brother, Sister, and Honey won second prize for their bikes. When fireworks began, Papa said, “God bless our country,” and everyone answered, “Amen.”

The Bear family got ready for a big Fourth of July celebration. The cubs decorated their bikes, and Mama and Papa prepared flags, bunting, and Papa’s army uniform. The children wondered whose birthday the holiday celebrated. Their parents explained that the country was born when settlers decided to live freely instead of being ruled by a king far away. The settlers wrote their decision, a war began, and they won. The family also talked about God’s will and a land where people from many places could be free. During the parade, red, white, and blue bikes led the way. Army bears, marching bands, fire engines, antique cars, tractors, wagons, historical floats, scouts, and cheerleaders followed. Fertie Facel won first prize with his high-wheeler and Abraham Lincoln costume. Brother, Sister, and Honey won second prize. As fireworks burst overhead, the family said, “God bless our country,” and “Amen.”

video_title: Appa Reads: The Cool Bean by Jory John illustrated by Pete Oswald

summaries.summary: The narrator is a bean who used to be part of a big group. Then some beans became famous at school for being cool because they could play guitar, draw superheroes, or jump high. The narrator tried sunglasses, slick hair, and swaggering, but still felt awkward and was picked last. He decided he was an ordinary bean and stopped trying. One day in the cafeteria, he dropped his lunch, and a cool bean helped clean it up. Later, another cool bean helped him after he fell on the playground. In class, a cool bean quietly told him which page to read when everyone laughed. These small acts made him feel confident again. Soon, he began spending time with the cool beans. A bean watches his old friends become the cool beans at school. One can play guitar, one can draw wonderful superheroes, and one can jump very high. The narrator tries to look cool too, but his sunglasses are too big, his hair is too slick, and he is still picked last. He feels like he has no special skills, so he keeps to himself. Then several cool beans show him kindness. One helps clean lunch from his loafers. Another dusts him off after he scrapes his knee. When the narrator is embarrassed in class, a cool bean whispers that the teacher asked him to read from page 32. The kindness gives him confidence and makes his day much better. Afterward, he starts spending time with the cool beans again. He discovers that true coolness means helping people, smiling, and being there when someone needs a hand.

Once, all the beans were one big group, but later the narrator’s friends became the cool beans and stopped spending as much time with him. The narrator felt ordinary and believed there were cool beans and beans like him. He went through school quietly until a difficult day changed everything. He dropped his lunch, scraped his knee, and felt embarrassed when he did not answer the teacher. Each time, a cool bean helped him. One cleaned his lunch, one dusted him off, and one whispered the correct page for reading. The narrator went home smiling because their kindness gave him confidence. He began hanging out with the cool beans again at lunch, after school, and on weekends. He realized that coolness is not about appearance or silly things. It is about a wink, a nod, a smile, helping someone up, dusting them off, and pointing them in the right direction.

video_title: A Baby Monster Surprise | Story Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Baby Monster is in a cave with Rabbit, Beaver, Squirrel, and Boore. The animals try to help her sleep. They read a story, sing a song, and count sheep.
