The animals of Little Nook babysit Baby Monster. Rabbit tries to make her sleepy with a story, a song, and sheep counting. Baby Monster does not sleep. She has fun making a big mess. She plays with toys, makes a den, throws food, drops books, rides on Boore, eats cake, and swings on Squirrel’s tail. Then she curls up in a blanket and sleeps. The tired animals sleep beside her. Later, Baby Monster wakes up and goes outside. She takes cake and leaves crumbs behind. Rabbit, Boore, Beaver, and Squirrel follow the crumbs. They see a sticky berry mess, broken sticks, crunchy acorn shells, and muddy footprints in their homes. Baby Monster is always just ahead. The trail goes through the forest and ends in sunshine. Baby Monster is asleep in her bed. Monster returns, and the babysitters pretend everything is fine, even though their homes need cleaning.

In Little Nook, four animals care for a baby monster while Monster is away. They want Baby Monster to nap, but she wants to play. She climbs, hides, throws things, eats cake, and swings on Squirrel’s tail. After many games, she sleeps in a cozy blanket nest. The babysitters are very tired, so they fall asleep too. Baby Monster wakes up and escapes outside with a piece of cake. When Rabbit wakes, the animals follow the crumbs. They look in Boore’s place, Beaver’s dam, Squirrel’s tree, and Rabbit’s log. At each place, they find a different mess, but Baby Monster is gone. The trail keeps going through the twisting forest. Finally, the animals reach a sunny place and find Baby Monster fast asleep in her bed. Monster comes home and says thank you. The four babysitters are relieved, but they remember that all their homes are still messy.

video_title: 🌱 We Are Growing! | Elephant & Piggie Like Reading!

summaries.summary: Piggy finds a new book called “We Are Growing.” The book says that a new friend is growing, and the friend is surprised. The other characters notice that everyone is growing in different ways. One is tall, one is curly, one is silly, one is pointy, and one is crunchy. A dandelion says he is the dandiest, and a weed says he has been called worse. Walt does not know what he is because he is not the tallest, curliest, silliest, pointiest, crunchiest, or dandiest. The others try to help him think. Then something makes a mess, and the characters are no longer what they were. They say not to worry because they will grow again. Before growing, they clean the place. Walt realizes that he is neat. The others agree that he is the neatest. Then they decide they are all the stumplingest. They enjoy the funny book and say that makes them readers.

A group of growing characters reads a funny book. First, they discover that their new friend has grown. They celebrate because everyone is growing. Each character has a special description. One is the tallest, another is the curliest, another is the silliest, and others are pointy or crunchy. A dandelion says he is the dandiest. But Walt feels confused because he is not any of those things. The others ask him to think about what he is. While they are thinking, there is a big mess. The characters lose their earlier descriptions, so they feel worried. The group tells Walt that they will grow again. Before they grow, they clean up the mess. Then Walt discovers something special about himself: he is neat. The others agree that he is the neatest. They also say they are the stumplingest. Everyone likes reading the funny book, and they learn that reading makes them readers.

The story begins with characters looking at a new book about growing. A new friend says he has grown, and the others agree. They name many ways they are growing: tall, curly, silly, pointy, crunchy, and dandy. A dandelion explains that he is a dandelion, while a weed says he has been called worse. Walt asks what he is, but he cannot find a description that fits him. The others encourage him to think. Then a mess happens, and the characters are not tall, curly, or like their other descriptions anymore. They remind one another that they will grow again. First, they clean the place. After cleaning, Walt figures out that he is neat. Everyone repeats that Walt is the neatest. Then they call themselves the stumplingest. The characters enjoy the book because it is funny. When they ask what loving to read makes them, they answer that they are readers.

video_title: Inside Out Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Inside Out - Welcome to Headquarters

summaries.summary: Riley is an 11-year-old girl with a loving family and great friends. Inside her mind, Joy works hard to help Riley stay happy. Riley also has Anger, Fear, Disgust, and Sadness. Her memories are kept in colored spheres, and happy memories are yellow. Riley’s personality is shaped by five islands: Family Island, Honesty Island, Hockey Island, Friendship Island, and Goofball Island. Her mind also has a Train of Thought, Forgetters, Imagination Land, Dream Productions, and a subconscious. Bing Bong, Riley’s old imaginary friend, still loves her even though Riley has forgotten him. At Dream Productions, workers create dreams for Riley, while guards protect her biggest fears. All of Riley’s emotions work together each day, helping her life grow from a good day into a good week, year, and life.

Inside Riley’s mind, Joy tries to keep Riley happy. Riley has a wonderful family, good friends, and many memories stored in spheres. Yellow spheres hold happy memories. Anger, Fear, Disgust, and Sadness also help Riley in different ways. Five personality islands show what makes Riley special: family, honesty, hockey, friendship, and goofball. The Train of Thought carries Riley’s daydreams, while the Forgetters remove old memories and send them to the memory dump. Riley’s imaginary friend Bing Bong lives in her memories and sometimes cries candy because Riley has forgotten him. Riley’s dreams are made at Dream Productions, where Rainbow Unicorn stars in happy dreams. Her fears are locked in the subconscious, watched by two guards. Together, Riley’s emotions help her through every day and help make a good life.

Riley is an 11-year-old girl whose mind is filled with busy places and helpful emotions. Joy wants Riley to be happy, while Anger looks for fairness, Fear keeps Riley safe, Disgust avoids gross things, and Sadness makes Riley sad. Riley’s memories are stored in spheres, and her happy memories are yellow. Five personality islands represent her family, honesty, hockey, friendship, and goofball side. Bing Bong was Riley’s imaginary friend when she was little, and he still loves her even though she sometimes forgets him. In Imagination Land, Riley has places such as Trophy Town, French Fry Forest, and Cloud Town. Dream Productions makes Riley’s dreams, and Rainbow Unicorn is the star of her best dreams. Her biggest fears stay locked in her subconscious. Riley’s emotions work hard each day, helping a good day become a good week, year, and life.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth: Episode 6, How to Put Your Parents to Bed

summaries.summary: A child notices that bedtime is easy for children to understand but hard for parents. The parents make excuses about laundry, dishes, and other tasks, so the child decides to take charge. First, the child helps them brush their teeth, even reaching the back molars. Next, the child guides them into pajamas while they become distracted by phones, magazines, television, the cat, and the dog. The child stays patient and keeps them moving toward the bedroom. At bedtime, the parents want their favorite stories, their usual number of stories, and several other things, such as a missing pillow, a check on the dog, and a drink of water. The child calmly handles each problem, tucks the parents in, kisses them goodnight, and reminds them not to make phone calls. The child takes their cell phones, closes the door, and listens for quiet. At last, the parents are in bed, but the child is exhausted and may need bedtime too.

The story pretends that children must put their parents to bed. The parents say they are not ready because they have laundry, dishes, and other excuses. The child tells them it is bedtime and helps them begin with tooth brushing. The parents argue that they will brush later, but the child squeezes out toothpaste and helps with the difficult back molars. Then the child gets them into pajamas. This takes a long time because the parents notice phones, magazines, television, the cat, and the dog. When they finally reach the bedroom, the parents still need many things. They want their favorite bedtime stories, their usual number of stories, a pillow, a check on the dog, and a cup of water. The child remains calm, takes care of each request, tucks them in, and says goodnight. The child takes away their cell phones so they will not make calls. The parents are finally quiet, while the tired child also needs sleep.

In this funny bedtime story, the child becomes the grown-up and the parents become the sleepy children. The child explains that parents are not very good at going to bed because they always have another excuse. The child takes charge by telling them to stop their activities, brush their teeth, and put on pajamas. The parents are easily distracted, so the child patiently keeps them walking toward the bedroom. Getting into bed is not the end. The parents become upset about small things and ask for familiar bedtime stories. They expect all the stories they usually hear, not fewer. Then they remember more needs, including a favorite pillow, checking on the dog, and a drink of water. The child handles every problem calmly, tucks the parents in, kisses them, and reminds them not to make phone calls. After taking their cell phones and closing the door, the child listens for quiet. The parents are asleep, but the child is exhausted too.

video_title: 🙈🫣 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Junior :  Mickey Mouse Clubhouse : Guess Who, Mickey!

summaries.summary: Mickey plays a guessing game with his friends. First, a sweet girl who wears polka dots cuddles kittens and has captured Mickey’s heart. She is Minnie Mouse. Next comes a feathered friend with a map, a quacky voice, a bright blue shirt, and a cap. He is Donald Duck. Then Goofy appears. He is silly, clumsy, tall, slim, and trying hard to surf, but he can swim. Daisy comes next. She wears a bow and ponytail, has a flower’s name, and is fond of Donald Duck. Donald feels the same. At the end, Mickey is described as the mouse with yellow shoes, red shorts, and bright white gloves. The guessing game asks, “Can you guess who?”

There are several friendly characters in Mickey’s guessing game. Minnie is charming, sweet, and smart. She likes to dress in polka dots, and she cuddles kittens in her arms. Donald Duck is a feathered fellow. He has a map, a quacky voice, a bright blue shirt, and a cap. Goofy is silly and clumsy. He loves to laugh, and he is tall and slim. He is trying to surf, but he can swim. Daisy wears a bow and ponytail. Her name is like a flower, and she likes Donald Duck. Donald likes her too. Finally, Mickey wears yellow shoes, red shorts, and bright white gloves. Everyone is asked to guess who he is.

The guessing clues name Mickey’s friends one by one. A girl in polka dots is charming, sweet, and smart. She cuddles kittens, and Mickey’s heart belongs to her. The answer is Minnie Mouse. A lost feathered fellow looks at his map. His voice is quacky, and he wears a bright blue shirt and cap. The answer is Donald Duck. A tall, slim friend is silly, clumsy, and loves to laugh. He is trying to surf, and he can swim. The answer is Goofy. A girl with a bow and ponytail has a flower’s name. She likes Donald, and Donald likes her. The last clues describe Mickey in yellow shoes, red shorts, and white gloves. The game ends by asking who he is.

video_title: Appa Reads: Bluey - Perfect

summaries.summary: Bluey and Bingo make Father's Day cards for Dad. Bingo draws a red heart and rainbow. Bluey wants to make a perfect picture of herself and Dad. She tries drawing Dad clapping, tickling, throwing, sitting in a chair, and throwing a boomerang. Each picture seems wrong to Bluey. Mom tells her that Dad will love anything made with care, and that she should do the best she can. Bluey feels sad because Bingo once made a picture that Mom called perfect, and it was put on top of Bluey's picture on the fridge. Mom explains that parenting and drawing can both be tough. She reminds Bluey that Dad says, “It’s a good thing you’re tough.” Bluey understands that drawing is tough, but she is tough too. She finishes her picture. On Father's Day, Dad loves both pictures and puts them straight on the fridge.

Bingo and Bluey are making cards for Father's Day. Bingo knows what she wants to draw, but Bluey keeps looking for the perfect picture. She draws Dad clapping, then tries to draw tickling, throwing, a big couch, a chair, and a boomerang. Bluey does not like any of her pictures because they do not seem perfect. Mom says Dad will love her drawing if she puts care into it. She tells Bluey that it does not need to be perfect; it only needs to be the best she can do. Bluey tells Mom that Bingo once made a picture Mom called perfect, and Mom put it on top of Bluey's picture on the fridge. Mom hugs Bluey and says that drawing is tough, just as being a parent is tough. Bluey remembers Dad saying that being tough is a good thing. She draws again. Dad sees both cards and puts them on the fridge.

For Father's Day, Bluey and Bingo make pictures for Dad. Bingo makes a heart and rainbow card. Bluey wants her picture to be perfect, so she keeps changing her idea. She tries to show Dad clapping, tickling, throwing, sitting on a couch, sitting in a chair, and throwing a boomerang. Bluey is unhappy with every drawing. Mom gently talks with her on the steps. Bluey remembers that Bingo once made a picture Mom called perfect, and that picture was placed over Bluey's picture on the fridge. Mom says she is not perfect either, because being a parent is hard. Bluey says drawing is hard too. Mom reminds her of Dad's words: “It’s a good thing you’re tough.” Bluey realizes that she can keep trying because she is tough. She completes her drawing. When Bluey and Bingo give Dad their pictures, Dad says they are brilliant and puts both of them on the fridge.

video_title: The Night Before Father's Day Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: On the night before Father’s Day, Dad rides his bike while Mom, Mike, and the narrator clean the garage. They throw away junk, pick up nails, stack paint cans and pails, hang cords and hoses, put away ladders and tires, sweep cobwebs, and clean oil spills. They set out Dad’s tools and wash and polish his car. Mom checks the dipstick and adds oil. Tired, everyone goes to bed. In the morning, they let Dad sleep late and serve him bacon and eggs on a big plate. They give him a card and lead him outside with a blindfold. Dad sees his clean, tidy dream garage and smiles. Then Mom brings out his shiny car. Dad is surprised and happy. The family gets inside and takes a long Sunday ride. Dad thanks them for the best Father’s Day.

Mom, Mike, and the narrator plan a special Father’s Day surprise for Dad. While Dad is away riding his bike, they work in the garage. They remove junk and stray nails, stack cans and pails, hang cords, hoses, and wires, and put away ladders and bicycle tires. They sweep cobwebs and scrub oil from the floor. Then they arrange Dad’s hammers, screwdrivers, and drills. They wash and polish his car, and Mom adds more oil when the dipstick shows that it is a quart low. After working hard, they sleep. The next morning, they serve Dad bacon and eggs and give him a card. They blindfold him and take him outside. Dad is amazed to see his neat garage. The shiny car is the last surprise. He invites everyone to ride with him, and they drive away together while he says thank you.

For Father’s Day, a family makes Dad’s garage clean and his car bright. First, Dad rides his bike while Mom, Mike, and the narrator tidy everything. They toss out junk, gather nails, stack paint cans and plastic pails, and hang cords, hoses, and wires on hooks. They store ladders and bicycle tires, sweep away cobwebs, and scrub oil spills. Dad’s tools are set up neatly. After the car is washed and polished, Mom looks at the dipstick and pours in more oil because it is a quart low. The family rests before the celebration. They let Dad sleep late, then bring him bacon and eggs and a card. With Dad blindfolded, they show him the garage. He is delighted by the clean space. Mom brings out the shining car, too. Everyone piles in for a long Sunday ride, and Dad thanks them.

video_title: Chrysanthemum Read Aloud by Kevin Henkes

summaries.summary: Chrysanthemum's parents were very happy when she was born, so they gave her the long, special name Chrysanthemum. She loved her name and thought it was perfect. When she started school, Joe, Rita, and Victoria laughed because her name was long and came from a flower. Chrysanthemum felt sad and wished she had a different name. Her parents comforted her with kind words, hugs, her favorite foods, and games. The children teased her again the next day, and Chrysanthemum had a scary dream about being picked like a flower. Then a music teacher named Mrs. Twinkle came to school. Mrs. Twinkle also had a long flower name, Davinium Delphinium Twinkle. She said Chrysanthemum was a perfect name and considered it for her baby. Chrysanthemum felt happy and proud again. Later, Mrs. Twinkle had a baby girl and named her Chrysanthemum.

Chrysanthemum loved her name because it sounded and looked beautiful. She was excited to begin school, but three classmates made fun of her. They said her name was too long, barely fit on her name tag, and sounded like a flower. Chrysanthemum became unhappy and even dreamed that a flower version of herself was picked apart. Her mother and father reminded her that her name was beautiful, precious, and perfect. At school, Chrysanthemum met Mrs. Twinkle, the music teacher. Mrs. Twinkle chose Chrysanthemum to be a daisy in the class musical. When the other children laughed at her name, Mrs. Twinkle explained that she also had a long name and was named after a flower. She said Chrysanthemum was a perfect name and might give it to her own baby. The teasing stopped, and the children wished they had flower names too. Chrysanthemum enjoyed the musical, and Mrs. Twinkle later named her baby Chrysanthemum.

On the day she was born, Chrysanthemum's parents called her perfect and chose a name they thought was perfect too. Chrysanthemum agreed with them until she went to school. Joe, Rita, and Victoria teased her because Chrysanthemum was a long flower name. She felt miserable, although her parents helped her feel better with loving words, dinner, dessert, hugs, kisses, and Parcheesi. At music class, the children laughed again when Chrysanthemum was given the part of a daisy. Their teacher, Mrs. Twinkle, asked why they were laughing. She told them her own name was Davinium Delphinium Twinkle and that she was also named after a flower. Mrs. Twinkle said Chrysanthemum was absolutely perfect and might use it for her baby. Chrysanthemum blushed, beamed, and bloomed with happiness. Joe, Rita, and Victoria then wanted flower names for themselves. Chrysanthemum performed wonderfully as a daisy, and Mrs. Twinkle eventually had a baby girl named Chrysanthemum.

video_title: Olafs Frozen Adventure (With Highlighted Words) Cd Audio: Read Along

summaries.summary: It is holiday time in Arendelle. Elsa, Anna, and Olaf prepare a surprise party, but the villagers leave to enjoy their own family traditions. Kristoff shows them a tradition with Sven and a mud troll, but Anna and Elsa do not want to lick the troll. Olaf learns that the sisters do not have a family tradition, so he and Sven travel from house to house. Families share their holiday customs, and Olaf collects things on a sleigh. On the way home, the sleigh catches fire, and nearly everything is lost. Olaf walks through the woods and is chased by wolves. Elsa and Anna find old artwork that Anna made for Elsa every year. They realize that Olaf helped keep them together, so Olaf is their family tradition. Elsa makes a sparkling ice tree, and everyone celebrates together.

Anna and Elsa want a special holiday party for the people of Arendelle. When the Yule bell rings, the villagers go home because they want to celebrate with their own families. Anna and Elsa feel sad because they cannot remember a family tradition. Olaf decides to find one for them. He and Sven visit many homes. One family makes candy canes, and other families share their holiday activities. Olaf puts pieces of each tradition on the sleigh. At Oaken’s trading post, Olaf joins a sauna tradition, but a hot coal makes the sleigh catch fire. Olaf loses almost everything and is later chased by hungry wolves. Elsa finds Anna in the attic, where Anna discovers a box of pictures she made for Elsa. The pictures show Olaf and were saved every year. The sisters understand that Olaf brought them together. They hug Olaf and celebrate with a new ice tree.

The holiday party in Arendelle does not go as planned. The villagers leave to enjoy traditions with their families, and Anna and Elsa think they have no tradition of their own. Olaf wants to help, so he and Sven search for holiday traditions. They visit families who make candy canes and do other activities together. They even visit Oaken’s family and try a sauna. Olaf gathers many special things, but a coal starts a fire, and the sleigh is destroyed. Olaf is separated from Sven and meets hungry wolves. Sven brings help to the castle. Meanwhile, Anna finds old artwork in Elsa’s box. Anna had made a picture of Olaf for Elsa every year and put it under her door. Elsa kept the pictures because they reminded her of Anna. The sisters say Olaf is their tradition. Everyone hugs Olaf, and Elsa makes a sparkling ice tree for their new celebration.

video_title: The Hat Read Aloud | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: Winter was coming, so Lisa hung her woolen clothes outside. A strong wind blew one stocking away. Hedgie the hedgehog found it and put his nose inside, but the stocking stuck on his prick Les. He decided it was a hat. The mother hen, the gander, the barn cat, the farm dog, the pig, and the pony all laughed at him. Hedgie told them his hat would keep him warm and dry in winter. Soon, Hedgie became tired of everyone laughing and went home. Lisa chased him because she had found the other stocking. She pulled the stocking off Hedgie’s head and laughed too. Then Lisa saw that the animals had taken her other woolen clothes. Each animal thought the clothes were wonderful hats. Lisa chased after them, while Hedgie reached his den. He thought the animals looked ridiculous wearing clothes.

Lisa took her warm woolen clothes outside before winter arrived. The wind carried one stocking away, and Hedgie found it. When he pulled it over his head, it became stuck, so Hedgie called it his new hat. Many animals saw him. The mother hen laughed, the gander laughed, the cat laughed, the dog and puppies giggled, and the pony called the hat ridiculous. Hedgie said the hat would keep him warm and dry when snow and cold wind came. He became upset and wanted to be alone. Lisa ran after him with the other stocking. She pulled the stocking off his head and laughed because animals do not wear clothes. Then Lisa discovered that the other animals had taken her woolens. They were all wearing the clothes and thinking they had magnificent hats. Hedgie went into his den and thought the dressed-up animals looked very silly.

A stocking blew off Lisa’s clothesline, and Hedgie found it. He poked his nose into it and ended up wearing it on his head. Hedgie proudly said it was a beautiful hat. The farm animals did not agree. The hen, gander, cat, dog, pig, and pony each laughed or asked why Hedgie was wearing such a funny thing. Hedgie explained that it would keep him dry in rain and cozy in snow. At last, he shouted that everyone should wear a hat in cold, snowy winter. Feeling unhappy, Hedgie hurried toward his den. Lisa followed with the matching stocking and removed the one from Hedgie’s head. Then she noticed that the animals had taken all her missing woolen clothes. They were wearing the clothes as hats and believing they looked magnificent. Lisa chased the animals, and Hedgie went home. From his den, Hedgie thought the animals looked just as ridiculous as they had thought he looked.

video_title: Children's Books Read Aloud - 🤝Encouraging Read Aloud For Kids ❤️

summaries.summary: Finn is in a horrible mood and thinks Grandpa will not understand. Grandpa asks Finn to take a walk. Finn agrees but stays under a covering. Grandpa says he will think about what is beneath things. In the forest, Grandpa talks about trees. Some parts are above the ground, and other parts grow below it. They look at a still boat, and Grandpa says that much may be moving beneath the quiet water. Grandpa sees something digging and thinks she may become a mother. He explains that beneath something solid may be something hollow, and beneath something falling apart, something new may begin. He says people are more than what we see. Beneath actions are explanations, and beneath differences may be sameness. Grandpa also says that someone who seems unable to understand may know exactly how another person feels. At the top of a hill, Finn sees the stars and smiles. Finn says he will remember to think about what is beneath.

Finn feels very upset. Grandpa wants to talk, but Finn says Grandpa will not understand. Grandpa asks him to walk. Finn comes along and stays under his covering. As they walk through the forest, Grandpa helps Finn think about hidden things. Trees have parts that cannot be seen. A boat may look still while water moves beneath it. Sometimes it is easy to guess what is beneath, and sometimes it is a mystery. Grandpa talks about something digging and says she may be a mother. He says that a solid thing may have a hollow place beneath it, and something falling apart may have something new forming beneath it. He says the outside and inside of plants, animals, and people are connected. People are more than they appear. Their actions have explanations, and differences can hide what is the same. Grandpa understands Finn’s feelings. Finn walks to the hill, sees the stars, smiles, and remembers what is beneath.

Finn is having a horrible day. He does not want to talk because he thinks Grandpa will not understand. Grandpa invites him to walk, and Finn agrees. In the forest, Grandpa points out that trees have unseen parts below the ground. He shows Finn a boat that looks still and explains that things may be moving underneath. Grandpa says guessing what is beneath can sometimes be easy, but sometimes it is a mystery. He says that beneath a solid thing there may be a hollow place, and beneath something breaking down, something new may be starting. He explains that what happens inside plants, animals, and people is beneath what happens outside. People have experiences beneath their appearances, explanations beneath their actions, and sameness beneath their differences. Grandpa says someone who seems not to understand may know exactly how Finn feels. Finn wants to keep walking. Together they climb a hill, see many stars, and Finn smiles.

video_title: Thomas & Friends - The Snowy Special, by Rev. W Awdry. Thomas the Tank Engine Audiobook. Read-aloud

summaries.summary: Winter covered Sodor with snow, and the tracks were slippery. Henry was the only engine to make all his deliveries on time. Thomas said Henry must have lucky trucks, so Henry felt happy and thought he would always be useful. The next morning, his trucks were gone because Edward needed them to carry coal to the villages. The Fat Controller sent Henry to collect presents for children. Henry slipped on Gordon’s icy hill, met logs blocking the track, and waited for Rocky to clear them. At last, Henry found Edward and his trucks, but he crashed into them and broke them. Henry was sad, but he remembered the children needed their presents. He went to the airport without his trucks, collected the presents, and delivered them all around Sodor. The children cheered when he arrived. Henry learned that his trucks were not lucky after all. He was lucky because he could still help the children.

Snow had come to Sodor. Henry the green engine puffed happily because his lines were clear, while the other engines were delayed. Thomas said Henry had lucky trucks. Henry liked this idea very much. The next day, Edward took the trucks to carry coal, and Henry had to collect presents from the airport. Henry slipped back down an icy hill. Then logs from James’s truck blocked the line. Rocky cleared the logs, but more snow caused more delays. Henry searched for Edward and finally found him with the trucks in the frosty forest. Henry went too fast and crashed into the trucks, breaking them. Edward said the children would have no presents if Henry did not hurry. Henry thought of the children and continued without his trucks. He carried the presents all over the island. At the last station, the children cheered. Henry felt proud and knew he was still a lucky engine.

A thick blanket of snow covered Sodor. Henry made his deliveries on time, so Thomas thought Henry’s trucks were lucky. Henry believed him and felt pleased. But the next morning, Edward had taken the trucks to carry coal. The Fat Controller gave Henry an important job: collect presents at the airport for children in the villages. Henry had trouble on the icy hill and found logs across the track. Rocky helped clear the logs. Henry kept looking for Edward, but the snowy lines made him late. When Henry finally found his trucks, he slid into them and broke them. He thought he could not go on, but Edward reminded him about the children. Henry set off with no trucks. His wheels slipped, yet he kept moving. He collected the presents and delivered them to the children. They cheered for good old Henry. Henry was proud. He understood that the trucks were not truly lucky; he could be useful without them.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse - The Musical Mix Up 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Minnie is ready to sing in the musical, but her voice sounds like a trumpet. Donald sings on the stage, and Goofy plays his violin. Goofy’s violin sounds like a piano. Minnie has the lead role in a musical, but her singing voice sounds like a trumpet. Donald puts on a costume and sings on the stage. Goofy tunes his violin, yet it sounds like a piano. The silly switch is moved back to normal. Then the musical can go on. Everyone is invited to choose an instrument and a beat. The performers play together, and the audience gives them a standing ovation.

During the musical rehearsal, Minnie sings, but her voice sounds like a trumpet instead of a normal singing voice. Donald goes onto the stage and sings for fun. Goofy plays his violin, but it sounds like a piano. The drum set sounds like a flute. Director Von Drake looks at the instruments and cannot understand the trouble. He asks about Pluto. video_title: Big Bad Bubble by Adam Rubin

summaries.summary: In La La Land, bubbles pop and reappear where the monsters live. The monsters are very afraid of bubbles. Mogo says bubbles are sneaky, travel in packs, and can hurt thousands of monsters. The other monsters listen to him and become frightened. They run in circles, climb trees, hide under covers, and worry about a bubble that suddenly appears. Then someone explains that a bubble is only a thin layer of soap and water around air. It is soft and delicate, and even a little finger can pop it. The monsters try using their fangs and claws. A very large bubble appears, but Wus bravely pops it. Everyone discovers that Mogo was wrong and bubbles are not so dangerous. The monsters feel better and enjoy bubble gum and bubble wrap. Wus even plays in a bath full of bubbles. At last, the monsters decide that bubbles may be safe after all.

A group of big, scary monsters lives in La La Land, but they are terrified of bubbles. Mogo became afraid when a chewing gum bubble attacked his face while he was little. Now he tells everyone that bubbles are sneaky, travel in packs, and kill thousands of monsters. Frul, Ybert, and Wus believe him. They run away, climb trees, and hide beneath a bed. Then the truth about bubbles is explained. A bubble is made from a thin layer of soap and water wrapped around air. It is soft, delicate, and easy to pop. Ybert uses his fangs, Frul uses his claws, and Wus tries to pop one too. A huge bubble appears, and everyone worries, but Wus pops it with a loud bang. The monsters learn that Mogo does not know what he is talking about. They enjoy bubbles, bubble gum, and bubble wrap, and Wus splashes in a bubble bath.

Bubbles often appear in La La Land, where monsters live. The monsters think bubbles are dangerous because Mogo tells them scary stories about bubbles. He says bubbles are sneaky, come in groups, and attack monsters, especially during summer. Because they believe him, Ybert runs around, Frul climbs a tree, and Wus hides under a bed. Another voice explains that bubbles are only soap, water, and air. They are soft and delicate, so a little finger can pop one. Ybert, Frul, and Wus each get a chance to try. A small bubble is easy to pop, but then a very big bubble appears. Wus is encouraged to be brave. He pops the large bubble with a loud kaboom. The monsters see that Mogo was mistaken. They are no longer so afraid. They enjoy bubble gum, bubble wrap, and a bath filled with bubbles. The story ends with the thought that bubbles may not be dangerous after all.

video_title: 🏖️☀️ Kids Book Read Aloud: Mickey And Friends : Minnie By The Sea

summaries.summary: Minnie is by the sea and looks around. She sees one green plane, two purple umbrellas, and three castles. Then she sees four red crabs and five yellow starfish. Next, Minnie sees six orange kites, seven pink shells, and eight brown houses. She also sees nine white birds and ten blue dolphins. The dolphins are nice too.

By the sea, Minnie counts the things she sees. First comes one green plane. Then there are two purple umbrellas and three castles. Minnie sees four red crabs, five yellow starfish, and six orange kites. She counts seven pink shells and eight brown houses. At the end, she sees nine white birds and ten blue dolphins. The dolphins are nice.

Minnie is at the sea. She sees many colorful things in order. There is one green plane, two purple umbrellas, and three castles. Four red crabs are nearby, along with five yellow starfish. Minnie sees six orange kites, seven pink shells, and eight brown houses. She counts nine white birds and ten blue dolphins. The blue dolphins are nice too.

video_title: Read Aloud Kids Book: Unicorn and Horse! | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Unicorn and Horse are very different. Unicorn has a sapphire horn, a silver coat, a rainbow mane, and white teeth. He eats pink cupcakes, makes rainbows, dances, and makes the other animals happy. Horse does not do these things, and Horse wishes he were like Unicorn. One night, two men take Unicorn from his paddock and tie him in their truck. The animals want to help, but Squirrel cannot run fast enough, Bird cannot fly fast enough, Fox cannot run on the road, and Turtle cannot run at all. Horse thinks carefully and races after the truck. With six great chumps of his large teeth, Horse frees Unicorn. Unicorn thanks Horse. After that, Horse sometimes eats cupcakes and Unicorn sometimes eats hay. They like different things, but most of all they like each other. Horse and Unicorn become friends, and their friendship is better than pink cupcakes.

Unicorn is loved by all the animals. He has a beautiful horn, hair, and rainbow mane, and he shares his pink cupcakes. Squirrel plays ring toss with his horn, and Bird uses his long hair to line a nest. Horse feels unhappy because he cannot make rainbows or dance like Unicorn. He says he does not like Unicorn, but he really wishes he could be like him. Later, two men sneak into the paddock and carry Unicorn away in a truck because they think he could make them money. The animals hear the truck leave. Squirrel, Bird, Fox, and Turtle each explain why they cannot chase it. Horse is the only animal who can help. He runs after the truck and frees Unicorn with his large teeth. Unicorn says thank you, and Horse says he is welcome. They discover that they can enjoy different foods and activities while still being friends.

Unicorn has many special qualities. He has a sapphire horn, a silver coat, a rainbow mane, perfect teeth, and a cheerful way of making rainbows. Horse is different: he is grumpy, likes races, and cannot do the things Unicorn does. The other animals enjoy Unicorn, but Horse wishes he were like him. Then two men steal Unicorn while everyone sleeps. They tie him with ropes and put him in their truck. The animals know Unicorn is in trouble, but none of them can catch the truck. Horse runs after it and uses six great chumps of his large teeth to set Unicorn free. Unicorn is grateful, and Horse welcomes him. After the rescue, they learn that their differences do not keep them apart. Sometimes Horse eats cupcakes, and sometimes Unicorn eats hay. Horse likes races, Unicorn likes ring toss, and both of them like one another. Their friendship is better than anything, even pink cupcakes.

video_title: The Word Collector by Peter Hamilton Reynolds

summaries.summary: Jerome collects words instead of stamps, coins, or rocks. He gathers words he hears, sees, and reads, including short words, long words, beautiful words, and words that sound like their meanings. He fills scrapbooks and sorts the words into groups such as dreamy, sad, action, and poetic. One day, Jerome slips while carrying his collection, and all the words fly away. When he gathers them, he sees that the words are mixed together. Jerome discovers that words can make surprising combinations, such as “whisper Symphony” and “electric peace.” He uses the words to write poems and songs, and he learns that simple words like “I understand,” “I’m sorry,” “thank you,” and “you matter” can be powerful. Later, Jerome shares his words with children by sending them into the wind. The children collect the words, and Jerome feels very happy. He learns to use his own words to tell the world who he is and how he will make it better.

Jerome loves collecting words. He collects words from things people say, things he sees, and things he reads. Some words are short and sweet, while others are long and musical. Some words are hard to understand, and some sound just like what they mean. Jerome puts his favorite words into scrapbooks and organizes them into groups. One afternoon, he carries his collection up a high hill, but he slips and the words scatter everywhere. As Jerome picks them up, he notices that the words have become jumbled. Big words are beside little words, and sad words are beside dreamy words. Jerome begins putting words together in new ways. He writes poems and makes songs with them. He also discovers that simple words can express important feelings. Jerome keeps collecting words until he has many more. At last, he releases the words into the wind, and children below collect them. This makes Jerome very happy.

Many people collect different things, but Jerome collects words. He notices special words wherever he goes. He likes words such as “spark,” “bloom,” “dream,” “geometry,” “wonderful,” and “Symphony.” He also enjoys words that are marvelous to say or that match their meanings. His collection grows, and he sorts the words into groups like dreamy, sad, action, and poetic. Then Jerome slips while moving his words, and the collection flies through the air. The words land in a mixed-up pile. Instead of putting them back exactly as before, Jerome joins them in fresh combinations. He makes poems and songs, and people enjoy them. Jerome learns that simple words can be strong, including “I’m sorry,” “thank you,” and “you matter.” The more words he knows, the more clearly he can share his thoughts, feelings, and dreams. Finally, Jerome sends his words into the wind. Children collect them, and he is happy. He encourages everyone to reach for their own words.

video_title: Library Lion by Michelle Knudsen

summaries.summary: One day, a lion walked into the library and went to sleep in the story corner. The library workers did not know what to do because there were no rules about lions. The lion listened quietly during Story Hour, but he roared sadly when the children had to leave. Miss Merryweather said he could return if he stayed quiet. The lion came early each day and helped by dusting books, licking envelopes, and helping children reach high shelves. Everyone loved him, but Mr. McBee thought lions did not belong in libraries. One day, Miss Merryweather hurt her arm and needed help. The lion roared to get Mr. McBee, so he broke the rules and left. The lion stayed away until Mr. McBee told him about a new rule allowing roaring to help an injured friend. Then Mr. McBee told Miss Merryweather that the lion was back, and she happily ran to see him.

A lion visited a library and quietly explored the books. He joined Story Hour and listened to every story. When Story Hour ended, he roared because he did not want to leave. Miss Merryweather told him that he could come back if he was quiet. The lion returned early the next day and helped around the library. Soon he dusted encyclopedias, licked envelopes, carried books, and let children stand on his back. The library workers decided he was very helpful, although Mr. McBee still believed lions could not understand library rules. Later, Miss Merryweather fell and hurt her arm while reaching for a book. She asked the lion to get Mr. McBee. The lion roared loudly because Mr. McBee would not listen. Thinking the lion had broken the rules, Mr. McBee sent him away. He later found the lion and made a new rule for helpful roaring. The lion came back, and Miss Merryweather ran to greet him.

The library gained a surprising helper when a lion came inside. At first, everyone was nervous, but the lion was quiet and enjoyed Story Hour. He returned every day and helped with library jobs. He dusted the encyclopedias, licked overdue notices, helped little children reach books, and made a soft backrest during stories. People soon wondered how they had managed without him. Mr. McBee was not convinced because he thought lions did not belong in libraries. One day, Miss Merryweather reached for a book, fell from a step stool, and hurt her arm. She called for Mr. McBee, but he could not hear her. The lion tried to get his attention and finally roared loudly. Mr. McBee thought the lion was breaking the rules, so the lion left sadly. Later, Mr. McBee learned that the lion had been trying to help. He told the lion about a new rule: roaring was allowed for a good reason, such as helping a hurt friend. The lion returned to the library.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Disney's MOANA Folk Tale Read Along - The Story of Maui Going Fishing

summaries.summary: After helping Moana restore the heart of Te Fiti, Maui was delighted to have his magical fishhook back. The hook made him feel unstoppable because it let him change shape and fight monsters. Maui flew as a hawk across the bright sky, then landed on a green island to rest. While exploring, he decided to go fishing. He built a canoe from a sturdy tree and paddled far from shore. Maui dropped his hook deep into the cold sea and waited. Soon, something pulled hard on the line. Using all his strength, Maui hauled it upward. A rocky point appeared, followed by a whole mountain. His hook had caught a hidden island. Maui pulled up more of it, revealing valleys, waterfalls, forests, and a curving beach. He admired the beautiful island and imagined Moana and her people discovering it. Then he freed his hook and sailed away, eager to fish up more islands for voyagers to find.

Maui had just received his magical fishhook from Te Fiti, and he felt powerful again. As the demigod of Wind and Sea, he could transform into different shapes, so he flew over the ocean as a hawk. After enjoying the open sky, Maui found a lively green island and decided to rest his wings. Then he got an idea: he would go fishing. Maui made a canoe from a strong tree and paddled until the island looked like a tiny speck behind him. He cast his hook into the deep water and waited. At last, the line tugged. Maui pulled with both hands, but the catch was very heavy. A jagged rock broke through the waves, and then a mountain rose from the sea. Maui kept pulling until an entire island appeared, complete with smaller mountains, valleys, waterfalls, forests, and a beach. He imagined Moana’s people finding it, then sailed off to catch more islands.

Maui was happy because Te Fiti had returned his magical fishhook. With the hook, he believed he could do almost anything, including changing shape and battling monsters. He flew high above the ocean in his hawk form, enjoying the wind and the wide blue sky. When he wanted to rest, he landed on a colorful island covered with green plants. There, Maui decided to fish. He carved a canoe from a sturdy tree and traveled far out to sea. After lowering his hook into the cold depths, he sang while he waited. Suddenly, the line pulled. Maui strained and dragged it upward, expecting a giant fish. Instead, a rocky point rose from the waves. It was attached to a mountain, and the hook was stuck in a rock. Maui continued pulling until valleys, waterfalls, forests, and a beach came into view. Proud of the new island, he freed his hook and went to make more.

video_title: 💫✨ Kids Book Read Aloud: Nickelodeon Paw Patrol : Mighty Pup Power!

summaries.summary: Mayor Humdinger wants to be the first mayor on the Moon. Harold starts the rocket, but it hits a meteor and sends it toward Adventure Bay. Everest and Jake see the meteor, so Ryder and the Paw Patrol move everyone to safety. When the meteor lands, the pups get special powers. Chase becomes very fast, Rubble becomes very strong, and the other pups get powers too. Harold also gets powers and uses the meteorite to make a giant robot. The robot captures the pups, but Chase remembers that a good leader never gives up. Marshall melts the nets and frees everyone. The robot then carries the Lookout into the sky with Ryder inside. The pups fly to the Lookout and take the meteorite from the robot. The robot loses power, and Sky slows the falling Lookout with wind. The Lookout lands safely. The pups lose their powers, but they save Ryder and Adventure Bay.

At Adventure Bay Beach, Mayor Humdinger plans to fly to the Moon. Harold accidentally launches the rocket, and it bumps into a meteor. The meteor falls toward Adventure Bay. Ryder sends the Paw Patrol to help people get safe. The meteor makes the pups mighty. Chase is super fast, Rubble is super strong, Sky can fly, Everest can make ice, Marshall can make heat, Zuma can shoot water, and Rocky can make glowing tools. Harold uses his new power to build a robot. The robot catches almost all the pups and takes Ryder away in the Lookout. Chase makes a plan. Rocky makes a tool belt, and Sky flies the pups to Ryder. They see the meteorite on the robot. Rubble opens the robot’s backpack, and Rocky takes the meteorite away. The robot stops working. Sky makes strong wind, and Chase makes it stronger by running fast. The Lookout lands safely, and the pups save Adventure Bay.

A meteor gives the Paw Patrol amazing powers after it falls near Adventure Bay. Ryder calls the pups Mighty Pups and sends them to help. But Harold also gets a power. He makes rocket shoes and builds a super vehicle with the meteorite. Harold and Mayor Humdinger take the meteorite, and Harold makes a giant robot. The robot catches the pups, but Chase escapes. Chase says that a good leader never gives up. Marshall melts the nets, freeing the pups. Harold tries to catch Chase, but the robot crashes into the Lookout. Its rockets lift the Lookout into the air with Ryder inside. The pups must rescue him. Sky carries them to the Lookout, and they find the meteorite in the robot’s backpack. Rubble opens the backpack, and Rocky removes the meteorite. The robot loses its power, but the Lookout begins to fall. Sky makes a whirlwind, and Chase runs fast to make it stronger. The Lookout lands safely. The meteorite stops glowing, and the pups’ powers disappear. They saved Ryder and Adventure Bay.

video_title: Shoo Fly Guy Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: A boy had a pet fly named Fly Guy. The boy’s name was Buzz, and Fly Guy could say, “Buzz.” Buzz played with Fly Guy, made him a glass house, and fed him his favorite food. It was brown, oozy, lumpy, and smelly. One day, Fly Guy flew away while Buzz and his family went on a picnic. When Fly Guy came home, Buzz was gone, so Fly Guy flew off because he was hungry. First, he found a brown hamburger, but a boy told him to shoo away. Then he found oozy pizza, but a girl told him to leave. Next, he found lumpy phones, but a dog growled at him. A smelly road cow was also not his food. Fly Guy became hungry, tired, and lost. At last, he found something brown, oozy, lumpy, and smelly. It was Buzz’s picnic, and Buzz gave Fly Guy his favorite shoe-fly pie.

Buzz loved his pet fly, Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name, and Buzz made him a little glass house. He also fed Fly Guy food that was brown, oozy, lumpy, and smelly. One day, Fly Guy went flying alone. When he returned, Buzz had left a note saying that he and the others were going on a picnic. Fly Guy was hungry, so he searched for food. He tried a brown hamburger, but it belonged to a boy. He tried oozy pizza, but it belonged to a girl. He tried some lumpy phones, but a dog claimed them. Then a bird told him to shoo away from a smelly road cow. Fly Guy flew for a long time. He was tired and lost. Finally, he saw food with all four qualities he liked. Buzz had found him at the picnic and gave him his favorite shoe-fly pie. Fly Guy was very happy.

Fly Guy was a pet who enjoyed a very unusual kind of food. His friend Buzz kept him in a glass house and fed him food that was brown, oozy, lumpy, and smelly. When Fly Guy flew out by himself, he came back to find Buzz gone. A note explained that Buzz had gone on a picnic. Since Fly Guy was hungry, he began looking for something to eat. He saw a brown hamburger, but its owner chased him away. He saw oozy pizza, but a girl also chased him away. A dog growled when Fly Guy went near some lumpy phones. A bird told him to shoo away from a smelly road cow. Fly Guy continued flying until he became tired and lost. Then he found the perfect food because it was brown, oozy, lumpy, and smelly. Buzz and the others had brought a picnic. They found Fly Guy and gave him shoe-fly pie, making him very happy.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑊𝑖𝑡𝑐ℎ𝑙𝑖𝑛𝑔𝑠 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Seven Salazar is a twelve-year-old witchling preparing for the Black Moon Ceremony, where every child is placed into a coven. She has worked hard because she dreams of joining House Hyacinth with her best friend, Poppy. Seven fears becoming a spare, one of the witches whose magic does not match anyone else’s. At the ceremony, Poppy’s amulet turns purple, but Seven’s turns muddy red. Seven is placed in the spare coven with Thorne, a new girl, and Valley Pepperhorn, Seven’s longtime bully. The three must form a circle, but it will not close. If they become forever witchlings, they will lose all their magic. Seven invokes the Claws of the Impossible Task, giving them one final chance. They have three weeks to complete a challenge. The oracle reveals their task: they must fell a night beast. Seven is frightened, but she knows this is their only chance to become full-fledged witches.

Seven has spent years hoping to become a member of House Hyacinth alongside Poppy. She studies, attends witching events, and even joins a toad-racing team because witches believe hard work helps them enter powerful covens. During the Black Moon Ceremony, the witchlings chant a spell and their amulets reveal their covens. Poppy’s amulet glows purple, but Seven’s remains dull until it fills with the red color of the spare coven. Seven is shocked to discover that Valley and Thorne are the other two spares. Their circle fails to seal, which means they could remain witchlings forever and lose their magic. Seven asks to use the Claws of the Impossible Task. The gran grants permission, but warns that they have only three weeks. The oracle delivers the challenge in front of the whole town: Valley, Seven, and Thorne must fell a night beast. If they fail, they will be turned into toads.

On the night of the Black Moon Ceremony, Seven worries that she will be left without a coven. She wants to belong, become a famous journalist, and share a magical future with Poppy. The ceremony begins with twenty-eight witchlings, and several covens form successfully. Poppy is chosen for House Hyacinth, but Seven is not. Instead, Seven joins the spare coven with Thorne and Valley, who has bullied her for years. Seven believes being a spare means being an outcast, with fewer opportunities to learn advanced magic. The three witches try to seal their coven, but their magical circle does not close. Seven realizes that failure could make them forever witchlings, causing them to lose all their powers. She invokes an ancient law called the Claws of the Impossible Task. The gran agrees, and the oracle gives them three weeks to solve an impossible challenge. Their task is to fell a night beast, a dangerous creature rumored to be a giant wolf that eats witchlings.

video_title: ❄️ It's Winter | Celebrate the Seasons!

summaries.summary: Winter arrives with falling snow. The child catches snowflakes, builds snow angels and snow people, and walks through bright snow in warm clothes. A woodpecker taps a tree, and each breath makes a little white puff. The child receives a letter and picture from Grandma and Grandpa in sunny Florida, where winter is warm. Up north, many animals sleep through winter. Bats, groundhogs, chipmunks, turtles, snakes, earthworms, frogs, and dragonfly nymphs rest in safe places. Honeybees huddle together to stay warm. Other animals stay awake. Deer eat twigs and bark, squirrels jump through the trees, and birds eat the seeds the child scatters. The sun sets early, and the child looks at Orion, the moon, and a halo in the sky. A white snowshoe hare hides in the snow. Soon the snow begins to melt, and spring will come. For now, the child enjoys sliding down snowy hills and cheers for winter.

The child loves winter. Snowflakes fall on the child’s face, hair, and tongue, while more snow covers the ground. The child puts on a snowsuit, scarf, hat, mittens, and boots, then makes deep footprints and snow angels. Snow people sparkle in the sun. In the cold woods, a woodpecker pecks, and the child hears boots squeak and crunch. A letter from Florida tells about warm sunshine and a beach, which is very different from the cold winter up north. Many animals sleep or rest during the cold months. Bats sleep in caves, bees crowd together in their hive, and many small animals sleep underground. Deer, squirrels, and birds still search for food. At night, the child sees stars, Orion, the moon, and a snowshoe hare whose white fur matches the snow. When the snow melts, spring is near, but the child still has fun in winter.

On a snowy winter day, a child watches flakes fall and wonders how deep the snow will become. The child dresses warmly and plays outside, making footprints, snow angels, and snow people. A woodpecker makes tapping sounds, and the cold air makes the child’s breath look white. The child learns that winter is sunny and hot for grandparents in Florida, while it is snowy and cold at home. Many animals protect themselves by sleeping. Bats barely breathe in caves, chipmunks sleep beside food, and turtles, snakes, earthworms, groundhogs, frogs, and dragonfly nymphs rest in the ground or mud. Bees stay warm by pressing together. Deer, squirrels, sparrows, cardinals, blue jays, and chickadees remain active and find food. Darkness comes early, and the child looks at Orion, the moon, and a halo. A snowshoe hare blends into the snow. Melting snow shows spring is coming, but the child celebrates winter and slides down hills.

video_title: Appa Reads: Little Blue Truck by Alice Schertle illustrated by Jill McElmmury

summaries.summary: A little blue truck drove down the road and beeped at many animals. The toad, sheep, cow, pig, chicken, chick, goat, horse, and duck were along the way. A big dump truck came by and said he was too busy for the animals. Then the dump truck drove into a muddy puddle and got stuck. The little blue truck went into the mud to help him, but Blue became stuck too. Blue called for help. The cow, pig, sheep, horse, goat, hen, chick, and duck came running. They pushed Blue, and Blue pushed the dump truck. The load was too heavy at first. Then the big green toad joined them. Everyone pushed together. One last push made both trucks free. The dump truck thanked Blue. Then Blue invited all the animals to ride in his truck.

Little Blue Truck traveled along the road, making friendly beeping sounds. He greeted a toad and many farm animals. A big dump truck hurried past and said he had important things to do. Soon, the dump truck saw mud and tried to turn away. He rolled into the mud, and his large wheels sank deep. The dump truck called for help, but no one heard or cared. Little Blue Truck came into the mud and pushed with all his strength. Then Blue got stuck beside the dump truck. Blue beeped for help, and the animals heard him. The cow, pig, sheep, horse, goat, hen, chick, and duck all came to push. They pushed Blue while Blue pushed the dump truck. The green toad joined them. Together, they pushed one more time and became free. The dump truck thanked Blue, and Blue gave everyone a ride.

Blue was a friendly little truck who drove down the road and beeped at the animals. The animals answered with their sounds. A large dump truck came along and did not want to stop for the animals. He drove around a puddle, but he went into the mud instead. His heavy tires sank, and he could not move. Little Blue Truck came to help. Blue pushed the dump truck, but both trucks became stuck. Blue called, “Help!” The animals heard his beeps and came quickly. The cow, pig, sheep, horse, goat, hen, chick, and duck pushed together. They pushed Blue, and Blue pushed the dump truck. The heavy load did not move at first. Then the big green toad came to help. Everyone pushed together one more time, and the trucks came free. The dump truck thanked Blue and said Blue had helped him. Blue then invited everyone inside.

video_title: The Cow that Went OINK Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A cow on a farm made an unusual sound: “Oink!” The cows that went “Moo” laughed at her, and the other animals laughed too. The cow felt very sad. One day, she met a pig that made another unusual sound: “Moo!” The pigs and the other animals laughed at the pig, so the pig felt sad too. The cow had an idea. She made loud “Oink” sounds, and the pig listened carefully. The pig tried again and again until she could oink. Then the pig taught the cow to moo. Other animals laughed, but the cow listened and practiced. At last, the cow could moo. The cow and the pig were happy because each could make both sounds. They were the only animals on the farm who could do both, so they had the last laugh.

There was a cow who went “Oink” instead of “Moo.” The other animals laughed at her, and she became sad. Then she heard a pig say “Moo” instead of “Oink.” The pigs and the other animals laughed at the pig too. The cow and the pig understood each other. The cow helped the pig learn to oink by making the sound and letting the pig listen. The pig practiced many times. The horse, donkey, and sheep thought it was funny, but the pig kept listening to the cow. Finally, the pig could oink. Then the pig helped the cow learn to moo. The rooster, turkey, and duck laughed, but the cow kept listening and trying. Finally, the cow could moo. The two friends were very happy. They could both moo and oink, and no other animal on the farm could do both.

A cow went “Oink,” and a pig went “Moo.” Because their sounds were different from the other animals’ sounds, everyone laughed at them. The cow was sad, and the pig was sad. Then the cow decided to help the pig. She made an “Oink,” and the pig listened. The pig tried to copy her. She tried again and again while the horse, donkey, and sheep laughed. At last, the pig learned to oink. Next, the pig helped the cow learn to moo. The rooster, turkey, and duck laughed while the cow practiced, but she listened to the pig and tried again and again. At last, the cow learned to moo. The cow and pig were happy together. Each one could make both “Moo” and “Oink.” They were the only animals on the farm who could do both, so they had the last laugh.

video_title: 🍁📖 Fall Read Aloud Book for Kids | County Fair, My First Little House Books

summaries.summary: Almanzo lived on a farm with his parents, his brother Royal, and his sisters Eliza Jane and Alice. One morning, the family went to the county fair. They brought pickles, preserves, jellies, embroidery, and Almanzo’s huge pumpkin. At the fair, Almanzo helped his father with the horses. He saw gray horses, cattle, oxen, pigs, sheep, and two strange mules that frightened him. Then he ate a very big dinner with many kinds of meat, vegetables, bread, and pies. Soon it was time to judge the pumpkins. Almanzo’s pumpkin was the largest. The judges tasted pieces from several pumpkins, and a tall judge gave Almanzo’s pumpkin a blue ribbon. Almanzo felt very proud. He and his father watched races, jumping, and throwing contests. The farmer boys won many contests. On the way home, the family learned that Alice and Eliza Jane had also won ribbons. Father said the Wilder family had done itself proud.

A little boy named Almanzo went to the county fair with his family. His father carried the family’s jars of food, and Almanzo’s giant pumpkin had already been taken to the fair because it was too big for the buggy. First, Almanzo and his father visited the animals. Almanzo admired three kind-looking gray horses. Then he saw two black mules. The mules looked partly like horses, but their rabbit-like ears and almost bare tails were different. One mule roared, and Almanzo ran back to his father. After seeing cattle, steers, oxen, hogs, and sheep, Almanzo went to dinner. He ate until he could not eat another bite. Next came the pumpkin judging. Almanzo’s pumpkin was the biggest, and the judges chose it for a blue ribbon. He felt happy and proud. At the fair, he watched several contests. When the family went home, Alice and Eliza Jane had won prizes too.

The Wilder family traveled to the county fair on a beautiful morning. Almanzo was excited because his enormous pumpkin was entered in the fair. He stayed with his father while the others helped prepare dinner. Together, they looked at horses and many farm animals. Almanzo was surprised by two mules. When one mule stretched out its neck and roared, Almanzo became scared, but Father explained what it was. Later, Almanzo enjoyed the crowded fair dinner. He ate ham, chicken, turkey, potatoes, gravy, beans, onions, bread, and many pies. Then the judges examined the pumpkins. Almanzo’s pumpkin was larger than all the others. After tasting the pumpkin slices, a judge pinned a blue ribbon on it. Almanzo felt as if he could finally breathe again. He and Father watched fair contests, where farmer boys won often. The whole family had prizes, and Father said they had done well. Almanzo was the proudest family member.

video_title: Slow🐢 and fast 🐇! @antonijastefek

summaries.summary: Turtle is snoozing in the sun when Hare bounces over and asks Turtle to run. Hare laughs because Turtle moves very slowly. Turtle says he is not lazy and suggests a race. The animals watch as they race to the top of a hill and back. Hare runs very fast and soon reaches the hilltop. Turtle keeps going slowly, one step at a time. Hare decides to take a nap while Turtle is still climbing. At last, Turtle reaches the top. The animals cheer as Turtle turns and walks down the hill. Hare wakes up and sees Turtle close to the finish. Hare runs as fast as possible, but it is too late. Turtle crosses the finish first and wins the race. Hare tells Turtle that he is not a lazy bones after all.

One sunny day, Turtle rests in the sun. Hare comes bouncing by and invites Turtle to race. Hare teases Turtle, saying that Turtle is always slow and can barely move. Turtle feels upset and says, “I’m not a lazy bones.” Then Turtle agrees to race Hare to the top of the hill and back. The animals gather to watch. Hare zooms away and quickly gets to the top of the hill. Turtle continues slowly, step by step. Hare thinks Turtle will take all day, so Hare lies down for a nap. Turtle does not stop. Turtle reaches the top and starts back down. The animals cheer. Hare wakes with a start and sees Turtle near the finish. Hare runs quickly, but Turtle wins. Hare congratulates Turtle and says Turtle is not lazy after all.

Hare thinks he will easily win a race against Turtle. Hare runs fast, while Turtle moves slowly. The race goes up a hill and then back down. When Hare reaches the top, he believes Turtle will need a very long time. Hare takes a nap. Turtle keeps moving, one slow step after another. Finally, Turtle reaches the top of the hill. The animals cheer for Turtle as Turtle begins coming down. Their cheering wakes Hare. Hare notices that Turtle is almost at the finish. Hare runs faster than the wind, but Hare has waited too long. Turtle reaches the finish first and becomes the winner. Hare asks what kept Turtle and then says well done. Hare understands that Turtle is not a lazy bones after all.

video_title: How Droofus the Dragon Lost His Head by Bill Peet

summaries.summary: Drus was the youngest dragon in a family that caused trouble. One day, fog separated him from the others. He found a cave and slept there. The next morning, Drus saved a grasshopper from a spider. He decided it was wrong to eat someone he had rescued, so he began eating grass instead. Soon he grew into a huge dragon. A king saw him and wanted his head, but knights could not find him. A farm boy discovered Drus sleeping beside a lost lamb, yet the boy kept his home secret because Drus was kind. Later, a storm hurt Drus badly. The boy cared for him, and Drus became strong again. He moved rocks, plowed fields, planted wheat, and helped the farm. The king finally found him, but Drus made a deal to visit the castle. There, his happy dragon head delighted everyone.

Young Drus became lost in a fog while traveling with his dragon family. He slept in a mountain cave and searched for breakfast. When he rescued a grasshopper from a spiderweb, he could not eat it. Drus gave up insects and learned to enjoy grass. He grew into a giant dragon. A king offered gold for Drus’s head, so knights searched the mountain, but they failed. A boy later found Drus beside a lamb and chose not to tell anyone. During a storm, Drus crashed into a field and was badly hurt. The same boy and his parents helped him recover. Drus thanked them by carrying away their rocks, plowing the land, pulling weeds, gathering wood, and guarding the wheat. When the king came, the family protected Drus. Instead of taking his head, the king paid Drus to visit festivals, where his smiling head made everybody sing and dance.

Drus was a little dragon who became separated from his family. He saved a grasshopper and then ate grass, which made him grow very large. When the king saw him flying, he wanted Drus’s head as a prize. Knights searched everywhere, but a farm boy found Drus first and kept him safe because Drus had not hurt his lamb. Drus later flew into a terrible storm. His wings were ruined, and he fell into a field. The boy gave him grass and water until he felt better. Drus could not fly, but he used his great strength to help the poor farm family. He moved giant rocks, plowed, planted wheat, cut firewood, and scared birds from the field. An old shepherd told the king about him. The king came for Drus, but agreed to pay for visits instead. At the spring festival, Drus’s cheerful head made the people happy.

video_title: Sleepy, The Goodnight Buddy by Drew Daywalt

summaries.summary: Rodri hated going to bed because he wanted to stay awake. He asked for stories, water, snacks, a pony, and many other things. His parents gave him a good night buddy named Sleepy. Rodri thought Sleepy looked like a moose or a bear, but Sleepy kept staring at him. When Rodri put him in the closet, Sleepy spoke. Sleepy was afraid of Rodri, too. Rodri then asked for water, help going to the bathroom, tooth brushing, stories, a closet check, a snack, a blankie, and help with his hard pillow. He even talked about puppets and a master puppeteer. Sleepy became very tired. Rodri said Sleepy was the worst good night buddy because he was supposed to help Rodri sleep, but instead he made Rodri even more tired. At bedtime, Sleepy wished Rodri good night.

Every night, Rodri found a new reason not to sleep. He asked for another story, a drink, and even a pony, although he did not really want a pony. His parents hoped a good night buddy would help, so they gave him a strange friend called Sleepy. Sleepy stared at Rodri until Rodri hid him in the closet. Then Sleepy spoke and said he was scared of Rodri. Rodri and Sleepy learned that they had both frightened each other by staring. Rodri continued delaying bedtime. He asked for water, help with going to the bathroom, tooth brushing, a story, a witch check, food, more tooth brushing, different lighting, a blankie, and help with his pillow. Sleepy finally became tired and a little mad. Rodri said Sleepy was a terrible bedtime helper because he had not helped Rodri sleep. Sleepy still said good night.

Rodri did not want to go to bed. He kept asking for things so he could stay awake longer, and his parents gave him Sleepy, a good night buddy. Rodri could not decide whether Sleepy looked like a moose or a bear. Sleepy watched him wherever Rodri put him, so Rodri tossed him into the closet. Sleepy suddenly talked. He said he was alive and had been afraid of Rodri. Rodri asked Sleepy to help him sleep, but then he made many more bedtime requests. He wanted water, a story, help checking for a witch, a snack, another tooth brushing, a change in the light, and a blankie. He also complained about his pillow and talked about puppets. Sleepy grew exhausted. Rodri said Sleepy was the worst good night buddy because he was supposed to take away scary thoughts and help him sleep. Sleepy answered with a good night.

video_title: 🐵 Grumpy Monkey Oh, No! Christmas

summaries.summary: Jim, a grumpy monkey, did not want to celebrate Christmas. The day was rainy, his banana was green, and he felt wet, muddy, cold, and unhappy. His friends Norman, Oxpecker, Water Buffalo, Mirabu, and the frogs tried to help him enjoy the holiday. They suggested decorations, songs, presents, cards, naps, candles, sugar plums, and kind deeds, but Jim still felt miserable. He ate the green banana because he thought it might ripen in his stomach, but then his tummy hurt. Norman offered him tea. Jim tried it, and the warm mint tea made his tummy feel better. Jim began noticing good things around him. Raindrops looked pretty on the leaves, the holiday tree made a good umbrella, and his loved ones were nearby. Norman explained that noticing good things can make problems seem smaller. Jim agreed, and he found a reason to celebrate.

On a wet December day, Jim did not feel like celebrating Christmas. First, he found a green banana instead of a ripe one. Then his friends talked about Christmas decorations, songs, holiday traditions, presents, cards, candles, naps, and doing nice things. Jim said no to everything because he was muddy, wet, cold, hungry, and bothered by a fly. He ate the green banana, but his stomach hurt even more. Norman asked Jim to try some tea made with mint leaves. Jim took a sip, and the warm tea helped his tummy feel better. He also learned that he had not noticed many good things. He saw pretty raindrops on leaves, a holiday tree that kept him dry, and friends who cared about him. Norman said that noticing good things can make problems seem smaller. Jim agreed, so he had a reason to celebrate.

Jim was having a very bad Christmas. His banana was green, the rain soaked him, mud covered him, and a fly bothered him. His friends kept telling him to celebrate because Christmas was a magical time of year. They decorated Water Buffalo, sang songs, and talked about holiday traditions. Jim became upset and said that everything stunk. Later, his tummy rumbled, so he ate the green banana. It did not help. His stomach hurt, his head hurt, and he felt cold and wet. Norman offered tea made from mint leaves. Jim tried the tea, and it warmed him and helped his tummy. Then Jim looked around carefully. He noticed beautiful raindrops, a holiday tree that worked like an umbrella, and the loved ones around him. Norman said that noticing good things can make problems seem smaller. Jim agreed, and that became something worth celebrating.

video_title: 'Moving' Read By Julian Clary | Halloween Short Stories

summaries.summary: The narrator refuses to leave Marlborough Court, the condemned housing project that has been his home for years. He lives alone with his spaniel, Poppy, and believes the council should not force him out simply because the estate is being demolished for a new intersection. Another resident, Mr. Malqueenie, also stays behind, but the two men do not get along. Strange events begin: a football appears outside the narrator’s door, every door in the estate seems to rattle, and horrifying faces appear on Mr. Malqueenie’s window. Soon Mr. Malqueenie dies, and Poppy disappears. The narrator follows Poppy’s yelps into an empty flat, where he discovers millions of cockroaches covering the floor, walls, and ceiling. Terrified, he leaves the estate. He sees his belongings being burned, then turns back, determined not to be bullied. Before he can return, a vehicle hits him. Later, he sees that the new intersection is completely gridlocked, so the project has not improved the city as promised.

A man refuses a council offer to move from Marlborough Court because, despite its rubbish, empty flats, graffiti, and burned-out cars, it is still his home. The council plans to demolish the estate and build a major intersection, but he says he will fight the eviction. The deserted buildings soon become frightening. Someone kicks a football against his door, although he cannot understand how it reached his balcony. That night, doors throughout the project bang as if burglars are breaking in. The next day, he finds Mr. Malqueenie dead, with ghostly faces covering the window. The police see nothing unusual. Later, Poppy vanishes, and the narrator hears her yelping beneath his flat. In the empty apartment below, he discovers a terrifying plague of cockroaches. He flees, but sees his possessions and Poppy’s basket thrown onto a bonfire. When he returns to challenge whatever is haunting the estate, a vehicle strikes him. Much later, the finished intersection is revealed to be a noisy, polluted traffic jam.

The narrator is determined to remain in Marlborough Court even though the council has condemned it and plans to replace it with a traffic intersection. He rejects a new home and becomes the only resident left after the others move away. His isolation grows until strange disturbances begin. A battered football appears outside his door, doors rattle all over the estate, and Mr. Malqueenie is found dead in his chair. The narrator then loses Poppy, but hears her calling from an empty flat below. He enters and finds the rooms filled with swarming cockroaches. Their presence reminds him of the creatures that once lived in his mother’s house, and he runs away from Marlborough Court. Behind him, unseen figures burn his furniture, books, clothes, and Poppy’s basket. He decides he cannot be driven away and turns back. A large vehicle hits him in the road, leaving him badly disabled. Years later, from a minibus, he sees the new intersection. Cars are jammed everywhere, showing that the promised solution has created an enormous traffic problem.

video_title: 🚧 Push! Dig! Scoop! 🚧 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Over by a dirt pile in the sizzling summer sun, a group of construction vehicles and their little helpers work together. First, a mama bulldozer and her little Dozer push. Then a papa excavator and two helpers dig. A papa wheel loader and three toddlers scoop, while a mama dump truck and four helpers spill their loads. Next, a papa pipe layer and five helpers lay pipes. A mama cement mixer and six helpers spin near a stack of bricks. A tall mama crane and seven helpers lift beams high into the sky. A strong papa grader and eight helpers scrape near the construction gate. A papa asphalt paver and nine helpers glide along in a line. Finally, a mama steamroller and ten helpers mash the ground. When their hard work is done, all the trucks toot, clean up, snuggle in, and listen to their truck lullaby. They whisper good night and dream about tomorrow at the construction site.

At a construction site beside a dirt pile, working trucks teach their young helpers how to do different jobs. The bulldozer family pushes dirt, and the excavator family digs. Three wheel-loader helpers scoop, while four dump-truck helpers spill their loads. Five pipe-layer helpers lay pipes, and six cement-mixer helpers spin. High above the site, a crane and seven little cranes lift materials. Near the construction gate, a grader and eight helpers scrape the ground. Then a papa asphalt paver and nine helpers glide in a long line. Last, a mama steamroller and ten little rollers mash the surface. Each group makes its own working sounds as it finishes. As the summer day sinks, the trucks shout, “Toot toot!” because the hard work day is done. They scrub themselves, snuggle together, watch the lights blink and dim, and whisper good night before dreaming of the next day.

The story follows construction families working over by a dirt pile. A mama bulldozer and her little Dozer push together. A papa excavator and two helpers dig, and a papa wheel loader with three little helpers scoops. A mama dump truck and four helpers spill materials. Then a papa pipe layer and five helpers lay pipes near arriving steel beams. A mama cement mixer and six helpers spin beside bricks. A tall mama crane and seven helpers lift things skyward. A strong papa grader and eight helpers scrape near the construction gate. A papa asphalt paver and nine helpers glide along a long line. Finally, a mama steamroller and ten helpers mash the ground. After all these jobs, the trucks toot to celebrate. They clean up, snuggle in, and listen to a truck lullaby while the moon glows. Soon they say good night and dream about returning to the big construction site tomorrow.
