video_title: Pancakes, Pancakes!

summaries.summary: A rooster crowed, and Jack woke up wanting a pancake. His mother said he could help make one. First, Jack cut wheat and took it to the mill. He and the miller beat the grain from the wheat and ground it into flour. At home, Jack got an egg from the hen house. Then he milked the cow for milk and churned butter. His mother told him they also needed firewood and strawberry jam, so Jack gathered those things too. When everything was ready, Jack and his mother mixed the ingredients in a bowl. They put butter in a hot pan and added the batter. Jack’s mother cooked the pancake and flipped it high into the air. It landed back in the pan. She put it on a plate and gave it to Jack. Jack said, “Mama, I know what to do now.”

Jack wanted a pancake when he woke up. His mother helped him learn what was needed. Jack cut wheat and carried it to the miller. Together, they beat the grain from the wheat and ground it into flour. Jack brought the flour home. Then he collected an egg from the hen house, milked a cow, and churned butter. His mother also asked for firewood and strawberry jam. Jack found each thing and kept asking if they could make the pancake. At last, his mother said yes. Jack and his mother mixed everything in a bowl. They put butter in a hot pan, and Jack added the batter. His mother cooked the pancake and flipped it. It flew up high, then came down into the pan. She placed the pancake on a plate and gave it to Jack. Jack said, “Mama, I know what to do now.”

After a rooster crowed, Jack thought about pancakes. He asked his mother for one, and she told him to help gather the ingredients. Jack cut wheat and took it to the mill. The miller showed him how to beat the grain from the wheat and grind it into flour. Jack carried the flour home. Next, he got an egg, milked the cow, and made butter by churning. He also gathered firewood and brought strawberry jam from the cellar. When all the needed things were ready, Jack and his mother mixed them in a bowl. They put butter into a hot pan and poured in some batter. Jack’s mother cooked the pancake and flipped it into the air. It landed safely in the pan. She put the pancake on a plate and gave it to Jack. Jack said, “Mama, I know what to do now.”

video_title: The Itsy Bitsy Reindeer -by: Jeffrey Burton- Read Aloud! @Children-12j #storytime #reels

summaries.summary: The Itsybitsy reindeer worked in Santa’s shop with the elves. The reindeer helped build toys, sang happy songs, and helped wrap presents for every girl and boy. The reindeer felt full of Christmas cheer. Then snow came down on the best night of the year. St. Nick came out, loaded the sleigh, and the Itsybitsy reindeer was ready as Santa went on his way.

In Santa’s shop, the Itsybitsy reindeer helped the elves with their Christmas work. It built toys, sang songs of joy, and helped wrap presents for children. The reindeer was very cheerful. Soon, snow fell on Christmas night. St. Nick loaded his sleigh, and the Itsybitsy reindeer went with Santa.

The Itsybitsy reindeer worked hard in Santa’s shop. With the elves, it helped make toys and wrap presents for girls and boys. It sang joyful songs and felt Christmas cheer. When snow fell on the special night, St. Nick came to the sleigh. He loaded it, and the Itsybitsy reindeer was ready for Santa’s journey.

video_title: SNOWMEN AT CHRISTMAS read aloud – Kids Christmas Book read along | Children’s Picture Book

summaries.summary: On Christmas Eve, a child makes a fat, jolly snowman dressed in red and green. While the child sleeps, the snowmen leave their places and travel through the snowy city. They look at bright toy-shop windows and gather in the town square for a Christmas party. They decorate the square and a big Christmas tree with holly, icicles, and balls of snow. Snow children play games, and their mothers serve ice cream, snow cones, and icy sweets. Then the snowmen dance while a fiddler plays. Snowman Kris Kringle arrives, opens his sack, and gives the children presents made of snow. Santa drinks cocoa, the reindeer play, and then they leave. The snowmen hold hands and sing songs about snow and the birth of a king. At dawn, they return to their places. On Christmas Day, they have glowing hearts, gentle smiles, and shining eyes as they dream about their Christmas celebration.

A child wonders how snowmen celebrate Christmas. On Christmas Eve, the snowmen quietly slip away from their snowy places and glide through the sleeping city. They meet friends and family in the town center. Together, they trim the square with holly and icicles and decorate a Christmas tree with snowballs. The snow children play freeze tag and red rover, while the mothers bring cold treats such as ice cream, snow cones, and iced sweets. A fiddle begins to play, and the snowmen dance. Then snowman Kris Kringle comes over the hill. He says a jolly hello and gives everyone snow presents from his sack. Santa drinks cocoa, and the reindeer romp before leaving. The snowmen sing about snow and the birth of a king. When Christmas morning comes, they are back in place, happily remembering their wonderful night.

The snowmen have a busy Christmas Eve. They travel along snowy avenues under glowing lamps and stop to peek at holiday treats in toy-shop windows. In the middle of town, snowmen from everywhere greet one another and prepare a party. They decorate the square and hang snowballs on the Christmas tree. Snow children play, and their mothers set out frozen treats. When a fiddler plays, all the snowmen dance down the middle. Soon snowman Kris Kringle arrives with a sack of presents made from snow. The children are excited. Santa sips cocoa, the reindeer play, and then they hurry away. Finally, the snowmen hold hands and sing songs about snow and the birth of a king. The children grow sleepy, and the grown-ups yawn. As Christmas dawns, the snowmen return to their places with happy hearts, tender smiles, and softly shining eyes.

video_title: How I Met My Monster

summaries.summary: One night, a child finds a note saying that monsters are meeting under the bed. The child does not believe in monsters, but five pairs of eyes appear in the darkness. Mr. Z, the monster teacher, explains the rules. Genas tries to roar, but makes a tiny blurp, so he is not the right monster. Gabe scares the child with his rumbling stomach, and the child jumps into bed. Morgan tries shadow puppets, but makes the child sneeze. Abigail makes a frightening shadow, but the child gets out of bed and leaves. Later, the child finds Gabe again. Gabe has grown huge because people food makes monsters grow. He asks for toes, but the child gives him a stuffed monster instead. Gabe likes the toy, and the child realizes that Gabe is the perfect monster for them. The child yawns and quickly falls asleep.

A child discovers that real monsters live under the bed. Their teacher, Mr. Z, tests each monster to see who can make the child stay in bed. Genas tries to roar, but his roar is only a little blurp. Gabe has a loud, rumbling stomach, and it makes the child jump safely into bed. Morgan tries to use shadow puppets, but her fluffy fur makes the child sneeze. Abigail makes a big shadow, but the child is out of bed again. The monsters vanish, and the hungry child goes downstairs for crackers. After returning upstairs, the child sees Gabe. Gabe is now very large because people food helps monsters grow. He asks for toes, but the child gives him a stuffed monster to play with. Gabe makes soft snorting sounds, and the child decides that Gabe is the right monster. The child feels safe and falls asleep.

The child thinks the note about a monster meeting is a trick from the parents. Then five monsters appear beneath the bed, led by Mr. Z. They must follow rules: surprise the child, keep the bed clear, get the child into bed, and keep the child there until sleep. Genas cannot scare the child, and Morgan’s shadow puppets only cause sneezing. Gabe’s hungry stomach sounds make the child leap into bed, but the child later sneaks away for crackers. Abigail tries to hide, yet she is found and sent away. Gabe finally meets the child in the bedroom. He has become enormous after eating people food and wants to munch toes. The child hides their toes and offers him a stuffed monster. Gabe enjoys the toy and makes comforting snorts. The child laughs, chooses Gabe as the perfect monster, and falls asleep.

video_title: The Gift of Being Different | The secret of your own superpower

summaries.summary: Abigail is eight years old and has trouble reading in school. She works in the blue group, where the books and activities seem less exciting than those in the yellow and green groups. Reading aloud is difficult because she needs time to join letters and sounds, and sometimes her brain flip-flops the letters. One day, her mother takes her to meet Dr. Laura. After playing games and reading books, Abigail learns that she has dyslexia. At first, she worries that dyslexia means she is stupid or not special. Her mother explains that dyslexia means learning differently. Abigail can think in pictures, notice hidden possibilities, use her senses, and imagine many things. Her mother tells her that famous people with dyslexia achieved wonderful things because they thought creatively. Abigail learns that extra help and special tools can help her use her superpower. When her brother Josh calls her a superhero too, she feels less alone and begins to see dyslexia as a powerful way to understand the world.

Abigail loves stories about dragons and griffins, but reading in class is hard for her. She practices often, yet words take a long time to come together, and other children sometimes look at her. Her teacher tells her to focus, although Abigail is already concentrating so hard that her head hurts. Then Abigail visits Dr. Laura, who talks with her about words, sounds, and books. Her mother explains that Abigail has dyslexia. Abigail feels confused because she does not think this sounds like a superpower. Her mother says dyslexia does not mean she is stupid. Instead, Abigail learns differently and may see solutions, possibilities, and hidden paths that other people miss. She also learns that inventors, artists, and engineers with dyslexia created important things in new ways. Abigail will receive reading help, because superheroes need the right tools. Later, Josh says that superpowers work better in pairs. Abigail realizes that dyslexia can help her look at the world differently, solve problems, and help others.

At school, Abigail notices that the blue reading group receives boring books while other groups enjoy more activities and conversation. She is a good talker, but reading sentences aloud makes her nervous and sometimes causes her head to hurt. A visit to Dr. Laura helps Abigail and her mother understand why reading is difficult. Abigail has dyslexia, which means her brain learns in a different way. Her mother shares that Abigail may think with pictures, understand things through her senses and feelings, and discover possibilities that others do not see. She also explains that many famous creative people had dyslexia and used their different thinking to do great things. Abigail still wonders why she needs extra reading help, but her mother says a tutor will give her the tools to use her gift. Dyslexia will not disappear, but Abigail can grow into it. When Josh calls himself her sidekick, Abigail feels happy and supported. She decides that having dyslexia no longer feels lonely because it gives her a new way to see and help the world.

video_title: How I Met my Monster- A Read Aloud

summaries.summary: One night, a child finds a note from Mr. Z saying that monsters are meeting under the bed for a final test. The child does not believe in monsters, but five pairs of eyes blink in the darkness. Mr. Z, the monster teacher, tests the monsters on their rules. Genghis tries to roar, but makes only a tiny blurp. Morgan tries shadow puppets, but makes the child sneeze. Gabe’s rumbling stomach makes the child jump into bed, so Gabe seems to be the right monster. Abigail tries to scare the child, but the child leaves the bed and sneaks to the kitchen. Later, Gabe finds the child and grows huge after eating crackers. The child keeps their toes safe by giving Gabe a stuffed monster instead. Gabe’s gentle snorts help the child fall asleep, and the child decides that Gabe is the perfect monster.

A child reaches under the bed for a toy truck and finds a mysterious note about monsters taking a final test. Soon, a yellow monster and four little monsters come out. Their teacher, Mr. Z, asks them to follow monster rules. Genghis cannot make a scary roar, and Morgan’s shadow puppets make the child sneeze. Green Gabe has a loud stomach rumble, and it sends the child into bed. Mr. Z says that Gabe may be a good match. Abigail makes a big shadow, but the child gets out of bed and walks to the kitchen for crackers. Gabe later appears in the bathroom doorway, so the child runs back to bed. Gabe grows bigger because people food makes monsters grow. He asks for toes, but the child gives him a stuffed monster. Gabe snuffles it happily. His soft sounds are comforting, and the child falls asleep beside the new monster friend.

The child thinks the noises under the bed are part of a trick until five monsters appear. Mr. Z explains that monsters must surprise children, get them into bed, and keep them there until they sleep. The monsters try different ways to scare the child. Genghis makes a tiny sound instead of a roar. Morgan creates silly shadows and fluffy fur that tickles the child’s nose. Gabe’s hungry rumble makes the child jump into bed, but the child soon leaves to find food. Abigail hides in the refrigerator, but she cannot keep the child in bed. After eating crackers, the child returns to the bedroom and sees a very large Gabe. Gabe says that people food makes monsters grow and asks for the child’s toes. The child gives him a stuffed monster instead. Gabe plays with it and makes soft snorting sounds. The child laughs, feels safe, and falls asleep. Gabe turns out to be the right monster for the child.

video_title: A Christmas Carol. PG 6+. Charles Dickens - Retold by Tony Mitton. Illustrated Children's audiobook.

summaries.summary: Ebenezer Scrooge is a wealthy but miserly man who dislikes Christmas and treats his clerk, Bob Cratchit, harshly. On Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his dead friend Marley, followed by the ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. The first ghost shows Scrooge his lonely childhood and the moments when he chose wealth over love. The second shows Bob’s poor but loving family, including Tiny Tim, and the difficult lives of working people. The final ghost shows Tiny Tim dying and a lonely grave marked with Scrooge’s own name. Frightened, Scrooge realizes he can change. On Christmas morning, he buys a turkey and gifts for the Cratchit family. He promises to become a better employer, pay Bob well, and use his wealth to help sick and poor people. Scrooge changes from a miser into a generous and kind man.

On Christmas Eve, old Ebenezer Scrooge sits in his cold office counting money while Bob Cratchit works nearby. Scrooge refuses to pay Bob for Christmas Day and calls Christmas foolish. That night, the ghost of Marley warns Scrooge to change his ways. Three spirits then visit him. The Ghost of Christmas Past shows him as a lonely boy and as a young man who gives up love while seeking wealth. The Ghost of Christmas Present shows Bob Cratchit’s loving but poor family and Tiny Tim’s serious illness. It also shows workers struggling while the rich grow wealthier. The Ghost of Christmas Future shows Tiny Tim dying and leads Scrooge to a grave bearing his own name. Scrooge understands that his future can change. He buys food and presents for the Cratchits, promises to pay Bob better, and decides to help the poor. He becomes a kind and generous Christmas man.

Ebenezer Scrooge has a huge fortune, but he is mean, miserly, and unwilling to share it. He keeps his office cold and complains when Bob Cratchit asks for Christmas Day off. After Marley’s ghost warns him, Scrooge is taken through memories and visions. Christmas Past reveals that he was once a lonely schoolboy and later rejected love to gain more wealth and power. Christmas Present brings him to Bob’s home, where the family has little money but plenty of care and love. Scrooge sees that Tiny Tim is weak and ill. Christmas Future shows him Tiny Tim’s death and a deserted grave with Scrooge’s name on it. When Scrooge wakes, he is grateful to have another chance. He sends a turkey to Bob’s family, buys gifts, and visits them. He vows to become a better boss, pay Bob well, and use his money to help people in need.

video_title: Cars Read Along Story Book | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids | Cars Storybook

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen was a shiny red race car who loved winning. He thought he could do everything alone, and his pit crews kept leaving. One night, Lightning made Mack drive too far. Lightning fell from the truck and became lost. He reached Radiator Springs and made a big mess on Main Street. The sheriff took him to jail. Lightning had to fix the road before he could leave. He worked too fast, so the road became bumpy. Doc challenged him to a race, but Lightning crashed into cactus plants. Mater helped him. Lightning then learned that Radiator Springs was special to its townspeople. He fixed the road and thanked his friends. They cleaned him, gave him new tires, painted him, and gave him oil. At the end, Lightning returned to racing with Doc and a new pit crew. His new teammates were also his best friends.

Lightning McQueen was a famous red race car with a lightning bolt. He cared more about winning than making friends. During a long drive to a big race, he fell out of Mack and got lost. Lightning drove into Radiator Springs and damaged the town. The sheriff took him to jail. Sally helped make a deal: Lightning could leave after fixing the road. Lightning hurried and made the road worse. Doc raced him, and Lightning lost when he crashed into a cactus patch. Mater helped Lightning, and Lightning began to understand his new friends and their town. He learned that Doc had once been a champion racer. Lightning repaired the road carefully. Then the townspeople made him look bright and new. When it was time to go, Lightning had Doc as his crew chief and a new pit crew. They were not only teammates. They were his best friends.

A red race car named Lightning McQueen wanted to reach a very big race quickly. He made Mack drive too long, and he fell out of the truck while sleeping. Lost and scared, Lightning raced into Radiator Springs. He knocked into many things and ruined Main Street. The sheriff put him in jail. Mater, a friendly rusty tow truck, became his friend. Lightning was told to fix the road before leaving town. He tried to finish quickly, but the road was too bumpy. Doc challenged Lightning to a race. Lightning crashed into cactus plants, and Mater helped him. Lightning learned that the townspeople loved Radiator Springs. He also learned about Sally and Doc. Then Lightning fixed the road. His friends cleaned him, gave him new tires, painted him, and gave him oil. The town looked bright again. Lightning went back to racing with Doc, a new pit crew, and many new friends.

video_title: The Hole Story of the Doughnut

summaries.summary: In 1844, thirteen-year-old Hansen Gregory left his family farm in Maine to work at sea. He became a cook’s assistant, climbed high into ship rigging, learned to steer by the sun and stars, and eventually became captain of a fast clipper ship. He even rescued seven sailors from a freezing sea. The story of his famous pastry began on June 22, 1847. Hansen and the cook were making fried cakes for hungry sailors. The cakes were crisp outside but greasy and raw in the middle, so sailors called them “sinkers.” Hansen used a pepper-can lid to cut holes in the dough before frying it. The new ring-shaped cakes were sweet, brown, and cooked all the way through. Hansen’s mother sold them to sailors, and the idea spread around the world. Later, sailors told exciting legends about how he invented donuts, but Captain Gregory said the holes made them well done and prevented indigestion.

Hansen Gregory was a brave young sailor from Maine. He went to sea at thirteen and worked hard until he became captain of the Hard Scrabble, a fast cargo ship. During one voyage, he rescued seven Spanish sailors from a cold and dangerous sea. But Hansen became famous for something made in a ship’s kitchen. One morning in 1847, he and the cook prepared fried cakes for breakfast. The cakes looked good on the outside, but their centers stayed heavy with grease. The sailors called these cakes “sinkers.” Hansen had an idea. He cut a hole in the center of every cake with the lid of a pepper can. When he fried the rings, they became brown, sweet, crisp, and fully cooked. Everyone enjoyed them. Hansen’s mother began making and selling the cakes, and ship cooks carried the invention around the world. Many sailors later created humorous legends about the donut’s beginning, but Hansen explained that the hole helped the pastry cook through.

The story of the donut begins with Hansen Gregory, who became a sailor when he was thirteen. He rose from cabin boy to captain and was known for courage, skill, and rescuing sailors in danger. In 1847, Hansen was helping prepare breakfast aboard the Ivanhoe. The crew often ate fried cakes, but the cakes were raw and greasy inside. The sailors nicknamed them “sinkers” because they felt heavy in their stomachs. Hansen took a round pepper-can lid and punched a hole through each piece of dough. The dough rings fried quickly in the hot lard, making cakes that were crisp around the edges and fully cooked in the middle. The sailors liked them, and a new breakfast tradition began. Hansen’s mother made batches to sell in stores and on the docks, helping the invention spread. Years later, sailors told dramatic stories about donuts saving ships or keeping sailors from drowning. Captain Gregory simply said the hole made them well done and stopped indigestion.

video_title: Kindness is my Superpower | A story about  Empathy & Compassion

summaries.summary: Lucas is an ordinary boy who loves sweets, cakes, and his favorite toy, Teddy. One day, he teases his friend Lisa because she wears glasses. Lisa cries, and Lucas feels sorry. At home, his mother explains that hurting people’s feelings is wrong and that kindness means using gentle words, helping others, and showing respect. Lucas thinks about her words all night. The next morning, he thanks his mother, puts away his toys, and makes his bed. On the bus, he invites a new boy to sit beside him and helps him find his classroom. At school, Lucas greets his friends and shares his crayons and pens. He apologizes to Lisa, and she smiles and says it is okay. Lucas keeps being kind by taking turns, helping a boy find his ball, picking up rubbish, helping an old lady cross the street, and caring for his family. He learns that kindness makes his heart happy and can be learned by anyone.

Lucas does something unkind when he teases Lisa about her glasses. Lisa cries, and Lucas’s mother tells him that hurting someone’s feelings is wrong. She teaches him that kindness can be shown with gentle words, respect, help, and good deeds. Lucas decides to change. He thanks his mother, makes his bed, and puts away his toys. He helps a new boy on the bus and at school. He greets his friends and shares his new crayons and pens. When Lucas sees Lisa, he says he is sorry for teasing her. Lisa smiles and forgives him. After school, Lucas waits patiently for the slide, helps a boy find his ball, and picks up rubbish. While shopping, he holds doors open and helps an old lady cross the street. At home, he covers a sleeping person with a blanket and helps his little sister tie her shoelace. Lucas stops teasing, shouting, and being selfish. He shares his toys and learns that kindness is good for everyone.

Lucas wants to become kind after his mother explains why his teasing hurt Lisa. He learns that people can be kind to friends, family, older people, younger people, and anyone who needs help. The next day, Lucas begins with small good deeds. He thanks his mother, cleans up his toys, and makes his bed. He welcomes a new boy on the bus, helps him find his classroom, and shares school supplies with his friends. Lucas feels bad when he sees Lisa, so he apologizes. Lisa gives him a smile and says it is okay. Lucas discovers that being kind makes him feel happy. He takes turns on the slide, helps find a lost ball, picks up rubbish, holds doors open, and helps an old lady cross the street. He also covers a sleeping person with a blanket and helps his sister tie her shoelace. Lucas no longer teases or acts selfishly. He shares, stays quieter, and learns that kindness comes back to you.

video_title: Frozen Read Along Story book | Read Aloud Storybooks for Kids | Frozen - Little Brothers!

summaries.summary: Olaf was excited to meet the little snowmen at the ice palace. He wanted to hug them and play with them. The little snowmen ran around and did not stop for hugs. Olaf tried skating, but they spun and crashed. Then they played in a pile, and Olaf thought one little snowman had won King of the Mountain. The little snowmen ran outside to Marshmallow. Marshmallow made a playpen with icicles. Olaf tried to play too, but he fell and slid down a hill. Then Marshmallow showed the little snowmen how to slide down the banister. They loved it and kept running upstairs to slide again. When it became dark, the little snowmen went inside and fell asleep in a big pile. Marshmallow fell asleep too. Olaf stayed awake and smiled because he thought his little brothers were the best brothers ever.

Olaf went to the ice palace because he wanted to welcome the little snowmen to the family. He planned to give them warm hugs. The little snowmen were busy running and playing, so they did not hug Olaf back. Olaf tried to skate with them, but they crashed into things. He tried to play tag and hugs, but the little snowmen kept choosing their own games. Outside, Marshmallow used icicles to make a playpen. Olaf picked up icicles, then slipped and slid down a small hill. Soon, everyone lined up for a new game. Marshmallow pushed each little snowman down the banister. The little snowmen loved sliding and hurried upstairs to do it again. They played until night. At last, all the snowmen slept together inside the palace. Olaf watched them and happily called them the best brothers ever.

At the ice palace, Olaf found many little snowmen having fun. He greeted them and wanted to play, but they were too busy running around. Olaf hugged one, but the little snowman bumped into Marshmallow. Olaf tried skating with the little snowmen, and he cheered when they spun and fell. They made a big pile, so Olaf called it King of the Mountain. He offered more hugs, but the little snowmen ran outside. Marshmallow was outside too. He made a little fenced space with icicles. Olaf tried to join the game and slid down a slope. Then Marshmallow began sending the little snowmen down the banister. The little snowmen took turns, then raced back upstairs for more rides. They continued until they were tired. Everyone went inside and slept in a pile. Olaf stayed awake, smiled at them, and said they were the best brothers ever.

video_title: fancy Nancy splendiferous Christmas Kids book Read Along

summaries.summary: Nancy loves Christmas and wants a very big, wonderful-smelling tree. Her dad says they must compromise, so the family chooses the tree her mom wants. On Christmas Eve, Nancy and her family take out old ornaments and wait for Grandpa, who always decorates the tree. While waiting, they bake cookies, wrap presents, and sing Christmas songs. Nancy asks to put up the beautiful tree topper before Grandpa arrives. It spins, flashes, and changes color. Then Nancy unwraps her sister’s tug toy, and Frenchie pulls hard. Nancy pulls harder, and the tree sways. The tree topper falls and breaks. Nancy feels very upset. Grandpa arrives and tells her that when something goes wrong, they can improvise, which means using what they have. Together, they make a new topper with glitter, pom-poms, and ribbons. Nancy learns that making something together can become a special heirloom. On Christmas morning, the tree is magnificent, joyous, sparkly, and splendiferous.

Nancy thinks Christmas should be fancy, and she enjoys every part of getting ready. Her family finds a tree, chooses ornaments, bakes cookies, wraps presents, and sings Christmas songs. They wait for Grandpa because he always decorates the tree. Nancy is excited about her special tree topper. It spins and flashes in many colors, so she asks to put it on the tree. While waiting, Nancy plays with Frenchie and a tug toy. The tree sways, and the tree topper crashes to the floor. It breaks into pieces, and Nancy is devastated. Grandpa comes and listens to what happened. He says that when life gives you cracked eggs, you make eggnog. He explains that improvising means using whatever is around to make something. Nancy, her family, and Grandpa create a new tree topper from glitter, pom-poms, and ribbons. Grandpa says Nancy may tell her future family how they made it together. Nancy calls the new topper an heirloom.

At Christmas time, Nancy’s house looks fancy, and she loves the holiday. She helps her family prepare by baking cookies, decorating presents, and singing. She also waits for Grandpa, who is coming to decorate the tree. Nancy wants the biggest tree, but her dad says the family must compromise. When Grandpa is late, Nancy asks her parents again and again if she may put up the tree topper. The topper is bright and exciting. While Nancy waits, she opens Frenchie’s present and plays tug with the dog. Frenchie pulls the toy, Nancy pulls back, and the tree moves. The topper falls and breaks. Nancy is extremely upset. Grandpa arrives and shows her how to improvise. They use glitter, pom-poms, and ribbons to make a brand-new topper. Grandpa says it may become an heirloom that Nancy tells her family about someday. Nancy enjoys decorating the tree with everyone. Christmas morning is magnificent, joyous, sparkly, and splendiferous.

video_title: THE LEGEND OF OLD BEFANA, by Tomie DePaola | Holiday kids Book read aloud | Picture Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Old Bifana lived alone in a small house in Italy. She was grumpy and did not invite people inside, but she swept her house, steps, and path every day. One night, a bright star woke her. The next morning, three kings and a great procession came by. They were searching for a baby king in Bethlehem. A boy told Bifana that the baby would change the world and that the kings were bringing gifts. Bifana decided to go too. She baked cakes, cookies, and candies, and packed them in a basket. She also brought her broom. However, she stopped to sweep before leaving, so the procession went ahead. Bifana ran after it, but her old legs grew tired. Angels then filled the sky and announced that the new king had been born. Bifana never found the baby, but she still searches. Every January 6, she visits sleeping children, leaves gifts, and sweeps their rooms, hoping one of them might be the baby king.

In a little Italian village, Old Bifana was known as a cranky woman who was always sweeping. She lived alone, baked wonderful food, and sometimes sang, but the neighbors did not understand her. One night, a brilliant star filled her room with light. Soon, three kings stopped at her house while traveling to Bethlehem to find a newborn child king. They explained that the baby had come for everyone, especially the poor, and that they were carrying gifts. At first, Bifana said she knew nothing about royal matters. Then she wondered whether she should visit the child. She baked many treats and put them in a basket. Before leaving, she swept her house and path one more time. This made her leave too late. She ran until she could go no farther. Angels announced the new king, and Bifana followed their song, but she never caught up. She continues searching each year by giving gifts to children on January 6.

Old Bifana spent her days sweeping her small home and road in Italy. People called her grumpy because she would not invite visitors inside. One night, a shining star woke her and kept her from sleeping. The next day, a magnificent procession arrived with camels, horses, elephants, three kings, and other travelers. The kings were looking for a special baby in Bethlehem. A boy said the baby king would change the world and help the poor. Bifana realized that she was poor too, so she decided to bring a gift. She made cakes, cookies, and candies, then packed them with warm coals and carried her broom. She paused to finish sweeping before starting her journey. By then, the procession had disappeared. Bifana ran after it, but became tired and lost. Angels sang that the new king was born and showed her a way through the sky. She still could not find him. Since then, she visits children on the Feast of the Three Kings, leaving gifts and cleaning their rooms.

video_title: The Berenstain Bears and the Spooky Old Tree Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Three little bears find a spooky old tree. One has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They dare to go inside. First, they climb a twisty old stair. Then they find a giant key and a moving wall. They go through the wall and into a spooky old hall. In the hall, they see Great Sleeping Bear. The bears dare to go over the sleeping bear because they have already gone into the tree, up the stairs, through the wall, and into the hall. Soon, the bears have no light, no stick, and no rope. Three little bears go into a spooky old tree. The first bear carries a light, the second carries a stick, and the third carries a rope. They are daring, so they go into the tree and climb a twisty old stair. They find a giant key and a moving wall. The bears go through the wall and enter a spooky old hall. There they see Great Sleeping Bear. The bears go over the sleeping bear, just as they dared to do. After that, they have lost the light, the stick, and the rope. All three bears have the shivers. They need to get out of the spooky place. They go up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. The bears run fast and arrive home safe at last.

Inside a spooky old tree are three little bears. One bear has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. The bears say yes when asked if they dare to enter. They climb a twisty old stair and find a giant key and a moving wall. They go through the wall and into a spooky old hall. A great sleeping bear is there. The three bears dare to go over the sleeping bear because they have already traveled through the tree, up the stairs, through the wall, and into the hall. Now they are without a light, without a stick, and without a rope. They all have the shivers. To escape, they go up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. Then they run fast and are safe at home.

video_title: The Story of Rapunzel | Disneyland Record 1969 | A Grimm Fairy Tale

summaries.summary: A man and his wife longed for a child. When the wife saw fresh lettuce in a powerful witch’s garden, she felt she would die without eating it. Her husband climbed into the garden, but the witch caught him. She allowed him to take lettuce only if he gave her the baby his wife was expecting. Afraid, he agreed. When the baby was born, the witch took her away. The child grew into a beautiful girl and was locked in a tower with no stairs or door. Her long golden hair allowed the witch to climb up. A prince heard the girl singing and visited her. They planned for her to escape, but the witch discovered them. She cut the girl’s hair and sent her into the forest. The prince fell from the tower and became blind. Years later, he found the girl. Her tears healed his eyes, and he took her to his kingdom. They lived happily together.

A husband entered a witch’s garden to get lettuce for his pregnant wife. The witch agreed, but only if they gave her their child. The frightened husband accepted, and the witch took the baby when she was born. The child grew into a beautiful girl and lived in a tower deep in the woods. The tower had only one high window, and the witch climbed up using the girl’s long golden hair. A prince heard the girl’s lovely singing and learned how to enter the tower. He and the girl planned to make a silk rope so she could escape with him. Before they could leave, the witch learned about the prince. In anger, she cut off the girl’s hair and sent her away. The prince came to the tower, fell, and lost his sight. After wandering for years, he found the girl in the forest. Her tears restored his sight, and they returned to his kingdom to live happily.

For many years, a man and his wife wished for a child. The wife wanted lettuce from a witch’s garden, so the man climbed over the wall to get some. The witch demanded their coming baby in return, and the man agreed because he was afraid. The witch took the baby and raised her in a tower when she was twelve. The girl could not leave, but her beautiful hair reached the ground when she lowered it from the window. A prince heard her singing and secretly climbed up. He asked her to marry him, and they planned an escape using silk. The witch discovered their plan and cut off the girl’s hair. She tricked the prince, who fell onto thorns and became blind. He wandered through the woods for years until he heard the girl’s voice. They found each other, and her tears made him see again. He brought her to his kingdom, where they were welcomed with joy and lived happily.

video_title: The House of Love - Read Aloud with Adriana Trigiani | Brightly Storytime Together

summaries.summary: Mia Valentina lives with her big family in an old house on a hill. Valentine’s Day is her favorite day, so she helps Mama clean and decorate. They find beautiful rose wallpaper under the old brown paper and make a candy tree with gumdrops. Mia also draws special valentines for each brother and sister. Then the family comes home, eats dinner, plays games, and enjoys cupcakes. Mia feels sad because everyone seems to have a valentine except her. At bedtime, she looks under her blanket and sheet, but finds nothing. Then she lifts her pillow and discovers a valentine from Mama. Mia is happy because Mama did not forget her. Mia Valentina wants her family to be home for the Valentine’s Day party. She and Mama do their chores, brush Phyllis the rescue dog, and decorate the old house. Mia removes dull wallpaper from the parlor and discovers roses underneath. Together, they make the room beautiful. Mama cuts a branch from the oak tree, and they hang colorful gumdrops on it. Mia draws a different picture for each brother and sister, showing the things they love. When the family arrives, they decorate the kitchen, eat macaroni, and enjoy cupcakes. In the parlor, everyone laughs at the funny valentines. Mia quietly feels unhappy because she thinks nobody made one for her. Later, she goes to bed and finds a special valentine under her pillow. It says she is Mama’s number one helper. Mia smiles and understands that she was remembered. The house becomes a true house of love.

The Amore family lives in an old house with five girls, two boys, Mama, Papa, and Phyllis the dog. Mia, the youngest child, loves Valentine’s Day and worries that her family might not return for the party. Mama tells her they will be home, and Mia helps prepare. They clean the house, decorate every room, uncover rose wallpaper, and build a sparkling gumdrop tree. Mia makes pictures for her brothers and sisters, while Mama hangs them in paper frames. When everyone arrives, the family shares food, stories, games, and laughter. Mia notices that every child appears to have a valentine except her, so she pretends not to be sad. At bedtime, she searches her bed and finds a valentine beneath her pillow. Mama thanks Mia for being her number one helper. Mia falls asleep happily. The house is old and imperfect, but the love inside it is bigger than all its rooms.

video_title: Are You Ready to Play Outside | elephant and piggie series, mo willems books, classroom reading time

summaries.summary: Piggy asks Gerald if they are ready to play outside. They plan to run, skip, and jump, but then it starts to rain. Gerald does not like the rain and says he is not happy. Piggy loves the rain and hopes it will last all day. But soon the rain stops. Now Piggy is unhappy again because Piggy likes the rain. Gerald tells Piggy not to worry because he has a plan. Piggy and Gerald are excited to play outside. They want to do everything, including running, skipping, and jumping. Suddenly, the rain begins. Gerald sees the heavy rain and says he does not like it. They splash in the water, run, skip, and jump. Soon, Piggy says, “I love rain,” and hopes it will rain all day. Then the rain stops, and Piggy becomes unhappy because Piggy now likes rain. Gerald says he has a plan. He says that rain elephants make the best friends.

Piggy and Gerald prepare for a fun day outside. They plan to run, skip, and jump. Their plans change when the sky brings a lot of rain. Gerald does not like the rain and is not happy. Piggy wonders how anyone can play outside in so much rain. Then Piggy sees splashing and decides to try. The two friends play in the rain by running, skipping, and jumping. Piggy begins to love the rain and wishes it would stay all day. But the rain stops, and Piggy is unhappy again. Gerald tells Piggy not to worry. Gerald has a plan. The story ends with Gerald saying that rain elephants make the best friends.

video_title: Kids Picture Book read aloud: PEYTON PICKS THE PERFECT PIE - Thanksgiving read aloud | Bedtime

summaries.summary: Peyton likes many things, such as animals, sports, music, and learning. But she is particular about food. She does not like foods that touch, or foods that are green, gooey, flaky, lumpy, or sticky. At Thanksgiving, her family and friends bring many different pies. The pie is lumpy and flaky, but Peyton takes several bites and likes it. She learns that sometimes a food can seem different when she looks at it another way. Peyton then tries chess pie and thinks she might even like learning chess. Everyone celebrates Peyton’s brave choices with pie à la mode.

Peyton does not think she is picky, because she enjoys trying new activities. She likes dogs, cats, bikes, math, saxophone, and every sport. Food is different. She dislikes foods touching on her plate and avoids many colors and textures. At Thanksgiving, her parents serve a meal and invite everyone to bring pies. The guests bring pies from many places, including lemon chess pie, ruffled milk pie, millionaire pie, plum galette, whoopie pies, and several fruit pies. Peyton worries because the pies look lumpy, sticky, or flaky. She chooses a piece of her mother’s apple pie. At first, it seems a little lumpy and flaky, but it is not as frightening as she expected. When Aunt Polly adds vanilla ice cream, Peyton feels braver and enjoys the pie. Peyton tells her mother she likes it. Then she asks for chess pie and wonders whether she might try chess, too.

Peyton’s family gathers for Thanksgiving, and every guest brings a pie. Peyton wants to try one new food, even though she usually avoids green, orange, and red foods and does not like gooey, gummy, sticky, slimy, frosted, flaky, chunky, or lumpy foods. During the celebration, she hears about many unusual pies. One pie has lemon and cornmeal, another has crisp pastry and wiggly custard, and others contain pineapple, plums, chocolate, mud, pumpkin, or pears. Peyton cannot find a pie that sounds plain. At the table, she eats turkey, a roll, and mashed potatoes while the guests give thanks. Then Aunt Polly brings ice cream and explains that pie with ice cream is called pie à la mode. Peyton tries apple pie with vanilla ice cream. She takes one bite, then another, and discovers that she likes it. She decides to try chess pie next and becomes more willing to try new things.
