video_title: Wish | A story about kindness, empathy & sharing

summaries.summary: Once a year, wishes float through the sky, and a lucky rabbit catches three. He does not know what to wish for, so he asks his friends. Mouse wishes to fly because the world feels big and Mouse feels small. Fox wishes to write stories that people admire and that offer knowledge, hope, and inspiration. Bear wishes for a boat so Bear can explore the open sea. Rabbit thinks about each wish and realizes that his friends’ wishes could help them. He uses all three wishes for Mouse, Fox, and Bear, leaving none for himself. Then his friends explain that Rabbit’s kindness helped them feel important and inspired. Mouse says Rabbit will guide him home, Fox begins writing wonderful stories, and Bear invites Rabbit on an adventure in his new boat. Rabbit’s selfless choice brings his friends joy and gives them chances to share their talents together.

Rabbit had never caught a wish before, but one day three wishes landed near him. Instead of choosing something for himself, he visited his friends to learn what they wanted. Mouse wished to fly over the world. Fox wished to write amazing stories filled with knowledge, hope, and power. Bear wished for a boat to travel beyond the sandy shore. Rabbit listened carefully and wondered whether each wish might be meant for him. Finally, Rabbit made his own wish: he wanted small creatures to feel tall, and he wanted everyone to share inspiration, spirit, and adventure. Then he granted Mouse’s, Fox’s, and Bear’s wishes. Afterward, Rabbit discovered that no wish remained for himself. His friends thanked him for treating them as equals and helping them feel brave and valued. Fox wrote exciting stories, Bear explored the sea, and all three friends invited Rabbit to join their adventures.

Three magical wishes fell from the sky and chose Rabbit. Rabbit could not decide what to wish for, so he asked Mouse, Fox, and Bear. Mouse said flying would let Mouse see the whole world. Fox wanted to create stories that people would admire and that could inspire them. Bear wanted a boat for exploring the open sea after traveling over mountains and climbing rocks and trees. Rabbit considered every answer before wishing for a world where small people felt uplifted and everyone could enjoy adventures together. He gave the three wishes to his friends. At first, Rabbit felt sad because nothing was left for him. However, his friends showed that his kindness had already helped them. Mouse felt taller, Fox found inspiration for writing, and Bear received a boat. Bear then invited Rabbit on an adventure, proving that Rabbit’s selfless act brought the friends together.

video_title: Wish | A story about kindness, empathy & sharing

summaries.summary: Marjorie loved growing seeds into gardens, knitting cozy creations, and watching her favorite baking show. She wanted a friend who enjoyed those things too, because she missed Granny, who had shared her interests. One day, Marjorie saw a sign for a senior group at the community center. Although children were not allowed, she disguised herself with flour, glasses, scarves, perfume, and her mother’s cardigan. Inside, Arthur welcomed her. She learned knitting from Patrick, gardening from Betty, and a stew recipe from Jill. When the group began dancing, Marjorie tried to leave, but she eventually joined the cha-cha-cha. Her disguise slipped off while she danced, and everyone discovered she was a child. Marjorie apologized and explained that she only wanted friends. Arthur told her that people may look old on the outside but still feel like children inside. The group welcomed Marjorie, and she became their youngest member.

Marjorie enjoyed gardening, crafts, and baking, but the neighborhood children did not share her excitement about yarn work and growing plants. She missed Granny and wished for a friend like her. When Marjorie found a community-center sign, she went there with her knitting needles, hoping to meet people with the same interests. The receptionist told her the group was only for seniors, so Marjorie made a disguise. She used flour, glasses, scarves, lavender perfume, and a woolly cardigan to look older. Arthur welcomed her and introduced her to Patrick, Betty, and Jill. Marjorie learned a knitting stitch, heard gardening advice, and received a stew recipe. When the group danced, she first tried to escape, but then she danced the cha-cha-cha. Her disguise fell apart, and she admitted she was a child. The seniors accepted her and invited her to stay, making her their youngest member.

Marjorie felt lonely because nobody her age cared about the hobbies she loved. She remembered that Granny never gave up when knitting or baking went wrong, so Marjorie decided not to give up on finding friends. She disguised herself as a granny and entered a senior citizens’ group. Arthur showed her around, and the members shared their skills: Patrick taught knitting, Betty gave gardening tips, and Jill offered a stew recipe. Marjorie enjoyed herself until the group started its cha-cha-cha. She became tangled while trying to leave, then bravely tried the dance. As she twirled, her scarf and glasses slipped, revealing that she was young. Marjorie said she had only wanted new friends. Arthur explained that people can look old while still feeling like kids inside. The group welcomed her interests and asked her to teach and help them. Marjorie stayed and became the youngest member.

video_title: LITTLE RED RIDING HOOD Read Aloud  | by Trina Schart Hyman | Folk Tale Kids Book Read Aloud by Mrs K

summaries.summary: Little Red Riding Hood lived with her mother near a village. Her grandmother gave her a beautiful red cloak, so everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood. One day, her sick grandmother needed bread, butter, and wine. Mother told Red Riding Hood to stay on the path, be polite, and come straight home. On the way, a hungry wolf asked where she was going. Red Riding Hood told him about her grandmother and her cottage. The wolf tricked her into picking flowers while he hurried to the cottage. He ate the grandmother and dressed in her clothes. When Red Riding Hood arrived, the wolf pretended to be Grandmother and ate her too. A huntsman found the sleeping wolf, opened his stomach, and rescued both of them. They were safe and happy. Red Riding Hood promised never to leave the forest path again.

A little girl named Elizabeth wore a red velvet cloak and became known as Little Red Riding Hood. Her mother sent her to visit her sick grandmother with fresh bread, sweet butter, and wine. She warned Red Riding Hood not to wander from the path. In the forest, a sly wolf learned where Grandmother lived. He encouraged the girl to stop and gather flowers. While she was away, the wolf went to the cottage, ate Grandmother, and climbed into her bed. Red Riding Hood came later and noticed that her “grandmother” looked strange. The wolf showed his sharp teeth and ate her. A huntsman heard loud snoring and discovered the wolf. He cut open the wolf and rescued Red Riding Hood and Grandmother. They thanked him, shared food, and felt happy. Red Riding Hood walked home, promising to obey her mother and stay on the path.

Little Red Riding Hood was asked to take food to her grandmother, who was sick in a cottage in the forest. Her mother told her to walk carefully, stay on the path, and use good manners. A hungry wolf met her and asked about the basket and the cottage. Red Riding Hood answered politely, not knowing the wolf was wicked. The wolf suggested that she look at the pretty flowers. She left the path and went deeper into the woods. The wolf reached the cottage first and pretended to be Red Riding Hood. He ate the grandmother, wore her nightgown, and waited in bed. When Red Riding Hood arrived, she asked about the big ears, eyes, hands, and teeth. The wolf ate her, too. A passing huntsman came in, cut open the sleeping wolf, and saved both of them. Grandmother became strong again, and Red Riding Hood learned not to wander from the path.

video_title: Monsters, INC Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Monsters, INC. - Monster Laughs

summaries.summary: Sully is worried because the monsters at Monsters, Inc. are not making enough children laugh. He watches Pauly tell an old joke, and the boy yawns. Another monster says a child threw milk at him and fell asleep. Sully and Mike decide to fix the problem. Mike writes new jokes and shows the monsters his funny acts with teeth, songs, and a bowling ball. But the monsters cannot perform Mike’s jokes well. Pauly’s joke gets no laugh, Ricky’s teeth are too small, and Spike gets stuck to the floor. The monsters feel sad because being scary seemed easier. Then Lanky slips on a banana peel and lands like a pretzel. Everyone laughs. Mike learns that the monsters should be themselves. Pauly uses his eyes, Ricky jokes about flossing, Spike makes a list about his spikes, and Lanky jokes about skinny jeans. Soon, children laugh loudly behind every closet door.

At Monsters, Inc., Sully notices a big problem: the monsters are not funny anymore. Pauly tells a joke, but a little boy has already heard it and falls asleep. Lanky says a child threw milk at him. Sully asks Mike for help. Mike writes new jokes and performs silly tricks with chattering teeth, a song, and a bowling ball. He gives his scripts to all the monsters. The jokes do not work because the monsters are different from Mike. Pauly’s joke makes a girl stare, Ricky cannot use the little teeth, and Spike gets stuck while trying the bowling ball trick. The monsters become unhappy. Then Lanky slips on a banana peel and lands like a pretzel. The other monsters laugh. Mike understands that each monster must use his own special talents. They make new jokes about eyes, teeth, spikes, and skinny jeans. Soon, the children laugh, and the power problem is solved.

Sully wants the laugh floor to make more power, but the monsters are not getting enough laughs. Mike promises to help and creates many jokes for them. He shows funny performances and tells the monsters to copy him. However, copying Mike does not work. Pauly’s one-eyed teacher joke is not funny to a little girl. Ricky cannot use the chattering teeth, and Spike cannot do the bowling ball routine. Mike first thinks the monsters need more practice, but Sully explains that they are not Mike. The next day, the monsters feel miserable. Then Lanky slips on a banana peel and bends like a pretzel. Everyone laughs at him. Mike sees the answer: the monsters should be themselves. Pauly makes an eye joke, Ricky jokes about flossing, Spike makes a top-ten list, and Lanky jokes about skinny jeans. The children laugh loudly at the monsters’ new routines. Sully says Mike did a great job, but Mike says the other monsters are naturals.

video_title: Doggy Jitters | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Doggy Jitters is a puppy who feels terrified by many noisy or surprising things. Fireworks boom, sizzle, sparkle, crackle, and fade, making Doggy Jitters shake and shiver. Rain, a thunderstorm, and a downpour make the puppy quiver and feel all aflutter. During movie night, popping corn, screeching, groaning, and ghoulish bright sounds leave Doggy Jitters uneasy. Music practice on Saturday brings drums, horns, and a loud “let’s play,” making the puppy shy. Even bubbles that blow and pop create furry fears. Again and again, the story asks what makes a puppy hide, quiver, shudder, feel uneasy, queasy, or shy. At the end, Doggy Jitters wonders what will make these fears disappear. The story closes with a quiet invitation: it is story time, so someone should turn the pages and read to Doggy Jitters.

The story follows Doggy Jitters, a puppy frightened by many everyday sounds and sights. First, fireworks boom, sizzle, sparkle, crackle, fade, and fizzle, so Doggy Jitters shakes and shivers. Then rain sprinkles and drizzles, while a thunderstorm pours down, causing the puppy to quiver and feel all aflutter. At movie night, popping corn and strange screeching, groaning, and ghoulish bright sounds make Doggy Jitters uneasy and queasy. On Saturday, music practice begins with drums and horns, and someone says, “Let’s play.” Doggy Jitters becomes shy because of the loud music. Next, bubbles blow and pop nonstop, adding even more furry fears. The story keeps asking what makes the puppy hide, quiver, shudder, and feel shy. Finally, Doggy Jitters asks what will make the fears disappear. The answer at the end is quiet story time and reading together.

Doggy Jitters has many fears, and the story names them one by one. Fireworks are the first problem because they boom, sizzle, sparkle, crackle, fade, and fizzle. Their sounds make the puppy hide, shake, and shiver. A rainy thunderstorm is another worry. Sprinkles, drizzle, and a downpour make Doggy Jitters quiver and feel all aflutter. During a movie night, popping corn and loud, strange sounds make the puppy shudder, feel uneasy, and feel queasy. Saturday music practice is also difficult because drums and horns play loudly, making Doggy Jitters shy. Then bubbles are blown nonstop. When they pop, the puppy has more furry fears. Throughout the poem, the same question returns: what makes a puppy feel this way, and what will make the fears disappear? At the end, the story offers a peaceful moment. Doggy Jitters asks for story time and wants someone to quietly turn the pages and read.

video_title: 🐟 The Pout-Pout Fish and the Bully-Bully Shark | A Pout-Pout Fish Adventure

summaries.summary: Mr. Fish and his friends are playing happily at the ocean park. A bully shark comes and tells them to move. Mr. Fish feels scared, and the happy park does not feel happy anymore. The shark comes back and uses a bad name. Later, he takes a guppy's lunch and laughs. Mr. Fish wonders what he can do because he is only one fish. Then he remembers that words can make a difference. Mr. Fish turns around and speaks clearly to the shark. He says that the shark has broken up their fun and that his actions are mean. He asks the shark to leave until he is ready to be respectful. Mr. Fish's friends stand together beside him, so nobody feels scared. Soon, the friends are laughing and playing again. They take turns, show empathy, and remember to be kind, be fair, and speak up when something goes wrong.

At a warm ocean park, Mr. Fish and his buddies enjoy laughter and play. A shark swims over, shows his teeth, and orders the little fish to move aside. Mr. Fish shrinks back and feels frightened. The shark returns another time, shouts that he is the boss, and calls Mr. Fish a bad name. The friends try to play, but they still feel worried. When the shark steals a guppy's lunch, Mr. Fish feels even more upset. He starts to leave, but then he has an important thought: even one fish can have a strong voice. Mr. Fish faces the shark and tells him that bullying has ruined their fun. He asks the shark to leave and come back only when he can treat everyone with respect. The friends gather together. They are brave, kind, and fair, and the park becomes happy again.

The ocean friends want their park to be a joyful place. They laugh and play until a bully shark arrives. He tells the fish to scram, scares them, says a bad name, and takes a guppy's lunch. Each time, Mr. Fish feels small, sad, and afraid. He asks himself what he can do. At first, he thinks he is only one fish. Then he learns that speaking up can help when something goes wrong. Mr. Fish turns back and talks straight to the shark. He explains that the shark's actions are mean and have broken up the friends' fun. He says the shark is not a bully by nature, but bullying is what he has done, and he must leave until he can be respectful. Mr. Fish's friends stand together. Their courage returns, and they play by taking turns and using empathy. They remember that bullying ends when friends speak up.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, The Little Mermaid Storybook 2

summaries.summary: Ariel is a mermaid princess who dreams of living above the sea. Her friends Flounder and Scuttle help her learn about humans, but her father, King Triton, wants her to stay away from them. During a storm, Ariel saves Prince Eric after he falls from a ship, and she falls in love with him. The sea witch Ursula takes Ariel’s voice and gives her legs. Ariel has three days to kiss Eric, or she will lose her legs and voice forever. Eric likes Ariel, but he is searching for the girl whose voice he heard. Ursula uses Ariel’s stolen voice and tries to marry Eric. Scuttle and his friends stop Ursula, but Ariel becomes a mermaid again. Ursula turns into a huge monster. Eric stops her, and King Triton makes Ariel human again. Ariel and Eric can finally live together forever.

Ariel wants to see the world above the sea, even though her father, King Triton, does not trust humans. One night, Ariel sees a storm and rescues Prince Eric when he falls from a ship. She sings to him and falls in love with him. Ariel visits Ursula, an evil witch, who takes her voice and gives her human legs. Ariel must kiss Eric in three days. Eric brings Ariel to the palace, and he likes her, but he does not know that she is the girl who sang to him because she cannot speak. Ariel and Eric ride on a boat and almost kiss, but Ursula’s eels tip the boat over. Ursula uses Ariel’s voice and makes Eric think he loves Ursula. Scuttle discovers the trick. Ariel’s voice returns, and Ursula becomes a huge monster. Eric stops Ursula. King Triton makes Ariel human, so she and Eric can be together.

Ariel is a mermaid and a princess. She loves humans and wants to live on land. Her father, King Triton, is angry because he wants Ariel to stay home. After Ariel saves Prince Eric from a storm, she goes to Ursula for help. Ursula gives Ariel legs, but she takes Ariel’s voice. Ariel has only three days to kiss Eric. Eric is looking for the girl who sang to him, and he brings quiet Ariel to the palace. He enjoys being with her, especially when she combs her hair with a fork. On a boat ride, Ariel and Eric almost kiss, but Ursula stops them. Ursula changes herself and uses Ariel’s voice. Eric thinks he loves Ursula and plans to marry her. Scuttle and his friends reveal Ursula’s trick. Ariel’s voice comes back, but she becomes a mermaid again. Ursula becomes a huge monster, and Eric stops her. King Triton makes Ariel human again, and Ariel and Eric live happily together.

video_title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff. Illustrated Children's read-aloud (audiobook) story.

summaries.summary: High in the mountains lived three billy goats named Baby Gruff, Middle Gruff, and Big Gruff. During the cold winter, they ate dry thistles and brambles. When the snow melted, they went down to a valley where fresh green grass grew across a stone bridge. A hungry troll lived under the bridge and wanted to eat anyone who crossed. Baby Gruff crossed first. He told the troll that Middle Gruff was bigger and tastier, so the troll let him pass. Middle Gruff did the same and said Big Gruff was fatter and yummier. When Big Gruff came, the troll tried to gobble him up. Big Gruff pointed his strong horns at the troll and butted him into the rushing river. The troll was swept far away. The three goats ate green grass all summer and never saw the silly troll again.

Three billy goats lived high in the mountains. Their names were Baby Gruff, Middle Gruff, and Big Gruff. All winter, the goats had only dry plants to eat. When spring came and the snow melted, they saw a meadow full of fresh, green grass. They had to cross an old stone bridge to reach it. A big, ugly troll hid under the bridge. He stopped Baby Gruff and said he would eat him. Baby Gruff asked the troll to wait for Middle Gruff because his older brother was bigger. The troll let him go. Middle Gruff crossed next and told the troll to wait for Big Gruff because Big Gruff was fatter and yummier. At last, Big Gruff arrived. He was strong and brave. When the troll jumped up, Big Gruff butted him into the river. Then all three goats enjoyed the meadow.

Baby Gruff, Middle Gruff, and Big Gruff were hungry after a long winter. They left the mountain to find better food in a green meadow. The meadow was on the other side of a bridge, but a stinky troll lived beneath it. Baby Gruff walked across first. The troll wanted to eat him, but Baby Gruff said that Middle Gruff would taste better. The troll let Baby Gruff go. Middle Gruff crossed next. When the troll stopped him, Middle Gruff said that Big Gruff was fatter and yummier. The troll waited again. Big Gruff then came across the bridge. The troll rushed out to eat him, but Big Gruff used his big, strong horns. He pushed the troll into the rushing river, and the river carried the troll away. Big Gruff joined his brothers. All summer, the three goats munched the delicious grass and did not see the troll again.

video_title: THE THREE LITTLE ALIENS AND THE BIG BAD ROBOT read aloud – Children's Technology Fiction read along

summaries.summary: Bork, Gork, and Nikowitz were three little aliens who needed homes of their own. Their mama told them to stay together and watch out for the Big Bad Robot. Bork chose a shiny space rover, while Gork chose a satellite near a planet with golden rings. Nikowitz built a strong house on a faraway blue planet. One day, the Big Bad Robot came. It broke Bork’s rover and Gork’s satellite, so the two aliens hurried to Nikowitz’s house. The robot tried to break the house with its hands and its blaster, but the strong house stayed safe. Then the robot climbed down the telescope chimney and became stuck. It struggled until it burst into many pieces. Bork and Gork were safe with Nikowitz. Nikowitz called their mama and invited her to visit their cozy house. Their mama came to tuck them in.

Three little aliens named Bork, Gork, and Nikowitz left their crowded home to find new planets. Their mama hugged them and reminded them to stay together and beware of the Big Bad Robot. Bork found a shiny rover on a dusty planet and decided to live there. Gork found a satellite circling a planet with golden rings. Nikowitz traveled farther and built a warm, bright house with strong walls. Then the Big Bad Robot appeared. It smashed Bork’s rover and Gork’s satellite. Bork and Gork flew away together and found Nikowitz. They all hid inside Nikowitz’s solid house. The robot hit the house many times and used a blaster, but the house did not fall. When the robot came down the telescope chimney, it got stuck and burst into pieces. The aliens were safe, and they called their mama to come home and tuck them in.

Mama Alien had three children: Bork, Gork, and Nikowitz. When their old house became too crowded, the children went into space to build homes. Bork found a space rover, and Gork made a home on a moving satellite. Nikowitz built the safest home on a blue planet with thirteen moons. Soon, the Big Bad Robot chased Bork and destroyed her rover. It also caught Gork and broke his satellite. Bork and Gork escaped together and went to Nikowitz for help. Nikowitz let them into his strong house just before the robot arrived. The robot bashed the walls, smashed the house, and zapped it with a triple blaster, but nothing could break it. The robot entered through the telescope chimney, where it became stuck. After struggling, the robot burst into pieces. The three aliens celebrated, then called their mama. She came to their cozy home and tucked them in.

video_title: How to Catch a Monster | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: School is over, and a child goes home feeling brave because they got to be the Ninja Master in the school play. The child sees a monster in the closet and decides to scare him. First, the child uses a bag of tricks, but the monster escapes. Then the child tries a sticky Ninja nabbing net, but the monster gets away again. The child looks at the monster and sees that his eyes are sad. The child says sorry and explains that the monster was accidentally scared because he was asleep. The monster smiles and says hello in his own funny way. Then he takes the child to meet his monster mom and dad. The child and the monster play, eat volcano pie, and fly high through the air. At bedtime, the monster helps brush the child’s teeth. Mom comes in, and the child feels safe and ready to say good night.

A child comes home from school after getting the role of Ninja Master in the school play. Feeling strong and brave, the child decides to catch the monster living in the closet. The monster roars, so the child tries several tricks. A first trap does not work, and the sticky Ninja nabbing net does not catch him either. When the child looks closely, the monster seems sad. The child says, “I’m sorry,” and explains that the monster was scared by mistake while he was sleeping. The monster pulls apart the bars, smiles, and gives a funny hello. He brings the child to his house and introduces his mom and dad. The two friends play for hours, eat volcano pie, and the monster throws the child very high. Later, the monster helps with tooth brushing. Mom tucks the child in, and the child feels safe and sound.

After a wonderful school day, a child goes home with the part of Ninja Master in the school play. The child wants to be a hero and plans to scare the monster in the closet. The monster makes a loud roar, but the child keeps trying. A trap fails, and a super sticky net fails too. Then the child notices that the monster’s eyes look sad. The child apologizes and says the monster was scared by accident because he had been asleep. The monster is not angry. He smiles, breaks open the bars, and says hello in a strange way. Next, he takes the child to meet his mother and father. The child discovers that the monster can be a fun friend. They play, eat volcano pie, and soar high when the monster tosses the child into the air. At night, the monster helps brush teeth, and Mom tucks the child in safely.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝐶ℎ𝑜𝑚𝑝 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Wahoo Cray lives with his father, Mickey, who works with wild animals. After a frozen iguana falls from a palm tree and injures Mickey, he stays on the couch with headaches and double vision. Wahoo cares for the family’s backyard zoo while his mother worries that their savings are disappearing. She must travel to China for two months to teach Mandarin, leaving Wahoo and Mickey alone. Soon, Wahoo accepts a well-paying job for them with a reality television show called Expedition Survival. Mickey is still sick, but the money could save the family. The show’s assistant, Raven Stark, visits and signs them up to provide animals. She wants Alice, their huge alligator, and Beulah, a large Burmese python. Wahoo explains that Alice once bit off his thumb when he was showing off. Raven says the program is committed to making its dangerous adventures seem real. Mickey and Wahoo do not yet know how much trouble the job will bring.

Mickey Cray has been unable to work since a dead, frozen iguana struck him on the head. His son Wahoo looks after the animals in their backyard zoo, including Alice the alligator, monkeys, parrots, tortoises, and snakes. Mickey’s injury gives him headaches and double vision, while Wahoo’s mother decides to leave for China to earn money teaching Mandarin. The family is sad and worried, but a television job offers hope. Expedition Survival wants Mickey and Wahoo to provide animals for its famous star, Derek Badger. Although Wahoo knows the show often fakes dangerous scenes, he believes the money is worth the risk. Raven Stark, Derek’s production assistant, arrives with a contract and a deposit. She rents Alice and asks about a large python. Wahoo shows her Beulah, a fourteen-foot snake that bites. Raven explains that Derek wants the show to feel real, even though the animals are trained and rented. The job begins with many dangers ahead.

Wahoo’s father, Mickey, is an animal wrangler whose backyard is filled with creatures used in movies and television. A falling iguana seriously injures him, so Wahoo must feed the animals and clean their cages. Mickey’s illness troubles the family, especially when Wahoo’s mother has to leave for China to teach business workers Mandarin. Then Wahoo hears about a television opportunity that pays one thousand dollars a day. He agrees to take the job with Mickey, even though Mickey’s headaches have returned. Raven Stark, the assistant for Expedition Survival, comes to inspect the animals. She signs a release and gives Mickey a deposit. Wahoo leads her to Alice, a twelve-foot alligator, and then to Beulah, a powerful Burmese python. He tells Raven that Alice once took his thumb while he was feeding her. Raven says Derek Badger wants wild-looking animals and believes in making the show seem real. Mickey is proud of Wahoo, but neither of them knows what will happen next.

video_title: 📖📚🍄 One, Two, buckle my shoe- nursery rhyme

summaries.summary: One, two: buckle my shoe. Three, four: knock at the door. Five, six: pick up sticks. Seven, eight: lay them straight. Nine, ten: a pretty hen.
The rhyme counts from one to ten. First, a shoe is buckled. Then someone knocks at the door, picks up sticks, lays them straight, and sees a pretty hen.
Numbers go from one to ten. A shoe is buckled, a door is knocked on, sticks are picked up and laid straight, and there is a pretty hen.

video_title: 1 Hour of Christmas Read Aloud Books | Little Blue Truck, Big Cheese, Construction Site, and Crayons

summaries.summary: A very proud cheese plans the biggest, brightest Christmas party ever. He has shiny decorations, tasty snacks, huge surprises, and many gifts. But his washing machine breaks, his costume tears, his tree lights go out, and his house floods. His friend Wedge invites everyone to a small, cozy party. They talk, laugh, eat, and enjoy being together. The cheese realizes Christmas is not a contest. It is a time to spend with friends, share kindness, and enjoy the moment. He still likes big celebrations, but he learns that a simple Christmas can be wonderful too.

The cheese believes Christmas must be enormous and dazzling. He makes his parties bigger every year. Then, while preparing his fancy outfit, his washing machine overflows and ruins his clothes and house. He cannot host his party. Wedge Wedgeman kindly offers his home instead. Wedge’s party has no loud music, fireworks, or grand decorations. Everyone simply talks, laughs, and shares the evening. The cheese feels surprised and a little jealous, but he also feels happy. He thanks Wedge for saving Christmas. On his walk home, he understands that friends, food, laughter, and being together matter more than winning or showing off.

The cheese wants to be the star of Christmas. He gives enormous presents, decorates everything, and hosts extravagant parties. This year, a broken washing machine floods his home and ends his plans. Wedge takes the guests to his cozy house. The guests enjoy a peaceful evening together, and Wedge gives everyone a handwritten card. The cheese sees that Wedge has made Christmas special without expensive things. He agrees that they might host a party together next year. Walking home, he thinks Christmas is about sharing time, laughter, music, food, and gifts. No one needs to win or lose.

video_title: 🏁 Blaze and the Monster Machines Blaze Loves to Race 🏁 Nickelodeon Stories for Kids Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Blaze and the Monster Machines are racing. Crusher zooms ahead and pushes a ramp the wrong way. Stripes jumps from it and gets stuck on a ledge. Blaze changes into a fire truck and raises his ladder, so Stripes climbs down. Then rocks block the road, and Zeg cannot get through. Blaze changes into a bulldozer and scoops away the rocks while Stripes helps. Zeg is free. Starla twirls her lasso, but a Grizzly truck pulls her into the woods. Blaze, Stripes, and Zeg make a wall, stopping the truck, and Starla pulls her lasso free. Darington races through a loop, falls, and lands safely in a net held by his friends. At last, the friends cross the finish line together. Everyone is a winner. Blaze loves racing, but he loves his friends even more.

The Monster Machines begin a race when the countdown reaches three, two, one, go. Crusher moves a ramp, and Stripes jumps onto it, landing on a ledge. Blaze helps Stripes climb down with a ladder. Next, rocks fall across the road and trap Zeg. Blaze becomes a bulldozer and scoops the rocks away, while Stripes helps clear the way. Zeg is free. Starla spins her lasso, but a Grizzly truck pulls her into the woods. Blaze, Stripes, and Zeg stand together to stop the truck, and Starla gets her lasso free. During the race, Darington tries a loop-the-loop, loses his balance, and falls. His friends hold up a net, and Darington lands in it safely. The friends hurry to the finish line and cross together. Everyone wins, and Blaze shows that he loves his friends even more than racing.

Blaze loves to race with his Monster Machine friends. When the race starts, Crusher pushes the ramp aside. Stripes jumps from the ramp but lands on a ledge and becomes stuck. Blaze changes into a fire truck, raises his ladder, and helps Stripes climb down. Soon, rocks block the road and bury Zeg. Blaze becomes a bulldozer and scoops up the rocks. Stripes helps him, and Zeg is free. Starla twirls her lasso, but a Grizzly truck pulls her into the woods. Blaze, Stripes, and Zeg make a big wall, so the truck stops and Starla pulls her lasso free. Later, Darington races through a loop-the-loop and falls. His friends spread a net and hold it high. Darington lands in the net, safe. The friends race to the finish line and cross together. Everyone is a winner, and Blaze loves his friends more than racing.

video_title: Llama Llama *feelings* by- Anna Dewdney- @Children-12j #storytime #llama

summaries.summary: Llama Llama is sleepy, so Mama Llama says it is time for bed. First, she puts him in the tub. Llama gets mad when Mama starts to scrub him. Mama brings him a new bath-time toy, and Llama is surprised. He forgets his angry cries, and bath time is over. Next comes reading time. Llama loves books that rhyme, so he happily reads in bed with Mama. Then Mama says it is time to sleep. She says good night and turns out the light. Llama feels worried, alone, and sad when Mama leaves. He breathes slowly, and his worries begin to go away. Soon he settles in his comfy bed and feels excited for the day ahead.

It is bedtime for Llama Llama. Mama puts him in the tub, but Llama gets mad when she starts to scrub. Mama helps him feel better by offering a new bath-time toy. Llama is surprised and stops crying angrily. When bath time ends, Mama and Llama have reading time. Llama loves books that rhyme, and he is happy reading in bed. Soon Mama says it is time to sleep. She says good night and turns off the light. Llama feels worried and alone because Mama is gone. Then he breathes slowly. As he breathes, his worries start to go away. Llama settles into his comfy bed. At the end, he is excited for the day ahead.

Llama Llama begins his bedtime routine feeling sleepy. Mama puts him in the tub, but he becomes mad when she scrubs him. Mama offers a new toy for bath time. The toy surprises Llama, and he forgets his angry cries. After the bath, it is time to read. Llama loves rhyming books and enjoys reading in his bed. Mama tells him it is time to sleep and turns out the light after saying good night. Llama then feels worried, alone, and sad. He breathes nice and slow, and his worries begin to leave. He settles into his comfy bed. The story ends with Llama feeling excited about the day ahead.

video_title: 🌺 Tiny Perfect Things

summaries.summary: Today, we look carefully for tiny perfect things. On the ground, we see a yellow leaf blown down by the wind. We see a spider’s web catching the light and a snail that climbed a fence. Crows sit in a tree, and they watch while we watch them. We find a red bottle cap, a man with a beautiful feather in his hat, and a flower growing through a crack in the sidewalk. Our shadows hold hands, walk when we walk, and stand when we stand. We see a cat on the steps and wave hello to someone we know. Then we see a red apple high in a blue sky and the pale, bright moon. It gets cold, so we go home. summaries.summary: One night, Geppetto, a kind wood carver, wished that his puppet, Pinocchio, could become a real boy. The Blue Fairy gave Pinocchio life, but said he had to be brave, truthful, and unselfish. Geppetto sent him to school. Instead, Pinocchio followed two tricky villains to a theater, where Stromboli locked him in a cage. The Blue Fairy freed him, but Pinocchio was tricked again and went to Pleasure Island. There, lazy boys changed into donkeys. Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket escaped and learned that Geppetto was trapped inside a giant whale named Monstro. Pinocchio bravely went into the sea to rescue his father. They escaped on a raft, but Monstro chased them and broke it. Pinocchio saved Geppetto from the waves, but became cold and still. Because Pinocchio had been brave, truthful, and unselfish, the Blue Fairy made him a real boy.

Geppetto loved his little wooden puppet, Pinocchio, and wished he were a real boy. The Blue Fairy made Pinocchio alive and gave him a chance to become a real boy if he proved himself brave, truthful, and unselfish. Geppetto told him to go to school, but Pinocchio listened to a fox and a cat instead. He performed in a puppet theater, and Stromboli locked him away. After the Blue Fairy helped him, Pinocchio promised to go home. Soon, he was fooled into visiting Pleasure Island. The boys there played and behaved badly, until they began turning into donkeys. Pinocchio escaped with Jiminy Cricket and discovered that Geppetto was inside Monstro, a giant whale. Pinocchio jumped into the ocean, found his father, and helped him escape. A wave carried them to shore. Geppetto found Pinocchio cold and still, but the Blue Fairy saw that Pinocchio had been brave and unselfish. She changed him into a real boy.

Pinocchio began as a wooden puppet made by Geppetto. One night, the Blue Fairy gave him life and told him that good choices would help him become a real boy. Pinocchio was supposed to attend school, but he followed dishonest strangers. He became a performer, was locked in a cage, and then was tricked into going to Pleasure Island. There, he met Lamp-wick and saw boys turn into donkeys because they were lazy and badly behaved. Pinocchio and Jiminy escaped through the sea. At home, they found a letter saying that Geppetto had been swallowed by Monstro. Pinocchio decided to save his father. He dove into the ocean, found Geppetto living inside the whale, and helped him escape on a raft. Monstro chased them and smashed the raft. Pinocchio kept Geppetto afloat until they reached shore. Pinocchio became cold and pale, but his brave and unselfish actions proved him worthy. The Blue Fairy then made him a real live boy.

video_title: Appa Reads: Pink Is For Boys by Robb Pearlman, Illustrated by Eda Kaban

summaries.summary: Pink is for boys and girls, and it can be on bows and fancy clothes. Blue is for girls and boys, and it can be on uniforms for a team. Yellow is for boys and girls, and it can be on a crown. Green is for girls and boys, and it can be seen in grass for running. Red is for boys and girls, and it can be on cars racing around a track. Orange is for girls and boys, and it can be on popsicles that drip down sticky chins. Purple is for boys and girls, and it can be on unicorns. Brown is for girls and boys, and it can be on teddy bears to cuddle. Black and white are for boys and girls, and puppies and kittens can be petted. All the colors are for everyone. They can be seen in flowers, butterflies, and rainbows in the sky.

The story names many colors and shows that each color is for both girls and boys. Pink can be on bows and fancy clothes. Blue can be on team uniforms, while yellow can be on a crown. Green is in grass where children can run. Red is on cars racing along a track. Orange is on popsicles dripping down sticky chins. Purple is connected with unicorns. Brown is on teddy bears that children can cuddle. Black and white are for everyone too, and children can pet puppies and kittens. At the end, the story brings all the colors together. Flowers, butterflies, and rainbows in the sky have many colors. The story says that all the colors are for everyone, girls and boys. Each color can be enjoyed with clothes, toys, animals, food, grass, racing cars, and things in the sky.

First, pink is for boys and girls, including bows on fancy clothes. Blue is for girls and boys, including uniforms on a team. Yellow is for everyone too, and it can be a crown to wear. Green is for girls and boys, like grass to run on. Red is for boys and girls, like cars racing along the track. Orange is for girls and boys, like popsicles dripping down sticky chins. Purple is for boys and girls, and the story says unicorns are purple because unicorns. Brown is for girls and boys, like teddy bears to cuddle. Black and white are also for boys and girls, with puppies and kittens to pet. Finally, all the colors are for everyone. They appear in flowers, butterflies, and rainbows in the sky. The colors belong to girls and boys alike.

video_title: Blizzard by John Rocco - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A young boy tells about a huge blizzard that began during recess. Snow kept falling, school closed, and the boy and his sister had to climb out a window because the front door was blocked. They played in the deep snow, but walking and pulling a sled were very hard. For several days, the family stayed warm by the stove and ate and drank what they had. The snow plows did not come, and the family’s food began to run out. On the sixth day, the boy made a list of food, prepared his sled, and traveled through the snow to the store. He checked on neighbors, helped make a snowman, and crossed many snowy places. At the store, he got the groceries and pulled them home. Everyone cheered when he returned. The family enjoyed hot cocoa with milk, and later the snow plows came. They had survived the blizzard.

One winter, nearly four feet of snow fell on a boy’s town. The storm closed school, covered the roads, and trapped the family inside their house. The boy and his sister escaped through a window and tried to walk through the soft snow, but it was deep and tiring. They made a camp near the wood stove and built tunnels and rooms outside. Days passed, and the snow plows still had not arrived. Soon, the family’s food was almost gone. The boy knew he was the only person light enough to walk on top of the snow, so he decided to go to the store. He wrote a food list, packed his sled, and traveled past buried landmarks and neighbors. After reaching the store, he loaded the groceries and hurried home before dark. The family welcomed him with cheers and drank warm cocoa. The plows finally arrived, and the family could return to school.

A boy and his family are caught in a powerful snowstorm. Snow falls for days and piles so high that they cannot use the front door. The boy and his sister go outside through a window, sink into the snow, and discover that even their sled cannot move easily. Inside, they warm themselves by the stove while the family waits for the snow plows. They dig snow tunnels and secret rooms, but the fun ends when the food begins to disappear. The boy studies what he knows, makes a list of milk, bread, eggs, and a candy bar, and prepares his sled. He journeys through the snowy town, visits neighbors, and eventually reaches the store. He is cold and tired, but he brings the groceries back. The family gives him smiles and cheers. That night, cocoa made with milk tastes especially good. Soon the snow plows arrive, and the family survives the Blizzard of 78.

video_title: Are You Ready to Play Outside (🐘 Elephant & 🐷 Piggie #7)

summaries.summary: Piggy and Gerald are ready to play outside. They plan to run, skip, and jump, and Piggy says nothing can stop them. Then rain begins to fall. Soon it is pouring, and Piggy says that he does not like rain and is not happy. Gerald thanks Piggy, but the rain keeps falling. Piggy wonders how anyone can play outside in so much rain. Then there is splashing and smashing, and they see that playing in the rain can be fun. They run, skip, and jump. Piggy now loves the rain and hopes it will rain all day. But then Doreen stops, and Piggy is unhappy again. Gerald tells Piggy not to worry because he has a plan. The story ends with the words, “Rain elephants make the best friends.”

Piggy and Gerald begin the day excited to play outside. They say they will run, skip, and jump. Suddenly, it starts to rain. The rain becomes very heavy, and Piggy says he has never seen so much rain in his life. He does not like the rain and is not a happy pig. Gerald thanks him, but the rain still does not stop. Piggy asks how anyone can play outside with all that rain. Then they hear splashing and smashing. The rain is becoming a game. Piggy and Gerald try to play. They run, skip, and jump together. Piggy changes his mind and says he loves rain. He hopes it rains all day. Then Doreen stops, and Piggy is unhappy once more. Gerald tells Piggy not to worry and says he has a plan. The final words are, “Rain elephants make the best friends.”

At first, Piggy is excited because he and Gerald are going to do everything outside. They will run, skip, and jump. Their plan changes when rain starts. The rain pours harder and harder. Piggy says he does not like rain and is not happy. He asks how anyone can play outside in such weather. Then splashing begins. Piggy and Gerald discover that they can have fun in the rain. They run, skip, and jump, and Piggy says, “I love rain.” He even hopes it rains all day. After that, Doreen stops, so Piggy becomes unhappy again. Gerald tells him not to worry because Gerald has a plan. The story closes with the statement, “Rain elephants make the best friends.” The events show Piggy moving from excitement, to sadness about the rain, to enjoyment of playing, and then to waiting for Gerald’s plan.

video_title: Disney Cars 📖 Read Along Storybook 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Mater tells Lightning about his days as the daredevil Mater the Greater. At a busy arena, a cheering crowd watches him try to jump over a long line of cars. Mater races up a ramp, but he lands on the first cars instead of flying over them. He carefully walks across the cars and reaches the other side, while the crowd cheers. Mater also tells about being shot from a cannon through flames, riding on an airplane, and diving into a tiny pool. These stunts cause crashes and injuries, but the audience loves them. Mater says his biggest stunt was jumping Carburetor Canyon. He says Lightning was there too, with rockets on his roof and special souvenir teeth. Lightning races down the ramp and flies over the canyon, but his rocket sputters out. Everyone waits to hear what happened. Mater tells Lightning that he did not make it, and the story ends before Lightning hears more.

Long ago, Mater performed daring stunts as Mater the Greater. At a packed sports arena, fans cheer while he tries to jump over many cars. He speeds toward a ramp, launches into the air, and lands on the first two cars. Then Mater tiptoes over every car until he reaches the other side. The crowd celebrates because he made it across. Mater remembers other stunts too. A cannon shoots him through a ring of fire, and he catches fire after a big explosion. He rides on an airplane, but he slips when the plane rolls upside down and hangs from its wheel. He also dives into a little pool and breaks the pool and many parts of his body. Finally, Mater talks about Carburetor Canyon. Lightning tries the jump with rockets on his roof, but one rocket stops while he is in the air. Mater says Lightning did not make it, and the story stops there.

Mater shares exciting memories with Lightning while everyone at Flo’s V8 Cafe listens. First, Mater performs at a sports arena filled with lights, cameras, reporters, and cheering fans. He races up a ramp to jump over a row of cars, but he lands on them and walks across them instead. The announcer says he did it, and the crowd goes wild. Mater then describes being fired through flames, dangling from an airplane, and diving into a tiny pool. Each stunt goes wrong in some way, yet the audience enjoys watching him. Mater says his greatest stunt was jumping Carburetor Canyon. In his story, Lightning has a new paint job, three rockets, and Mater the Greater teeth. Lightning launches across the canyon, but his rocket sputters out halfway through. Lightning asks what happened. Mater says Lightning did not make it, and then the transcript ends.

video_title: Jumanji

summaries.summary: Judy and Peter were left at home while their parents went to the opera. Bored, they went to the park and found a strange board game called Jumanji. The instructions warned that the game would not end until someone reached the golden city. Peter rolled first and released a hungry lion into the house. Judy and Peter kept playing because the lion would not disappear until the game ended. Their rolls caused monkeys to destroy the kitchen, a monsoon to flood the rooms, a lost guide to appear, sleeping sickness, a rhinoceros stampede, a python, and an erupting volcano. Finally, Judy rolled the number twelve and shouted, “Jumanji!” Everything returned to normal. The children hid the game in the park, cleaned up, and fell asleep. When their parents came home, the children described their “exciting afternoon,” but the adults thought they had only dreamed it. Later, two boys found the game in the park.

After their parents left, Judy and Peter became bored and made a mess with their toys. They went to the park, where Peter found a long, thin box containing Jumanji, a jungle adventure game. A note said that the game was fun for some people but not for all, and the instructions said it had to be finished once it began. Peter rolled a seven and brought a lion into the house. Judy and Peter discovered that every message on the board became real. Monkeys wrecked the kitchen, rain poured inside, a confused guide appeared, and Peter fell asleep with sleeping sickness. Then rhinos smashed the furniture, a python entered the room, and a volcano sent lava and steam everywhere. Judy found a shortcut and rolled twelve. She shouted the city’s name, and the house became normal again. The children put the game back in its box and left it in the park. Later, two other children found it.

Judy and Peter thought their afternoon would be boring, but a game from the park changed everything. Jumanji showed a path from the jungle to a golden city. Its rules said the first player to reach the city and call its name would win, but the game could not stop early. Soon, Peter’s roll brought a lion, and the children understood that the game’s dangers were real. While they took turns, monkeys stole food, a monsoon filled the house with rain, and a map-carrying guide became lost. Peter caught sleeping sickness, and rhinos charged through the rooms. A python wrapped around the clock, and a volcano erupted, filling the room with hot steam. Judy discovered a shortcut. She needed a twelve, rolled two sixes, and yelled, “Jumanji!” The animals and disasters vanished, and the house was restored. The children hid the game and fell asleep. Their parents returned, and two boys later carried the mysterious box away.

video_title: Appa Reads: Halloween Is Coming

summaries.summary: Halloween is coming, and many signs appear. It gets darker at dinner, leaves fall, spiders spin webs, and hay rides happen at the autumn fair. Then pumpkins, jack-o'lanterns, scarecrows, and corn mazes arrive. Children play on castles made from hay bales. Mom buys candy, skeletons decorate doors, and children practice saying trick-or-treat. At school, they march in a parade wearing costumes. At last, the full moon shines, and the streets fill with people in costumes. Children can be cowboys, soldiers, witches, doctors, ghosts, queens, wizards, astronauts, robots, knights, princes, princesses, and many more. They visit houses for tricks and treats. Halloween brings frights and fun for everyone. The signs are clear: Halloween is finally here.

The signs of Halloween begin to show. Dinner comes earlier in the dark, leaves cover the lawn, spiders spin webs, and people enjoy hay rides at the autumn fair. At the farmers market, pumpkins wait to be chosen. There are jack-o'lanterns, scarecrows, corn mazes, and castles made from bales of hay. Mom buys candies, while skeletons stand on front doors and candy apples are sticky and sweet. Children practice saying trick-or-treat and march in a school parade wearing frightening costumes. Then the special night arrives. A full moon peeks through clouds, and costume crowds fill the streets. People dress as cowboys, witches, doctors, ghosts, queens, wizards, astronauts, robots, and many other things. There are tricks, treats, frights, and fun. Halloween is finally here.

Halloween gets near as the air turns chilly, dinner gets darker, leaves fall, and spiders spin webs. Hay rides take place at the autumn fair. Soon there are pumpkins, jack-o'lanterns, scarecrows, and corn mazes. Children play on hay-bale castles. Mom buys candy, skeletons decorate the front door, and candy apples taste sticky and sweet. Children practice shouting trick-or-treat and march in a school parade in costumes they made. On Halloween night, the moon shines through clouds and streets fill with costume crowds. People may be cowboys, soldiers, witches, doctors, ghosts, goblins, queens, rock stars, wizards, astronauts, farmers, zombies, robots, knights, princes, princesses, clowns, mimes, mummies, wolfmen, or Frankenstein. Everyone can be what they want. They visit houses for tricks and treats, and Halloween is full of spooky things, frights, and fun.

video_title: Thanksgiving Stories ~ A PLUMP AND PERKY TURKEY Read Aloud ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books

summaries.summary: The people of Squawk Valley wanted a turkey for their Thanksgiving feast, but no turkey could be found. They were worried they might have to eat shredded wheat instead. Ebenezer Beezer had an idea. The people would hold an arts and crafts fair with turkey as the theme. They made turkey pictures and statues from potatoes, clay, rope, oatmeal, paper, and soap. They put posters in the forest to invite a turkey to pose. Pete, a proud, clever, hungry turkey, saw the signs and volunteered. The people hired him. On Thanksgiving Day, Pete judged all the turkey artwork. There were turkey creations everywhere, so Pete hid among them. When the people searched, Pete was gone. They found a note saying he had taken his modeling fee. The oatmeal turkey was missing too. The people had no real turkey, so they ate shredded wheat. They learned that a plump, perky turkey can be very clever.

In Squawk Valley, Thanksgiving was coming, but the people did not have a turkey for their feast. They decided to make a turkey arts and crafts fair. Everyone created turkeys from potatoes, clay, rope, oatmeal, paper, and soap. They placed posters around the forest, hoping a turkey would come to model. Pete, a cocky and clever turkey who loved to eat, found the posters. He thought he was perfect for the job and joined the fair. Before Thanksgiving, Pete posed while the townspeople made even more turkey art. On Thanksgiving Day, the people asked Pete to judge the artwork. As he walked among the many turkey creations, he quietly disappeared. The crowd searched everywhere, but Pete had hidden himself in the colorful display. He left a note saying he had taken his modeling fee, and the oatmeal turkey was gone too. The people ate shredded wheat and learned that turkeys can be clever.

The people of Squawk Valley were sad because their Thanksgiving turkey was missing. They needed a turkey for their planned feast, but turkeys had become smart and hid when autumn arrived. Ebenezer Beezer suggested a trick: the people could invite a turkey to an arts and crafts fair. They announced that the grand prize would be a turkey-themed event. Pete, a plump and perky turkey, saw the posters and proudly offered to pose. The townspeople were happy because Pete seemed to solve their problem. They made many turkey crafts, including turkeys from spuds, clay, rope, oatmeal, paper, and soap. On Thanksgiving Day, Pete judged the crafts. The room was filled with turkey shapes, which gave him the perfect place to hide. While everyone looked at the artwork, Pete escaped. He left a note and took the oatmeal turkey as his payment. The people could not eat Pete, so they shared shredded wheat. They remembered that a clever turkey is hard to trick.

video_title: 👧🏻 The Gingerbread Girl Goes Animal Crackers

summaries.summary: It was the Gingerbread Girl’s birthday. The little old man and woman gave her a box of animal crackers tied with a licorice ribbon. When she opened it, the lion, bear, elephant, gorilla, kangaroo, crocodile, and polar bear crackers jumped out and ran away. The Gingerbread Girl chased them while farmers, a cat, a mouse, sheep, children, chickens, and scouts watched or joined the noisy chase. Soon, the crackers reached the river, where the hungry fox waited. He promised to carry them across, but he planned to eat them. The Gingerbread Girl told the crackers that the fox had very sensitive ears. The crackers ran to his ears and made a huge, loud roar. The fox became frightened and ran away. The animal crackers returned home with the Gingerbread Girl, and everyone celebrated her birthday. That night, the tired crackers slept safely together.

On her birthday, the Gingerbread Girl received a special present: a box of animal crackers. She hoped the crackers would be friends, but they burst out of the box and raced through the countryside. They made loud sounds and sang that nobody could catch them. The Gingerbread Girl followed them past farmers, a cat and mouse, sheep, kite-flying children, a mother hen and chicks, and a troop of scouts. At the river, the same fox who had hurt the Gingerbread Boy tried to trick the animal crackers. He told them to climb onto his tail, then his back, and then his head. He wanted to eat them. The Gingerbread Girl quickly made a plan. She explained that the fox’s ears were very sensitive. The crackers gathered near his ears and made their biggest roar. The fox fled, and the crackers safely went home for a birthday celebration.

The Gingerbread Girl wanted friends for her birthday, so the little old man and woman gave her animal crackers. The crackers were not quiet friends. They escaped from their box and ran everywhere, making a great deal of noise. A gorilla, elephant, lion, kangaroo, crocodile, and polar bear cracker each sang while the Gingerbread Girl chased them. Many animals, children, farmers, and scouts saw the chase. Then the crackers met the fox beside a deep river. The fox smiled and offered to help them cross, but he was really planning to eat them. The Gingerbread Girl warned her new friends and asked them to use their loud voices. The animal crackers rushed to the fox’s ears and made a tremendous roar. The fox jumped out of the water and ran away. The crackers hugged the Gingerbread Girl and returned home. Her birthday cake was waiting, and the old friends and new friends celebrated together. Later, the animal crackers slept peacefully beside her.

video_title: Appa Reads: The Rainbow Fish by Marcus Pfister

summaries.summary: The Rainbow Fish was the most beautiful fish in the sea, but he did not play with the other fish. A little blue fish asked for one shiny scale, but the Rainbow Fish said no and swam away. Then the other fish left him, and he was all alone. The Rainbow Fish asked the starfish for help. The starfish sent him to the wise octopus. The octopus told him to give away his shiny scales so he could have friends. At first, the Rainbow Fish cried because he did not want to share. Then the little blue fish came back and asked for one scale. The Rainbow Fish gave him a tiny scale. The little blue fish was happy, and the Rainbow Fish felt happy too. Soon, the Rainbow Fish gave scales to all the fish. He had only one shining scale left, but he was the happiest fish in the sea because he had friends.

A beautiful Rainbow Fish lived in the sea. He thought he was too beautiful to play with the other fish. When a little blue fish asked for one of his shining scales, he refused. The other fish swam away, so the Rainbow Fish became lonely. He asked the starfish why nobody liked him. The starfish told him to ask the wise octopus. The octopus said that he should give away his shiny scales. The Rainbow Fish did not want to do this because he might not look as beautiful. Then the little blue fish returned and asked for one scale. The Rainbow Fish gave him one tiny scale. The little blue fish was pleased, and this made the Rainbow Fish happy. Other fish came, and the Rainbow Fish shared his scales with them one by one. At last, he had one scale left and many friends to play with. He was very happy.

The Rainbow Fish had the shiniest scales and was called the most beautiful fish in the sea. But he would not play with the other fish. When a little blue fish asked for a shining scale, the Rainbow Fish said no. The fish swam away, and the Rainbow Fish was alone. He went to the starfish and asked why nobody liked him. The starfish told him to visit the octopus. The wise octopus said, “Give away your shiny scales. You will not be as beautiful, but you will have friends.” The Rainbow Fish cried because he did not want to share. Soon the little blue fish asked again for one scale. The Rainbow Fish gave him a tiny scale. The little blue fish felt pleased, and the Rainbow Fish felt happy. Then all the fish came, and he gave them scales one by one. When he had only one shining scale left, he swam away to play with his friends. He was the happiest fish in the sea.

video_title: My Very Punny Dad  Written by Ryan Milligan

summaries.summary: A child wakes up and sees that Dad is full of puns. At breakfast, Dad says a quiet person should walk with sneakers on, then balances his plate on one leg and calls it a balanced breakfast. At school, his puns continue with space drawings and an apple sticker that says, “You’re awesome to the core.” After school, Dad jokes about a traffic jam caused by grapes, a spider’s web, bright homework, mushroom soup, a stuffed teddy bear, and a paused television. The child loves Dad but asks him to stop because some puns are confusing. Dad listens, and the family spends a quieter evening together. At bedtime, the child remembers Dad’s old jokes and realizes that some are funny. Then the child makes a dinosaur joke: a sleeping dinosaur becomes a dino snore. Dad is delighted, and they share a laugh before saying good night.

The child’s dad tells puns all day long. In the morning, he jokes about the sun and says that quiet walking goes with sneakers. He stands on one leg while eating and calls his meal a balanced breakfast. At school, Dad has drawn Earth and Mars and written about going to outer space. He also places a message on the child’s apple saying, “You’re awesome to the core.” When the child comes home, Dad jokes about grapes causing a traffic jam, a spider’s web, bright homework, mushroom soup, and a teddy bear being stuffed. He even says the dog pressed pause on the television. The child asks for no more puns, and Dad agrees. Later, the child thinks about Dad’s silly jokes and admits that some make them smile. Before bed, the child tells a dinosaur pun. Dad laughs proudly, and they say good night.

Dad’s favorite way to talk is with puns, and his child hears them from morning until bedtime. Dad jokes when the sun rises, when breakfast is served, and when the child leaves for school. At school, his jokes appear in science drawings and on an apple sticker. After school, Dad explains that grapes made him late because they caused a traffic jam. He jokes about a spider, homework, sunglasses, mushroom soup, a teddy bear, and the television remote. The child finally says that the puns are confusing and asks Dad to stop. Dad does not get upset. He rubs the child’s head and agrees. The family then plays a game without word jokes. In bed, the child remembers more of Dad’s jokes and decides that some are funny after all. The child makes a dinosaur joke about a “dino snore.” Dad smiles, praises the joke, and sends the child to sleep.

video_title: The Snail and the Whale by Julia Donaldson. Children's read-aloud story with illustrations.

summaries.summary: A tiny sea snail lived on a black rock with other snails, but she dreamed of seeing the wide world. One night, a great grey-blue humpback whale came near the rock. The snail left a silvery trail and climbed onto the whale’s tail. The whale carried her past icebergs, faraway lands, golden sand, caves, fish, sharks, waves, and storms. The snail saw many wonderful things, but she felt very small. One day, speedboats frightened the whale, and he became stuck on the shore when the tide went away. The whale could not move on land. The snail crawled to a school and wrote, “Save the whale,” with her silvery trail. The children called the firemen, who dug a pool and kept the whale cool. When the tide came back, the whale returned safely to the sea. The snail had saved him, and later many snails sailed on the whale’s tail.

A little snail wanted to travel around the world. Her fellow snails told her to stay on their smooth black rock, but she made a curly, silvery trail that said she wanted a ride. A huge humpback whale found her and invited her to sail. Together they traveled through wild seas. They saw tall icebergs, fiery mountains, golden sands, coral caves, stripy fish, sharks, sunny skies, and loud thunderstorms. Then speedboats raced nearby and made the whale swim too close to the shore. The tide slipped away, and the whale was left on the sand. He was too big to move, and the snail felt helpless. Then the snail had an idea. She crawled to a school and made a trail saying, “Save the whale.” The children brought firemen, who dug a pool and sprayed water. The tide came in, and the whale went safely back to sea.

The story begins with a tiny snail who gazes at ships and wishes to sail. A friendly humpback whale carries her on his tail across the sea. The snail sees ice, mountains, sand, waves, caves, fish, sharks, stars, and storms. She is amazed by the wide world, though she says she feels small. Later, racing speedboats disturb the whale, and he becomes stranded in a bay when the tide goes out. The whale cannot move because he is so large. The snail decides she must help. She crawls across a school board and leaves a shiny message: “Save the whale.” The children understand and run for help. Firemen dig a pool and spray water to keep the whale cool. Soon the tide returns, and the whale and snail travel safely away. Back at the rock, they tell their wonderful tale. The whale then carries many snails to sea.

video_title: 👏🏼👏🏼 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse : Mickey’s Handy Helpers

summaries.summary: Mickey and his friends came to the Clubhouse for dinner. The handy helpers were broken, so Mickey, Minnie, Goofy, Pluto, and Professor Vondre went to fix the handy dandy machine. First, they tightened loose bolts with shape wrenches. The machine started, but then it stopped. They put on a small gear, a medium gear, and a large gear. The gears moved a little, but they got stuck, and Goofy was caught between them. Shampoo made the gears slippery and helped Goofy get loose. Then a spring sent Goofy into the air, but a butterfly net caught him safely. Pluto found a squeaky blue ball under a heart-shaped gear. The mystery tool was a giant pair of toy tweezers, and it pulled out the ball. The machine worked again, so the handy helpers could help make veggie stew. Then everyone did the Muska Dance.

Everyone came to Mickey’s Clubhouse for dinner, but the handy helpers were not working. Mickey and his friends went downstairs to fix the handy dandy machine. Loose bolts were stopping the gears, so they used shape wrenches to tighten them. The machine turned on, but it stopped again. New small, medium, and large gears were added. The gears became stuck, and Goofy became stuck too. Shampoo made the gears slippery, and Goofy slipped free. A broken spring then sprung Goofy into the air. Minnie and the others caught him in a butterfly net. Pluto noticed a squeaky blue ball beneath a heart-shaped gear. The ball was making the strange squeaking sound and stopping the machine. A mystery tool, giant toy tweezers, pulled the ball out. The machine worked, and the handy helpers were ready to help make veggie stew.

Mickey, Minnie, Goofy, Pluto, and their friends wanted to have veggie stew for dinner. The handy helpers should help them, but every helper was broken. The friends found loose bolts on the handy dandy machine and tightened them with shape wrenches. They counted while Minnie turned the crank, and the machine began to work. Soon it stopped, so they changed the gears. A small gear, a medium gear, and a large gear were put on. The gears stuck, trapping Goofy. Shampoo helped him slide out. A spring suddenly sprang Goofy up into the air, and a butterfly net caught him before he hit the floor. Pluto found the real problem: his squeaky blue ball was under a heart-shaped gear. Giant toy tweezers pulled the ball out. The machine worked again, and all the handy helpers worked too. Now the helpers could help make dinner, and everyone did the Muska Dance.

video_title: 🧸 Kids Book Read Aloud: You're All My Favorites by Sam McBratney

summaries.summary: A mother bear, a father bear, and their three baby bears lived together. Their mother explained that their father had said the same thing when he first saw them. Later, each baby bear began to worry. The first thought the others might be nicer because they had patches. The second wondered if her father loved the others more because they were boys. The third worried because he was the littlest. That night, they asked their father who was his favorite. He told them they could all be the best. He hugged each bear and explained that patches, being a girl or boy, and being little made no difference. He loved all three just the same. The bears went to sleep happily, knowing they were all favorites.

Three baby bears often heard their mother say, “You’re the most wonderful baby bears in the whole wide world.” They asked how she knew. Their mother remembered that their father had said they were the nicest baby bears when he first saw them. The babies felt happy, but later each one had a worry. The first baby bear thought the others might be nicer because they had patches. The second baby bear wondered if her father loved the others more because they were boys. The third baby bear felt small because he was the littlest. At bedtime, the babies asked their father which one he liked most. Father Bear said they could all be the best. He called the first perfect even without patches, said being a girl or boy did not matter, and said the littlest bear was loved just the same. The three bears fell asleep happily.

A bear family had three baby bears: a first, a second, and a third. Their parents always told them they were wonderful. One night, the babies asked how their mother knew. She said their father had called them the nicest baby bears when they were born. Later, the babies started comparing themselves. The first noticed that the other bears had patches. The second worried because she was not a boy. The third worried because he was smaller than everyone else. They asked their father who was his favorite. Father Bear answered that all three could be the best. He cuddled the first and said patches did not matter. He hugged the second and said being a girl or boy made no difference. He lifted the third and said they loved him just the same, whether he was big or little. Then the three baby bears went to sleep happily because they were all favorites.

video_title: The Enormous Crocodile - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook

summaries.summary: The Enormous Crocodile lived in a muddy African river and wanted to eat children. Humpy Rumpy warned Toto and Mary, then knocked the crocodile away. Next, the crocodile pretended to be a seesaw, but Muggle-Wump warned the children. Trunky warned four children and grabbed the crocodile with his trunk. He swung the crocodile around and threw him high into the sky. The crocodile flew past the moon, stars, and planets before crashing into the hot sun. He was sizzled up like a sausage, and the children were safe.

A very large crocodile lived in the biggest, brownest, muddiest river in Africa. He was greedy and planned to eat little children. His friend, the smaller crocodile, said that children were tough and chewy, but the enormous crocodile bragged that he had clever tricks. As he traveled through the jungle, Humpy Rumpy the hippopotamus, Trunky the elephant, Muggle-Wump the monkey, and the Roly-Poly Bird all learned about his plan. The crocodile tried four disguises. He became a coconut tree, a seesaw, a wooden crocodile on a merry-go-round, and a picnic bench. Each time, one of the jungle animals warned the children. At last, Trunky caught the crocodile by his tail. He swung him faster and faster until he released him like a rocket. The crocodile flew into space and crashed into the sun. His hungry plans ended, and the children escaped.

The Enormous Crocodile wanted a lunch of juicy children, so he left his river and went toward the town. Muggle-Wump saw the danger and shouted for the children to run. At the fair, the crocodile hid between wooden animals and hoped to eat Jill. The Roly-Poly Bird flew down and warned her. The crocodile made one last plan at the picnic place. He looked like a long bench while four children approached with their food. Trunky the elephant rushed out and told them to stand back. He wrapped his trunk around the crocodile's tail and swung him through the air. The crocodile flew higher and higher, past the moon and stars, and crashed into the hot sun.

video_title: Aladdin Read Along Storybook in HD

summaries.summary: Aladdin is a poor boy who lives in Agrabah with his monkey, Abu. One day, he helps Princess Jasmine when she gets in trouble at the marketplace. Aladdin wishes to become a prince so he can marry Jasmine. Jafar steals the lamp and becomes a powerful sorcerer. He traps Jasmine and changes the Sultan into a puppet. Aladdin dreams of a better life, while Princess Jasmine wants freedom to make her own choices. They meet when Jasmine gives fruit to a hungry child and gets into trouble because she does not know she must pay. Aladdin leads her away safely, and they begin to care for each other. Jafar takes Aladdin to the Cave of Wonders to retrieve a magic lamp. Abu touches forbidden treasure, and the cave collapses. The magic carpet saves them, and Aladdin discovers the Genie inside the lamp. With the Genie’s help, Aladdin becomes a prince and visits Jasmine. Jafar later steals the lamp and uses its magic to trap Jasmine and control the palace. Aladdin challenges Jafar by reminding him that a genie has great power. Jafar becomes a genie and is trapped in a lamp. The Sultan lets Jasmine choose her husband. She chooses Aladdin, and Aladdin gives the Genie freedom.

video_title: Mr. Men book 44 Mr. Cool, children’s bedtime story read aloud in an English accent

summaries.summary: Jack Robinson is sick in bed and feels bored because he cannot go outside with his friends. Then a small blue man named Mr. Cool flies through the window and promises fun. Poor Jack Robinson has been ill in bed for days. He wishes he could play outside, but he is not allowed to leave his bed. Suddenly, Mr. Cool arrives through the open window. Mr. Cool clicks his fingers and takes Jack on exciting adventures. First, Jack flies a jet plane across the Atlantic Ocean and back. Then Jack goes to a football match, puts on the team strip, and scores the winning goal. Next, Mr. Cool takes him to Mount Everest. Jack and Mr. Cool sledge from the top of the mountain to the bottom. Finally, Jack returns to his bedroom. Mr. Cool tells him to look in the mirror before leaving. Jack Robinson is stuck in bed because he is unwell, and he is bored. A blue figure wearing a hat flies into his room. It is Mr. Cool, who thinks they should have fun. video_title: Are You My Monster? - Read Aloud Kids Book - A Bedtime Story with Dessi!

summaries.summary: A monster boy draws a picture of the monster he wants to find. The monster is green and brown, with sharp teeth, scratchy claws, and a long tail. The boy keeps looking, even though he wonders if he will ever find his monster. At last, he sees a green-and-brown monster with sharp teeth, scratchy claws, and a long tail. A little monster boy wants to find the monster in his drawing. He looks for three things: sharp teeth, scratchy claws, and a long tail. He also looks for a green-and-brown body. He says the monster is his, and then he goes to sleep.

The story begins with a monster boy showing the monster he drew. His picture has sharp teeth, scratchy claws, a long tail, and green-and-brown colors. The boy visits many monsters and checks each one carefully. Some have the right color but not the right teeth, claws, or tail. Some have claws and tails but no teeth. It is green and brown, just like the drawing. The boy is happy because every part matches. He says, “Yay! You are my monster!” After finding the monster, the boy can go to sleep. video_title: 🌬🛫 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Pixar Cars : Air Mater

Mater is a tow truck who wants to fly. He visits Prop Wash Junction and meets Skipper at a flight school. video_title: Mr. Men., Little Miss series book 30 Little Miss Somerset children’s bedtime story red aloud

summaries.summary: Little Miss Somersault is full of energy. She does not walk from place to place. She cartwheels instead, climbs over her roof, balances on chairs, and jumps over things. Little Miss Somersault is always somersaulting, cartwheeling, climbing, and jumping. She enjoys doing things differently from other people. video_title: Franklin Goes To The Hospital

Franklin had never been to a hospital before. One day, a soccer ball hits him in the chest. Dr. Bear discovers a crack in his shell and schedules an operation. video_title: Snow White 📚 Read Along Storybook 📖 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

One spring day, Snow White visited the seven dwarfs with a special plan. She knew the dwarfs worked hard, so she wanted them to come home to a clean cottage and a warm supper. Then Snow White and her friends made soup, bread, and a blueberry pie. A bluebird warned Snow White that the dwarfs were coming home, so she hid outside and watched through a window. The dwarfs were surprised by the tidy room and tasty food. They tried to guess who had helped them. After eating the pie, they went upstairs and found seven neat beds with fluffy pillows.
