Snow White lived in a castle with her prince, but she still visited the dwarfs whenever she could. One day, she brought her animal friends to help with a surprise. They cleaned the cottage from top to bottom. Snow White swept, the birds collected crumbs, the squirrels dusted, and the chipmunks and deer cleaned the dishes. The helpers made the beds, too. Snow White picked blueberries and made a pie. She and her friends also picked flowers and prepared soup and bread. Soon the dwarfs returned from work. Snow White hid outside while they looked around the cottage. The dwarfs saw the clean floors, the tidy room, the flowers, and the pie. They guessed that one of them had done the work, but they were wrong. After supper, the dwarfs found their beds ready. They fell asleep happily and planned to tell Snow White about the surprise.

video_title: Kids Read Aloud Books -🐸 Funny Story About Seeing Past Our Differences

summaries.summary: Frog was hiding in the leaves when he saw a juicy fly. Just as Frog tried to catch it, Toad’s tongue snapped out too. The two argued about who had seen the fly first, and the fly escaped. Frog and Toad then insulted each other, arguing about their bodies, hopping, eyes, strength, cleverness, and smell. Frog and Toad both wanted to eat a fly. When their tongues reached for it, they began arguing. Frog said he had seen the fly first, while Toad insisted he was not a slimy frog. They bragged about being clever and strong, then argued about whether frogs or toads smelled worse. Their bickering became louder until they started slinging mud. A frightening voice stopped them. An alligator told them that frogs and toads tasted the same to him, and he was hungry. Frog and Toad were surprised to learn that they were related. They decided that although they were different, they could both be right. After apologizing, they welcomed one another into the family. When they called the alligator a crocodile, he explained that alligators and crocodiles are completely different.

A hungry Frog hid among leaves and prepared to catch a juicy fly. Toad suddenly tried to catch the same fly, so the two animals blamed each other. Their argument drove the fly away. Frog and Toad continued squabbling as they compared their looks, hopping, eyes, strength, intelligence, and smell. They walked toward the swamp while boasting that their own kind was better. Frog finally threatened to stop talking unless Toad said another word, but their quarrel turned into mud-slinging. They were too busy fighting to notice an approaching animal. The animal revealed that he was hungry and that frogs and toads tasted the same to him. Frog and Toad were frightened, then recognized that they were related. They admitted that they could be different while both being right, apologized, and joined the family. At the end, the alligator corrected them when they called him a revolting crocodile.

video_title: 🌺 Encanto Family is Everything 🌺 Disney Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Mirabel Madrigal is kind, funny, and loves her family. She lives with her family in the magical Casita. Her sisters, Louisa and Isabella, have special gifts, but Mirabel does not. Mirabel loves her family, even though she has no magical gift. Her family lives in Casita, where Louisa is strong and Isabella makes flowers. video_title: The Apple pie Tree

Every year, a girl and her sister watch their apple tree change. In winter, it has no leaves and looks brown and bare. In spring, leaves grow, pink flowers appear, and two robins make a nest. A family watches an apple tree through all the seasons. The tree is brown and bare in winter. In spring, leaves grow on its branches, two robins build a nest, and tiny pink flower buds appear. The robins guard their eggs, and baby robins hatch when the buds open. Blossoms cover the tree as the babies grow feathers. Mama and Papa Robin teach them to fly. video_title: Paddington Set Sail (With Highlighted Words) Read Along: Cd Audio

summaries.summary: One morning, Mr. Brown surprised Paddington, Jonathan, and Judy by saying they were going to the beach. They find the plant’s roots and Captain Marvel trapped nearby. Fighting does not work, so Miss Marvel thinks of another idea. She tells Spectrum to use light because plants respond to light. Spectrum changes into light, and the frightened plant stops attacking. The heroes learn that the plant came from space and is searching for the things it needs to live. Captain Marvel says Miss Marvel saved the day. Then the three heroes plan to find the plant’s planet and help it go home.

One day, Captain Marvel and Miss Marvel answer an alarm in Jersey City. A huge alien plant has grown through the city. Captain Marvel cuts the vines, and Miss Marvel carries people away from danger. Then Miss Marvel notices that the plant is searching instead of hurting people. Captain Marvel keeps fighting, and the plant pulls her beneath the streets. Miss Marvel calls Captain Marvel’s friend Spectrum. Together, they follow strange vines to a reservoir and find Captain Marvel caught beside the plant’s roots. The plant attacks when Miss Marvel tries to help. Spectrum is ready to blast it, but Miss Marvel asks them to communicate instead. Spectrum turns into light, and the plant understands them. The heroes discover that it fell from space and wants the soil, water, and light from its own planet. Captain Marvel praises Miss Marvel for listening and solving the problem. The Marvels decide to use a device to find the plant’s planet, beginning a space mission.

video_title: The Little House by Virginia Lee Burton

summaries.summary: A little house lived happily on a hill in the country. She watched the sun, moon, stars, flowers, trees, children, and the changing seasons. The man who built her said she would stay for many generations. As the years passed, roads, cars, buildings, trains, and city lights came closer. The quiet countryside became a busy city. The little house felt lonely, dirty, and sad. She could hardly see the sun, moon, or stars. One spring day, the great great granddaughter of the builder saw the little house and recognized her. Movers lifted the house onto wheels and carried her away from the city. They found a green hill with grass and apple trees. The house was placed there, repaired, painted pink, and lived in again. She was happy to see the seasons and stars once more. She never wanted to live in the city again.

The Little House stood on a country hill and enjoyed every day. In spring, she watched robins, green grass, blossoms, gardens, and children playing. In summer, she saw leaves, daisies, apples, and children swimming. In fall, she watched colorful leaves, the harvest, and children returning to school. In winter, she watched children coast and skate. Then the country changed. Cars and roads appeared, followed by houses, stores, schools, tall buildings, trolley cars, elevated trains, and a subway. The city became noisy, smoky, and crowded. The little house became shabby and lonely, and she missed her hill and apple trees. A descendant of the builder found her and learned that she could still be moved. The house traveled back to the country. She was repaired, painted pink, and placed on a hill with apple trees. There she was happy again.

Long ago, a man built a strong little house in the country. The house loved watching the sunrise, sunset, moon, stars, and seasons. She was happy on her hill with daisies, apple trees, and children nearby. Years later, roads and cars came. More houses, stores, schools, trains, and tall buildings surrounded her. The city was noisy and bright, and the little house could no longer enjoy the countryside. She became dirty, broken, and very sad. Then the builder’s great great granddaughter stopped to look at her. She knew the little house belonged to her family. Movers lifted the house onto wheels and took her away from the city. They found a country hill surrounded by green grass and apple trees. The little house was placed on a new foundation. Her windows and shutters were fixed, and she was painted pink. She could once again watch the sun, moon, stars, and seasons. She was peaceful and happy in the country.

video_title: Christmas in the Big Woods by Laura Ingalls Wilder - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Laura lived with her family and their bulldog Jack in a little log house in the snowy Wisconsin woods. Christmas was coming, so Ma baked bread, apple pie, and cookies. Laura and Mary helped make candy from hot molasses syrup poured into snow. The day before Christmas, Aunt Eliza, Uncle Peter, and their children arrived in a big bobsled. Everyone played in the snow, then hung stockings by the fireplace and went to bed. On Christmas morning, Laura found red mittens, peppermint candy, and a beautiful rag doll with button eyes and a calico dress. She named the doll Charlotte. Ma made pancake people for breakfast. Since it was too cold to play outside, the children ate candy, admired their mittens, and looked at pictures in Paw’s green book. Then the cousins went home through the woods. Laura held Charlotte, and everyone remembered what a happy Christmas it had been.

In the snowy Big Woods, Laura lived in a small log house with Paw, Ma, Mary, Carrie, and Jack. Ma prepared many Christmas treats, including bread, pie, cookies, and molasses candy. Laura and Mary could eat one piece of candy, but the rest was saved for Christmas Day. Soon, Aunt Eliza, Uncle Peter, and their children came by sleigh. The house became full of happy children. They played in the deep snow until nighttime, then hung their stockings and went to sleep so Santa Claus would come. In the morning, the children found red mittens and peppermint sticks. Laura also received a rag doll and named her Charlotte. For breakfast, Ma made a pancake man for each child. The children stayed indoors because it was cold. They enjoyed their gifts and Paw’s picture book. When the visitors left in the bobsled, the sleigh bells faded away, and the wonderful Christmas ended.

Christmas brought lots of joy to Laura’s little house in the Big Woods. Her family made food and candy for the holiday. Laura and Mary poured hot sugar and molasses syrup into snow, where it quickly became candy. The next day, relatives arrived in a bobsled covered with blankets. Laura, Mary, and their cousins played outside in the soft snow, but later they put on nightgowns and hung their stockings. On Christmas morning, every child received red mittens and striped peppermint candy. Laura was especially happy because her stocking held a lovely rag doll. She called the doll Charlotte and shared her with the other children. Ma cooked pancake men for breakfast, and the children ate them at different speeds. They played quietly indoors, enjoyed their candy, and looked at Paw’s book. Finally, the relatives traveled home. Laura kept Charlotte in her arms, and the family’s happy Christmas came to an end.

video_title: Lady And The Tramp (With Highlighted Words) Read Along: Cd Audio

summaries.summary: On a frosty Christmas morning, Jim Dear gives Darling a Cocker Spaniel puppy. They name her Lady. Lady gets a blue collar and license, and her friends Jock and Trusty see how much her family loves her. Then a baby comes. Lady learns that there is room in the family for both the baby and the dog. While Lady’s owners travel, Aunt Sarah cares for the baby, but she does not like dogs. She puts a tight muzzle on Lady and takes her to the pet store. Lady escapes and meets Tramp, a dog without a home. Tramp helps Lady remove the muzzle, and they share spaghetti. Later, a dog catcher takes Lady to the pound. Tramp helps her escape, and Lady warns everyone about a rat near the baby. Lady’s family comes home, but the dog catcher takes Tramp away. Jock, Trusty, and Lady help. At Christmas, Tramp lives with Lady, and they have four puppies.

Lady is a loved puppy who lives with Jim Dear and Darling. She wears a blue collar and a license, and her friends Jock and Trusty admire her. When a baby joins the family, Lady worries that her people may not want her anymore, but she discovers that they love the baby and her. Aunt Sarah comes to care for the baby. She dislikes Lady and puts a muzzle on her. Lady runs away and meets Tramp, a friendly dog who has no collar, license, or home. Tramp takes Lady to a beaver, who bites off the muzzle. The two dogs eat spaghetti together. After a chicken chase, Lady is taken to the pound, but Tramp helps her. Lady then sees a rat near the baby. Tramp catches it, although Aunt Sarah misunderstands what happened. Lady’s family returns and searches for Tramp. Jock and Trusty help, and Tramp finally joins Lady’s family. They celebrate Christmas with four puppies.

Lady begins life as a Christmas puppy and soon becomes part of Jim Dear and Darling’s family. She receives a collar and license and enjoys being with Jock and Trusty. When the family has a baby, a stray dog named Tramp says that the baby will replace Lady, but Lady learns that this is not true. Aunt Sarah later puts a muzzle on Lady because she does not like dogs. Lady escapes and finds Tramp. A beaver removes the muzzle, and Lady and Tramp enjoy a special meal of spaghetti and meatballs. The next day, their fun with the chickens leads to trouble, and Lady is sent to the pound. Tramp visits her and helps her get away. Then Lady notices a rat entering the baby’s room. Tramp chases the rat away and protects the baby. Aunt Sarah does not understand and calls the dog catcher. Lady’s family comes home, while Jock and Trusty try to rescue Tramp. At Christmas, Tramp returns with Jock and Trusty. He now lives with Lady, and they have four puppies.

video_title: On the Road Peppa Pig | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Peppa Pig and her family find a golden ticket that sends them to America to make a movie with Super Potato and Hash Brown. First, they visit New York City. They see tall buildings, bright lights, and the Statue of Liberty. Then they drive in a motor home toward Hollywood. At a diner, they eat eggs, dance, and watch a monster truck jump over mud. In the desert, they find shells and visit the Grand Canyon. Peppa rides in a helicopter and a raft, then sees old drawings in caves. At last, Peppa reaches Hollywood and puts on a funny vegetable costume. Super Potato is filming a battle with naughty carrots, but he does not know how to finish the movie. Peppa has an idea. Everyone can eat the carrots. The universe and the movie are saved, and Peppa goes home happy after her big adventure.

Peppa has always wanted to see other places. One day, she finds a golden ticket, and she and her family win a trip to America. They fly to New York City and take a cab tour with Miss Rabbit. Peppa looks at tall buildings through a telescope and enjoys the colorful city lights. Then the family drives a long way across America in a motor home. They stop at a country diner, where they eat, dance, and watch a monster truck show. Next, they visit the Grand Canyon. Peppa learns that a river made the canyon long ago. She rides in a helicopter and a raft and sees pictures drawn on cave walls. Finally, Peppa arrives in Hollywood to make a movie. The carrots cause trouble in the movie, so Peppa suggests eating them. The plan works, and Peppa and her family return home after a wonderful trip.

A shiny golden ticket gives Peppa and her family a trip to America. Their movie will be made in Hollywood. They begin in New York City, where another Miss Rabbit shows them very tall buildings and bright lights. Peppa pretends to be the Statue of Liberty while holding her ice cream. The family then rents a motor home and travels through the large country. At a diner, they eat fresh eggs, dance to music, and watch Mr. Coyote drive a monster truck through mud. They continue through the desert and visit the Grand Canyon. Peppa learns about the river that made it and sees old cave drawings. After a long drive, she reaches the movie studio. In the film, Super Potato is fighting naughty carrots, but he cannot finish the story. Peppa says they can eat the carrots. All the Miss Rabbits help, the universe is saved, and Peppa says the whole visit was the best part.

video_title: A Little Spot of ANXIETY

summaries.summary: A peaceful green spot explains that an anxiety spot appears when someone feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It may ask questions like, “What if I am bad at soccer?” or “What if I fail?” Children can answer, “I can do this.” Small worries can sometimes protect us, but too many worries can cause a tummy ache, sweating, or missed fun. Healthy food, plenty of rest, drawing, music, and writing can help. The peaceful spot then teaches a calming trick. Children imagine gray worry spots on their fingers, draw a line toward the green spot in their palm, and say, “I can do this. I can be calm.” Then they take a deep breath and blow the worry away. They practice this on the first day of school and at a party. Each time they shrink the anxiety spot, their peaceful spot grows stronger.

The story teaches children about a gray anxiety spot and a green peaceful spot. The anxiety spot can grow when children try something new, take a test, meet people, attend a party, or stay away from their parents or guardian. It may make them feel scared, worried, or nervous, and it can even cause a tummy ache or sweating. The story says that healthy eating and rest help prevent big worries. Art, music, and writing can also help children express their worries. When anxiety grows quickly, children can imagine gray spots on their fingers and a green spot in their palm. They draw an imaginary line to the green spot while saying, “I can do this. I can be calm.” Then they breathe deeply and blow the worry away. Practicing this helps the peaceful spot become stronger and gives children confidence in new situations.

A little peaceful green spot shows how to handle an anxiety spot. Worry may appear when a child plays soccer for the first time, takes a test, starts school, meets new people, or goes to a party. The worry asks, “What if?” and can become so large that the child feels bad or misses enjoyable things. The story explains that rest and healthy food give the body energy, while drawing, music, and writing help express worries. To calm down, a child imagines five gray spots on the fingers and one green spot in the palm. The child moves an imaginary line from a gray spot to the green spot and says, “I can do this. I can be calm.” Next, the child takes a deep breath and blows the worry away. After practicing at school and at a party, the child says, “I can do this,” and feels more confident.

video_title: The Leaf Thief & The Snow Thief 🍂❄️ | Read Aloud Compilation for Kids | Reading with Rollin

summaries.summary: Squirrel enjoys the colorful leaves around her nest, but then one leaf is missing. She asks Bird and Mouse if someone stole it. More leaves disappear, and Squirrel becomes worried. Bird shows her that the wind shakes the trees and carries the leaves away. Squirrel learns that leaves change color in autumn and grow back in spring. When winter arrives, snow covers the grass. Bird teaches Squirrel about snowballs, snowflakes, cold breath, and ice. Squirrel has fun playing and skating, but she notices that her hidden hazelnuts are gone. Bird explains that the other squirrel was only made of snow. The next morning, all the snow has disappeared. Squirrel decides there really is a snow thief. She follows the clues and finds that the snow squirrel took the snow, but it forgot to take Squirrel’s hazelnuts.

Squirrel thinks a leaf thief is stealing the leaves from her tree. She asks Bird and Mouse, but neither one took anything. Bird explains that losing leaves is normal in autumn. Soon Squirrel sees the wind shaking trees and blowing leaves away, so she understands that there is no leaf thief. In winter, snow falls and covers the grass. Bird shows Squirrel how to play with snowballs and skate on frozen puddles. Squirrel even meets another squirrel, but Bird explains that it is only a snow squirrel. Squirrel then discovers that her hazelnuts are missing and wonders if the snow squirrel took them. The next day, the snow is gone. This time Squirrel believes there is a snow thief. She finds the snow squirrel’s trail and learns that it carried away the snow, while leaving her hazelnuts behind.

Squirrel is happy in her leafy nest until she notices that leaves are missing. She worries that a thief is taking them, but Bird teaches her that autumn wind blows the leaves away. Squirrel feels calm again. Later, snow covers the grass and makes everything white and cold. At first Squirrel stays in her tree, but she soon learns to enjoy snowball fights, snowflakes, and skating. While skating, she bumps into a snow squirrel. She also finds that her hidden hazelnuts are gone. Bird reminds her that the snow squirrel is not real because it is made of snow. The following morning, Squirrel wants to play in the snow, but all the snow has vanished. She thinks a snow thief took it. Squirrel discovers that the snow squirrel disappeared during the night and carried away the snow. However, the snow thief left Squirrel’s hazelnuts behind.

video_title: 🐓 Interrupting Chicken

summaries.summary: At bedtime, Papa reads a story to Little Red Chicken. She promises not to interrupt, but she quickly jumps into the story about Hansel and Gretel. When a witch invites the children inside her candy house, Chicken warns them not to go in. Papa says she interrupted and asks her to try again. In the next story, Little Red Riding Hood meets a wolf. Chicken interrupts again and tells her not to talk to strangers. Papa says Chicken has interrupted two stories, but Chicken explains that the wolf was mean. Papa tries one more story about Chicken Little, who thinks the sky is falling after an acorn hits her. Chicken interrupts and says not to panic because it was only an acorn. Finally, Papa says there are no more stories. Chicken tells Papa a bedtime story, reads many stories, gives him warm milk, and helps him fall asleep.

Little Red Chicken is ready for bed, and Papa begins reading Hansel and Gretel. Chicken promises to be good, but she interrupts when an old witch invites Hansel and Gretel into her candy house. Chicken says they should not go inside. Papa reminds her that she interrupted. He then reads Little Red Riding Hood. A wolf meets Red Riding Hood in the woods, and Chicken interrupts again to warn her not to talk to strangers. Papa says Chicken is still not sleepy. For the last story, Papa reads about Chicken Little, who is frightened when an acorn hits her and thinks the sky is falling. Chicken interrupts once more and says it was only an acorn. She asks for another story, but Papa says he is out of stories. Then Chicken tells Papa a story about a little red chicken who reads to her father and gives him warm milk until he finally sleeps.

Papa wants Little Red Chicken to sleep, so he reads three bedtime stories. In Hansel and Gretel, the children find a candy house, and a witch asks them to come inside. Chicken interrupts to protect them. In Little Red Riding Hood, a wolf meets Red Riding Hood in the woods. Chicken interrupts again and says not to talk to strangers because the wolf is mean. In Chicken Little, an acorn hits Chicken Little, and she thinks the sky is falling. Chicken interrupts a third time and tells her not to panic. Papa says there are no more stories. Chicken says she cannot sleep without one, so Papa asks her to tell a story. Chicken tells about a little red chicken who puts Papa to bed, reads him one hundred stories, and gives him warm milk. Nothing helps at first because Papa stays awake. At last, Chicken says good night, and Papa can sleep.

video_title: Travis the Troll and the Three Goats Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Travis was a troll who graduated from troll academy. He was chosen to protect the cemetery of the fallen trolls and the beautiful mountain. The trolls believed the green fields showed that the fallen warriors were pleased. Travis guarded the only bridge to the mountain. One day, three hungry goat brothers planned to take the mountain because they wanted its green grass and food. First, little Blinky tried to cross, but Travis hit him with his club and sent him back. Then Brighty made a plan. He told Travis that their biggest brother, Buffy, would come for a fight. Buffy arrived with many forest animals. Travis threw Buffy and Blinky away when they attacked together. But Brighty came from behind and knocked Travis over the bridge into the rushing river. The three goats believed Travis had been washed away, and they returned to the forest.

In a faraway mountain village, civilized trolls trained to be warriors. Travis was the best student, so he became the protector of the luscious mountain. The mountain could be reached only by crossing a bridge over a deep, dangerous river. Travis was brave and carefully watched the bridge. In a nearby forest lived three goat brothers who ate all the grass and food wherever they went. They wanted the mountain too. Little Blinky went first, but Travis stopped him with his club. Brighty then spoke to Travis and promised that his older brother would come to fight. The next day, Buffy arrived with Blinky, Brighty, and many forest animals. Buffy charged, but Travis caught his horns and tossed him back. Blinky and Buffy attacked together, yet Travis knocked them away. Brighty then surprised Travis and bucked him into the rapids. The goats stood on the mountain while Travis fell.

Travis felt proud when the troll academy chose him to protect the mountain. The trolls cared about the green fields around it and believed the fields honored fallen warriors. Travis guarded the bridge across the dangerous river. Meanwhile, three goat brothers were searching for more land and food. They had already eaten the land around an old farm, so they planned to conquer the luscious mountain. Blinky, the smallest goat, rushed at Travis, but Travis struck him with a club. Brighty tried a clever plan. He told Travis that Buffy, their older brother, would fight for the mountain. Buffy came with a large group of forest animals. Travis used his training to defeat Buffy and Blinky when they attacked him together. Then Brighty secretly came from the side. He lowered his head and bucked Travis over the bridge. Travis fell into the rapid waters, while the goats celebrated and went back to the forest.

video_title: 🔠 Take Away the A

summaries.summary: This playful alphabet story shows what happens when one letter disappears from a word. Without A, a beast becomes the best. Without B, a bride goes for a ride. Without C, a chair has hair, and without D, dice become ice. Bears stay behind bars when E is gone, while a scarf hides a scar without F. A glove falls in love without G, and three climb a tree without H. Stairs lead to stars without I, and jam becomes “I am” without J. The word games continue: a monkey makes money, plants wear pants, and a farm is too far. The moon says moo, four wear fur, and a plate is late. A figure goes to the fair, a crab hails a cab, and snow falls now. Boats carry boas, an aunt is an ant, seven are seen, and a witch has an itch. Foxes are foes, yours is ours, and without Z, the children cannot sing their ABCs.

The story is an alphabet game made from funny word changes. Each part removes one letter and creates a new sentence. When A is taken away, the beast becomes the best. Removing B lets the bride go for a ride, while removing C gives a chair some hair. Without D, dice become ice, and without E, bears stay behind bars. A scarf hides a scar when F is gone. A glove falls in love without G, and three climb a tree without H. Later, stairs lead to stars, jam becomes “I am,” and a monkey makes money. Plants wear pants, a farm is too far, and the moon says moo. Four wear fur, a plate is late, and a crab hails a cab. Boats carry boas, an aunt is an ant, and a witch has an itch. Foxes are foes, yours is ours, and losing Z means the ABC song cannot be sung.

A parade of alphabet letters disappears one at a time, making familiar words sound surprising. The beast becomes the best when A is removed. A bride goes for a ride without B, and a chair has hair without C. Dice turn into ice when D is missing. Bears stay behind bars, a scarf hides a scar, and a glove falls in love as E, F, and G disappear. Three climb a tree, stairs lead to stars, and jam sounds like “I am.” Then a monkey makes money, plants wear pants, and the farm is too far. The moon says moo, four wear fur, and the plate is too late. A figure goes to the fair, a crab hails a cab, and snow falls now. Boats carry boas, an aunt is an ant, seven are seen, and a witch has an itch. Foxes are foes, yours is ours, and without Z, the ABCs cannot be sung.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Embarks On A Wild West Adventure

summaries.summary: Mickey packed his suitcase because he and his friends were going to the Lucky Star Dude Ranch. Mickey wanted to learn to ride a horse. Goofy wanted to ride and twirl a lasso. At the ranch, Goofy sat on a horse backward. The horse bucked, so Goofy held its tail. Minnie used a carrot to help the horse come closer. Cowboy Bob taught the friends how to ride. Mickey and Minnie practiced riding, while Goofy practiced his lasso. Goofy caught his own foot with the lasso and fell down. On rodeo day, Mickey forgot to set his alarm. He hurried to the rodeo and landed on a bucking bronco. He rode so well that he broke the ranch record. Goofy tried to lasso the bronco, but he lassoed Mickey instead. Minnie, Mickey, and Goofy all received ribbons. Later, Goofy wanted to lasso a coyote, but everyone laughed and said no.

Mickey and his friends went to a ranch to learn cowboy skills. Mickey wanted to ride a horse, and Goofy wanted to twirl a lasso. When Goofy first arrived, he jumped onto a horse backward. The horse bucked and moved in circles. Minnie held out a carrot, and the horse came to her. Then Cowboy Bob showed everyone how to ride. Mickey and Minnie practiced riding. Goofy practiced with his lasso, but the rope caught his own foot and made him fall. On the big rodeo day, Mickey was asleep because he forgot his alarm. He woke up, ran outside, and jumped onto a bucking bronco. The crowd cheered as he held on. Mickey broke the ranch record for the longest bronco ride. Goofy tried to help, but he lassoed Mickey. At the end, Minnie, Mickey, and Goofy each won a rodeo ribbon.

At the Lucky Star Dude Ranch, Mickey, Minnie, and Goofy learned about horses and rodeos. Mickey was excited to ride. Goofy was excited to use a lasso. Goofy made a funny mistake when he climbed onto a horse backward. The horse bucked, and Goofy held its tail. Minnie saved him with a carrot. Cowboy Bob gave the friends riding lessons. Mickey and Minnie learned quickly. Goofy practiced his lasso, but it caught his foot instead of a horse. Soon the rodeo began. Mickey had forgotten to set his alarm, so he rushed to the show. He jumped over a fence and landed on a bucking bronco. The people cheered, and Mickey rode longer than anyone at the ranch before him. Goofy tried to lasso the bronco, but he caught Mickey. Minnie won a ribbon for caring for the horses, Mickey won for riding, and Goofy won for trying. They laughed beside the fire.

video_title: Gratitude is my Superpower | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Betsy is seven years old and loves her turtle, Mr. T, who is seventy. Betsy worries that his big shell keeps him from having fun, but her mother explains that turtles are quiet, shy animals who are happy with what they have. Mom gives Betsy a gratitude stone and teaches her to hold it when she feels upset. When rain ruins Betsy’s outdoor plans, she remembers that rain helps plants grow, fish live, and rivers flow. Before school, the stone helps her feel thankful for her friends and teacher. At school, Betsy is grateful for Mr. T when she has no sibling to talk about. She also feels thankful for her healthy dinner, warm bed, turtle pajamas, and family. Later, Betsy helps a new boy feel better by sharing the stone. He becomes thankful for his spacious new home. Betsy learns that gratitude is in everyone’s heart and can make people happier.

Betsy notices that Mr. T, her seventy-year-old turtle, moves slowly and never seems to run or jump. She worries that he is unhappy, but her mother explains that turtles have different needs and enjoy hiding in their shells. Mom gives Betsy a special stone for practicing gratitude. Betsy uses it when rain stops her from playing outside and remembers that rain helps nature. She squeezes it before school and thinks about her friends and Mrs. Blaine, her teacher. During sibling day, Betsy cannot talk about a brother or sister, so she says she is thankful for Mr. T. She also finds reasons to appreciate a simple meal, her turtle pajamas, and her cozy bed. When a new boy cries because he moved, Betsy shares her gratitude idea. He thinks of his large garden and smiles. Betsy and her family discover that noticing what they have helps them feel happier.

Betsy learns that gratitude can change the way she feels. Her mother tells her that Mr. T is not sad because turtles are naturally quiet and content. She gives Betsy a stone to hold whenever something goes wrong. Betsy first uses it when rain keeps her indoors. Instead of staying upset, she thanks the rain because it helps plants, fish, and rivers. She uses the stone again before school and remembers her friends and teacher. On sibling day, she is thankful to have Mr. T. At dinner, she appreciates having a warm, healthy meal, even though it is not cake. At bedtime, she is grateful for her pajamas and bed, and then discovers she can practice gratitude without the stone. The next day, she helps a new classmate who misses his old home. He finds something good about his new home. Betsy begins carrying stones to share gratitude with others.

video_title: 🌱 You Belong Here

summaries.summary: The stars, moon, winds, whales, fish, trees, birds, frogs, turtles, and many other creatures each have a special place where they belong. The child belongs where they feel loved and at home. After every day, the child can be right next to the person who loves them. In the desert, hares, foxes, lizards, crickets, and bees belong among rocks, hills, light, walls, and clover. Winter also has its place after fall. The child is part of the world’s song and is here in the place meant for them. Pines belong on snowy mountains, and bears belong in caves during storms. Every creature is whole in its own place, whether it lives on land, in the air, or in the sea. Wherever the child travels and whatever wonders they see, they will always belong with the person who loves them.

The story shows many things living in places that fit them. Stars and the moon belong in the night sky. Whales and fish belong in the sea, birds belong in nests, and deer belong in the shade of trees. Frogs, lilies, turtles, and other creatures belong near lakes and streams. The child also belongs in a loving home, close to the person who cares for them. In the desert, hares belong among red and gold rocks, foxes belong in canyon hills, and lizards rest in the warm light. Crickets belong in old stone walls, and bees belong in clover. The child is called a dream that the world once dreamed and is now part of its song. Pines belong on snowy mountains, and bears hide in caves when storms blow. Every creature has a place, and the child will always belong with their loved one.

The world is full of places where living things belong. The moon and stars belong in the sky, waves belong by the shore, grasses belong among the dunes, and birds belong in warm nests. The child belongs where they are loved and held close. Frogs and lilies belong in a clear lake, turtles belong in sandy homes near water, and creatures of the stream belong along its banks. Hares, foxes, lizards, crickets, and bees each have their own desert or woodland places. Winter comes after fall, and pines cover the mountains under snow. Bears hide in caves when storms begin. Some creatures are made for land, some for air, and some for the sea, but each is whole in the place it belongs. The child belongs in the world and always belongs with the person who loves them.

video_title: Giraffe and a Half | Being Different is Special

summaries.summary: Giraffe was a giraffe and a half. She had six legs and three ears, which helped her listen to bird song and crunch leaves. But Giraffe felt different, so she played alone beneath a tree. One day, a bird with three wings and three legs found her. Bird had many friends and asked why Giraffe was alone. Giraffe said she was too different. Bird sang that having extra legs or ears did not make her strange, and that she should be proud and brave. Giraffe watched Bird dance with his friends and joined them. When other animals stared, Giraffe froze, but Bird told her to keep dancing. The elephant asked to join, and soon everyone danced and sang together. Giraffe played with her new friends all afternoon. She realized they were not thinking about her extra legs and ears. Giraffe knew she was different, but she would never have to play alone again.

Giraffe had six legs and three ears. She liked listening to birds and crunching leaves, but she worried that she was weird. Because of this, she went out to play by herself. While hiding beneath a tree, she was found by Bird, who had three wings and three legs. Bird had lots of friends and wondered why Giraffe was alone. Giraffe explained that nobody wanted to play with her because she was different. Bird sang that extra legs and ears were not reasons to hide. He showed Giraffe that being different could be wonderful. Giraffe joined Bird and his friends in dancing and singing. She became nervous when other animals watched, but Bird encouraged her to continue. Then the elephant asked to join. Everyone played together for the afternoon. Giraffe stopped worrying about her unusual body because her new friends were busy enjoying games with her. She learned she could be different and still have friends.

A lonely Giraffe had six legs and three ears, so she believed she was too different to play with others. She hid beneath a beautiful tree and played hide-and-seek alone. Then Bird found her. Bird had three wings and three legs, yet he was surrounded by friends. He asked Giraffe why she was alone. Bird sang that more legs, more ears, and hiding away did not matter. He told her to show herself to the world and be proud, strong, brave, and bold. Giraffe saw Bird dancing and singing and joined in. When other animals stared, she became frightened, but Bird told her to keep dancing. The elephant asked to join, and all the animals danced and sang together. Giraffe spent the whole afternoon playing favorite games with her new friends. She realized that her friends were not focused on her extra legs and ears. Giraffe was still different, but she no longer had to play alone.

video_title: Arthur's New Puppy Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Arthur loved his new puppy, Pal, and wanted to train him, even though Pal was very active and naughty. Pal did not like staying in the garage, so Mother let him sleep in the house for a few days. Pal made messes, ate quickly, played at night, and destroyed the living room. Arthur’s parents decided Pal should move to the garage, but the garage key disappeared. Arthur’s friends told him that puppies could be hard to train. Arthur kept trying and taught Pal to sit, lie down, stay, and do tricks. He planned a puppy show to prove that Pal could behave. Pal performed well, so the family decided he could stay in the house. Then Pal found the missing garage key behind the rose bushes. Later, Arthur could not find Pal’s leash, and nobody noticed Pal run behind the rose bushes again.

Arthur was happy to have a new puppy named Pal. He made Pal a home in the garage, but Pal hid there, so Mother allowed him inside. Pal was difficult to care for. He got excited, ate his food very fast, ran away from his leash, cried during the night, and made a mess in the kitchen. He also ruined Mother’s drapes and DW’s doll. The family thought Pal might have to live in the garage or on a farm. Arthur wanted to save him, so he began training Pal with kindness. Every day, Arthur practiced a new lesson. Soon Pal could sit, lie down, stay, and perform tricks. At the puppy show, Pal behaved well, and the family said he could remain in the house. Pal then returned the missing garage key. When Arthur later searched for his leash, Pal quietly ran behind the rose bushes again.

Pal was Arthur’s new puppy, and Arthur cared about him very much. At first, Pal caused many problems. He disliked the garage, so he stayed in the kitchen. He made a mess, woke the family at night, and tore up things in the living room. Mother and Father decided he should move to the garage, but the family could not find the key. Arthur’s friends explained that other puppies had also been too much trouble. Arthur did not give up. He taught Pal with love instead of using a whip. They practiced sitting, lying down, staying, and doing tricks. Arthur held a puppy show for the family. Pal followed the commands and impressed everyone, so he did not have to live in the garage or on a farm. Then Pal brought back the missing key. However, when Arthur looked for the leash, Pal disappeared behind the rose bushes again.

video_title: Otto's Tales: From Sea to Shining Sea  | PragerU Kids

summaries.summary: Ellis the elephant wanted to learn how America became one nation from sea to shining sea. He learned that George Washington became the first president, and that Washington, D.C., was built as the nation's capital. Thomas Jefferson became president and bought the Louisiana Purchase, making the country much bigger. Jefferson sent Meriwether Lewis and William Clark to explore the new land. Their team, the Corps of Discovery, traveled for more than two years. Sacagawea and her husband helped them speak with tribes and cross the Great Plains. The explorers faced cold weather, mountains, rivers, and a frightening grizzly bear. Their friends, the Nez Perce, taught them to make canoes. At last, they reached the Pacific Ocean and later returned home. Settlers moved west, new states joined the Union, and Robert Fulton invented the steamboat. Wagon trains carried pioneers toward new frontiers. Ellis saw how courage, freedom, and exploration helped America grow.

Ellis the elephant read about the growing United States. George Washington led the American Revolution and became the first president. A capital city called Washington, D.C., was founded, and President John Adams lived there with Abigail in the White House. Later, Thomas Jefferson bought the Louisiana Purchase from France. The land made America twice as big, so Jefferson asked Lewis and Clark to explore it. The Corps of Discovery trained in Illinois and traveled west. The explorers made maps, studied plants and animals, and celebrated Independence Day. Sacagawea and her husband joined them and helped them communicate with tribes. The explorers spent a cold winter near the Mandans, saw a grizzly bear, and learned to build dugout canoes from the Nez Perce. They reached the Pacific and returned home. Then settlers moved west and new states joined the Union. Steamboats and wagon trains helped people travel, carry goods, and find new homes.

Ellis learned that America grew through many brave choices. The people chose George Washington as their first president and built Washington, D.C., as the capital. Thomas Jefferson bought a huge area called the Louisiana Purchase. To learn about the new land, Jefferson sent Meriwether Lewis and William Clark with a team called the Corps of Discovery. They traveled through forests, plains, mountains, and rivers. They wrote notes, made maps, and studied new animals. Sacagawea helped the explorers talk with tribes, and her husband traveled with them. The team stayed in a fort during a very cold North Dakota winter. They met the Mandans and later learned canoe-building from the Nez Perce. After seeing the Pacific Ocean, they began the long trip home. Settlers followed, forming new territories and states. Robert Fulton’s steamboat helped carry people and goods on rivers, while wagon trains carried pioneers west. Ellis understood that freedom and courage helped unite a growing nation.

video_title: Beauty and the Beast Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Belle's Friendship Invention

summaries.summary: Belle goes with her father, Maurice, to the town’s first invention convention. While Maurice sets up, Belle explores the busy square and looks at many clever inventions. She sees Simone, a girl her age, showing a Blue Ribbon-winning machine. The machine presses leaves into paper, so Belle helps Simone test it. The machine suddenly makes a strange sound and produces many sheets of paper. Simone feels embarrassed, but Belle helps gather the paper. Belle suggests writing messages that will make people smile. Together, the girls write notes and secretly give one to the florist and one to the bookseller. Then they give a final note to Maurice. Maurice reads, “Smile, you are loved.” At the end of the day, the convention closes. Belle says goodbye while Simone packs her invention. That night, Belle opens her book and knows her new friendship with Simone will last.

Today is the invention convention, and Belle visits it with her father, Maurice. The town square is full of inventions. Belle meets Simone, who is demonstrating a machine that turns leaves into paper. Simone asks Belle to put leaves into the machine. Belle does so, and Simone pushes a red button. One piece of paper comes out, but then the machine makes a strange sound and spits out many pieces. When there are no leaves left, the machine stops. Simone worries about all the paper. Belle helps her collect it and has an idea. The girls write kind messages on the sheets. They give a note to the florist, another to the bookseller, and one to Maurice. Maurice reads the note aloud: “Smile, you are loved.” Simone packs up at day’s end, and Belle knows their friendship will last.

Belle is excited about the first annual invention convention. She explores the town square and finds Simone, a girl her age, surrounded by people. Simone has won a Blue Ribbon for her invention. Her machine is meant to press leaves into smooth paper. Belle volunteers to help. She places leaves inside, and Simone presses a red button. At first, the invention works. Then it makes a strange sound and produces many pieces of paper. Simone feels embarrassed because she does not know what to do with it all. Belle kindly gathers the paper and suggests using it to write messages. The two girls sit under a tree and write notes to make people smile. They deliver notes to the florist, the bookseller, and Maurice. Maurice reads, “Smile, you are loved.” After the convention, Belle and Simone part, but Belle knows their friendship will continue.

video_title: PICKLE-CHIFFON PIE read aloud by Mrs. K. | A Children’s Story about Kindness and Compassion

summaries.summary: A kind princess had many princes visit her, and each dinner meant less pickle chiffon pie for her father, the king. The king chose three princes to compete for the princess’s hand. Musclebalm searched the forest and brought back a juggling lion. Wellred found a giant who could play chopsticks on two pianos. Bernard found a three-nosed snozzle making pickle chiffon pie. Bernard began taking the snozzle to the castle, but then he saw its little children crying behind the trees. He realized they would be alone without their parent. Bernard cared more about the snozzle’s family than winning the contest, so he let the snozzle go and returned empty-handed. Musclebalm and Wellred showed the king their marvelous discoveries. Bernard told the king why he had brought back nothing. The king learned that Bernard had shown kindness, love, and care for others. He chose Bernard to marry the princess. At the wedding, the lion entertained everyone, the giant played music, and the snozzle sent the newlyweds a huge pickle chiffon pie.

Long ago, a wise king and his queen lived in a happy kingdom. The queen made the king a pickle chiffon pie every day. The princess was beautiful and kind, so many princes visited her. When she invited them to dinner, the king had less pie. He decided that three princes would search a magical forest, and the one who found the most wonderful thing could marry the princess. Musclebalm found a three-headed dragon, a glasses-wearing demduzzle, and a lion juggling root beer soup. Wellred found a clever witch, a many-footed gazoo, and a giant playing two pianos. Bernard found a three-nosed snozzle making pie. He started bringing it home, but he saw the snozzle’s children and understood that they needed their parent. Bernard released the snozzle and returned with nothing. The king was pleased by the other discoveries, but Bernard explained his choice. The king said Bernard had brought back kindness and love, so Bernard won the princess. The snozzle later sent them a giant wedding pie.

The king wanted his daughter to marry one of three princes, so he gave them a forest challenge. They had three days to bring back something unusual and wonderful. Musclebalm was strong and brave. He found a three-headed dragon, a demduzzle with glasses, and a lion wearing a velvet vest and roller skates while juggling six cans of root beer soup. Wellred was very smart. He found a witch with a special frog-changing trick, a seven-plus-footed gazoo with different shoes, and a giant with a green beard playing chopsticks on two pianos. Bernard was not the strongest or smartest, but the princess liked him best. He found a snozzle with three noses, fuzzy ears, and a polka-dotted tie making the queen’s special pie. Bernard thought this would win, but he saw the snozzle’s children and felt sorry for them. He let the snozzle return to them. Although Bernard came back empty-handed, the king chose him because he had shown kindness and consideration. Bernard married the princess, and the snozzle sent them a giant pie.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝘕𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵𝘣𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘴 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Alex sneaks out of his apartment at night with a backpack full of stories he plans to burn in the basement boiler. The elevator takes him to the wrong floor, where he hears a favorite horror movie coming from a stranger’s apartment. A woman named Natasha invites him inside with the promise of the movie, cookies, and pumpkin pie. Once Alex enters, the television and food disappear, the door vanishes, and Natasha reveals that she is a real witch. Alex wakes in a magical room connected to endless identical rooms. He cannot escape, and no one outside can hear him. A mysterious girl briefly tells him that Natasha likes stories. When Natasha returns, Alex tries to attack her but is stopped by magic. He saves himself by offering to tell a story from one of his night books. Natasha listens to “Lost Dog,” a frightening tale about a dog that appears before people die. She decides Alex’s stories are useful and locks him away until tomorrow, when his real work will begin.

After his family falls asleep, Alex leaves home to destroy the strange stories he has written. He accidentally exits the elevator on the fourth floor and is drawn to an apartment playing Night of the Living Dead. Natasha, a mysterious woman, uses the movie and the smell of pumpkin pie to lure him inside. She is a witch, and her enchanted apartment removes the door and traps Alex in a repeating maze of rooms. Alex discovers children’s clothes in a closet and worries that other children may have been captured before him. He screams for help, but the apartment blocks every sound. A girl outside only whispers that Natasha likes stories. Alex plans to surprise Natasha, but magic throws him to the floor. Before Natasha can use another spell, Alex offers to read from his backpack. He tells “Lost Dog,” about a supernatural white dog whose appearances come before deaths. Natasha is impressed enough to keep Alex alive as a storyteller, though she locks him up for the night.

Alex believes he is not brave, but being trapped by a witch forces him to act. Natasha explains that she sells magic oils and intends to use Alex for her collection if he is not useful. She begins preparing a spell, so Alex quickly mentions that he writes scary stories in journals called night books. Natasha agrees to hear one. Alex reads about Greg, who sees a white dog with a black triangular tag before his friend Eric dies in a fire. Later, the same dog appears before Renee Wilson dies in her sleep. Greg eventually sees the dog at the top of a new roller coaster and realizes that disaster is coming, but he cannot stop the ride. Natasha questions whether Alex really wrote the story. Alex explains that he invented it by wondering whether the Grim Reaper might have a pet. Natasha seems pleased by his imagination. She listens at the wall, decides his stories will be useful, and tells him to sleep. Before leaving, she says that his real work will begin the next day.

video_title: I Must Have Bobo! by Eileen Rosenthal - Read Aloud Storybooks for Kids

summaries.summary: When Willie wakes up, he cannot find Bobo. Willie says that he needs Bobo because Bobo helps him with everything. Bobo is brave on the slide and holds Willie’s hand when they walk past a big dog. Willie looks for Bobo while he sees a buddy bug and then Earl. At breakfast, Bobo expects pancakes, but Bobo does not like raisins in oatmeal. Willie and Bobo color a house blue. Then Willie asks Earl to build a fort, but Earl cannot come in. Soon, Bobo is missing again. Willie wonders if pirates or Earl took Bobo. He asks Earl if Bobo is inside. Willie calls, “Bobo! Earl!” At last, Willie finds Bobo and says, “Here’s my Bobo.”

Willie’s day begins with a problem: Bobo is not where Willie expects him to be. Willie needs Bobo for many things. Bobo goes down the slide, holds Willie’s hand near a big dog, and comes with Willie to breakfast. Bobo thought they would eat pancakes, but Bobo does not like raisins in oatmeal. Bobo likes coloring, so Willie colors a house blue. Later, Willie wants to build a fort with Earl, but Earl cannot come inside. Then Willie notices that Bobo is gone. He searches and asks whether pirates or Earl may have taken Bobo. Willie asks Earl if Bobo is in there and calls for both Bobo and Earl. Finally, Willie finds Bobo. The story ends when Willie happily says, “Here’s my Bobo.”

Willie is worried when he wakes up and cannot see Bobo. He says Bobo helps him with everything. Bobo is not afraid to go down the slide, and Bobo holds Willie’s hand as they pass a big dog. Willie and Bobo go to breakfast, where Bobo thought there would be pancakes. Bobo does not like raisins in oatmeal, but Bobo likes coloring. Willie says that the house will be blue. Willie then wants to build a fort with Earl, although Earl cannot come in. After that, Willie asks where Bobo is. He wonders if Bobo was stolen by pirates or by Earl. Willie checks with Earl and repeats their names while searching. At the end, Willie finds Bobo and says, “Here’s my Bobo.”

video_title: Amos and Boris

summaries.summary: Amos was a little mouse who loved the ocean. He built a boat called the Rodent, filled it with food and tools, and sailed away to see the world. At first, he became seasick, but soon he enjoyed the waves, whales, and stars. One night, Amos fell into the sea and could not reach his boat. A whale named Boris found him and carried him safely home. During their week together, Amos and Boris became close friends and promised to help each other. Many years later, a terrible hurricane washed Boris onto the shore. The huge whale could not return to the water. Amos hurried away and came back with two elephants. The elephants pushed Boris into the sea while Amos gave directions. Boris was saved, and the friends said goodbye with happy, sad tears. They knew they might not meet again, but they would always remember each other.

Amos the mouse dreamed about faraway places across the ocean, so he built a boat and sailed. After a day of seasickness, he became a fine sailor. But while looking at the beautiful night sky, Amos rolled off the deck and lost his boat. He floated alone in the cold ocean until a whale named Boris appeared. Boris carried Amos toward his home. The two animals learned about one another and became dear friends. Boris loved hearing about life on land, while Amos enjoyed hearing about the deep sea. When they reached the shore, they promised never to forget each other. Years later, a hurricane stranded Boris on the beach. Amos saw that his friend was in danger and quickly found two elephants. Together, the elephants pushed Boris back into the water. Amos had saved Boris just as Boris had once saved Amos. The old friends said goodbye, knowing their friendship would last forever.

A mouse named Amos loved the sea so much that he built a boat and sailed far from home. He carried food, water, tools, and other supplies. One night, Amos fell overboard and was left alone in the enormous ocean. He was tired, cold, and afraid until Boris, a friendly whale, rescued him. Boris offered to take Amos home, and Amos rode on his back. They spent a week traveling together. They shared secrets, talked about their lives, and admired the different things each could do. At the shore, Amos thanked Boris for saving his life and promised to help him someday. Much later, a hurricane threw Boris onto the beach. He was too large for Amos to move, but Amos did not give up. He brought two elephants, and they pushed the whale into the sea. Boris and Amos were joyful and grateful. They parted as true friends and promised never to forget one another.

video_title: 🐣🐯 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Mickey Mouse Babies : I CAN DO IT!

summaries.summary: There is a county fair with tents, taffy, pickles, pies, and pumpkins. Baby Mickey and Baby Minnie want to go. The wind is cold, so they need warm coats. Baby Minnie shows how to put on a coat. She lays it on the floor, puts her arms in the sleeves, reaches up, and swings the coat over her head. Then Baby Mickey and Baby Minnie ride in their bright red wagon. They see Baby Goofy and ask him to come too. Baby Goofy wants to go, but he does not know how to put on his coat. He tries, but the coat goes upside down, backward, and inside out. Baby Minnie helps him get free. Baby Mickey shows him the coat trick. Baby Goofy tries again and puts on his coat by himself. Then all three friends ride warmly to the fair.

Baby Mickey and Baby Minnie are going to a fun county fair. They put on warm coats because the wind is chilly. Baby Minnie lays her coat on the floor, puts her arms in the sleeves, and swings the coat over her head. Baby Mickey and Baby Minnie ride in a red wagon to Baby Goofy’s house. They invite Baby Goofy to join them for balloons, rides, games, and shows. Baby Goofy is happy, but he cannot put on his coat. He tries many ways. First the coat is upside down. Then it is backward. Then it is inside out, and Baby Goofy gets tangled. Baby Minnie helps him out. Baby Mickey shows Baby Goofy how to lay the coat down and swing it over his head. Baby Goofy copies him and puts on the coat all by himself. The three friends ride to the fair, warm and happy.

A county fair is happening, and Baby Mickey and Baby Minnie want to visit it. The cold wind means they must wear coats. Baby Minnie teaches the coat trick: put the coat on the floor, place arms in the sleeves, and swing it over the head. The two friends ride in their bright red wagon and find Baby Goofy. They ask him to come to the fair. Baby Goofy likes fair rides, so he is excited. But he needs help with his coat. He tries to put it on, but it is upside down, backward, and inside out. He becomes tangled and says he cannot do it. Baby Minnie helps him out. Baby Mickey says he can help and demonstrates the coat trick. Baby Goofy follows the steps and gets dressed by himself. He smiles and says he can do it. Then the three friends ride together to the fair in their warm coats.

video_title: 🎁💝 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse : Daisy's Gift

summaries.summary: Daisy says she wants to get Donald a gift. Daisy sees something for herself, then looks for something Donald can have. Donald says he does not see how he could carry the gift. Daisy points to several things, but some are not for Donald. At the end, Donald says, “Wait.”

Daisy tells Donald that she wants to get him a gift. She notices something for herself and says she sees one more thing for herself. Then Daisy looks for something for Donald. Donald says he could not carry it. Daisy points out more things, but Donald says they are not for him.

Daisy begins by saying, “I want to get you a gift.” Donald asks if she does. Daisy looks at things for herself, then tries to find something for Donald. Donald says one thing would be hard to carry. Daisy shows him other things, but he says they are not for him.

video_title: Can Ants Predict Earthquakes? 3D Animation | Pebbles And The Biggest Number Ep.5

summaries.summary: Pebbles fluttered down to the forest floor and saw an army of ants marching by. Pebbles asked one little ant what the biggest number was. The ants shouted, “20 quadrillion!” One ant suddenly cried, “Quick, run!” All the ants scuttled away. Nearby, a group of ants was carrying a giant spider. Then the ground began shaking. A scream and a strange “maau” screech filled the air as something flapped its wings. Wily and Pebbles quickly zipped away. The story follows Pebbles as she meets busy ants, hears about the enormous number of ants, and then experiences shaking ground and a loud screech. The ants’ quick escape and the shaking ground happen one after another, making the forest scene surprising and exciting.

In the forest, Pebbles found many ants marching together. She greeted a little ant and asked about the biggest number it knew. The ants answered, “20 quadrillion.” Before Pebbles could ask more, one ant shouted for everyone to run. The whole army of ants scuttled off. The story then showed a group of ants carrying a giant spider. Suddenly, the ground started shaking. A scream and a “maau” screech could be heard while something flapped its wings. Wily and Pebbles zipped off as as it could. The events move from a quiet meeting with the ants to a sudden escape. Pebbles learns the ants’ answer, watches them run, and then leaves when the forest becomes noisy and shaky.

Pebbles visited the forest floor, where an army of ants marched past her. She spoke to a little ant and asked which biggest number it knew. The ants called out, “20 quadrillion!” Then one ant warned the others to run. Every ant scuttled away at once. A group of ants was also carrying a giant spider. Soon after, the ground began to shake. There was a scream, followed by a “maau” screech and flapping wings. Wily and Pebbles zipped away as as it could. This short story connects Pebbles’ question about a giant number with a sudden forest emergency. The ants run first, and then the shaking ground, loud sounds, and flapping wings cause Wily and Pebbles to leave too.

video_title: A Little Girl After God's Own Heart by Elizabeth George - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: This story teaches a little girl how to live with a heart like God’s. First, she learns to fill her heart with love by sharing toys, smiling, and helping others. She can also choose joy and peace, even when things go wrong, and share comfort with her family and friends. Next, the story explains patience. Instead of becoming angry when she must wait, she can sit quietly and stay calm. The girl should show kindness and goodness by saying helpful words, doing what is right, and cheering up people who are sad. She should also be faithful, keeping her promises so others can trust her. When problems happen, gentleness helps her speak politely instead of yelling. Finally, self-control helps her say no to bad actions and keep from hurting others. She asks God to help her grow into a loving, good, and gentle girl.

A girl after God’s heart tries to show God’s love in everything she does. She learns that love means sharing, smiling, and helping people who feel sad. Joy and peace help her stay happy and calm, even when a day is difficult. She can share peace with her parents, brothers, sisters, and other people. When she has to wait, patience helps her avoid getting angry or throwing a fit. Kindness and goodness mean using helpful words, doing good things, comforting troubled children, and showing mercy. Faithfulness means being someone others can trust. If she promises to visit a friend, she should keep her promise. Gentleness means speaking carefully and not yelling, fighting, or acting bossy. Self-control helps her stop before doing something hurtful or bad. At the end, she asks God to help her become sweet, loving, faithful, and more like Him.

The story describes many good qualities for a little girl to practice. Love teaches her not to be selfish or stingy, but to share what she has. Joy and peace help her encourage people when their days feel mixed up. Patience helps her wait quietly instead of becoming very angry. Kindness and goodness guide her to help people, speak comforting words, and bring cheer to those who are troubled. Faithfulness teaches her to keep her word, because friends should be able to count on her. Gentleness teaches her to step back, calm down, and use polite words when something goes wrong. She should not be hateful, bossy, or ready to fight. Self-control helps her hold in angry feelings and refuse what is bad. The story ends with a prayer asking God to help the girl grow in love, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and truth.

video_title: Wolf Camp (Adventure & Friendship) #kids #story #toddlers #kindergarten #education #familybook #dog

summaries.summary: Homer is a dog who sometimes feels wolfish. He has wondered what it would be like to live as a real wolf, so he goes to Wolf Camp for a week. His people say goodbye and let him go. At camp, counselors Fang and Gr greet Homer and the other campers, Pixie and Rex. Fang teaches them about safety. The dogs learn to mark, howl, and trap. Soon they hunt a bunny and eat food that tastes unusual because it has hair on it. Homer writes home asking for doggy snacks and flea medicine. At night, the campers learn how real wolves sleep. Homer misses home, but each day the dogs become more comfortable and confident in the wild. At the end, they receive certificates. Homer feels sad to leave, but he howls with the pack one last time. When he returns home, he is an honorary wolf.

Homer wants to know what life as a real wolf would be like, so he joins Wolf Camp. His people take him there, and counselors Fang and Gr introduce him to Pixie and Rex. After a safety talk, the campers practice being wolves. They mark, howl, and trap. When they see a bunny, it is time to hunt. Homer waits behind the others, and the campers eat a strange dinner with hair on it. Homer does not like the food, so he writes home for Grandma Piey's pampered pooch doggy snacks and flea medicine. At bedtime, the dogs discover that wolves sleep in the wild, with many unusual sounds around them. Homer misses his home at first. Then the campers adjust and grow more confident. They earn certificates proving they completed camp. Homer is sad to leave, but he is happy to come home as an honorary wolf.

Homer begins as a dog who sometimes feels wolfish. He travels to Wolf Camp because he wants to live like a real wolf. Fang and Gr are the counselors, and Pixie and Rex are his fellow campers. The group listens to a safety talk, then starts wolf activities. They mark, howl, and trap. When they find a bunny, they go hunting and have a dinner that tastes unusual because it has hair on it. Homer writes a letter home. He says the food is yucky and asks for bacon-flavored doggy snacks and flea medicine because there are many bugs. At night, the campers learn how wolves sleep. Homer misses his people, but the dogs slowly adjust to wild life and gain confidence. By the end, they are practically wolves and receive certificates. Homer feels sad when camp ends. After one last howl, he goes home changed and becomes an honorary wolf.

video_title: Virtual Bilingual Storytime with Ms. Claudeth: How Are You? ¿Cómo estás?

summaries.summary: The Itsy Bitsy Spider went up, went up, and went up. Then the rain came and took the little spider away. After that, the sun came out and everything became dry. When the rain was gone and the world was dry again, the little spider went up once more. The spider kept climbing, even after the rain carried it away. The story follows the spider’s repeated journey upward, the rain, the drying sun, and the spider’s return to climbing. It ends with the little spider going up, up, and up again.

A little spider begins by going up. It goes up and up. Then rain comes down, and the rain takes the spider away. The sun appears, and everything dries. When the ground is dry again, the little spider starts going up once more. The spider’s journey happens in this order: climbing, rain, being taken away, sunshine, drying, and climbing again. The little spider does not stop forever. At the end, it goes up, went up, went up, and went up again.

The story is about the Itsy Bitsy Spider and its upward journey. First, the little spider goes up, up, and up. Next, the rain comes and takes the spider away. Then the sun comes out and dries everything. After the rain and wetness are gone, the little spider begins to climb again. The spider goes up repeatedly, and the story ends with another climb. The main events are simple: the spider goes up, the rain carries it away, the sun dries everything, and the spider goes up again.

video_title: Dinosaurs Love Underpants  | Funny Bedtime Children's Book Read Aloud in an English Accent.

summaries.summary: Long ago, dinosaurs lived everywhere. They had big teeth and long necks, and Tyrannosaurus Rex was the scariest. The story says cavemen first dreamed of underpants because they felt embarrassed without clothes. When T-Rex saw a pair of men's knickers, he did not want to eat the caveman. video_title: 🍪 Cookies: Bite size Life Lessons

summaries.summary: The cookie examples teach many life lessons. Cooperating means adding the chips while someone else stirs. Being patient means waiting for the cookies to finish. A pessimistic person is sad about having only half a cookie, while an optimistic person is happy to still have half. Being polite means asking nicely and saying thank you. Being honest means telling the truth about taking a cookie. Courage means taking a deep breath and telling the truth. The examples also show envy, loyalty, open-mindedness, regret, contentment, and wisdom.

A group of cookie examples shows what different qualities look like. First, people cooperate by adding chips and stirring together, and they are patient while the cookies bake. A compassionate friend gives part of a cookie to someone who needs one, while a greedy person takes them all. A generous person shares with everyone. One person thinks having half a cookie is awful, but another thinks it is still great. A polite person asks for cookies and says thank you. An honest, courageous person admits taking a cookie. Envy looks at another cookie and wishes for it. Loyalty stays with a best friend, open-mindedness tries a new cookie, regret wishes for fewer cookies, contentment enjoys a few cookies, and wisdom knows there is still much to learn.
