Clayton and Desmond keep making their snowmen bigger, but they discover that their snow people are still the same size as the others. They both think of a new plan. When they meet in the field, they agree that no one said they could not build together. The two mice roll every piece of both snowmen into one pile. Clayton puts on a floppy hat. Desmond gives the snowman a scarf, coal eyes, and a giant carrot nose. The finished snowman is the biggest ever. The mayor awards the prize to both mice, and they celebrate happily as partners.

video_title: Me First Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Pinkerton was a pink, plump pig who always wanted to be first. He pushed ahead at school, on the slide, at Story Time, and during Pig Scout activities. At the beach, he was first onto the bus, into the water, and into the picnic basket. During a hike, Pinkerton heard someone asking who would care for a sandwich. He hurried away from the other Scouts because he wanted to be first. At the top of a sandy hill, he found a little creature who said she was a sandwich. She took Pinkerton to her sand castle and made him powder her nose, comb her toes, feed her, wash dishes, sweep, do laundry, curl her hair, and tell a bedtime story. Pinkerton was very tired. He told a story about a pig who learned that being first was not always best. Then he hurried back to the bus, glad to be last.

Pinkerton liked being first more than anything. He rushed past others and shouted, “Me first!” at school and with his Pig Scout Troop. One day, the Scouts went to the beach. Pinkerton was first everywhere, but while they hiked, he heard a voice asking who would care for a sandwich. He ran ahead, imagining a sandwich filled with many tasty foods. Instead, he met a small creature who lived in the sand and called herself a sandwich. She brought Pinkerton to her castle. Because he wanted to be first to care for her, she gave him many jobs. He powdered her nose, combed her toes, fed her supper, washed dishes, swept, did laundry, curled her hair, tucked her in, and told a story. Pinkerton was exhausted. In his story, a pushy pig learned that first was not always best. Pinkerton then left and felt glad to be last.

Pinkerton was always pushing to get ahead. He wanted to be first in line, first down the slide, first at Story Time, and first during every Pig Scout activity. At the beach, he rushed away from the Scouts when he heard a voice asking for someone to care for a sandwich. Pinkerton thought he would get a delicious sandwich, so he ran as fast as he could. A little sand creature met him and said she was the sandwich. She took him to her sand castle and made him do all the caring. Pinkerton powdered her nose, combed her toes, fed her with a shovel, cleaned the castle, did laundry, curled her hair, tucked her in, and made up a bedtime story. His story said that a pig learned first was not always best. The sandwich let him go. Pinkerton hurried to the bus and was glad to be last.

video_title: A little Princess Treasury | I want my mum! | Mother's Day #readaloud #bedtimestories #storytime

summaries.summary: The little princess is painting a picture of her family when she knocks over the water pot. The paint runs, and her best picture becomes a colorful mess. Her mother loves it anyway and calls it “a rainy day.” Later, the princess hurts her knee on a seesaw and goes to the doctor. At home, Mom kisses her knee better. That night, the princess is scared of a monster under her bed, but Dad explains that it is only a teddy bear. Mom reads to them, and the princess falls asleep. At breakfast, she refuses an egg, so Mom pretends it is a dinosaur egg. During the day, many people try to play with her, but she keeps saying, “I want my mom.” Finally, she goes to a duchess’s sleepover. She feels sad at first, but the video and crisps make her smile. Her parents miss her while she is away.

One rainy day, the little princess paints a family picture. She accidentally spills the water used to clean her brushes, ruining the painting. Her mother sees the wet colors and says it looks like a rainy day, then hangs it up. After the rain stops, the princess plays on a seesaw and hurts her knee. A doctor treats her, but Mom’s kisses make it better. At bedtime, she imagines that a teddy bear is a frightening blue monster. Dad tells her there is no monster, and Mom reads stories until she falls asleep. The next morning, the princess says she hates eggs. Mom turns the egg into a pretend dinosaur egg, and the princess happily chases her. The maid, admiral, and little prince all try to entertain her, but she still wants Mom. Then she is invited to a sleepover. She cries because she does not want to leave, but Mom says she and Gilbert are coming too. At the sleepover, the princess enjoys a funny video and crisps.

The little princess wants her mother throughout a busy day. First, she spills water on her painting, but Mom likes the soggy picture and hangs it up. Then the princess hurts her knee while playing outside. The doctor puts something on it, and Mom kisses it better when she gets home. At night, a teddy bear looks like a monster under the bed. Mom stays and reads stories, so the princess falls asleep. At breakfast, the cook gives her an egg, but she refuses it. Mom pretends it is a dinosaur egg, and the princess enjoys the game. The maid brings games, the admiral brings boats, and the little prince brings toys, yet the princess still cries for Mom. Finally, Mom tells her about a sleepover at the little duchess’s castle. The princess worries about going, but Mom and Gilbert go with her. At the castle, the princess watches a funny video, eats crisps, and smiles. Back at the palace, her parents swing together and miss her while she has fun.

video_title: WOOLBUR Read Aloud by Mrs. K. | A Story About Being Yourself | Kids Books Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Wilbur is a sheep who likes doing things differently. He runs with the dogs instead of standing still with the herd. He also keeps his wool, cards it himself, rides on the spinning wheel, dyes himself, and puts his forelock into the loom. His mother and father worry because Wilbur does not act like the other sheep, but his grandpa tells them not to worry. At last, Ma and Pa tell Wilbur to follow the flock and do everything like the other sheep. Wilbur thinks all night. Then he teaches the other sheep to run with the dogs, grow their wool, card it themselves, spin wild yarn, use colors, and weave their forelocks. Soon, all the sheep are acting like Wilbur. Ma and Pa wonder how they will find him, but Grandpa says not to worry. Wilbur shows that trying new things can help everyone discover a different way to do things.

Wilbur does not behave like the other sheep. He would rather run with the dogs than stand still in the herd. He does not want to have his wool sheared, so he lets it grow. He cards his own wool, rides around on the spinning wheel, dyes himself, and weaves his forelock in the loom. Each time, his parents are surprised and worried, while Grandpa says, “Don’t worry.” Finally, Ma and Pa tell Wilbur that he must follow the flock and do things like every other sheep. Wilbur thinks about this all night. The next day, he teaches the whole flock his unusual ways. The sheep learn to run with dogs, grow their wool, make their own yarn, experiment with color, and weave their forelocks. Soon everyone looks and acts like Wilbur. Ma and Pa cannot tell which sheep is their son, but Grandpa remains calm.

Wilbur is a sheep with his own ideas. He thinks running with dogs is great, and he enjoys being woolly. He makes his own choices about carding, spinning, dyeing, and weaving wool. His parents keep pulling on their wool because they are worried about him. Grandpa tells them not to worry, but Ma and Pa finally ask Wilbur to do everything the usual sheep way. Wilbur thinks hard during the night. Instead of giving up his different ways, he teaches them to all the other sheep. The sheep learn to run with the dogs, let their wool grow, card their own wool, spin crazy yarn, try new colors, and weave their forelocks. After that, every sheep looks and acts like Wilbur. Ma and Pa wonder how they can find him among the flock. Grandpa again says not to worry. Wilbur’s different ideas have become ideas everyone can enjoy.

video_title: 🦖🚀 Kids Book Read Aloud: Step Into Reading : DC Super Friends : T-Rex Trouble!

summaries.summary: Dinosaur fossils are on parade when Lex Luthor sprays a T-Rex with super foam. The foam makes the T-Rex come alive, and Lex rides it. He brings more dinosaurs to life, too. The dinosaurs scare people while Lex takes their money and valuables. Flash sees the trouble and calls the Super Friends. Batman, Green Lantern, and Superman come to help. The dinosaurs attack. Batman lassos a Triceratops, and Green Lantern saves Flash with a tornado. Superman holds the T-Rex’s sharp-toothed jaws open. Then Batman sees a grocery truck and has an idea. He steers the Triceratops toward the truck, where meat and fish pour out. The dinosaurs run to the food and stop causing trouble. Flash grabs Lex, so Lex’s plan fails. The Super Friends make friends with the dinosaurs and build them a home. Everyone cheers.

Lex Luthor wants to cause trouble at a dinosaur fossil parade. He sprays super foam on the T-Rex bones, and the T-Rex comes to life. Lex rides the dinosaur and makes more dinosaurs come alive. A flying dinosaur grabs Flash, and the dinosaurs scare the people. Lex takes their money and valuables. Flash calls the Super Friends. Batman stops Lex and lassos the Triceratops. Green Lantern uses a tornado to save Flash and sets him safely on the ground. Superman fights the T-Rex and keeps its sharp jaws from snapping shut. Batman then uses a grocery truck full of meat and fish. The dinosaurs run to the food and begin eating. Flash grabs Lex, and Lex’s plan fails. The Super Friends make friends with the dinosaurs and build a home for them. Everyone cheers when the dinosaurs are safe.

A T-Rex is only a fossil until Lex Luthor sprays its bones with super foam. Then the T-Rex comes to life, and Lex rides it through the parade. Lex makes other dinosaurs come alive, including a flying dinosaur and a Triceratops. The dinosaurs frighten people, and Lex steals their money and valuables. Flash calls the Super Friends for help. Batman lassos the Triceratops, Green Lantern rescues Flash with a tornado, and Superman holds back the T-Rex’s sharp jaws. Batman notices a grocery truck and steers the Triceratops into it. Meat and fish fall out, so the hungry dinosaurs run to eat. While the dinosaurs eat, Flash grabs Lex. Lex’s plan has failed. The Super Friends do not fight the dinosaurs anymore. Instead, they make friends with them and build a home where they can stay. Everyone cheers together.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Today I'll Be A Princess by Paula Croyale

summaries.summary: A child imagines being a princess. She will wear pretty dresses that swish and swirl, sparkly shoes, a beautiful crown with jewels, and ride in a royal carriage. Then Mommy says that princesses do not get to play in the mud. The child decides maybe she will be a princess tomorrow.

The child says, “I’ll be a princess.” She imagines fancy clothes, sparkly shoes, a royal carriage, and a crown covered with jewels. But Mommy says princesses cannot play in the mud. Because of this, the child thinks she may be a princess tomorrow instead.

A child dreams about princess things. She wants pretty dresses, sparkly shoes, a royal carriage, and the most beautiful jeweled crown. The child also wants to play in the mud, but Mommy says princesses do not get to do that. So the child says she might be a princess tomorrow.

video_title: Jack and the Beanstalk Read Aloud | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: Jack lived with his sick mother, and they had no money. His mother told him to sell their cow. On the way to town, Jack traded the cow for five magic beans. His mother was angry and threw the beans outside. By morning, a giant beanock had grown to the clouds. Jack climbed it and found a castle. A giantess gave him work and hid him from her hungry husband. Jack saw the giant counting gold and took some gold home. Later, he returned and carried away a goose that laid golden eggs. On his third visit, he found a golden harp. The harp cried out, and the giant chased Jack down the beanock. Jack’s mother used an axe to cut the beanock. Jack finished cutting it, and the giant fell with it. Jack, his mother, the goose, and the harp lived happily together.

Jack was a kind boy who did not always think carefully. When his mother asked him to sell their cow, he traded it for five magic beans because he believed they might have magic powers. The beans grew into a tall beanock. Jack climbed up and discovered a castle where a giant and his wife lived. The giantess gave Jack chores and hid him in a cupboard. Jack escaped with gold after seeing the giant fall asleep. He came back another day and took a goose that laid golden eggs. Even though his mother warned him, Jack returned once more. He hid in a washtub and listened to a beautiful golden harp. When Jack grabbed the harp, it called for its master. The giant chased Jack down the beanock, but Jack and his mother cut it down with an axe. The giant fell, and the family lived happily.

A widow and her son Jack were very poor, so Jack was sent to sell their cow. A stranger offered five magic beans, and Jack accepted them. His mother threw the beans out the window, but a huge beanock grew during the night. Jack climbed up and reached a castle in the clouds. The giantess made him scrub floors and wash dishes while she kept him safe from the giant. Jack watched the giant count gold and later carried the goose, which laid a golden egg, down the beanock. His mother told him not to climb again, but Jack returned for the golden harp. He hid in a washtub until the giant fell asleep. When the harp shouted, the giant woke and chased Jack. Jack slid down and called for his mother. She chopped the beanock with an axe, and Jack chopped it too. The giant and beanock crashed down together.

video_title: A Little Spot-4 Books Collection | Kids Picture Story | Read Aloud-American English | Listen & Learn

summaries.summary: Spot is a colorful little sticker with a sticky back. Spot helps children remember to be kind. A child uses encouraging words when someone feels sad, shares toys, says hello to someone alone, and says please when asking for water. When the child breaks a crayon, the child apologizes. The child also helps, cleans up, waits patiently, and tries not to get upset. Each kind action adds happiness to people’s hearts. Spot reminds children that being supportive, friendly, polite, apologetic, helpful, tidy, and patient are all ways to show kindness. At the end, Spot asks children to put a kindness spot on their hand and mark one each day they are kind. The story shows that small choices can help kindness stick and spread to other people.

A little spot named Spot explains that kindness can be remembered with a colorful sticker. The sticker has a sticky back so kindness can “stick” to a person. A child learns many ways to be kind. The child encourages someone who thinks their drawing is bad, shares a dinosaur, welcomes a lonely child, and politely asks for more water. After accidentally breaking a friend’s favorite pink crayon, the child says sorry. The child also accepts help and lends a helping hand. Then the child cleans up a mess and waits patiently in line. Spot explains that every kind choice adds happiness to hearts. Finally, Spot asks children to place a spot on their hand and mark it whenever they do something kind. Children are invited to practice kindness every day and see if they can be kind all week.

Spot is not an ordinary spot. Spot is a little spot of kindness that comes in many colors and helps children remember kind choices. The child first uses encouraging words when someone feels unhappy. Then the child shares toys, greets someone who is alone, and uses polite words to ask for water. When a favorite crayon is broken by accident, the child apologizes. The child says yes to help and learns that helping is kind. The child also cleans up after making a mess and stays calm while waiting in line. Spot explains that being supportive, sharing, being friendly, being polite, apologizing, helping, cleaning, and being patient are all kinds of kindness. The child puts a spot on a hand and marks each kind day. Spot reminds children that kindness brings happiness to their hearts and to the hearts of others.

video_title: A Little Spot-4 Books Collection | Kids Picture Story | Read Aloud-American English | Listen & Learn

summaries.summary: A messy room needs help, so little spots of organization show children how to clean it. First, they find containers and sort toys into piles for toys, games, cars, and blocks. The room feels overwhelming, so they divide it into sections and work on one section at a time. They can also play a song and finish putting things away before it ends. Labels and colored bins help them find things quickly. They make keep, donate, and trash piles. Donating old toys can help a child who has none, and birthdays are a good time to do it. After organizing, the room looks wonderful. The spots explain that organizing also trains the brain to separate and categorize things. Routines, magnets, lists, notes, calendars, and story maps can help people remember. When Scribble Spot’s emotions become tangled, identifying the feeling helps guide it to a peaceful spot.

Little spots of organization help clean a messy room. They begin by finding containers and sorting objects into piles. Because the job feels too large, they divide the room into sections and complete one section at a time. They play a song, pick up the items, and return each thing to its proper place. Labeled, color-coded bins make sorting easier. They also choose things to keep, donate, or throw away. Old toys can be donated after a birthday to help another child. Soon, everything has a spot. The story explains that organizing grows memory because the brain learns to separate and categorize. Routines can help children remember daily jobs and grow responsibility and confidence. To-do lists and notes help with tasks, while colored calendar spots show family plans. A story map helps organize a story’s setting, characters, beginning, middle, and end. Finally, naming an emotion helps Scribble Spot find peace.

A child wonders how a room became so messy. The organization spots suggest containers, sorting piles, smaller sections, and a song to make cleaning easier. Every object gets a place, and color-coded labels help locate things. The child makes keep, donate, and trash piles. Donating toys that are no longer used helps another child, especially after a birthday. The room is quickly organized. The spots then show that organization helps memory and reading because readers keep track of characters, plots, events, and details. A routine can remind children to make their beds, brush their teeth, pick up toys, do homework, and complete other jobs. Lists, visible notes, and a color-coded calendar help organize tasks and family activities. A story map organizes ideas. When Scribble Spot feels tangled emotions, identifying the feeling helps guide it to a peaceful spot.

video_title: A Little Spot-4 Books Collection | Kids Picture Story | Read Aloud-American English | Listen & Learn

summaries.summary: A peaceful spot explains that a sadness spot appears when someone is upset, disappointed, lonely, or has experienced a loss. Crying may release sadness, but a person can also look sad by frowning or moping. When someone is lonely, a friend can ask if they are okay and listen. If a new child feels worried and sad, saying hello and introducing friends can help. When a small problem feels big, teamwork can help. If someone loses a pet, friend, or family member, a hug and happy memories can bring love and comfort. Friendship can help when someone misses a loved one who is far away. Children can also calm their own sadness with music, drawing, or writing. The story teaches a hand exercise: imagine blue and green spots, circle them, count the swirls, and take deep breaths.

A blue sadness spot can visit anyone. It may come with upset feelings, disappointment, loneliness, or loss. The peaceful spot shows how to notice sadness by looking for crying, frowning, or moping. A sad person may need a friend. Asking if they are okay and listening can help them feel less alone. A new child may feel both anxious and sad, so welcoming the child and introducing friends can bring compassion. Sometimes teamwork helps when a problem seems larger than it is. When someone loses a pet or loved one, hugs and talking about happy memories can help. Friendship can comfort someone who misses a person far away. Children may calm their own sadness with music, drawing, or writing. They can also trace imagined spots on their palm, count the circles, and breathe deeply.

The story explains that sadness is a normal emotion, but a sadness spot can feel too large or stay too long. People can recognize it through tears, frowns, moping, or loneliness. Friends can help by asking questions, listening, showing empathy, and welcoming someone who feels new or worried. Teamwork can help when a problem seems difficult. Love and hugs can comfort someone after the loss of a pet, friend, or family member, especially when people remember happy times together. Friendship can help someone who misses a loved one far away. When children feel sad without knowing why, creativity such as music, drawing, and writing may relax the mind. A calming exercise uses imagined blue and green spots on the palm. Children circle them, count the swirls, and take a deep breath each time.

video_title: A Little Spot-4 Books Collection | Kids Picture Story | Read Aloud-American English | Listen & Learn

summaries.summary: Spot is a thankful spot who explains that writing down things we appreciate can make us happier. Spot is thankful for parks, nature, warm and cool clothing, rain, snow, flowers, sunshine, ice cream, and swimming pools. Spot is also thankful for emotions, because sadness can show others when help is needed, anger can bring passion, and anxiety can warn about danger. Spot appreciates love, peaceful feelings, friends, family, celebrations, schools, teachers, libraries, books, music, a pet fish named Tommy, art supplies, clean water, lights, food, toothbrushes, sleep, and many other everyday things. Spot is thankful for kindness, respect, responsibility, courage, patience, and honesty too. At the end, Spot asks children to make their own thankful lists. Questions about colors, people, animals, toys, books, and things that make them smile can help children think of things they appreciate.

A little thankful spot has been making a long list. The list begins with playing in the park, trees, slippers, hats, sandals, rain boots, umbrellas, snowmen, and spring flowers. It continues with sunshine, ice pops, ice cream, pools, feelings, love, rainbows, the Earth, planets, the moon, and stars. Spot is thankful for friends, parties, cake, balloons, family, schools, teachers, libraries, books, paper airplanes, music, and Tommy the pet fish. Spot also appreciates dressing up, performing with courage, time, patience, cardboard boxes, clean water, lights, crayons, paint, rocks, toothbrushes, nutritious food, tissues, signs, and sleep. Spot says children can make a thankful list too. They can write about something red, soft, big, small, a person, an animal, a toy, or a book. These questions help children notice happy things around them.

Spot learns that thankfulness means being happy with what we have and not comparing ourselves with others. Spot’s list includes outdoor play, changing seasons, comfortable clothes, sunny and rainy days, summer treats, feelings, love, nature, friends, family, schools, teachers, libraries, reading, music, art, pets, and creative play. Spot is thankful for useful things such as clean water, lights, food, toothbrushes, tissues, safety signs, and sleep. Spot also names qualities like respect, kindness, responsibility, courage, patience, and honesty. The list becomes very long because ordinary objects and experiences can be appreciated. At the end, Spot invites children to write something thankful every day. Questions about colors, sizes, textures, people, animals, toys, books, and what makes them smile give children ideas for their own lists.

video_title: Hush Now Banshee - Narration - NRYKB

summaries.summary: One little banshee is looking for fun, but everything around her seems quiet. She visits two ghosts reading by a lake and makes a loud cry. Then she visits three hobgoblins, four fishermen, five bog monsters, six typing trolls, seven fairy warriors, eight leprechaorns, and nine druids. Each group asks her to be quiet because they are reading, dozing, fishing, cleaning, typing, training, painting, or meditating. Banshee feels sad and says she is on her own. Then ten creatures come from the trees. They say they want to be her friends, but she is too loud. Banshee says she is sorry and will try quiet time. A ghost teaches her to count quietly from ten to one. Banshee tries, but she shouts that she loves quiet time. Her friends tumble everywhere, laugh, and say she made it to ten. They invite her to try again.

Banshee wants to have fun with the creatures, so she says hello to them in very loud ways. Two ghosts are reading, three hobgoblins are dozing, and four sleepy locals are fishing. Then five bog monsters are cleaning, six trolls are typing, seven fairy warriors are training, eight leprechaorns are painting, and nine druids are meditating. Every group jumps, trembles, or wakes up and says, “Hush now, Banshee.” Banshee wonders why everyone seems cranky. She sighs and says being alone is hard. Ten upset creatures fly from the trees and explain that they want to be her friends, but she is way too loud. Banshee says she is sorry and agrees to try quiet time. A ghost counts down from ten to one. Banshee is happy, but she says it loudly. Her friends fall everywhere, then laugh and tell her she can try again.

Banshee travels through a quiet place and meets many creatures. She sees ghosts reading, hobgoblins sleeping, locals fishing, bog monsters cleaning, trolls typing, fairy warriors training, leprechaorns painting, and druids meditating. Each time Banshee calls out, her loud voice surprises them. They all ask her to hush because they are busy with quiet activities. Banshee does not understand at first, and she says she is on her own. Ten creatures then come from the trees and ask for quiet time. They tell Banshee they want to be her friend, but she is too loud. Banshee apologizes and says she will try to be quiet. A ghost shows her how to count from ten down to one. Banshee counts and cries that she loves quiet time. Her friends tumble everywhere because she is still loud. They laugh kindly and say she made it to ten, then ask her to try again.

video_title: Dandelion Magic Read Aloud with Author Darren Farrell | Brightly Storytime Together

summaries.summary: Jonah finds a dandelion. His Nana says that one magical dandelion grows somewhere in the world each year. Long ago, she found one, made a wish for a grandson, and Jonah appeared. Jonah tries the dandelion with a wish, but he turns into a pineapple. He tries again and becomes a pirate. His boat will not move, so a big gust of wind sends him toward treasure. A sea serpent, a giant squid, and a dragon get in his way. Jonah and his helpers scare them and stop the dragon’s fire. Then the wind makes a huge hurricane, and Jonah’s boat is in danger. With one last wish, Jonah is saved by Super Nana. He comes home safely and goes to bed. Somewhere, another magical dandelion will grow one day.

Jonah’s Nana believes dandelions can be magical. She once wished on one and wished for a grandson. Then Jonah appeared. When Jonah finds a dandelion, he and his friends make wishes. The first wish turns Jonah into a pineapple. The next wish makes him a pirate with a boat. Wind pushes his boat toward treasure. Jonah meets a sea serpent, a giant squid, and a dragon. The sea serpent is scared away. The squid is distracted, and the dragon’s fire is put out. The blowing becomes too strong and starts a hurricane. Big waves make Jonah’s boat unsafe. Jonah has one wish left. A wish for useful things does not help, but one magic fuzz remains. Super Nana comes to rescue him. Jonah is saved and goes home for a peaceful night.

Jonah discovers a dandelion, and Nana says it may be magical. She tells him that a magical dandelion grows somewhere every year. Nana once used one to wish for a grandson, and Jonah appeared. Jonah makes a wish and becomes a pineapple. He wishes again and becomes a pirate. His boat needs wind, so strong blowing moves it toward treasure. On the way, Jonah faces a sea serpent, a giant squid, and a dragon. The sea serpent leaves, the squid is distracted, and wet raspberry blowing puts out the dragon’s fire. The blowing also creates a hurricane, with waves bigger than Jonah’s boat. Jonah is in danger. He has one last chance to wish. A pizza is wished for, but Super Nana uses the last magic fuzz to save Jonah. He returns home and sleeps peacefully.

video_title: Today I Am Mad by Michael Gordon / Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Josh wants his favorite engine, but Tom is playing with it. Josh grabs the toy and feels happy for a moment. Then he sees that Tom is sad, so Josh says he is sorry. Tom forgives him, and the boys decide to share the engine and play together. Later, Josh takes a cookie before dinner. His mother takes it away and tells him to play outside. Josh feels very angry. He breathes in and out, counts slowly from one to ten, and begins to feel better. He kicks a ball and feels proud because he managed his anger. That night, Dad hugs Josh and says he is proud. The next day, two classmates argue about a game. Josh sees that Jordan is sad, so he hugs Jordan until Jordan feels better. Josh learns that saying sorry, sharing, breathing, counting, and giving hugs can help when people feel mad or sad.

Josh has a difficult day with many strong feelings. At school, he wants the engine Tom is using. He grabs it and shouts, but he feels sorry when he notices Tom looks sad. Josh apologizes, and Tom forgives him. They agree to share the engine, beginning a new friendship. At home, Josh takes a chocolate cookie while dinner is cooking. Mom takes the cookie away, and Josh stomps outside because he is angry. He remembers to breathe deeply and count to ten. Soon he feels good again and plays with his ball. Josh is proud that he let go of his angry feelings. At bedtime, Dad hugs him and praises him. The next day, Jordan is upset after an argument about a game. Josh gives Jordan a tight hug. Jordan begins to feel good, showing that a hug can help someone who is sad.

Josh wants things to go his own way when he sees Tom playing with his favorite engine. He takes the toy and yells, but then he notices Tom is unhappy. Josh says sorry, and Tom forgives him. The boys decide to share the engine and have fun together. Later, Josh becomes angry when Mom takes away a cookie because dinner will be ready soon. He goes outside, breathes deeply, and counts from one to ten. His anger starts to go away, and he kicks a ball around the yard. Josh feels proud because he managed his emotions. That night, Dad hugs Josh and tells him he is proud. The next day, Josh sees Jordan feeling sad after a disagreement about a game. Josh hugs Jordan tightly until Jordan feels better. Josh’s actions show the different ways he handles anger and helps a friend: he apologizes, shares, calms himself, and gives a hug.

video_title: The Donkey Who Carried a King by R.C. Sproul - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Riley feels sad because the other boys choose him last for games. His father tells him that he also felt hurt when he was young, and Grandpa tells Riley about Davey, a little donkey near Jerusalem. Davey is too young to work, so he spends his days waiting, eating, and sleeping. He wishes someone would choose him. One day, two men take Davey because the Lord needs him. Jesus climbs onto his back, and Davey carries him into Jerusalem while people sing and wave palm branches. Davey feels proud. The next day, he must carry heavy sacks of olives, and he complains. Later, he sees Jesus carrying a rough wooden beam and learns that Jesus will die to save his people. Davey decides to be a willing servant. Riley understands that every job matters and chooses to be thankful, even when he is picked last. Grandpa explains that Jesus rose again and reigns forever.

When Riley comes home crying, he tells his mother that other children always choose him last. His father understands because the same thing happened to him. Grandpa then shares the story of Davey, a young donkey who feels useless because he has no work. Davey listens to stories about donkeys who helped important people, and he hopes for a special job. Soon, two men take him because the Lord needs him. Davey carries Jesus into Jerusalem while a happy crowd places coats and palm branches on the road and calls Jesus a king. Davey thinks he is a very special donkey. The next day, ordinary work carrying olives makes him grumpy. Later, Davey sees Jesus hurt and carrying a heavy wooden beam. Barnabas explains that Jesus is carrying the cross to be crucified and save his people. Davey learns to serve without complaining. Riley learns to be thankful and do his best in every role.

Grandpa helps Riley think about being chosen last by telling him about Davey. Davey lives with other donkeys, but he is too young to work and is never chosen for a task. He dreams of doing something important. One day, two men take Davey to Jesus. People cover his back, and Jesus rides him toward Jerusalem. The crowd sings, shouts, and waves palm branches because Jesus is the King. Davey carefully carries Jesus and feels proud. However, his next job is carrying heavy sacks of olives, and he does not want to do ordinary work. Later, he sees Jesus carrying a wooden cross while wounded. Jesus falls, and a soldier makes another man carry the beam. Barnabas tells Davey that Jesus will die to save his people. Davey decides to follow Jesus' example and serve willingly. Riley also chooses thankfulness. Grandpa explains that Jesus died, rose again, and reigns forever.

video_title: I'm A Frog!

summaries.summary: Piggie says, “Ribbit!” and tells Gerald that she is a frog. Gerald is surprised because Piggie looks like a pig and is named Piggy. Piggie explains that she was a pig, but she became a frog about five minutes ago. Gerald wonders what it would be like to be a frog. Piggie says he could hop, eat flies, and ribbit all day. Gerald does not want to be a frog, so Piggie explains that she is only pretending. She tells Gerald that pretending means acting like something you are not. Gerald learns that everyone pretends, even grown-ups. Piggie asks Gerald to pretend to be a frog. Gerald keeps saying he cannot do it. At last, he explains that he is a cow and says, “Moo!” Piggie says, “Ribbit!” and Gerald says, “Ribbit!” too.

Piggie suddenly acts like a frog and makes many funny ribbit sounds. Gerald asks what she is doing. Piggie says she is a frog, even though she looks like a pig. She explains that she was a pig and became a frog only a few minutes ago. Gerald imagines becoming a frog. He thinks about hopping everywhere and eating flies, but he says he does not want to be one. Piggie tells him it is pretend. Gerald asks what pretending means. Piggie explains that pretending is acting like something you are not. Gerald is amazed that he can do this. Piggie asks him to pretend to be a frog. Gerald says he cannot, while Piggie says he can. They repeat this many times. Finally, Gerald gives the reason: he is a cow. He says, “Moo.” Then Piggie and Gerald make frog sounds together.

Gerald learns something new from Piggie. Piggie is pretending to be a frog, so she hops, thinks about eating flies, and says, “Ribbit!” Gerald first believes she is really a frog. Piggie explains that she was a pig before, but now she is pretending to be a frog. Gerald learns that people can act like something they are not, and that even grown-up people pretend. Piggie invites him to try pretending to be a frog. Gerald says, “Ribbit,” but then says he cannot pretend. Piggie encourages him again and again. Gerald keeps answering, “No, I can’t,” until Piggie asks why. Gerald says he cannot pretend to be a frog because he is a cow. He proves it by saying, “Moo!” Piggie answers with “Ribbit,” and Gerald says “Ribbit” too. Their pretend game ends with both animal sounds.

video_title: Lady Pancake & Sir French Toast

summaries.summary: Deep inside a refrigerator, Sir French Toast sees a strange flying dessert shining a light over Chili Lagoon. The light knocks him over, so he runs to tell Lady Pancake. At first, Lady Pancake does not believe him because everything looks normal. When something blasts Potato Mash Mountain, Toast takes the party guests to see it, but the flying dessert is gone again. Pancake and Toast argue about whether the strange objects are real. Then a bright light carries Baron von Waffle away, and Pancake realizes Toast was right. The refrigerator foods prepare for battle. Soon, shiny silver creatures appear. Toast remembers seeing a fork at Chili Lagoon and understands that the creatures are searching for their lost daughter. The fork family is reunited. The silverware explains that they accidentally took Waffle because his eyepiece looked like metal. They return Waffle and make his birthday party wonderful. Pancake and Toast say sorry, and their friendship is mended.

Sir French Toast is painting near Chili Lagoon when a flying pastry appears in the sky. It shines a light and knocks him down. Toast hurries to Lady Pancake and asks her to come see it. Lady Pancake wants to attend Baron von Waffle’s birthday party, so she is annoyed when the strange sight disappears. Later, Toast sees another blast at Potato Mash Mountain and brings the party guests there. Again, nobody can find the flying dessert. Pancake says Toast is mistaken, and the two friends argue. Suddenly, a flash of light lifts Baron von Waffle away. Pancake knows Toast told the truth, and both friends apologize. They gather the refrigerator foods to face the visitors. Toast then discovers that the visitors are silver forks and other utensils looking for a lost daughter. A small utensil is found at Chili Lagoon, and the family is reunited. The visitors apologize for taking Waffle by mistake. Waffle’s party begins, and Pancake and Toast celebrate together.

Lady Pancake and Sir French Toast live in a busy refrigerator filled with valleys, mountains, fountains, and chateaus. One day, Toast sees a mysterious flying dessert over Chili Lagoon. It shines a light and causes trouble, but Lady Pancake does not see anything when she arrives. Toast tries again to warn her after another blast, yet the flying object vanishes. The two best friends argue because Pancake thinks Toast is wrong. Then a flash takes Baron von Waffle, so Pancake understands that Toast was right all along. The refrigerator community puts on armor and prepares to fight. Silver creatures come from the light. Toast remembers that one of them looked like the fork he saw earlier. He asks if they are looking for a missing family member. The creatures say their daughter disappeared long ago. Toast leads them to Chili Lagoon, where their daughter is trapped. The family is reunited. The visitors explain that they mistook Waffle’s metal eyepiece for cutlery. They bring Waffle back and create a wonderful party. Toast and Pancake make up and remain friends.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse Read Along Story book | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids | Three Cheers For Us

summaries.summary: Pete's team wins on the baseball field, and Goofy worries that Pete cannot be beaten. Mickey says the friends can try hard because a big relay race is coming. The pals train in many ways. Goofy lifts weights, rides a bike, rows, tries archery, jumps in the pool, plays tennis, and learns that golf helps hand-eye coordination. Some things are hard. Mickey gets a flat tire, Donald falls behind while rowing, and Goofy's arrow flies backward. Pluto is the best swimmer. When the relay race begins, Pete's team is fast. The clubhouse team is faster. Mickey runs to the early lead, and his team keeps going. The clubhouse pals win the race. Mickey says, "We did it!" Then he gives three cheers for the team.

On the baseball field, Pete's team wins again. Goofy says they will never beat Pete, but Mickey says they will train for the relay race. The friends practice together. Goofy lifts weights because Pete is bigger and stronger. He rides a bike while Mickey gets a flat tire. Donald and Daisy fall behind. The pals row, but Donald's paddle feels very heavy. Goofy tries archery, and his arrow flies backward. Minnie says maybe Elle can give him tips. Goofy goes to the pool, while Pluto shows a good doggy paddle. Goofy also plays tennis, where the ball bounces back, and Mickey talks about golf. At the big race, Pete's team starts fast. The clubhouse team goes faster. Mickey runs into the early lead, and the team stays ahead. Mickey celebrates by saying, "Three cheers for us!"

Mickey and Goofy see Pete's team win baseball again. Goofy feels that Pete is too hard to beat, but Mickey points to the relay race next week and asks the pals to train hard. The friends practice many sports. Goofy lifts weights, rides quickly, rows with the others, aims an arrow, swims, plays tennis, and hears that golf helps with hand-eye coordination. The training does not always go smoothly. Mickey's bike tire becomes flat, Donald cannot keep up with the rowing, and Goofy's arrow goes backward. Pluto is the best swimmer. Goofy asks when the training celebration will happen. On relay-race day, Pete's team is ready and fast. The clubhouse pals are ready too, and their team is faster. Mickey sprints to the early lead. The friends keep the lead and win. Mickey says they did it and gives three cheers.

video_title: Doc McStuffins Read Along Storybook: Peaches Pie, Take a Bath! | A Read-Along Storybook in HD

summaries.summary: It is a rainy day, and Alma brings her new doll, Peach's Pie, to Emmy's house. Peach's Pie smells like peaches. Then Rudy the dog runs in while he is wet. He grabs the doll, and the girls chase him. When Rudy lets go, Peach's Pie is soaked and smells like wet dog. Alma feels sad, so Doc helps. At the toy checkup, Peach's Pie notices the wet-dog smell. The King gets a checkup first, and Lammy has a dance class. Peaches dances, but Hermie dances close to her, and her dress is smelly. At last, Doc checks Peach's Pie. Doc says she has a soggy dog problem and knows what to do. Everyone gives Peach's Pie a bath. She becomes peachy clean and smells like peaches again. She feels better and is ready to go home with Alma.

Alma has a new doll named Peach's Pie. The doll smells like peaches, but a wet dog named Rudy grabs her and makes her all wet. The girls chase Rudy and get the doll back. Now Peach's Pie smells like wet dog, and Alma is sad. Doc says she will help. The toys are busy: the King needs a checkup, Lammy starts dance class, and Peaches dances. Hermie dances near Peaches, and her dress smells bad. Then Doc is ready to see Peach's Pie. Chili whispers that the dress smells bad, and Doc hears about the soggy dog problem. Peach's Pie feels sad, but Doc knows what to do. Everyone helps wash her in a bath. Pizza says she is sweet as pie. After her bath, Peach's Pie is peachy clean and smells like peaches again. When Emmy and Alma come, the toys go still. Peach's Pie feels better and is ready to go home.

At Emmy's house, Alma shows her sister Emmy a new doll called Peach's Pie. The doll smells like peaches. Rudy the dog runs inside, wet from the rain, and grabs Peach's Pie. The girls ask Rudy to come back and let go. The doll is left wet and smells like wet dog, so Alma is sad. Doc helps her. Before Peach's Pie's checkup, the King sees Doc, Lammy begins a dance class, and Peaches dances. Hermie dances close to Peaches, and the dress is smelly. Then Doc examines Peach's Pie. Chili whispers that the dress smells bad, and Doc says there is a soggy dog problem. Peach's Pie is sad, but Doc knows she needs a bath. Everyone helps clean her. Pizza says she is sweet as pie. Peach's Pie is now peachy clean and smells like peaches again. She feels better and is ready to go home when Emmy and Alma return.

video_title: The Mitten

summaries.summary: Nikki wanted white mittens like snow, so his grandmother Baba knitted them for him. Baba warned that a white mitten could get lost in the snow. While Nikki played, one mitten fell off and stayed behind. A mole found it and crawled inside to be warm. Then a rabbit, hedgehog, owl, badger, fox, bear, and tiny meadow mouse all climbed into the mitten. The animals squeezed together because the mitten was warm and cozy. The mitten stretched bigger and bigger, but Baba’s knitting held it together. The little mouse sat on the bear’s nose. The bear’s nose tickled, and he gave a huge sneeze. The sneeze sent the mitten flying and scattered all the animals. Nikki saw the white mitten in the sky and ran to get it. When he came home, Baba saw that Nikki was safe and still had both mittens, but one mitten was much bigger than the other.

Baba made Nikki a pair of snow-white wool mittens, even though she worried that one might disappear in the snow. Soon, Nikki lost one mitten. A tired mole found the mitten and made a warm home inside it. A snowshoe rabbit came next, followed by a hedgehog, an owl, a badger, a fox, and a great bear. Each animal entered the mitten, and the others moved over to make room. The mitten became very full, but it kept stretching because Baba had knitted it well. Finally, a meadow mouse slipped inside and sat on the bear’s nose. Her whiskers tickled him. The bear sneezed loudly, and the mitten flew into the air. All the animals flew out in different directions. Nikki noticed the mitten and ran after it. At home, Baba checked that Nikki was safe and saw that he still had his mittens. One was now much larger than the other.

Nikki asked Baba for mittens as white as snow. Baba knitted them and told him to be careful, because a white mitten would be hard to find in the snow. Nikki went outside, and one mitten fell off. A mole discovered it and crawled inside. Soon many animals wanted the same warm mitten. A rabbit, hedgehog, owl, badger, fox, and bear joined the mole. They squeezed close together and made room for each new animal. The mitten grew and stretched far beyond its usual size. Then a very small meadow mouse climbed into the last space and rested on the bear’s nose. The mouse’s whiskers tickled the bear, and he sneezed with great force. The sneeze threw the mitten into the sky and sent the animals running away. Nikki saw the mitten against the blue sky and caught it. Baba looked out the window when he returned. Nikki was safe, and he still had his mittens, but one was much bigger.

video_title: Adelita Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Adelita was the daughter of Francisco and Adelia, who lived in a village in Mexico. Adelita’s mother died soon after Adelita was born, so Esperanza helped care for the family. Francisco later married Dona Michaela, who had two daughters, Valentina and Dulce. After Francisco died, Dona Michaela treated Adelita cruelly. She sent Esperanza away and made Adelita work in the kitchen. When the family went to a fiesta for Javier, Adelita felt sad because she could not attend. Esperanza returned and helped her find her mother’s beautiful dress and rebozo. At the party, Adelita disguised herself as “Ciencienta.” Javier fell in love with her, but she ran away at midnight. The next day, Javier searched for her. He saw the rebozo at Adelita’s house and recognized her. He asked Adelita to marry him. Adelita invited Dona Michaela, her stepsisters, and Esperanza to the wedding. Adelita and Javier lived happily ever after.

In a Mexican village, a merchant named Francisco and his wife, Adelia, welcomed a baby girl named Adelita. Adelia died after Adelita’s birth, and Esperanza helped raise the child. Years later, Francisco married Dona Michaela, whose daughters were Valentina and Dulce. When Francisco died, Dona Michaela moved Adelita to the attic, gave her old clothes, and made her do all the housework. She also sent Esperanza away. One day, the family went to a ranch fiesta for Javier’s homecoming. Adelita was not allowed to go, but Esperanza came back to help her. Adelita wore her mother’s dress and shawl and went to the party as a mysterious young woman called Ciencienta. Javier danced with her and declared his love, but Adelita left at midnight. Javier searched for Ciencienta and followed the rebozo to Adelita’s home. He remembered her from childhood and asked her to marry him. Adelita said yes, and they married happily.

Adelita grew up surrounded by love from her father and Esperanza, but her life changed after her father died. Her stepmother, Dona Michaela, was jealous of her and treated her like a servant. Adelita cleaned, cooked, and served her stepsisters, Valentina and Dulce. When they went to a fiesta to meet Javier, Adelita stayed home and cried. Esperanza returned with a cart and helped Adelita open her mother’s trunk. Inside was a lovely white dress and a rebozo decorated with birds and flowers. Adelita went to the fiesta disguised as Ciencienta. Javier was delighted by her and stayed beside her all evening. Adelita loved the wonderful night, but she ran away when Javier kissed her and said he loved her. The next day, Javier visited homes looking for Ciencienta. He saw Adelita’s mother’s rebozo and realized who she was. Adelita told him her name, and he asked her to marry him. Esperanza attended their wedding, and Adelita and Javier lived happily ever after.

video_title: 🦄 Stories for Kids Read Aloud 🦄 I’m A Unicorn by Mallory C. Loehr [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: A unicorn says that it is moonlight white and has a magical horn. It looks a lot like a horse, but it is a unicorn. Its horn can make water clean or heal a hurt. The unicorn can be strong and fierce, and it can also be sweet and gentle. It frolics in the forest and prances in the fields. Sometimes, it gallops with its herd, and they play hide and seek together. At other times, the unicorn likes to be alone in the quiet of dawn. The unicorn says it is magic and mystery, then asks if we believe in it. It says, “I believe in you.”

This story is about a moonlight-white unicorn. The unicorn has a magical horn. The horn can make water clean or heal a hurt. The unicorn looks like a horse and can be strong and fierce. It can also be sweet and gentle. The unicorn moves through nature by frolicking in the forest and prancing in the fields. It says it is a force of nature. Sometimes, the unicorn gallops with its herd. Together, they play hide and seek. Sometimes, the unicorn chooses the quiet of dawn and loves to be alone. The unicorn says it is magic and mystery. Then it asks, “Do you believe in me?” and answers, “I believe in you.”

A magical unicorn tells us about itself. It is moonlight white and has one magical horn. Although it looks a lot like a horse, it is a unicorn. Its horn can make water clean or heal a hurt. The unicorn has many sides: it can be strong and fierce, or sweet and gentle. It frolics in the forest, prances in the fields, and calls itself a force of nature. Sometimes, it gallops with its herd while they play hide and seek. Sometimes, it enjoys being alone in the quiet of dawn. The unicorn says, “I am magic. I am mystery.” At the end, it asks if we believe in it and says it believes in us.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: A judge wants to reach a train show, so Thomas takes her. Thomas tries to hurry, but many things are in the way. A goat stands on the track, a dark tunnel makes him slow down, and a cow blocks the rails. Then logs cover the track, and a crane engine clears them. Mud is waiting ahead, but Thomas races through it and keeps going. He passes a town and a dog. At last, Thomas reaches the train show covered in mud. The judge sees red trains, blue trains, old trains, new trains, and Thomas. She likes every train, but the muddy little blue train is her favorite because Thomas worked hard and never stopped.

Thomas promises to take the judge to the train show. He climbs a hill, but the brakes make him slow. A goat jumps away from the track, and Thomas travels down the hill. He goes through a dark tunnel and over a bridge so quickly that the judge loses her hat. A cow, some logs, and mud make the trip difficult. The crane clears the logs, and Thomas splashes through the mud. Nothing stops him. He goes past a town and a dog and finally reaches the show. The judge sees many wonderful trains. Even though Thomas is small and muddy, she chooses him as her favorite train.

The judge is excited to see a train show, and Thomas takes her there. The journey is not easy. Thomas must slow down for a goat, a tunnel, a cow, logs, and mud. Sometimes the judge tells him to hurry because they are late. A crane engine removes the logs, and Thomas races through the mud. He travels faster and faster until he reaches the show. The judge sees trains of many colors and ages. Thomas is covered in mud, but he has made it all the way. The judge says that all the trains are fun. Then she says the muddy little blue train is her favorite.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: Thomas is carried on a raft behind a boat, but the chain snaps during the night. He floats alone to a far-off island and does not know how to get home. He meets Bash, Dash, and Ferdinand, who tease him but then show him a tunnel leading toward Sodor. Rocks fall inside the dark tunnel, trapping all four engines. The engines tell Thomas to puff hard. His puffs rise into the sky. Percy sees them from Sodor and brings help. The engines clear the rocks, and Thomas is rescued from the tunnel.

Cranky places Thomas on a raft for a trip to the mainland. When the chain breaks, Thomas is left behind and reaches a strange island. Bash, Dash, and Ferdinand offer to help him. They lead Thomas into an old tunnel that they say goes to Sodor. The tunnel is dark and twisty, and rocks crash down and block the way. Thomas puffs as hard as he can. Percy sees the puffs and understands that Thomas needs help. Percy brings the Sodor engines, and they rescue Thomas from the rocks.

Thomas becomes separated from a boat when the chain on his raft snaps. He is frightened and floats to a far-off island. Three engines named Bash, Dash, and Ferdinand take him to a tunnel that should lead home. Inside, rocks fall and trap them. Thomas follows their plan and sends three big puffs high into the sky. Percy notices the puffs from Sodor. He races to get help, and the Sodor engines rush through the rocks. Thomas and the other engines are saved.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: Thomas visits Farmer Trotter's farm and learns that a pig will soon have piglets. The farmer asks him to bring straw for a soft bed. Thomas also wants to bring gifts, so Percy shares milk, James shares apples, and children share chestnuts. Thomas fills his truck with the gifts and has no room for straw. He returns the gifts to the farm and hurries back for straw. Thomas arrives just in time. The farmer opens the barn, and the sleepy piglets are ready for their bed. Farmer Trotter spreads the warm straw on the ground. The piglets lie down and fall asleep. The farmer thanks Thomas and names one piglet Thomas.

A pig on Farmer Trotter's farm is going to have piglets. Thomas is asked to bring straw, but he wants to bring presents too. Percy gives him milk, James gives him apples, and children give him chestnuts. When Thomas reaches the straw farm, his truck is already full. He rushes back, drops off the gifts, and returns for the straw. The piglets are born while he is away. Thomas brings lots of soft straw just in time. The farmer makes a warm bed, and all the piglets fall asleep. Farmer Trotter is thankful and gives one piglet Thomas's name.

Thomas wants to help make a cozy bed for new piglets. He collects milk from Percy, apples from James, and nuts from children. Because his truck is full, he cannot carry the straw at first. Thomas brings the gifts to Farmer Trotter's farm and then hurries back for straw. He returns as the piglets are born. The farmer places the soft straw in the barn, and the sleepy piglets lie down. They quickly fall asleep on their warm bed. Farmer Trotter thanks Thomas for helping and names one of the new piglets Thomas.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: Mr. and Mrs. Seahorse swim gently through the sea. Mrs. Seahorse lays her eggs in a pouch on Mr. Seahorse's belly. Mr. Seahorse promises to care for them. As he swims, he meets several fish fathers. Mr. Stickleback cares for eggs in a nest. Mr. Tilapia carries eggs in his mouth. Mr. Curtis carries babies on his head, Mr. Pipe carries eggs along his belly, and Mr. Bullhead babysits babies that have hatched. At last, Mr. Seahorse wiggles and twists, and the baby seahorses come out of his pouch. They swim away. One baby tries to return, but Mr. Seahorse says the baby is ready to be on its own.

Mrs. Seahorse lays her eggs in Mr. Seahorse's belly pouch, and he promises to keep them safe. During his journey, he sees other fish fathers caring for their eggs or babies in different ways. One has a nest, one holds eggs in his mouth, one has babies on his head, and another carries eggs on his belly. Mr. Bullhead watches babies that have already hatched. Then Mr. Seahorse's babies are ready. He wiggles and twists until the tiny seahorses tumble out and swim away. A baby turns back toward the pouch, but Mr. Seahorse gently tells it that it is ready to live on its own.

Mr. Seahorse and Mrs. Seahorse live in the sea. Mrs. Seahorse puts her eggs into Mr. Seahorse's pouch because he will care for them. He swims past many fish and learns that fathers care for eggs and babies in many different places. Some use nests, mouths, heads, or bellies. When the time comes, Mr. Seahorse moves back and forth, and his babies are born. The little seahorses leave the pouch and swim away. One baby wants to come back. Mr. Seahorse loves the baby, but he explains that the baby is ready to be on its own.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: Otis is a friendly little tractor who works on a farm. After work, he plays on the hills, near Mud Pond, and with the ducks. One night, a frightened baby calf comes to the barn. Otis's soft purring helps her sleep, and soon she follows him everywhere. Then a big yellow tractor takes Otis's place, and weeds cover his tires. One day, the calf gets stuck in Mud Pond. Farm hands, the yellow tractor, and a fire truck cannot free her. Otis hears the trouble and circles the pond. The calf follows his sound, and the mud lets her go. Otis and the calf become friends again and stay together on the farm.

Little Otis works happily with his farmer and plays after each busy day. A baby calf comes to the barn and feels safe when she hears Otis's gentle sound. The calf follows Otis over the hills and around the farm. Later, the farmer brings a new yellow tractor and leaves Otis behind the barn. Otis becomes covered by weeds and cannot play. When the calf sinks into Mud Pond, many helpers try to pull her out, but nothing works. Then Otis arrives. He circles the pond, and the calf turns around with him until she is free. The two friends return together, and Otis is loved and useful again.

Otis is a small tractor with a big friendship. He meets a baby calf and comforts her when she is scared. They play together and sit beneath the apple tree. When a new tractor replaces Otis, he becomes lonely behind the barn. The calf later wanders into muddy water and gets stuck. The farm workers, a tractor, and a fire truck all try to help, but the calf sinks farther. Otis comes when he hears the crowd. His soft purr makes the calf turn around the pond. The mud loosens, and she walks out. Otis leads her home, and they remain special friends.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: In a quiet napping house, everyone is asleep. A granny sleeps on a cozy bed. A child sleeps on the granny. A dog sleeps on the child. A cat sleeps on the dog. A mouse sleeps on the cat. Finally, a wakeful flea sits on the mouse. The flea bites the mouse, and the mouse scares the cat. The cat claws the dog, the dog thumps the child, and the child bumps the granny. The movement breaks the bed. The peaceful pile falls apart, and nobody is sleeping anymore.

A house is full of sleepers. First there is a cozy bed, then a snoring granny, a dreaming child, a dozing dog, a snoozing cat, and a slumbering mouse. A wakeful flea is on top of the mouse. The flea bites, and one small action causes a big chain of actions. The mouse scares the cat, the cat claws the dog, the dog thumps the child, and the child bumps the granny. The bed breaks, and the napping house is no longer quiet because everyone is awake.

Everyone in the napping house is resting in one big stack. The granny is on the bed, the child is on the granny, the dog is on the child, the cat is on the dog, and the mouse is on the cat. A flea is awake on the mouse. When the flea bites, the mouse moves the cat, the cat moves the dog, and the dog moves the child. The child bumps the granny, and the bed breaks. The sleepers are all disturbed, so no one is sleeping at the end.

video_title: 2 Hours of Kids Read Aloud Story -American English | Picture Story Read-Listen Books

summaries.summary: The Little Red Chicken is ready for bed, but she wants Papa to read a story. Papa reads about Hansel and Gretel, but the chicken interrupts to warn them about a witch. Papa tries Little Red Riding Hood, and the chicken interrupts again to warn her about a wolf. Papa reads Chicken Little, and the chicken interrupts once more to say that the falling sky is only an acorn. Papa says there are no more stories. The chicken tells Papa a story instead. In her story, a little red chicken reads many stories to her papa and gives him milk, but he stays awake. Then Papa falls asleep, and the chicken says good night.

Papa wants the Little Red Chicken to sleep, so he begins a bedtime story. The chicken keeps jumping into the stories. She warns Hansel and Gretel that the old woman is a witch, tells Little Red Riding Hood not to talk to the wolf, and tells Chicken Little not to panic about an acorn. Papa says they have run out of stories. The chicken asks him to let her tell one. Her story is about a little red chicken trying to put Papa to bed with stories and milk. Nothing works until Papa finally falls asleep.

At bedtime, the Little Red Chicken asks Papa for a story and promises not to interrupt. She cannot keep the promise. She interrupts three tales because she wants to protect the characters from a witch, a wolf, and fear about an acorn. Papa becomes tired and says there are no more stories. The chicken tells a story of her own. In it, the chicken tries to make Papa sleepy by reading one hundred stories and giving him more milk. Papa stays awake for a long time, but at last he falls asleep. The Little Red Chicken says good night.

video_title: The Berenstain Bears and the Spooky Old Tree [Audiobook by Riggan Reads]

summaries.summary: Three little bears go to a spooky old tree. One has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They ask if they dare go into the tree, and they dare. They find a twisty old stare and go up it. Then they have a giant key and see a moving wall. They ask if they dare go through the wall and into the spooky old hall. They dare. Inside, they have one light and two shivers. A great sleeping bear is there. The bears ask if they dare go over the bear. They do, because they came into the tree, climbed the stair, went through the wall, and entered the hall. Then they have no light, no stick, and no rope, and all have the shivers. They get out by going up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. They run fast home, safe at last.

Three little bears visit a spooky old tree. The first bear has a light, the second has a stick, and the third has a rope. They dare to go inside. Next, they find a twisty old stare, and they dare to go up it. They find a giant key and a moving wall. The bears dare to go through the wall and into a spooky old hall. In the hall, one bear has a light, but two bears have the shivers. They see a great sleeping bear. The bears dare to go over the sleeping bear. Soon, they have no light, no stick, and no rope. All three have the shivers. They must find a way out. They go up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. Then the three little bears run fast and get home safe at last.

The three little bears begin with a light, a stick, and a rope. They go into a spooky old tree because they dare. They climb a twisty old stare and dare to go up. Then they find a giant key and a moving wall. The bears go through the wall and into a spooky old hall. There is a great sleeping bear. The bears ask if they dare go over the bear, and they do. After they pass the sleeping bear, the three bears have no light, no stick, and no rope. They all have the shivers. The bears need to leave the spooky tree. They go up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. At the end, the three little bears run fast. They are home again and safe at last.

video_title: Where do Steam Trains Sleep at Night? (Satisfies Curiosity) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten

summaries.summary: The story asks where different trains sleep at night. Steam trains puff down the tracks and may have hot cocoa before bed. Snowplow trains finish clearing the tracks, and their moms may say it is bedtime. Passenger trains drop off girls and boys, then may fill their seats with teddy bears and cuddly toys. Break trains reach the end of their trips and rest after their engines are back on the rails. Fire trains are washed with water after helping. High-speed trains slow down while moms read sleepy stories. Trolleys ring their bells like soft lullabies. Subway trains stop and rest under a blanket of city lights. All the trains sleep beneath the moon and bright stars. When a child drifts off to Dreamland, the child’s choo-choos may be sleeping too, in steamed land.

At bedtime, many kinds of trains need a place to rest. Steam trains finish puffing along the tracks and may enjoy hot cocoa. Snowplow trains stop when the tracks are clear. Passenger trains have carried girls and boys home, and their seats may hold teddy bears and bedtime toys. A break train rests after its cargo reaches its destination and its engine is put back on the rails. Fire trains get a special shower after being heroes. High-speed trains calm down after speeding all day while a train mom reads. Trolleys finish showing through the streets and ring their bells softly. Subway trains reach their final stop and sleep beneath a quilt of city lights. The trains do not sleep on mattresses. The tracks are their beds, with a special blanket, a bright nightlight, the moon, and stars.

The story wonders if train families prepare their trains for sleep. Moms may make cocoa, read bedtime stories, or tell rescue tales. Dads may let trains rest on a flatbed, wash fire trains with water, or rock break trains after their engines return to the rails. Passenger trains have finished carrying girls and boys, and trolleys have finished traveling through the streets. Subway trains are done when they reach their final stop. At night, trains may sleep in a roundhouse, a freight yard, or a shed. They sleep on the tracks instead of on a mattress. Their blanket is special, and their nightlight is bright. Above them are the crescent moon and a sky full of stars. Then the story asks where a child’s trains sleep. When the child drifts off to Dreamland, all the little choo-choos may be fast asleep too.

video_title: This Is Not My Hat | Calm & Clever Story Time For Kids

summaries.summary: A little fish takes a hat from a big fish while the big fish is asleep. The little fish thinks the big fish will sleep for a long time and may not notice the missing hat. If he notices, the little fish thinks he may not know who took it. If he guesses, he may not know where the little fish is going. The little fish swims toward plants that grow big, tall, and close together. He believes the plants will hide him because it is hard to see there. Another someone has already seen which way he went, but that someone promised not to tell. The little fish knows stealing the hat is wrong and knows it does not belong to him. Still, he plans to keep it because it was too small for the big fish and fits him just right. He reaches the thick plants and says he made it. He still believes nobody will find him.

A fish has a hat that is not his. He stole it from a big fish who was sleeping. The fish thinks the big fish will stay asleep for a long time. He also thinks the big fish might not notice the hat is gone. Even if the big fish notices, the fish believes he will not know who took it. If the big fish guesses, the fish thinks he will not know where to look. The little fish chooses a hiding place among plants that are big, tall, and close together. It is difficult to see in the plants, so he believes nobody will find him. Someone saw him go that way, but promised not to tell anyone. The fish admits that stealing a hat is wrong and that the hat does not belong to him. He decides to keep it because it was too small for the big fish and fits him perfectly. Then he reaches the plants and feels safe.

A little fish takes a hat from a sleeping big fish. He makes many guesses about what might happen. The big fish may sleep for a long time. He may not see that his hat is missing. He may not know who took it, and he may not know where the little fish went. The little fish plans to hide where plants grow big and tall and close together. The plants are hard to see through, so he thinks nobody will find him. One someone has already seen him, but that someone said he would not tell which way the little fish went. The little fish knows the hat belongs to the big fish and knows taking it is wrong. Even so, he wants to keep it. The hat was too small for the big fish, but it fits the little fish just right. At last, the little fish reaches the thick plants and says he made it. He thinks he is hidden.

video_title: Miss Nelson has a Field Day read aloud

summaries.summary: The Horace B. Smedley School was gloomy because its football team, the Smedley Tornadoes, had lost every game and had not scored a point. The players only horsed around, and Coach Armstrong became so upset that he had to rest at home with the measles. Everyone needed a real expert before the Thanksgiving game against the strong Werewolves. Miss Nelson heard that Viola Swamp was the meanest substitute teacher in the world, so she put on an ugly black sweatsuit and called for help. Coach Swamp quickly made the players work hard. They did leg raises, ran faster, and stopped horsing around. In a few days, the team looked much better. When Coach Armstrong came back, he was surprised to see the players working like a real team. On Thanksgiving Day, the Tornadoes beat the Werewolves, 77–3. Miss Nelson went home tired and happy after getting tough with the team.

Miss Nelson noticed that everyone at school was sad. The football team was especially unhappy because the Tornadoes had not won a game or scored a point all year. Their Thanksgiving game against the Werewolves was coming soon, but the players thought they would lose, so they joked and played instead of practicing. Then Coach Armstrong became ill and needed a long rest. The players decided they needed someone who could get results. They talked about Viola Swamp, a very tough substitute teacher. Soon, Coach Swamp arrived in her black sweatsuit and began training them. She made them do many leg raises and run faster. She told them never to horse around because she would be watching. The players became a real team. When the Thanksgiving game arrived, the Tornadoes clobbered the Werewolves, 77–3. Mr. Blandsworth gave the team hot dogs, and Miss Nelson went home happy.

At Horace B. Smedley School, the cafeteria ladies, Mr. Blandsworth, and the children had lost their sparkle because the school football team was doing terribly. The Tornadoes had lost all year and had not scored once. Their big Thanksgiving game was near, and the players did not want to practice. Coach Armstrong became upset and had to stay home. Miss Nelson learned that the players wanted an expert who could get results. She hurried home, found an ugly black sweatsuit, and made an important call. The next day, Viola Swamp appeared as Coach Swamp. She looked frightening and made the players work very hard. They did leg raises, ran quickly, and learned not to horse around. Soon, the team was playing much better. Coach Armstrong returned and saw that the players worked like a real team. On Thanksgiving Day, the Tornadoes defeated the Werewolves, 77–3. Miss Nelson was tired and happy, and Barbara said she could help anytime.

video_title: A Letter From Your Teacher

summaries.summary: On the first day of school, a teacher writes a welcome letter to a student. The teacher says that every word is true and that their relationship will grow during the year. The teacher wants to learn about the student's sports, drawings, family, travels, favorite subject, and awards. Each morning, the teacher will greet the student with a smile and offer high fives, hugs, or fist bumps. The teacher will celebrate the student's exciting news. At school, the teacher will help the student learn science, math, reading, writing, and other skills. The teacher also hopes the student learns empathy, kindness, and respect. The student should listen, follow directions, care for supplies, set goals, and try their best. When school feels hard, the teacher will help. Together, they will make learning fun. The teacher is excited each day because the student means so much to them.

A teacher welcomes a student at the beginning of a school year with a caring letter. The teacher wants to know what makes the student special, including whether the student plays sports, likes to draw, does kung fu, or has a favorite subject. The teacher hopes to meet the student's family and hear about places the student has been. Every morning, the teacher promises a smile and welcomes high fives, hugs, or fist bumps. The classroom will be a place for learning science, math, reading, writing, and other important skills. The teacher explains that school is also about empathy, kindness, and respect. The student is asked to listen carefully, follow directions, care for supplies, set high goals, and work hard. Some days may be difficult, but the teacher will help when the student cannot do something yet. The teacher will make learning fun and says the student is very important.

The story is a letter from a teacher to a student on the first day of school. The teacher says they are eager to learn about the student's interests, family, favorite subject, and accomplishments. The teacher promises to greet the student happily each morning and celebrate exciting news together. The teacher will help with science, math, reading, writing, and the skills needed for school. However, the teacher says learning includes more than schoolwork. The student can grow in empathy and kindness by listening with their ears and eyes, following directions, and taking care of supplies. The teacher encourages the student to set high goals, keep going through tests, and always try their best. If a challenge makes the student think, "I just can't do it," the teacher will help them through it. The teacher will also make the student laugh and make learning fun. At the end, the teacher says they love being the student's teacher and that the student means a great deal to them.

video_title: 📖🍂 The Very Last Leaf | Read Aloud Kids Book

summaries.summary: Lance Cottonwood is a bright leaf who does very well in school. He enjoys his classes about leaves, sunlight, and changing colors. But during the autumn semester, he learns that his final test is to let go of his tree and fall to the ground. Lance is afraid. He wishes he were like Doug Fir, an evergreen who can stay on his branch all winter. While the other leaves float down, Lance makes excuses and remains alone in the tree. His teacher tells him that it is okay to be scared and listens to his worries. Lance sees children making a leaf pile and collecting leaves for crafts. His friends are having fun below, so Lance decides to try. He takes a deep breath, lets go, and floats gently into the pile. Lance is the last leaf to finish, but he does not fail. His friends cheer because he did it.

From the beginning of school, Lance Cottonwood is one of the best students in his class. He is proud of his work, but he becomes worried when autumn brings his final exam. Every cottonwood leaf is expected to fall from the tree, while Doug Fir, an evergreen, can remain on his branch through the winter. Lance wants to stay like Doug, so he gives excuses when the other leaves leave. Soon, Lance is the only leaf still in the tree. His teacher understands that he is frightened and helps him talk about landing in a gutter, sticking to a windshield, or falling where the dog did his business. After sharing his fears, Lance looks down and notices a leaf pile, crafts, and happy friends. He remembers how hard he studied. With his teacher and classmates cheering, Lance takes a deep breath and lets go. He floats safely to the pile and completes his test.

Lance Cottonwood starts as a talented and confident student. He succeeds in lessons about wind resistance, photosynthesis, and changing leaf colors. Then he discovers that his final test is a fall from the top of his tree to the grass. The other leaves are ready, but Lance is scared because cottonwood trees lose their leaves in autumn. He envies Doug Fir, whose evergreen tree lets him stay on his branch during the cold winter. One by one, the leaves fall, while Lance makes excuses and listens to other leaves tease him. When Lance is left alone, his teacher tells him that being scared is okay and helps him think about his worries. He notices children using leaves for a pile and crafts, and he sees that his friends are safe. Lance decides to take the leap. He breathes deeply, lets go, and floats to the pile. He finishes last, but he passes.

video_title: 👑 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Princess : Ariel's Dolphin Adventure by Andrea Posner-Sanchez
