summaries.summary: Ariel loved dancing with Prince Eric, but she missed her sea friends. Eric made a safe lagoon with a wall so Ariel could visit them. There, Ariel and her friends found a baby dolphin. The baby dolphin was frightened and could not find his mother. Ariel, Eric, Flounder, and Sebastian searched, but they could not find her. During a storm, Ariel worried about the little dolphin. Eric saw that his wall had caused a problem, so he helped keep the dolphin safe. Ariel called for her father, King Triton. King Triton came and found the dolphin’s mother. She could not enter because the gate was closed. King Triton used his trident to knock down the wall. Then the mother and baby dolphin reunited in the lagoon. Many sea creatures came to play, and Ariel was happy to be with her friends.

Ariel wanted to see her sea friends more often. Prince Eric built a lagoon near the palace. The lagoon had a wall to keep sharks and other dangerous creatures away, and a gate for Ariel’s friends. Flounder, Sebastian, and Scotto greeted Ariel there. Soon, they saw a baby dolphin swimming alone. The little dolphin was scared, and everyone wondered where his mother was. They searched everywhere, but they could not find her. That night, a storm made huge waves. Ariel knew the baby dolphin was frightened. Eric helped move him to calmer water, and Ariel asked King Triton for help. The king arrived and called the dolphins. They found the baby’s mother, but the gate would not open. King Triton knocked down the wall with his trident. The mother joined her baby, and they happily splashed Ariel and Eric.

video_title: Thunder Cake Read Aloud | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: A child visits Grandma, whom she calls Babushka, on a hot summer day in Michigan. Storm clouds gather, and the child hides under the bed because thunder is frightening. Grandma says it is good weather for making Thunder Cake. She teaches the child to count between lightning and thunder to learn how far away the storm is. Together, they collect eggs from Nelly Peckin, milk from Kick Cow, and chocolate, sugar, and flour from the dry shed. They also gather tomatoes and strawberries. The child is scared but keeps helping Grandma. In the kitchen, they mix the batter, make frosting, and put the cake in the oven before the storm arrives. Grandma tells the child that these brave actions show courage. They frost and eat the cake while rain and thunder shake the house. After that day, the child is no longer afraid of thunder.

During a summer storm, a child hides under the bed at Grandma's farm. Grandma calls the storm baking weather and invites the child to help make a Thunder Cake. She explains that counting after lightning and stopping when thunder sounds tells how many miles away the storm is. The child first counts ten, then nine, eight, seven, six, and five miles as the storm comes closer. Grandma and the child hurry to gather eggs from a pecking hen, milk from a large cow, and ingredients from the dark dry shed. They climb a trellis for tomatoes and pick strawberries. The child remains frightened but does each job with Grandma's gentle help. They mix the ingredients and get the cake into the oven when the storm is three miles away. Grandma points out that the child has been brave. When the storm reaches the farm, they frost the cake and drink tea. The child smiles and is never afraid of thunder again.

A Michigan storm frightens a little child who loves visiting her Russian grandmother, Babushka. video_title: Giraffe Problems by Jory John Read Aloud Video and Post-Reading Questions and Activities

summaries.summary: Edward the giraffe feels unhappy about his very long neck. He thinks everyone stares at it, so he tries scarves, ties, shrubs, ditches, trees, and even the river to hide it. Cyrus explains that he has waited seven days for a banana to fall from a tree, but his short neck cannot reach it. Edward stretches his own long neck and gets the banana for Cyrus. Cyrus enjoys the banana and tells Edward that his neck is impressive because it can reach and grab things. Edward tells Cyrus that his neck is elegant and works well with his shell. At the end, both friends feel good about their necks for once.

Edward is a giraffe who thinks his neck is too long, bendy, narrow, stretchy, and necky. He tries many ways to cover it or hide it because other animals seem to have better-looking necks. Cyrus wishes he had a long neck because he has spent seven days trying to reach one ripening banana on a distant tree. Edward reaches the banana easily and gives it to him. Cyrus eats the banana and realizes that Edward’s long neck is useful and impressive. Edward then looks at Cyrus’s neck in a new way. He says it is elegant, dignified, and a good match for Cyrus’s shell. The two friends discover that each animal has a neck with special qualities. They both begin to feel better about themselves.

Edward the giraffe spends much of his time worrying about his neck. He thinks it looks strange and wishes it were like the necks of zebras, elephants, or lions. video_title: Julius - The Baby of the World by Kevin Henkes

summaries.summary: Before Julius was born, Lily was excited to be a big sister. She gave him things, told him secrets, and sang to him. After he arrived, Lily became jealous. Cousin Garland said Julius had a slimy nose, beady eyes, and fur that needed a diaper change. Lily suddenly defended her little brother. She said his nose was shiny, his eyes sparkly, and his fur smelled like perfume. She showed Garland how special Julius was and made him say, “Julius is the baby of the world.” At last, Lily felt that she and Julius were almost twins.

Lily thought she would be the best big sister before Julius was born. But when the baby came, she took back her gifts, pinched his tail, and said she hated him. She realized that those words sounded wrong when someone else said them. Lily stood up for her brother, praised his shiny nose, sparkly eyes, and perfumed fur, and showed Garland how to admire him. Then Lily called Julius the baby of the world and said they were almost twins.

Julius was a new baby, and Lily did not want to share her family or room with him. She wanted to be the queen, while her parents called Julius beautiful and extraordinary. Cousin Garland then called Julius a silly lump with a slimy nose, beady eyes, and dirty fur. Lily's nose twitched, and she became angry. She said Garland was talking about her brother. video_title: Oh Say Can You Say Di-no-saur  - All About Dinosaurs - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook - NO ADS

summaries.summary: The Cat in the Hat talks about dinosaurs that lived long ago. We know about them because teeth, eggs, and bones became fossils in the muck and stone. video_title: The Sweetest Fig read aloud

summaries.summary: A fussy dentist keeps his apartment perfect and treats his dog, Marcel, very strictly. One morning, an old woman gives him two figs because he will not accept her money. She says the figs can make dreams come true, but he thinks she is crazy. After eating one fig, the dentist dreams that he is wearing only underwear in front of a cafe. The next morning, that strange dream happens, and the Eiffel Tower bends like rubber. He realizes the woman told the truth. He saves the second fig and dreams about being rich. He plans to eat it before sleeping, but Marcel climbs onto the table and eats it instead. Angry, the dentist goes to bed. In the morning, he wakes beneath his bed and sees his own face. When he tries to shout, he can only bark. The transcript ends at this surprising moment.

The story follows a very neat dentist and his little dog, Marcel. The dentist does not like dirt, noise, or dog hairs on his blue suit. An old woman with a toothache visits him and gives him two special figs instead of money. She says they make dreams come true. The dentist eats one fig and later dreams that he is standing in his underwear beside a cafe. Soon, he discovers that the dream has become real, and the Eiffel Tower also bends as it did in his dream. He decides to save the second fig and teaches himself to dream about wealth. Night after night, he imagines speedboats, airplanes, and life on the Riviera. At last, he places the second fig on a dish. Before he can eat it, Marcel chews it up. The dentist becomes furious, but the next morning he has changed places with his dog and can only bark.

A strict dentist receives two figs from an old woman after helping her tooth. She tells him that the figs can make his dreams come true, although he does not believe her. He eats the first fig and dreams about standing in his underwear outside a cafe. The following morning, he really is wearing only underwear, and the Eiffel Tower bends over. The dentist understands that the fig worked. He keeps the second fig while the tower is repaired and reads books about hypnotism. Each night, he repeats that he is the richest man on Earth. In his dreams, he enjoys a speedboat, an airplane, and luxury on the Riviera. He finally prepares to eat the last fig and become rich. However, Marcel reaches the table and eats it. The dentist angrily threatens the dog, then falls asleep. He wakes beneath the bed, sees his own face, and discovers that he can bark instead of speak.

video_title: BATS AT THE BEACH Read Aloud by Mrs. K | Written by Brian Lies | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: When the sun goes down, bats fly out from their homes. They gather buckets, blankets, books, and other things, then fly over the trees to the beach. At lunchtime, they eat beetles, ants, bugs, crickets, moss, pickled slugs, and other treats. Later, they roast bug mallows and listen to the old bats sing. The little bats climb onto leathery laps to rest. When the sky begins to turn purple and morning comes, the bats pack up, say goodbye to their new friends, and fly home. They snuggle together and sleep, dreaming about their wonderful night at the beach.

The beach day for these bats begins at night. As the moon rises, bats leave their barns, caves, and rafters and fly toward the ocean. They carry blankets, towels, books, buckets, and trowels. Soon they reach the shore, feel the warm sand, and spread out their blankets. The bats enjoy lots of beach fun. They scratch in the sand, bury their friends, meet bats from other places, fly like kites, dig caves, surf, and have wingboat races through salty sea spray. Then they share a big meal of insects and other treats. After eating, they roast bug mallows while their cousins play in the ocean. The old bats sing songs, and the little bats rest on their laps. At last, the sun starts coming up. The tired bats pack away their things, help the gulls with a handout, and fly home before daytime. They fall asleep together, happy about their perfect beach night.

A group of bats waits for the moon and then travels to the beach. They fly above dark trees and land where the ocean meets the shore. Their bags hold many things for a fun night, including buckets, trowels, blankets, books, towels, and banjos. At the beach, the bats spread blankets and play in the sand and water. They bury friends, dig caves, make new friends, fly like kites, surf the summer tide, and race wingboats. When they become hungry, they eat baskets of beetles, ants, milkweed bugs, crickets, moss, pickled slugs, damselflies, and salted skeeters. summaries.summary: Sharks are fish that live in every ocean and were on Earth before dinosaurs. Instead of bones, they have soft cartilage, which helps them bend and swim. They can smell tiny amounts of blood, see in dark water, and take a test bite before eating. Different sharks have different teeth for catching, grinding, or ripping food. A shark moves quickly and quietly through the ocean. Sharks have cartilage instead of bones, rough skin, special fins, and many rows of teeth. If a tooth falls out, another tooth moves forward. This story explains many amazing things about sharks. Sharks live in all the oceans, and they have lived on Earth for millions of years. Growing sharks become predators with sharp senses. They can smell one drop of blood in many drops of ocean, see in deep water, and test food with a bite. A little donkey had never been able to carry anyone. Children made him wobble, and his owner called him useless before sending him away. The people eat popcorn and hot dogs, drink from cups, and wear team caps. Down on the field, players catch and throw. Runners race to the bases. Then the bat cracks, and a home run flies. The ball comes down into one lucky fan’s mitt. The fans stand and stretch late in the game. The home team is almost winning, and then it wins. Everyone cheers and chants, “We’re number one!” The crowd says goodbye. When nighttime comes, the story says good night to the teams and the parts of the baseball field. It also says good night to the bat, mitt, popcorn boxes, mascot, fans, friends, cars, and stadium under the stars. At last, it says good night to Daddy, Moon, and baseball in the room.

The baseball game begins at a stadium outside of town. Fans and friends come from far away, walk through the gates, and take their places. They have popcorn, hot dogs, drinks, and caps showing their favorite teams. They watch players catch and throw while runners race across the field. A bat makes a crack, and a ball is hit for a home run. The ball lands in a lucky fan’s mitt. Near the late seventh inning, the fans stand and stretch. The game keeps going while the home team is close to winning. Then the home team wins. The fans cheer and chant, “We’re number one!” The crowd waves goodbye, and the teams are told to sleep well. The nighttime goodbyes continue: diamond, grass, home plate, bat, mitt, popcorn boxes, mascot, fans, friends, cars, and the stadium under the stars. The chicken makes a mistake and says, “I’m no good at this.” The story explains that everybody makes mistakes and that mistakes help us learn. The person has tried their best and may need a rest. While friends sleep, the chicken shares an important idea: kind, encouraging words can help someone who feels blue. The biggest “woohoo” is the one people say to themselves each day. The story ends by reminding everyone that they are doing great and should give themselves a cheer.

At the beginning, someone may feel unsure, unprepared, or overwhelmed by all the things there are to learn. A chicken says it knows what is needed and promises to wave and cheer. The chicken cheers for a person learning to skate, practicing ballet, and baking a cake. It also says “way to tap” and “way to nap,” but then the person wakes the chicken. The chicken feels bad after making a mistake and says it is no good at the activity. Then the story gives a different message: everyone makes mistakes, and mistakes are how we learn. The person has tried their best and might need a rest. While two friends are sleeping, the chicken says that an encouraging word or a kind cheer can help someone who feels sad. Most of all, people should say “woohoo” to themselves each day because they are doing great.

The story begins with questions for someone who feels low, lost, slow, or unsure about what to do. A chicken offers help and says it will wave and cheer. It celebrates many efforts: learning to skate, practicing ballet, and making a cake. The cheering continues with words about tapping and napping. When the chicken is woken up, it says, “Oh no, I made a mistake,” and feels no good at what it did. The story reminds the chicken and everyone else that all people make mistakes and learn from them. After trying their best, a person may also need a little rest. Then, while friends snooze, the chicken shares that kind words and cheers are nice to hear, especially for someone feeling blue. The finest cheer is the one each person gives themselves. The final message is, “Woohooo, you’re doing great,” so remember to cheer for yourself.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  The Old Lady Who Swallowed a FLY

summaries.summary: An old lady swallowed a fly. No one knew why, and perhaps she would die. Then she swallowed a spider that wiggled, jiggled, and wriggled inside her. She swallowed the spider to catch the fly. Next, she swallowed a bird to catch the spider. Then she swallowed a cat to catch the bird. After that, she swallowed a little dog to catch the cat. Each time, she swallowed the animals that came before. She kept trying to catch the fly, even though the fly was still inside her. Then the old lady swallowed a cow to catch the dog. She swallowed the dog, cat, bird, and spider to catch the fly. Finally, she swallowed a horse. The story ends by saying that she was dead, of course.

The story begins with an old lady swallowing a fly. The words say that nobody knows why she swallowed it and that perhaps she will die. Soon, she swallows a spider because she wants to catch the fly. The spider wiggles and wriggles inside her. Then she swallows a bird to catch the spider, a cat to catch the bird, and a little dog to catch the cat. The animals keep forming a funny chain inside the old lady. She continues by swallowing a cow to catch the dog. Then she swallows the dog, the cat, the bird, and the spider to catch the fly. At last, the old lady swallows a horse. The final line says, “She’s dead, of course.”

An old lady starts by swallowing a fly, but she does not know why she did it. She says perhaps she will die. To catch the fly, she swallows a spider. The spider wiggles and wriggles inside her. Next, she swallows a bird to catch the spider. Then she swallows a cat to catch the bird. After the cat, she swallows a small dog to catch the cat. The old lady still wants to catch the fly, so she swallows a cow to catch the dog. She swallows the dog, cat, bird, and spider in turn, trying to reach the fly. video_title: The Day the Crayons Came Home (humorous, colorful adventure) Kids Picture Story Book | Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Duncan and his crayons were coloring when many postcards arrived. The crayons had been lost, forgotten, or hurt. Maroon Crayon was stuck in the couch and had been broken, but Paper Clip helped hold him together. Pea Green changed his name to Esteban and wanted to see the world. Neon Red was left at a hotel pool and began walking home. Yellow and Orange were melted together after being left outside. Tan, or Burnt Sienna, had been eaten by a dog and was covered with carpet fuzz. Glow-in-the-Dark Crayon was forgotten in the basement. Gold was worn down from coloring coins. Turquoise was stuck to a sock after the dryer. A toddler crayon was mistreated by Duncan's baby brother, and Brown was embarrassed by a brown scribble. Duncan gathered the crayons and built a special place where all of them could feel at home.

Duncan received postcards from crayons who needed help. Some crayons had been lost in strange places, such as a couch, a hotel pool, a basement, and a dryer. Yellow and Orange had been melted together, Gold had become blunt from coloring coins, and Tan or Burnt Sienna had been eaten by a dog. A crayon belonging to Duncan's baby brother was tired of being bitten, put in a cat's nose, and used on walls and garbage. Brown wanted Duncan to use him for candy bars, puppies, and ponies instead of a final brown scribble. The crayons slowly made their way home from faraway places. Duncan felt sad about how the crayons had been treated, so he gathered them up. Because they no longer fit in their box, he built a new place where every crayon could feel at home.

A stack of postcards told Duncan that his crayons were unhappy and wanted to come home. Maroon Crayon needed Paper Clip after being broken in the couch. Pea Green became Esteban the Magnificent and ran away. Neon Red was forgotten by a hotel pool but traveled home through many countries. video_title: You Can Do It!

summaries.summary: Lyndon has a painful tooth and accidentally makes a loud duck sound in class. His classmates laugh, and he feels embarrassed. He is also worried because his brother Tony, Sherry, and Lauren seem to know what they want to be when they grow up, but Lyndon does not. Tony reminds him to trust God and dream big. At home, Lyndon's parents learn about the duck sounds and discover that his tooth hurts. Lyndon explains that he likes making people smile, but he does not know his dream. His family prays for him. The next morning, Dad shows Lyndon tiny living things through a microscope and explains that a dream can be big or small, and faith and hard work can help him find it. At the dentist, Lyndon learns many interesting things and sees that Dr. Clark makes people smile. Later, Lyndon decides he wants to become a dentist. Mrs. Lee and Tony tell him they know he can do it, and he does.

At school, Lyndon is having a difficult day. His tooth hurts, and touching his cheek makes him quack like a duck. The children laugh when it happens, and they laugh again when Lyndon says maybe he will be a duck. Lyndon feels even worse because he does not know what he wants to be, while his family members have ideas. Tony encourages him with the words, “You can do it. Trust God and dream big.” Lyndon's parents help his sore tooth and listen to his worries. Tony prays for Lyndon to find his dream. The next morning, Dad takes Lyndon to his science lab before their dentist visit. Dad says a person's “it” is something he loves and has a talent for. At the dentist, Lyndon asks many questions and notices how Dr. Clark helps people smile. During show-and-tell, Lyndon announces that he wants to be a dentist. His teacher and Tony encourage him, and Lyndon reaches his dream.

Lyndon does not know what his dream is. At school, a sore tooth causes him to make a loud duck call, so the other children laugh. He likes making people smile, but he does not want to be known only for quacking. On the walk home, Tony throws him a football and reminds him that he can do whatever he wants if he trusts God and dreams big. At home, Lyndon tells his parents that his tooth hurts and that he feels different because the others know their dreams. His family prays for him. Dad says that people find their dreams in their own time and shows Lyndon a microscope at the science lab. Then Lyndon visits Dr. Clark. The dentist fixes his cavity, answers his questions, and makes him smile. Lyndon realizes that he also likes making people feel good. Weeks later, he tells his class that he wants to become a dentist. Mrs. Lee and Tony say they believe he can do it, and he does.

video_title: ✈️ Pig the Tourist ✈️ Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Pig was a pug who traveled on vacation, but he made every trip difficult. People could make careful plans for a happy holiday, yet Pig destroyed those plans. He behaved badly, broke rules, and ignored traditions. At celebrations, he caused even more trouble. He spoiled parties, parades, and processions with chaos and disrespect. The local people became so unhappy that they gathered together and shouted, “Go away!” Pig did not stop right away. He kept rolling and playing until his wild behavior became impossible to control. Pig wanted to offend people, but every wild party eventually ended. The story says that when someone treats local people badly, they may come back to bite. Later, Pig learned not to ruin a whole holiday. Still, the truth remained: Pig might try to travel, but he did not travel well.

When Pig the pug went on vacation, trouble followed him. Careful travel plans could not keep Pig from ruining the trip. He caused dismay, behaved badly, broke rules, and flaunted traditions. In places where people were celebrating, Pig created great devastation. If he found an ancient taboo to break, he did not think twice. His behavior spoiled parties, parades, and processions. The locals watched his chaos and foul disrespect, and finally they gathered to shout, “Go away!” Pig kept rocking and rolling until his horseplay spun out of control. His need to offend was very large, but the wild party had to end. The story warns that people who treat locals with little regard may be bitten hard. In later days, Pig changed. He learned not to ruin an entire holiday. Even so, he was still not a good traveler, because although he might try, Pig did not travel well.

Pig was a pug with a very bad way of behaving on vacation. People might carefully plan a happy trip, but Pig would make the plans unravel. video_title: Goldi Rocks and the Three Bears

summaries.summary: Three bears played in a band. Papa Bear drummed, Mama Bear strummed, and Baby Bear played the keys. They did not have many fans because they could not sing the very high notes, so they went to find a soprano. Goldie came to their unlocked studio and explored. She tried the microphone, headphones, and instruments. The microphone stand broke, but Baby Bear’s headphones fit her. Goldie sang well, played with the band’s instruments, and fell asleep on Baby Bear’s keys. When the bears returned, they found their things used and saw Goldie sleeping. Papa Bear, Mama Bear, and Baby Bear had a rock-and-roll band, but they needed a singer who could reach high notes. While they were away holding tryouts, Goldie entered their unlocked studio. Goldie enjoyed the music so much that she fell asleep on Baby Bear’s keys. The bears returned after hearing singers who were too twitchy, too pitchy, or simply okay. They were upset to find their studio messy and their belongings used. Then they discovered Goldie. When she woke, she sang a very high note. The bears asked her for a melody and loved what they heard. Goldie joined them, and they wrote and practiced a new song. Their song became a hit, and the band became famous.

A bear family made music together: Papa Bear played drums, Mama Bear played strings, and Baby Bear played the piano keys. Their band needed a soprano because they could not sing the notes high enough. Goldie arrived at their studio and tried to perform. She used the microphone, headphones, and instruments. Some things did not fit or sounded wrong, but Baby Bear’s headphones fit her, and the piano sounded perfectly grand. After moving and grooving, Goldie became sleepy and fell asleep on Baby Bear’s keys. The bears came home from their tryouts and found their studio in a terrible mess. They noticed that Goldie had used their music equipment. Goldie woke with a high scream, and the bears asked her to sing a full melody. Mom, Pop, and Baby Bear were impressed. Goldie joined the band, and they created a new song. They practiced all night, made a hit single, and played for cheering fans across the country.

video_title: 💎 Stories for Kids Read Aloud 💎 Dora the Explorer Crystal Kingdom Adventures [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: The Crystal Kingdom had four special crystals. The yellow crystal made sunshine, the blue crystal made the sky blue, the green crystal made trees green, and the red crystal made the rainbow shine. A greedy king hid all the crystals because he did not want to share. Then the kingdom had no colors, and the people were sad. Ally looked everywhere for the crystals. Dora, Boots, and Map helped her. First, a dragon helped them get the yellow crystal from rocks on a cliff. Next, a butterfly helped them find the green crystal inside a cocoon and gave them wings. The king shared and made Ally queen.

The king said, “Mine, mine, mine,” but they said, “Share, share, share!” He gave them the red crystal. The colors came back, and Ally became queen.

Ally wanted to bring colors back to the Crystal Kingdom. The colors came from four crystals: yellow for sunshine, blue for the sky, green for trees, and red for the rainbow. The king had hidden them because he would not share. Ally looked and looked until Dora and Boots found her. Map showed the friends four places to search. A dragon helped them free the yellow crystal from rocks. In a cave, cocoons opened and a butterfly revealed the green crystal. She also gave the friends wings. The blue crystal was waiting in a magic castle. The king had locked the castle, but the friends flew through a window and found it. The red crystal was in the king’s crown at the top of a volcano. The friends flew there, and the king gave it to them after they asked him to share. All four crystals returned. The kingdom became colorful, and the king made Ally queen.

video_title: Taco Falls Apart

summaries.summary: Taco feels pressured because everyone expects him to stand tall, stay open, and remain strong. One day, the pressure becomes too much, and Taco cracks, tips over, and falls apart. He says he is terrible at being a taco and cannot keep himself together. His food friends feel worried, but Nacho explains that thoughts, feelings, and actions are connected. Taco has a very hard day. He believes the world wants too much from him, so he cracks, falls over, and cannot keep himself together. Taco feels terrible and says that everything he does is terrible. He feels stronger, stands up, and shares a group hug.

At first, Taco tries to meet everyone’s expectations. He must be tall, open, and strong. Then Taco reaches his breaking point and falls apart. The other ingredients help by naming things that make them terrific. The lettuce can be crisp, sour cream gives terrific flavor, and beans are good for the heart. Taco says he will never understand the thinking lesson, but Nacho explains that this thought is not useful or true. Taco also worries that he will fall apart again the next day. His friends remind him that he cannot see the future and should use helpful thoughts. Taco remembers that he can stand together tall and hold everyone together. That thought makes him feel terrific. He stands up, asks everyone to pull it together, and gives them a group hug. Later, Taco still has difficult days, but he can think about what he can do and feel strong.

video_title: Truck Full Of Ducks Read Aloud

video_title: 📚 TOO MUCH GLUE - Kids Books Read Aloud

Maddie’s art teacher warns her that too much glue never dries. Maddie loves glue anyway, and she squeezes glue from several full bottles until decorations float in a glue lake. video_title: All We Need is Love and a Really Soft Pillow! Read Along Video, Questions and Activities!

Each new day is a chance to notice blessings and enjoy time with people we love.

The story begins when Poppy asks the little one what is needed. The little one answers that love is all they need, and then remembers a very soft pillow. As they keep talking, they add things that make life useful or fun: a roof, walls, water, chocolate, a pot, a bathtub, a garden, a fruit tree, books, and a toilet. They name each thing and feel that their life is simple and just right. Then a storm blows in because the roof has a leak. Poppy tells the little one to hold on tightly. The storm takes away all the things they collected. Only Poppy and the little one remain safe because they hold on to a tree with deep roots. Afterward, they rest while wet and tired. The little one says they lost everything, but Poppy reminds them that they still have each other and love. They agree that love is what they need, plus a soft pillow, and they remember to count their blessings.

Poppy and the little one make a long list of things for their sweet and simple life. They start with love and a really soft pillow. Then they decide they also need shelter, water, food, places to cook and bathe, plants, books, and a toilet. Each new item makes their list bigger. At last, they say they have everything they need, including love. But the roof leaks, and a storm comes. Poppy tells the little one to hold on. Wind and rain sweep away their toilet, books, fruit, vegetables, bathtub, cooking pot, chocolate, water, roof, walls, and pillows. Poppy and the little one hold on to a deep-rooted tree, so they are not carried away. When the storm stops, they are wet and weary. They think they lost everything. Then Poppy says they still have each other and love. The little one agrees and remembers the soft pillows. The story ends by saying that every day brings a new chance to count blessings and share the journey with loved ones.

video_title: Storytime! ~ CHRYSANTHEMUM read aloud ~ Story Time ~  Bedtime Story Read Aloud Books

summaries.summary: Chrysanthemum loved her long, special name. Her parents said it was perfect, and she enjoyed hearing it, seeing it on paper, and writing it with her orange crayon. When she started school, Joe, Rita, and Victoria teased her because her name was long and came from a flower. Chrysanthemum felt sad and wished her name were Jane. Her parents comforted her with kind words, hugs, and favorite foods, but the teasing continued. Then a music teacher named Mrs. Twinkle joined the class. Mrs. Twinkle also had a flower name, Delphinium, and said Chrysanthemum was absolutely perfect. Chrysanthemum felt happy and proud again. The children began sharing their own flower names. Chrysanthemum did wonderfully in the school play, and Victoria forgot her lines. Later, Mrs. Twinkle had a baby girl and named her Chrysanthemum too.

When Chrysanthemum was born, her parents chose a beautiful, very long name for her. She thought it was perfect. At school, however, some children laughed and said it would hardly fit on her name tag. Victoria also said that a chrysanthemum was a flower living near worms and dirt. Chrysanthemum became unhappy and dreamed frightening dreams about being picked apart like a flower. Her parents reminded her that her name was beautiful and that it was everything she was. One day, the new music teacher, Mrs. Twinkle, gave the children parts in a musical. The children teased Chrysanthemum again because she was a daisy and had a flower name. Then Mrs. Twinkle explained that her own name was Delphinium and that she loved flower names. Chrysanthemum felt proud. Joe, Rita, and Victoria proudly shared flower names too. Chrysanthemum succeeded in the play, and Mrs. Twinkle later named her baby Chrysanthemum.

Chrysanthemum's parents were delighted when she was born, so they gave her the name Chrysanthemum. She loved every part of her name. She loved how it sounded, how it looked, and how it felt to write. On her first school day, classmates teased her because it had thirteen letters and came from a flower. Chrysanthemum felt her name was dreadful. Her parents helped her feel better with loving words, dinner, dessert, and hugs. Still, the teasing happened again, and Chrysanthemum even had a nightmare about being turned into a flower. Then Mrs. Twinkle became the music teacher. She chose Chrysanthemum to be a daisy in the class musical. When other children laughed, Mrs. Twinkle said that she too had a flower name, Delphinium, and thought it was perfect. Chrysanthemum became happy and confident. The musical was a success, and later Mrs. Twinkle named her new baby girl Chrysanthemum.

video_title: 👸🏻🌋Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Snow White and The Seven Dwarfs

summaries.summary: Snow White meets a handsome prince, and her jealous queen learns that Snow White is now the fairest of all. The queen tells a Huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her. The Huntsman cannot hurt her, so he tells her to run away. Snow White finds a cottage and cleans it with help from forest animals. The cottage belongs to seven Dwarves. They find Snow White sleeping and let her stay. The queen discovers Snow White is alive and disguises herself as an old Peddler woman. She gives Snow White a poisoned apple. Snow White takes a bite and falls asleep. The Dwarves chase the queen, and lightning sends her into the valley. A prince kisses Snow White, breaking the spell. Snow White wakes up, says goodbye to the Dwarves, and leaves with the prince. They live happily ever after in a castle in the clouds.

Snow White wishes for the one she loves and sees a prince near the wishing well. The queen becomes jealous when her mirror says Snow White is more fair than she is. She sends a Huntsman into the forest with Snow White, but he cannot kill the princess. He warns her to hide, so Snow White runs away. Forest animals lead her to a small cottage. She cleans the cottage and falls asleep in three tiny beds. The seven Dwarves come home from their diamond mine and find her. Snow White asks to stay because the queen wants to kill her, and she promises to wash, sew, sweep, and cook. The queen disguises herself as a Peddler woman and offers Snow White a poisoned apple. Snow White eats it and falls. The Dwarves chase the queen away. Later, the prince kisses Snow White, and she wakes up. She goes with him to their castle.

The queen asks her magic mirror who is fairest. When the mirror names Snow White, the queen sends her away with a Huntsman. He feels sorry for Snow White and tells her to hide in the woods. Snow White is frightened, but animals help her find a cottage. There she cleans and waits for its owners. Seven Dwarves arrive and discover the sleeping princess. Snow White tells them the queen may hurt her, so they let her stay. The queen makes a magic potion and becomes an ugly old woman. She visits the cottage with a shiny poisoned apple. Birds try to protect Snow White, but Snow White takes a bite after hearing that the apple can make wishes come true. She falls under a spell. The Dwarves return and chase the queen, who falls into the valley. The prince kisses Snow White, and the spell breaks. She leaves with him, and they live happily ever after.

video_title: ❤️🦫Groundhug Day🦫❤️ Groundhog Day Read Aloud Book for Kids

summaries.summary: Moose planned a big Valentine's Day party with Squirrel, Bunny, and Porcupine. They wanted Groundhog to come, but Bunny explained that Groundhog might see his shadow on Groundhog Day and stay in his hole for six more weeks. The friends made many plans to stop him from seeing the shadow, but they argued all night and missed Groundhog coming out. Groundhog saw shadows everywhere and went back inside. The animals learned that shadows frightened him. Moose and his friends then showed Groundhog dancing leaf shadows, silhouettes, cloud shadows, and shadow puppets. Groundhog enjoyed them, especially the puppets. Later, he said he had to return to his warm hole because winter was cold. The friends gave him hugs and a nose kiss. Six weeks later, Groundhog came out wearing a green hat and invited everyone to a St. Patrick's Day party. Bunny was missing because he was staying in his hole too.

Valentine's Day was coming, and Moose wanted all his friends, including Groundhog, at his party. Bunny worried because Groundhog Day was the next day. If Groundhog saw his shadow, he would return to his hole for six weeks and miss the party. The animals tried to think of ways to hide the shadow, but they argued until morning. Groundhog came out, saw shadows, and hurried back underground. He told Moose that he was afraid of shadows. Instead of hiding them, the friends decided to show Groundhog that shadows could be fun. They made dancing shadows with leaves, drew silhouettes, watched cloud shadows, and created shadow puppets. Groundhog enjoyed the whole day. Even though he was no longer afraid, he still wanted to go home because it was cold outside and his hole was warm. The friends shared warm hugs before he left. Six weeks later, Groundhog came out and planned a St. Patrick's Day party, but Bunny was still in his hole.

Moose wanted to celebrate Valentine's Day with a party, and he hoped Groundhog would attend. The animals remembered that Groundhog might see his shadow and stay underground for six more weeks. They thought about changing his calendar, blindfolding him, covering his hole, or sitting on it. While they argued, morning arrived. Groundhog saw many shadows and went back into his hole. Moose discovered that Groundhog was scared of shadows. The friends then offered to show him wonderful kinds of shadows. Leaves made shadows that danced, Bunny made silhouettes, Squirrel showed cloud shadows, and Porcupine performed shadow puppets. Groundhog had a wonderful time and liked the shadow puppets best. When night came, he returned to his warm hole because the air outside was cold. Before he left, the friends gave him hugs and Porcupine received a special nose kiss. Six weeks later, Groundhog came out for a St. Patrick's Day party, but Bunny stayed underground.

video_title: 🚒🏎️💨 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Pixar Cars : Radiator Springs Road Trip

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen was going to race Chick Hicks in a big Piston Cup race. Sally said Lightning could beat anybody. While looking, Mater found fun antenna balls. Doc heard Chick say he would use a dirty trick and push the rookie off the track. Doc and Mater tried to warn Lightning, but a guard stopped them. Mater cheered Doc with a Lightning antenna ball. Doc joined the pit crew, and Ramone painted “Fabulous Hudson Hornet” on him. Lightning saw his friends and felt their support. He raced fast while Doc warned him about Chick. Lightning was ready, and he sped down the track. Kachow!‍

In Radiator Springs, Lightning McQueen announced a big race against Chick Hicks. His friends wanted to go to California and cheer for him. Sally believed Lightning could win. Mater searched near the Rusty Lightning tent and then followed Flo to find decorations. Chick Hicks was planning to force Lightning off the track. Lightning saw everyone from home and raced with his friends beside him.‍

Lightning McQueen had an important Piston Cup tiebreaker race. His friends in Radiator Springs decided to travel to California so they could cheer for him. The trip was long and hot. Flo had the oil stand, Guido had tires and tools, and Ramon worked on painting. Lightning was hard to find in the crowded speedway. While searching, Mater found souvenirs and picked Lightning antenna balls. Doc then heard Chick Hicks tell his crew about a plan to force Lightning off the track. Doc and Mater tried to warn Lightning, but a guard blocked the press area. Mater gave Doc an antenna ball with Lightning's number. Doc understood that the friends should help their Star Car. video_title: Don't Hug Doug: (He Doesn't Like It). Read Aloud Kids Books

summaries.summary: Doug likes people, but he does not like hugs. Hugs feel too squeezy, squashy, squishy, and smooshy to him. Doug enjoys sorting rocks, trying on socks, drawing with chalk, and listening to harmonica bands. Even on his birthday, people should not hug him. He says no to hello hugs, goodbye hugs, home run hugs, and hugs after dropped ice cream. Doug likes only a gentle bedtime hug from his mom. Other people must ask before hugging. Finn, Grandma Mac Jin, an identical twin, and a child may answer yes or no. Doug’s pot belly pig likes hugs, but people must be gentle because she is scared of strangers. Some people love hugs, some do not, and some like hugs only at certain times. Doug still likes you. He especially likes high fives, including straight, double, low, side, spinny, elbow, jump, granny, piggy, Franken, and puppy high fives.

Doug is a friendly boy who does not want anyone to hug him. He likes his rock, sock, and chalk collections, and he likes harmonica bands. Hugs are too squishy for Doug, so he says no when people ask about hello hugs, goodbye hugs, baseball hugs, and ice cream hugs. The only hug he likes is a gentle bedtime hug from his mom. Before hugging other people, children should ask, “Can I hug you?” Some people say yes, and some say no. Doug’s pot belly pig likes hugs, too, but she needs gentle hugs because strangers make her nervous. People have different feelings about hugs. Some love them, some do not, and some like them only at special times. Doug does like the person listening to his story. He also likes high fives. He can give many kinds, such as low fives, side fives, elbow fives, jump fives, and puppy fives. He says yes to a high five.

The story asks readers not to hug Doug because he does not like hugs. Doug likes many other things, including rocks, socks, chalk, and harmonica bands. He says no to many kinds of hugs, even when someone wants to hug him or when it is his birthday. Doug explains that hugs feel too squeezy, squashy, squishy, and smooshy. He likes one special hug: a gentle bedtime hug from his mom. When people wonder about hugging Finn, Grandma Mac Jin, an identical twin, or another child, the story says to ask first. The person may say yes or no. Doug’s pot belly pig can be hugged gently because she likes hugs but feels scared around strangers. Everyone has different feelings about hugs. Doug does not want a hug, but he does like people and enjoys high fives. He gives many kinds of high fives, and he happily says yes when asked for one.

video_title: 🚘🏎️ Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Junior: Mickey And Friends : Mickey's Perfecto Day!

summaries.summary: Mickey and his friends travel to Madrid for a special day. They want to see the sights, and Donald plans to sing. On the way, a baby bull sees a rose. The rose falls onto Minnie, and Minnie puts it behind her ear. The bull follows the rose to the market. Minnie looks at dresses, but she does not see the bull. Mickey sees him, so Mickey and Minnie ride away in a cart. The cart rolls into a churro cart, and Mickey orders two churros. Later, Donald eats spicy potatoes, and Daisy gives him water. When Donald tries to sing, no sound comes out. Daisy sings with the band, while Donald eats dessert. Then Donald’s voice returns. He joins the band, and the crowd loves the music. Mickey, Minnie, Donald, and their friends go to Madrid. They hope to have a Perfecto day, with Donald singing at a show. A baby bull smells a rose, but the rose falls and lands on Minnie. Minnie wears the rose in her hair, so the bull follows her. At the market, Minnie looks at dresses and does not notice the bull. Mickey notices him. Mickey and Minnie hurry away in a cart, and the cart bumps into a churro cart. They get two churros. At lunch, Donald eats potatoes that are very spicy. Daisy gives him water. Soon it is time for the show, but Donald opens his mouth and no sound comes out. Daisy sings with the band. Donald eats dessert and watches. Then his voice becomes good again, so he joins the band. The baby bull sits by Minnie. Minnie gives him the rose, and he gives Mickey a kiss.

The friends pack up and drive to Madrid. Donald wants to sing, and everyone expects a happy day. A little bull is smelling a rose when the rose falls from a bush. Mickey and Minnie escape in a cart, but the cart rolls into a churro cart. At lunch, Donald tastes potatoes and says they are very spicy. Daisy gives him water. The crowd enjoys the show. The little bull comes near Minnie and smells the rose. Minnie gives him the flower, and the bull kisses Mickey.

video_title: Penguin Problems

summaries.summary: Mortimer the penguin wakes up early and feels unhappy. His beak is cold, the snow is too bright, and he is hungry. He tries to find a fish, but the ocean smells salty and he sinks. When he dives, it is dark, and he sees an orca, a leopard seal, and a shark. Mortimer also dislikes being hunted, waddling, and being unable to fly. He cannot recognize his family because all the penguins look alike. Then a walrus speaks to him. The walrus asks Mortimer to notice the mountains, ocean, blue sky, warm sun, and penguin family around him. Mortimer still has difficult moments, but the walrus says he is exactly where he needs to be. Afterward, Mortimer thinks about the walrus’s words. He realizes that he loves the mountains, ocean, and sky, and that he has friends and family. The penguin world is his only home and life, so he feels that things may work out after all.

Mortimer has many penguin problems. He wakes up when it is too early, and his beak is cold. More snow fell, the snow is too bright, and he wants a fish. The ocean is salty, he sinks, and the water is too dark. An orca, a leopard seal, and a shark make him feel hunted. His flippers ache, and he thinks his waddle looks silly. Mortimer wishes he could fly, but he also feels confused because every penguin looks the same. He even says he does not know which penguins are his mother and father. A walrus notices that Mortimer is having a difficult day. The walrus points out the beautiful mountains reflected in the ocean, the blue winter sky, the warm sun, and the penguins who care about him. Mortimer listens. He remembers that he loves the mountains, ocean, and sky, and that his friends and family are with him. He decides that his home and life may be all right after all.

A penguin named Mortimer complains about nearly everything. He is cold, hungry, and bothered by snow and early darkness. He wants a fish, but the ocean smells salty and he sinks in the water. Diving is dark and dangerous because an orca, a leopard seal, and a shark are nearby. Mortimer dislikes being hunted, sore flippers, and waddling. He wishes he could fly and cannot tell his family apart from other penguins. Mortimer says that nobody cares about his problems. A walrus then talks with him and asks him to look around. The mountains shine in the ocean, the winter sky is blue, the sun warms his back, and his penguin family cares for him. The walrus says that hard moments happen to all animals, but he would not trade his life. Mortimer thinks about this after the walrus leaves. He sees that he loves his surroundings and has friends and family. His home is the only home he has, and he begins to believe life may work out.

video_title: Peppa Pig, Peppa goes on holiday. Children’s bedtime story read aloud in an English accent..

The car’s satnav speaks Italian, and many drivers beep their horns. Peppa then remembers that she left Teddy on the airplane. A kind policeman brings Teddy back to the family. The next day, Gabriella Goat shows them her village. Mommy Pig buys many things, and Gabriella’s uncle teaches Peppa and George how to make pizza. Daddy Pig is stopped by the policeman again, and Teddy is returned once more. When the family goes home, the policeman stops Daddy Pig a third time and tells him to take better care of Teddy. Peppa is happy to see Susie Sheep and play in muddy puddles at home.

Peppa, George, Mommy Pig, and Daddy Pig travel to Italy for a holiday. They take a taxi to the airport, fly in a plane, and ride in a car after they land. Peppa notices that everyone is beeping their horns, but Mommy Pig thinks they are saying hello. Then Peppa remembers that Teddy is missing. A policeman on a motorbike finds Teddy and returns him to Peppa. The family enjoys sightseeing with their friend Gabriella Goat. They see her pretty village, buy things, and learn how pizza is made. Daddy Pig is pulled over again, and Teddy is found in the policeman’s bag. After several days, the family says goodbye and travels home. The policeman stops Daddy Pig one more time and returns Teddy. At home, Susie says it rained. Peppa is glad because she loves muddy puddles even more than holidays.

Peppa’s family packs for a trip and flies to Italy. After landing, they drive away in a car, but the satnav speaks Italian. Peppa hears horns beeping and then remembers that Teddy stayed on the airplane. Soon, a policeman stops Daddy Pig and gives Teddy back to Peppa. During the holiday, Gabriella Goat takes the family around her village. Mommy Pig buys so many things that they need another suitcase. Gabriella’s uncle shows Peppa and George how to put tomato and cheese into an oven to make pizza. On the way back to the holiday house, Daddy Pig is stopped again, and the policeman returns Teddy. When the holiday ends, the family says goodbye and starts for home. Daddy Pig is stopped for a third time, and the policeman asks him to care for Teddy. Peppa hugs Teddy and is excited to return to muddy puddles.

video_title: 🚨 Kids Book Read Aloud: Nickelodeon Paw Patrol : Chase Is On The Case!

summaries.summary: Ryder learns that the lighthouse light is out. Without the light, ships could crash into Seal Island. Captain Turbot calls Ryder, but he cannot find the lighthouse because fog is all around him. The Paw Patrol gets ready to help. Ryder asks Chase to use his searchlight, and the team takes Zuma’s hovercraft to the island. Wally the walrus blocks the way because he wants a treat. Ryder gives him one, and Wally gulps it down. Then the pups reach the island and see a big ship coming. The lighthouse door is locked, so Chase shoots out his net. Ryder climbs up, goes through a window, and unlocks the door. The lighthouse at Seal Island has no light, and ships may crash into the rocks. Captain Turbot is lost in the fog, so he calls Ryder for help. Ryder says the Paw Patrol must fix the lighthouse. Wally gulps the treat, and the pups can go on. When they arrive, a big ship is coming toward the island. Chase tries to help, but the lighthouse door is locked. He shoots out his net, and Ryder climbs up to a window. Ryder unlocks the door. Chase turns on his searchlight, and the ship sees it. The ship turns away from the rocks. Captain Turbot brings a new bulb, and the lighthouse is fixed.

Ryder sees that the lighthouse is dark. The light helps ships stay away from Seal Island, but now a ship could crash. Captain Turbot calls for help, although fog has made him lose the lighthouse. The Paw Patrol answers the call. Ryder asks Chase for his searchlight, and the team uses Zuma’s hovercraft to travel to Seal Island. Wally the walrus stops them because he wants a treat. Ryder gives him a treat, and Wally eats it quickly. Soon the pups reach the island. A big ship is coming, but the lighthouse door will not open. Chase fires his net. Ryder climbs the net, enters through the window, and unlocks the door. Chase turns on his searchlight. The ship sees the light and moves away from the rocks, so it is safe. video_title: The Princess and the Frog | English Fairy Tale Read Aloud for Kids | Let's Read | I Can Read

summaries.summary: A pretty princess had a gold chain that she liked very much. One day, she lost it and cried all day. The king sent his men to look everywhere, but they could not find the chain. Then a frog came to the princess. He said he would find the chain if she let him sleep on her bed. The princess promised that she would. The frog searched everywhere and found the gold chain. He brought it back, and the princess was happy. But when the frog asked to sleep on her bed, she said no because he was dirty and ugly. The sad frog said she had broken her promise and went away. The next day, the princess found him very ill in her garden. She said she was sorry, picked him up, and put him on her bed. The next morning, the frog became a handsome prince. He married the princess, and they lived happily ever after.

There was a pretty princess who owned a gold chain. She loved the chain, but one day it disappeared. The king ordered his men to search for it. They looked everywhere and found nothing, so the princess cried all day. A frog then hopped up to her and offered to find the chain. He asked if he could sleep on her bed when he brought it back. She said he was dirty and ugly and could not sleep on her bed. The frog became very sad and told her that she had broken her promise. The next day, the princess found the sick frog in her garden. A princess lost her favorite gold chain and could not find it, even after the king’s men searched everywhere. She was very sad and cried all day. Then a frog offered to search for the chain. video_title: Last Stop on Market Street (celebrates kindness, empathy, gratitude) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: After church, CJ waits for the bus with his Nana in the rain. He wishes they had a car, but Nana shows him that the bus can bring wonderful things. CJ says he is glad they came, and Nana agrees.

CJ and Nana leave church and wait for a bus in the rain. CJ asks why they do not have a car. Nana says their bus breathes fire and carries them to interesting people. During the ride, CJ notices many passengers. He gives up his seat to a man who cannot see. Nana tells CJ that some people watch the world with their ears and noses. The man enjoys Nana's perfume. Two boys stand in the back, and CJ wishes he had what they have. Nana says CJ already has the real-life thing nearby and suggests asking the guitar player for a song. Music fills the bus. With his eyes closed, CJ imagines beautiful scenes in the sky and sea. At the last stop, the neighborhood looks dirty, but Nana points out its beauty. CJ sees a rainbow over the soup kitchen and says he is glad they came.

Rain falls as CJ and Nana travel from church to the last stop on the bus. CJ feels unhappy because his friends have cars, but Nana helps him notice thirsty trees and the special people on their bus. CJ meets a guitar player, a woman with butterflies, a man with a spotted dog, and other riders. He gives his seat to the man with the dog. The man says that he uses his ears and nose to experience the world. A song begins, and CJ closes his eyes. The music carries his imagination over crashing waves, through sunset colors, and toward hawks and dancing butterflies. CJ gives his coin to the musician when the song is over. Their neighborhood has broken sidewalks and dirty buildings, but Nana tells CJ that dirt can help him notice beauty. video_title: 🎄Christmas in the Big Woods | My First Little House Books Read Aloud for Kids

summaries.summary: Laura lives with her family and their Bulldog Jack in a little log house in the snowy Big Woods. Before Christmas, Ma cooks bread, pies, and cookies. In the Big Woods of Wisconsin, Laura shares a snowy Christmas with her parents, sisters, and Bulldog Jack. Pa returns from shoveling snow and gives Laura a big hug, while Ma prepares many Christmas treats. Laura and Mary help make molasses candy by pouring syrup into snow. They save most of it for Christmas Day. Soon, Aunt Eliza, Uncle Peter, and three cousins arrive by sleigh. The children put on warm clothes and play together in the deep snow. They are excited, but they go to bed after hanging their stockings by the fireplace. On Christmas morning, every child receives red mittens and peppermint candy. Davis is in class with his teacher. She begins by telling him, “No, David,” and gives him several rules. He must not yell, push, or run in the sauce. Because Davis is tardy, he must sit down. video_title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs | Classic Fairy Tale Read Aloud for Kids | Movie Story in 5 Minutes

summaries.summary: Snow White was a beautiful baby whose name came from the soft snow falling when she was born. After her mother died, her father married a queen who was vain and cruel. The queen asked her mirror who was fairest, but one day it answered, “Snow White.” Jealous, the queen told a huntsman to take Snow White away. The huntsman warned her to run, so she fled through the forest and found seven kind dwarfs. The queen tried to hurt Snow White with a tight sash and then a poisoned comb, but the dwarfs saved her both times. At last, the queen gave Snow White a poisoned apple. Snow White fell lifeless, and the dwarfs placed her in a glass coffin. A prince came by after a year and a day. When he lifted Snow White, the apple piece flew from her mouth, and she woke up. Later, Snow White and the prince married, while the seven dwarfs carried her train.

A king and queen had a baby girl named Snow White because snow fell when she was born. The queen died, and the king married another queen with a cold heart. Each morning, the new queen asked her mirror who was fairest. The mirror said Snow White was fairest, so the jealous queen sent Snow White into the forest. A kind huntsman told Snow White to run, and she found a little house where seven dwarfs lived. They welcomed her and promised to care for her. The queen disguised herself and tried to hurt Snow White with ribbons. The dwarfs found Snow White and rescued her. Later, the queen used a poisoned comb, but the dwarfs saved Snow White again. Then the queen gave her a poisoned apple, and Snow White fell to the ground. The dwarfs put her in a glass coffin. A prince found her after a year and a day. The apple flew out when he lifted her, and Snow White woke up. They married a year later.

Snow White grew into a sweet and kind girl, but the new queen became jealous when the magic mirror said Snow White was the fairest. The queen ordered a huntsman to leave Snow White in the forest. Instead, he told Snow White to run. She ran until she found seven dwarfs in a little house. The dwarfs listened to her story and invited her to stay. The queen kept trying to find her. First, she used a sash that made Snow White collapse. Then she came with a glittery comb filled with poison. The dwarfs rescued Snow White from both tricks. Finally, the queen brought a poisoned apple and told Snow White to try it. Snow White took one bite and fell lifeless. The dwarfs were very sad, so they placed her in a glass coffin. A prince rode past after a year and a day. He lifted Snow White, and the apple piece flew out. Snow White opened her eyes. She and the prince married, and the seven dwarfs carried her train.

video_title: The Day it Rained Hearts (celebrates thoughtfulness and the joy of giving personalized gifts) #kids

summaries.summary: One day, hearts began falling from the sky where Cornelia Augusta lived. She caught one, then another, and then many more. Cornelia thought Valentine’s Day must be near, so she decided to use the hearts to make cards. She noticed that every heart looked different. She studied them from the front, back, and side, choosing special hearts for her friends. She threaded seven hearts together for one person. For another card, she pasted a handsome heart onto paper and added a soft, white cotton ball. She had eight hearts left. She cut circles from the biggest heart and arranged the small hearts on paper. Then she painted colorful patterns around them and folded the paper. She stamped and mailed all her Valentines. The rain of hearts never came again, but Cornelia kept finding other ways to make Valentines in the years that followed.

Cornelia Augusta had a surprising day when hearts started raining down. She caught several hearts because catching them was easy. Thinking about Valentine’s Day, she began making presents for her friends. First, she examined every heart carefully because no two hearts were the same. She chose seven similar hearts, joined them with needle and thread, and knew who should receive them. Next, she used a particularly handsome heart to make a card. She pasted it on paper and glued a very white, very soft cotton ball in its center. Then she worked with eight more hearts. She cut circles from the largest one, placed the tiny hearts on paper, painted colorful designs around them, and folded the paper. Cornelia Augusta knew who would get these cards. She put stamps on each Valentine and mailed them. Hearts did not rain again in her home, but every year afterward she discovered new ways to make Valentines.

The sky brought Cornelia Augusta a wonderful surprise: it began raining hearts. She caught many of them and decided they would become Valentine cards. Cornelia looked carefully at each heart from every side and matched them with her friends. Seven hearts that looked almost alike were tied together with thread. She also made a card from a handsome heart, paper, and a soft white cotton ball. Eight hearts remained. Cornelia drew circles on the biggest heart and cut them out carefully. Because the other hearts were small, she placed them all on one piece of paper. She painted many-colored patterns around them and folded her design. She was sure about who should receive the cards. Then she stamped every Valentine and mailed them. After that day, hearts never rained again where Cornelia lived. Still, she was not worried. The next year, and every year after, she found other ways to create Valentines.

video_title: THERE WAS AN OLD MUMMY WHO SWALLOWED A SPIDER ~ Halloween Stories for Kids ~ Children's Halloween

summaries.summary: An old mummy swallows a spider, though nobody knows why. Then he swallows a rat to chase the spider. Next, he swallows a crow to poke the rat. A funny old mummy begins by swallowing a spider. He does not know why he swallowed it, but he opens his mouth wider. Soon he swallows a rat so it can chase the spider. At the end, the mummy says the story is true and tells everyone to look out, because he may swallow them too. He finishes with a loud boo.

There was an old mummy with a very wide mouth. First, he swallowed a spider. Then he swallowed a rat to chase the spider, and a crow to poke the rat. The mummy kept repeating that he did not know why he swallowed the spider. After swallowing all these things, he said the story was true. He warned that he might swallow the listener too. The silly mummy ended by opening wider and saying, “Boo!”

video_title: 📸🎥 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse : Snap Goes The Camera

Minnie wants to join Daisy's funniest-photo contest. She grabs her camera and searches the clubhouse for funny pictures. First, she sees Donald working with an unusual watering can. video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Curious George and The Pizza Party by H.A. Ray & Margret Ray

summaries.summary: George is a curious little monkey who is very excited to go to a girl's pizza party. He puts on a white chef's hat and an apron. video_title: If I Ran the Zoo (Classic Seuss). Read Aloud Kids Books. Dr.Seuss's Books

Young Gerald McGrew looks at a zoo and decides it needs more exciting animals. He imagines opening the cages and starting again with creatures nobody has seen before. Gerald McGrew imagines being the keeper of a very special zoo. He believes ordinary lions and tigers are not enough, so he dreams of collecting the strangest animals in the world. Gerald would search in cold places, high mountains, deep caves, far islands, and thick jungles. video_title: Penguin Problems (meaningful lesson about gratitude & perspective) #readaloud #reading #story #books

summaries.summary: Mortimer the penguin wakes up early and immediately notices many problems. His beak is cold, the snow is too bright, and he is hungry for a fish. The ocean tastes salty, and he sinks when he tries to swim. Under the water, it is dark, and he sees an orca, a leopard seal, and a shark. Mortimer also dislikes being hunted, waddling, and looking like all the other penguins. He cannot even recognize his own parents. Then a walrus speaks to him. The walrus says that life can be difficult, but Mortimer should notice the mountains, ocean, sky, warm sun, and penguin family around him. Mortimer thinks about the walrus's words. He realizes that he loves his home, friends, and family. His beak is still cold, and it still gets dark early, but he begins to feel that things may work out after all.

Mortimer says that being a penguin is full of problems. He is cold, hungry, and bothered by the snow and bright light. He wants a fish, but the ocean is salty, and swimming is hard because he sinks. When he goes down into the water, he meets dangerous animals. Mortimer also complains that his flippers ache, that he waddles too much, and that he cannot fly. Since all the penguins look alike, he cannot tell which penguins are his parents. A walrus hears him and gently asks him to look around. The walrus points out the beautiful mountains reflected in the ocean, the blue winter sky, the warm sun, and the penguins who love him. The walrus says that everyone has difficult moments, but he would not trade his life for another one. Mortimer thinks about this and remembers that the penguin world is his home. He still has small problems, but he feels better about his life.

A young penguin named Mortimer feels unhappy from the moment he wakes up. His beak is cold, he does not like the snow, and he cannot find a fish to eat. The ocean seems too salty, swimming makes him sink, and the dark water contains an orca, a leopard seal, and a shark. Mortimer says that he is hungry, his flippers hurt, and he looks silly when he waddles. He wishes he could fly and is confused because the penguins all look the same. Then a walrus talks with him about the good things nearby. The mountains look like a painting in the ocean, the winter sky is blue, the sun warms his back, and his penguin brothers, sisters, and elders adore him. Mortimer listens and thinks about his home. He loves the mountains, ocean, sky, friends, and family. His beak remains cold, but he decides that perhaps life will work out.

video_title: The Velveteen Rabbit Read Aloud

A flower grows from his tear, and a fairy appears. She takes him to the wild rabbits and makes him real to everyone. In spring, the boy sees a rabbit that looks like his old friend. It is the velveteen rabbit, who has returned to see him.

The velveteen rabbit begins as a soft, beautiful toy in a Christmas stocking. After the boy receives many presents, he forgets the rabbit, and the proud toys ignore him. The Skin Horse tells him that love makes a toy real. Soon the boy chooses the rabbit for his bed and plays with him every day. They make tunnels, visit the garden, and share happy adventures. The rabbit's fur wears away, but the boy loves him even more and says, “He is real.” When two wild rabbits meet him, they tease him because he cannot hop like them. The rabbit feels sad, but he remains the boy's loving companion. Then the boy becomes ill, and the rabbit is sent away to be burned because the doctor fears germs. A nursery fairy finds him and changes him into a real rabbit. He learns to hop with the wild rabbits. Much later, the boy sees him in the woods and recognizes his old bunny.

The Skin Horse teaches the velveteen rabbit that being real comes from being deeply loved, not from how a toy is made. The boy loves the rabbit, sleeps with him, whispers to him, and carries him everywhere. Their friendship makes the rabbit real to the boy, even though his fur fades, his whiskers disappear, and his body becomes shabby. When the boy gets scarlet fever, the rabbit is placed in a sack with toys that must be burned. He remembers all the wonderful times he and the boy shared and sheds a real tear. A magical flower grows, and the nursery fairy comes out. She explains that loved toys are changed into real creatures when children no longer need them. She carries the rabbit to the forest and gives him real fur, ears, whiskers, and hind legs. The rabbit joins the wild rabbits. In the spring, he returns to the woods, where the boy sees him and remembers his beloved bunny.

video_title: 🚓🐒 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse : The Mystery of the Missing Muffins

Mickey had six warm muffins for his friends. A fan cooled the muffins while Goofy held them. Then a doorbell rang. Donald arrived hungry, but the muffins were missing. Mickey and Donald became detectives. They found a handprint and followed crumbs to a little door. They checked Goofy with a measuring tape, but he was too big for the door. They also found a wooden box and a mud puddle. The Clubhouse door was locked, so they used a triangle key to open it. Donald looked at the friends. Minnie had no mud, while Daisy had mud on her. Donald said Daisy took the muffins, but Daisy said she did not. Daisy matched a puzzle box to the muffin tray. When she turned on the fan, the box moved. The muffins were inside the muddy box. video_title: The Pigeon Needs a Bath | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

A pigeon tries many excuses to avoid taking a bath. He says he is clean, says he bathed recently, and says his smell is normal for a pigeon. He even says that bathing can be impolite in some places. When flies buzz around him, he calls them a coincidence. At last, he agrees to take a bath, though he expects not to like it. The pigeon complains about the water again and again. video_title: Clark the Shark (teaches impulse control-time & place etiquette) #kids #story #books #reading #learn

Clark the Shark has a happy life at Theodore Rooster Fish Elementary. He enjoys his teacher, his friends, and school games. Clark makes rhymes so he can remember to stay cool. In class, he says, “When teacher’s talking, don’t go walking.” At lunch, he remembers to munch only his own lunch. At playtime, he says, “Easy does it,” and his friends let him join them. Then a new squid named Sid breaks the playground. Clark understands that Sid wants to play, so he invents games for him. Clark the Shark loves school with all his heart. He loves reading, lunch, games, and being with his friends, but he is often too loud and too rough. The fish around him become unhappy, and even Joey tells Clark to cool his jets. Clark asks Mrs. Inky Dink what is wrong. She says he does many things too hard and reminds him that there is a time and a place for everything. Clark first tries to stay cool, but he pushes a swing too hard, eats many lunches, and becomes excited by a book. Then he creates rhymes to guide himself. He learns to sit during lessons, eat only his own lunch, and play gently. His friends return to him. One day, Sid the Squid arrives and accidentally damages the playground. Instead of being afraid, Clark plays energetic games with Sid and helps him settle down. Clark says that staying cool is important, but sometimes a shark must help.

video_title: How Do Apples Grow? (nature’s wonders both fun and informative) Kids Picture Story Book | Read Aloud

summaries.summary: An apple begins as a flower on an apple tree. In winter, tiny leaf buds and flower buds wait under the cold snow. When spring brings warmer, longer days, the buds open. Green leaves and pink-and-white flowers appear. The flowers have male and female parts. Bees visit the flowers to collect nectar, and pollen sticks to their bodies. When bees fly to another apple tree, pollen reaches the flower's sticky tubes. The male cells travel to the ovary and join the female cells. Then the flower is fertilized, its petals fall, and an apple starts growing where the flower meets the stem. The ovary becomes the apple's core and seeds, while the white part swells around it. Leaves use sunlight, water, and air to make sugar for the fruit. Apples grow all summer, become sweet in fall, and are picked when ripe. Their seeds can grow into new trees.

In winter, an apple tree may look bare, but tiny buds are waiting inside. In spring, sunlight, warmth, and longer days open the leaf buds and flower buds. Pink-and-white flowers bloom on the twigs. Each flower can become an apple. Bees help this happen. They collect sweet nectar and carry pollen from one apple tree to flowers on another tree. The pollen travels through tiny tubes to the ovary, where male cells join female cells. After the flower is fertilized, the petals fall away. The ovary grows into the apple's core, and the rest of the fruit grows around it. The apple has seeds inside, and those seeds may grow into new apple trees. Leaves make sugar from sunlight, water, and air to feed the growing fruit. Through summer, apples get bigger and sweeter. In fall, their skins may turn red or yellow, or remain green. Ripe apples are picked.

The story explains how an apple grows from a flower. During winter, an apple tree holds tiny leaf buds and flower buds. In spring, the buds open, leaves appear, and bunches of small flowers bloom. The flowers smell sweet and attract bees. Each flower contains male parts that make yellow pollen and a female part called a pistol, which has tubes leading to an ovary. Bees carry pollen from a different apple tree. The pollen reaches the sticky tops of the tubes, and male cells travel down to join female cells in the ovary. Then the petals fall, and the fertilized ovary begins to grow into an apple. The ovary becomes the core, and seeds form inside it. Leaves make sugar to feed the fruit. Apples grow during summer and become sweet in fall. Some turn red, some yellow, and some stay green. People pick ripe apples, while fallen seeds may grow new trees.

video_title: How Many Seeds in a Pumpkin? (Don't judge a pumpkin—or a person—by its size) #toddlers #kindergarten

summaries.summary: Charlie was the smallest child in Mr. Tiffen’s class, and he was always at the front or back when the children lined up. The children made groups so they could count faster. Some counted by twos, some by fives, and Charlie counted by tens. The big pumpkin had 340 seeds, and the medium pumpkin had 316. Charlie discovered that the little pumpkin had 350 seeds—the most of all! Mr. Tiffen explained that size does not always show how many seeds a pumpkin has. To count them, the children formed clubs. One club counted by twos, another by fives, and Charlie’s club counted by tens. The big pumpkin had 340 seeds. The medium pumpkin had 316 seeds. Charlie counted 35 groups of 10 in the little pumpkin and found 350 seeds. His small pumpkin had the most. Mr. Tiffen said that a pumpkin’s size is not the only clue. Its lines and time on the vine can matter too. Charlie proudly led the children home.

Mr. Tiffen asked his class, “How many seeds are in a pumpkin?” The children had many guesses, but they could not know the answer until they opened the pumpkins. Mr. Tiffen explained that pumpkins can have clues on their skin. More outside lines can mean more rows of seeds inside, and a pumpkin that grows longer can become darker and get more lines. video_title: The Not Very Merry Pout-Pout Fish #kids #story #christmas #kidslearning #readaloud #christmasgifts
