summaries.summary: A color pipe begins blocked, so the reader shakes and turns the book to help. Red appears first, followed by yellow. Red and yellow make orange, but too much yellow must be dumped. Yellow then reaches blue, and the colors make green. Green takes over while blue nearly disappears. The reader drains blue, but it drips onto red and becomes purple. Finally, the pipes break and colors explode everywhere, so the book must be shut.

The book starts with blocked color pipes. Shaking it releases red, and turning it straight allows yellow to pour out. Red and yellow mix into orange. After some yellow is removed, yellow reaches blue and creates green. Green spreads until blue is almost gone. Draining blue saves it briefly, but blue smears across red and turns purple. A loud spray follows, and the broken pipes send colors everywhere. The only solution is to shut the book.

The reader helps unblock a colorful pipe system by shaking and turning the book. Red and yellow mix to make orange. Then yellow meets blue and makes green, which begins taking over. The reader drains blue, but the blue falls onto red and changes into purple. Soon the pipes make loud whooshing and splatting sounds. The pipes break, colors explode, and the reader quickly shuts the book.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: A child gets a pet unicorn and learns why people warn against letting unicorns scribble. The unicorn eats a crayon, so the child demonstrates how crayons work. The unicorn eats another crayon because she cannot hold it properly. The child ties crayons to her horn, and glittering rainbow scribbles burst everywhere. Expecting trouble, the child explains the mess to her mother. Instead of becoming angry, Mom reveals that the scribbles are a glowing masterpiece on the easel.

The child wants to understand why a unicorn should never scribble. First, the unicorn eats a pink crayon. After watching the child make different scribbles, she eats part of a teal crayon too. The child decides that the problem may be holding crayons, so crayons are tied to the unicorn’s horn. Sparkling scribbles cover the room. Mom sees the result and says it is not a mess but a masterpiece. The child realizes great art can begin with a scribble.

A unicorn seems unable to use crayons because she keeps eating them. Her owner tries teaching her by making colorful scribbles, then attaches crayons to her horn. The unicorn creates a shower of glittering rainbow marks, apparently covering the room. The child apologizes to Mom, but Mom finds that the marks are actually gathered on the easel and form amazing art. The experience shows that even unusual artists need a chance to begin.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Zoe wakes her mother and spends a busy day with her. At the library, she reads quietly; at the park, she runs; at Grandma’s house, she splashes. At school, she paints on paper. She plays outside the store and climbs during a couch-fort play date. Each place has a rule, but Mom shows Zoe where she can be wild. At bedtime, Mom says there are no more adventures today, then encourages Zoe to dream wild.

Zoe and her mom enjoy many activities from morning until night. They visit the library, park, and Grandma, then go to school for painting. Zoe also walks Buttons, plays near a store, and builds a couch fort. Zoe repeatedly asks whether she can be noisy, run, splash, paint, play, or climb. Mom explains that every place has limits, but there are proper places for each kind of fun. Finally, Zoe goes to sleep and dreams.

A sunny morning begins Zoe’s day of adventures. She follows quiet behavior at the library, stays off the grass at the park, keeps wet shoes away from Grandma’s house, and paints on paper at school. Later she plays, climbs, and enjoys time with her mother and friends. At bedtime, Mom stops the day’s adventures but gives Zoe one final freedom: she may dream as wildly as she wishes.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Leo has so much work that he wishes there were two of him. Soon many extra Leos appear, but the growing group only finds more tasks and becomes busier. Leo grows exhausted and takes a nap. The others scold him because dreaming is not on their list. Leo realizes that multiplying himself has not solved the problem. As the extra Leos disappear, he decides to do less, do his best, and keep time for dreaming.

A long list makes Leo feel that one person cannot finish everything. Two Leos become three, then ten, yet the work continues to grow. The Leos organize, rush, and refuse to rest. Tired Leo secretly naps and says he was dreaming. The others reject this because it was not listed. Leo keeps smiling as they vanish, then chooses a simpler life with one Leo working carefully and having time to dream.

Leo is busy and believes more copies of himself will make life easier. Extra Leos arrive one after another, but each adds to the frantic work. When Leo pauses for a dream, the others complain. Their reaction helps him understand that a crowded schedule is not the answer. He asks what would happen if he did less but did his best. In the end, one Leo is enough.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Ken and his little sister Jen pretend to cook a chocolate cake during a tea game. Ken uses dirt, sand, nuts, and berries, while Jen adds water and leaves. When Jen pours too much water, the mixture becomes mushy, so Ken fixes it with sand. They put the pretend cake in the sun. When it is done, Mommy and Daddy ask for pieces, but Jen asks for a donut. Both children receive donuts.

Ken decides to make a chocolate cake from outdoor materials. Jen joins him and pours in water, but she pours too quickly and makes mush. Ken adds sand to repair the cake, then they decorate it with nuts, berries, and leaves. After mixing, they place the pan in the sun. Their parents want cake, but Jen wants a donut, so Mommy gives both children donuts.

While playing, Ken cooks a pretend cake and lets Jen help. Dirt forms the cake, water makes the mixture mushy, and sand saves it. Ken adds nuts and berries, while Jen adds leaves. They stir everything and leave the pan in the sun. When the cake is ready, their parents ask for some. Jen chooses a donut instead, and Ken receives one too.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: A boy has no toys, so he watches other children at the park. One day he finds an unusual stick with words about imagination carved into it. When he holds it, he pretends to be many different people. The stick inspires him as he grows up, and he becomes successful while giving to others. As an old man, he leaves the stick for a girl who has no toys. She discovers her own imagination.

The boy feels sad because he lacks toys. A magical stick changes that by helping him imagine being a pirate, player, knight, fisherman, and explorer. The message carved on it guides him throughout his life. He grows into a generous man with a home and a successful life. Later, he notices a lonely girl under the same tree and gives her the stick so imagination can help her too.

A child without toys finds a stick beneath a park tree. The stick’s message teaches him that imagination can help him become anything. He uses it in many places and carries its inspiration into adulthood, where he works hard and helps others. When he becomes old, he sees another child without toys and leaves the stick for her. She picks it up and begins imagining new lives.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Mr. Fairy feels useless because he cannot perform the jobs of other fairies. He leaves his forest and enters a gray city where people are unhappy. By waving his wand, he adds color, makes people laugh on a train, and turns umbrellas into cotton candy. When he returns, his forest friends have lost their laughter. Mr. Fairy restores their joy and discovers his own special gift: spreading happiness.

Unlike the other fairies, Mr. Fairy cannot wake animals, make kisses happen, or heal boo-boos. Feeling sad, he travels to a gloomy city. There he brings bright colors to a wall, tickles passengers into laughter, and changes umbrellas into giant pink candy balls. Back home, he finds his friends unhappy. His wand brings back their colors and smiles, showing that his special magic is joy.

Mr. Fairy believes he is the fairy of nothing because his magic does not work like other fairies’ magic. In a gray city, he experiments and discovers that he can make people smile and laugh. When his forest friends later lose their happiness, he uses the same magic to help them. Mr. Fairy finally understands that making others happy is an important kind of magic.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: A boy on a river island sees floods destroy trees and leave animals homeless. The village elders give him twenty bamboo saplings, and he plants and waters them every day. To help more plants grow, he carries soil-making materials and seeds from other villages. Over many years, his small planting becomes a large forest. Animals return, and he solves problems by adding grasses and fruit trees. He also protects the forest from cutting and hunting.

Floodwaters are shrinking the boy’s island and destroying animal homes. He begins with twenty bamboo plants and patiently cares for them. He builds a watering system, improves the sandy soil, and brings seeds from nearby places. The bamboo patch becomes a forest filled with many kinds of wildlife. Tigers and elephants cause difficulties, but the man responds by planting food for them. His continued work creates the Molai Forest.

Jadav Molai Payeng loves trees and worries when floods destroy the island’s forest. He starts planting bamboo on a barren sandbar. Daily watering, richer soil, and new seeds help the plants spread. Years later, a large forest supports buffalo, rhinos, birds, elephants, and other animals. Jadav protects the forest when people want to cut or hunt there, and his persistence turns an empty sandbar into a living home.

video_title: Creativity Stories for Kids | Animated Read Aloud Kids Books | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: Willa loves the wind and wishes she could fly like leaves. She tries running down a hill, jumping from a swing, and riding a giant paper airplane, but none of these plans works. Her father helps her stand on his shoulders. A gust makes her feel like she is flying, but he catches her when she falls. Dad explains that freedom and courage are already inside her.

Willa watches leaves dance in the wind and wants to do the same. Her cape, swing, and paper airplane all fail to lift her. Feeling disappointed, she accepts her father’s idea and stands on his shoulders with her arms out. The wind gives her a moment of flight, and Dad catches her safely. He tells her that she is free and that the wind is in her heart.

A girl tries three ways to fly: running with a cape, leaping from a swing, and jumping in a paper airplane. Each attempt fails. Her father then holds her ankles while she balances on his shoulders. When a strong gust arrives, she feels airborne, though she later falls into his arms. Willa learns she does not need to become the wind; bravery and freedom are already part of her.

video_title: 🐷 The 3 Ninja Pigs—Kids Book Short Funny Three Little Pigs Read Aloud Story

summaries.summary: A wolf liked to huff and puff and knock down houses, so three little pigs decided to learn ninja skills. Pig One tried aikido, but he became bored and quit. Pig Two studied jujitsu, learned some blocks and punches, and then stopped studying because he thought he was ready. Pig Three practiced karate every day. She learned many moves, earned her last belt, and felt ready to face the wolf. The wolf came to Pig One’s straw house, and Pig One missed when he tried to hit him. Then the wolf knocked down Pig Two’s door, and Pig Two’s kick failed. The pigs ran to Pig Three. She bowed politely, did flips and kicks, and broke a pile of bricks. The wolf saw that Pig Three was stronger than he was and ran away. The pigs returned to school, trained hard, earned degrees, and opened their own dojo. Their lives became wolf-free.

Three little pigs were tired of a wolf who blew houses down. They agreed to train at a ninja school. The first pig took aikido lessons, but he got bored and left quickly. The second pig learned jujitsu and could block and punch, but he also quit before studying enough. The third pig chose karate. She trained for months, practiced every move, earned her belt, and learned to break boards. Soon the wolf visited the pigs. Pig One tried to fight him, but missed. Pig Two tried a flying kick, but the wolf dodged it and knocked down the door. The pigs escaped to Pig Three’s house. Pig Three showed the wolf her back flips, butterfly kicks, and powerful karate. She struck a stack of bricks and split it apart. The wolf became afraid and ran away. The pigs cheered, went back to school, and trained until all three earned degrees. Then they ran a dojo together.

The three pigs wanted to stop a bully wolf, so each pig went to ninja school. Pig One learned a little aikido but quit when the drills became boring. Pig Two learned jujitsu and believed he was ready after learning to block and punch, even though his teacher told him to study more. Pig Three worked hard at karate. She practiced without stopping, mastered her moves, paid her dues, and earned her final belt. When the wolf came, Pig One missed his punch. The wolf chased him to Pig Two, blew down the door, and dodged Pig Two’s kick. Both brothers ran to their sister. Pig Three politely bowed and showed the wolf her flips, kicks, and strength. She smashed a stack of bricks with one mighty strike. The wolf knew he was outmatched, so he ran away. The brothers celebrated with Pig Three. Then all three pigs returned to training, earned degrees, and ran a dojo where wolves no longer bothered them.

video_title: 🐖 A Very Mercy Christmas 🐖 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Stella Endicott feels joyful and hopes something miraculous will happen, so she decides to go caroling. Her brother Frank says she needs a plan, but Stella visits the Watsons instead. Mr. Watson is struggling with a fruit cake, so Mercy the pig goes with Stella. Eugenia Lincoln does not want to carol with a pig, and Horus Broom is too busy studying the planets. Stella feels less joyful, but she decides to sing alone. She sings “Joy to the World,” and Mercy makes a beautiful, hopeful sound. General Washington the cat joins in, and Maybelline the horse sings too. They search for Leroy Ninker while singing “Deck the Halls.” Soon Frank, the Watsons, Baby Lincoln, and Horus join them. Leroy arrives after finding his horse, and everyone sings together. Eugenia plays “Silent Night” on her accordion. Stella realizes that something miraculous has happened as the stars shine above them.

Stella wants to share Christmas joy by singing carols. Frank thinks caroling needs careful planning, but Stella goes to the Watsons and asks them to join her. Their fruit cake is causing trouble, so Mercy the pig comes along. The Lincoln family does not join, and Horus Broom says he is busy watching the sky. Stella wonders if one person can carol, then begins singing with all her might. Mercy sings too, making a sound filled with hope and wonder. General Washington adds a long meow, and Maybelline the horse joins the song. The group sings loudly while looking for Leroy Ninker. Afterward, Frank and several neighbors arrive and sing “God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen.” Leroy appears because he has found his horse, and he sings with everyone. Horus talks about the music of the stars. The friends return to the Watsons’ home, where Eugenia plays “Silent Night.” Stella sees the shining stars and knows a miracle has happened.

On a cold, dark Christmas evening, Stella Endicott feels happy and wants to sing. She asks Frank to go caroling, but he says she needs a plan. Stella gathers Mercy the pig, then tries to invite Eugenia Lincoln and Horus Broom. Neither one joins at first. Stella becomes a little sad, but she keeps going with Mercy and General Washington the cat. When Stella sings “Joy to the World,” Mercy begins to sing in her own special way. The cat meows, and Maybelline the horse joins them. Together they sing “Deck the Halls,” though their music is loud and not very musical. In the quiet afterward, Stella hears her name. Frank, the Watsons, Baby Lincoln, and Horus come to sing with her. Leroy Ninker arrives after finding Maybelline. Everyone sings together, and Horus explains that the universe may have music of its own. Eugenia finally plays “Silent Night,” and the group stands beneath bright stars. Stella feels sure a miracle has happened.

video_title: Goodnight Moon

summaries.summary: In a great green room, there is a telephone, a red balloon, and a picture of a cow jumping over the moon. Three little bears sit on chairs. Two little kittens, mittens, a little toy house, a young mouse, a comb, a brush, and a bowl of mush are there too. A quiet old lady whispers, “Hush.” Then the room says good night to many things. It says good night to the room and moon, the cow and the light, the bears and chairs, the kittens and mittens, the clocks and socks, the little house and mouse, the comb and brush, nobody, and the mush. It also says good night to the old lady who is whispering. At the end, the stars, the air, and all the noises everywhere receive a good night.

A quiet good-night scene takes place in a great green room. Inside are a telephone and a red balloon. There is a picture of a cow jumping over the moon. Three bears sit on chairs, and two kittens are near mittens. A little toy house, a young mouse, a comb, a brush, and a bowl of mush are also in the room. An old lady whispers, “Hush.” The good-night words begin with the room, the moon, and the cow. Then the light, balloon, bears, chairs, kittens, and mittens are named. The clocks and socks are named next. The little house, mouse, comb, and brush are next. Good night is said to nobody and to the mush. The old lady is included too. Finally, the stars, the air, and every noise everywhere are told good night.

The story shows many things in one green room at night. A telephone and red balloon are there, along with a picture of a cow jumping over the moon. Three little bears sit on chairs. Two little kittens, a pair of mittens, a toy house, and a young mouse are there. A comb, a brush, and a bowl full of mush are also in the room. A quiet old lady whispers, “Hush.” One by one, the story says good night. It says good night to the room, moon, cow, light, and balloon. It says good night to the bears, chairs, kittens, and mittens. It says good night to the clocks and socks, then the little house and mouse. The comb, brush, nobody, and mush receive good nights. The old lady, stars, air, and noises everywhere are named at the end.

video_title: The Napping House

summaries.summary: There is a quiet house where everyone is sleeping. A granny sleeps on a cozy bed. A dreaming child sleeps on the granny. A dozing dog rests on the child, and a snoozing cat rests on the dog. A little mouse sleeps on the cat. Then a flea is awake on the mouse. The flea bites the mouse. The mouse scares the cat. The cat claws the dog. The dog thumps the child. The child bumps the granny. The granny breaks the bed. Suddenly, the cozy bed is broken, and no one in the napping house is sleeping anymore.

In a napping house, everyone is asleep. A snoring granny lies on a cozy bed. A dreaming child lies on the granny. A dozing dog lies on the child, and a snoozing cat lies on the dog. A slumbering mouse lies on the cat. Then an awake flea appears on the mouse. The flea bites the mouse, and the mouse scares the cat. The cat claws the dog. The dog thumps the child. The child bumps the granny. The granny breaks the bed. The house is no longer quiet. The bed is broken, and everyone who had been sleeping is awake.

A house is called the Napping House because everyone is sleeping. A cozy bed holds a snoring granny. A dreaming child is on the granny. A dozing dog is on the child, a snoozing cat is on the dog, and a slumbering mouse is on the cat. Then a flea is awake on the mouse. The wakeful flea bites the mouse. The mouse scares the cat, the cat claws the dog, and the dog thumps the child. The child bumps the granny, and the granny breaks the bed. At the end, the bed is broken, and no one is sleeping in the Napping House.

video_title: 🧛🏽 Stories for Kids Read Aloud 🧛🏽 Asiago by Adam McHeffey [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Asiago is a young vampire who lives with his great uncle Gouda. One hot day, Wendy invites him to the beach with Sam and Tom. Asiago wants to try it, but the sun makes him turn bright red. He uses his towel as a cape and sits under an umbrella. Then he gets a wooden splinter on the boardwalk and eats baked clams that may contain garlic. Soon he has a sunburn, a splinter, and a terrible stomachache, so he goes home. His friends want to cheer him up. They invite him back to the beach at night. The moon is cool, and Asiago plays his accordion. When he disappears, his friends look up and see that he has changed into a little bat. He eats mosquitoes and decides that the beach may not be so bad after all. Then he tells Great Uncle Gouda about his wonderful night.

Asiago has never visited a beach, so he is curious when Wendy invites him. He goes with Wendy, Sam, and Tom, but the sunny beach is difficult for a young vampire. The hot sun makes him red, and he must hide beneath an umbrella with a towel tied around his neck like a cape. On the boardwalk, he gets a wooden splinter and worries about it. Later, he eats many baked clams and gets a stomachache because there may be garlic in them. Asiago leaves feeling that the beach is not a good place for him. Wendy, Sam, and Tom think of a better plan. They bring him to the beach after sunset. Asiago keeps his shoes on, avoids the garlic because the snack hut is closed, and enjoys the cool moonlight. He turns into a bat and eats mosquitoes. At last, he thinks the beach can be fun and tells Gouda about his night.

A young vampire named Asiago goes to the beach with his friends Wendy, Sam, and Tom. At first, he is excited because he has never seen a beach. However, the hot sun hurts him, a wooden splinter frightens him, and baked clams give him a stomachache when he worries that they contain garlic. Asiago returns home with a sunburn, splinter, and stomachache. His friends do not want him to feel sad, so they plan a nighttime beach party. They explain that the sun will be setting, Asiago can wear shoes, and the snack hut will be closed. At night, the moon shines without making the beach hot. Asiago plays his accordion while Wendy builds a sand castle and Tom and Sam catch a strange creature. Asiago disappears and becomes a small bat. He finds that mosquitoes are good for him and decides the beach is not so bad. Then he shares his happy adventure with Great Uncle Gouda.

video_title: The Pout-Pout Fish 🐟 | Read Aloud for Kids | Bedtime Story | Reading with Rollin

summaries.summary: Deep in the water lives a glum fish with a pouty face. He says he spreads gloom everywhere. A clam sees him and asks him to turn his frown upside down, but the fish says he cannot change. A jellyfish asks him to be friendlier, and a squid asks for a smile, joy, and hope. The fish gives the same answer each time. An octopus also tells him that his sulking is unattractive, but the fish still says he is destined to be glum. Then a bright, silver fish swims up. She does not say hello. She gives the pout fish a kiss and swims away. The fish is surprised. He thinks about it and says he was wrong. He is not only a pout fish. Now he is a kiss kiss fish, spreading kisses and smooches everywhere.

A pout pout fish swims in the deep water. His face looks sad, and he says he spreads gloom all around. First, a smiling clam gives him advice and asks him to turn his frown upside down. The fish says that is just how he is. Next, a jellyfish asks him not to greet everyone with a grimace and growl. The fish says he would like to be friendly, but he has no choice. Then a squiggly squid asks for a smile, joy, and hope. The fish still says he must stay glum. An octopus tells him that his sulking is not attractive, but nothing changes. At last, a bright silver fish swims near and kisses his pout. The fish is amazed. He realizes he was wrong about himself. He becomes a kiss kiss fish and says he will spread happy kisses with his new kiss kiss face.

The story begins with a gloomy fish who always wears a pout pout face. He believes he must spread gloom wherever he goes. A clam, a jellyfish, a squid, and an octopus each speak to him. They ask him to smile, be friendly, show joy, and stop sulking. The fish listens, but each time he says he cannot change. He thinks being glum is simply the way he is. Then a quiet, bright, silver swimmer comes along. She does something different from the others: she gives the fish a kiss on his pout and swims away. The fish is astonished and stands still like a statue. Soon he understands that he was wrong to think he had to be pouty. He calls himself a kiss kiss fish. His face is now a kiss kiss face, and he promises to spread kisses and smooches all over the place.

video_title: HOW TO BABYSIT A GRANDMA | A Funny Mother’s Day Read Aloud Picture Book | Storytime | Kindergarten

summaries.summary: A child goes to babysit a grandma for a sleepover. At the door, the child uses a disguise and a secret knock, then says hello and hugs the parents goodbye. The child tells Grandma about many fun plans. They choose activities, go to the park, slide, swing, and feed the ducks. At home, they sing songs, play Shoe Shop, decorate Grandma with ribbons and stickers, and make silly food faces. When it gets dark, they look for the first star. Then they read books and talk about when the child’s mom was little. The child shows Grandma how to say “I love you” without words. Grandma chooses a place to sleep. They make shadow puppets and say good night. In the morning, the child dresses as a twin, packs up, hugs Grandma, gives her things to borrow, and asks when they can babysit her again.

A babysitter spends the night at Grandma’s house. First, the child knocks in a special way, says, “Guess who?” and tells the parents not to be sad because the child will be home soon. The child has many ideas for keeping Grandma busy, such as baking, doing yoga, playing hide-and-seek, reading, making hats, and going to the park. At the park, they use slides, swing gently, and feed ducks. At home, they sing together, line up shoes for Shoe Shop, and decorate Grandma. They add sprinkles to food and make silly faces with dinner. Later, they look for a star, snuggle up, and read slowly. Grandma tells stories about the child’s mom. The child says “I love you” with eyes, a heart, and a point to Grandma. They choose a sleeping place, make shadow foxes, and say good night. In the morning, they say goodbye with hugs and love.

The child is lucky to have a sleepover while babysitting Grandma. The visit begins with a secret knock, a funny greeting, and goodbye hugs for Mom and Dad. The child and Grandma have a busy, happy time. They go to the park, ride slides, swing, and feed the ducks. They also bake, play games, look at family pictures, read books, and make a puppet show. At home, the child and Grandma sing a duet and play with shoes. Grandma is decorated with ribbons, bows, and stickers. During dinner, they add sprinkles and arrange food into silly faces. At night, they find the first star and read together. The child asks Grandma about Mom when she was little, then shows love without speaking. Grandma chooses where to sleep. They make shadow puppets and tell Grandma that Mom and Dad will return in the morning. After breakfast time comes, the child packs up, hugs Grandma, and asks to babysit her again.

video_title: 🛁 The Pigeon Needs a Bath by #MoWillems 📚 Kids Story Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A pigeon is told that he is filthy and needs a bath. The pigeon says he does not need one because he had a bath last month, and he says clean and dirty are only words. He gives many reasons to avoid the bath, saying that he does not smell and that flies around him are only a coincidence. At last, he agrees to take a bath. First, the water feels too hot, too cold, too wet, too deep, and not deep enough. Then the pigeon decides the bath is okay. He splashes, washes, sings, and plays with bubbles. He looks at his wrinkly toes and pretends to be a fish. After ten hours, the pigeon enjoys the bath so much that he asks if he can stay in the tub forever.

Someone notices that the pigeon is filthy and asks for help because the pigeon needs a bath. The pigeon disagrees and says he took a bath last month. He says he feels clean, asks why a bath matters, and explains that his smell is normal for a pigeon. He even says the flies buzzing around him are just a coincidence. When he is told to take a bath, he finally says he will do it. The pigeon complains about everything in the tub: the water is too hot, too cold, too wet, too deep, or not deep enough, and there are too many or too few toys. Then he finds that the bath is okay. Soon he is having fun, washing, singing, and loving the bubbles. He plays like a fish and, ten hours later, wants to stay in the tub forever.

The pigeon does not want a bath. He says he had one last month and believes that he is already clean. He asks why he should spend his short life taking a bath and says that his smell is normal. The other voice reminds him that he needs a bath, so the pigeon agrees, even though he expects not to like it. In the tub, he says the water has many problems. It is too hot, too cold, too wet, too deep, and not deep enough. He also notices the toys and the reflection. Finally, he decides the bath is okay. Then everything changes. He splashes in the water, washes, sings, and says that this is the life. He loves the bubbles, looks at his wrinkly toes, and pretends to be a fish. After ten hours, he does not want the bath to end.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - The Monkey who looked for Trouble

summaries.summary: In Haiti, a mother kept many bees and made sweet honey for her children. One day, she carried a large pot of honey to the market. As she dreamed about buying oranges, peppers, potatoes, yams, and mangoes, she tripped. The pot broke, and the honey spilled everywhere. She called the spilled honey “trouble.” A little monkey heard her and tasted the honey. He thought trouble was yummy, scrummy, and delicious, so he wanted more. He found Papa God and asked for lots of trouble. Papa God gave him a sack and told him to open it in the desert. Four big dogs jumped out and chased the monkey. He ran until a little tree appeared, then climbed up safely. The dogs left when the sun went down. Back home, his mother gave him honey and explained that honey was the trouble he wanted. Papa God had helped him when he needed it.

A young mother in Haiti had bees and used their honey to feed her children. She filled a clay pot with extra honey and carried it through the forest to the market. While thinking about food for her family, she tripped over a root. The pot shattered, and the golden honey covered the path. The mother was sad and called it trouble. A little monkey watched from a tree. He did not ask his mother or his friend what trouble was. Instead, he tasted the honey and decided that trouble was delicious. He went to Papa God and asked for even more trouble. Papa God gave him a brown sack to open in a desert. Four slobbering dogs came out and chased him. The monkey had nowhere to climb, but a small tree appeared. He climbed it, and the dogs waited below until they finally went away. The monkey returned home, where his mother gave him honey and showed him what he had really wanted.

A little monkey saw a mother lose a pot of honey. She called the accident trouble, but the monkey only heard that Papa God had given her trouble. He tasted the honey left on the ground and loved it. Believing trouble was something delicious, he decided to find Papa God and ask for more. Papa God warned him to be sure, then gave him a sack and sent him to the treeless desert. When the monkey opened the sack, four large brown dogs rushed out. They chased him across the sand. The monkey became frightened because there were no trees nearby. Just as he was ready to give up, one small tree appeared. He climbed it, and the dogs could not follow. After the dogs left, he ran home. His mother explained that he had wanted honey, not trouble. She gave him a jar, and he happily tasted it. Papa God had provided the tree to give the monkey a little help.

video_title: 🐯 Ravi's Roar | Big Bright Feelings

summaries.summary: Ravi was the youngest and smallest in his family, so he often had trouble keeping up. At a picnic, he came last in the race, squeezed into a seat with Dad and Biscuits, and could not join the games easily. The monkey bars and log gaps were too big, and a man said Ravi was too small for the slide. Then Ravi missed out on ice cream. He became so angry that he turned into a tiger with a tail, ears, teeth, and orange fur. As a tiger, Ravi could use the playground and make everyone move aside. But when he roared and growled too much, nobody wanted to play with him. Ravi became sad and could not remember why he was so angry. He said sorry, Dad said it was okay, and Ravi turned back into a boy. After that, he did not become a tiger again, though he sometimes growled.

Ravi was smaller than everyone in his family, even Biscuits the dog. At the picnic, Ravi was last in the race and had to squeeze into a seat. At the park, he could not find anyone while playing hide and seek. The monkey bars were too high, the logs were too far apart, and a man said Ravi was too small for the big slide. Ravi also arrived last for ice cream, and there was none left for him. He became furious and changed into a tiger. The tiger roared, got ice cream, and made people move away from the benches. He enjoyed swinging, leaping, and sliding because nobody dared to say no. Soon, however, nobody wanted to play with him. Ravi felt sad and became less angry. He quietly said he was sorry. Dad accepted his apology and praised him. Ravi changed back into a boy and only sometimes had a little growl afterward.

Ravi did not like being the smallest. During a picnic, he was last in a race, had to sit tightly with Dad and Biscuits, and missed out on fun at the playground. He could not find anyone, the monkey bars were too high, the log gaps were too wide, and he was told he was too small for the big slide. When he came last for ice cream and found none left, Ravi became furious. A stripy tail, furry ears, sharp teeth, and orange fur appeared, turning him into a tiger. Ravi liked being powerful. He roared so people moved away, then swung on the monkey bars, crossed the logs, and slid down the big slide. But his roaring and growling made everyone stop playing with him. He felt sad and no longer knew why he was angry. Ravi said sorry in a quiet voice, and everything felt better. Dad said it was okay, and Ravi became a boy again.

video_title: Frog and Toad Together: Cookies

summaries.summary: Toad baked cookies and thought they smelled and tasted wonderful. He ran to Frog’s house so Frog could taste them. Frog loved the cookies, and the friends kept eating them. Frog said they should stop before they became sick, but they kept choosing one last cookie, then one very last cookie, and then another. Frog explained that willpower means trying hard not to do something you really want to do. The friends put the cookies in a box, tied the box with string, and placed it on a high shelf. Each time, they found a way to get the cookies again. At last, Frog took the box outside and called to the birds. Birds carried away every cookie. Toad was sad because there was not even one left. Frog said they had lots and lots of willpower. Toad let Frog keep it and went home to bake a cake.

Toad made a bowl of cookies and hurried to show them to Frog. They both ate many cookies because the treats were so good. Frog noticed that they might soon be sick and suggested stopping. Toad agreed, but the two friends continued eating one last cookie and one very last cookie. When Toad asked about willpower, Frog explained that it is trying hard not to do something you really want. Frog tried to help by putting the cookies in a box. Toad pointed out that they could open it, so Frog tied it with string. Toad still knew they could cut the string, so Frog put the box high on a shelf. They could still climb up and get it. Finally, Frog brought the cookies outside and gave them to the birds. The birds took every cookie. Toad had no cookies left, but Frog said they had lots of willpower. Toad went home to bake a cake.

Toad baked cookies for himself and Frog. The cookies smelled good, tasted even better, and seemed like the best cookies Frog had ever eaten. Frog and Toad ate cookie after cookie. They said they should stop, but they kept eating while promising it would be the last one. Frog said they needed willpower and explained what the word meant. Then he put the cookies in a box and tied the box shut. The friends realized they could still open it, so Frog placed it on a high shelf. They also realized they could climb up, bring it down, cut the string, and open it. Frog did exactly that, but then he carried the box outdoors. He called the birds, and birds flew in from everywhere. They picked up all the cookies and flew away. Toad sadly said there were none left. Frog answered that they had lots and lots of willpower. Toad gave the willpower to Frog and went home to bake a cake.

video_title: OVER AND UNDER THE POND read aloud | A great education story about ecology | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A child and Mom paddle over a pond and wonder what is underneath. Mom explains that a hidden world lives below the water. Minnows, crayfish, turtles, and bullfrogs swim there. Above the pond, beetles twirl and painted turtles slide from a log. Below, minnows dart through grass and a trout waits to lunge. The child sees birds building nests, a caddisfly making a pebble shelter, and a moose eating water lilies. Beavers dive for roots, a goldfinch gets ready to fly, and tadpoles grow legs and lose their tails. A heron catches a minnow. Later, the child sees a woodpecker, an otter, dragonflies, ospreys, raccoons, mink, and a crayfish. At sunset, the child and Mom go home while the pond’s animals settle into the night.

The pond looks like a mirror with sky, sunshine, and clouds, but the child discovers that much is happening under the water. While the child and Mom paddle, minnows swim through grass, a brook trout waits, and turtles slip from a wet tree. Cattails move in the wind, red-winged blackbirds fly by, and one carries grass for a nest. Under the pond, a caddisfly larva builds a shelter from pebbles and sand. A moose is eating water lilies, and beavers dive down and bring up roots. A goldfinch balances on a branch, while tadpoles change and grow legs. A great blue heron catches a minnow. The child also sees an otter, dragonflies catching minnows, and animals searching for supper. When the sky grows dark, the child and Mom glide back to shore. The pond becomes quiet but remains full of animals.

A child travels across a pond with Mom and learns that the pond has two busy worlds. On top, the child sees lily pads, reeds, rushes, beetles, cattails, birds, trees, a moose, and a goldfinch. Underneath, minnows swim, a trout waits, turtles move away, and a caddisfly makes a tiny home. Beavers use their powerful tails to dive for roots. Tadpoles change as they grow legs and lose their tails. A great blue heron steps carefully and catches a quick minnow. The child looks up and sees a woodpecker, then notices an otter below. A dragonfly rests on the child’s knee, while dragonfly larvae catch minnows under the water. As shadows grow, ospreys circle, raccoons and mink search the shore, and a crayfish hides. The child and Mom return home when a loon calls good night, and darkness settles over the pond.

video_title: Valentine's Story~ FROGGY'S FIRST KISS Read Aloud ~ Story Time ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books

summaries.summary: The week before Valentine's Day, Froggy saw Fralina, the new girl in his class, and thought she was very pretty. He felt wiggly inside whenever she smiled at him. Froggy watched her instead of his work and fell off the monkey bars. At lunch, Fralina gave him an apple. Later, while Froggy watched her play tetherball, the ball hit him. The next day, she gave him a heart-shaped cookie. Froggy made a valentine that said, “I love you,” but he hid it under his desk and bumped his head. Then Fralina gave Froggy a kiss on the cheek. Froggy felt strange and could not eat. His classmates teased him on the bus. At home, his mother asked about school. On Valentine's Day, Froggy made his mother breakfast, gave her the heart, and said she was someone special. She gave him candy kisses.

Froggy thought Valentine's Day meant candy and love at school. When Fralina, a new frog in his class, smiled at him, Froggy felt soft and wiggly inside. He stared at her and had little accidents, including falling from the monkey bars and getting hit by a tetherball. Fralina was kind to him. She gave him a juicy apple, then a heart-shaped cookie. Froggy made a special valentine saying, “I love you,” and tried to hide it. He bumped his head, and the children laughed. The next day, Fralina gave Froggy a big kiss on his cheek. Froggy felt so strange that he could not eat his lunch or dessert. Max and the other children sang that Froggy had a girlfriend. Froggy wondered why his heart felt heavy. On Valentine's Day, he made his mother breakfast, gave her the special heart, and told her she was someone special. His mother gave him many candy kisses.

Fralina was the new girl in Froggy's class, and Froggy liked looking at her when she smiled. He forgot to pay attention, fell on his head at recess, and was hit by a tetherball at lunch. Fralina gave him an apple and a heart-shaped cookie. Froggy made a valentine for someone special. It said, “I love you,” but he hid it under his desk because he did not want Fralina to see it. When he stood up, he hit his head, and the class laughed. The next day, Fralina gave Froggy a kiss on the cheek. Froggy became red, felt strange, and left his lunch behind. His friends teased him on the bus by singing that he had a girlfriend. At home, Froggy wondered whether his heavy heart meant love, hunger, or his full backpack. The next morning, he made breakfast for his mother and gave her the heart. His mother gave him candy kisses.

video_title: The Legend of Rock Paper Scissors (absurdity, laughter & bombastic performances)Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Rock was the strongest warrior in the backyard kingdom, but he felt sad because nobody could challenge him. He defeated a clothespin and an apricot, yet both battles were too easy. In another place, Paper was the smartest warrior, but nobody could outwit him. He beat a computer printer and a bag of trail mix. Scissors was the fastest blade. She defeated a roll of tape and dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets. Each warrior traveled away from home to find an equal. Rock and Scissors met in a garage and battled. Rock won, but then Paper arrived and challenged Rock. Paper beat Rock. Finally, Scissors challenged Paper and won. The three warriors were delighted because they had found their matches. They hugged, danced, became fast friends, and began a giant three-way battle. The story says their joyful game still continues whenever children play rock paper scissors.

In the kingdom of backyard, Rock searched for a worthy opponent because he was the strongest warrior. He fought a clothespin and an apricot, but neither battle made him happy. Paper had the same problem in Mom’s home office. Although he was very clever, no one could outwit him. He defeated a computer printer and a bag of trail mix. In the kitchen realm, Scissors was the fastest blade. She beat a roll of tape and frozen chicken nuggets shaped like dinosaurs. Then Rock met Scissors in a two-car garage. Their epic battle ended with Rock winning. Rock proudly said no warrior could beat him, but Paper appeared and challenged him. Paper defeated Rock. After that, Scissors fought Paper and won. At last, all three warriors had met someone equal to them. They hugged, danced, and became friends. Then they started battling together in a huge three-way contest, which is why children still play rock paper scissors.

Rock, Paper, and Scissors were three great warriors who each wanted a real challenge. Rock was strong and won against a clothespin and an apricot. Paper was smart and defeated a computer printer and trail mix. Scissors was fast and beat a roll of tape and frozen chicken nuggets. None of them felt satisfied because every opponent was too easy. While searching for a match, Rock met Scissors in a garage. Rock won their battle. Rock then met Paper, who challenged him and won. Paper was happy, but Scissors soon challenged Paper. Scissors won, so each warrior had finally met a match. The three friends hugged and danced with joy. They were so pleased that they began a new battle with all three together. Their huge, happy struggle continued round and round. The story explains that children honor these warriors by playing rock paper scissors in backyards, playgrounds, and classrooms.

video_title: Waiting is not easy Mo Willems Read Aloud Video and Post-Reading Questions and Activities

summaries.summary: Gerald tells Piggy that he has a surprise. Piggy asks if it is big, pretty, and something they can share, and Gerald says yes. Piggy is excited, but Gerald says the surprise is not ready yet, so Piggy must wait. Piggy tries to wait, but waiting feels very hard. Piggy asks to see the surprise and then says he is finished waiting. He thinks the surprise may not be worth such a long wait. Piggy decides to wait a little longer. The friends wait as the day becomes dark. Piggy worries that they have waited all day for nothing. Then Gerald shows Piggy the beautiful surprise in the sky. Piggy says it was worth the wait. Gerald explains that he wants to show Piggy the sunrise tomorrow morning. Now Piggy says he cannot wait for that surprise either.

Gerald has a surprise for Piggy, but the surprise is not there yet. Piggy asks many questions and becomes eager to see it. Gerald tells Piggy that he must wait. Piggy says he will wait, but soon he complains that waiting is not easy. He wants the surprise right away. Piggy becomes tired of waiting and says the surprise may not be worth it. Still, he agrees to wait some more because Gerald says it will be worth it. The friends wait and wait while the sky grows darker. Piggy thinks they have wasted the whole day. At last, Gerald shows him what they have been waiting for. Piggy sees the surprise and decides it was worth waiting. Then Gerald tells Piggy that he wants to show him the sunrise in the morning. Piggy is excited and says he cannot wait.

Piggy is told that Gerald has a surprise, and Piggy wants to know what it is. Gerald says it is big, pretty, and shareable, but it is not ready yet. Piggy must wait. He tries, even though he says waiting is not easy. After some time, Piggy says he will not wait anymore because he does not think the surprise is worth all the waiting. Gerald encourages him to wait a little longer. Piggy agrees. The two friends wait until it gets dark. Piggy worries that they will not be able to see each other or anything at all. He asks what they waited for all day. Then the surprise appears, and Piggy says it was worth the wait. Gerald has another plan for tomorrow morning: he wants to show Piggy the sunrise. Piggy is ready to wait for that beautiful surprise.

video_title: Moana Discovers Maui's Magic | Disney Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Long ago, Maui took the heart of Teiti, the mother island, and lost it with his magical fish hook. Then darkness spread over the world. Moana had the heart, and she found Maui. She told him to return it and save the world. Maui wanted his fish hook first, so he and Moana sailed to Laachai, the realm of monsters. A giant crab had the hook in its shell. Maui and Moana worked together and got it back. Maui was not confident at first. He changed into a bug and a pig by accident. Moana talked with him, and he practiced until his skills returned. Maui flew like a hawk toward the lava monster. He fell from the sky, but the friends did not stop. Maui blocked the monster while Moana carried the heart to Teiti. The heart made Tea become Teiti again. The islands were saved, and Maui and Moana became heroes and friends forever.

Maui once stole Teiti's heart, and then he lost the heart and his fish hook. A darkness began to spread across the world. Moana received the heart from the ocean and found Maui when she was a teenager. Maui sailed away in her canoe, but the ocean brought Moana back to him. Moana asked Maui to help save the world. Maui agreed, but he needed his hook. They sailed past tiny coconut-armored bandits to Laachai. A huge crab monster had the hook in its shell. Moana and Maui worked together and took it back safely. Maui could not use it well at first because he had lost confidence. He became a bug and a pig by accident. After Moana spoke with him, he practiced and became skilled again. Maui flew toward the lava monster, but he was knocked down. He and Moana kept going. Moana placed the heart in Teiti's spiral, and the monster became Teiti. The islands were saved.

The story begins when Maui loses Teiti's heart and his magical fish hook. Without the heart, darkness spreads over the world. Moana has the heart because the ocean gave it to her. She finds Maui and asks him to help return it. Maui first takes her canoe and sails away, but the ocean brings Moana back. Together, they travel to the realm of monsters to find Maui's hook. A giant crab has hidden it in his shell, and the two friends get it back. Maui is unsure of himself. He changes into a bug and a pig without meaning to. Moana talks with him, and he practices until he can change into a hawk again. Maui flies toward the lava monster while Moana sails toward Teiti. Maui is knocked from the sky, but he blocks the monster's fiery fist. Moana places the heart in Teiti's glowing spiral. Tea changes back into Teiti, the islands are saved, and the two friends are heroes forever.

video_title: The ugly duckling. Children’s bedtime stories read aloud in an English accent..

summaries.summary: Mother Duck had six eggs, but one was much bigger than the others. When it finally opened, a very large, ugly duckling came out. The other animals laughed at him, pecked him, and chased him away. He ran to a swamp, where wild dogs laughed at him while hunters and dogs searched the area. A fierce dog would not eat him, so the duckling escaped. He stayed briefly in an old woman’s house, but the hen and cat sent him away because he could not lay eggs or purr. At a lake, he lived alone through the cold weather. He saw beautiful white birds with long necks and learned they were swans. In spring, he grew stronger wings and flew to a garden. Looking into the water, he discovered he was a swan. The other swans welcomed him, and the ducks called him the most beautiful one of all.

A mother duck waited for five small white eggs and one huge egg to hatch. The small eggs opened first, and their ducklings explored the grass. The large egg opened later, revealing a duckling who was much bigger and uglier than the others. Mother Duck tested whether he could swim, and he could, but the farmyard animals still treated him badly. Geese laughed, hens pecked, a turkey gobbled, and a farm boy chased him away. The lonely duckling hid in a swamp, escaped a hunt, and then tried living with an old woman. Her hen and cat rejected him because he could not do what they wanted. He found a lake and survived the cold months alone. In spring, he flew to a pond where three swans lived. When he looked at his reflection, he saw that he had become a beautiful swan. The swans welcomed him, and the ducks admired him.

The ugly duckling began life in a huge egg beside Mother Duck’s other eggs. Because he looked different, an old duck called him a turkey chick, although he proved that he could swim. At the farmyard, animals laughed at him, pecked him, and chased him away. He wandered to a swamp and hid while hunters and dogs passed through it. A fierce dog saw him but decided he was too ugly to eat. Later, the duckling escaped into the wind and found an old woman’s house. The hen asked if he could lay eggs, and the cat asked if he could purr. Since he could do neither, they made him leave. He lived beside a lake, ignored by the animals, and endured the cold. One evening, he saw shining white swans and thought they were beautiful. After winter, his wings became strong. He flew to a garden, looked into the pond, and discovered he was a swan. The other swans stayed beside him, and the ducks admired his beauty.

video_title: How to Catch A Leprechaun Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A quick leprechaun visits houses on St. Patrick’s Day while people try to catch him. He warns that he will pull out shoelaces, put glitter in hair, scatter gold coins, and turn a house upside down. At the first house, he slips in and out of a trap. He escapes a shoebox trap, fixes smelly shoes, eats the nuts left as bait, and drinks the dandelion tea meant for him. Next, he gets away from an iron cage and a fancy trap with dancing. An engineer builds a trap that fills the whole house from ceiling to floor, but the leprechaun still walks out the door. A very large trap scares him, but he says a four-leaf clover is needed to catch him. He declares that no one can catch him unless a brilliant child makes the perfect trap, so the story ends with, “Better luck next year.”

The streets are quiet, and St. Patrick’s Day is close. A mischievous leprechaun taps his hammer and tells everyone that he is nearby. He plans to make trouble and says that no trap will catch him. People build many traps for him. One trap is in the first house, but he enters and leaves quickly. Another is a shoebox on a stick, and he dances away. He visits another house, fixes the shoes, eats the nuts set out as bait, and fills his belly. When someone offers dandelion tea, he takes the tea for free. An iron cage is clever, but the leprechaun says that he has lived for 200 years and will not be caught. Even an engineer’s trap covering the whole house cannot stop him. A trap called the Leprechaun 3000 scares him, but he escapes. He says only a brilliant child might design the perfect trap.

The leprechaun wants everyone to know that catching him will be very hard. He promises to cause silly trouble, including tangling laces, adding glitter, and making a green toilet. Then he tests one trap after another. He gets in and out of the first trap without trouble. He escapes a shoebox trap while dancing, then visits another house, repairs the shoes, eats the nuts, and leaves with a full belly. A cup of dandelion tea does not catch him either because he takes it and speeds away. He also escapes an iron cage and a fancy dancing trap. An engineer makes the entire house into one big trap, but the leprechaun still strolls out the door. The Leprechaun 3000 gives him a scare, yet he is not caught without a four-leaf clover. He says a brilliant child may someday build the perfect trap, and ends by saying, “Better luck next year.”

video_title: 📚 Kids Book Read Aloud: THE BUBBLE BOOK by Elizabeth Ember

summaries.summary: A tiny bubble needs to become bigger. First, telling it to grow does not work. Then the child tries belly breaths. Hands go on the belly, and a big breath is blown out. The bubble grows bigger. More belly breaths make it grow even more. Soon, something can be seen inside the bubble. The child pops it with a finger, and many more bubbles appear. The bubbles need help too. Big belly breaths make them bigger, and the purple bubble needs extra blowing. Finally, all the bubbles are popped. The story says that taking belly breaths helps people feel good, calmer, and more relaxed.

There is a very tiny bubble. The child wants to make it bigger, but telling it to grow does not work. The child learns to use belly breaths, a special tool for getting calm. With hands on the belly, the child breathes in and blows out. The bubble grows. The child blows again and makes it even bigger. Something is inside, so the child pops the bubble with a finger. More bubbles come out. The child uses very big belly breaths to grow them. The purple bubble needs extra help, so the child blows on it too. When all the bubbles are big, the child pops them one by one. Belly breaths help the child feel good, calm, and relaxed.

The story begins with a tiny bubble. It does not grow when someone simply tells it to grow. The child tries belly breaths instead. The child puts hands on the belly, breathes in, and blows out. The bubble becomes bigger, and more breaths make it bigger still. The child sees something inside and pops the bubble with a finger. The popped bubble makes more bubbles appear. The child blows big belly breaths to grow the new bubbles. One purple bubble needs more help, so the child blows on it again. Then every bubble is popped with several little pops. At the end, the story explains that belly breaths help us feel good. They can help us feel calmer and more relaxed.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime - 𝐻𝑎𝑟𝑏𝑜𝑟 𝑀𝑒 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Haley remembers the six students who once met in their school’s art room: Haley, Holly, Esteban, Thiago, Omari, and Ashton. She listens to a recording of Esteban and thinks about how their group changed her life. At home, Haley is also facing change because her uncle, the parent who raised her, is moving to Manhattan. Her father has returned home and plays the piano while her uncle packs. At school, the group began with eight students, but two left. Esteban then arrived upset because his father had disappeared, and he feared that his family might be taken next. Haley recognizes his fear because her own father was imprisoned when she was little, and her uncle raised her. Later, Miss Laverne creates Room 501, called the A.R.T.T. room, or A Room to Talk. Every Friday, the six students will meet there without grown-ups so they can talk, draw, and learn to face unfamiliar experiences together.

At the start of seventh grade, Haley looks back on the school year when six students formed a close group. Their class was an experiment for children who learned differently and had been teased in larger classrooms. Miss Laverne made them feel accepted. Esteban was especially troubled because his father had been taken away, and no one knew where he was. Haley understood his fear because her own father had gone to prison, while her uncle became her main parent. When Esteban returned after being absent, he explained that his family was packing because he feared they might be taken too. Miss Laverne then led the students to Room 501. She explained that they would meet there every Friday to talk privately. The students were unsure why they needed the room, but Amari invented the name A.R.T.T., meaning A Room to Talk. The group slowly began accepting the new space and its purpose.

Haley remembers a rainy September at school and the six children who remained in Miss Laverne’s special class. Their learning had felt difficult in ordinary classrooms, where other students laughed at them. Esteban arrived late one day, soaked and wearing an oversized jacket. He shared his carrots and everything else with his friends. Rabbit learned that carrots were not meant only for collecting. Sharing made life better for everyone.

video_title: Sleeping beauty. Children’s bedtime story read aloud in an English accent

summaries.summary: A king and queen wanted a baby. One day, a green frog said the queen would have a baby, and soon Rose was born. The king invited seven fairies to a feast. The fairies gave Rose beautiful gifts, cleverness, dancing, music, and singing. But the fairy Nightshade was angry because she was not invited. She put a spell on Rose: on her sixteenth birthday, Rose would prick her finger on a spinning wheel. Jasmine changed the spell so Rose would sleep instead, and only true love's kiss could wake her. Rose grew up happy and talented. At her birthday ball, she found a spinning wheel and pricked her finger. Everyone in the castle fell asleep, and thorny bushes covered the castle. After one hundred years, Prince Floren came. His sword changed the thorns into roses. He kissed Rose, and she and everyone else woke up. Rose and Floren married the next day.

Rose was born in a magical castle after a frog gave the queen good news. Her father, the king, made a feast, and seven fairies came to celebrate. Each fairy wished for something special for Rose. Nightshade, a mean fairy who was not invited, came in green smoke. She wished that Rose would die after touching a spinning wheel on her sixteenth birthday. Jasmine made the spell gentler. Rose would sleep, and a kiss from true love would wake her. The king burned all the spinning wheels he could find. Rose grew into a lovely girl who danced, sang, played music, and won at chess. At her birthday ball, she followed singing to a tower. An old woman showed her a spinning wheel, and Rose pricked her finger. The castle fell asleep and became hidden by thorns. Prince Floren found the castle after one hundred years. His sword made roses from the thorns. He kissed Rose, and everyone woke. Rose and Floren were married.

A frog told a sad queen that she would have a baby, and baby Rose was born. The king and queen celebrated with a feast. Seven fairies blessed Rose with beauty, wisdom, dancing, music, and singing. The uninvited fairy Nightshade made a dark spell about a spinning wheel. Jasmine changed it so Rose and the castle would only sleep until a true love kissed Rose. Rose grew up and became a happy, clever, musical girl. On her sixteenth birthday, she played hide-and-seek during a grand ball. She climbed a tower and saw an old woman spinning. Rose touched the thread, pricked her finger, and fell asleep. The king, queen, guests, and all the castle slept too. Roses and thorns grew over the castle for one hundred years. Prince Floren came to help. His sword turned each thorn into a rose. He kissed Rose, and she opened her eyes. The castle woke, and Rose and Floren married the next day.

video_title: 📚 I NEED MY MONSTER - Kids Books Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Ethan looks under his bed and finds a note saying that Gabe, his monster, has gone fishing for a week. Ethan cannot sleep without Gabe's scary breathing, claws, and green ooze, so he calls for another monster. Herbert arrives, but he has no claws. Ralph has smooth claws covered with nail polish. Cynthia has sharp claws and a slimy tail, but Ethan sends her away because she is a girl monster. Mac is a scruffy boy monster, but his tail is short, so Ethan rejects him too. Ethan worries that he will never sleep. Then Gabe returns from fishing. He says the fish were too easy to scare and that Ethan is a good challenge. Gabe makes green ooze, shows his spiked tail, and sharpens his claws. Ethan says no monster can scare him like Gabe. Gabe asks for Ethan's pinky, and Ethan gives him a pillow instead. Everything feels normal again, and Ethan can sleep.

Gabe is Ethan's regular monster, and Ethan needs him under the bed at night. One evening, Ethan finds a note saying Gabe has gone fishing. Ethan tries to sleep, but he misses Gabe's noises and green ooze. He calls for a new monster. Herbert comes first, but he is not scary enough and has no claws. Ralph has claws, but they are smooth and shiny with nail polish. Cynthia has wonderful sharp claws and a slimy tail, but Ethan wants a boy monster. Mac is a big, scruffy boy with good claws, but he has a short tail. Ethan laughs when Mac says he might lick him, and Mac leaves. Ethan is still awake when Gabe finally comes home. Gabe says fishing was boring because the fish were easy to scare. He makes his frightening ooze and tail appear. Ethan tells Gabe that nobody scares him the same way. Gabe asks to nibble Ethan's pinky, but Ethan offers a pillow. Then Ethan is ready to sleep.

Ethan wants a monster under his bed because monsters help keep him in bed. Gabe is away fishing, so Ethan calls for a replacement. Herbert knows about monsters but only has an overbite and makes panting sounds. Ralph has shiny claws, but his fur and polished nails do not seem frightening. Cynthia has jagged claws and a slimy tail, yet Ethan sends her away because he thinks boys should have boy monsters. Mac is a scruffy boy monster with excellent claws, but his tail is stumpy. His long tongue makes Ethan laugh instead of feel scared. After Mac leaves, Ethan wonders how he will sleep. At last, Gabe comes back. He says the fish were not challenging, but Ethan is. Gabe spreads green ooze and shows his spiked tail. Ethan says that no other monster can scare him like Gabe. Gabe wants to nibble Ethan's pinky, so Ethan gives him a pillow. With Gabe back, everything returns to normal, and Ethan will soon be asleep.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Disney's MOANA Folk Tale Read Along - "Maui and the Eel"

summaries.summary: A big storm hurt the island. Trees fell, fields flooded, boats were damaged, and the villagers lost much of their food. Then a giant eel came into the lagoon. It ate the fish and wanted the chickens and pigs the villagers gave it. The villagers were afraid the eel would eat them, too. Maui, a strong demigod, came to help. He rode with a villager to the eel’s cave. Maui hit the eel with his fish hook, but the eel attacked him. Maui changed into a little fish and then back into a man. The eel wrapped around him and opened its mouth. Maui pushed the eel’s coils up, so the eel bit itself. The eel fled, but Maui chased it and defeated it with his magical hook. He buried its head. A coconut tree grew there, giving the villagers a useful fruit.

After a terrible storm, the villagers worked to repair their island, but their harvest was ruined. The fishermen caught very few fish because a huge eel had come to the lagoon. The eel ate the fish and then demanded gifts from the village. Soon the villagers had nothing left and worried that the eel would eat them. Maui heard them and flew down to help. A villager showed Maui where the eel lived. Maui swam to the cave and struck the eel with his fish hook. The angry eel came after him. Maui became a small fish to escape, then became a man again and used his hook. The eel wrapped around Maui and tried to bite him. Maui pushed the eel’s body upward, and the eel bit itself. Maui chased the hurt eel and defeated it near the beach. He buried its head, and the first coconut tree grew there.

A storm caused great trouble for a village. It damaged trees, fields, and boats, and left little food. Then a giant eel began eating the fish in the lagoon. It also wanted the villagers’ chickens and pigs. The villagers were scared because the eel kept asking for more. Maui came from the sky to fight the monster. He went to the eel’s deep cave with one villager. Maui struck the eel’s nose with his magical fish hook. The eel rushed out and attacked. Maui changed into a tiny fish, moved away, and changed back into a man. The eel caught Maui around the waist and tried to bite him. Maui pushed hard against the eel’s coils. The eel bit itself and became hurt. It tried to run away, but Maui followed it to the beach and defeated it. Maui buried the eel’s head. A coconut tree grew from that place, and the villagers thanked Maui for the useful coconuts.

video_title: 👍 Kids Book Read Aloud: KINDNESS GETS A THUMBS UP! by Brenda Li

summaries.summary: Dot walks to school on a cloudy morning and sees Mr. Sloth feeling sad. Dot smiles, waves, and says good morning. Mr. Sloth feels happy again. Then Dot sees Mr. Hippo drop his mail. Dot helps pick it up, and Mr. Hippo feels happy too. At school, Dot notices Bonnie, a new girl who feels worried and scared. During recess, Dot stays with her. He shows her the playground, plays hopscotch, eats lunch with her, holds the door, lends her his favorite pencil crayons, and praises her drawing. Bonnie feels much better and thanks Dot. On the way home, Bonnie sees Mrs. Monkey drop her bananas. She picks them up and returns them. Then Mrs. Monkey sees Dot drop his pencil crayons and helps him. Dot helped others without asking for a reward, and kindness came back to him.

One morning, Dot chooses to be kind as he walks to school. Mr. Sloth looks sad, so Dot greets him warmly. Mr. Sloth changes from a thumbs down to a thumbs up. Next, Mr. Hippo drops all his mail. Dot helps gather it, and Mr. Hippo becomes happy and thanks him. At school, Dot sees Bonnie sitting quietly and looking nervous. He asks her to play. Dot shows Bonnie the swings, seesaw, monkey bars, merry-go-round, and slide. They hopscotch and eat lunch together. Dot holds the door while Bonnie carries books, lends her pencil crayons, and says he likes her drawing. Bonnie's nervous feelings disappear, and she has a better first day. Later, Bonnie helps Mrs. Monkey by returning her dropped bananas. Mrs. Monkey then helps Dot pick up his pencil crayons. The story says to be kind without expecting anything in return.

Dot learns that small acts of kindness can help people feel good. He first smiles and waves at Mr. Sloth, who is feeling sad. Then he helps Mr. Hippo pick up the mail he dropped. Both animals feel happy and show thumbs up. At school, Dot meets Bonnie, a quiet new classmate who feels worried and scared. He invites her to play and shows her the playground. They play, eat lunch, and spend the day together. Dot helps Bonnie carry her books by holding the door, lends her his favorite pencil crayons, and says something nice about her drawing. Bonnie's first day becomes much better, and she thanks him. On her way home, Bonnie sees Mrs. Monkey drop bananas and returns them. Later, Mrs. Monkey sees Dot drop his pencil crayons and picks them up. Dot helped without expecting a reward, and another kind act came back to him.

video_title: 🐶 Drop It, Rocket! 🐶 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Rocket and the Little Yellow Bird love words and their word tree. The bird asks Rocket if he is ready to find new words, and Rocket says yes. Rocket finds a leaf. The bird tells him to drop it, and Rocket drops it. Then Rocket finds a hat and a star. Each time, Rocket drops the item when the bird asks, and the bird says he is a good dog or a good boy. Next, Rocket finds a red boot. Rocket likes the boot and will not drop it. The bird offers a ball, but Rocket still will not drop the boot. video_title: How to Catch a Witch - A Halloween Read Aloud with Moving Pictures

summaries.summary: Some children put on their Halloween costumes and went out on trick-or-treat night. Soon, they saw ghosts, ghouls, goblins, zombies, dinos, ghost wolves, and other monsters everywhere. They guessed that a witch had brought all the creatures. The witch flew high in the sky on her broom and started a dance party with a wave of her hand. The children wanted to catch her so the creatures would go away, and they also hoped to find chocolates and sweets. They tried spider webs, roadblocks, and a tunnel of tricks. The clever witch noticed the traps and even sent a bat to investigate. She flew over the boat on her broom, because she could fly very fast. At last, the monsters cheered at the wonderful party. Then the witch opened a portal, and all the goblins and creatures left in a flash. The children said she could come back for Halloween next year.

On Halloween, children dressed carefully in costumes and walked outside beneath carved pumpkins. High above them, a witch rode a broom and carried invitations. She waved her hand, and music began. The children welcomed her back next Halloween.

A group of children went out in costumes for a spooky Halloween night. They noticed that ghosts, ghouls, goblins, and many other creatures were appearing all around town. A witch in the sky had invited them and made them dance with her. The children decided they needed to catch the witch, both to send the creatures back and to find Halloween candy. They made plans with spider webs, traps, roadblocks, and a tunnel of tricks. But the witch was very wise. She brought many friends, and soon there were even more monsters. When the children made a trap with their dad's toolbox, the witch came to look inside. She sent a bat ahead to check it, then flew over the boat on her broom. The children learned that catching her would be difficult because her broom was so fast. Finally, every monster cheered at the big dance party. The witch opened a portal, and the creatures left in a flash.

video_title: 🤸‍♀️🤸Kids Book Read Aloud: Barbie : I Can Be A Gymnast

Barbie wants to do well as a gymnast, so she practices with her team. Teresa, Skipper, and Summer are on the team, and Coach Jenna coaches them. video_title: Unicorn Diaries - The Goblin Princess - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook

summaries.summary: Bo and Sunny want to play with their friends, but everyone chooses a different game. Mr. Rum Twinkle tells them to use their imaginations, so they invent Yuna Skip Ball. Bo and Sunny believe a wish can help Princess Greta fly, so they make her queen for a day. Greta is thrilled and tells everyone what to do. She orders dragons to make fireworks, fairies to sing, trolls to juggle rocks, and mermaids to do flips. These orders make the forest creatures unhappy, use up the river water, and leave many animals exhausted. Bo and Sunny feel responsible, but their friends help repair the damage. They heal the trolls, refill the lagoon with rain, give the fairies hot honey and lemon, and carry water to the dragons. Greta explains that she became overexcited because she did not understand her queen powers. The unicorns then help her in a better way. video_title: Flat Stanley by Jeff Brown

summaries.summary: Stanley Lambchop is an ordinary boy until a bulletin board falls on him while he sleeps. He is not hurt, but he becomes as flat as a pancake. A heavy bulletin board falls on Stanley Lambchop and makes him flat. Dr. Dan examines him and says that Stanley is healthy, even though he is only half an inch thick. Dressed as a shepherdess and placed in an empty frame, Stanley waits for the thieves and calls the police when they arrive. He receives a medal. Stanley’s flat shape causes many surprising adventures. His family worries at first, but Stanley is fine and soon uses his shape in helpful ways. He rescues his mother’s ring and visits California by being mailed in a large envelope. Stanley’s brother Arthur feels jealous, so Stanley lets Arthur fly him like a kite. He tells Arthur that he is tired and unhappy. Arthur realizes that Stanley needs help. He finds an old bicycle pump and carefully pumps air into Stanley. video_title: How to Catch a Leprechaun - An Animated Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On a quiet night before St. Patrick's Day, a leprechaun visits houses and tries to stay away from traps. He pulls out laces, puts glitter in hair, and leaves gold coins around. The streets are dark and quiet, and St. Patrick's Day is near. A leprechaun tells everyone he is there by tapping his hammer. A speedy leprechaun visits several houses before St. Patrick's Day. He warns that no one will catch him, then makes playful trouble. video_title: 🎃 Kids Book Read Aloud: THE WORST HALLOWEEN BOOK IN THE WHOLE ENTIRE WORLD by Joey Acker

video_title: Slowly Slowly Slowly Said the Sloth | An Eric Carle Read Aloud | BaBa's Books

video_title: Nelson Mandela (Little People, Big Dreams) Read-Along Video

Nelson Mandela began life as a South African boy called Rala. His family had important connections to a clan, but no one in the family had received a formal education. video_title: 💵 I AM MONEY - Read Aloud with the Author | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: Money explains that it does not grow on trees and can be used to buy basic needs and fun things, such as pizza, clothes, a houseboat, or a guinea pig. The story is told by money, who says it is valuable but does not grow on trees. Money can buy things people need and enjoy, but buying things cannot make people happier forever. Money teaches children how to use it wisely. First, money can pay for necessities and playful items, but it cannot decide how valuable a person is or make someone endlessly happy.
