video_title: Wonders Grade 5 When Is a Planet Not a Planet

summaries.summary: For many years, children remembered the planets with the sentence “My very eager mother just served us nine pizzas,” which included Pluto. Scientists later learned more about Pluto and began to question its place among the planets. Pluto is rocky even though it is far from the sun, its orbit crosses Neptune’s orbit, its path is tilted and stretched out, and it is very small. In 1976, astronomers discovered that Pluto had a moon named Charon, making Pluto seem even smaller. In 1992, scientists found the Kuiper Belt, a region filled with icy objects like Pluto. Mike Brown and his team later discovered Eris, an object larger than Pluto, which caused a debate about what counts as a planet. In 2006, the IAU decided that planets must orbit the sun, be round, and clear their orbital neighborhoods. Pluto and Eris became dwarf planets. The story shows that scientific ideas can change when new information is discovered.

Pluto was once taught as the ninth planet, but scientists eventually changed its classification. First, astronomers discovered that Pluto was made of rock, unlike the gas giants that are farther from the sun. They also noticed that Pluto’s orbit was unusual: it was tilted, stretched out, and sometimes crossed Neptune’s orbit. Pluto’s small size became clearer after James Christy discovered its moon, Charon. Later, astronomers found the Kuiper Belt, a distant disk containing thousands of icy objects. Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo, and David Rabinowitz used computers and a telescope to search this region. Their discovery of Eris, which was larger than Pluto, led to a worldwide argument about the meaning of “planet.” The International Astronomical Union created three categories and required a planet to clear nearby objects from its orbit. Pluto did not meet all the requirements, so it became a dwarf planet. Scientists continue studying Pluto and asking new questions about space.

The solar system formed from a nebula containing dust, rocks, ice, and gas. Near the young sun, heat removed much of the gas, creating the rocky planets Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. Farther away, cooler materials kept their gas and became Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Pluto did not fit neatly into this pattern. It was distant but rocky, tiny, and followed an unusual orbit. Astronomers also discovered that Pluto had a moon, Charon, and that many icy objects existed in the Kuiper Belt. When scientists found Eris, a distant object larger than Pluto, they had to decide what a planet really was. In 2006, the IAU said that a planet must orbit the sun, be round, and clear its neighborhood. Pluto, Charon, Ceres, and Eris were classified as dwarf planets because they had not cleared their neighborhoods. The New Horizons mission was launched to study Pluto and Charon more closely and help scientists learn about the solar system.

Cats can have many kinds of fur, colors, tails, and markings. Baby kittens are born tiny and helpless. Their mother feeds them, cleans them, and keeps them warm. Soon they open their eyes, play, and learn to hunt. At six weeks, a kitten can drink from a dish, and in less than a year it can care for itself. Chester, Cookie, and Sam are pet cats, and each one has a special habit. Chester naps on a warm TV, Cookie comes and goes through a window, and Sam runs to his family when the alarm rings for breakfast. Cats also include wild lions, tigers, leopards, and panthers. They are quiet hunters with sharp claws, moving ears, good night vision, and whiskers that help them judge spaces. Their fur may be short, long, curly, striped, spotted, or many colors. Newborn kittens keep their eyes and ears closed and stay beside their mother. She feeds them and protects them. After a few days they can hear, smell, and taste. When their eyes open, they play, hide, pounce, and learn to hunt. They grow independent, but house cats need people to provide dry shelter, food, and water. In return, cats may greet, purr, cuddle, and listen like caring friends.

Cats can look and act very differently, but they all belong to the same family. Some cats are quiet, some have loud voices, and some have special tails, curly fur, stripes, spots, or colored markings. Cats are skilled animals. They walk on soft padded feet, climb with claws, hear faint sounds, see in darkness, and use whiskers to feel their way. Kittens begin life with closed eyes and ears. Their mother keeps them warm, clean, fed, and safe. Later, kittens open their eyes, play games, chase string, and learn to hide and hunt. At six weeks, they can drink milk from a dish, and before long they can care for themselves. Cats enjoy being independent, so they do not always come when called or stay when held. video_title: Little Red Riding Hood~ Read Aloud

video_title: 📚 Kids Book- Read-Aloud  📚 The Night Before Preschool 🧸 By Natasha Wing. Illustrated by Amy Wummer.

summaries.summary: Billy is going to preschool for the first time. At night, he feels shy and worried. His tummy hurts, and he wonders about the children he will meet. At school, Justin welcomes him and starts a clapping game. The children sing, dance, hear a story, dress up, and play. Billy watches quietly and draws a big dinosaur. He does not eat his snack. Outside, the children ride tricycles, garden, and play in the sand. At nap time, Billy misses his teddy, Jerome, and cannot sleep. A little girl gives him her soft bunny. Billy feels better and falls asleep. After nap, he plays with Charlene. Soon the parents come. Billy’s mom brings Jerome. Billy sees that his first day is over, and he says he will come back because preschool is fun.

The night before preschool, Billy is awake in bed. He is worried, shy, and unsure about meeting new friends. In the morning, Justin says hello to every child and invites them to play a clapping game. Billy watches while the children sing, dance, listen to a Mother Goose rhyme, and dress up. He stays by himself, but he draws a dinosaur and shows it to Justin. The class has a snack, plays outside, and then rests on mats. Billy cannot nap because his teddy, Jerome, is at home. A little girl sees that he is sad and shares her fuzzy bunny. Billy’s tummy feels better, and he sleeps. After nap, Billy plays with Charlene and chooses blue rings. When the parents arrive, Billy’s mother brings Jerome. Billy is happy and tells everyone that preschool is fun.

Billy feels nervous about his first day at preschool. He hides behind his mother and worries about making friends. His teacher, Justin, welcomes him and leads the children in songs, dances, stories, costumes, and games. Billy is quiet at first. He watches the other children and draws a tall dinosaur. He skips his snack, then joins the class outside for tricycles, gardening, and sand play. During quiet time, Billy misses his teddy, Jerome, so he cannot sleep. A little girl kindly lends him her soft rabbit. Billy cuddles the bunny, feels calm, and falls asleep. Later, he plays with Charlene and helps make pretend blue and green rings. Soon the children hear the parents arriving. Billy’s mother brings Jerome and gives him a hug. Billy is glad to see his teddy. He is no longer afraid of preschool and happily says he will return the next day.

video_title: 🐱 Stack the Cats 🐱 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: One cat sleeps. Two cats play. Three cats stack. Four cats teeter, and five cats totter. Six cats prefer two stacks of three cats. Seven cats nap. Eight cats try to stack, but eight cats tumble. Nine cats agree to make three groups of three. Ten cats are too many, so one cat sleeps. Two cats climb up and away. Two cats hide, two cats seek, and three cats stack. The story ends by asking how you will stack the cats.

The cats are counted from one to ten. One cat sleeps, while two cats play and three cats stack. Four cats teeter, and five cats totter. Six cats choose two stacks of three cats. Seven cats nap. Eight cats try, but they tumble. Nine cats agree to three, three, and three. Ten cats are too many, so one cat sleeps. Two cats climb away. Then two cats hide, two cats seek, and three cats stack. How will you stack the cats?

First, one cat sleeps. Then two cats play, three cats stack, four cats teeter, and five cats totter. Six cats prefer two stacks of three, and seven cats nap. Eight cats try to stack, but eight cats tumble. Nine cats agree to three groups of three. Ten cats are just too many, so one cat sleeps. Two cats climb up and away. Two cats hide, two cats seek, and three cats stack. The cats leave a question: how will you stack the cats?

video_title: 'The Lonely Trail' Read By Lesley Grantham | Halloween Short Stories

summaries.summary: Albert is a private investigator following a mysterious woman on a train. She wears a fur coat, a red scarf, dark glasses, and high heels, and she never seems to look back. Albert was hired by an unknown man to discover what the man’s wife was doing. The woman leaves the train at Lancaster and walks through town to a bus station. Albert follows her onto a double-decker bus heading toward Morecambe Bay. After they reach the promenade, she walks onto the beach, even though the weather is cold and the sand is dangerous. Albert realizes that she may be planning something terrible and runs after her. He reaches the water and sees her without her disguise. She is Angela, someone he recognizes. Before he can speak with her, several hard-faced men arrive. Angela says she has no choice while the men attack Albert and carry him toward the quicksand. She cries as they take him away, leaving a lonely trail of tears on her cheek.

A private detective named Albert watches a woman during a long train journey. He notices her unusual clothing and follows her because an unknown client paid him to learn what she is doing. The woman travels from the train to a town information office, then boards a bus. Albert follows without knowing where she is headed. The bus carries them toward the bleak coast of Morecambe Bay. When the woman leaves the bus, she walks along the empty promenade and turns onto the beach. She continues toward the water in dangerous conditions, and Albert begins to suspect that she is not meeting a lover at all. He struggles through wet sand and freezing seawater to reach her. At the shore, the woman removes her scarf and sunglasses. Albert recognizes her as Angela, although her hair has been changed to a false red color. Before they can escape, men come from the dunes and beat Albert. Angela says she cannot stop them, and they carry him toward quicksand while she cries.

Albert’s assignment begins when he follows a disguised woman wearing a fur coat, crimson scarf, sunglasses, and black shoes. His unknown employer wants information about his wife, and Albert expects a large payment. The woman travels north by train, leaves at Lancaster, and walks to a bus station. Albert carefully stays behind her and follows her onto a bus. The journey ends beside the sea at Morecambe Bay, where she walks across the beach toward the water. The sand is shifting, the tide is dangerous, and the weather is bitterly cold. Albert understands that she may be going to do something desperate, so he hurries after her. At the water’s edge, the woman removes her disguise. Albert discovers that she is Angela, whom he knows. She looks at him, but armed-looking men appear behind him. Angela tells him she has no choice. The men punch Albert and carry him toward quicksand while Angela remains behind, weeping.

video_title: PING | A charming book about making that personal connection

summaries.summary: Ping is a way of sending something from yourself into the world. You can ping with your voice, fingers, brush, poem, or a small or big gesture. You can express feelings, say, “I love you,” and share your mind, heart, and dreams. You can ping to one person, a few people, everyone, or life itself. The other person gives the pong, and you cannot decide how that person will respond. The pong may smile, become scared, become angry, or not notice. After you ping, breathe deeply and keep your heart open. Then listen for the pong. It may give you something to learn, think about, be thankful for, keep, or let go. Sometimes you may need to pause. The story asks what your next ping will be.

The story tells a friend to ping bravely and openly. A ping can be made with a voice, fingers, brush, poem, or gesture. It can carry feelings that need to come out, such as saying, “I love you.” A person can ping one person, many people, everyone, or life. A ping can bring thoughts, dreams, and feelings into the real world. But the pong belongs to someone else. The other person may smile, feel scared, feel angry, or not notice, so the response is not under the sender’s control. The story says to ping freely, generously, curiously, passionately, and kindly, even when scared. After sending a ping, breathe deeply and listen with an open heart. The pong may offer a lesson, a thought, thankfulness, a challenge, or something to keep or release.

Ping begins with sending something out into the world. It may be a word, a poem, a brush mark, a little gesture, or a big gesture. It may show love and bring a person’s heart, mind, and dreams into real life. The story reminds us that the pong comes from the other person. That person might smile back, become scared, become angry, or not notice the ping. Since the response cannot be controlled, the story encourages sending pings freely, bravely, joyfully, persistently, and with love. When the ping is finished, the sender should breathe deeply and leave the heart open. Then it is time to listen. The pong may bring something to learn, think about, appreciate, keep, release, or use as a challenge. A pause may also be needed, for a short time or as long as necessary. The story ends by asking about the next ping.

video_title: 🛻💨 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Pixar Cars Toon : Tokyo Mater

summaries.summary: Mater tells Lightning McQueen about a big adventure in Tokyo. First, Mater helps an older car named Osan and tows him all the way to Tokyo. There, Mater bumps into Kabuto, the leader of some ninja cars. Kabuto challenges Mater to a drift race to the top of Tokyo Tower. Other cars give Mater blue paint and a big spoiler. During the race, Mater misses a turn and gets chased by a police car. He drives through a donut shop and then meets ninjas. Lightning joins the adventure and helps Mater send the ninjas flying. Mater and Lightning slide on spilled oil, and an explosion sends Mater into the air. At the tower, Mater drives backward and wins the race. Kabuto loses his special changes and becomes a plain car. Mater celebrates and becomes king of the Drifters.

One day, Mater drives from Carburetor County to Tokyo while towing Osan. Tokyo has very tall buildings, and Mater accidentally scratches Kabuto's paint. Kabuto is angry and challenges Mater to a race. The cars must drift up to Tokyo Tower. Mater gets shiny blue paint and a large spoiler, but Kabuto is still faster. Mater misses a turn and drives the wrong way. A police officer follows him into a donut shop, where cars spin around. Then ninja cars surround Mater and make him slow down. Lightning McQueen comes to help. Lightning kicks the ninjas away, and the two friends chase Kabuto. They slide on oil at a construction site, and an explosion sends Mater over the city. Mater lands near Kabuto and drives backward up the tower road. Kabuto pushes him over a railing, but Mater uses his tow hook to pull himself up. Mater reaches the top first and wins.

Mater says he was once an import car. His story begins when he takes Osan to Tokyo. After Mater bumps Kabuto, Kabuto challenges him to a drift race. The winner will be king of the Drifters, and the loser will lose all his modifications. Mater gets a blue paint job and a spoiler for the race. Kabuto leads through the streets, while Mater misses a turn and is chased by a police officer. Mater escapes through a donut shop, but ninjas surround him. Lightning McQueen appears and saves Mater by knocking the ninjas away. Together, they hurry toward Tokyo Tower. A crane spills oil, so the cars slide. Lightning helps Mater fly through an explosion. Mater then lands in front of Kabuto and drives backward up the tower road. Kabuto pushes Mater over the railing, but Mater catches the tower with his tow hook. He climbs to the top first, wins the race, and celebrates.

video_title: A Camping Spree With Mr. Magee (unexpected adventures) #kids #story #toddlers #kindergarten #reading

summaries.summary: Mr. McGee and his little spotted dog, D, packed their camper and drove to the mountains for a camping trip. They found a beautiful place beside a stream and a waterfall. They made a fire, cooked hot dogs, and roasted marshmallows before going to sleep. During the night, a bear smelled the sweet marshmallows. The bear could not see well, so he pushed under the hitch while trying to reach the treat. The hitch came loose, and the car and camper began rolling in different directions. The camper rolled into the stream with McGee and D inside. They were swept toward the waterfall, but the camper became stuck on a rock. The bear saw the hitch in the water and thought it was a marshmallow. He pulled the camper back to the bank, then dropped the hitch when he tasted it. The camper rolled into bushes. McGee and D fixed it, went home, and decided to camp in their backyard instead.

Early one morning, Mr. McGee and his dog D went camping in the mountains. They chose a high hill with lovely mountain views and a brook that flowed over a waterfall. After dinner and marshmallows, they climbed into their cozy camper beds. A kind but nearsighted bear came looking for a marshmallow snack. While squeezing beneath the camper’s hitch, he accidentally knocked it loose. The camper rolled down the hill and splashed into the stream while McGee and D slept inside. They woke up in the rapids and saw that they were moving toward a tall waterfall. Just before going over the edge, the camper caught on a rock. The bear then saw the hitch floating in the stream and thought it was a marshmallow. He pulled the camper from the rock and dragged it to shore. When he discovered that the hitch was not food, he left. The camper rolled into bushes beside the car. McGee and D connected everything again and drove home. Their camping trip ended in the backyard.

Mr. McGee told D that camping would be wonderful, so they drove to a quiet mountain campsite. They enjoyed the view, cooked hot dogs, and roasted marshmallows by the fire. After they went to bed, a hungry bear followed the marshmallow smell. The bear tried to squeeze under the hitch, and the hitch snapped loose. The camper and car started rolling. The car went along an old logging road, but the camper rushed toward the stream with McGee and D asleep inside. It splashed into the water and carried them through the rapids toward a waterfall. The camper stopped on a rock near the edge, keeping them from falling. Then the bear saw the hitch floating and mistook it for a marshmallow. He pulled the camper off the rock and back to the bank. When he learned that the hitch tasted bad, he dropped it and went away. The camper rolled into bushes beside the car. McGee and D fixed it, drove home, and chose the backyard for their next camping trip.

video_title: Franklin's Valentines - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook - NO ADS

summaries.summary: Franklin made Valentine cards for all his friends and carefully put them in his bag before school. At school, he was excited for the party, but when he opened his bag, his cards were gone. His mother found them outside in a puddle of slush, and the cards were ruined. Franklin felt sad and thought he could not join the party. Mr. Owl reminded him that if Bear lost his cards, Franklin would still give Bear a Valentine because Bear was his friend. Soon, Franklin’s friends gave him many cards. Bear said he did not need a Valentine to know Franklin was his friend. Franklin felt happy. That night, Franklin decided to make extra-special cards for his friends. The next morning, he made cards and gave them to everyone. He called it Friendship Day and said it could be any day.

Franklin knew many things, and he was especially ready for Valentine’s Day. He had made cards for his friends, but the cards disappeared from his school bag. His mother discovered that they had fallen into slush, so they were ruined. Franklin cried and hid in the cloakroom because he had no cards to give. Mr. Owl helped Franklin think about Bear. Franklin knew he would still give Bear a card if Bear had lost his, because Bear was his friend. Mr. Owl said Bear might feel the same way. Franklin returned to the party, where his friends gave him cards. Bear told him that a card was not needed to know they were friends. Franklin opened cards from Snail, Goose, and Fox, and everyone laughed together. Later, Franklin made new cards and gave them to his friends the next day. He called the day Friendship Day.

On Valentine’s Day, Franklin counted the cards he had made and brought them to school. When the party began, he searched his bag, but he found only other things. His Valentines were missing. His mother said the cards were outside in slush and ruined. Franklin felt he did not belong at the party. Mr. Owl asked whether Franklin would refuse to give Bear a card if Bear lost his Valentines. Franklin said no, because Bear was his friend. Then Franklin understood that Bear could still be his friend too. His classmates gave Franklin cards, including a turtle cutout, a turtle poem, and a turtle riddle. Bear said their friendship did not depend on a Valentine. Franklin thanked his friends and planned to make more cards. The next morning, he made cards and gave them to everyone. He said Friendship Day could happen on any day.

video_title: Clifford Goes to Kindergarten - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook

summaries.summary: Emily Elizabeth is going to kindergarten, and she feels scared at first. Her mother tells her that she will make friends and learn about writing, counting, animals, and her neighborhood. Emily visits the school and meets Miss Tate. She worries about missing home and having no friends, but her mother says Miss Tate will help her. Emily brings Clifford on the first day because her teacher says children may bring something from home. The children smile when they see him. Clifford joins the welcome song by howling, takes a turn answering a question, and gives slobbery kisses to children who feel nervous. He knocks over paint with his tail, but everyone still likes him. At recess, the children play with Clifford and make friends. At nap time, Clifford lets everyone snuggle with him, so they fall asleep. Emily decides her first day was a big success and wants to return tomorrow.

Before her first day, Emily Elizabeth learns that kindergarten can be a place for making friends and learning new things. She visits the classroom with Clifford and practices playing school at home. Emily asks what will happen if she misses home or cannot make friends. Her mother explains that Miss Tate will help her. When a letter says each child may bring something comforting, Emily knows she will bring Clifford. At school, Clifford surprises Miss Tate and makes the other children happy. He howls during the welcome song and joins the class activities. He helps nervous children with kisses, although they are very slobbery. During painting, Clifford wags his tail and spills water and paint. At lunch, Miss Tate says everyone must eat their own food. At recess, Clifford helps the children play and make friends. Later, the tired children cannot get comfortable on the rug, so Clifford lets them cuddle with him. They nap, wake up ready to learn, and Emily loves school.

Emily Elizabeth tells about her first kindergarten day with her big dog, Clifford. She was worried before school, but visiting the school and meeting kind Miss Tate helped her feel better. Her mother also explained that Miss Tate would help if Emily felt sad or had trouble making friends. Emily brought Clifford from home to feel comfortable. The other children brought toys, blankets, or stuffed animals, and they were glad to see Clifford. He tried to sing, answered a board question, and helped children who were nervous about writing. His wet kisses made them laugh. Clifford missed home when Emily painted a picture of it, and his fast wagging tail spilled the paint and water. At lunch, the children ate their own food. At recess, Clifford played with everyone, and Emily made many friends. During nap time, the children found the rug uncomfortable. Clifford let them snuggle close, and everyone fell asleep. Emily woke up happy and said kindergarten was a big success.

video_title: 101 Dalmations@Readingtimewithnana

summaries.summary: Pongo, Pita, and their fifteen puppies lived happily with Roger and Anita in London. Cruella DeVille wanted to buy the puppies, but Roger and Anita said no. One cold night, two men took the puppies away in a big bag. The puppies were brought to a house with many other puppies. Pongo and Pita were very sad, so they used the Twilight Bark to send a message to dogs everywhere. The message reached Colonel and Sergeant Tibs. They found the puppies and helped them escape through a hole in the wall. Pongo and Pita came through a window and fought the men. On the way home, other dogs helped the family. The dogs hid under black soot so they could ride in a van. Cruella chased them, but her car slid into a ditch. The puppies arrived home safely. Roger and Anita counted 101 Dalmatians and bought a big country house.

In London, Pongo and Pita lived with fifteen puppies, Roger, and Anita. Cruella DeVille asked to buy the puppies, but the family refused. Later, two men kidnapped all fifteen puppies and took them to a mansion where many other Dalmatian puppies were waiting. Pongo and Pita wanted to find their babies. They barked the Twilight Bark, a dog message made of long and short barks. Dogs across London heard it, and the message reached Colonel and Sergeant Tibs on a farm. The two helpers went to the mansion and saw the puppies. When Cruella ordered the men to make coats, Tibs helped the puppies squeeze through a hole. The puppies ran, and Pongo and Pita rescued them. Many dogs helped them travel home. The dogs used soot to look like black Labradors. Cruella chased them, but her car crashed into a ditch. Everyone reached home, and the family became 101 Dalmatians.

Pongo and Pita had a cozy home in London with their fifteen spotted puppies. Their friends Roger and Anita loved them. Cruella DeVille wanted the puppies, but Roger and Anita would not sell them. Soon, two men stole the puppies and carried them to a house filled with Dalmatian puppies. Pongo and Pita sent news through the Twilight Bark. Colonel and Sergeant Tibs heard the message and hurried to the mansion. They learned that the puppies had been stolen. Tibs made a small escape hole, and the puppies squeezed through it. The men chased them, but Pongo and Pita broke through a window and saved the puppies. The dogs crossed a frozen stream and received help from other dogs. They hid their spots with soot and climbed into a moving van. Cruella followed them, but her car slipped on the icy road and landed in a ditch. The puppies returned to Roger and Anita. The family counted 101 Dalmatians and lived happily in a country home.

video_title: The Legend of Rock Paper Scissors. Read Aloud for Kids.

summaries.summary: Rock was the strongest warrior in Back Garden, but he felt sad because nobody could challenge him. He defeated Cloth Pig and an apricot in the garden, yet neither battle made him happy. In another place, Paper was the cleverest warrior, but nobody could outwit him. He defeated a computer printer and a bag of trail mix, then left to search for a true match. Scissors was the fastest warrior in a tiny kitchen village. She beat a roll of tape and dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets, but she also wanted a worthy opponent. At last, Rock met Scissors in a garage and defeated her. Then Rock met Paper, and Paper defeated him. Scissors then defeated Paper. The three warriors were delighted because each had finally found a match. They hugged, danced, and became best friends. They played a great three-way battle, and children still honor them by playing rock, paper, scissors.

In the kingdom of Back Garden, Rock was very strong, but he had no equal. He traveled through the garden and defeated Cloth Pig and an apricot. Rock still wanted a harder fight. Paper lived in the Empire of Mama study. He was very clever, but no warrior could outwit him. He battled a computer printer and a bag of trail mix, winning both times. Scissors lived in a tiny kitchen village and was the fastest warrior. She defeated a roll of tape and dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets. She also went searching for someone equal to her. Rock and Scissors finally met in a garage, and Rock won. Then Rock faced Paper, and Paper won. Scissors faced Paper and won too. The three warriors were happy because each one had met a warrior who could beat them. They hugged and danced together. Their joyful battle continued, and children around the world play their game to remember them.

Rock, Paper, and Scissors were three great warriors who each wanted a worthy opponent. Rock was strong, Paper was clever, and Scissors was fast. Rock traveled around Back Garden and won against Cloth Pig and an apricot. Paper crossed desk Mountain and defeated a computer printer and a bag of trail mix. Scissors traveled through the kitchen and beat a roll of tape and dinosaur-shaped chicken nuggets. None of them felt satisfied because their opponents were not equal. In a garage, Rock and Scissors met. Rock won their battle. Soon Rock met Paper, and Paper won. Paper then met Scissors, and Scissors won. At last, every warrior had found a match. The three friends hugged and danced. They began a huge three-way battle that was full of joy. The story says their battle still continues today, because children play rock, paper, scissors in gardens, on playgrounds, and in classrooms.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse 📖 Read Along Storybook for Kids | Space Adventure

summaries.summary: Mickey and his friends fly into space with a treasure map. They must find ten bright treasure stars before they can reach a mystery planet. Space pirate Pete follows them because he wants the treasure. Pete tries milk cartons, a pretend old lady, and other tricks. Mickey and his friends find three stars on the moon and three stars on Mars. Pete takes their map, but Pluto helps Mickey after he floats among space rocks. They find four more stars near Saturn and get the map back. At planet Mickey, Pete's sticky web catches Quoodles and Toodles. Mickey and Pete work together and break the web, so both friends are free. Pluto digs up a treasure chest. Inside is a remote control. Mickey pushes the button, and a Mickey Mouse face house rises from the ground. Everyone dances, and Mickey and his friends fly home.

Mickey, Minnie, Goofy, Donald, Pluto, and Toodles begin a space trip with Professor Von Drake's treasure map. The professor says they need ten treasure stars to find the hidden treasure. Pete secretly follows them with Quudles. First, Pete surrounds the rocket with milk cartons, but Toodles brings a giant cookie, and the cartons float away. On the moon, Moonmen Chip and Dale show the friends three treasure stars. On Mars, Martian Mickey leads them to three more stars in a Star Tree. Pete tricks Goofy and takes the map. Mickey and Donald chase him around Saturn, and Pluto rescues Mickey from space. The friends find the last four stars and recover the map. The stars lead them to planet Mickey. Pete's web catches Quoodles and Toodles. Mickey and Pete work together to break it. Pluto finds the treasure chest, and Mickey's button brings up a new Mickey Mouse face house.

A treasure hunt takes Mickey and his friends to the moon, Mars, Saturn, and planet Mickey. They need ten stars to show the way. Pete wants the treasure, so he follows the rocket and keeps making tricks. His milk-carton plan fails when Toodles sends a big cookie into space. Moonman Chip and Moonman Dale help the group find stars one, two, and three. Martian Mickey helps them find stars four, five, and six. Pete then pretends to be a lost old lady and gets the map from Goofy. During the chase, Mickey floats away, but Pluto saves him. They find stars seven, eight, nine, and ten, and Donald gets the map back. On planet Mickey, a sticky web traps Quoodles and Toodles. Pete asks for help, and Mickey says they can work together. Mickey and Pete break the web. Pluto digs up the treasure, which is a remote control. Mickey presses it, and a Mickey Mouse face house rises from the ground.

video_title: ♥️ 🐈‍⬛ Pete the Cat Valentines Day is Cool | Read Aloud Story Book for Kids

summaries.summary: Pete the Cat does not think Valentine's Day is cool. His friend Callie tells him that it is a special day for telling people how much they mean to you. Pete thinks about her words and decides to make cards. At home, he tries to make perfect cards for everyone in his class. His mom tells him to do his best and write why each person is cool. Pete makes cards for Larry, the boys, the girls, and his mom. The next morning, Pete remembers that he forgot Mr. Ted, the bus driver. He quickly makes a card and gives it to him. Pete and Callie also make cards for Mrs. Gold and other people. After school, Pete goes to Callie's party. He worries because he forgot her card, but Callie says spending time together is better than a card. Pete decides it is the best Valentine's Day ever.

The day before Valentine's Day, Pete rides home and sees Callie holding a red heart. Callie says Valentine's Day is her favorite holiday because it helps people tell others they are special. Pete first says the holiday is not cool, but then he changes his mind. He gathers paper and crayons and starts making cards. Pete wants every card to be perfect, so he worries he will not finish. His mom tells him to do his best and think about what is cool about each cat. Pete makes cards for Larry, Josh, Trey, Rob, John, the girls in his class, and his mom. On the bus, Pete notices he forgot Mr. Ted. He makes a card before school, and Mr. Ted says it made his day. Pete and Callie then make more cards for people, including Mrs. Gold. At Callie's party, Pete forgets her card, but Callie says being together is better.

Pete learns that Valentine's Day can be cool. At first, he does not want to make cards, but Callie explains that cards help show people they are special. Pete goes home and works at the kitchen table with pencils, paper, crayons, and markers. He makes cards for his classmates and a large heart-shaped card for his mom. His mother helps him by saying that he should do his best and tell Larry why he is cool. The next day, Pete tells Callie that she was right about Valentine's Day. Then he remembers that Mr. Ted has no card. Pete draws one on the bus and thanks Mr. Ted for taking the children to school. Mr. Ted is happy. Pete and Callie decide to make Valentines for everyone, including Mrs. Gold. Later, Pete visits Callie's party and realizes he forgot her card. Callie says that spending time with Pete is better than any card, and Pete calls it the best Valentine's Day ever.

video_title: The Hat by Jan Brett - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Winter was coming, so Lisa put her woolen clothes outside to air. A strong wind blew one stocking away. Hedgy the hedgehog found it, and it got stuck on his prickles like a hat. The hen, gander, cat, dog, puppies, pig, and pony all laughed at him. Hedgy said the hat would keep him warm and dry, but the animals ran away to find clothes of their own. Hedgy became tired of being laughed at and went toward his den. Lisa followed with the other stocking. She pulled the stocking from Hedgy’s head and said that animals do not wear clothes. Then Lisa saw that the other animals had taken her woolens. Each animal thought it was wearing a magnificent hat. Hedgy reached his den and looked at the animals. He thought they looked ridiculous and wondered if they knew that animals should never wear clothes.

Lisa hung her woolen clothes outside on a winter day. The wind carried away one stocking, and Hedgy found it. When Hedgy pulled his nose out, the stocking stayed on his prickles. He called it his new hat. Many animals saw him. The mother hen laughed, the gander laughed, the cat called him silly, and the dog and puppies giggled. Hedgy told them that his hat would keep him cozy, warm, and dry. The animals began running away, and soon they found Lisa’s other woolen clothes. A pig asked Hedgy what he was doing, and Hedgy said he was making sure his hat would not blow away. The pony laughed too, and Hedgy felt sad and wanted to be alone. Lisa caught him and took off the stocking. She said animals do not wear clothes. Then Lisa saw the animals wearing her woolens as hats, while Hedgy watched from his den.

A stocking blew from Lisa’s clothesline while winter was near. Hedgy found it and accidentally wore it on his head. He liked having the stocking there and told the other animals it was a hat. The hen, gander, cat, dog, puppies, pig, and pony all made fun of him. Hedgy explained that the hat would protect him from rain, snow, and icy wind. The animals listened and then hurried away. Hedgy became upset because everyone laughed, and he worried that the stocking would keep him from fitting inside his den. Lisa came after him with another stocking. She pulled the first stocking off his head and told him that animals do not wear clothes. When Lisa returned to the clothesline, she discovered that the animals had taken her missing woolens. They were now wearing the clothes as magnificent hats. Hedgy reached his den, saw the animals, and thought they looked ridiculous because animals should never wear clothes.

video_title: Falling Up - a poem by Shel Silverstein

summaries.summary: A child tripped on a shoelace and fell upward instead of downward. The child went up to the rooftops, over the town, past the treetops, and over the mountains. The child kept going to a strange place where colors blended into sounds. Being so high and seeing everything around made the child very dizzy. When the child looked around, the dizziness became worse. The child got sick to the stomach and threw down. The poem follows the child’s surprising journey upward and ends with the child feeling ill.

The story begins when the speaker trips on a shoelace. Instead of falling down, the speaker falls up. The journey rises to the rooftops, passes over the town and treetops, and continues over the mountains. The speaker reaches a place where colors blend into sounds. This unusual height and view make the speaker dizzy. After looking around, the speaker feels sick to the stomach. The story ends when the speaker throws down. The events happen in order: a trip, an upward fall, a journey above familiar places, dizziness, sickness, and throwing down.

A shoelace causes the speaker to trip, but the fall goes upward. The speaker travels up to the rooftops, over the town, past the treetops, and over the mountains. The speaker goes even farther, to a place where colors blend into sounds. The strange journey makes the speaker dizzy. When the speaker looks around, the feeling becomes too strong, and the speaker gets sick to the stomach. At the end, the speaker throws down. The poem describes an unusual upward fall from the ground to the rooftops, town, trees, mountains, and beyond.

video_title: Peanut Butter & Cupcake! (Children’s Book Read Aloud)

summaries.summary: Peanut Butter gets a ball for his birthday, but playing alone is not much fun. His mom tells him to go outside and find a friend. He asks Hamburger, Cupcake, Egg, Meatball, French Fries, and Soup to play. Hamburger is busy, Cupcake is building sprinkle castles, Egg cracks jokes and then cracks, Meatball is counting jumps, French Fries must help Hamburger, and Soup shows Peanut Butter the letters N and O. Peanut Butter becomes tired and sad and sits on a bench. Then Jelly comes over. Peanut Butter asks Jelly to play, and Jelly agrees if Peanut Butter will teach her to balance the ball on her head. They teach each other, laugh together, and soon the other children come to play too. Everyone knocks the ball with their feet, heads, and even buns. Peanut Butter is happy because all the friends go together like peanut butter and jelly.

Peanut Butter wants someone to play ball with him. He visits many children, but each one is busy or says no. Hamburger is walking dogs. Cupcake is making sprinkle castles and does not want her castle hit. Egg makes a funny joke and cracks. Meatball is counting jumps to make a record. French Fries needs to help Hamburger, and Soup says no with letters in a spoon. Peanut Butter keeps walking until he is tired and nearly gives up. Then Jelly says hello. Peanut Butter asks her to play, and Jelly says she will be his friend if he teaches her to balance the ball on her head. Jelly is good with her feet, so they teach each other. Their laughter brings the other children over. The children join the game, and Peanut Butter laughs because all of them can play together.

Peanut Butter receives a ball and tries to find a playmate in his new town. He can balance the ball on his head, but he is not very good at kicking it. He first meets Hamburger, Cupcake, Egg, Meatball, French Fries, and Soup. None of them plays with him. Some are busy, some are counting, and some are helping someone else. Soup shows Peanut Butter an N and an O, so Peanut Butter moves on. He feels sad on a bench until Jelly walks up and says hello. Jelly wants to be his friend, but she needs help balancing the ball on her head. Peanut Butter teaches Jelly, and Jelly teaches Peanut Butter to use his feet. They laugh together. Their laughter brings the other children, who ask to join. Soon everyone plays with the ball, and Peanut Butter feels happy with his new friends.

video_title: I Want to Sleep Under the Stars!

summaries.summary: Zoom Squirrel tells Zip Squirrel that sleeping under the stars is a dream. Zoom loves the stars, peace, and quiet, but has never slept outside before. Zip calls the other squirrel friends, and they decide to help. The friends explain that encouragement means telling someone, “You can do it,” so that person feels brave. They build a little tower and cheer, “Go Zooie!” and “Sleep!” Zoom does not like the cheering and asks them to stop. Zoom wants peace and quiet instead. The squirrels try to become Team Peace and Team Quiet, but their repeated sounds still do not help. Zoom is awake, and the stars have disappeared. The squirrels decide this is a squirrel problem and promise to find a squirrel solution. Zoom learns that squirrels do not know much about sleeping under the stars, but the friends show that they do not give up on a friend.

Zoom Squirrel wants to sleep under the stars because the stars are beautiful and quiet. Zoom has never done it before, so the squirrel friends gather to help. They learn that encouragement means giving a friend courage by saying that the friend can do something new. The squirrels make a little tower and cheer for Zoom. Their loud cheering does not feel helpful to Zoom. Zoom says, “Please stop,” and explains that peace and quiet are needed for sleep. The friends change their plan and call themselves Team Peace and Team Quiet. They say “Peace” and “Quiet” again and again, but Zoom is still awake. When Zoom looks up, the stars are gone. The friends wonder if it is too late or too early, then decide to search for a squirrel solution. At the end, Zoom learns that squirrels know little about sleeping under the stars, but they know not to give up on a friend.

One night, Zoom Squirrel tells Zip Squirrel, “I want to sleep under the stars.” Zoom likes the stars and dreams of sleeping peacefully outside. Zip and the other squirrels want to help Zoom try something new. They explain encouragement and cheer for Zoom from a little tower. However, Zoom does not want cheering. Zoom wants everything to be peaceful and quiet. The squirrels listen and try another plan. They become Team Peace and Team Quiet, making soft-sounding words and repeating “Peace” and “Quiet.” Even this plan does not work. Zoom tells the friends that sleep is not happening. Zoom is still awake, and the stars have gone away. The squirrels do not leave. They decide to find a solution together because this is a squirrel problem. Zoom then says that squirrels do not know much about sleeping under the stars. The story also shows that the squirrels do know one important thing: they do not give up on a friend.

video_title: Bluey the Beach kids book read along

summaries.summary: Bluey, Bingo, Mum, and Dad go to the beach. They put up a tent, play in the sand, and race to the water. Mum walks along the beach by herself. Bluey finds a beautiful shell and wants to show it to her. Dad says Bluey may go alone, but she must stay out of the water. Bingo tells Bluey to follow Mum’s footprints. Bluey hops, runs, skips, and does cartwheels. A wave washes the footprints away. Bluey sees a crab, walks like it, and pretends to have crab legs. Then she meets a jellyfish and uses a stick to poke it. She passes an old castle and a pelican. Bluey feels unsure, but she is brave and walks around the pelican. Mum finds her. Bluey shows Mum the shell and says she loves walking by herself. When Mum asks why, Bluey says, “I don’t know. I just do.”

At the beach, Bluey and Bingo play with Mum and Dad. Mum decides to walk along the sand alone. Bluey finds a shell and asks to take it to Mum. Dad lets her go, as long as she does not enter the water. Bingo says Bluey can follow Mum’s footprints, so Bluey follows them while running, skipping, and doing cartwheels. Seagulls are in her way, but Bluey politely asks them to move. Then a big wave covers Mum’s footprints. Bluey worries because she does not know where Mum went. She sees a crab and copies its sideways walk. She gets past a jellyfish with a stick, then passes an old castle and meets a pelican. Bluey looks back and sees Dad far away. She remembers the creatures she passed and bravely walks around the pelican. Mum’s voice calls to her. Bluey gives Mum the shell and says she likes walking alone.

Bluey goes to the beach with Bingo, Mum, and Dad. While they play, Mum goes for a walk. Bluey wants to bring Mum a beautiful shell, so Dad lets her walk after Mum’s footprints. Bluey pretends she is a mermaid with legs. She hops from footprint to footprint and does cartwheels in the sand. First, she meets seagulls. Then a wave washes the footprints away, and Bluey cannot follow them anymore. A crab walks by, and Bluey copies its sideways steps. Next, she sees a jellyfish. Bluey pokes it with a stick and keeps going. She finds an old castle and leaves the stick there. A pelican blocks her path, and Bluey feels she has walked far enough. Dad is only a tiny speck behind her. Bluey remembers being brave and walks around the pelican. The pelican flies away, and Mum appears. Bluey shows Mum the shell and says she loves walking by herself.

video_title: All About Bluey - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: Bluey wakes up ready to play. She makes games with her little sister, Bingo, and likes choosing the rules. Bluey pretends to be a grown-up. She plays shop, hotel, and doctor games. Her friends join her, but sometimes they take a long time deciding who will play each part. At school, Bluey listens to stories and makes things. Her friends play in different ways. Some protect things, and Rusty likes building. Together, the children have big adventures. At home, Bluey plays with Dad. They laugh, play games, and act silly. Bluey also loves hugs and stories from Mom. Sometimes new things, like riding a bike, are hard. Bluey is learning to be brave. At the end of the day, she enjoys being with her whole family.

Bluey starts her morning with a happy idea. She and Bingo make up games and pretend to be grannies, shopkeepers, hotel workers, and doctors. Bluey enjoys being in charge, but choosing the rules and characters can take a long time. At school, she listens to stories, makes things, and sees that every friend has a different way to play. The children protect things, build, and go on adventures together. At home, Bluey and Dad play Magic Xylophone, Wrestle, and Freeze. They laugh a lot, even when Bluey forgets what game they were playing. Bluey loves Mom's hugs and her exciting stories. When a game goes wrong, Mom is ready for a chat. Bluey likes trying new things, but riding her bike is hard. She is learning ways to be brave. In the evening, Bluey ends her fun day by spending special time with her family.

Bluey is a playful puppy who loves games and adventures. She begins the day by jumping out of bed and playing with Bingo. They pretend to be grown-ups and make games about shops, hotels, grannies, and doctors. Sometimes Bluey and Bingo disagree about whose turn it is. At school, Bluey listens to stories and makes things with her friends. The friends all have special ways to pretend. They protect, build, and explore together. At home, Bluey plays with Dad. They play, laugh, and become silly. Bluey likes hugs from Mom, too. Mom tells stories and goes on pretend adventures with her. When Bluey has a problem, Mom is there to talk. New activities can be difficult for Bluey, especially riding her bike. She says it is not fair, but she is learning to be brave. Later, she enjoys a happy evening with her family.

video_title: Bonaparte Falls Apart: A Halloween Book for Kids and Toddlers. Read Aloud Kids Books

summaries.summary: Bonapart was falling to pieces. When he rode his bike, played catch, or went to the doctor, his bones sometimes rolled away. He worried that children at school would laugh at him. His friends tried to help. Frankystein glued and screwed Bonapart's bones together, but Bonapart could not move. Blacky Widow spun and pinned a web around him, but he became tangled. Mamula wrapped and strapped his bones, but Bonapart could not see. Each friend had to undo the work. Then Bonapart's head fell off because he was worried. His friends searched for another idea. A dog ran by carrying a bone, so they brought the dog to Bonapart. Bonapart trained the dog, named Mandible, to retrieve his bones. At school, Mandible helped him. The children enjoyed Bonapart at recess, lunch, and science class, and nobody made fun of him. Bonapart was happy with his friends and his dog.

Bonapart was made of bones that could come apart. His bones rolled away when he rode his bike, played catch, or visited the doctor's office. He was afraid school would be difficult because other children might make fun of him. Frankystein tried to glue and screw the bones together, but Bonapart could not walk. Blacky Widow tried to hold him with a web, but he became tangled. Mamula wrapped and strapped him, but he could not see. All three friends had to take their ideas apart. While they were thinking, Bonapart's head fell off. His friends promised to keep looking. Then they saw a dog with a bone. They brought the dog to Bonapart and taught him to retrieve his loose bones. Bonapart named the dog Mandible. At school, he became a hit at recess, lunch, and science class. He could hang loose without being teased, and that made him very happy.

Bonapart was worried because his bones often fell apart and rolled away. He wondered what would happen when school began. His friend Frankystein glued and screwed him together, but Bonapart could not move. Blacky Widow pinned him in a web, but he was tangled. Mamula wrapped and strapped him, but he could not see. The friends removed each unsuccessful fix and looked for a better answer. Bonapart became so worried that his head fell off, but Frankystein put it back. Then a dog came by with a bone in its mouth. Mamula said the dog would be perfect for Bonapart. The friends brought the dog over, and Frankystein explained that Bonapart could teach it to retrieve bones. Bonapart named the dog Mandible and trained it for two weeks. At school, Mandible helped him. Bonapart was popular in every class and could relax without being made fun of.

video_title: The very busy spider! By: Eric Carle, Read Aloud kids book.

summaries.summary: One morning, a little spider came to a farm. A thin thread floated from her body, and she landed on a fence post. She began to spin a web. Many animals came by. The horse asked her to ride. The cow asked her to eat grass. The sheep asked her to run, and the goat asked her to jump. The pig, dog, cat, and duck also invited her to play. The spider did not answer because she was busy making her web. At last, her web was finished. A fly buzzed by, and the spider caught it in the web. An owl asked who made the beautiful web, but the spider was too tired to answer. It had been a very busy day for the spider.

The story begins when the wind blows across a farm and a spider starts making a web on a fence post. A horse wants a ride, and a cow wants to eat grass. A sheep wants to run, while a goat wants to jump on rocks. Then a pig wants to roll in mud. A dog wants to chase a cat, a cat wants to take a nap, and a duck wants to swim. Each animal speaks to the spider, but she does not answer. She keeps spinning her web. When the duck has finished talking, the spider has finished the web too. Soon, a fly comes buzzing near her. The spider catches the fly in her web. An owl asks who built the beautiful web, but the tired spider does not answer. It was a very busy day.

A spider begins a busy morning by spinning a web on a fence post. She keeps working while animals visit the farm. The horse asks her to ride. The cow asks her to eat grass. The sheep asks her to run in the meadow, and the goat asks her to jump on rocks. The pig invites her to roll in mud. The dog wants to chase a cat, the cat wants to sleep, and the duck wants to swim. The spider stays quiet and continues spinning. She is busy making her web. When the web is complete, a fly buzzes by. The spider catches the fly in her web, just like that. An owl sees the beautiful web and asks who built it. The spider is too tired to answer. She has worked all day, and it has been a very busy day.

video_title: Read Aloud Books for Kids | The Way I Act | With Comprehension Questions

summaries.summary: A child learns many ways to act well. The child is curious and wants to learn about the world. The child is responsible by doing homework, fixing a sister's sled, and making the bed. The child is compassionate by holding Grandma's hand and helping friends who fall. The child is trustworthy by leaving things that do not belong to the child and telling the truth. The child is brave at school, while skating, and in the pool. The child is friendly and invites others to read, draw, or climb. The child keeps trying until a puzzle is finished. The child is respectful, cooperative, capable, active, considerate, and imaginative. At the end, the child says that these actions show who the child is and how the child wants to grow.

The story shows a child practicing good choices every day. First, the child asks questions and learns because the child is curious. The child does homework, fixes a sled, and makes the bed because the child is responsible. The child cares for Grandma, friends, and small creatures. The child is trustworthy by not taking what is not theirs and by telling the truth. The child bravely goes to school, skates, and jumps into the pool. The child welcomes friends to read, draw, or climb a tree. The child keeps trying to finish a puzzle. Then the child uses polite words, does not push or tease, passes a soccer ball, and helps fly a kite. The child can sweep, sing, and run, stays active, and treats others gently. The child also enjoys pretend games as a wizard or star. These actions show who the child is and how the child wants to grow.

A child describes many caring and helpful actions. The child wonders about planets and wild keys, showing curiosity. The child works hard at home by doing homework, fixing a sister's sled, and making the bed. When Grandma is sad, the child holds her hand, and when friends fall, the child helps them. The child tells the truth and does not take things that belong to someone else. The child is brave on the school bus, at school, while skating, and in the pool. The child asks others to play, read, draw, or climb. The child finishes a puzzle by not giving up. The child says please, avoids pushing and teasing, shares a soccer ball, and helps with a kite. The child sweeps, sings, runs, dances, jumps, and spins. The child does not scream or hit and gives Grandpa a chair. Finally, the child enjoys imaginative play and wants to keep growing.

video_title: 1 MINUTE READ ALOUD: How Do Dinosaurs Say Happy Birthday? #shorts

summaries.summary: A little dinosaur is having a birthday. The story asks if she takes all the cake, licks all the ice cream, screams at her guests, grabs every present, or makes the party game hard. No, she does not do those things. She greets every guest and says that their presents are simply the best. She gives everyone a large helping of cake. She also shares party favors that she helped make. When the birthday party is over, she thanks Mom and Dad for the very best birthday she has ever had. The party was such fun, and there will be more birthday fun next year. The little dinosaur celebrates by welcoming everyone, sharing cake and favors, and saying thank you.

A dinosaur child celebrates her birthday with many guests. At first, the story asks if she will hog the cake, lick the frosting and ice cream, scream at guests, grab the presents, or make Pin the Tail on the Dinosaur hard. The answer is no. Instead, she greets every guest and tells them that their presents are simply the best. She gives everyone a large helping of cake, so the cake is shared at the party. She also shares party favors that she helped to make. After the party ends, she thanks Mom and Dad for the very best birthday she has ever had. The birthday was such fun, and next year there will be more. Then everyone wishes the little dinosaur a happy birthday.

The little dinosaur has a birthday party. She does not keep all the cake for herself, lick all the ice cream, scream a T-Rex scream at her guests, take all the presents, or make the party game difficult. Instead, she welcomes every guest. She tells each guest that the presents are simply the best. Then she gives everyone a large helping of cake. She shares party favors that she helped to make, too. When the celebration is over, she thanks Mom and Dad. She says it was the very best birthday she has ever had. The party was such fun, and there will be another happy birthday next year. The story ends by wishing the little dinosaur a happy birthday.

video_title: Harrison P. Spader, Personal Space Invader. Read Aloud kids' book.

summaries.summary: Harrison P. Spider loved life and wanted to share his joy with everyone. But he often sat too close, shook hands too hard, and gave very big high-fives. Teachers, coaches, and parents noticed that Harrison was not leaving enough personal space. His dad talked with him and taught him a space saver. Harrison stretched his arms out front and wide, then brought them back to his sides. If he could do this without touching anyone, he knew he had left enough room. Harrison practiced again and again, and soon his whole family practiced too. The next day, he used the space saver at school. Later, his dad explained that when a place was crowded, Harrison should simply put his arms down, be still, and stay in his own space. Harrison chose his own seat on the bus, kept space during baseball, and sat on his own mat at story time. He did not do it perfectly, but he got better most of the time.

Harrison P. Spider was a very loving spider who liked being close to people. Sometimes he got much too close. He sat near others, shook hands too strongly, and gave high-fives that were too hard. His family was used to lots of love, but teachers, coaches, and other parents began calling about Harrison's space. His dad explained that people need room around them. He showed Harrison a simple space saver: stretch the arms forward, stretch them wide, and bring them back down without touching anyone. Harrison practiced many times with his family. At school, he used the space saver whenever he could, even when he did not need it. Then his dad gave him another helpful reminder. In a crowded place, Harrison could keep his arms down, stay still, and remain in his own space. Harrison used this advice on the bus, at baseball, and during story time. He still made mistakes sometimes, but he learned to give people more room.

Harrison P. Spider had a big, joyful way of showing love. He wanted to be close to everyone, but his closeness caused trouble. People sometimes had to move away from him because he sat too close, shook hands too hard, or gave enormous high-fives. After hearing from teachers, coaches, and parents, Harrison's dad talked to him about personal space. He taught Harrison the space saver. Harrison held his arms out in front, opened them wide, and then placed them by his sides. This helped him see how much room he needed. Harrison practiced until he could use the space saver at school. His dad also told him that a crowded place needed a quieter plan: put his arms down, be still, and stay where he was. Harrison followed this plan on the bus instead of squeezing beside two friends. He kept space while playing baseball and sat on his own mat during story time. Harrison was not perfect, but he learned and usually gave others enough space.

video_title: 🐤 Ellie The Tiny Little Chick

summaries.summary: Ellie is a happy little chick who loves making friends, talking, and jumping from her bed, chair, and steps. She does not cry when she falls. But Ellie does not like going to bed because she thinks she cannot do anything while asleep. Her mother asks what she will do tomorrow, so Ellie turns on the light and tells her many plans. She wants to cook pasta, drive a race car, save the city, care for sick people, teach, play sports, sail for treasure, catch bad guys, and paint. Ellie gives each dream a special name, such as Chef Ellie and Artist Ellie. After naming all the things she wants to do, Ellie yawns and becomes very sleepy. Her mother tells her that she can be whoever she wants to be because she is precious. Ellie receives a good-night kiss and falls asleep, deciding that sleep is not so bad after all.

Ellie is a tiny chick who is always happy and enjoys talking and jumping. When bedtime comes, she says she is not sleepy. Ellie wants to stay awake and think about tomorrow because she has many things she wants to do. Her mother asks about her plans. Ellie jumps out of bed, turns on the light, and shares her big dreams. She wants to cook like her mother, race cars, be a superhero, help sick people, teach her friends, play baseball and hockey, sail across the sea, catch bad guys, and make art. Ellie imagines becoming many different kinds of people. Then she yawns and feels very sleepy. Her mother smiles and calls her sleepy Ellie. She says Ellie can be whoever she wants to be because she is her precious little chick. After another good-night kiss, Ellie says good night and drifts off to sleep.

Little Ellie does not want to sleep. She says she cannot do anything when she is asleep, and she wants to prepare for the next day. Her mother asks what Ellie would like to do. Ellie turns on the light and names one exciting dream after another. She wants to make yummy pasta, race a car, save the city from monsters, look after sick people, teach her friends, play baseball and hockey, sail to find treasure, catch bad guys, and draw and paint. Ellie gives herself names for these dreams, including Chef Ellie, Racer Ellie, Superhero Ellie, and Artist Ellie. While she is talking about all her plans, Ellie begins to yawn. Her mother tells her it is time for bed and says she can be whoever she wants to be. Ellie gets a kiss, says good night to Mommy, and falls asleep. Before drifting off, Ellie says that being sleepy is not bad after all.

video_title: Moana Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Moana loved the ocean when she was little. She listened to Grandma Tala tell how Maui took the heart of Te Fiti, making nature lose its balance. Moana’s father said the people must not sail past the reef, but the ocean chose Moana and gave her a special gift. When Moana grew older, Grandma Tala showed her old canoes and told her that their ancestors were wayfinders. Moana sailed across the ocean to find Maui and return Te Fiti’s heart. A storm carried her to an island, where Maui joined her. They escaped the Kakamora, visited the monster realm, and found Maui’s fishhook. Maui taught Moana to follow the sun, stars, moon, and currents. At Te Fiti, they met the lava monster Te Kā. Moana bravely gave Te Kā the heart. Te Kā remembered she was Te Fiti, and the world became balanced again. Moana returned home as a daughter, leader, and wayfinder.

A young girl named Moana felt close to the ocean. Her grandmother told her about Maui and the missing heart of Te Fiti. Moana’s father feared the sea, so no one was allowed to sail beyond the reef. Later, Grandma Tala led Moana to a secret place filled with canoes. Moana learned that her ancestors traveled across the ocean, and she set out to restore Te Fiti’s heart. A storm carried Moana to an island, where she met Maui. Maui wanted his magic fishhook, so the two traveled together. They passed the Kakamora and entered Lalotai, where Moana tricked Tamatoa and helped get the fishhook. Maui taught her how to find her way using the sky and sea. At the end of their journey, Te Fiti was missing, and Te Kā stood in her place. Moana gave Te Kā the heart. The lava monster became Te Fiti, the island bloomed, and Moana went home.

Moana loved the sea, but Chief Tui told everyone to stay near the island. Grandma Tala knew Moana had a special connection to the ocean. She also knew that Moana’s people had once been brave voyagers. When Moana was sixteen, Grandma Tala showed her the ancient canoes and asked her to find Maui and return Te Fiti’s heart. Moana sailed away with the heart in her necklace. She met Maui after a storm, and the ocean kept them together. They faced coconut bandits and a giant crab named Tamatoa. Moana helped Maui recover his magic fishhook, and Maui taught her to use the sun, stars, moon, and water to travel. Grandma Tala’s spirit reminded Moana who she was. At Te Fiti, a lava monster named Te Kā blocked the way. Moana gave Te Kā the heart, and the monster became Te Fiti. The island grew again, balance returned, and Moana came home a leader and wayfinder.

video_title: Daffy Duck in Duck Troop to the Rescue - Golden Story Book 'n' Tape (Audio Only)

summaries.summary: Daffy Duck and Bugs Bunny work at Camp Water Maroon. Daffy cares very much about winning, and his team, Duck Troop, is behind Bugs's Bunny Brigade. Daffy trains the little ducks hard for the camp Olympics. He wants a medal, so he plans to cheat. During the mountain hike, Daffy uses a shortcut, but it ends in a thorn bush. The little ducks rescue him and guide the team back to the trail. Duck Troop reaches the mountaintop first. Daffy tries to cheat in fishing and the sack race too, but the ducks win fishing and the bunnies win the sack race. In the swimming race, Duck Troop wins while Daffy runs from a giant frog. The team wins the Olympics because the little ducks work hard. Daffy gets no medal because he cheated, but he learns that he should play by the rules next year.

At summer camp, Daffy Duck wants Duck Troop to beat Bugs Bunny's team. He makes the little ducks practice knots, running, jumping jacks, and push-ups. Daffy says he loves training, but he really wants to go home and is planning to cheat. First, he leads the ducks along a secret shortcut during a mountain hike. The shortcut stops at a thorn bush, and Daffy gets trapped. The little ducks use their Trail Guide, free Daffy, and return to the real trail. Their hard work helps them reach the mountaintop first. Daffy hides a store-bought fish for the fishing contest, but it falls into the water, and Daffy gets caught instead. Duck Troop still wins. A spring sends Daffy into a tree during the sack race, and the bunnies win. Duck Troop wins the swimming race and the whole Olympics. Daffy feels proud of the ducks and ashamed of cheating.

Daffy Duck thinks winning is the only important thing at Camp Water Maroon. He is upset because the Bunny Brigade has won more games than Duck Troop. Before the camp Olympics, Daffy trains his little ducks and secretly prepares tricks for every event. His mountain shortcut fails, leaving him lost in a thorn bush. The ducks help him and use their Trail Guide to reach the mountaintop first. Daffy then tries to use a bought fish, but the fish slips away and he is pulled from the water. Elmer Fudd still declares Duck Troop the winner. In the sack race, Daffy's powerful spring shoots him into a tree, while the bunnies win. The ducks congratulate the bunnies. During the swimming race, Duck Troop wins, while Daffy escapes a giant frog. The team wins through hard work, and Daffy receives no medal because he cheated. He decides to follow the rules next year.

video_title: Nobody Likes a Goblin by Ben Hatke - Children's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Goblin lived in a dungeon with his best friend, Skeleton. They counted bats, played R the dice, and shared stories. One day, adventurers came into the dungeon and took the gold, maps, books, gems, Scrolls, and Skeleton. Goblin put on his crown and went to find his friend. A hill troll told Goblin that Skeleton had gone over the mountains with the adventurers. Goblin met a farmer, but the farmer called him filthy and chased him. Then elves and an inkeeper chased him too. At the Haunted swamp, Goblin found Skeleton and grabbed him. They hid in a cave because everyone was chasing them. Skeleton said he liked goblins. Then other goblins found them and called Goblin their Goblin King. Together, they chased away the farmer, inkeeper, elves, and adventurers. Goblin, Skeleton, and their new friends went home together.

In a deep dungeon, Goblin had a very best friend named Skeleton. Goblin cared for the dungeon, and he liked visiting Skeleton in the treasure room. They counted bats, played R the dice, and listened to stories about Skeleton being a mighty warrior. Then adventurers stormed the dungeon. They took all the treasures and carried Skeleton away. Goblin followed them into the wide world. A hill troll told him where Skeleton had gone, but warned that nobody liked a goblin. A farmer chased Goblin, and then an inkeeper and elves chased him to the Haunted swamp. Goblin saw Skeleton on a treasure cart and rescued him. The friends hid in a cave. Skeleton said he liked goblins. Many goblins appeared and asked if Goblin was their king. Goblin said yes. The goblins defended him, so the people ran away and the adventurers were never heard from again. Then everyone traveled home to the dungeon.

Goblin woke in his dungeon and wanted to visit Skeleton, his best friend. Skeleton lived in the treasure room and let Goblin wear an old crown. Goblin pretended to be the Goblin King. Soon, adventurers entered and took everything, including Skeleton. Goblin went outside to look for him. The hill troll said Skeleton had been taken over the mountains. Goblin promised to help. A farmer saw Goblin and chased him through an Inn. The inkeeper and elves joined the chase. At the Haunted swamp, Goblin saw Skeleton with the adventurers. He grabbed his friend, and they ran into a cave. Goblin worried that nobody liked him, but Skeleton said he liked goblins. Then many goblins came from the darkness. They had seen Goblin's crown and asked if he was the Goblin King. Goblin said yes. The goblins defended their king. The farmer, inkeeper, and elves ran away, and the adventurers disappeared. Goblin, Skeleton, and the goblins went back to the dungeon together.

video_title: The Bear Ate Your Sandwich

summaries.summary: A bear left his den on a warm, bright morning. He smelled ripe berries, ate a feast, and fell asleep in the sunshine. While he slept, a great rumbling carried him far away to a new forest. The new forest had trees to climb, bark to scratch, soft mud, and many smells. Then the bear found a beautiful sandwich lying all alone. He waited quietly and ate it. Just before he finished, he heard a strange sniffing, snuffling, slobbering, and snorting sound. Someone had seen him, so the surprised bear ran away through the park and down the street. He climbed a tall tree and saw his own forest. Waves carried him home, where he heard familiar birds and bugs. The bear made it home safely. Only a little lettuce was left because the bear dropped it while running away.

The story begins with a bear waking up and following the smell of berries. After eating, he rested in the sun and fell asleep. A loud rumbling then swept him away like a leaf and brought him to a forest he did not know. He enjoyed the trees, bark, mud, and interesting smells. Soon, leafy green smells guided him to a sandwich. The sandwich was beautiful and delicious, so the bear waited until he thought nobody was watching and ate it. Near the end of the meal, he heard someone making sniffing and snorting sounds behind him. The bear knew he had been seen and ran out of the park. He found a tall tree and looked from the top toward his forest. Then the waves rocked him until he slept, and familiar branches, birds, and bugs helped him know he was home. The sandwich was gone, except for a piece of lettuce.

On a sunny morning, a bear came out of his den and found ripe berries. After his berry feast, he fell asleep while bees buzzed nearby. A rumbling woke him, and he was carried to a different forest. There he found climbing places, scratchy trees, nice mud, and many smells. Green leafy smells led him to a sandwich that was waiting alone. The bear made sure nobody saw him, then he began to eat. When he was almost finished, a sound behind him said, “Sniff, snuffle, slobber, snort!” The bear had been discovered. He ran through the park and down the street until he reached a tall tree. From the top, he could see his forest, and he decided it was time to go home. The waves rocked him, and he returned to familiar branches and evening sounds. The bear ate the sandwich, leaving only a small piece of lettuce behind.

video_title: The Good Dinosaur Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Crash, Boom, Roar!

summaries.summary: Arlo hears many sounds. He hears Papa’s crash, boom, and roar. He hears cracks, the river, and a storm. Spot is there, and Arlo howls. Arlo and Spot play with animals. The animals make popping sounds. Then a T-rex roars, and Spot bites Arlo. Arlo yells, and he goes out. Arlo hears a fire crack and says, “Oh, snap!” At last, Arlo sees Mama. Arlo is with Mama, and Mama is home. The story ends with the sound of home being the best sound of all.

First, Arlo hears Papa make a loud crash, boom, and roar. A sound cracks, and Arlo is there. Arlo hears the river gurgle and hears a storm crash, boom, and bang. Spot is with Arlo, and Arlo howls. Arlo and Spot play while animals make popping sounds. Then a T-rex roars. Spot bites Arlo, and Arlo yells. Arlo goes out and hears a fire crack. He says, “Oh, snap!” Then Arlo finds Mama. Arlo is with Mama, and Mama says that the sound of home is the best sound of all. The story moves from loud sounds to Mama and home.

Arlo listens to sounds all around him. Papa makes a crash, boom, and roar. Arlo hears cracks, the river’s gurgle, and a storm’s crash, boom, and bang. Spot is there, and Arlo howls. Arlo and Spot play with animals that go pop, pop, pop, pop, pop. A T-rex roars, and Spot bites Arlo. Arlo yells, “Ah!” and goes out. He hears a fire crack and says, “Oh, snap!” Then Arlo hears Mama and sees her. Arlo and Mama are together. The last words say that the sound of home is the best sound of all.

video_title: 👻 The Little Ghost Who Was A Quilt

summaries.summary: A little ghost is made from a quilt, while his family and friends are light sheets. Because he has many fabric layers, he is heavy, slow, and unable to fly like the others. At the park, he hides from a family, but a boy drops ice cream on his face. Other ghosts laugh, and he feels embarrassed about being different. Halloween makes him happy, so he decides to be brave and join the fun. He hides on a porch, but a mother picks him up and wraps him around her cold little ballerina. They ride in a wagon to a house. Inside, the girl keeps him warm under her legs while she sorts candy. Her mother admires his colorful fabric and stitching. When the family goes upstairs, the little ghost flies away. His friends cheer, and he realizes that being a quilt helped him have this special adventure.

The little ghost who is a quilt does not understand why he is different. His parents and friends are sheets that fly quickly, but his quilt layers make him heavy and slow. He feels sad when other ghosts call him Scrappy, and he feels worse after a boy drops sticky ice cream on him at the park. On Halloween, the ghosts watch children from the trees. The little quilt ghost wants a better view, so he bravely hides on a porch. A mother mistakes him for something useful and wraps him around her cold daughter in a wagon. He worries because he cannot escape. At the house, the girl sits with him under her legs while she sorts her candy. Her mother smiles at his fabrics and stitches. Later, he flies out through the chimney. His friends celebrate, and he is happy because his quilt body made the adventure possible.

A quilt ghost feels unhappy because he cannot fly like the sheet ghosts. He is heavy, gets hot when he tries to go fast, and is laughed at after ice cream lands on his face. His mother tells him that other family members are different too, but he still wishes he were made from one fabric. Halloween gives him courage. He plans to hide on a porch and watch the celebration. When a mother and a ballerina girl arrive, the mother picks up the quilt ghost and wraps him around the girl to keep her warm. The ghost is frightened as they travel in a wagon, but he stays calm and tries to be brave. In the house, he sees decorations like the ghosts in the trees and feels cozy with the girl. After the mother admires his stitching, he escapes through the chimney. His friends cheer, and he learns that being different helped him.

video_title: Pick a Pumpkin (pumpkin-filled adventure/favorite holiday tradition) #toddlers #kindergarten #kids

summaries.summary: A child picks a pumpkin from a farm patch. The pumpkin may be tall, short, orange, white, or green. The child puts it in a wagon, enjoys spicy punch and toffee apples, and brings the pumpkin home. The pumpkin is cleaned and placed on papers so carving will not make a mess. A bowl, spoon, tracing tool, and plastic saws are gathered. Friends join the pumpkin-carving crew, while grown-ups cut the top.
