The seeds and sticky pieces are pulled out, and the inside is scraped clean. Together, the friends carve eyes, a nose, and a mouth. They decorate with cobwebs, ghosts, spiders, tombstones, bats, skeletons, and witches’ hats. Then they put on trick-or-treat clothes, carry the pumpkin outside, and light a candle. The pumpkin glows as a jack-o’-lantern and guards the house while everyone has fun on Halloween.

First, a pumpkin is chosen from the patch. It can be tall or short, fat or lean, and orange, white, or green. The pumpkin is carried home with treats from the farm. At home, it is wiped clean and placed in a carving space covered with papers. A bowl, spoon, face tool, and saws are ready. Friends come to help, but grown-ups cut the pumpkin top. The group reaches inside, pulls out seeds and lumpy strings, and scrapes the pumpkin empty. Then they make funny eyes, a nose, and a mouth. The face may have circles, a slit, one eye, a triangle nose, a smile, a frown, or pointy fangs. Decorations are added around the area. At last, the pumpkin is taken outside for trick-or-treating. A candle is lit, and the pumpkin shines with red-hot eyes and a fiery grin. It becomes a jack-o’-lantern for Halloween.

A pumpkin is picked at the farm and carried in a wagon. After enjoying spicy punch and sweet toffee apples, the pumpkin comes home. It is brushed clean and made smooth. Papers are placed under it, and tools are collected for carving. One or two friends join the crew. Grown-ups cut the top so hands can reach inside. The children pull out seeds, sticky strings, and other pieces, then scrape the sides until the inside is clean. Everyone helps carve a face. They choose surprising eyes, a nose with many shapes, and a mouth that may smile, frown, smirk, snarl, or show fangs. Before lighting it, they add cobwebs, ghosts, spiders, tombstones, bats, skeletons, and witches’ hats. They put on clothes for trick-or-treating and carry the pumpkin outside. A match lights the candle wick. The pumpkin glows by the door as a jack-o’-lantern while the family has Halloween fun.

video_title: All You Need for a Snowman (Encourages kids to see the magic in everyday activities)#readaloud #kids

summaries.summary: A small snowflake falls from the sky. The story says that more snowflakes are needed for a snowman, so many that they pile up in a mound. The snow is patted, packed, and rolled into one big, cold, well-rolled ball. A middle-sized ball and a small ball go on top. A short, flat hat or a tall hat goes on the snowman’s head. Two round bottle caps become the snowman’s eyes. A carrot can go in the empty space in the middle as the snowman’s nose. Walnut buttons, a belt, boots, a big wool scarf, a broom, mittens, ear muffs, a fanny pack, and something to read give the snowman clothes and things to hold. Then more snow fills the sky and piles up high. That is all needed for a snowman’s friend.

First, one snowflake flutters down, but a snowman needs many more. Snowflakes pile into a mound. They are patted, packed, and rolled into a large ball. The snowman also needs a middle-sized ball and a small ball on top. A hat is placed where the hat should go. Round bottle caps are put under the hat to make surprising eyes. There is an empty space in the middle of the face. A carrot can fill that space as the snowman’s nose. Then the snowman can have walnut buttons in a row, a belt, boots, a big wool scarf, and a broom. Mittens can keep his hands from getting cold. Ear muffs, a fanny pack, and something to read are also listed. At the end, snow falls everywhere and piles up high, making all that is needed for a snowman’s friend.

One little snowflake starts the story. Soon, three flakes, four, 5, 6, 7,000, 8 million more, and billions of snowflakes are piled in a mound. The snow is rolled into one big ball. Another middle-sized ball and a small ball are needed to make the snowman. A hat sits on top. Two round, flat bottle caps go under the hat as eyes. The snowman’s face has an empty place for a carrot nose. His clothes and things include five walnut buttons, a belt, boots, a big wool scarf, a broom, mittens, ear muffs, a fanny pack, and something to read. Then the sky is seen again. One small snowflake falls, followed by soft white snowflakes that float down everywhere and pile up high. The falling snow is all that is needed for a snowman’s friend.

video_title: THE GREAT PASTA ESCAPE read aloud – A Funny Children’s picture book read along | Kids Learn to Read

summaries.summary: At a pasta factory, the noodles followed strict rules. Macaroni, rotini, fettuccine, ramen, bow ties, and jumbo shells stayed with their own kinds, remained inside their packages, and never spoke to humans. Then they learned that people planned to get rid of them, so the pasta would eventually be eaten. Fettuccine became upset, Ramen became angry, and the other noodles began looking for a plan. Some wanted to protest quietly, while Ramen wanted to burst from the packages. The pasta argued, and chaos spread across the factory. Then Angel Hair said they should use their noodles together. The pasta worked as a team and made clever signs saying the factory was out of order and that the packages should be sent to a wonderful island. Their plan worked. Instead of being separated, the pasta escaped and lived together in a super place, with a sign saying, “Do not disturb. Geniuses at work.”

Earlier that morning, many kinds of pasta were packed at a factory. They stayed still and quiet because that was the rule. Macaroni, rotini, fettuccine, ramen, bow ties, and jumbo shells were placed in different packages. Soon, the noodles discovered that humans had made them to be eaten. Fettuccine was frightened, and Ramen was outraged. The pasta gathered to discuss what to do. Bow Tie suggested a quiet protest, but Ramen wanted everyone to break out and speak their minds. Other noodles offered ideas, and the disagreement became noisy. The ravioli were upset when a plan seemed to require sacrificing them. Just when the floor became chaotic, Angel Hair brought everyone together. She said they could succeed by using their noodles as one team. They made signs and labels that fooled the factory. The packages were sent to a super awesome island paradise. In the end, the pasta lived together there and placed a sign outside: “Do not disturb. Geniuses at work.”

The pasta at the factory had always obeyed. Each kind stayed in its own group, and every noodle stayed inside its package without speaking to people. Then the pasta learned that it would be taken to Average Joe's supermarket and eventually eaten. Fettuccine looked worried, while Ramen became furious. The noodles examined their packages and decided they needed a plan. Bow Tie wanted to sit quietly until the humans changed their minds. Ramen wanted to break free, and the pasta argued about different ideas. The ravioli became outraged when one plan might sacrifice them. Suddenly, Angel Hair spoke up. She told the noodles to work together. The pasta quickly created a clever escape plan using messages such as “Factory closed,” “Out of order,” and “Mail to super awesome Island Paradise.” The factory workers followed the messages, and the packages were sent away with care. At last, all the pasta lived together in a very super place, where their sign announced that geniuses were at work.

video_title: 🐱 Bad Kitty

summaries.summary: Kitty used to be good, but one day there was no regular food for her. The family offered her many vegetables, and Kitty was very unhappy. She decided to become a very bad kitty. She ate homework, bit Grandma, clawed curtains, damaged dishes, bothered the goldfish, flooded the bathroom, frightened guests, irritated the baby, knocked over a lamp, was mean to the family, and made trouble for the neighbors and vet. Then the family brought home many different foods from the grocery store. Kitty became very happy and decided to be good again. She apologized, bought toys, cleaned her cat box, helped with homework, hugged the little mouse, cared for the goldfish, mopped, helped the family, and lulled the baby to sleep. Everyone called her a very good kitty. To reward her, the family brought Kitty a new friend to play with and share food with.

At first, Kitty was a good kitty. Then the family ran out of food and gave her vegetables instead. Kitty did not like the food, so she chose to be a very bad kitty. She ate homework, bit Grandma, scratched the curtains, hurt the dishes, bothered the goldfish, flooded the bathroom, made trouble with guests, upset the baby, knocked down a lamp, and was unkind to the family. She also troubled the neighbors, the little mouse, and the vet. Later, the family returned from the grocery store with many unusual foods, including pizza, ravioli, sushi, lasagna, yogurt, and zebra ziti. Kitty was happy and chose to be a very good kitty. She apologized, cleaned, helped, studied, hugged the mouse, cared for the goldfish, treated the vet politely, fixed the curtains, tied shoes, vacuumed, washed a car, and helped the baby sleep. The family rewarded her with a new friend.

Kitty changed when she was given food she did not want. The family had only vegetables, and Kitty became unhappy. She decided to be bad and caused trouble in many places. She ate a homework paper, bit Grandma, clawed curtains, damaged dishes, endangered the goldfish, flooded the bathroom, bothered guests, made the baby upset, knocked over a lamp, and was mean to her family. She also quarreled with a neighbor, tormented a little mouse, acted violently with the vet, wrote on walls, and yelled all night. Then the family brought Kitty a large assortment of foods from the store. Kitty became very happy and decided to be good. She apologized to Grandma, cleaned her box, helped at home, finished homework, hugged the mouse, kissed the goldfish, mopped, helped the family, behaved politely, repaired curtains, vacuumed, washed a car, and lulled the baby to sleep. The family praised her and brought her a new friend.

video_title: My Magical Words | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids | Full Story

summaries.summary: The story says that words have power. Saying “I am” and something nice can bring sunshine to a day. A child can say, “I am special,” because every child is unique, from their hair and toes to the way they speak. The child can say, “I am giving,” and share with others without asking for something back. The child can also be peaceful by slowing down, closing their eyes, and breathing. Kind words, compliments, thanks, and please can lift people up. The story says the child is loved, smart, strong, healthy, thankful, and happy. The child learns, exercises, eats good food, drinks water, and remembers to say thank you. The child tries hard, learns new things, and feels proud. At the end, the story says beauty comes from inside and shines through a smile. The child can believe in good things and use magical words because the magic is in them.

A child learns that spoken words can bring sunshine or rain showers, so the child practices saying kind “I am” words. First, the child is special and unique. The child is also giving, sharing what is theirs and letting others have a turn. When the child needs quiet, the child can be peaceful by sitting down, closing their eyes, and breathing in and out. The child is kind when using nice words, compliments, thanks, and please. The child is loved because of who they are, and smart because they listen, learn, and can teach others. The child is strong by running, jumping, playing, and exercising. The child is healthy by eating fruits and vegetables, drinking water, and not eating too many sweet treats. The child is thankful and happy, and helps people who feel down. The child works hard, tries new things, and feels proud. Finally, the child is beautiful inside and outside, because love shines from the heart.

The magical words in the story help a child remember many wonderful things. The child can say, “I am special,” because differences make the child unique. The child can say, “I am giving,” and share so more people can play. The child can say, “I am peaceful,” and find quiet when it is time to rest. The child can say, “I am kind,” and use words that do not offend or tease. The child is loved and cared for, smart and ready to learn, and strong from moving and playing. The child is healthy by eating fruits and vegetables, drinking water, and being careful with sweet treats. The child is thankful for loved ones, places to stay, gifts, and fun. The child is happy when laughing and spreading joy. The child is proud when trying their best and learning every day. At the end, the child learns that true beauty comes from the heart. Saying “I am” helps the child believe in the magic inside.

video_title: 🐶READ ALOUD: BISCUIT'S EARTH DAY CELEBRATION by Alyssa Capucilli

summaries.summary: Biscuit wakes up on a beautiful spring Earth Day. The child tells Biscuit that they have learned about Earth Day at school and are going to a celebration. First, they practice saving water by turning off the water while brushing teeth. Then they help small creatures. Biscuit finds twigs that birds can use to build a nest, and they leave birdseed too. At the celebration, everyone plants a garden with flowers, vegetables, and trees. They give the seeds sunshine and water, and Biscuit finds a watering can and a wiggly worm. Next, they take a cleanup walk and pick up paper and litter. Biscuit shakes near the pond and helps keep it clean. The child also decorates a reusable grocery bag for Mom and Dad. They sing, share snacks, and learn to keep the planet safe. Biscuit and the child are good helpers on Earth Day and every day.

On Earth Day, Biscuit and a child get ready for a fun celebration. The child explains that Earth Day is a time to take care of the world. They begin by saving water. The child turns off the water while brushing teeth because every drop matters. They also help birds by leaving twigs for a nest and some birdseed. Soon, the celebration begins. Biscuit helps dig while everyone plants flowers, vegetables, and trees. With sunshine and water, the seeds can grow. Biscuit finds the watering can and a wiggly worm. After planting, they go on a cleanup walk. They pick up paper and litter so the woods stay clean. Biscuit’s big shake helps keep the pond clean too. The child has made a special bag for Mom and Dad to carry groceries again and again. They call this recycling. At the end, everyone sings, shares snacks, and remembers to help the planet every day.

Biscuit joins a child for an Earth Day celebration on a bright spring day. They learn that people can care for the Earth in many ways. The child saves water by turning it off while brushing teeth. Biscuit helps birds when the child finds twigs for a nest and leaves birdseed. Then they join a garden planting. They dig and plant flowers, vegetables, and trees. The child explains that sunshine and water will help the seeds grow. Biscuit finds both a watering can and a wiggly worm. During a cleanup walk, they collect paper and litter to make the woods nice and clean. Biscuit also shakes near the pond and helps clean it. The child shows a decorated grocery bag for Mom and Dad. They can use it again and again, which is called recycling. The celebration ends with songs and snacks. Biscuit and the child learn that they can be good helpers on Earth Day and every day.

video_title: Pig the Slob - Moving Picture Read Out Loud Story | Funny Children's Book | Pig the Pug

summaries.summary: Pig was a pug who spent nearly all his time lying on the couch. He ate candy, soda, mozzarella, nuggets, pie, and ice cream while watching TV and playing video games. His only exercise was swiping a screen or sometimes lifting a remote. Pig became so settled into the couch that he seemed like part of it. His friend Trevor worried because Pig's health was at risk. Trevor asked Pig to go jogging or take a brisk walk, but Pig said no and went back to his snacks and game. Then they heard the floorboards groan. Pig wondered if his tummy was making the noise, but the floorboards exploded. After that, Pig changed. He got off the couch, played outside, did cartwheels and squats, practiced yoga, and went jogging. Pig worked hard, although he liked resting when his workouts were finished.

Pig was a very lazy pug. He stayed flat on the sofa, eating candy, soda, mozzarella, nuggets, pie, and ice cream. He watched TV and played video games, and even lifting the remote made him tired. Pig was so still that he seemed stuck in the couch. Trevor was worried about him and said they should take a quick jog or a brisk walk. Pig refused and answered with a fart. Trevor tried again, saying they would have fun, but Pig ignored the idea and returned to his snacks and game. Then the floorboards began to groan. The first groan was quiet, but the next groan was loud. Pig thought the sound might be his tummy. Suddenly, the floorboards exploded. After this, Pig made an effort to come out and play. He did cartwheels, squats, yoga, and jogging. When he came home, he enjoyed having a nice rest.

At first, Pig the pug was a full-time sofa dweller. He lay on his back, watched TV, played games, and ate many snacks. Swiping a screen was his main exercise, and lifting a remote made him tired. Trevor saw that Pig's health was at risk, so he suggested a jog or a brisk walk. Pig said no, made a rude fart, and went back to his ice cream and video game. Then something unexpected happened. The floorboards started groaning. Pig asked what was going on and wondered if his tummy was making the noise. The groans grew louder, and the floorboards exploded. After that, Pig's days became different. He got up from the couch and came out to play. He did cartwheels and squats, practiced yoga, and went jogging lots. Pig's workouts were great. Even so, his favorite part was returning home after exercising and having a nice rest.

video_title: The Gift That I Can Give (core message of kindness) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks

summaries.summary: A child knows she is one of a kind and exactly the person God made her to be. She wonders what special gift she can give as she grows, loves, and learns how to live. She thinks her gift might be dancing or singing. It might be giving her all and helping her team by passing the ball. She also wonders if her gift could be caring for a stray animal, cheering for a friend in a race, helping a marching band, visiting a sick child, raising money so hungry children are fed, or giving her family a big squeeze. She asks if her gift could be all these things. God asks her to show others the gift she can give. He helps her find ways to give it away because he lives in her heart every day. His love is the gift she can give.

The story begins with a child saying that she is one of a kind and just the person God made her to be. She remembers that God placed something good deep in her heart when she was small. She asks God to show her the gift she can give while she grows, loves, and learns. At first, she thinks the gift might be a talent for dancing or singing. Maybe it is helping her team by passing the ball. Then she thinks about other ways to give: taking care of a stray animal, cheering for a friend, helping with a marching band, visiting a sick child, raising money for hungry children, or giving her family a big hug. She wonders whether all of these can be her gifts. God asks her to show others the gift she can give and helps her give it away. His love is that gift.

A child is trying to understand her gift. She knows she is special and that God made her exactly as she is. She believes God put something good in her heart from the very beginning, so she asks him to help her discover it. She considers talents such as dancing and singing, and she thinks about helping her team by passing a ball. Then she realizes a gift might also be an act of kindness. She could care for a stray animal, cheer for a friend who is racing, lend a hand with a marching band, visit a sick child, help raise money for hungry children, or give her family a very big squeeze. She asks if her gift might be all these things. The answer is to show others the gift she can give. God helps her find ways to give it away, and his love is the gift she can give.

video_title: 🐉 Kids Book Read Aloud: Pete the Cat : Pete The Brave by James Dean

summaries.summary: Sir Pete rides his horse and listens to Lady Callie play her harp. One night, a spell makes everyone fall asleep, and Lady Callie disappears. Sir Pete promises to find her. He follows a dragon’s footprints and sees a dragon carrying Lady Callie and her harp across a lake. Sir Pete rows to the dragon’s cave. It is dark, but he hears music and keeps looking. He finds a harp, then climbs a hill. The hill moves because it is the dragon’s back! Sir Pete slides down while the dragon roars. Sir Pete and Lady Callie argue about who should save whom. Then the dragon cries and says it only wanted to sing along and did not want to hurt anyone. Sir Pete asks the dragon for a ride home. The dragon takes them home, joins their song, and Sir Pete says that good friends can make music together.

Sir Pete is brave and enjoys Lady Callie’s harp music. During one beautiful song, a spell puts everyone to sleep. When Sir Pete wakes up, Lady Callie is gone. He follows big footprints and discovers that a dragon has taken Lady Callie and her harp across the lake. Sir Pete cannot fly, so he rows to a dark dragon cave. He hears music, but he finds only the harp. He keeps searching and climbs a high hill. Then the hill growls and moves because it is really the dragon’s back. Sir Pete slides down the dragon’s back. The dragon roars, and Sir Pete says he will save Lady Callie. Lady Callie says she came to save him too, and they begin to argue. The dragon starts crying. It explains that it only wanted to sing with them. Sir Pete asks for a lift, and the dragon brings them home. Then the dragon sings with everyone.

At dinner, Sir Pete cheers loudly whenever Lady Callie plays her harp. One night, a spell makes the whole group sleep, and Lady Callie vanishes. Sir Pete sets out to rescue her. He finds a dragon footprint, follows the trail, and sees the dragon flying over a lake with Lady Callie and her harp. Since Sir Pete cannot fly, he rows across the water and enters a very dark cave. Music leads him onward, but only the harp is there. Sir Pete does not give up. He climbs the highest hill and hears a growl. The hill begins moving, and Sir Pete discovers he is standing on the dragon. He slides down its back. When the dragon roars, Sir Pete and Lady Callie both say they will save each other, and they argue. The dragon cries because it wanted to sing along, not hurt anyone. Sir Pete asks for a ride home. The dragon carries them home and joins the song. Everyone is happy.

video_title: Peter’s Chair by Ezra Jack Keats

summaries.summary: Peter built a tall block building, but it crashed down. His mother asked him to play quietly because there was a new baby in the house. Peter looked at the baby's room and saw that the cradle, high chair, and crib were painted pink. Peter thought those things belonged to him, and he noticed that his old chair had not been painted. He carried the chair away and decided to run away with his dog Willie. Peter packed cookies, dog biscuits, toys, and a baby picture. Outside, he arranged everything and tried to sit in the chair, but he was too big. His mother called him home for a special lunch. Peter hid behind a curtain, then came out and sat in a grown-up chair. He asked his father to paint his little chair pink for Susie, and they did.

Peter was playing with blocks when his tall building fell down. His mother reminded him to be quieter because a new baby was in the house. Peter saw that his old cradle, high chair, and crib had been painted pink. He thought they were his things, but his old chair was still unpainted. Peter took the chair to his room and said he would run away with Willie. He packed cookies, dog biscuits, his blue chair, a toy crocodile, and a picture of himself as a baby. Outside, Peter tried to sit in the chair, but he was too big for it. His mother called him back for a special lunch. Peter hid, then shouted that he was there. He sat in a grown-up chair beside his father and asked to paint the little chair pink for Susie.

Peter reached up high while building a tower, but the tower crashed. His mother told him to play more quietly because the family had a new baby. Peter looked around and saw that the baby's cradle, high chair, and crib were pink. His own old chair was not painted, so Peter took it and planned to leave home with Willie. He packed food for himself and Willie, along with his blue chair, toy crocodile, and baby picture. Peter made a place outside and tried to sit down. The chair was too small because Peter had grown too big. His mother called from the window and invited him home for a special lunch. Peter hid behind the curtain, then came out and sat in a grown-up chair. He and his father decided to paint the little chair pink for Susie.

video_title: 📖 Ralph Tells a Story

summaries.summary: Ralph’s teacher says stories are everywhere, but Ralph cannot think of one to write. He looks for excuses to leave his desk and asks Daisy for help. Daisy shows him many stories she has written about things Ralph has done, but she tells him he must look around and find a story himself. Ralph searches the classroom and then remembers an inchworm he saw at the park. He tries to write about it but gets stuck. When the class shares stories, Ralph tells everyone about the inchworm. His classmates ask many questions, and Ralph realizes that something really did happen. He remembers naming the inchworm Nick, building him a house, and rescuing him from a baby’s diaper. Everyone cheers when Ralph finishes. Ralph is no longer embarrassed. After that, he writes stories all the time and keeps finding stories everywhere.

Ralph thinks nothing interesting ever happens to him, so he cannot write during writing time. He watches the ceiling, wanders around school, and tries to help the lunch ladies instead. Daisy says she has written lots of stories about Ralph and shows him her pages. She tells him to look around for his own story. Ralph looks in the classroom, under his desk, and outside the window. Then he remembers lying in the grass at the park and seeing an inchworm crawl on his knee. His teacher asks about his story, but Ralph gets stuck when he tries to write it down. At sharing time, he nervously tells the class about the inchworm. The children’s questions help him remember more. He names the inchworm Nick, follows him, and saves him from a baby. The class applauds, and Ralph learns that he can find stories in his own experiences.

Ralph wants to be a good writer like Daisy, but he believes he has no stories. Daisy reminds him that ordinary things he has done can become stories. Ralph finally finds an idea when he remembers an inchworm from the park. He saw it crawl on his knee, but writing about it feels difficult. When Ralph shares the small beginning with his class, everyone asks questions. Their questions help Ralph remember what happened next. He picked up the inchworm, named him Nick, and made him a house. Nick crawled away, so Ralph followed him. A baby grabbed Nick and put him in a diaper, but Nick escaped by crawling up the baby’s stomach. Ralph rescued him, and they spent the afternoon together. The children clap and cheer. Ralph feels proud instead of embarrassed. Later, he writes stories often because he keeps noticing stories everywhere.

video_title: What Mommies Do Best 💖 by Laura Numeroff 📖 Kids Book #Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Mommies do many kind things with you. They teach you to ride a bicycle, make a snowman, and bake a delicious birthday cake. They help a garden grow, give you a piggyback ride, and care for you when you are sick. Mommies watch the sunset with you, sew the loose button on your teddy bear, and hold you when you feel sad. They take you trick-or-treating, help you give the dog a bath, and play with you in the park. At bedtime, a mommy reads a story, tucks you in, and kisses you good night. Mommies can do many loving things, but best of all, mommies give you lots and lots of love.

A mommy can share many everyday moments with you. She can teach you how to ride a bicycle and make a snowman with you. She can bake a delicious cake for your birthday. She can help you make a garden grow, carry you with a piggyback ride, and take care of you when you are sick. Together, you can watch the sunset. She can sew the loose button on your teddy bear and hold you when you feel sad. She can take you trick-or-treating, help bathe the dog, and play in the park. When the day is over, she reads a bedtime story, tucks you in, and kisses you good night. Best of all, a mommy gives you lots and lots of love.

Mommies help, play, and care for you from morning until bedtime. They can teach bicycle riding, make a snowman, and bake a birthday cake. They can help your garden grow and give you a piggyback ride. When you are sick, they take care of you. When you watch the sunset, a mommy can be beside you. If the button on your teddy bear is loose, she can sew it. If you feel sad, she can hold you. Mommies can take you trick-or-treating, help you give the dog a bath, and play with you in the park. At night, they read a bedtime story, tuck you in, and kiss you good night. All these things show what mommies do best: give you lots and lots of love.

video_title: Moana Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Te Fiti is an island that once gave life to everything. Maui takes Te Fiti’s heart, but he loses it. Darkness spreads, and people stop sailing on the open ocean. Moana lives on an island and loves the ocean. The ocean gives her the shiny heart. Moana grows up and sees a cave filled with boats. Grandma Tala tells Moana to find Maui and return the heart. Moana agrees, even though she does not know how to sail. A storm makes her lost, but she finds Maui. Maui does not think she can learn the way. The ocean helps teach Moana. She learns about the sun, stars, and waves. A monster comes, and big waves rock the boat. Moana holds on and sails fast. She returns the heart. Darkness leaves, plants grow, and life comes back. Moana goes home and leads her people to new islands.

Long ago, Te Fiti gives life to the islands. Maui takes her heart and then loses it. After the heart is lost, darkness spreads, and people no longer sail across the open ocean. Moana lives near the ocean. She receives a shiny heart from it. When Moana grows up, she sees old boats in a cave and learns that people once loved to sail. Grandma Tala tells her to find Maui and bring back the heart. Moana goes on the ocean, but a storm leaves her lost. She meets Maui. At first, Maui does not think Moana can find the way, and he does not want to help. The ocean makes him teach her. Moana works hard. She learns to use the sun, watch the stars, and feel the waves. A strong monster and big waves challenge her. Moana stays strong and smart. She returns the heart, and the darkness goes away. Plants grow, the island blooms, and Moana returns home.

Moana’s journey begins when the heart of Te Fiti is lost. Maui took the heart, and darkness spread afterward. People stopped sailing on the open ocean. Moana loves the ocean, and it gives her a shiny heart. Grandma Tala shows Moana boats and tells her to find Maui. Moana promises to go and return the heart. She does not know how to sail, but she tries. A storm comes, and Moana becomes lost. She finds Maui, who does not believe she can learn to find the way. The ocean helps make Maui her teacher. Moana learns about the sun and feels the waves. She works hard and uses the stars. Then a monster comes, and big waves shake the boat. Moana sails quickly and holds on. She is smart and finds a way. She returns the heart. The darkness leaves, plants grow, and life returns. Moana goes home, where her family is happy. She leads her people to new islands.

video_title: You Be You | A story about finding yourself & being true to who you are

summaries.summary: A child visits a whispery house where Old Master Paint asks, “What’s your name?” The child is shy and cannot answer. The master gives the child a brush, a bucket, and a ladder, then leads the child to a huge white canvas. The child first makes a small stick figure, but then discovers that painting can be fun. The child splashes and splishes paint everywhere. The master dislikes the painting and makes it vanish. The child becomes very angry, tries to destroy the canvas, and tears a hole in it. Dark eyes, a troll, and wolves frighten the child. Then the child sees the brush and remembers that life is made from choices. The child paints bravely, sends the monsters away, and creates a beautiful painting. At last, the child can answer clearly: “You be you!”

Old Master Paint welcomes a child and repeatedly asks for the child’s name. The child’s tongue feels twisted, so no answer comes out. The master takes the child upstairs to a giant white canvas called the canvas of Life. He leaves a brush, a bucket, and a ladder, and the child must make choices. At first, the child paints only a little stick figure. Soon the child laughs and covers the canvas with colorful splashes. The master says the work is disappointing and makes it disappear. The child gets furious, blames the canvas, and tears a hole in it. The hole becomes dark and scary, and a troll and wolves appear. The child is frightened, but then notices the brush in hand. The child understands that the painting is like life and choices. With courage, the child paints, sends the monsters away, and steps into the light beside a beautiful painting.

A child arrives at a strange house at the edge of the wild. Old Master Paint wants to know the child’s name, but the child is too nervous to speak. A voice whispers that the child should shout the name to the sun. Upstairs, the master shows the child a very large, bright white canvas. The child may choose what to paint. The first picture is only a stick figure, but the child soon enjoys making splashes and covering the canvas with paint. The master does not like it and removes it. Angry and frustrated, the child attacks the canvas and makes a hole. The child tries to cover the hole, but sad eyes appear in the darkness. Then a troll and wolves come near. The child finds the brush and learns that the brush represents life and choices. The child paints boldly, sends the monsters away, and makes a beautiful picture. Finally, the child smiles and proudly says, “You be you.”

video_title: A BAD KITTY CHRISTMAS – A Funny Christmas Read Aloud Picture Book | Storytime

summaries.summary: Bad Kitty is surrounded by Christmas presents, but she wants even more gifts and special foods. She tears through the presents and makes a huge mess. Her family is upset, and Kitty runs away when they leave for the city. Puppy runs away too. In a dark alley, Kitty meets a kind lady. The lady dries Kitty, gives her food, and shows her a tree covered with family photographs. She explains that Christmas is about family and memories, not about having lots of things. Kitty is still homesick. When Puppy finds her, Kitty rushes away, but then she returns to the lady’s door. At home, everyone worries about Kitty and Puppy. Soon they come back with the kind lady. The family welcomes them all, and the lady moves in. Kitty is home, and the lady becomes part of the family.

On Christmas morning, Bad Kitty destroys the gifts and decorations because she wants more presents. Her family tells her that she is selfish and begins cleaning. Later, Kitty escapes through an open window, and Puppy follows her. Kitty wanders alone through the cold city until a friendly lady finds her. The lady takes Kitty upstairs, dries her wet fur, and shares her food. She shows Kitty a small Christmas tree decorated with black-and-white family pictures. The lady says that Christmas is not about presents, food, or spending lots of money. It is about family and the memories people share. Kitty misses her own home. When Puppy appears at the door, Kitty runs after him. The lady thinks Kitty has gone home and prepares to sleep alone. Then Kitty returns and says she wants to stay too. Later, Kitty and Puppy bring the lady home, and she joins the family.

Bad Kitty causes trouble on Christmas by ripping open presents and ruining the decorations. Even though many gifts are waiting for her, she wants more animals, food, and things. Her family is disappointed, so Kitty leaves. Puppy leaves as well. Kitty sits alone in a cold, scary alley and cries until a kind lady helps her. The lady does not have many decorations or possessions, but she has a tree filled with photographs of people she loves. She shares a snack and explains that Christmas is about family, just as other celebrations are about being together. Kitty listens, but she is still homesick. When Puppy comes to the door, Kitty runs out to follow him. The lady is lonely until Kitty returns. Soon Kitty, Puppy, and the lady arrive at the family home. Everyone is happy to see them. The lady stays for a Christmas snack and becomes family.

video_title: Chloe the Calm in The Bedtime Blues Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Miko is told that it is bedtime because she needs rest for her ballet recital tomorrow. Miko says she is not tired and does not want to go to bed. She feels very mad because she might miss fun, her friends stay up late, she has many things to do, and she is not sleepy. Then Chloe the Calm comes to help. Chloe takes a slow breath in and out and asks why Miko is mad. Chloe suggests that Miko imagine special places, sleep well, and enjoy the ballet recital tomorrow. She also reminds Miko that her friends need rest too. Miko thinks, “What if I am calm?” and immediately feels better. Chloe tells Miko that the power to be calm is inside her whenever she needs it. Miko says good night, and realizes that calmness may have always been there inside her.

At bedtime, Miko does not want to sleep. She says she is not tired and becomes very angry. Miko worries that she will miss all the fun, that her friends stay up late, and that there are still many things she wants to do. She also says she is not tired at all. Chloe the Calm appears and listens to Miko. Chloe tells her to breathe in and out, and Miko feels better after breathing. Chloe asks Miko to imagine being calm and dreaming about special places. She explains that a good night’s sleep can help Miko do her best at the ballet recital. Chloe also says that the real fun can be enjoying tomorrow without missing anything, because Miko’s friends need rest too. Miko decides to be calm and feels better right away. Chloe says Miko has the power to be calm inside whenever she needs it.

Miko is getting ready for bed before her ballet recital, but she strongly protests. She says she is not tired and does not want to stop playing or miss the fun. Miko is mad because her friends stay up late, she has many things she wants to do, and she does not feel sleepy. Chloe the Calm hears her and asks what is wrong. Before helping, Chloe pauses to breathe in and out, which makes her feel much better. Chloe then offers Miko several calm thoughts. Miko can dream about special places, sleep well, perform her best at the recital, and enjoy the next day without missing anything. Miko’s friends need rest too. Miko tries the idea of being calm and says she already feels better. Chloe explains that Miko now has the power to be calm inside whenever she needs it. After saying good night, Miko wonders if that calm power has always been inside her.

video_title: Bear Feels Sick 🐻🤒 by Jane Chapman 📖 Kids Book #Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Bear feels sick in his cave. His nose is stuffed, he cannot sleep, and he coughs and sneezes. His friends come to help him. They make a warm place, bring water, cook broth, use a cool cloth, and gather herbs for tea. Mouse tells Bear that his friends are there. Bear still feels sick for a while, so the friends stay close, whisper, walk softly, and sing lullabies. At last, Bear wakes up feeling good. He says he is better and thanks his friends. The friends go outside to play in the leaves, but Mouse and Hair begin to feel sick too. Bear takes care of them. He tucks them into bed, covers them up, kisses them, and says they will soon feel better. Bear cared for his friends, and then his friends cared for Bear.

On a windy autumn day, Bear stays alone in his cave because he feels sick. His nose is stuffed, he is tired, and he cannot sleep. Bear’s friends ask him to play, but Bear says he is too sick. Mouse, Hair, Badg, Gopher, Mole, Raven, Owl, and ren all help in different ways. They make a cozy spot, bring water, cook broth, place a cool cloth on Bear, and bring herbs for tea. The friends watch him carefully and sing quiet lullabies while he rests. After many hours, Bear wakes up and feels good again. He says he feels like new and thanks everyone. The friends celebrate by playing in the leaves. Soon Mouse and Hair feel sick, and the other friends do too. Bear tells them not to worry. He puts them to bed and cares for them just as they cared for him.

Bear is sick and cannot sleep in his cave. He tosses, sneezes, wheezes, coughs, and shivers. His friends come to his den and try to make him comfortable. Mouse hugs Bear and says everything will be fine. Badg brings water, Gopher makes broth, Mole uses a cool wet cloth, and some friends gather herbs for tea. The friends stay near Bear, speak in whispers, walk on tiptoe, and sing lullabies. Bear finally falls asleep. When he wakes, he feels better and says he is thankful for his friends. Everyone goes out to jump and play in the leaves. Then Mouse and Hair start to feel sick, and the friends become sick too. Bear comforts them and tucks each one into bed. He covers them, kisses them, and promises to care for them. The friends helped Bear, and Bear helps them in return.

video_title: X Men:  Night of the Sentinels - Book and Cassette

summaries.summary: Henry Peter Gyrich captured Jubilee because he thought she could lead him to the X-Men. At the X-Mansion, the team learned that Morph had died and Beast was in jail. Wolverine was very sad and angry, so he left to be alone. Cyclops found him and offered a plan to locate the Sentinels, the robot policemen that had attacked the mutant Control Agency. Cyclops went to Jubilee's father's house and made a Sentinel follow him. He blasted the robot, and Storm followed it in the Blackbird. The damaged Sentinel led them to its secret base. Jubilee escaped when her cuffs lost power, but more Sentinels surrounded her. The X-Men arrived to help. Cyclops blasted one, Gambit rescued Jubilee, Storm used lightning, Rogue smashed another robot, and Wolverine destroyed the last one with his claws. Gyrich fled. Jubilee then said goodbye to her foster parents and went to Professor Xavier's school to learn to use her powers with the X-Men.

The X-Men returned home with terrible news: Morph was dead, and Beast was waiting for trial in jail. Wolverine felt the loss deeply and promised to avenge his friends. Cyclops needed Wolverine's help, so he told him about the Sentinels and asked him to help find their home base. Meanwhile, the President ordered Gyrich to stop the mutant Registration Program because it might endanger mutants. Cyclops visited Jubilee's father, and Gyrich sent a giant Sentinel after him. Cyclops used his powerful eyes to damage the robot. Storm tracked it with the Blackbird, and the wounded machine crashed into the generator at the Sentinel base. Its crash turned off Jubilee's electromagnetic cuffs, allowing her to blast through a wall and escape. The Sentinels surrounded her, but Cyclops and the other X-Men came to rescue her. They defeated the robots together. Afterward, Jubilee chose to join Professor Xavier's school, where she could learn with the other young X-Men.

Jubilee was held by Gyrich at a secret base, while the X-Men were trying to protect mutants from the Sentinel robots. The team was also grieving because Morph had died and Beast had been arrested. Wolverine was hurt and angry, but Cyclops helped him make a plan. Cyclops let a Sentinel find him near Jubilee's father's house, then blasted the robot so it had to return for repairs. Storm watched the robot's path and guided the Blackbird after it. The damaged Sentinel crashed into the power generator at its base. When the power went out, Jubilee's cuffs opened. She used plasma from her hands to break through a wall, but Gyrich sent more robots to stop her. Cyclops told Jubilee to duck, and the X-Men attacked the Sentinels. Gambit swung to Jubilee, Storm struck with lightning, Rogue smashed a robot, and Wolverine used his adamantium claws to bring down the last one. Jubilee left her old life and went to Professor Xavier's school to become part of the X-Men.

video_title: Cars 📖 Read Along Storybook 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen and Mater like telling spooky stories, but their friends are scared. While Lightning and Mater drive home, they hear a strange sound. They decide to find out what is making it. Near Ramon's paint shop, they see a scary shape and wonder if it is a monster. Lightning looks inside and finds only paint cans. At Doc's shop, the sound gets louder, and sparks and flames make them wonder about a fire monster. Doc is fixing Sarge, so there is no fire monster. The sound follows them past tires and into the desert. Mater sees a light in the sky, but Lightning sees Aloft taking a night flight. Then the sound is right behind them. Lightning turns around slowly. It is Sheriff, driving in his sleep. They are not afraid—until they see two glowing eyes.

Lightning McQueen and Mater hear a spooky sound while driving home. They are curious and want to discover what it is. First, they pass Ramon's paint shop. A scary shape makes them ask whether a monster is inside, but Lightning finds paint cans and no monster. Next, they visit Doc's shop. Sparks and flames make the sound seem like a fire monster, but Doc is simply fixing Sarge. The sound comes closer near Casadelier. A creepy shape looks like a monster with two heads, but Lightning finds tall piles of tires while Luigi and Guido have a sale. In the desert, Mater sees a light in the sky. It is Aloft taking a night flight, not a glowing monster. The sound follows them. Lightning turns around and finds Sheriff driving in his sleep. Then two glowing eyes appear, and they do not want to find out what they are.

Lightning and Mater are not afraid of spooky stories, even though their friends are scared. On the way home, they hear a sound and search for its cause. They look near Ramon's paint shop, where a shape seems scary, but there are only paint cans. At Doc's shop, sparks and flames seem dangerous, yet Doc is fixing Sarge. Later, the sound is closer. A creepy shape seems to have two heads, but it is only a tall pile of tires while Luigi and Guido have a sale. In the desert, Mater sees a light, but Aloft is taking a night flight. The sound comes right behind them, and Mater becomes very scared. Lightning slowly turns around. The sound is Sheriff driving in his sleep, not a monster, a fire creature, a two-headed creature, or a glowing creature. Then they see two glowing eyes and stop looking.

video_title: Prince Cinders By Babette Cole

summaries.summary: Prince Cinders is a small, scruffy prince with three big, hairy brothers. His brothers tease him and leave him at home to clean while they go to the Palace disco. Prince Cinders wishes he could be big and hairy like them. One night, a fairy falls down the chimney and grants his wishes. An empty can becomes a car, his rags become a suit, and Prince Cinders becomes big and hairy. But the spell turns him into a big, hairy monkey. He goes to the disco, but the car is too small and he cannot fit through the door. At midnight, he changes back and loses his trousers while hurrying away. Princess Lovely Penny announces that she will marry whoever fits them. The trousers fit Prince Cinders, so they marry. The princess turns his mean brothers into house fairies who do palace housework forever.

Prince Cinders lives with three brothers who make fun of his small and skinny body. They go to the Palace disco with princess girlfriends, while he stays behind to clean. Prince Cinders wishes to be big and hairy. A dirty fairy arrives and uses magic to give him a car, a suit, and a big, hairy body. The magic goes wrong, and he becomes a big, hairy monkey without knowing it. He tries to attend the disco, but the car is too small, and he is too large to enter the building. He takes a bus home with a princess nearby. When midnight comes, he becomes himself again and drops his trousers as he runs away. Princess Lovely Penny searches for their owner and promises to marry the person who can wear them. The trousers fit Prince Cinders, not his brothers. He marries the princess, and she makes his brothers house fairies.

Prince Cinders wishes for a happier life because his three hairy brothers tease him and make him clean the house. A fairy comes down the chimney and tries to help. The fairy changes an empty can into a car, changes Prince Cinders's rags into a suit, and makes him big and hairy. However, the spell makes him a big, hairy monkey. Prince Cinders goes toward the disco, but the car is too small and the doorway is too narrow for him. He meets Princess Lovely Penny at the bus stop. At midnight, the magic ends, and he becomes himself again. The princess thinks he scared away the monkey, but he is too shy to wait and loses his trousers. She announces a marriage test using the trousers. Many princes and Prince Cinders's brothers cannot wear them, but they fit Cinders. He and Princess Lovely Penny marry, and she changes his brothers into palace house fairies.

video_title: Thanksgiving Stories ~ CLIFFORD'S THANKSGIVING VISIT Read Aloud ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books

summaries.summary: Last Thanksgiving, Clifford stayed home while his family visited Grandma. His kind neighbors took care of him, but Clifford thought about his family and especially his mom, who lived in the city. He decided to visit her for Thanksgiving. The trip became difficult. Cars bumped into him, and a drawbridge opened beneath him, making him wet and cold. Clifford went through a dark tunnel, where a train surprised him. He pushed the train back to the station and reached the street. In a strange neighborhood, he climbed a tall building and saw his old neighborhood and his mom’s house. A parade blocked the way, so he used the park as a shortcut. He accidentally joined a football game before finally finding his mom. She was happy, and they had a nice Thanksgiving dinner. Emily thought about Clifford at Grandma’s house. Clifford hurried home, and Emily did too. They were thankful for each other.

Clifford wanted to spend Thanksgiving with his mother because he missed his family while they were away visiting Grandma. Early in the morning, he traveled toward the city. At first the road was easy, but soon there were many cars. Drivers hurried, bumped Clifford, and honked. Then Clifford reached a bridge. The cars had stopped because the bridge was opening, and Clifford became wet and cold. He chose a dark, narrow tunnel instead. A train came toward him, but Clifford pushed it back to the station and climbed to the street. He did not know the neighborhood, so he climbed a tall building and looked for his mother’s house. A Thanksgiving parade blocked him, and he used the park. He accidentally joined children playing football. At last, Clifford found his mother, and they shared a Thanksgiving dinner. Emily missed Clifford too, so they both hurried home because they were thankful for one another.

Clifford’s family went to visit Grandma for Thanksgiving, so Clifford stayed with kind neighbors. Even though he was cared for, he thought about his father, sisters Bonnie and Claudia, brother Nero, and most of all his mother in the city. He set off to see her. The city trip had many surprises. Busy drivers bumped and honked at him. A drawbridge opened under him and left him wet and cold. A dark tunnel led him to a train, which he pushed back to the station. After reaching the street, Clifford climbed a tall building and spotted his old neighborhood and his mother’s house. A parade stopped him, so he crossed the park. He accidentally became part of a football game, then finally found his mother. She was glad to see him, and her owner served them Thanksgiving dinner. Emily was thinking about Clifford at Grandma’s house. Clifford and Emily both hurried home because they were thankful for each other.

video_title: We Are (Not) Friends! | Animated Read Aloud Kids Book | Vooks Narrated Storybooks

summaries.summary: The story begins when someone says, “We are not friends,” and another asks to play. They say yes and start making plans. They think about playing dinosaur hunters, but they also look for a friend who is not yet playing. When that friend comes back, everyone can play together. They decide to build a car, a Jeep. Then they notice that the Jeep is a two-seater, so one friend asks where to sit. The answer is that the friend can be the dinosaur. The dinosaur game begins with an attack, loud roars, and a sniff. After playing, they say they are not friends; they are best friends, and they have a new friend too. Then they ask about playing spies, and another friend asks, “Can I play too?”

At first, the children say they are not friends, but one child asks to join the play. Soon they agree to do a duet and think about playing dinosaur hunters. They wonder where their friend is and ask who the friend is. When the friend returns, all of them can play dinosaur hunters together. One child has an idea to build a car, which is also called a Jeep. They agree that their minds think alike. The Jeep is a two-seater, so one child asks where to sit. The others say that child can be the dinosaur instead. The game becomes an exciting T-Rex attack with roars, louder roars, and a sniff. Then they say they are best friends and welcome a new friend. Finally, they plan to play spies, and someone asks to play too.

The friends begin by saying they are not friends. A child asks to play, and the answer is yes. They talk about doing a duet, then decide to play dinosaur hunters because it is getting hot. They ask about a missing friend, and that friend soon says, “I’m back.” Now everyone can play together. They decide to build a car, a Jeep, and say, “Great minds think alike.” But the Jeep has only two seats. One child asks where to sit, and the answer is to be the dinosaur. The child becomes a T-Rex. The others say, “Attack!” and ask for a louder roar. After the dinosaur sniffs, they say they are not friends after all—they are best friends, and there is a new friend. Then they ask to play spies, and another child asks if they can play too.

video_title: Tacky the Penguin Read Aloud story by Helen Lester

summaries.summary: Tacky lived with five penguin companions in a cold, icy land. Goodly, Lovely, Angel, Neatly, and Perfect were quiet, polite, graceful, and liked neat marching and pretty songs. Tacky was different. He greeted them with a hearty slap, marched in a silly way, made splashy cannonballs, and sang a funny song about fish toes. One day, hunters came to catch the pretty penguins. The five companions hid behind a block of ice, but Tacky stood alone. The hunters asked for pretty penguins who marched neatly, dived gracefully, and sang sweet songs. Tacky showed them his funny march and a big cannonball. Then the other penguins sang Tacky’s silly song as loudly and badly as they could. The hunters covered their ears and ran away, leaving their things behind. The penguins hugged Tacky because his odd ways saved them all. Tacky was different, but he was very nice to have around.

In a nice, icy land, Tacky the penguin lived with Goodly, Lovely, Angel, Neatly, and Perfect. The five companions acted quietly and politely. They marched in order, dived gracefully, and sang pretty songs. Tacky did everything differently. He gave hearty slaps, marched with strange numbers, made splashy cannonballs, and sang, “How many toes does a fish have?” Then loud footsteps came closer. Hunters had arrived with maps, traps, rocks, and locks. They wanted to catch pretty penguins and sell them. The five polite penguins hid behind ice, while Tacky faced the hunters. He asked if they wanted penguins who marched neatly, dived gracefully, and sang pretty songs. Tacky did his silly march and a wet cannonball. Then all the penguins sang the funny fish-toes song terribly. The hunters could not bear the noise. They ran away with their ears covered. The penguins hugged Tacky, whose odd behavior had saved them.

Tacky was an unusual penguin who lived with Goodly, Lovely, Angel, Neatly, and Perfect. His companions greeted one another politely, marched in straight patterns, dived beautifully, and sang lovely songs. Tacky used a hearty slap to say hello, marched with mixed-up numbers, made big splashes, and sang a silly song. One day, the penguins heard hunters coming. The hunters planned to catch the pretty penguins, march them with a switch, and sell them. Goodly, Lovely, Angel, Neatly, and Perfect became frightened and hid behind ice. Tacky stayed outside. When the hunters came, he showed them his strange march. He showed them a splashy cannonball, which made the hunters wet. Then Tacky started singing. His companions joined him and sang the silly song loudly and dreadfully. The hunters thought this was not the land of pretty penguins. They covered their ears and ran away, leaving their maps, traps, rocks, and locks. The companions hugged Tacky because he had helped them.

video_title: Snow kids book read along

summaries.summary: Snow falls, and the children come outside to play. They like snow, even though they do not like snow in their faces. They dig it, throw it, slide on it, make tracks, and make snow angels. They climb a steep hill with their dog, then race down quickly. They make snowballs and build a snow house. Inside, they eat bread and meat, and leave some bread for the birds. Next, they roll a very big snowball and make a huge snowman named Ned. Ned has a head and a hat. Then the sun comes out. The warm sun makes Ned smaller and melts the snow. The children save some snow before it is gone. They put the snow away so they can play with it another day.

The children ask everyone to come out into the snow. They say snow is fun for people and horses. Snow lets them slide, ride with their dog, make tracks, and make snow angels. They climb a snowy hill and come down fast. Sometimes they use long feet and walk over the hills, and sometimes they ski downhill with their dog. Then they make many snowballs and build a snow house. They go inside to eat bread and meat, leaving bread for birds. After eating, they roll another snowball until it grows very big. They use it to make the biggest snowman they can. They name him Ned and give him a head and a hat. The sun appears and makes Ned very small. The children gather snow and keep it inside for another snowy day.

The snow is deep, but the children are happy to play. They dig and throw snow, slide on it, make pictures, and ride with their dog. They go up a steep hill and hurry back down. They make a wall from snowballs and finish a little snow house. They ask about bread and meat, then eat inside. Some bread stays outside for the birds. The children make one more snowball and push it until it grows and grows. They decide to make a man from snow. Their snowman, Ned, becomes very big and tall. They put a head and a hat on him. Soon, the sun comes out and shines on Ned. The snowman becomes very small, and the snow outside begins to disappear. The children run to save some snow. They put it away, so they can play with it on another day.

video_title: Antoinette

summaries.summary: Mrs. Bulldog had four puppies: Rocky, Ricky, Bruno, and Antoinette. Rocky was clever, Ricky was fast, and Bruno was strong. Antoinette had not yet found the special thing she could do, but her mother told her to keep her chin up. At the park, the puppies played with Fifi, Fufu, Ooh La La, and Gaston. Then Ooh La La disappeared. Rocky looked for paw prints, Ricky searched around the lake, and Bruno looked everywhere, but they could not find her. Antoinette felt a tug in her heart and a twitch in her nose. She followed smells past sidewalks, street vendors, signposts, buggies, bicycles, and broomsticks. Even a garbage truck did not stop her. At the city museum, she ran past the guard and found Ooh La La just in time to save her from a fall. Mrs. Bulldog was proud because Antoinette had been brave. Later, Antoinette became a famous police dog in Paris.

Antoinette lived with her mother, Mrs. Bulldog, and her brothers Rocky, Ricky, and Bruno. Each puppy was special. Rocky was clever, Ricky was fast, and Bruno was strong, but Antoinette was still wondering what she was good at. One day at the park, Ooh La La went missing. The dogs searched for her. Rocky followed paw prints in the mud. Ricky raced around the lake. Bruno left no stone unturned. Still, Ooh La La was nowhere to be found. Antoinette would not give up. Her nose led her through the city, past many busy things. She reached the museum with the other dogs. A guard pointed to a sign saying that dogs were not allowed, but Antoinette kept going. She ran around the guard, through the doors, and down a corridor. She found Ooh La La and saved her from a dangerous fall. Everyone praised Antoinette. Years later, she became a famous police dog in Paris.

The puppies loved going to the park. They chased biscuits, balls, and butterflies while playing with their doggy friends. Then Mrs. Poodle discovered that her puppy Ooh La La was missing. Rocky, Ricky, and Bruno each tried to help. Rocky used his cleverness to track paw prints. Ricky used his speed to search around the lake. Bruno used his strength to look everywhere. Their searching did not work. Antoinette felt that she had to keep looking, so she followed her heart and her nose. She sniffed through the streets and dodged buggies, bicycles, broomsticks, and a loud garbage truck. Her search led the dogs to the city's museum. A guard said no dogs were allowed, but Antoinette was unstoppable. She ran inside and raced through a long corridor. At the right moment, she saved Ooh La La from falling. Mrs. Poodle was happy, and Mrs. Bulldog was proud. Antoinette later became one of Paris's most famous police dogs.

video_title: 👻🎃 CLIFFORD'S HALLOWEEN | Read Aloud Book for Kids

summaries.summary: Emily Elizabeth loves holidays, and her big red dog, Clifford, loves them too. Clifford can be Santa at Christmas, blow a horn on New Year's Eve, be Emily's Valentine, and dress as an Easter Bunny. On April Fool's Day, Clifford does not trick anyone, and no one tricks him. On Thanksgiving, he gets a very big turkey. Emily says Halloween is the best holiday. Last year, she dressed as a pirate, while Clifford chose to be a ghost. At the party, the children could not guess who was inside the big ghost costume. Emily and Clifford bobbed for apples, and Clifford won an apple game. Mommy told a ghost story, but nobody was afraid because Clifford was there. Afterward, they went trick-or-treating, had little luck, and went to bed. Now Halloween is here again, and Emily will be a fairy princess. She wonders whether Clifford should be an Indian or a knight.

Emily Elizabeth introduces Clifford and tells how much they enjoy holidays together. At Christmas, Clifford looks like Santa because he already has a red coat. On New Year's Eve, they stay awake so he can blow his horn. Clifford is also a Valentine, an Easter Bunny, and a gentle dog who plays no April Fool's tricks. He receives a great big turkey on Thanksgiving. Halloween is their favorite holiday. At last year's party, Emily wore a pirate costume. Her daddy suggested that Clifford be a devil, and Emily thought he could be a clown or a witch. Clifford wanted to be a ghost. The children could not tell who the large ghost was. Emily and Clifford played apple games, and Clifford won one. Mommy told a ghost story, but the children were not scared because Clifford took care of them. Later, Emily and Clifford went trick-or-treating. They found little luck, but it was bedtime. This year, Emily will be a fairy princess and needs help choosing Clifford's costume.

Holidays are fun for Emily Elizabeth and Clifford, her big red dog. Clifford can take part in many celebrations. He is Santa at Christmas, blows his New Year's horn, becomes Emily's Valentine, and makes a wonderful Easter Bunny. On April Fool's Day, he and everyone else leave one another alone. On Thanksgiving, Clifford gets a great big turkey. Halloween is the most exciting holiday. During last year's party, Emily dressed as a pirate. Daddy suggested a devil costume for Clifford, and Emily suggested a clown or witch, but Clifford chose a ghost. When the children arrived, they could not discover the ghost's identity. They played bobbing for apples and another apple game, which Clifford won. Mommy told a ghost story, but the children felt safe because their giant ghost was taking care of them. After the party, Emily and Clifford went trick-or-treating. They did not have much luck, and they went to bed. Halloween has returned. Emily plans to be a fairy princess, and she asks whether Clifford should be an Indian or a knight.

video_title: The Gruffalo's Child Read Aloud | Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: The Gruffalo tells his child not to go into the deep, dark wood because the Big Bad Mouse may be there. He remembers that the mouse is very strong, with a long tail, fiery eyes, and tough whiskers. One snowy night, the Gruffalo's child feels bored and brave, so she goes into the wood. She follows a trail, claw marks, and a track. A snake, a bird, and another creature each pretend that the Big Bad Mouse is nearby. The Gruffalo's child says she is not scared. Then she sees a little mouse and plans to eat him. The mouse asks her to wait and shows her a huge shadow in the moonlight. The child thinks the Big Bad Mouse is real and runs back to the cave. She is less brave and less bored, while the Gruffalo sleeps and snores.

The Gruffalo warns his child about the Big Bad Mouse. He says the mouse is terribly strong and has a long tail, fiery eyes, and whiskers tougher than wire. The child goes into the snowy wood because she is bored and brave. She sees signs in the snow and meets creatures in a log pile house, a treetop house, and an underground house. Each creature says the Big Bad Mouse is somewhere else. The child keeps saying she is not scared. At last, she finds a small mouse. She wants to make him a midnight feast, but the mouse says he has a friend to show her. He climbs a hazel tree. The moon makes his shadow look huge, with long whiskers and a big nut. The child believes the Big Bad Mouse is there and returns to the Gruffalo cave. She is not so brave anymore, but she is no longer bored.

The Gruffalo's child hears about a frightening Big Bad Mouse and decides to search for him in the deep, dark wood. Snow falls and the wind blows as she follows different marks. A snake, a creature with short tail, and another creature with whiskers all tell her that the mouse is nearby. She does not believe them and says she is not scared. Then a little mouse comes out of his house. The child thinks he will be a good midnight feast. The mouse climbs a hazel twig and tells her to wait. The bright moon makes a terrible, enormous shadow on the ground. The child sees the shadow and thinks the Big Bad Mouse is big, bad, and strong. She runs back to the Gruffalo cave. Her adventure makes her less bored and less brave, while the Gruffalo continues to snore.

video_title: I am Ruby Bridges

summaries.summary: Ruby Bridges is almost six years old in 1960. She does not like her old-fashioned name, but she loves her grandmother, who chose it, so she decides to live with it. Ruby enjoys her first school, where she makes friends, likes her teacher, and earns many gold stars. Then her parents tell her she must change schools. She takes a test and passes. The next morning, four white federal marshals take her to William France Elementary School. Outside, angry white people scream, and Ruby does not understand why. Inside, she meets a white principal and, the next day, Mrs. Henry, her white teacher. Ruby discovers she is the only child and the only Black person in the school. Her mother explains that a court case changed the laws so Black children could attend white schools. Ruby learns that being first helps make school fairer for all children.

Ruby Bridges begins school happily. She plays with many children, makes best friends, enjoys her kind teacher, and receives gold stars. Soon, her parents say she will attend a better school if she passes a test. Ruby passes, and her mother tells her to behave at the new school. On her first day, four tall white federal marshals drive Ruby there because the president sent them. White people are shouting outside, but Ruby does not yet know why. The next day, she meets Mrs. Henry, her new white teacher. Ruby is surprised to find that she is the only student in the classroom and the only person in the whole school who looks like her. Her mother explains that the Supreme Court changed the rules after Brown versus Board of Education. Ruby is the first Black child at the school. She hopes other children will come soon because school should be for everyone.

When Ruby Bridges is nearly six, she thinks mostly about her name and starting school, not about history. Her first school is friendly, and she loves earning gold stars. Then she passes a test and must move to William France Elementary, a white school. Four federal marshals escort her because many white people are angry outside. Ruby first thinks the crowd looks like a celebration, but there are no beads. At school, the principal and teacher are white, and Ruby discovers that she is the only child there. She also realizes she is the first Black student in the school. Ruby’s mother tells her that Brown versus Board of Education ended school segregation and allowed Black children to attend schools with white children. Ruby understands that her presence helps make this possible. She believes children are alike no matter their skin color and waits for other children to join her.

video_title: Cloudette kids book read along

summaries.summary: Claudette is a very small cloud, but she likes being small. She can fit into tiny spaces, hide, watch fireworks, and sleep in her cozy little place. Sometimes the bigger clouds go away to make storms and rivers. Claudette wants to do something important too. She dreams of growing gardens, making brooks babble, making waterfalls, and giving children a day off from school. She asks the fire department and a garden center for work, but they do not need her. Then a big storm blows her far away. In her new neighborhood, Claudette meets a frog whose pond has dried into a muddy puddle. Claudette puffs up, becomes blue-gray, and makes rain. The puddle becomes a pond, and many frogs jump in happily. The higher-ups praise her rain. Claudette feels tired but happy, and she goes off to find more important things to do.

Small Cloudette has many advantages. She can squeeze through tight places, find a good view at crowded fireworks, and hide in little spaces. Still, she feels left out when larger clouds make huge storms and help crops and rivers. Cloudette wishes she could do something big. She imagines helping firefighters and gardeners, but the fire department has a new truck, the plants are watered by machines, and nobody needs her. Soon, a strong storm carries her away. Cloudette meets new clouds and hears a frog. The frog shows her a pond that has dried up into a muddy puddle. Cloudette gets an idea. She puffs up, turns blue-gray, rumbles softly, and pours rain onto the puddle. The water grows into a large, perfect pond. Frogs of many kinds come jumping in and thank her. The higher-ups say her rain was wonderful and tell her that a little cloud can do big things.

Claudette is often called Pip-Squeak, Small Fry, and Shortcake because she is smaller than other clouds. She does not always mind, because her small size helps her find friends and cozy places. But she wants to help with important cloud work. She watches other clouds make storms, water crops, and move rivers. Claudette tries to find a job, yet the fire department and garden center already have what they need. Afterward, a powerful storm blows her away from home. In a strange place, she meets a frog with no real pond. Its pond dried up and became a muddy puddle. Claudette decides to help. She grows big, turns blue-gray, makes a rumbling sound, and rains for a long time. Her rain fills the puddle until it becomes a pond. Frogs of every stripe and spot arrive and cheer. Claudette is exhausted and happy. The higher-ups admire her and say she can do other important things.

video_title: Nugget & Fang: Friends Forever or Snack Time? (undersea story of friendship) #kids #story #books

summaries.summary: Nugget and Fang were best friends in the deep ocean. They swam together everywhere. Then Nugget went to school and learned that sharks have sharp teeth and eat minnows. Nugget worried because Fang was a shark. He told Fang that sharks and minnows could not be friends, then swam away. Fang wanted his best buddy back, so he tried to show that he was not scary. He visited the minnows, wrote Nugget an invitation to dinner, and tried a tattoo, a special delivery, and a song and dance. Nothing worked. One day, a net fell on the minnows. Fang used his big sharp teeth to chomp and chew the net and save them. Nugget saw that Fang was a very special shark. He counted 10 minnows and Fang, making 11 friends. Then they swam together again, and everyone smiled.

In the deep, deep ocean, Nugget and Fang did everything together. Nugget loved his friend, but school made him worried. In reading, math, and science, Nugget heard that a big bad shark could eat minnows. He learned that sharks were scary and that sharks and minnows could not be friends. Nugget told Fang this and swam far away. Fang felt sad because he could not stop being toothy, but he wanted his friend back. He tried many ways to look friendly. He smiled at the minnows, invited Nugget to dinner, and tried a tattoo, a special delivery, and a song and dance. On Friday, a net caught the minnows. Fang made a plan. He used his sharp teeth to chomp and chew the net until the minnows were safe. Nugget understood that Fang was special. Ten minnows and Fang were 11 friends, and they swam happily together.

Nugget and Fang were two friends who swam over, under, and around glug. Their happy life changed when Nugget went to school. His lessons said sharks had sharp teeth, ate minnows, and were scary. Nugget believed the lessons and said that sharks and minnows could not be friends, even though Fang was his best friend. Fang tried to prove he was friendly. He visited the minnows with a smile, sent Nugget a dinner invitation, and tried several other ideas. Nugget still did not come back. Then a net dropped onto the little minnows and pulled them upward. Fang was alone, but he made a plan. His big sharp teeth chomped and chewed the net, and he saved the minnows. Nugget swam to Fang and counted the friends: 10 minnows and one special shark. There were 11 friends altogether. They swam together again, and everyone was all smiles.

video_title: Virtual Storytime with Miss Andrea: "Bringing in the New Year" by Grace Lin

summaries.summary: A family is getting ready for the New Year. Gigi sweeps the old year out of the house. Baba hangs spring happiness poems. Mama makes get-rich dumplings. Maymay gets a fresh haircut, and the child puts on a new dress for the New Year feast. Then fireworks appear, but the New Year has not come yet. Lions arrive to scare away last year’s bad luck. The family carries lanterns to light the way. Soon they see a dragon. Auntie wakes the dragon by opening its eyes. The dragon wakes up, and everyone knows the New Year must be coming. At last, the New Year arrives. Everyone cheers and says, “Happy New Year!”

The family hopes the New Year will come, so everyone helps welcome it. Gigi sweeps the old year from the house. Baba hangs spring happiness poems, and Mama cooks special get-rich dumplings. Maymay has a fresh haircut, while the child wears a new dress for the feast. Fireworks fill the sky, but they do not bring the New Year yet. Next, lions come to scare away the bad luck from last year. The family carries lanterns to light the New Year’s way. Then they find a dragon. Auntie opens the dragon’s eyes, and the dragon wakes up. The family watches and waits. At last, the New Year comes. The family is happy and cheers, “Hooray!” They celebrate together and say, “Happy New Year, everyone!”

The New Year is coming, and a family prepares for it. They clean away the old year, hang happiness poems, make dumplings, get a haircut, and put on a new dress for a feast. Then the family sees fireworks and wonders if the New Year has arrived. It has not arrived yet. Lions come to scare away last year’s bad luck. After that, the family carries lanterns to light the way. They see a dragon, and Auntie opens its eyes. The dragon wakes up. This makes the family think the New Year is near. They look and wait. Then the New Year finally arrives. Everyone celebrates with happy cheers. The family says, “Hooray!” and wishes everyone a happy New Year.

video_title: Somebody Loves💕You, Mr. Hatch #reading #kids #valentinesday #story #books #bedtimestories #learning

summaries.summary: Mr. Hatch lived alone and followed the same quiet routine every day. He worked at the Shoelace Factory, ate lunch by himself, and went to bed early. On Valentine’s Day, the postman brought him a heart-shaped box of candy with a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch became happy and began smiling, talking, helping people, and sharing candy. He watched Mr. Smith’s news stand while Mr. Smith visited the doctor, found Mr. Todd’s missing little girl, and baked brownies and lemonade for the neighborhood. Then the postman discovered that the valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch became lonely again and stopped helping and laughing. His neighbors remembered his kindness and planned a surprise. They decorated his porch, gave him candy and a harmonica, and held up a sign saying, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.” Mr. Hatch realized that people truly loved him, and he smiled and laughed with his friends.

Mr. Hatch was a tall, thin man who kept to himself. He did not smile or speak much, and everyone thought he had no friends. One Saturday, he received a Valentine’s Day package. Inside was candy and a card saying, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch thought he had a secret admirer, so he laughed, wore a bright tie, and greeted people on his walk. At work, he shared chocolates.
