He also helped Mr. Smith by watching the news stand, helped Mr. Todd by finding Melanie at school, and made brownies and lemonade for neighborhood children and parents. Mr. Hatch’s days became full of laughter and parties. Later, Mr. Goober said the valentine had gone to the wrong address. Mr. Hatch felt unloved and returned to his lonely routine. His neighbors then explained how he had helped them and decided to show their love. They decorated his home and made a sign. Mr. Hatch smiled and hurried to join them.

At first, Mr. Hatch lived a very quiet life. He walked to work, ate lunch alone, bought a newspaper and a turkey wing, and went to bed early. A heart-shaped box of candy arrived with a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” The message made Mr. Hatch cheerful. He wore a yellow tie, smiled at neighbors, talked with people, and shared his candy. He helped Mr. Smith go to the doctor by watching the news stand. He helped Mr. Todd by bringing Melanie home from school. He baked brownies and lemonade, and the neighborhood enjoyed a picnic with music and dancing. Then Mr. Goober returned the valentine because he had delivered it to the wrong address. Mr. Hatch thought nobody loved him, so he stopped smiling, helping, baking, and playing music. His friends told one another about his kindness. They decorated his porch and gathered in his yard with candy, a harmonica, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.” He understood that he was loved after all.

video_title: The Grumpy Reindeer: A Winter Story About Friendship and Kindness. Read Aloud Kids Books

summaries.summary: It was Christmas Eve at Santa’s workshop. All the reindeer were excited, but Ronnie was grumpy. He did not like the noisy carols or bright lights. He stayed alone in his warm stable and would not play or share carrots with the other reindeer. Then Santa came to Ronnie’s door. One sleigh of presents still needed to be delivered, and Santa needed help. Ronnie wanted the children to have their presents, so he tried his best. But the big sleigh needed more than one reindeer. Santa told Ronnie that kind and cheerful reindeer are treated kindly too. Ronnie thanked the other reindeer, said he was sorry for being grumpy, and asked them to help. They agreed because everyone needs help sometimes and teams can work together. With a little magic, they delivered presents around the world. Ronnie liked helping and being with his friends. His frown turned into a smile, and he became the happiest reindeer of all.

Ronnie was a grumpy reindeer at Santa’s workshop. While the other reindeer prepared a Christmas party, Ronnie stayed in his stable. He did not like Christmas songs or bright lights, and he did not play with the others or share their carrots. On Christmas Eve, Santa knocked on his door. A sleigh full of presents still needed to go to children, and Santa asked Ronnie to help. Ronnie said yes, but the sleigh was too big for him to pull alone. The other reindeer might not help because Ronnie had been unkind and grumpy. Santa gave him an idea: be kind and cheerful, and others may be kind too. Ronnie thanked the reindeer, praised them, and said he was sorry. He asked them to work with him. The reindeer agreed. Together, they flew around the world and delivered presents. Ronnie discovered that helping and being with friends made him happy.

On the night before Christmas, Ronnie was the only grumpy reindeer in Santa’s workshop. He wanted to be alone in his warm stable. He thought the carols were too noisy and the lights were too bright. The other reindeer invited him to play and offered to share carrots, but Ronnie would not join them. Then Santa arrived and asked Ronnie to deliver one last sleigh of presents. Ronnie wanted to help the children, but he could not pull the enormous sleigh by himself. Santa said that kindness and cheerfulness can bring kindness back. Ronnie thanked his friends for sharing and playing with him. He admired their snow deer and antlers, then said he was sorry for being grumpy. He asked them to help deliver the presents. The reindeer said yes. They worked as a team and flew around the world. Ronnie liked helping, liked his friends, and became the happiest reindeer.

video_title: How Much Is A Million? Read Aloud

summaries.summary: The story shows how enormous large numbers can be. With one million kids standing on one another’s shoulders, the tower would rise higher than buildings and mountains and farther than airplanes fly. Counting from 1 to 1 million would take about 23 days. A million goldfish would need a bowl big enough to hold a whale. A million tiny stars would fill 70 pages, and taking the seven-page journey ten times would pass a million stars. Then the story asks about a billion. A billion-kid tower would reach past the moon, counting would take 95 years, a billion goldfish would need a stadium-sized bowl, and a billion stars would stretch almost 10 miles across pages. Finally, a trillion kids would reach beyond the moon, Mars, and Jupiter, almost to Saturn’s rings. Counting would take nearly 200,000 years, and a trillion goldfish or stars would need city-harbor or world-spanning space.

First, the story explores one million. If one million children climbed onto each other’s shoulders, they would rise above the tallest buildings and highest mountains. Counting to one million would take about 23 days. A bowl holding one million goldfish would be large enough for a whale. The book then shows stars: 100 stars are shown, and a million tiny stars would fill 70 pages. Repeating the seven-page journey ten times would pass one million stars. Next comes one billion. A billion children in a human tower would stand past the moon. Counting to one billion would take 95 years. A billion goldfish would fill a bowl as large as a stadium, while a billion stars would stretch almost 10 miles. Last is one trillion. A trillion-child tower would go beyond the moon, Mars, and Jupiter, almost to Saturn’s rings. A trillion would need a city harbor for fish and a roll from New York to New Zealand for stars.

The story compares a million, a billion, and a trillion using children, counting, goldfish, and stars. One million children would make a tower taller than buildings and mountains, and counting to that number would take about 23 days. One million goldfish would need a bowl large enough for a whale. The book’s tiny stars would fill 70 pages if there were a million of them. Ten seven-page journeys would pass a million stars. For one billion, the children would make a tower reaching past the moon. Counting would take 95 years, a goldfish bowl would be as big as a stadium, and the stars would stretch almost 10 miles across pages. One trillion is even greater. Children would reach beyond the moon, Mars, and Jupiter, nearly to Saturn’s rings. Counting would take almost 200,000 years. A trillion goldfish would need a city harbor, and a trillion stars would stretch from New York to New Zealand.

video_title: The Detective Dog by Julia Donaldson. Children's story audiobook, kids read-aloud.

summaries.summary: Nell is a clever dog who can smell things. She helps Peter find lost clothes and toys, such as a sock in the sofa and a shoe in the shed. Every Monday, Nell goes with Peter to school and listens to children read books. One Monday, the books are gone. Nell finds a cap and follows the thief’s smell past farms, a zoo, and a field. She finds a man named Ted sitting with the books in a sack. Ted says he is sorry and only meant to borrow them. Nell has an idea. She leads everyone to a library filled with books. Peter tells Ted he can join the library and borrow books for free. Ted gets a library card and reads in his backyard. Nell returns to school and listens to more books.

Detective Dog Nell lives with Peter, a six-year-old boy who often loses his things. Nell uses her keen nose to find Peter’s bus, book, sock, shoe, teddy, and ball. On Mondays, she goes to Peter’s school, where children read stories to her. Nell loves the smell of books about dinosaurs, knights, planets, frogs, dragons, and dogs. Then one Monday, Mr. Jones says all the school books have disappeared. Nell finds a cap on the bookshelf and follows the thief’s smell. She runs with Peter and the children through many places until they find a man named Ted with the books. Ted says stealing is wrong and that he wanted to return them. Nell leads them to a library. Peter explains that Ted may borrow books there for free. Ted gets a library card and begins reading happily.

Nell is a detective dog with a very good nose. She solves little mysteries and helps Peter find his missing clothes and toys. At school, Nell listens while children read, and she enjoys smelling the books. One Monday, Peter cries because every book has vanished from the classroom. Nell searches for a clue and finds a cap. She follows the smell from the cap, past a farm, a zoo, a shop, a field, and a wood. Behind a gate, she finds Ted with the missing books. Ted feels sad and says he is sorry. He knows stealing is wrong, but he wanted to borrow the books. Nell leads Ted and the children to a library full of books. Peter says Ted can join and borrow books for free. Ted receives a library card and reads at home. Nell keeps visiting school to hear stories.

video_title: Princess Hair by Sharee Mille | Kids & Family Picture Story Book Time | Read Aloud

summaries.summary: All princesses wear crowns, but their hair can be different. Some princesses have Puffs and play pretend. Some have twist outs and twirl around. Princesses with dreadlocks draw many pictures, while princesses with Kinks think. Princesses with frohawks rock, and princesses with head wraps take long naps. Princesses with curls wear pearls. Princesses with a teeny weeny afro wear teeny weeny bows. Princesses with banto knots bake a lot. Princesses with braids throw parades, and princesses with buns love to run. Princesses with blowouts bounce again and again. Princesses with twists wrap gifts, and Nappy princesses are happy. A glowing candle created the Encanto, where the Madrigal family lived in their magical house, Casita. The family had many gifts, but Mirabelle had none. She felt different until Casita started cracking. Wanting to save her home, Mirabelle searched for Bruno’s vision. Bruno helped her see that Casita and the family were in danger. Mirabelle discovered that Isabella was not truly happy being perfect, and Abuela had become frightened that the family might lose its protection. The candle melted, everyone’s powers faded, and Casita crumbled. Mirabelle ran to the river, where Abuela told her about Abuelo Pedro’s loss and the miracle that had protected Abuela and her triplets. Abuela realized that her sadness had made her live in fear. Mirabelle reminded her that the family itself was the miracle. Abuela, Mirabelle, and Bruno returned home. The whole family worked together to rebuild Casita. When Mirabelle put in the doorknob, the house came alive, the magic returned, and Mirabelle knew she was loved and important.

video_title: Grace For President

summaries.summary: Grace Campbell learns that the United States has never had a woman president, so she decides to run for president in her school election. Her teacher lets the class hold an election, but another class chooses Thomas Cobb as its candidate. Thomas is good at spelling, science, and soccer, so Grace knows she must work hard. The children learn about electoral votes and that a candidate needs 270 votes to win. Grace promises a peaceful, clean school and better lunches, while Thomas promises tutoring, soccer lessons, and fish tacos. Grace makes posters, gives speeches, hands out cupcakes, and helps improve the school. On Election Day, the states cast their votes. Thomas and Grace are very close, and only Wyoming remains. Sam gives Wyoming’s three votes to Grace because he thinks she is the best person for the job. Grace wins with 270 votes and tells the class she will become president someday.

One day, Grace sees a poster of presidents and discovers that no woman has ever been president. She thinks this is unfair and decides to become the first girl president. Mrs. Barrington organizes a school election, but Thomas Cobb runs too. Thomas is a spelling champion, a prize-winning science student, and a soccer captain. The class learns that each state has electoral votes and that 270 votes are needed to win. Grace listens to her classmates and promises no bullies, no littering, and better hot lunches. She campaigns with posters, speeches, cupcakes, and rallies. She also keeps her promises by joining the safety squad, helping beautify the school, and working in the cafeteria. At the election assembly, Grace and Thomas receive almost the same number of votes. Sam casts Wyoming’s three votes for Grace because he believes she is best for the job. Grace wins and confidently says she will be president of the United States when she grows up.

Grace wants to be president after learning that the country has never had a woman president. Her school holds an election, and Thomas becomes her opponent. The students represent states and learn how electoral votes work. Grace creates the slogan “Make history” and promises to make school peaceful, clean, and happier at lunchtime. Thomas promises tutoring, soccer lessons, and fish tacos. Grace works hard during the campaign. She speaks at recess, gives out cupcakes, holds rallies, and helps the school before the election even happens. Thomas thinks the boys have more electoral votes, so he is not worried. At the final assembly, the representatives announce their state votes. Near the end, Thomas and Grace are close, with Wyoming still undecided. Sam looks at Grace’s handmade flag and then gives all three Wyoming votes to her. Grace reaches the needed 270 votes and wins. Sam explains that he chose her because he thought she was the best person for the job.

video_title: What Do You Do With a Problem

summaries.summary: One day, the narrator suddenly had a problem. The narrator did not want it, ask for it, or like it, and wondered why it was there. The narrator tried to make it go away by shooting it, scolding it, and ignoring it, but nothing worked. Then the narrator became very worried. The more the narrator worried, the bigger the problem seemed to become. Hiding and disguising did not help, because the problem kept appearing everywhere. Finally, the narrator could not take it anymore and decided to face the problem. Although the narrator was afraid, the narrator tackled it and looked closely. The problem was not what the narrator had imagined. Inside it was something beautiful: an opportunity to learn, grow, be brave, and do something. Now the narrator is not afraid of problems and knows that every problem has an opportunity for something good if it is carefully examined.

The narrator tells about a problem that appeared one day without being wanted or requested. At first, the narrator tried many ways to get rid of it. The narrator shot at it, scolded it, ignored it, hid from it, and even used disguises. None of these plans worked. Instead, worry made the problem seem larger. The narrator worried about being swallowed, attacked, or losing everything. The problem seemed to be everywhere, and the narrator thought about it all the time. At last, the narrator said, “This has to stop,” and wondered whether fear had made the problem look worse than it was. The narrator then faced the problem and tackled it. When they met face to face, the narrator discovered that the problem contained something beautiful. It held an opportunity to learn, grow, be brave, and do something. Now problems look different to the narrator, because each one may hide something good.

A problem came to the narrator, and the narrator wished it would disappear. The narrator asked what the problem wanted and tried to force it away. When that failed, the narrator began worrying about many possible dangers. The narrator worried about what might happen, and the problem grew bigger in the narrator’s mind. Hiding did not help either. Even while disguised, the narrator was found by the problem, and avoiding it made the problem seem to appear everywhere. The narrator felt bad and finally decided that this could not continue. Looking carefully at the situation, the narrator realized the problem had not swallowed or attacked them. The narrator chose to face it despite being afraid and tackled it. Face to face, the narrator found that the problem was different from what had been expected. It contained a beautiful opportunity to learn, grow, become brave, and do something. The narrator now looks for good opportunities inside problems.

video_title: Luca Movie Storybook 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Luca is a young sea monster who lives in the ocean but dreams of seeing the land. He meets Alberto, and they discover that sea monsters become humans when they come out of the water. The friends build pretend Vespas and dream of traveling. Luca's parents worry and want him to live with his uncle, so Luca runs away to find Alberto. In the town of Portorosso, they meet Julia and join a race to win money for a real Vespa. They practice swimming, eating pasta, and riding a bike. Alberto feels left out and reveals that they are sea monsters. During the race, rain changes Alberto, and Luca rescues him. Massimo accepts the boys, and they win because they cross the finish line. Alberto sells the Vespa so Luca can go to school. Alberto stays with Massimo, and the friends keep their happy memories and friendship.

Luca lives under the sea with his family and wonders what life is like above the water. When he meets Alberto, the two young sea monsters go to land and become boys. They make pretend Vespas and have wonderful adventures together. Luca's parents want to send him deep into the ocean with his uncle, but Luca leaves to find Alberto. In Portorosso, Luca and Alberto meet Julia. They join her for the Portorosso Cup because the prize can buy a real Vespa. They train for swimming, pasta eating, and bike riding. Alberto becomes upset when Luca wants to attend school with Julia, and he shows Julia that they are sea monsters. During the race, rain reveals the boys to everyone. Luca saves Alberto from a net, and Julia helps stop the bully. Massimo accepts the friends. They win the race, share a meal with their families, and Luca gets a train ticket for school. Alberto stays in town with Massimo.

A curious sea monster named Luca wants to see the world above the ocean. He meets Alberto, and they turn into humans on land. Together, they build Vespas from things they find and dream of going anywhere. Luca travels with Alberto to Portorosso, where Julia joins them for a race. The friends hope to win enough money to buy a real Vespa. They train hard, but Alberto feels sad when Luca wants to go to school with Julia. Alberto reveals their sea-monster secret, and danger follows. Luca later promises that they will still get a Vespa. In the race, Luca wears a diving suit, eats pasta, and rides quickly. Rain turns Alberto into a sea monster, so Luca saves him from a net. The crowd sees Luca's secret too. Massimo accepts both boys, and they win the race. They share a meal with Luca's family. Luca goes to school, while Alberto stays with Massimo, and their friendship continues.

video_title: 🐌 Blockhead: The Life of Fibonacci (Math)

summaries.summary: Leonardo loves numbers and enjoys counting everything around him. At school, he solves a math problem quickly, but his teacher becomes angry when Leonardo daydreams about birds and calls him a blockhead. Leonardo feels hurt and leaves. His father sends him to Africa, where Alfredo tells him to study what makes him happy. Leonardo learns Hindu-Arabic numerals, fractions, geometry, division, and subtraction during his travels. He writes about a rabbit puzzle and discovers a pattern: each number comes from adding the two numbers before it. Later, people in Pisa still make fun of his ideas. Alfredo helps Leonardo notice the same numbers in flowers, starfish, apples, and square shapes. Leonardo draws a spiral using the pattern. He realizes that Mother Nature uses these numbers in many places, so he no longer feels ashamed of being called Blockhead.

As a boy, Leonardo is much faster at math than the other students. While waiting for them, he wonders about the birds outside, but his teacher thinks he is lazy and calls him Blockhead. Leonardo is sad, yet Alfredo understands that numbers make him happy. In Africa, Leonardo studies the easier Hindu-Arabic numerals and learns more mathematics from wise people in many countries. He creates a rabbit problem for his book. By watching how rabbit pairs grow, he finds the number pattern one, one, two, three, five, and more. The pattern reaches the ruler Frederick II, who is impressed by Leonardo’s skill. Back in Pisa, some people still reject the new numerals, making Leonardo doubt himself. Alfredo encourages him. Together they find the same pattern in flowers and other parts of nature. Leonardo uses squares to draw a spiral and learns that the numbers help order the universe.

Leonardo has always been happiest when thinking about numbers, even though teachers and other people call him a blockhead. His father takes him to Northern Africa, where Alfredo advises him to learn everything about numbers. Leonardo studies new numerals and travels to learn about fractions, geometry, division, and subtraction. He writes a book containing a puzzle about rabbits. The rabbit pairs produce a growing sequence because each new number is made by adding the previous two numbers. Leonardo becomes known for his mathematical work, and Frederick II praises him. However, people in Pisa still criticize his use of numerals from India. Leonardo feels sad until Alfredo reminds him that his numbers are important. They count petals and discover the same sequence in nature. Leonardo arranges squares based on the sequence and draws a spiral. He understands that these numbers appear throughout nature and feels proud of his way of thinking.

video_title: All By Myself Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A child does many things all by myself. First, the child runs to the bathroom, sits, washes, and brushes. The child gets dressed by pulling up blue jeans, buttoning and zipping them, putting on socks, and tying the right and left shoes. Then the child combs their hair. Breakfast is ready, so the child pours, crunches, and says, “Yum.” The child opens the school door and goes on the way. At school, the child builds, paints, writes, and sings all day. After school, there is still more to do. The child goes here and there, enjoys quiet, and practices a lesson. Then the child helps with dinner. When night comes, the child takes off the clothes, washes in the tub, and gets clean and dry. The child chooses a book, snuggles close, says good night, and sleeps sweet dreams.

The day begins in the bathroom. The child sits, washes, brushes, and does it all by myself. Next, the child gets dressed. The bottoms go on, the top goes on, and the shirt is snapped. Blue jeans are pulled up, buttoned, and zipped. Socks and shoes go on, and the shoes are tied. After combing, the child is done. At breakfast, the child pours, crunches, and enjoys the food. The school door opens, and the child goes to school. There is building, painting, writing, and singing all day. After school, the child goes here and there, enjoys some quiet, and practices a lesson. Soon it is time to eat, and the child helps with dinner. At bedtime, clothes come off. Water runs, and the child splashes, rubs, squeezes, cleans, and dries. Then the child chooses a book, snuggles close, turns off the light, says good night, and sleeps.

One busy day starts with the child going quickly to the bathroom. The child washes and brushes without help. Then the child dresses: bottoms, top, shirt, blue jeans, socks, and shoes. The child buttons, zips, ties both shoes, and combs. Breakfast is ready. The child pours, eats, and says, “Yum.” Then the child opens the school door and goes on the way. At school, the child builds, paints, writes, and sings. When school is over, the child still has things to do. The child goes here and there, has quiet time, and practices a lesson. The child helps with dinner, too. After the whole day, night time comes. The child unsnaps, unzips, and gets ready for a bath. Water runs, and the child splashes, squeezes, rubs, cleans, and dries. The child says goodbye to the tub, chooses a book, snuggles close, says good night, and sleeps.

video_title: The Caboose Who Got Loose

summaries.summary: Katie Caboose rode at the very back of a long train. She did not like the smoke, bumps, loud noises, dark tunnels, high mountain tracks, or deep rocky places. Katie wished she could be a tree, a house, or a quiet little cabin. One night, a small switchman’s shack told Katie that it wished it could be a caboose because Katie had the best life. Katie began to feel happier about being herself. Soon, a train took her away again. On a hot mountain climb, the train gave a big jump, and Katie’s old coupling bolt broke. Katie flew loose down the track. She went faster and faster and flew over the treetops. Two tall spruce trees caught her and held her safely. A train came looking with a crane and a bright light, but it did not see Katie. She stayed in the trees with squirrels and birds. At last, Katie was free and loved her new home.

Katie was a caboose at the end of a freight train. The engine was proud and strong, but Katie felt sad because she had to follow through smoke, noisy yards, tunnels, cliffs, and mountains. She dreamed of living quietly in a tree, a house, or a little cabin in the forest. In a freight yard, Katie met a small shack high on a post. The shack wished to be a caboose, while Katie wished she could trade places. Before they could change anything, another train came and pulled Katie away. Katie decided to try to be a happy caboose. Later, while the train climbed a hot mountain, a jolt broke her coupling. Katie became loose and rushed down the track. She flew over the trees, but two spruce trees caught her. A rescue train searched for her, but the light missed her hiding place. Katie remained safely in the treetops, where birds and squirrels visited her. She was finally free.

Katie Caboose wanted a quiet life instead of being last on a noisy train. She disliked the smoke and jolts and was frightened by boulders, steep mountain edges, dark tunnels, and imaginary caboose-eating monsters. She wished to be a tree, a house, or a forest cabin. Then a little switchman’s shack said it wanted to be a caboose because Katie seemed to have a wonderful life. Katie started to see her own life differently and promised to stop complaining. But on a hot mountain road, the engine made the cars jump. Katie’s rusty coupling broke, and she rolled away alone. She sped down the hill toward a dangerous curve and flew like a kite. Two evergreen trees caught her between their trunks. A train with a crane and bright light searched for her, but it could not see her. Katie stayed among the trees with squirrels and birds. She was free at last and was happy there.

video_title: The Bad Seed by Jory John

summaries.summary: A seed believes he is a bad seed. He does many unkind and careless things. He is late, cuts in line, tells silly jokes, stares at people, and does not listen. Long ago, he lived happily with many other seeds on a sunflower. Then the flower drooped, and the seeds were put into a bag. The seed was swallowed by a giant and was spit out under bleachers. After that frightening event, he stopped smiling and stayed away from everyone. He lived in a soda can and did not care about anything. One day, he decided he did not want to be bad anymore. He began trying to be happy and kind. He still made mistakes, but he also said please and thank you, smiled, and held doors open. He learned that trying to change could make him feel good, and others began to see that he was not so bad anymore.

The Bad Seed thinks everyone sees him as bad. He never puts things away, arrives late, cuts in line, interrupts people, and forgets to listen. He says he cannot help being this way. But he was not always unhappy. At first, he was a humble seed living on a sunflower with his large seed family. They had fun and stayed close. Then the flower drooped, and a giant swallowed him. He screamed until the giant spit him out. He landed under bleachers, where gum softened his fall. After that, he became lonely and stopped smiling. He hid in a soda can and acted as if he did not care. Later, he made an important choice. He decided to stop being a bad seed and began taking one day at a time. He still arrived late and talked during movies, but he also used polite words, smiled, and helped people. He felt both bad and good while he kept trying.

A little seed says, “I’m a bad seed.” He explains that he lies about unimportant things, cuts in line, glares at people, and finishes their sentences. He remembers that he once lived happily with his seed family on a sunflower. When the flower drooped, he ended up in a bag and then inside a giant. He was spit out and landed under bleachers with a loud thud. Gum made his fall softer. After this, something changed. He stopped smiling, became a friend to nobody, and lived inside a soda can. For a while, he did not care. Then he decided he wanted to be happy instead. Being good was difficult because he was used to being bad, but he practiced every day. He said please and thank you, smiled, and held doors open. He still made mistakes, but sometimes he felt good. At the end, someone says he is not so bad anymore, and he hears it.

video_title: Encanto - Mirabel's Discovery 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Mirabelle lives with her magical family in the Encanto. Everyone has a gift except her. At her cousin Antonio’s fifth birthday, Antonio receives the gift of talking to animals. His magical room is a beautiful rainforest. Then Mirabelle sees cracks in the house, but they disappear before anyone else can see them. She learns that the magic is fading and that Bruno once saw a vision of the cracked house with Mirabelle in the center. Mirabelle finds Bruno and helps him finish the vision. It says she must embrace Isabella. Isabella admits she is tired of being perfect and can make prickly plants as well as flowers. The cracks return, and the candle goes out. Abuela explains that Abuelo Pedro’s love made the Encanto, but her broken heart damaged Casita. Mirabelle and Abuela return home. The family rebuilds together, and the magic comes back. Mirabelle feels proud of her family and herself.

The Madrigal family lives in the Encanto, a magical place created after Abuelo Pedro was lost while protecting the family. Abuela Alma cares for the miracle, which gives family members magical gifts. Mirabelle has no gift, so she feels sad when her cousin Antonio receives one. Antonio can talk to animals, and his room becomes a rainforest. Soon, Mirabelle notices cracks spreading through the house. Her family thinks she imagined them, but Mirabelle discovers that the candle is melting and the Encanto’s magic is dying. Luisa tells her about Bruno’s unfinished vision. Mirabelle finds Bruno, and together they complete it. The vision points to Isabella, who seems perfect but secretly dislikes always being perfect. She shows that she can grow prickly plants too. The house breaks, and everyone loses their gifts. At the river, Abuela says her sadness caused the damage, not Mirabelle. The family rebuilds Casita, and the magic returns.

Mirabelle is the only member of her family without a magical gift. She still helps her nervous cousin Antonio walk to his gift door. Antonio receives the power to talk to animals, and his animal friends lead him through his rainforest bedroom. During the party, Mirabelle sees cracks in the house. The cracks vanish, so the family does not believe her. Mirabelle then hears Abuela worrying that the candle and the Encanto’s magic are fading. Bruno’s vision shows a broken house with Mirabelle in the middle. Mirabelle finds Bruno hiding and helps him complete the vision. She visits Isabella, who can make flowers but is tired of being perfect. Isabella reveals another power: she can make prickly plants. After the cracks return, the candle goes out and the family’s gifts disappear. Abuela finds Mirabelle at the river and explains that her broken heart damaged Casita. Mirabelle and Abuela go home, and the family works together to rebuild the Encanto. The magic is restored, and Mirabelle is proud to belong.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑇ℎ𝑒 𝐿𝑎𝑏𝑜𝑟𝑠 𝑜𝑓 𝐻𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝐵𝑒𝑎𝑙 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Hercules Beal is starting seventh grade at a new environmental sciences academy. He lives with his older brother, Achilles, after their parents died and Achilles returned home to run the family farm and nursery. Hercules wants a dog, and he unexpectedly finds Mindy, a brave brown-and-white dog who protects him from Achilles. At school, a strict retired Marine lieutenant colonel assigns Hercules a project about the twelve labors of the mythical Hercules. Hercules researches the first labor, capturing the Nemean lion, and realizes that a dangerous problem near his home may be its modern equivalent. Eleven ugly cats are living in an abandoned summer house and threatening Mindy and local birds. With Ellie, Henry, and Ty, Hercules tries to drive the cats out and board up the house. He is injured but finishes the job. When he meets the scarred one-eyed cat afterward, she unexpectedly shows affection, and Hercules feels some of his deep sadness begin to loosen.

Hercules Beal feels uncomfortable about his name, his missing parents, and moving from Truro Middle School to a new academy. His brother Achilles is responsible for him and the family nursery, so Hercules cannot have the border collie he wants. Instead, a wonderful dog appears at the beach and becomes his pet, with Ellie naming her Mindy. At school, Lieutenant Colonel Hooper gives Hercules a difficult assignment: connect each of Hercules' twelve mythological labors to events in his own life. Hercules studies the Nemean lion, a creature that could not be harmed by ordinary weapons and that Hercules defeated in its den. Soon Mindy chases a frightening one-eyed cat to an abandoned house filled with twelve dangerous cats. Hercules and his friends plan to remove the cats and seal the house. During a storm, the cats attack, and Hercules is scratched while escaping. He returns and boards up the house. The scarred cat then approaches peacefully, purrs, and lets Hercules hold her, helping him feel less burdened by grief.

After a painful year following an accident, Hercules Beal begins a new school year with his brother Achilles and his dog Mindy. His new teacher, Lieutenant Colonel Hooper, is stern but gives him a meaningful project about applying the twelve labors of the ancient Hercules to modern life. Hercules' first task is connected to the Nemean lion, which he learns was captured only after Hercules used a club because the beast could not be wounded by arrows or swords. Hercules soon notices a group of savage cats living in an abandoned summer house. They have already killed birds and chase Mindy, so Hercules decides they are his modern Nemean lions. With three friends, he searches the house and attempts to force the cats outside. The animals attack from the ceiling during a thunderstorm, and Hercules suffers cuts on his arm and legs. He nevertheless boards up the windows and completes the labor. The last cat, badly scarred and missing an eye, does not attack him. Instead, it purrs against his bleeding legs, and comforting it makes Hercules feel lighter inside.

video_title: Moana 2 Read Along Storybook 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Moana returns to her island in a canoe and sees her family, including her little sister, simia. Moana learns that she must find the Lost Island M toitu and break an old curse. She takes a sea star from home and leaves with Moy, Kay, and loto. On the ocean, a giant clam swallows their canoe. Inside the clam, Moana is separated from her friends. The crew meets Maui, while Moana meets the demigod Matangi. Matangi tells Moana to get lost so she can find her way out. Moana finds a portal, and everyone escapes into the cursed sea. They make a plan to reach Moda fitu. Maui blocks the storm's lightning, and Moana swims to the island. Together, they pull it from the ocean and break the curse. Wayfinders come from across the ocean, and Moana reunites with simia.

Moana is a master wayfinder who loves the ocean. After receiving a vision, she begins a journey to find M toitu and connect the people of the ocean again. Her crew includes Moy, a historian, Kay, a farmer, and loto, a canoe builder. A giant clam swallows their canoe, and the crew lands inside the clam on a pile of trash. Moana is missing, but her friends find Maui. Moana meets Matangi, who says they are trapped and gives her a strange clue: she must get lost to find her way out. Moana clears the darkness and discovers a portal. Everyone escapes into a strange, sick-looking sea. Maui cheers Moana when she feels defeated. They distract the storm god, while Maui blocks lightning and Moana swims to Motu. Moana places the sea star on the island. Maui and Moana lift it from the ocean, break the curse, and bring the ocean people together.

Moana leaves her island with a sea star from home because a vision tells her to find the Lost Island and break an old curse. Her new friends travel with her, but a giant clam swallows their canoe. Inside the clam, the crew meets Maui, and Moana meets Matangi. Matangi explains that everyone is trapped and tells Moana that getting lost can help her find a way out. Moana finds a portal, and the crew escapes to the cursed sea. The island they need is under the water, and everyone feels defeated. Maui uses kind, encouraging words to help Moana. They make a plan. Maui uses his magical hook to stop the storm's lightning, while Moana swims with all her strength. She puts the sea star on the island, and her spirit appears proudly. Maui and Moana pull the island up, break the curse, and connect the ocean people. Moana celebrates and is happy to see her sister again.

video_title: Beauty and the Beast (a Big Golden Book)

summaries.summary: A prince turns away an old woman who offers him a rose, so she turns him into a beast and enchants his castle. The spell can end only if he learns to love and is loved before the rose loses its last petal. Belle, a kind girl who loves books, goes to the castle to rescue her father, Maurice. She agrees to stay in his place. At first, Belle is frightened, but the castle objects welcome her. The Beast saves Belle from hungry wolves, and she cares for his wounds. They spend time together, and Belle teaches him patience and good manners. Belle sees his kind heart. When Belle sees that her father is sick, the Beast lets her leave. Gaston attacks the castle. Belle returns and tells the Beast she loves him just before the last petal falls. The Beast changes into a prince, and the enchanted objects become human again.

Long ago, an enchantress punished a selfish prince by changing him into a beast. A magic rose showed that he had little time to learn love. In a village nearby, Belle loved reading, while Gaston only cared about himself. Belle's father, Maurice, became lost and found the Beast's castle. The Beast locked him away, so Belle offered to stay instead. At the castle, talking objects helped Belle feel welcome. Belle and the Beast slowly became friends. The Beast showed her his library, and Belle helped him learn good manners. The Beast saved Belle from wolves, and Belle cared for him when he was hurt. Belle later saw her father in a magic mirror and left to help him. Gaston told the villagers the Beast was dangerous and attacked the castle. Belle came back when the Beast was hurt. She said, “I love you,” and the spell broke. The Beast became a prince, and everyone lived happily ever after.

A poor old woman asks a prince for shelter, but he refuses because of her appearance. She reveals that she is an enchantress and changes him into a beast. Belle lives nearby with her inventor father, Maurice. When Maurice becomes lost and is captured by the Beast, Belle takes his place in the castle. She meets Mrs. Potts, Chip, Lumiere, and Cogsworth, who are enchanted objects. Belle explores the castle and finds the magic rose. Wolves chase her, but the Beast saves her and gets hurt. Belle stays to help him. They grow closer while reading, talking, and dancing. Then Belle sees that Maurice needs help, and the Beast lets her go with a magic mirror. Gaston locks Belle and Maurice away and leads villagers to the castle. The Beast fights Gaston but is badly hurt. Belle returns and says she loves him before the final rose petal falls. The Beast becomes a prince, and the castle friends become human.

video_title: Frozen Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Frozen - Elsa's Icy Magic

summaries.summary: Elsa's coronation goes badly when Anna pulls off Elsa's glove during an argument. Elsa's hidden icy magic bursts out and freezes things around her. The people become afraid, so Elsa runs to the North Mountain and builds an ice palace. Anna comes to tell Elsa that the whole kingdom is frozen. Elsa tries to help, but her magic hurts Anna. Hans and his men capture Elsa and put her in a dungeon. Elsa becomes very upset, breaks free with icy blasts, and runs into the storm. Hans tells her that Anna has died because her heart was frozen. Elsa feels heartbroken. When Hans raises his sword, Anna jumps in front of Elsa and becomes frozen. Elsa hugs Anna and cries. Then something amazing happens: Anna thaws and hugs Elsa back. Elsa has found her sister again and will never let her go.

Elsa keeps her magical power secret, but during her coronation, Anna pulls off her glove while they argue about Prince Hans. Elsa's magic freezes everything, and the kingdom thinks she is dangerous. Elsa escapes to the North Mountain, where she makes a beautiful ice palace and feels free. Anna finds her and explains that Elsa has frozen the kingdom. Elsa cannot stop the winter, and an icy blast hits Anna. Hans surrounds Elsa with guards and later locks her in a dungeon. Elsa is frightened and frustrated. Her magic breaks her chains and the dungeon wall, allowing her to escape. Hans tells Elsa that Anna has perished because Elsa froze her heart. Elsa falls down, and the storm stops. Hans lifts his sword, but Anna protects Elsa and is frozen solid. Elsa holds her sister. Then Anna thaws and hugs Elsa. The sisters are together again.

On her coronation day, Elsa argues with Anna about Anna's engagement to Prince Hans. Anna pulls away Elsa's glove, and Elsa accidentally uses her icy magic in front of everyone. The kingdom becomes afraid of her, so Elsa runs away and builds an ice palace on the North Mountain. Anna visits with terrible news: Elsa's magic has frozen the entire kingdom. Elsa loses control and hits Anna with an icy blast. Hans brings men to capture Elsa and places her in a dungeon. He says people may punish her unless summer returns, but Elsa does not know how to end the winter. Later, Elsa breaks out with powerful ice blasts and escapes into a storm. Hans says Anna's heart was frozen and that she has died. Elsa is devastated. Hans raises his sword, but Anna steps between him and Elsa. The sword breaks, and Anna becomes frozen. Elsa hugs Anna and cries. Then Anna thaws and hugs her sister back.

video_title: a little Golden Book Biography Katie Ledecky kids book read along

summaries.summary: Katie Lei loved swimming from the time she was little. Her family learned to swim, and Katie and her brother joined a summer swim team when she was six. Katie practiced often, wrote down goals, and kept trying when swimming was hard. Her coach taught her a special freestyle stroke that helped her swim faster. Katie dreamed of going to the Olympics, and in 2012, when she was fifteen, she joined the United States team in London. She won the 800-meter freestyle, earned a gold medal, and broke a record. Katie kept swimming and setting new records. In 2016, she won more gold medals in Rio and beat her own record. Later, she swam at Stanford University and won medals at the Tokyo Olympics. In 2023, she won the same world championship event for the sixth year in a row. Katie says anything is possible when children work hard and follow their dreams.

Katie Lei grew up in a family where swimming was important. Her mother taught Katie and her brother to swim, and Katie quickly discovered that she loved the water. She joined a summer swim team at age six and soon raced all year. Katie enjoyed other sports, but swimming was her favorite. She practiced before and after school, ate food that gave her energy, and learned a new stroke from her coach. In eighth grade, Katie made a goal to reach the Olympics. She achieved it in 2012 and became the youngest member of the United States team in London. Katie won the 800-meter freestyle by more than four seconds and broke a record. She continued winning races and medals, including four gold medals and one silver in Rio. She graduated from Stanford while preparing for another Olympics. Katie later won medals in Tokyo and made history in 2023. She keeps setting goals and working hard.

Katie Lei became a great swimmer because she loved challenges and did not give up. As a child, she learned to swim with help from her family, joined a swim team, and practiced many times each week. Katie set goals for her swimming speed and worked until she reached them. At fifteen, she went to the 2012 Olympic Games in London. Although many people did not expect her to win, Katie took the lead and won the women’s 800-meter freestyle. She received a gold medal and broke the United States record. Katie also worked hard outside the pool. She finished high school, helped others, and later graduated from Stanford University. She won many races and medals at the Rio and Tokyo Olympics. In 2023, she became the first swimmer to win the same world championship event six years in a row. Katie continues to set goals. Her advice is to believe anything is possible, work hard, and follow dreams.

video_title: The Backyard BUG Book for Kids

summaries.summary: A little caterpillar comes out of its tiny egg and begins exploring the backyard. It eats leaves and grows bigger and bigger, shedding its skin as it grows. The caterpillar sees many creatures. A ladybug has protected wings, a grasshopper can leap far, and colorful jewel beetles have beautiful wings. It hears a singing cricket and watches bees do a waggle dance to find flowers. It also sees strong ants, a dangerous spider, a stick insect hiding like a twig, and a roly poly curled into a ball. Dragonflies fly fast, and fireflies glow at night. When the caterpillar becomes very big, it rests in a chrysalis. Inside, its body changes. Then it comes out as a beautiful butterfly. The caterpillar has grown into something new after patiently changing inside its little house.

A young caterpillar starts life by chewing out of its egg. It eats the eggshell and then munches leaves all day. As it grows, it meets backyard bugs and learns about them. Ladybugs have two pairs of wings. Grasshoppers can make giant leaps, and jewel beetles come in many colors. Male crickets sing, while bees share directions by dancing. Ants are tiny but very strong. The caterpillar stays away from a spider’s sticky web and notices that a stick insect can hide like a branch. A roly poly rolls up tightly, while a dragonfly flies quickly and even backward. At night, fireflies shine their lights. Soon the caterpillar is too big for its old life. It makes a chrysalis on a tree and sleeps inside. Its body changes there. After the change is finished, the caterpillar becomes a beautiful butterfly.

A caterpillar leaves its safe egg and wonders what it will become. It eats and grows while looking at creatures in the backyard. The caterpillar wishes it could be like the ladybug, grasshopper, jewel beetle, cricket, bees, ants, dragonfly, and glowing fireflies. Along the way, it learns that grasshoppers jump far, only male crickets sing, bees dance to show where food is, and ants can lift very heavy things. It is careful around a spider’s web and discovers that some animals, such as spiders and roly polies, are not insects. A stick insect stays safe by looking like a stick. When the caterpillar is very large, it settles on a tree and forms a chrysalis. Inside, it changes. Then the little caterpillar comes out in a new form: a beautiful butterfly with wings of its own.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Ariel and the Big Baby

summaries.summary: Arielle was excited because whales were coming near her reef. She went to see them, and Flounder swam with her. Arielle did not tell Flounder about the whales because he was jumpy and might not come. They met Sebastian and his band, who were ready for a deep-sea duet. Arielle loved singing, but she wanted to see the whales, so she and Flounder hid behind a rock and swam away. At the reef, they could not see any whales. Flounder said the whales were enormous, and Arielle called him a big baby. Flounder felt hurt and swam away. Then bubbles burst from the sea, and a mother whale and baby whale appeared. Flounder called the baby whale a big baby. Arielle said she was sorry and told him it was okay to be afraid. The whales sang goodbye, and Arielle and Flounder went home for the duet.

Arielle wanted to watch whales swim nearby. Her friend Flounder joined her, but Arielle thought he would not come if he knew about the whales. She said she was only going for a swim. On the way, they met Sebastian and his band preparing to sing. Arielle wanted to sing too, but she did not want to miss the whales. She and Flounder quietly hid behind a rock, then hurried to the reef. They looked across the deep blue sea, but no whales were there. When the whales finally appeared, Flounder saw a mother and a baby whale. Before that, Arielle had hurt Flounder's feelings by calling him a big baby because he was afraid of the enormous whales. Flounder swam away. Arielle followed and apologized. She said it was okay to be afraid. Then the whales sang a beautiful goodbye song. Arielle and Flounder returned home and arrived in time to sing with Sebastian's band.

On an exciting day, Arielle went out to see whales. Flounder swam beside her and asked where she was going. Flounder was jumpy, so Arielle said she was just going for a swim. Soon, they found Sebastian and his band setting up a deep-sea duet. Arielle loved singing, but she chose to keep looking for the whales. She and Flounder slipped behind a rock and dashed to the reef. Arielle searched the blue sea, but the whales had not arrived. When Flounder saw how enormous they were, he cried out. Arielle told him not to be a big baby. Flounder felt hurt and started to leave. Then bubbles burst, and a mother whale and baby whale came up from the sea. Flounder called the baby a big baby. Arielle apologized for hurting him and said it was okay to be afraid. The whales sang a beautiful song as they said goodbye. Arielle and Flounder went home for the deep-sea duet.

video_title: Disney Descendants The Rise of Red Paint This Town Red kids book read along

summaries.summary: Red, the daughter of the Queen of Hearts, is invited to attend Auradon Prep by Uma and Fairy Godmother. Her mother allows her to go, but the Queen has taken over Auradon and wants Red to become mean like her. A Looking Glass shows Red a frightening future in which she sits beside her evil mother. Red decides to use Maddox's time machine to change what happened. Chloe, Cinderella's daughter, follows her, even though she thinks Red may be evil. They travel back to the time when the school was called Merlin Academy. There, they meet young Bridget, the Queen's kind younger self, and Ella, Chloe's mother. Ulana, leader of the villain kids, plans a cruel trick against Bridget. Red and Chloe discover that Ulana needs a magic book. After overcoming angry eels and getting help from Ella, they enter Merlin's office. Ulana is frozen by a spell, and the girls stop the prank, hoping the future will be better.

Uma and Fairy Godmother invite Red, who lives in Wonderland, to Auradon Prep. Red's mother, the Queen of Hearts, is difficult and wants Red to act cruelly. When the Queen takes over Auradon, Red knows her mother's plan is wrong. Red wants her mother's approval, but she also wants to live her own life. Using Maddox's time machine, Red travels into the past with Chloe. They arrive when Auradon Prep is still Merlin Academy. Red meets Bridget, her mother's younger self, who is kind and makes cupcakes for the students. Chloe and Red also meet Ella and Prince Charming. The villain kids, led by the mean Ulana, do not like Bridget. Ulana plans to steal a magic book from Merlin's office so she can play a trick on Bridget. Red saves Chloe from angry eels, and Chloe decides to help after asking Ella for advice. They find the book, and a spell freezes Ulana. The girls stop the prank and return home, hoping things have changed.

Red receives an invitation to school, while Chloe receives glass shoes from Cinderella before leaving home. At Auradon Prep, Chloe learns that Cinderella and the Queen of Hearts were once friends, but the Queen later became evil. The Queen's Looking Glass shows Red a possible future where Red looks evil beside her. Then the Queen interrupts the school welcome and takes control of Auradon. Red decides she must stop her, so she uses a time machine with Chloe. In the past, they meet young Fairy Godmother, Merlin, Ella, Prince Charming, and Bridget, who is friendly to everyone. They also meet villain children, including a pirate and Ulana, their leader. Ulana is especially unkind to Bridget and plans to steal Merlin's magic book for a prank. Red and Chloe follow the villain kids to the Black Lagoon and later to Merlin's office. Morgi watches from a tree while the others search. Ulana takes the book, but a spell freezes her. Red and Chloe recover it, stop the prank, and go home hoping the future will improve.

video_title: Hey That’s My Monster

summaries.summary: One night, a child looks under the bed and finds a note saying that Gabe, the child’s monster, has gone to help someone else. The child learns that little Emma needs a monster because she keeps climbing out of her toddler bed at night. Gabe gives the child three chances to find a monster that can scare Emma to sleep. Agatha is slimy, but Emma laughs and wipes her noses. Cynthia has sharp claws, but Emma calls her pretty and decorates her tail. Vladimir has many tentacles, but Emma plays with them like jump ropes. Gabe returns and tries to scare Emma, but she calls him a fuzzy monster. Then Gabe’s little sister, Stella, arrives with a hiccup. Stella loves toes, and Emma quickly hides her feet. Gabe sees that Stella is the perfect monster for Emma. Stella stays with Emma, while Gabe returns to the child’s room, and everything becomes normal again.

Gabe is the child’s special monster, so the child is upset when Gabe leaves a note and goes away. Emma needs help staying in bed, because she likes to wander and play at night. The child calls three monsters from under Emma’s bed. Agatha is covered in slime, but Emma thinks she is funny. Cynthia has jagged claws, but Emma thinks she is pretty and puts bracelets on her tail. Vladimir has tentacles and tries to reach Emma, but Emma jumps over them and has fun. None of the three monsters can make Emma sleepy. Gabe comes back and tells Emma to get into bed. She does get into bed, but she keeps singing and is not afraid of Gabe. Then Stella, Gabe’s little sister, appears. Her hiccups and love of toes make Emma squeal and tuck in her feet. Stella becomes Emma’s perfect monster, and Gabe can go back to being the child’s monster.

The child wants Gabe back, but Gabe says he must help Emma first. Emma is supposed to sleep in her toddler bed, yet she keeps getting out to play. The child tries to summon a monster by having Emma knock on the floor. Agatha comes out, but Emma laughs at her slime. Cynthia comes next, but Emma plays with her claws and bracelets. Vladimir appears with tentacles, but Emma uses them as jump ropes. Because Emma enjoys every monster, the child worries that Gabe will be lost forever. Gabe returns and uses his loud voice, green ooze, sharp claws, and steam to scare Emma into bed. Still, Emma is not frightened enough to sleep. Then Stella comes looking for a snack. Stella walks toward Emma while hiccuping and says she loves toes. Emma hides her feet and giggles. Gabe realizes Stella can keep Emma in bed. Stella stays with Emma, and the child happily returns to bed with Gabe.

video_title: Beep! Beep! Go to Sleep! Bedtime Story for Kids

summaries.summary: Three little robots are getting ready for bed. They dim their infrared, brush their rotors, clean their shields, and power down. But the robots are not quiet for long. One robot needs a coil, says its sensor aches, and wants more oil. After that is fixed, the robots go back to bed. Then another robot needs a light because its fan belt is loose and its bolts are too tight. The robots try again to sleep. They keep beeping, talking, squeaking, squawking, blinking, and worrying. At last, one robot asks for a bedtime story. The story tells about many noisy robots that beep, buzz, bounce, and make other sounds. But these three robots become quiet. In the end, they finally put their boy to sleep.

It is bedtime for three little robots. They are told to dim their infrared, brush their rotors, clean their shields, and power down. At first, there is not a peep. Then one robot says it needs a coil, that its sensor aches, and that it wants more oil. After getting help, the robot rests its head. The robots return to bed, but another robot needs a light. Its fan belt is loose, and its bolts are too tight. The robots try to settle down again. Still, there is beeping, talking, squeaking, squawking, and many blinking and worrying sounds. Finally, the robots ask for a bedtime story. The story describes robots making many noisy sounds, but not these robots. The three little robots become quiet, and they finally put their boy to sleep.

Three little robots are supposed to sleep. They prepare for bed by dimming their infrared, brushing their rotors, cleaning their shields, and powering down. Soon, one robot says, “I need my coil. My sensor aches. I want more oil.” The robot gets what it needs and goes back to bed. Then another robot says it needs a light because its fan belt is loose and its bolts are too tight. Even after that, the robots remain awake. They make sounds by beeping, talking, squeaking, squawking, blipping, blinking, and worrying. The robots are told to go to sleep, but one more request comes: a bedtime story. The story is about robots beeping, buzzing, bouncing, and making many sounds. These robots are different. They become quiet, with not a peep, and finally put their boy to sleep.

video_title: How Santa Lost His Job

summaries.summary: Every year, Santa prepared for his Christmas ride, but he often worked slowly and caused a last-minute rush. Muckle, an elf, believed Santa was too old-fashioned and wasted time. He built a machine called the delator, which could prepare quickly, match gifts with children, and travel through chimneys. The elves tested Santa and the machine. The delator won because it got ready faster, sorted gifts quickly, and ignored the milk and cookies that slowed Santa down. Clara warned that Santa cared about doing things correctly, not only about speed, but the elves chose the delator. On Christmas Eve, storms and extra gifts confused the machine. It flew in circles while Santa stayed home, unable to relax. The elves finally asked Santa to return. Everyone helped him prepare, and he completed the ride. Afterward, the elves accepted Santa’s delays because they understood that his careful way was normal and important.

Santa’s elves became tired of the rush before Christmas and wondered why Santa could not plan better. Muckle decided to replace him, so he created the delator, a fast machine that could carry gifts and travel up and down chimneys. The elves challenged Santa and the delator in several contests. The machine got ready first, matched children with gifts faster, and raced through a chimney without stopping. Santa lost each contest, even though he noticed a child might not like a certain toy and enjoyed the chocolate-chip cookies left for him. Clara said Santa was not simply trying to meet a schedule; he wanted to get things right. The others ignored her and loaded the delator with gifts. When a storm changed the route and more presents were added, the machine became confused and spun around in the sky. The elves then asked Santa to take back his job, and he agreed.

Muckle thought Santa was too slow and set in his ways, so he secretly built the delator to do Santa’s work faster. Clara questioned the plan because Santa already delivered toys, but the elves wanted proof. In the contests, the delator prepared sooner, sorted gift requests more quickly, and raced through chimneys without stopping for treats. Santa lost, but he showed that he cared about whether gifts were suitable and about the children receiving them. The elves chose the delator anyway. On Christmas Eve, they gave Muckle extra directions, changed the number of gifts, and sent the machine into stormy weather. Its weight and new instructions confused it, so it circled in the sky instead of completing the journey. Santa tried to enjoy a quiet night, but he could not relax. When the elves asked for help, Santa returned. Muckle and the others helped him load the sleigh, and nobody tried to replace him again.

video_title: When I Am Angry - by Michael Gordon. Children's audiobook (read-aloud) how to overcome  anger.

summaries.summary: Josh is usually sweet and playful, but he often gets angry. One morning, he wants cake before lunch, and Mum says no. Josh breathes hard and grits his teeth. Mum teaches him to pretend his anger is a ball and throw it far away. Josh throws three anger balls and soon feels better. Later, Josh sees a stray black-and-white cat and wants to take it home. Mum says no, so Josh throws an anger ball, but he is still upset. His sister teaches him to take a deep breath, count to four, and let the feeling out. At home, Josh wants to follow some big boys to the park, but Dad says he is not big enough. Dad breathes with Josh until he calms down. The next day, Josh has a big store tantrum, but Mum helps him breathe and throw away his anger. She says it is fine to be angry, but anger should not ruin the day.

Josh has many angry moments. First, he wants cake before lunch, but Mum says no. His heart beats fast, and he feels very mad. Mum shows him how to imagine anger as a ball and throw it away. Josh throws three balls and feels happy enough to eat lunch and cake. At the park, Josh sees a stray cat and wants to keep it. Mum says no again. Josh throws an anger ball, but he still needs help, so his sister teaches him to breathe deeply, count to four, and let his anger out. Later, Josh wants to go to the park with some big boys. Dad says Josh must stay where his parents can see him. Josh feels tight and angry, so Dad breathes with him. The next day, Josh wants a new toy in a store. Mum says no, and Josh yells, cries, kicks, and stomps. Mum helps him breathe and throw anger balls until he calms down.

Josh is a fun little boy who sometimes loses his temper. When he asks for cake before lunch, Mum says no, and Josh becomes angry. Mum teaches him to throw his anger away like a ball. This helps him calm down. Later, Josh and his sister find a stray cat. Josh wants to take it home, but Mum says no. Josh throws an anger ball, then uses his sister's breathing trick: take a deep breath, count to four, and let the feeling out. When Josh wants to go to the park with older boys, Dad says he must stay near his parents. Josh feels angry and tight in his chest. Dad breathes with him until Josh can calm himself. The next day, Josh wants a new toy while shopping. He yells, cries, kicks, and stomps. Mum takes him outside the store, and they breathe and throw anger balls. Josh calms down, and Mum is proud.

video_title: Bubble Trouble by Margaret Mahy

summaries.summary: Mabel blows a bubble, but it floats away with her baby brother inside it. The baby smiles as the bubble bobs over tables, fences, gardens, and people. Mabel calls for Mother, and Mother runs after it. Many neighbors join the chase. Gribble Gribble carries his book, Tibble pulls Sybil along, the Kapil couple hurry down the lane, and a jogger named Neville joins them. The bubble rises above the town toward the chapel steeple. Everyone tries to think of a way to bring the baby down. Abel climbs the steeple with a pebble and throws it at the bubble. The pebble bursts the bubble, and the baby falls. Mabel, Tibble, Gribble, and Neville quickly stretch out Mrs. 3-ball’s patchwork quilt. The baby lands safely on it. His worried cries become happy giggles, and Mother holds him tightly. The people remember how Mabel and the others saved the baby and the day.

A little bubble causes big trouble when it breaks away from Mabel and carries her baby brother into the air. The baby enjoys wobbling inside the bubble, but Mabel is frightened and calls for Mother. Mother follows the bubble, and neighbors come running too. Christa, Gribble Gribble, Tibble, Sybil, the Kapil couple, and Neville all chase it through the town. The bubble keeps rising until it is high above the people and near the chapel steeple. Cannon dapple says they must find a way to bring the baby down. Abel climbs up with a pebble and aims at the bubble. His pebble breaks it, and the baby tumbles through the air. Everyone is scared, but Mabel and several helpers act quickly. They spread out Mrs. 3-ball’s pretty patchwork quilt. The baby bounces safely onto the quilt. Soon he is giggling and wriggling, and Mother hugs him tightly. The baby is safe because the group worked together.

Mabel’s bubble floats away with her baby brother trapped inside. It passes over many people, and the baby smiles and dribbles while he rides in the air. Mabel and Mother run after him, followed by a growing crowd from the town. The people hurry past shops and toward the chapel. The bubble rises higher and higher, so everyone worries about the baby. Cannon dapple says they must grapple with the problem and bring him down. Abel, who likes trouble, climbs the steeple with a pebble. He throws the pebble at the bubble, and the bubble bursts. The baby falls, making the crowd groan and gasp. Mabel, Tibble, Gribble, and Neville do not freeze. They quickly take Mrs. 3-ball’s patchwork quilt and hold it out. The baby bounces onto the quilt instead of falling to the ground. His cries turn into giggles. Mother catches him and holds him close, while the people tell the story of how Mabel and her helpers saved the day.

video_title: Frozen Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Frozen - Anna Loves Elsa

summaries.summary: Anna loves her sister Elsa. Anna says Elsa is the best big sister in the whole world. Elsa is good at hide and seek, and she pushes Anna on a swing. Anna asks for the swing to go higher and higher. Elsa shares her chocolate with Anna. Elsa also builds a pillow fort, and Anna thinks it is amazing. Elsa giggles. Anna says Elsa is the fastest sock slider in the kingdom and cheers for her. At the end, Anna says that her favorite thing about Elsa is that Elsa is her sister. Anna tells Elsa, “I love you, Elsa.”

Anna and Elsa are sisters who enjoy many things together. Anna loves Elsa and calls her the best big sister in the whole world. Elsa plays hide and seek and pushes a swing very high. Anna shouts, “Higher, higher!” Elsa shares her chocolate, and she builds the best pillow forts. Anna says, “This is amazing!” Elsa giggles. Elsa is also called the fastest sock slider in the kingdom, and someone cheers, “Go, Elsa, go!” All these fun things make Anna happy. Still, Anna's favorite thing is not the swing, chocolate, pillow fort, or sock sliding. Her favorite thing is that Elsa is her sister. Anna ends by saying, “I love you, Elsa.”

Elsa is a loving big sister to Anna. Anna says Elsa is the best big sister in the whole world. Elsa is great at hide and seek when Anna can find her. She pushes a swing, and Anna asks her to go higher and higher. Elsa shares chocolate with Anna. She makes the best pillow forts, and Anna says they are amazing. Elsa giggles during their happy play. Elsa is also the fastest sock slider in the kingdom, so someone cheers, “Go, Elsa, go!” Anna enjoys all the things Elsa does. But the most important thing for Anna is that Elsa is her sister. Anna tells Elsa that she loves her. The story shows Anna's love for Elsa through their play, sharing, cheering, and Anna's final loving words.

video_title: The Empty Pot read aloud

summaries.summary: Ping was a boy in China who loved flowers. Whatever he planted grew into beautiful flowers, bushes, or trees. The old emperor loved flowers, too, and needed to choose the next emperor. He gave every child a special seed and said the child with the best plant after one year would become the successor. Ping carefully planted his seed, watered it every day, and moved it to a bigger pot with better soil. Still, nothing grew. When spring came, the other children brought big, beautiful plants to the palace. Ping felt ashamed, but his father told him that doing his best was good enough. Ping brought his empty pot. The emperor asked what happened, and Ping told the truth. Then the emperor smiled. He had cooked all the seeds, so none could grow. Ping was the only child who brought the truth. Because Ping was brave and honest, the emperor gave him the kingdom and made him emperor.

In China, Ping was known for growing wonderful plants. The emperor was very old and wanted to find a successor. Since he loved flowers, he gave flower seeds to all the children in the land. He promised that whoever showed the best flower after a year would become emperor. Ping was excited and planted his seed in rich soil. He watered it every day and waited for a flower to appear. When nothing grew, he tried a larger pot and better black soil. He waited two more months, but the pot stayed empty. At the palace, the children showed the emperor their beautiful flowers. Ping felt embarrassed. His friend asked why he had not grown a flower, but Ping explained that his seed would not grow. His father encouraged him to take his empty pot. Ping told the emperor everything. The emperor revealed that all the seeds had been cooked. Ping was rewarded because he had the courage to be truthful.

The emperor of China loved flowers and needed to choose who would follow him. He invited every child to the palace and gave each one a seed. The child with the finest plant in one year would become the next emperor. Ping believed he could grow the best flower, so he planted his seed carefully and watered it every day. Nothing happened. He changed the soil and moved the seed into a bigger pot, but the seed still did not grow. After a whole year, Ping saw other children carrying wonderful plants. He worried that they would laugh at his empty pot. His father said that his best effort was enough, so Ping went to the palace. He honestly told the emperor that he had cared for the seed all year. The emperor then explained that the seeds had been cooked and could never grow. Ping had shown courage by bringing the empty truth. The emperor chose Ping and gave him the whole kingdom.

video_title: When’s Your Birthday? | A fun story about the best day ever!

summaries.summary: The birthday child keeps wondering when the special day will arrive. The child asks where the birthday is and how many days are left. The child wonders if it will be on Tuesday, tomorrow, winter, or spring. The child hopes for singing, dancing, and jumping. Then the child imagines birthday presents, including a pony, a necklace, a chicken, and a ball. The child also wants a big chocolate cake with six candles. There are wishes, kisses, berries, and tiny sandwiches with soup. Many people are invited, and they may wear fancy dresses, fuzzy slippers, feathered hats, or helmets. The child waits through the night, yawns, and dreams about the birthday. In the morning, the birthday finally arrives. It is time for cake, and the child celebrates with a happy birthday song of their own.

A child is very excited about a birthday and asks many questions about it. The child wants to know when the birthday will come, where it will be, and how long the wait will be. The child imagines singing a happy song, dancing around, and jumping again and again. The child thinks about wonderful birthday gifts, such as a pony, a necklace, a chicken, and a bouncing ball. A large cake is important too, especially one with lots of chocolate and six candles. The child wishes for kisses, berries, and little sandwiches with soup. Everyone is welcome to the birthday party. Guests can wear dresses, slippers, feathered hats, or helmets. At last, the child waits, yawns, and dreams through the night. When daytime comes, the birthday is finally here, and it is time to wake up and enjoy the cake.

The story follows a child waiting eagerly for a birthday. First, the child asks whether the birthday is soon and whether it will happen tomorrow, in winter, or in spring. The child imagines a celebration with singing, dancing, and jumping. Next, the child describes birthday wishes: a pony, a necklace, a chicken, a ball, and a big chocolate cake with six candles. The child also wants wishes, kisses, berries, and tiny sandwiches with soup. The child invites many people and says they can dress in many different ways, from fancy dresses to fuzzy slippers, feathered hats, or helmets. The child keeps asking if the birthday is almost here. During the night, the child does not sleep, but waits, yawns, and dreams. Then morning arrives. It is finally the birthday, and the child celebrates the happy time for cake.

video_title: THE VERY IMPATIENT CATERPILLAR Read Aloud by Mrs. K. | Ross Burach | Kids Book Read Aloud by Mrs. K.

summaries.summary: A little caterpillar learns that he can become a butterfly. He asks many questions while the other caterpillars build their chrysalises. He wants to know how to spin, when he will have wings, and how long the change will take. When he hears that it will take two weeks, he worries about being inside. He asks for a comic book, a snack, pizza, the bathroom, and a game. Soon, he decides he has waited long enough and comes out too early. He tries to fly, but he has no wings and falls. The caterpillar says he cannot be patient, but then he practices each day. He counts the days and learns to wait. After two weeks, he becomes a beautiful butterfly and says he will be more patient. Then the other butterflies begin migrating, and he asks them to wait for him.

The very impatient caterpillar watches other caterpillars prepare to change into butterflies. He is excited because he wants wings, too. He asks what to do next and builds a chrysalis, but he does not want to wait. He keeps asking if he is a butterfly yet. Inside the chrysalis, he thinks two weeks will be much too long. He asks for food, pizza, a book, a bathroom, and someone to play with. On the first day, he gives up and comes out. He expects to be a butterfly, but he has no wings, so he falls down. He tries to tell himself that he can be patient, then practices patience one day at a time. At last, two weeks pass. He comes out as a butterfly and feels transformed. He decides to be more patient, but then he has to hurry after the migrating butterflies.

A caterpillar hears that he will transform into a butterfly with wings. He is very excited and wants everything to happen right away. After making a chrysalis, he asks again and again whether he is a butterfly. The other caterpillars tell him to be patient and let nature take its course. The caterpillar worries about staying inside for two weeks. He tries to order pizza and thinks of many ways to make the time pass. On day one, he breaks out too soon. He calls himself a beautiful butterfly, but he cannot fly because he has no wings. After falling, he realizes he must try to wait. He says he can be patient, then counts the days and takes deep breaths. On day seven, eight, and nine, he keeps practicing. Two weeks later, he really is a butterfly. He feels changed and says he will be more patient. Then he follows the others as they migrate.

video_title: KID SHERIFF AND THE TERRIBLE TOADS Read Aloud - Written by Bob Shea | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Dry Water Gulch has a big problem: two terrible toad brothers steal gold, kiss cattle, insult chili, and make lots of noise. Mayor McMuffin needs a sheriff, so a seven-year-old boy named Ryan arrives riding a tortoise. Ryan cannot shoot, ride a horse, do rope tricks, or stay up late, but he knows a lot about dinosaurs. When the bank is robbed, Ryan says a T. rex did it. When a stagecoach is robbed, he blames velociraptors. The toads hear this and become angry because they committed those crimes. They also admit to shoplifting and insulting the chili. Ryan keeps naming dinosaurs until the toads say they did everything themselves. Then the toads rush into the jail, and Ryan locks them inside. The people cheer. Ryan leaves on his tortoise because he is a lawman, not a town paleontologist.

The people of Dry Water Gulch are frightened by outlaw toads. The toad brothers steal gold, kiss cattle, insult chili, and cause trouble everywhere. Mayor McMuffin is happy when Ryan comes to town to be sheriff. Ryan is only seven and cannot do ordinary sheriff jobs, but he knows many dinosaur names. After the bank is robbed, Ryan says it must have been a T. rex. After a stagecoach is robbed, he says velociraptors were responsible. The toads cannot stand hearing dinosaurs receive credit for their crimes. They confess that they robbed the bank, robbed the stagecoach, shoplifted from the mercantile, and insulted the chili. Ryan tells them that large dinosaurs belong in jail, so the toads charge through the jail door to prove they are real criminals. Ryan quickly locks the jail. The townspeople cheer, and the toads complain. Ryan then rides away on his tortoise.

Mayor McMuffin thinks Dry Water Gulch is ruined because two loud, rude toads are stealing and causing trouble. A young sheriff named Ryan arrives slowly on a tortoise. He cannot use a gun, ride a horse, or perform rope tricks, but he knows a really lot about dinosaurs. Ryan uses that knowledge to fool the toads. He says a T. rex robbed the bank and velociraptors robbed the stagecoach. The toads insist that dinosaurs did not do these things because the toads themselves committed the crimes. They also confess to kissing cattle, shoplifting, and insulting the town’s chili. Ryan says the jail is needed for real criminals and mentions that dinosaurs are mighty big.
