The toads rush inside to show that they are criminals, and Ryan locks them in. Everyone cheers. The mayor asks Ryan to stay, but Ryan says he is a lawman and rides into the sunset.

video_title: Aladdin Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Disney Princess - Jamine the Matchmaker

summaries.summary: Jasmine and Raja saw a circus tent in Agrabah. Raja seemed quiet and did not eat his lunch, so Jasmine wondered what was wrong. The next day, Jasmine, Aladdin, Raja, and Abu went to the circus. Raja did not enjoy the acts at first. Then a beautiful tigress named Malika came into the ring. Raja looked happy because he loved her. Jasmine asked the circus owner if Malika could live at the palace, but he said she was the circus star. Raja became very sad. Later, the owner brought Malika to Jasmine because Malika would not eat, sleep, or perform without Raja. Raja and Malika touched noses and were happy together. Jasmine saw that the owner would lose his circus, so she made a plan. The circus moved to a park beside the palace. Everyone celebrated at a royal ball and lived happily ever after.

One morning, Jasmine and Raja found a colorful circus tent. Raja soon became quiet and would not eat. Jasmine took him back to the circus with Aladdin, Abu, and herself. The circus had clowns, acrobats, animals, and many exciting acts, but Raja still looked sad. Then Malika, a beautiful tigress, appeared. Raja's face lit up, and Jasmine understood that he loved Malika. When Malika went backstage, Raja became sad again. Jasmine tried to help him with favorite meals, a new bed, and tiger friends, but nothing worked. The circus owner later arrived with Malika. He explained that Malika would not eat, sleep, or perform because she loved Raja. He gave Malika to Jasmine so the tigers could be together. Jasmine then helped the owner by moving the circus to a park near the palace. A royal ball celebrated the new circus, and everyone was happy.

Jasmine noticed that Raja was unhappy after seeing a circus in town. She and Aladdin brought him to the show, hoping he would enjoy it. Raja watched the clowns, acrobats, and animals, but he stayed solemn. When Malika, the circus's beautiful tigress, came out, Raja became bright and happy. Jasmine tried to bring Malika to the palace, but the owner said Malika was needed for the circus. Raja returned home sadly, and Jasmine tried many ways to cheer him. None of them helped. Then the owner came to the palace with Malika. Malika was also sad and would not eat, sleep, or perform. The owner understood that she loved Raja, so he gave her to Jasmine. Raja and Malika were reunited and touched noses. Jasmine realized the owner needed help, so she moved the circus to a park beside the palace. The circus stayed there, and everyone celebrated together.

video_title: DC Super Friends: Monster Madness | #ReadAlong | @dckids

summaries.summary: Metropolis held a Halloween costume party to thank the Super Friends. The heroes came dressed as themselves, and everyone was happy. Then Scarecrow came from the shadows. He opened his jack-o-lantern and filled the room with strange fog. The guests began to act like the monsters on their costumes. A vampire tried to bite Batman. Batman used his bat rope to pull the vampire away. A werewolf chased Green Lantern, so Green Lantern caught it in a net. A strong zombie came toward Superman. Superman cut down ghost decorations, and the zombie became tangled in the sheets and ropes. Other heroes fought the pirates, witch, and black cat. Batman saw that some guests were still people. He put popcorn on Scarecrow. Two giant crows wanted the popcorn and chased Scarecrow into the night. Batman said everyone would be safe, and the gas would wear off by midnight.

On Halloween night, the people of Metropolis had a big party for the Super Friends. Scarecrow did not like the heroes, so he released mind-bending gas from his jack-o-lantern. The gas made party guests act like monsters. The werewolf howled, the zombie moved slowly, the vampire showed his fangs, and pirates and a witch attacked. Batman told the heroes not to hurt the guests. He pulled the vampire away with a rope. Green Lantern caught the werewolf in a green net. Superman used his heat vision to drop ghost decorations around the zombie, trapping it in sheets and ropes. Cyborg and Aquaman fought too. Robin was chased by a black cat with sharp claws. Batman then used popcorn to make Scarecrow interesting to two human-sized crows. The crows chased Scarecrow away. Batman said the guests would be safe, and the gas would stop working by midnight.

The Super Friends went to a costume party in Metropolis. They were there because the city wanted to thank them for saving everyone many times. Scarecrow secretly came to the party and made a foul fog. His gas made people behave like the costumes they wore. The guests became a werewolf, zombie, vampire, pirates, a witch, and a dangerous cat. The Super Friends worked carefully to stop them without hurting them. Batman lassoed the vampire. Green Lantern caught the werewolf in a dog catcher's net. Superman trapped the zombie in fallen decorations. Cyborg and Aquaman fought the pirates and witch, while Robin escaped the cat. Batman then found a clever way to stop Scarecrow. He covered Scarecrow with popcorn. Two large crows saw the food and chased him away. Batman said the people would be safe and the gas would wear off before midnight.

video_title: Batman: Birds of A Feather | #ReadAlong | @dckids

summaries.summary: Valuable things disappeared from homes in Gotham City. Batman found a bird feather at every crime scene, so he studied the clues with Bruce Wayne. Alfred showed him a report saying that birds were acting strangely, and some were missing. Then Batman and Alfred saw a vulture flying away with an umbrella full of valuables, including Batman's cell phone. The phone had a tracker, so Batman followed the birds to a skyscraper. The birds carried stolen things into the Penguin's Iceberg Lounge. The Penguin had trained them to steal and made them attack Batman. Batman turned on a fire alarm, and cold sprinklers freed the birds from the Penguin's control. The birds flew away. The Penguin tried to escape in a rocket umbrella, but Batman threw a freeze capsule and covered him with frost. Commissioner Gordon and the police arrested the Penguin because Batman had found evidence.

Batman was investigating many robberies in Gotham City. At each home, he found a bird feather. Bruce Wayne learned that birds were not acting normally, and some had gone missing. Soon, a large vulture flew away with an umbrella filled with stolen treasures. It had also taken Bruce Wayne's cell phone, but the phone had a tracking device. Batman followed the signal and saw many birds flying around a skyscraper. They carried umbrellas full of stolen items into the Iceberg Lounge, where the Penguin was waiting. The Penguin whistled, and his trained birds attacked Batman. Batman used a Batarang to start the sprinklers. The cold water surprised the birds and broke the Penguin's control over them. They flew out through the skylight. The Penguin tried to fly away in a rocket umbrella, but Batman used a freeze capsule to put him on ice. The police arrived and took the Penguin to jail.

People in Gotham City were losing valuable belongings, and Batman noticed a bird feather at every crime scene. He and Alfred discovered that city birds were behaving strangely. A vulture then flew away with stolen goods and Batman's phone. Because the phone had a tracker, Batman followed the bird from the Batplane. He found many birds carrying umbrellas full of stolen things to the Penguin's hideout. The Penguin laughed and said he had trained the birds to help him. He whistled, and they attacked Batman. Batman did not hurt the birds. Instead, he set off a fire alarm, and sprinklers sprayed them with cold water. The birds became free and flew away through a skylight. The Penguin escaped briefly in a rocket umbrella. Batman threw a freeze capsule and covered him with frost. Commissioner Gordon and the police arrived, found the Penguin frozen, and took him away with enough evidence for a long jail stay.

video_title: Jangles - A Big Fish Story by David Shannon

summaries.summary: Jangles is a giant trout who lives in Big Lake. His crooked jaw is covered with shiny lures and rusty hooks, so they clink when he swims. People try many ways to catch him, but he is too smart and strong. When the narrator is a child, an anchor comes loose while he fishes, and his boat drifts into the dark middle of the lake. He reels in an old fishing rod, then hears Jangles and is pulled into the water. Jangles takes him to an underwater cave and tells him wonderful stories. On the way back, the child tricks Jangles and ties him upside down. Jangles asks to be freed and says he is more than a fish—he is a storyteller. The child realizes doing what is right matters more than proving the catch, so he lets Jangles go. Later, Dad gives him a tackle box full of hooks and lures as proof of the amazing adventure.

A father tells his child about Jangles, the biggest fish anyone had seen or heard. Jangles has many hooks and lures on his huge jaw, and they make a jingling sound. He can eat eagles and beavers, but people say he once gently rescued a baby from a tipped canoe. Many fishermen want to catch him, yet every trick fails. One day, the narrator drifts into the middle of Big Lake while fishing. A line pulls, but it brings up an old fishing rod. When the narrator reels again, Jangles appears and drags the boat and child into the lake. The child can breathe underwater and visits Jangles’s cave. There, Jangles tells stories about the earth, trees, animals, and ancient fish. The child later turns Jangles upside down and catches him. Jangles asks to be released, and the child decides that doing what is right is more important than keeping the fish.

When Big Lake becomes smooth and misty, someone might glimpse Jangles, a legendary giant trout. The narrator remembers Dad telling the story beside a fireplace. Jangles is covered with old fishing hooks and lures, and everyone wants to catch him for prize money. Fishermen use turkeys, tuna, and even dynamite, but Jangles escapes. Years later, the narrator fishes near a creek, drifts far from shore, and catches an old fishing rod on the line. A jingling sound grows louder, and Jangles pulls the narrator into the lake. Instead of hurting the child, Jangles brings the child to his cave and shares amazing stories. When they return to the surface, the narrator uses the old fishing line to turn Jangles upside down. Jangles says the narrator has tricked him and asks whether proving the catch is more important than doing right. The narrator says no, frees Jangles, and receives Dad’s hook-filled tackle box as proof of the secret story.

video_title: Some Pets | A fun story about animals

summaries.summary: Some pets sit and stay. Some pets fetch, and some pets play. The story asks what a pet likes to do. Pets can slither, bound, and scurry round and round. They can squeal, squawk, squeak, and talk. Some pets pick and nibble. Some pets drool on their kibble. Some pets squeeze, nuzzle, lick, and cuddle. Pets can look different. They may be fluffy, feather, crawly, cute, silly, strange, scaly, big, small, or a blend. Even though pets are different, some pets can be someone’s best friend. The story asks whether your pet is your best friend. Then the speaker says that their pet was their best friend and that he was the best.

The story begins by showing that pets do many things. Some pets sit and stay, while others fetch and play. It asks, “Do you have a pet?” and asks what that pet likes to do. Different pets move in different ways. Some slither, some bound, and some scurry round and round. Pets also make different sounds. They may squeal, squawk, squeak, or talk. Some pets pick, nibble, drool on their kibble, squeeze, nuzzle, lick, or cuddle. Pets may be fluffy, feather, crawly, cute, silly, strange, scaly, big, small, or a blend. All these differences are part of the story. It says that some pets can be someone’s best friend. At the end, the speaker says, “My pet was my best friend. He was the best.”

Pets can sit, stay, fetch, and play. The story invites us to think about a pet and what that pet likes to do. One pet may slither, another may bound, and another may scurry round and round. Pets can also squeal, squawk, squeak, or talk. Some pick and nibble. Some drool on their kibble. Some squeeze, nuzzle, lick, and cuddle. Pets come in many forms. They can be fluffy, feather, crawly, cute, silly, strange, scaly, big, small, or a blend. The story asks if a pet is your best friend. It then tells about a pet that was the speaker’s best friend. The speaker says that this pet was the best. The beginning shows many pet actions, the middle describes their movements, sounds, and looks, and the ending shares the special friendship between a pet and its person.

video_title: A Charlie Brown Christmas~ A Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Charlie Brown feels sad even though Christmas is coming. He talks to Lucy, and she asks him to direct the Christmas play. Charlie Brown sees Snoopy decorating his doghouse for a contest, and Sally asks him to help write a letter to Santa. At the play rehearsal, nobody listens because everyone wants to dance. Charlie Brown chooses a tiny green tree for the play, but the children laugh at it. Linus then tells everyone about the shepherds, the angel, and the birth of Christ. Charlie Brown understands that Christmas is not about greed. He takes the tree outside and tries to decorate it, but a heavy ornament makes it fall over. After Charlie Brown leaves, Linus and the other children decorate the little tree. When Charlie Brown returns, the tree is beautiful. His friends wish him Merry Christmas and sing carols with him. Charlie Brown feels happy and expects the best Christmas ever.

Christmas is near, but Charlie Brown does not feel joyful. Lucy tells him to help with a Christmas play, so he becomes the director. Snoopy is busy decorating his doghouse, and Sally wants money from Santa. At rehearsal, the actors dance and ignore Charlie Brown. Lucy says they need a big aluminum tree, but Charlie Brown and Linus find a small, scrawny green tree instead. Charlie Brown brings it back because he thinks it needs a home. The children laugh at the little tree, and Charlie Brown asks what Christmas is about. Linus answers by telling the Christmas story about shepherds, an angel, and a Savior. Charlie Brown feels happy and decides to care for the tree. A red ornament makes the tree fall, so he walks away sadly. Linus and the other children give the tree love and decorate it with Snoopy's decorations. The tree becomes beautiful, and Charlie Brown sings with his friends.

Charlie Brown is unhappy during the Christmas season. Lucy gives him a job directing the Christmas play. He notices that Snoopy wants to win a prize for his decorated doghouse, and Sally asks for help writing to Santa. The play rehearsal goes badly because the children do not listen. Charlie Brown brings a tiny green tree instead of the large aluminum tree Lucy wanted. Everyone laughs, and Charlie Brown feels that he has failed. Linus explains Christmas by speaking about shepherds, angels, and the birth of Christ. Charlie Brown learns that Christmas should not be spoiled by greed. He carries the little tree outside and puts a red ornament on it, but the ornament makes the tree topple over. Linus and the other children find the tree and decide it needs love. They move decorations from Snoopy's doghouse onto the tree. Soon it looks magical. Charlie Brown returns, sees the beautiful tree, and joins his friends as they sing Christmas carols.

video_title: I am Stronger than Anger | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Little Nick went to the zoo with his parents and saw a koala. He wanted to take the koala home, but his mother said no because the koala had a mother and father who would be sad. Nick stomped, shouted, and felt very angry. A monkey told him to take deep breaths and blow slowly. Nick tried, but he still felt upset. The monkey suggested counting to ten, and a kangaroo suggested exercising by jumping, doing sit-ups, or squats. Then Nick met a parrot who explained that people can handle anger by counting, talking, or writing an apology letter. Nick thought carefully and understood that the koala was wild and should stay with its family. He breathed, counted, and exercised again. Then he apologized to his mother. She was proud, hugged him, and offered to buy him a new toy. The story says to express anger safely so it does not hurt others or ruin their day.

On a sunny day, Little Nick visited the zoo with his parents. He saw a koala in a tree and asked his mother if he could have it. She explained that the koala belonged with its mother and father, but Nick did not like her answer. He stomped and shouted until his heart beat hard, his throat tightened, and tears filled his eyes. A monkey taught Nick to breathe slowly and count to ten. A kangaroo showed him that exercise could help anger fade. Nick then heard a parrot talking about anger. The parrot said that counting, speaking with someone, or writing an apology could help. Nick thought about the koala and realized his mother was right. The koala was a wild animal and needed to be left alone. Nick took breaths, counted, and exercised. When he felt calm, he told his mother he was sorry. She hugged him, kissed him, and said she would buy him a new toy instead. The story teaches safe ways to handle anger.

Little Nick was excited to see a koala at the zoo. He wanted the koala for himself, but his mother said no because the koala had a family. Nick became furious. He shouted and felt anger in his body, with a fast heartbeat, tight throat, and tears. The monkey told him to take a deep breath and slowly let the air out. Nick practiced breathing and counting to ten. He was still a little sad, so a kangaroo told him to exercise. Nick jumped and exercised, and his anger began to fade. A parrot then shared more ways to deal with anger, such as counting leaves, talking to someone, or writing an apology letter. Nick thought about what had happened. He understood that the koala was a wild creature and that his mother had been right. After breathing, counting, and exercising again, Nick went to his mother and said he was sorry. His mother saw that he was calm and felt proud. She hugged and kissed him, then offered a new toy. Anger should be expressed safely.

video_title: Ninja Red Riding Hood by Corey Rosen Schwartz

summaries.summary: A hungry wolf could not catch food, and his belly ached for bacon. Huffing and puffing did not help, so he went to ninja school. He practiced katas and learned many moves. Soon he met Red Riding Hood, who was carrying a treat to her grandmother. The wolf sent her to pick blossoms and hurried to Grandma’s house. He put on her robe and waited in bed. Red noticed that Grandma’s eyes, ears, muscles, and teeth looked strange. The wolf jumped up to eat her, but Red had also learned ninja skills. They grappled and fought until they were evenly matched. Then Grandma arrived from taichi. Red dodged the wolf, threw him over her hip, and held him down. The wolf promised to give up red meat. Red and the wolf bowed, and Grandma shared peach pie. Later, the wolf tried yoga and felt peaceful.

A wolf was growing hungry because he could not catch any prey. He decided to train as a ninja, practicing katas and learning to whirl, flip, and jump. In the woods, he met Red Riding Hood, who was taking a treat to her grandmother. The wolf told Red to pick flowers while he went to Grandma’s house. Since Grandma was away, he wore her robe and waited for Red. Red asked why Grandma had such big eyes, long ears, huge muscles, and sharp teeth. The wolf said they were useful for seeing, hearing, hugging, and chewing. He tried to gobble Red, but she had attended ninja school too. Red escaped his grabs and fought back. Grandma came home from taichi, and Red threw the wolf onto his back. She made him promise to stop eating red meat. Grandma gave him peach pie, and the wolf chose yoga to calm his stress and find peace.

A wolf wanted a good meal, but he kept failing to catch prey. He went to school and became a trained ninja. When he saw Red Riding Hood, he made a plan to reach her grandmother first. He wore Grandma’s robe and waited in her bed. Red soon saw that the pretend Grandma looked unusual. The wolf explained that the big eyes, long ears, large muscles, and sharp teeth would help him see, hear, hug, and chew. Then he leaped out to eat Red. Red was ready because she had gone to ninja school as well. The two fighters grappled, twisted, and blocked each other. Grandma arrived, and Red protected her. Red dodged the wolf’s swing, lifted him over her hip, and put him on his back. The wolf promised that his days of eating meat were finished. Grandma shared her peach pie, and the wolf began yoga, which helped him feel calm and peaceful.

video_title: Appa Reads: Bluey - The Creek

summaries.summary: Blue is bored at the playground because she has played on everything twice. McKenzie suggests going to the creek, and Dad takes the children there. Blue is unsure because the creek has thorns, spiders, leeches, uneven ground, and slippery rocks. Dad and Bingo show them how to hop across the water. Blue tries it and begins to get the hang of the creek. Dad says the creek is an adventure, and he remembers playing there when he was young. At first, Blue does not know what to play. Then a dragonfly flies by, and Blue skips stones, makes boats, and builds dams. She decides the creek is fun. The children play Daddy Day Spa with mud. Blue goes to get more mud and sees a Podaroo. Then the gang goes home. Blue knows that McKenzie and Bingo were right: the creek is beautiful.

Blue has nothing new to do at the playground, so McKenzie suggests a trip to the creek. Dad takes the children down the slope. Blue is nervous because the creek is not like the playground. It has thorns, spiders, leeches, uneven ground, and rocks that can be pointy, wobbly, or slippery. McKenzie and Bingo think the creek is beautiful. Dad shows the children the place where he played as a kid, and they hop from rock to rock. Blue crosses the water and starts to feel more comfortable. Dad calls the creek an adventure. Blue wonders what to play, but then a dragonfly passes by. She skips stones, makes boats, and builds dams. Soon, Blue thinks the creek is fun. The children use mud for a Daddy Day Spa and put a mud pack on Dad. While getting more mud, Blue sees a Podaroo. The gang goes home, and Blue knows the creek is beautiful.

Blue is bored with the playground, but McKenzie has a new idea: visit the creek. Dad carries Bingo and takes the children there. Blue stays back because she does not know what the creek will be like. The path is sloping and uneven, and the creek has thorns, spiders, leeches, and slippery green rocks. Dad and Bingo lead the way across the water. Blue tries the rock hopping and hears Dad say she made it. Dad says the creek is an adventure and remembers visiting it when he was young. Blue still does not know what to play. Then she sees a dragonfly and begins skipping stones, making boats, and building dams. The creek becomes fun for her. The children play Daddy Day Spa and cover Dad with mud. Blue goes for more mud and finds a Podaroo, which looks at her and runs away. When the gang goes home, Blue knows the creek is beautiful after all.

video_title: Even Superheroes Have Bad Days by Shelly Becker

summaries.summary: When superheroes have a bad day, they may feel sad or angry. They could kick, punch, shout, crush crates, bend gates, throw trucks, knock down buildings, start forest fires, or flatten the town’s tires. But they have other choices. They can hike or go mountain biking to let their angry steam out. They can rescue people, do good deeds, build fun theme parks, catch bad guys, and tame scary beasts. Even when they feel upset again, they could make blizzards, twisters, sticky webs, or trouble for the whole world. Real superheroes do not choose to rampage. They look into their strong hearts and fight the urge to hurt others. They notice their sorrow, anger, and pain while they wait for those feelings to pass. They may frown, sigh, slump, or cry. Then they get up and continue saving the world in their own super way.

The story shows that superheroes can have sad, mad, and difficult days too. With their great powers, they could make a terrible mess by pounding things, throwing buses, breaking buildings, starting fires, or damaging the town. They could also make icy storms, huge twisters, sticky webs, or even change the planet’s time. Instead, upset superheroes can choose helpful actions. They can move fast outdoors, rescue people, do kind deeds, build places for laughter, catch wanted bad guys, and tame dangerous beasts. Sometimes they still feel tempted to cause a bad scene. However, real superheroes do not rampage. They find the strong powers in their hearts and use their talents as heroes. They let themselves feel sorrow, anger, and pain. They can frown, sigh, slump, or cry while the big feelings pass. Then they stand up and spend the day saving the world.

A superhero’s powers could be used for destruction during a bad day. A sad or angry superhero might shout, crush crates, bend gates, throw vehicles, knock down buildings, or use laser eyes and boomerangs to hurt the world. But superheroes have better choices. They can hike, bike through outer space, rescue people, perform good deeds, build joyful theme parks, catch bad guys, and turn scary beasts into safe ones. Even so, a displeased superhero might want to make blizzards, typhoons, sticky webs, or worldwide trouble. The superheroes remember that real heroes do not choose a super rampage. They use the strength in their hearts and battle the urge to do harm. They accept their sadness, anger, and pain. It is all right to frown, sigh, slump, or cry. After the feelings begin to pass, they get up, continue their day, and save the world in a super way.

video_title: 👧🏻 The Girl Who Thought in Pictures: The Story of Dr. Temple Grandin (Amazing Scientists)

summaries.summary: Temple Grandin was a girl who experienced the world differently. Loud sounds, crowded places, tags on clothes, and hugs upset her. She did not speak until she was three, and some people wrongly thought she should be sent away. Her mother believed in her and found teachers who helped her. Temple was teased at school and was eventually sent to stay with her aunt on a ranch. There, she felt comfortable around cows and realized that she thought in pictures, just as she imagined the cows did. A teacher helped her discover her love of science. Temple built a machine that used boards to give a comforting squeeze. Later, she studied animals and designed better, kinder farm equipment. Her ideas changed many farms. Temple became a speaker who told people that every person is special and that being different can help someone do important things.

When Temple Grandin was born in Boston, she was unusual from the beginning. She loved spinning objects but disliked loud noises, busy places, uncomfortable clothes, and hugs. Temple had strong tantrums and did not speak until she was three. Her mother refused to give up on her, and teachers helped her learn to talk. Temple was diagnosed with autism. School was difficult because children teased her, and she was expelled after throwing a book. Her mother sent her to a ranch, where Temple found peace with the cows and began thinking about pictures in her mind. At a new school, a teacher encouraged her interest in science. Temple built a squeeze machine and then studied animal science. She designed systems that made farms kinder for animals. Even when people ignored her ideas, she kept learning and working. Temple became famous for her inventions and speeches, teaching that different minds can give the world valuable ideas.

Temple Grandin often felt different from other children. Bright places, loud sounds, scratchy clothing, and hugs were hard for her, and she had trouble speaking and controlling her frustration. Some people believed she could never be normal, but her mother said Temple should not be sent away. With special teachers, Temple learned to talk. After children bullied her at school, she visited her aunt’s ranch. The farm was calmer, and Temple loved watching the gentle cows. She thought that she and the cows understood the world through pictures. A teacher later helped Temple see that science was one of her strengths. She remembered a farm machine and built her own squeeze machine with boards. Temple studied animal science and created designs that helped farms treat animals better. Her work changed people’s minds and brought her honors. As an adult, she became a speaker and encouraged everyone to value their unique minds, stand tall, and follow their strengths.

video_title: Mr. MEN - A Christmas Pantomine by Roger Hargreaves. Children's audiobook (read-aloud).

summaries.summary: Little Miss Trouble likes to cause trouble at Christmas. She takes Little Miss Neat’s cake and blames Mr. Greedy. She tricks Little Miss Splendid and sends Mr. Chatterbox a giant gobstopper. At the auditions for the Christmas pantomime, Little Miss Bossy refuses to give her a part because she expects trouble. Little Miss Trouble goes home and says she will show Little Miss Bossy trouble. During rehearsals, many things go wrong. Itching powder bothers Widow Twanky, an egg goes into the wizard’s slipper, the lamp lid is stuck, and a mouse scares Aladdin. Little Miss Bossy knows who caused the disaster. She lets Little Miss Trouble join the pantomime. On opening night, Little Miss Trouble arrives early and hides inside the pantomime horse. When the cast looks for her, a muffled voice comes from the horse, and Little Miss Stubborn tells her to keep still.

Before the Christmas pantomime, Little Miss Trouble plays tricks on everyone. She steals a piece of cake, makes people blame one another, and sends Mr. Chatterbox a very large gobstopper. Little Miss Bossy does not give her a role in Aladdin because she thinks Little Miss Trouble will cause trouble. Other friends get the parts, but rehearsals become a mess. Someone puts itching powder in Widow Twanky’s wig, tricks the princess, puts an egg in the wizard’s slipper, shuts the genie inside the lamp, and puts a mouse in Aladdin’s cave. Little Miss Bossy knows Little Miss Trouble is responsible, so she visits her house and offers her a part. Little Miss Trouble is very excited on opening night. She comes early to see her costume. Then Little Miss Bossy asks where she is. The cast hears a muffled answer from inside the pantomime horse. Little Miss Trouble has found a surprising part.

Little Miss Trouble causes many Christmas problems. She pinches Little Miss Neat’s cake and blames Mr. Greedy. She also makes Little Miss Splendid unhappy and gives Mr. Chatterbox a gobstopper while pretending it is a present. Because of her tricks, Little Miss Bossy says she cannot be in the pantomime. But after rehearsals begin, the show becomes a disaster. The princess is upset, the evil wizard has an egg in his slipper, the magic lamp will not open, and a mouse frightens Aladdin. Little Miss Bossy understands that Little Miss Trouble has caused all the problems. She changes her mind and tells Little Miss Trouble to come on opening night for a part. Little Miss Trouble is thrilled and arrives early. When everyone gathers before the show, they cannot see her. Little Miss Bossy smiles, and a muffled voice answers from the back of the pantomime horse. Little Miss Trouble is hiding inside it.

video_title: It's OK to be Different by Sharon Purtill. Children's audiobook about diversity and kindness 💕

summaries.summary: This story says that every child is different. Some children like swimming, hiking, dancing, or riding bikes. Some like blue, yellow, or pink. Some build block towers, and some wear different colored socks. Children can have different hair, skin, heights, and sizes. Some are good at science and math, while others enjoy sports, music, instruments, or singing. Some children wear glasses, speak with an accent, or use a chair, ramp, crutches, a wheelchair, or a sling. The story says that these differences are part of each person. It is never okay to make fun of someone because of how they look, act, or sound. Every child is an individual, just like you. The story reminds children to be kind to people who are different, because everyone is different from someone else. It is okay to be different, and it is okay to be yourself.

The story explains that no two children have to be exactly alike. One child may love to swim, while another likes hiking. One may dance, and another may ride a bike. Children may choose different favorite colors, build with blocks, or wear colorful socks. They may have light or dark hair and skin, and they may be big, small, short, or tall. Children also have different talents. Some like science and math, while others choose sports, music, instruments, or singing. Some children need glasses, use a chair and ramp, or have crutches, wheelchairs, or slings. The story clearly says not to laugh at these things. Although children may look, act, or sound different, each one is an individual. The ending reminds us to be kind to people who are different from us. Everyone is different from someone else, so every child can be themselves.

A child in this story learns that people can be different in many ways. Children enjoy different activities, such as swimming, hiking, dancing, biking, building towers, playing sports, or making music. They may like different colors and have different kinds of hair, skin, bodies, and heights. Some children are good at school subjects, some play instruments, and some sing. Other children wear glasses, speak with an accent, or use a chair, ramp, stairs, crutches, a wheelchair, or a sling. These differences do not make anyone less important. The story says that it is never okay to make fun of a person’s differences. Even when children do not look, act, or sound alike, every child is an individual. The story ends with a kind reminder: be kind to people who are different from you, because you are different to them too. It is okay to be different, and it is okay to be you.

video_title: Monsters University Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

The cabin is full of children, but they do not fear Mike. Mike fears them. Sulley finds him, and they work together because Sulley is scary and Mike is smart. Mike coaches Sulley. video_title: TAD and DAD by-David Ezra Stein, READ ALOUD!                @Children-12j #storytime

summaries.summary: Tad loves his dad, who has big eyes, strong legs, a huge mouth, and a loud song. Tad swims with Dad and sleeps in Dad’s bed because he does not want Dad to miss him. Tad dreams of being like Dad. First, Tad grows legs and hops. Then he grows a big mouth and sings. Later, Tad grows very big and shares a feast with Dad. At night, Dad tells Tad that wiggling, poking, kicking, and croaking keep him awake. Tad says sorry and swims away to sleep alone. Dad is happy for a moment, but then Tad hears a loud splash. Dad cannot sleep without him. Tad comes back to give Dad company. Soon Dad falls asleep, and Tad knows Dad missed him. They say good night until they meet again. Tad and Dad love being together, even at bedtime.

A little tad swims everywhere with his dad. Dad has buggy eyes, strong legs, a huge mouth, and a loud burp-like song. Tad loves Dad very much and follows him into bed each night. Tad dreams that he can swim like Dad. Then Tad grows legs and learns to hop. He dreams of jumping like Dad and grows a big mouth so he can sing. The pond becomes full of music from Tad and Dad. Later, Tad grows big and hungry, and they enjoy a feast together. One night, Dad says Tad’s wiggling, poking, kicking, and croaking stop him from sleeping. Tad leaves the bed and swims away. Dad says, “Peace at last,” but soon Dad is the one making a loud ruckus. Tad sees that Dad cannot sleep alone. Tad returns to keep him company, and Dad quickly falls asleep.

Tad wants to be close to Dad all the time. He swims beside Dad, sleeps in Dad’s bed, and dreams of growing just like him. Tad grows legs for hopping, a big mouth for singing, and a large body that makes him very hungry. He and Dad sing together in the pond and eat a feast. At bedtime, Dad explains that Tad moves and makes sounds all night, so Dad cannot sleep. Tad feels sorry and decides to sleep somewhere else. For the first time, Tad swims away from Dad. Dad thinks he can finally rest, but the quiet does not last. Soon, Tad hears someone splashing and making a big noise. It is Dad, who is wiggling, poking, kicking, and croaking. Dad still cannot sleep. Tad says Dad needs company and comes back. Dad feels better and falls asleep. Tad knows Dad missed him.

video_title: Pirate Boy by Eve Bunting

summaries.summary: Dany and his mom finish reading a book about a pirate boy. Dany wonders what would happen if he became a pirate and sailed away. His mom says she would be sad, but she would still come to help him. If Dany wanted to come home, a friendly dolphin could take them to the pirate ship. If sea monsters came, Mom would use magic spray to make them as small as Dany’s goldfish. If the pirates tried to keep Dany, Mom would spray them until they were no bigger than bugs. Dany asks how they would get home, and Mom says they could sail the ship to Summer Beach and then run home. The pirates could use the magic spray to become big again and sail away. Dany and Mom plan to play on the beach, tell Daddy everything, and share cookies. Dany gives Mom the biggest cookie because she is very brave. He knows she would even come get him from the moon.

After reading Pirate Boy, Dany asks his mom many questions about sailing away on a pirate ship. Mom tells him she would be sad, but she would always come after him. A friendly dolphin might carry them to the ship. If no dolphin came, Mom would swim. If sea monsters tried to eat them, her magic spray would make the monsters tiny, like Dany’s goldfish. If the pirates were bigger than Mom or wanted Dany to stay, she would spray them until they were as small as bugs. Mom says she made the spray that day and keeps it in a bottle. They could take the pirate ship to Summer Beach, play with shells and sea pebbles, and build a sand castle. The pirates were not really bad, so Mom would leave the spray for them to grow big again and sail away. At home, Dany could tell Daddy the adventure while everyone ate cookies and milk.

Dany imagines being a pirate and leaving home on a ship. His mom listens and promises to bring him back if he does not like it. She would find a friendly dolphin, swim to the ship if needed, and use magic spray on any sea monsters. The spray would make them smaller and smaller. Mom would also use it if the pirates were too big or did not want Dany to leave. When Dany asks about getting home, Mom says they could take over the ship and sail to Summer Beach. Dany wants to be captain, and they decide they would leave the ship and run home. Mom says the pirates could use the magic spray to become big again because they were not really bad. Before going home, Dany and Mom would find shells, sea pebbles, and make a sand castle. Daddy would hear the story, and everyone would have cookies and milk. Dany gives Mom the biggest cookie and asks if she would get him from the moon too. She says yes.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑇ℎ𝑒 𝑈𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑏𝑙𝑒𝑠 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Kiana Roubini arrives at Greenwich Middle School after moving from California. Her baby brother, Chauncey, cries during the drive and then throws up in the car, so Kiana's stepmother, Louise, leaves to take him to a pediatrician. Kiana waits alone and misses registration. While she is outside, Parker, a fourteen-year-old farmer with a provisional license, nearly hits her with his pickup truck and damages her backpack. Parker's schedule gets mixed up with Kiana's papers, and the secretary accidentally sends Kiana to Room 117. Kiana discovers that Room 117 belongs to the SCS8 class, known as the Unteachables. She expects ordinary students but finds children roasting marshmallows over a fire in a wastebasket. In the second chapter, Mr. Kermit learns that he must teach the Unteachables. He believes the superintendent is trying to make him quit before early retirement because of an old cheating scandal. When he enters Room 117, he finds even more chaos, but he puts out the fire with his coffee and introduces himself as their teacher.

On her first day at a new school, Kiana is left waiting when Louise drives home with baby Chauncey after he vomits in the SUV. Kiana is already unhappy about living temporarily in Greenwich while her mother works on a film. Then Parker arrives in a rusty pickup, nearly runs her over, and tears a hole in her backpack. He explains that his provisional license lets him drive for his family farm. When Louise sends a message saying she is taking Chauncey to the pediatrician, Kiana tries to register alone. The secretary gives her Parker's schedule by mistake and directs her to Room 117. Kiana learns that the room holds the school's “Unteachables,” students placed in a special class because adults have given up on them. She enters and sees students making a fire and roasting marshmallows. Meanwhile, Mr. Kermit is assigned to teach the class. Angry about the assignment and an old cheating scandal, he decides not to resign. He enters Room 117, extinguishes the fire with his coffee, and announces that he is their teacher.

Kiana begins school in Greenwich under confusing circumstances. Her stepmother, Louise, is delayed after Chauncey becomes sick, leaving Kiana without an adult to register her. Outside the school, Parker's pickup truck almost strikes Kiana, and its mirror destroys her backpack. Parker says he is fourteen and has a provisional license because he helps his family farm. Kiana later receives his schedule and follows it to Room 117 rather than waiting all day in the office. The schedule reveals that Parker belongs to the SCS8 class, which other students call the Unteachables. Kiana thinks the class must contain students who have been pushed aside, but she finds them setting a wastebasket on fire and cooking marshmallows. Mr. Kermit also arrives at the room after the superintendent assigns him the class. He remembers how an earlier cheating scandal damaged his career and suspects the new assignment is meant to force him out before retirement. Instead, he accepts the challenge, puts out the fire, and greets the class.

video_title: The Nightmare Before Christmas by Tim Burton~ A Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Jack Skellington lives in Halloween Land, but he is tired of the same scares and wants something new. He finds a special door in the forest and enters Christmas Town. Jack loves the bright lights, toys, snow, and happy feeling. He takes Christmas things home and decides he can be Santa. Jack's friends help him take Santa, and they prepare a coffin sleigh. Fog covers the way, but Zero's glowing nose guides the sleigh. Jack gives children Halloween presents, such as spooky toys and a scary doll. The children and grown-ups are frightened, but Jack does not understand. They shoot at the sleigh, and Jack and Zero fall in a cemetery. Santa tells Jack that taking over Christmas was wrong, even though Jack meant well. Jack returns home sadly. Then Santa brings Christmas to Halloween Land.

In Halloween Land, Jack Skellington feels bored because everyone always scares people. His little ghost dog, Zero, stays near him, but Jack hardly notices. One night, Jack finds three wooden doors and opens the Christmas door. He discovers Christmas Town and sees many wonderful things. Jack brings Christmas decorations and gifts back to Halloween Land. He thinks he should become Santa and spread happiness. Jack's friends take Santa to Halloween Land, and Jack explains his plan to give the presents himself. On Christmas Eve, Zero helps guide Jack's coffin sleigh through the fog. Jack visits homes and leaves frightening gifts. He thinks the noise outside means people are celebrating, but it is really people trying to stop him. A missile brings down the sleigh. Santa finds Jack and explains that Christmas is not Jack's job. Jack learns that Halloween is the right place for him, and Santa brings Christmas to Halloween.

Jack Skellington is a tall skeleton who lives in Halloween Land. He wants more than graveyards, fright, and saying boo. After finding Christmas Town, Jack becomes excited by its lights, snow, toys, and presents. He takes these things back to his friends and decides to be Santa for one year. Jack and the Halloween creatures carry Santa away and prepare a strange sleigh. When thick fog blocks the journey, Zero flies in front and lights the way with his bright nose. Jack travels from house to house, leaving spooky presents for children. The children are scared, and people try to stop the sleigh with bullets and missiles. Jack and Zero fall in a cemetery. Jack feels sad because his plan failed. Santa tells him that he did not mean to cause trouble, but taking over Christmas was wrong. Jack goes home, and Santa brings Christmas to Halloween Land.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Ariel's Dolphin Adventure

Erik protected the baby from the waves and took him near some rocks where the water was calmer. Erik told King Triton that the wall was his fault. video_title: Cinco de Mouse O, kids book read along

video_title: Toy Story A Roaring Adventure (With Highlighted Words) Read Along: Cd Audio

video_title: Why we need teachers kids book read along

They help children understand birds, seasons, and other parts of the world. Even when classroom work is tough, teachers help children get through it. They can make hard ideas clearer and help children notice what they love and what they are good at. Teachers teach the heart as well as the brain. Their lessons about kindness and caring can guide children through every age and stage. They encourage children to help friends, understand different viewpoints, and care for one another. They make learning enjoyable with projects, art, and stories, and they help turn ideas into life. Teachers are examples for children, while coaches and swimming trainers teach in other ways. Since teachers give so much, children are encouraged to thank them and remember how much they helped them grow.

video_title: Freckle Face Strawberry Read Aloud

The makeup hides them, but it makes her hot and itchy, and her friends do not recognize where she is. At the playground, she meets a baby and talks with another person who has freckles. The person says some freckles may fade when she grows up. Soon, Freckleface Strawberry hears her friends calling for her and inviting her to play. She feels happy because she has many friends. When she grows up, her freckles do not disappear, but she does not care as much. She lives happily ever after, and a speck of dirt is mistaken for a freckle.

A little girl named Freckleface Strawberry is like other children in many ways. She is seven, short, and can ride a bike, but she has red hair and freckles. People make unkind comments about her freckles, so she wants them gone. She scrubs them, tries lemon juice, draws on herself with markers, and finally wears makeup to cover them. The makeup hides her freckles, but it also makes her hot and itchy. At school, even her friends cannot find her because they do not know she is the girl with freckles. After school, she sits alone at the playground. A baby laughs at her freckles, and someone tells her that freckles might fade while growing up. Then her friends call her name and ask her to play and meet a new girl. Freckleface Strawberry becomes joyful. Her freckles stay as she grows, but she no longer worries so much about them.

Freckleface Strawberry has a family, a red-haired head, and freckles covering her body. People often point out the freckles and say she looks dirty, like a giraffe, or like one big freckle. She feels unhappy and tries to make them disappear. Scrubbing, lemon juice, and markers do not work. Makeup hides the freckles, but it makes her uncomfortable, and her friends cannot recognize her. At the playground, she is lonely and sits in the shade. A baby laughs when she sees the freckles. Another person explains that freckles may become lighter after growing up, though Freckleface Strawberry does not know if that will happen. Then her friends find her and invite her to play. She is no longer sad, hot, or itchy, and she realizes that having many friends matters more to her than having many freckles. Her freckles remain when she grows up, but she still lives happily.

video_title: DINOSAUR LADY: The Daring Discoveries of Mary Anning, the First Paleontologist Read Aloud by Mrs. K

summaries.summary: Mary Anning searched the beaches and cliffs near her home in England for seashells and fossils. She wanted to understand the bones she found, so she read books, copied papers, drew pictures, and wrote many notes. One day, Mary and her brother found a huge head in the rock. Mary then searched for the rest of the creature. After a storm caused landslides, she found its ribs, backbone, and flippers. The skeleton was named ichthyosaurus, and people learned that it was millions of years old and belonged to a creature that had become extinct. Mary later discovered fossilized poop and fossils that held ink. When she was twenty-four, she found a flying reptile called a pterosaur. Women could not join scientific societies, but scientists came to Mary for help. Her discoveries helped create paleontology, the study of prehistoric life through fossils. Mary kept exploring and learning with her simple tools and great determination.

Mary Anning lived near the beach at Lime Regis, England, where she collected fossils to sell. She was curious about every bone and fossil, so she studied books and made careful drawings and notes. While exploring with her brother, Mary found a large eye socket in a cliff. They uncovered a giant head, and Mary searched for the body for almost a year. A storm exposed more of the cliff, allowing her to find ribs, vertebrae, and flippers. The creature was called ichthyosaurus. Scientists discovered that it had lived millions of years ago and that some creatures could become extinct. Mary also examined strange stones and correctly decided they were fossilized poop. Another fossil contained a substance that became ink when water was added, showing how ancient sea creatures hid from predators. She found a pterosaur too. Although women were not allowed in scientific groups, experts visited Mary because of her knowledge. Her work helped form paleontology.

Mary Anning bravely explored dangerous cliffs and beaches to find fossils. She wanted answers about the ancient creatures whose bones she discovered, so she taught herself by borrowing books, copying scientific papers, sketching fossils, and taking notes. Mary and her brother first uncovered the head of a strange animal. She kept searching until a storm caused landslides and revealed the creature's body. The skeleton had ribs, vertebrae, and flippers, and scientists named it ichthyosaurus. Its age showed that the earth was much older than many people believed, and its remains showed that a species could disappear. Mary continued making discoveries. She identified fossilized poop and found fossils containing ink from ancient aquatic creatures. At age twenty-four, she found a flying reptile called a pterosaur. Mary was not allowed to join London's Geological Society or attend classes, but scientists still came to her cottage with questions. Her discoveries helped establish paleontology, the study of prehistoric life through fossils.

video_title: Kids Books Read Aloud Story 📚 Son You Are A King by Tená V. Baker

A young boy faces teasing, unfair choices, unkind teachers, and doubt about his future. He wants to do his best, but he wonders why people make things so hard for him. Their card became a giant Valentine mouse. They gave it to Mrs. Mousley, and everyone cheered.

Clayton and Desmond started as friends who wanted to make a special Valentine for Mrs. Mousley. They worked together, but they disagreed about the hearts and glitter. Dr. De Soto was a careful mouse dentist with a sign saying that he would not treat dangerous animals. A fox with a very sore tooth came to his office and cried for help. A mouse named Dr. De Soto was a gentle dentist who treated large animals from a ladder. He usually kept away from foxes because they could hurt mice. One day, a crying fox came with a bad tooth. Dr. De Soto felt sorry for him and agreed to help. He pulled out the rotten tooth while Mrs. De Soto helped keep the fox's mouth open. The fox was already thinking about eating the dentists, even though they were helping him. Dr. De Soto and his wife decided to finish the job but also protect themselves. Harry believes he is not good at things, so he says, “I can’t,” even when he wants to join his friends. A special letter puzzle makes him think about those words. They read together, fed birds, played in the snow, and danced. Belle missed her father, so the Beast used a magic mirror to see him and let Belle leave. Gaston and the villagers attacked the castle. video_title: How Santa Got His Job

Santa wanted a job that kept him moving, so he tried several kinds of work. He cleaned chimneys, but no one believed him because he was never covered in soot. He worked at the post office, but his nighttime deliveries caused many complaints. At a diner, he tasted food before serving it and became very heavy. Santa's first jobs helped him discover what he was good at. He liked moving around, so he cleaned chimneys, delivered mail, cooked at a diner, watched animals, and performed in a circus. People could not see proof that he cleaned chimneys, nighttime mail deliveries upset the postmaster, tasting diner food made him gain weight, and jealous animals caused him to lose his zoo job. In the circus, Santa loved flying from a cannon so much that he could not pretend to be frightened. The ringmaster fired him and the reindeer. Nyasha and Manyara live in a village with their father, Mufaro. Manyara believes she should be queen and thinks Nyasha's kindness is weakness. Nyasha does not argue. They laugh at him, while his mother loves him just as he is. A boy teases Dumbo, and Mrs. Jumbo is locked in a cage. The elephants turn away from Dumbo, but Timothy the mouse stays with him. Timothy tries to make Dumbo important in an elephant pyramid. Dumbo trips, and the pyramid falls. Then Dumbo is made to be a clown. He is frightened when he drops from a burning building into sticky goo. Timothy brings Dumbo to his mother for a visit. Soon, crows help Dumbo learn that he can fly. Dumbo flies with his ears, even after he drops a feather. The crowds cheer for him. Dumbo becomes a star, and the ring Master frees his mother.

A baby elephant named Dumbo is born at a circus. His ears are much bigger than the other elephants' ears, and the elephants laugh. Dumbo's mother, Mrs. Jumbo, hugs him and loves him. After Mrs. Jumbo scares some teasing boys, she is put in a cage. Dumbo is left alone, and the other elephants blame him. Timothy the mouse promises to help. Dumbo tries to stand on an elephant pyramid, but his big ears make him fall and the pyramid crashes down. He is then dressed as a clown and dropped into a tub of goo. Timothy takes him to see his mother. Later, Dumbo and Timothy fall from a tree into a pond. A crow says Dumbo may have flown. With a feather, Dumbo learns to flap his ears and fly. At the circus, he flies over the crowd and everyone cheers. Dumbo becomes famous, and his mother is released to live with him.

video_title: Incredibles 2 Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

video_title: The Scariest Story You’ve Ever Heard | A rhyming, funny, scary story!

summaries.summary: During a dark, rainy night, two boys are in bed when the power suddenly goes out. They hear a creek, a crack, stomping, clanging, and loud bangs. They become frightened and hide under their blankets because they think a monster is coming to eat them. The sounds move toward the kitchen, and the boys become curious as well as scared. They go to the door with blankets over their heads. First they hear slurping and crunching, while the dog whimpers and barks. After a strange silence, the boys hear a shriek and a splatter. They leave their room and creep down the hall. When they enter the kitchen, they discover that the frightening intruder is not a monster. It is their dad, holding a spoon and eating. Their fear turns into laughter when Dad says he is sorry and explains that everything was for a bowl of delicious ice cream.

The story begins in a house during a storm. Thunder booms, rain pours, and the power goes out just before midnight. Two boys wake up and listen carefully. A creek becomes a crack, and then they hear frightening sounds. Their hearts beat quickly, so they hide beneath the covers. The sounds seem to belong to a monster that is coming closer. The mysterious visitor stomps, clangs, and knocks something onto the floor. The boys wonder what it wants and decide to look. They stand near the door with blankets over their heads. They hear slurping and crunching, and even the dog whimpers and barks. The boys think something terrible may have happened. Finally, they walk down the hall and find a man with a spoon. The man is their dad, not a monster. He is eating ice cream, and the boys laugh after he apologizes for scaring them.

Two brothers are frightened when a nighttime storm causes the electricity to go out. In the darkness, they hear many unusual noises: a creek, a crack, growling, clanging, stomping, and a bang. They imagine that an intruder or monster is in the house, and they hide under their blankets. Soon the sounds come from the kitchen. The brothers are still afraid, but they also want to know what is happening. They creep to the door and hear slurping and repeated crunching. Their dog whimpers and barks, which makes the scene seem even scarier. After a shriek and a splatter, the boys decide that hiding will not help. They creep into the room and discover a familiar man. Dad is holding a spoon and chewing. The frightening mystery ends when Dad says he is sorry for scaring them. The noises were caused by him eating a bowl of delicious ice cream.

video_title: Chicken little and  big bad wolf kids book read along

summaries.summary: Chicken Little thought there were only chickens nearby, but then something big, furry, and gray appeared. She believed it was the Big Bad Wolf and warned everyone to run. The chickens argued about whether to capture the wolf or escape. They tried to fly over a fence, even though chickens are not very good at flying. Chicken Little decided they needed facts, so she went to speak with the wolf. She asked if he was bad. The wolf said he tried to make good choices and did not eat meat. He was actually very nice, but the chickens were still afraid because of his name and appearance. Chicken Little learned that the wolf had left his pack because he did not want to eat other animals. The chickens welcomed him into their flock, and they became better together.

One day, Chicken Little saw a large, furry, gray animal and thought it was the Big Bad Wolf. She shouted for everyone to run. In the barnyard, the chickens quickly made plans. Some wanted to capture the wolf, while others wanted to escape. They tried to fly away, but Chicken Little told them to stop and look at the facts. Then she investigated the wolf herself. The wolf explained that he tried to make good choices and that he did not eat meat. Chicken Little saw that he was super nice. The other chickens were worried because they thought a wolf could not be trusted. Then they learned that the wolf had left his pack because he did not fit in and did not want to eat other animals. The chickens welcomed him, and he found a place with them.

Chicken Little heard about a Big Bad Wolf and became frightened. The chickens in the barnyard were frightened too. They talked about capturing the wolf or running away, but they could not agree on a plan. When they tried to fly over a fence, Chicken Little told them to slow down and look at the facts. She went to ask the wolf questions. The wolf said he was not bad, tried to make good choices, and was a vegetarian. He said that people were afraid of him even though he did not eat meat. The chickens discovered that he had left his old pack because he did not fit in. He wanted a place where he belonged. Chicken Little and the flock invited him to join them. They made veggie burgers and kale salad, and the wolf was welcomed into the flock.

video_title: Toy Story 🤠 Read Along Storybook 📖 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Emperor Zerg took Buzz’s special turbo suit. Buzz needed to bring it home, so he asked Woody and Rex to help him. They flew to Planet Zerg and saw many Zerg Bots. Woody and Rex kept the robots busy while Buzz looked for Emperor Zerg. Buzz met a Zerg Bot named Zeni. Zeni said he was different and wanted to sing. Zeni showed Buzz where the turbo suit was, but the Zerg Bots caught Buzz, Woody, and Rex. Zeni sang loudly. Falling rocks made a cage around Emperor Zerg. Zeni freed the friends. Buzz put on the turbo suit, and the four friends defeated the Zerg Bots. They locked up Zerg and flew away. Zeni taught the other robots to sing. Then Planet Zerg changed. Its dark caves and cliffs were replaced by flowers and trees. Planet Zerg became beautiful.

Buzz Lightyear went to Planet Zerg with Woody and Rex. Emperor Zerg had taken a very important turbo suit, and Buzz wanted to get it back. On the rocky planet, many Zerg Bots ran toward them. Woody and Rex fought the robots while Buzz searched for Zerg. Then Buzz met a little Zerg Bot named Zeni. Zeni said, “I want to sing.” Buzz was not sure he could trust him, but Zeni led Buzz to the cave with the turbo suit. The Zerg Bots caught the three friends. Emperor Zerg came out and thought he had won. Zeni began to sing. His loud song made the cave rocks fall around Zerg and hold him in a cage. Zeni freed Buzz, Woody, and Rex. Buzz put on the turbo suit, and they defeated the Zerg Bots. They took Zerg with them. Later, Zeni taught the robots to sing, and flowers and trees grew on Planet Zerg.

A special suit was missing, so Buzz, Woody, and Rex traveled in a spaceship to Planet Zerg. They found many Zerg Bots, but Woody and Rex fought them while Buzz went on. A Zerg Bot named Zeni followed Buzz. Zeni said he was not like the other robots and wanted to sing. He showed Buzz the cave where the turbo suit was hidden. Soon, Zerg Bots caught Buzz, Woody, and Rex, and Emperor Zerg appeared. Zeni sang to help them. His voice grew louder, and stalactites fell from the ceiling. The rocks made a cage around Zerg. Then Zeni freed Buzz, Woody, and Rex. Buzz climbed into the turbo suit, which made his Space Ranger powers greater. Buzz, Woody, Rex, and Zeni battled the Zerg Bots and won. They locked Zerg in the spaceship. Zeni stayed behind and taught the robots to sing. The dark planet changed, and flowers and trees began to grow. Planet Zerg became beautiful.

video_title: The Neighbors | A joyful celebration of wonder and curiosity.

summaries.summary: A child lives in a building that is seven stories high. Each floor has a different door and a surprising neighbor. Behind a red door with a wheel lives a family of acrobats who practice improving their act. On the fourth floor, the light goes out because a vampire lives there. The fifth door smells like pickled fish, and a pirate lives inside with his love. On the sixth floor, music fills the hall, and the musical family celebrates a birthday at least once a week. On the seventh floor, the child lives with their parents. The parents may seem boring, but the child loves them, and they love the child too.

video_title: Disney Mickey Mouse - Haunted Halloween 🎃 Read Along Story books for Kids 📚 Halloween Stories

summaries.summary: Mickey wants to have a Halloween party. He puts up a cobweb and makes popcorn balls. Then he goes up to the dark attic to find his old pirate costume. A storm begins. A white shape passes the window, and they think it is a ghost. Mickey comes downstairs with the skeleton. His friends scream because he looks like a monster. The lights come on, and they see Mickey. Mickey is getting ready for a Halloween party at his house. He decorates the living room and makes popcorn balls, but he still needs his costume. The skeleton is only a plastic decoration, so Mickey carries it downstairs. Outside, Donald, Goofy, Minnie, and Daisy arrive in heavy rain. They hurry into the house because their costumes might get soaked. The lights go out, and they hear thumps from upstairs. A strange white thing goes past the window, and Daisy calls it a ghost. Mickey comes down with his skeleton, and everyone screams. The lights return, showing that the scary monster is Mickey. Then Pluto comes through the doggy door. He is wet, so Mickey dries him with a towel. The friends call it the scariest Halloween ever.

video_title: DreamWorks Trolls Band Together kids book read along

video_title: 🐉 Me and My Dragon

summaries.summary: A child wishes for a dragon instead of a dog or cat. The child chooses a small fire-breathing dragon because a big dragon would not fit in the house. video_title: Go, Dog. Go!

video_title: The Night Before Mother's Day | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: The night before Mother’s Day, Dad quietly made a plan. He sent Mom outside for a jog with her friends. While she was gone, the children hurried into the kitchen. They mixed cake batter, made frosting, and created fancy cards with loving messages and a helpful coupon. The kitchen became messy, but Dad told Mom that nothing had happened when she returned. The children went to bed and waited for morning. On Mother’s Day, they gave Mom a bouquet and their cards. Mom was touched and loved their surprise. The family made a pretend spa in the kitchen. They served her coffee, rubbed her shoulders and feet, wrapped her hair in a towel, used a mud mask, and painted her nails. Then Mom dressed for a special brunch. Everyone toasted the world’s greatest mom, and Mom wished every day could be Mother’s Day.

Dad wanted to make Mother’s Day special, so he helped the children surprise Mom. He arranged for Mom’s running friends to take her jogging. As soon as she left, the children raced to the kitchen. They measured ingredients for a cake, mixed frosting, and made cards for Mom. They even added a coupon she could use. When Mom came home and noticed the messy sink, Dad gave a wink and said nothing had happened. The next morning, the children gave Mom a big bouquet and their cards. She was happy and surprised when they offered her a private spa session. In the kitchen spa, Dad gave her a large cup of coffee. The children massaged her shoulders and feet, covered her hair with a towel, put on a mud mask, and painted her nails with glitter. Afterward, they prepared a gourmet brunch. They raised juice glasses and thanked their wonderful mom.

Before Mother’s Day, a family prepared a secret celebration for Mom. Dad’s plan began when Mom’s friends came to take her running. Mom put on her sweatsuit, red cap, and earphones, then jogged away. The children quickly worked in the kitchen. They made cake batter and frosting, although the frosting splattered, and they created cards for Mom. When Mom returned, she saw the kitchen mess, but Dad winked and said nothing. On the next morning, the children presented a giant bouquet and wished her a happy Mother’s Day. They showed her a special spa in the kitchen. Dad served black coffee, and the children rubbed Mom’s shoulders and feet. They made her a towel turban, applied a mud mask, and painted her nails. Then Mom dressed for brunch. The family admired her and toasted her as the world’s greatest mom. Mom thanked them and wished for Mother’s Day every day.

video_title: Sleeping Beauty Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

Aurora meets a small dragon named Crackle while riding with Prince Philip. Moonlight is afraid at first, but Crackle gently licks her nose, and they become friends. At the ball, Crackle helps by lighting candles, warming food, and keeping everyone warm.

video_title: Chester’s Way

Lily taught them new tricks, and they taught her some of their ways. Soon, the three friends dressed together, went on picnics, shared an umbrella, and cared for one another. Then Victor moved into the neighborhood.

She wore disguises, talked backwards, waved at cars, and carried a squirt gun. Chester and Wilson stayed away from her. Later, some older boys surrounded the two friends. Lily used a disguise that looked like a scary cat, and the boys ran away. Chester and Wilson thanked her and invited her to lunch. They discovered that Lily liked some of the same things, too. The children began playing together and teaching each other new skills. They became three close friends who shared holidays, picnics, and outdoor fun. Then Victor moved into the neighborhood.

Chester liked croquet, peanut butter, making his bed, and following his usual routines. Wilson was his best friend, and the boys enjoyed doing everything together. They used hand signals, shared food and games, dressed in matching costumes, and helped each other stay safe. Lily moved into the neighborhood with her own unusual ways. She wore Band-Aids and disguises, spoke backwards, waved at cars, and carried a loaded squirt gun. At first, Chester and Wilson hid from her. video_title: Kids Books Read Aloud Story 📚 LeBron James: The Boy Who Would Become King by Anthony Curcio

summaries.summary: LeBron James was born in Akron, Ohio, and his mother, Gloria, raised him with help from family. After Gloria’s mother and grandmother died, Gloria and LeBron had very little money and moved many times. LeBron missed school and often stayed home alone, but he loved sports. A football coach saw how fast he was and invited him to join the team. The coach helped with rides and fees, and LeBron soon became a star. Coach Frankie Walker and his wife, Pam, also helped him play basketball. LeBron practiced hard and dreamed of the NBA. When he and Gloria had to move again, the Walkers let LeBron stay with them. He followed their rules, worked hard at school, and practiced basketball every day. Gloria eventually found a home for them. In high school, LeBron became a great football and basketball player. He chose basketball, went first in the NBA draft, won many awards, and later helped families through his foundation. He became a king by caring about others too.

When LeBron was a baby, his mother Gloria worked hard to care for him in Akron. They were poor and moved from home to home because they could not pay for a steady place to live. LeBron missed school and felt different from other children. One day, a football coach watched him win a race and asked him to play. The coach promised to take him to practice, so LeBron joined the team and scored a long touchdown in his first game. The coach, Frankie Walker, and his wife, Pam, then helped LeBron discover basketball. He practiced constantly and dreamed about playing in the NBA. When Gloria needed to move again, LeBron stayed with the Walkers. He made his bed, helped at home, finished his homework, and went to school every day.
