summaries.summary: Snow White’s mother dies, so her father, the king, looks for a new queen. He chooses Miss Malka Hose, who owns a magic mirror. For ten years, the mirror tells the queen that she is the fairest of all. Then the mirror says Snow White is prettier. The angry queen sends a huntsman to hurt Snow White and bring back her heart. In the forest, Snow White begs for a break. The huntsman sees that she has done no wrong and lets her go. He buys a heart and steak from a butcher to trick the queen. Snow White travels to the city and works for seven little dwarfs. The dwarfs lose their money betting on horses. Snow White takes the mirror from the palace and asks which horse will win. It names Mistletoe. The dwarfs bet on Mistletoe, win, and become rich with Snow White.

After Snow White’s mother dies, the king finds another wife named Miss Malka Hose. She brings a magic talking mirror that always gives the right answer. The queen asks who is fairest every day, and the mirror always praises her. One day, it says Snow White is prettier. The queen becomes furious and orders the huntsman to take Snow White into the forest. Snow White says she has done no wrong, and the huntsman feels sorry for her. He lets her escape and buys a heart from a butcher so the queen will believe Snow White is dead. Snow White reaches the city and finds seven small dwarfs. They are kind, but they waste their money betting on horses, so they have no dinner when they lose. Snow White gets the magic mirror. It says Mistletoe will win the next race. The dwarfs bet on Mistletoe, win, and share the money with Snow White.

The king chooses a queen who has a magic mirror. The queen loves asking the mirror who is the fairest. For many years, it says she is the fairest, but then it says Snow White is prettier. The queen sends a huntsman after Snow White. In the forest, Snow White asks him not to hurt her. He listens and lets her run away. He buys a heart and takes it to the queen, who believes Snow White is gone. Snow White finds work with seven funny little men. The seven dwarfs like horse racing, but they keep losing all their money. Snow White has an idea. She secretly takes the queen’s mirror and asks which horse will win the Ascot race. The mirror names Mistletoe. The dwarfs borrow and gather money, bet on Mistletoe, and win. After that, the mirror helps them win every day. Snow White and the dwarfs become millionaires.

video_title: Three Little Kittens-by: Igloo Books Ltd. #nurseryrhymes @Children-12j

summaries.summary: Three little kittens lost their mittens. They began to cry and told their mother, “Oh, mother dear, we sadly fear that we have lost our mittens.” Their mother heard that the mittens were lost and called them silly kittens. She said they would have no pie. The little kittens said, “Meow,” and heard again that they would have no pie.

The three little kittens had a problem: their mittens were lost. Because they could not find them, they began to cry. They went to their mother and told her that they sadly feared they had lost their mittens. Their mother answered, “Lost your mittens, you silly kittens!” Then she said the kittens would have no pie. One kitten said, “Meow.” The story ends with the mother saying again, “No, you shall have no pie.”

Three little kittens lost their mittens, so they cried. They spoke to their mother and said they sadly feared that the mittens were gone. Their mother replied that they were silly kittens because they had lost their mittens. She then told them they would not have any pie. The kittens answered with a meow. Their mother repeated that they would have no pie. The story shows the kittens’ problem and their mother’s response, ending with the kittens without pie.

video_title: A Cat with No Name | A story about love and loss

summaries.summary: One morning, Olive finds a little black-and-white kitten at her window. She opens the window, gives the kitten milk, and asks her mother if they can keep her. Mother says the kitten may belong to someone, but she can stay safely for now. Olive and the kitten play, walk, and sleep together. The kitten goes outside and always comes back, so Olive hopes she will stay forever. Then, on the eighth day, the kitten does not return. Olive and Dad search, put up flyers, and ask people in town. At the bakery, they learn that a girl called Stella found the kitten. The kitten had run away from that girl, who had been looking for her. Olive feels very sad, but Dad explains that Stella belongs with her family. Olive cried because she missed the kitten. Dad reminds her that she kindly cared for Stella and that Stella will not forget her. The name Stella means star, so Olive can remember her by looking at the sky each night.

Olive is eating breakfast when she hears a kitten at the window. She lets the kitten inside and gives her some milk. Olive's mother says the kitten may already have an owner, so they will keep her safe until someone comes to find her. Olive is happy because the kitten stays with her. They play together, walk together, and sleep on Olive's bed. The kitten often goes outside but keeps coming back. After one week, Olive calls her friend and wishes she could stay forever. The next day, however, the kitten disappears. Olive and Dad search all over town. A baker tells them that a little girl called Stella found the kitten and took her home. The girl had been looking for her for many days. Olive wishes the kitten could live with her, but Dad says it is good that the kitten found her way home. Olive cries because she misses her. Dad says Olive was kind to care for her and that neither of them will forget the other. Olive smiles and remembers Stella as a star in the sky.

A kitten climbs through Olive's window during breakfast. Olive welcomes her, gives her milk, and asks to keep her. Olive's mother agrees that the kitten may stay temporarily because she might be lost and have an owner. Olive loves looking after the kitten. They spend many happy days playing and walking together, and the kitten sleeps on Olive's bed. When the kitten goes outside, she comes back each time. Olive begins to hope her new friend will stay forever. Then the kitten does not come home one day or the next. Olive and Dad search for her and ask people if they have seen her. At the bakery, they hear that a little girl shouted, "Stella," and the kitten jumped into her arms. The girl had been searching for her lost kitten. Olive feels sad because she wanted Stella to stay with her. Dad explains that Stella belonged to the other girl and had returned home. Olive cries, but Dad tells her she was kind and Stella will remember her. He says Stella means star, so Olive can think of her whenever she looks at the night sky.

video_title: A Cat with No Name | A story about love and loss

summaries.summary: Finding kindness means noticing many small ways to help and care. Kindness can be a cup and a card, a cookie, a carrot, or a key. It can be sharing a sandwich, giving someone a seat, waving to a baker, or helping with a ladder, truck, tree, crane, shovel, or house. Kindness can also mean taking a break with someone who feels sad, forgiving yourself after a mistake, or forgiving a friend who became angry. The story shows kindness toward animals too. It can be cuddling puppies, holding a door, giving a toy or treat, seeing animals others ignore, and giving an animal a leash, a lick, and a home. Kindness can be soup for a sick neighbor, helping someone who falls, reading a story, feeding a fish, kissing a sister, and wishing a wish. The story ends by showing that kindness can be found in ordinary things, including a bug, a cup, and a card.

The story looks for kindness in everyday actions. At first, it names simple helpful things, such as giving a cup and card, sharing food, offering a seat on a train, waving to a baker, or giving someone a boost. Kindness can happen while people build, plant, dig, rake, or make a house with trees that will give shade. Then the story describes caring for feelings. A kind person can sit with someone who is sad, forgive a mistake, or forgive a friend who is mad. Kindness also includes caring for animals by cuddling puppies, holding a door, giving a toy, noticing animals others ignore, and helping an animal find a home. Near the end, kindness appears as soup for a sneezy neighbor, a scoop for someone who falls, reading, feeding a fish, kissing a sister, and wishing a wish. The story shows that kindness is made of many little actions, objects, and moments.

Kindness can look different from day to day. It may begin with a cup, a card, a cookie, a carrot, or a key. It may be sharing, making space, taking a photo, giving a ride, helping with tools, or building houses and planting trees. Kindness also means stopping to rest with someone who is sad. It means forgiving yourself when you make a mistake and forgiving a friend who gets mad. The story includes gentle care for puppies and other animals. Holding a door, offering a treat, combing, noticing animals, and giving a leash and a home are all examples. Kindness can help a sick neighbor with soup or help someone who falls with a scoop. It can be reading a story, feeding a fish, kissing a sister, and wishing a wish. By the end, kindness is found in many ordinary things, from a bucket and book to a bug, cup, and card.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse Read Along Story book | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids | Friends Like You

summaries.summary: Mickey and Minnie find a book at the library called How to Be a Friend. They take the book back to the clubhouse and learn that being a friend can make people happy. They decide to look for someone who needs a friend. In the kitchen, Goofy needs help with the dishes. Mickey calls Toodles, and Toodles gives them soap. Mickey and Minnie learn that friends share work and chores. Then they go to the garden and see Donald's big pumpkin. Minnie says Donald needs a friend to tell him what a wonderful job he did. Toodles gives them a trophy, so Donald can receive a prize. Back at the clubhouse, Toodles has one mystery Mousekatool left. It is a cake. Mickey and Minnie plan a best friend's party. Mickey says having friends is almost as much fun as being a friend.

At the library, Mickey sees many how-to books. The book on top is called How to Be a Friend, and Mickey and Minnie check it out. At the clubhouse, Minnie says the book is wonderful. They decide to find someone who needs a friend. They hear noises in the kitchen and see that Goofy could use help with the dishes. Toodles brings soap, and the friends use it to clean. The book teaches them that friends share work and chores. In the garden, Minnie sees Donald's big pumpkin. She says Donald needs a friend to tell him he did a wonderful job. Toodles brings a trophy, and Donald deserves a prize. Then Toodles reveals a mystery Mousekatool. It is a cake. Mickey and Minnie have a best friend's party. They enjoy having friends and being friends too.

Mickey and Minnie want to learn how to be good friends, so they borrow a friendship book from the library. They read it at the clubhouse and look around for a friend who needs help. In the kitchen, Goofy is doing dishes. Mickey asks Toodles for a Mousekatool, and Toodles gives them soap. Mickey and Minnie help with cleaning because friends share work and chores. Next, the friends visit the garden. Donald has a big pumpkin, and Minnie says he needs a friend to praise his wonderful work. She asks which Mousekatool will help. Toodles gives them a trophy, and Donald deserves a prize. When they return to the clubhouse, Toodles has a final surprise. The mystery Mousekatool is a cake. Minnie suggests a best friend's party to finish the happy day. Mickey says having friends is fun, and being a friend is almost as much fun.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Story book 🧜‍♀️ StoryBooks for Kids 📖 Quest for the Purple Pearl

summaries.summary: Ariel hears her sister Adella crying. Adella’s face has pink and green spots, and a quarter says that bubbles are serious. The quarter says a special lotion made from a purple Pearl can help. The pearls grow inside oysters far away, across a dangerous kelp forest. Ariel wants to help Adella, so she and Flounder swim to Blackbeard’s Trench. The kelp has long thorns and a strong current. Flounder tries to make a path, and Ariel rides the rushing water safely through the kelp. At the bottom of the trench, they find beautiful oysters with glowing pearls. Flounder tests one, and it snaps the driftwood in half. Ariel uses a feather on a stick to tickle an oyster. The oyster sneezes, and a purple Pearl flies into Ariel’s hands. But Adella says the bubbles went away on their own. Ariel keeps the pearl in her treasure grotto.

Adella’s face is covered with colorful spots, and Ariel wants to help her. A quarter tells Adella that a purple Pearl can make a cure. The pearls are inside triple-banded sea oysters in Blackbeard’s Trench. Ariel and Flounder travel through a barbed kelp forest to find one. The kelp is full of sharp thorns, and the water pushes hard. Flounder cannot make enough room, but the current opens the kelp. Ariel rides the current like a dolphin and swims through without getting scratched. Deep in the trench, Ariel and Flounder see many pretty oysters with glowing pearls. Flounder throws driftwood into one oyster, and it bites the wood in half. Ariel finds a feather, ties it to a stick, and tickles an oyster. The oyster sneezes out a purple Pearl. Ariel brings it to Adella, but Adella’s face is already clear. She explains that bubbles go away by themselves and that her story was a joke. Ariel smiles and saves the pearl.

Ariel hears that Adella needs help, so she decides to find a purple Pearl. Flounder warns her that the pearl is in Blackbeard’s Trench, beyond a huge forest of thorny sea kelp. Ariel and Flounder go together. Flounder swims ahead because he is smaller, but there is still not enough space for Ariel. Then the Riptide pulls the kelp apart. Ariel gets an idea and lets the current carry her through the forest. She and Flounder reach the bottom of the trench, where shining pearls rest inside open oysters. Flounder checks whether the oysters are safe by tossing in driftwood. One oyster bites it in half. Ariel uses a pointed feather on a stick to tickle another oyster. It sneezes, sending a purple Pearl into Ariel’s hands. Ariel returns to Adella, but Adella is already cured. She says the bubbles disappear on their own and that she was teasing Ariel. Ariel keeps the beautiful pearl in her collection.

video_title: MISS SPIDER'S TEA PARTY Read Aloud by Mrs. K. | Written by David Kirk | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Miss Spider wanted friends, so she made tea and set out chairs, cakes, cups, and plates. Beetles, fireflies, bumblebees, rubber bugs, ants, butterflies, and moths saw her web or her many legs and hurried away. Miss Spider felt sad because no bug would stay. Then a little moth came in from the rain. The moth was wet, and his wings were too damp to fly. Miss Spider gently covered him with a checkered cloth. They talked and ate tea and pie until his wings were dry. Miss Spider carefully tossed him into the air. The moth told Ike, and Ike told May, that Miss Spider had never meant to hurt anyone. Soon, eleven insects came to Miss Spider’s tea party. They saw her drink tea and eat flowers. Before long, Miss Spider knew all the bugs and their children, and she had the friends she wanted.

A lonely spider watched many insects and wished they would come for cakes and tea. She invited two beetles, three fireflies, four bumblebees, some rubber bugs, six ants, seven butterflies, and nine moths. Each group was afraid or did not want to stay. Miss Spider set the table anyway, but the room was empty. She felt so sad that she cried over ten little cups of tea. Then a small moth came in from a storm. Rain had soaked his wings, so he could not fly. Miss Spider helped him with a cloth and shared tea and pie with him. When his wings were dry, she gently tossed him into the air. The moth told the beetles that Miss Spider was not harmful. Later, eleven insects came to tea. They saw that Miss Spider ate flowers and drank tea. The insects became her friends, and she knew them and their children.

Miss Spider lived alone and hoped to have insect friends. She invited bugs to her tea party, but they were scared of her web and thought a spider might eat them. Beetles dashed away. Fireflies flew away. Bumblebees refused, and the ants turned up their noses. Even the moths fled when Miss Spider came near. Miss Spider was left with a table full of cups and cakes, and she cried. A little moth then came from the rain. His wings were wet and could not fly. Miss Spider did not hurt him. She covered him with a checkered cloth, talked with him, and gave him tea and pie. When he was dry, she gently lifted him into the air. The moth told the other insects that she meant no harm. Soon, eleven insects came to tea. Miss Spider ate flowers and drank tea, so the bugs felt safe. They became her friends.

video_title: Raya and the Last Dragon Movie Storybook 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Rya became a guardian of the Dragon Gem with help from her father, Chief Bena. The gem broke when Namari tried to take it, and the dark drun turned Bena to stone. Rya escaped with Tuck Tuck and grew into a brave warrior. After six years, she found the dragon Cisu. Together, they searched for the four missing gem shards. They met B, No, and the Onis, and some enemies tried to stop them. Rya learned that Cisu wanted everyone to trust one another. At Fang, Namari hurt Cisu by mistake, and Rya and Namari fought. Then Rya understood that trust could bring peace. Rya gave Namari her shard, and her friends gave theirs too. Namari put the gem together. A bright blast destroyed the drun, rain brought everyone back, and Rya found her father again. Candra was restored.

In Heart, Rya passed a test to guard the Dragon Gem. Her father, Bena, hoped the five lands could become friends again. But Namari tried to steal the gem, and it broke into five pieces. The drun returned and turned Bena to stone. Rya and Tuck Tuck carried one piece away. Years later, Rya found Cisu, a dragon who could help. They traveled through Tail, Talon, and Spine to find the other shards. They made new friends, escaped traps, and faced Namari and her army. At last, they went to Fang. Namari brought a shard and a crossbow, and Cisu was hurt. Rya and Namari stopped fighting and worked together. Rya trusted Namari and gave her the last piece. The others gave their pieces too. The Dragon Gem became whole, destroyed the drun, and brought back the people and dragons. Rya reunited with Bena.

Rya wanted to save her father after the Dragon Gem shattered and Bena became stone. She searched for the dragon Cisu for six years. Cisu agreed to help Rya find the missing gem pieces. In Tail, they found a shard and escaped Namari. In Talon, Rya caught No and the Onis after they stole the shards, then invited them to help. In Spine, Rya faced Namari while her friends escaped. Cisu became a dragon and protected Rya. The friends found another shard and traveled to Fang for the last one. Namari brought the shard, but an arrow hurt Cisu. Rya and Namari fought, then joined together when the drun attacked others. Rya gave up her protection so Namari could rebuild the gem. B, No, and Tong gave up theirs too. The completed gem destroyed the drun, and everyone, including the dragons, came back to life.

video_title: Elmer read aloud- read by a second grader

summaries.summary: Elmer was a special elephant covered in many bright colors. He made the other elephants happy with games and jokes, but Elmer was not happy because he thought they might laugh at his patchwork body. One morning, he left the herd and found a bush full of berries the color of elephants. He shook the bush, rolled in the berries, and rubbed berry juice all over himself. Soon he looked like an ordinary elephant. When he returned, the elephants stood very still and serious. Elmer wanted to make them laugh, so he shouted, “Boo!” Everyone jumped, and then everyone laughed. Rain fell and washed away the berry juice, showing Elmer’s bright colors again. The elephants said his joke was the biggest laugh of all. They decided to celebrate Elmer every year with a colorful parade.

There was an elephant named Elmer who was yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, green, black, and white. He was different from the other elephants, but he was also the one who made them laugh. Elmer felt unhappy and wondered who would want a patchwork elephant, so he secretly walked away. In the jungle, he found elephant-colored berries. He shook them from a bush and rolled in them until no bright color could be seen. Elmer went back to the herd looking like an ordinary elephant. The other elephants were quiet and serious, so Elmer could not resist playing a joke. He lifted his trunk and shouted, “Boo!” The elephants jumped, then laughed and laughed. A rain cloud burst, and the rain washed the berry juice away. Elmer’s colors appeared again. The elephants were happy to have him and made a special day to honor his best joke.

Elmer kept his elephant friends cheerful with funny games and jokes, even though he did not like being different. He was a patchwork elephant, while almost all the others were the same color. One morning, Elmer left the jungle herd and searched for a way to look ordinary. He found a bush covered in elephant-colored berries. After shaking the berries down, he rolled over them and covered his body with their juice. Then he returned to the elephants. They did not know who he was, but they stood silently and seriously. Elmer wanted to see them laugh, so he raised his trunk and called, “Boo!” The surprised elephants began laughing with him. Soon rain fell from a cloud, and Elmer’s berry covering washed away. His colorful patches came back. The elephants said they would celebrate Elmer’s joke every year with a parade.

video_title: Leave me Alone! | Irvington Public Library: Story Time With Ms. Charles

summaries.summary: An old woman lives in a small house with her very big family. Winter is coming, and she needs to knit, but her grandchildren keep asking questions about her yarn. She becomes very tired of the interruptions, packs her things in a big sack, and calls, “Leave me alone!” She goes into a dark forest, but a bear family comes near her fire. She leaves and climbs a mountain. Mountain goats visit her and fight over snacks, so she leaves again. The woman climbs all the way to the moon. Little green moon men examine her, but they cannot hear her because they have no ears. She travels through a wormhole to a dark, quiet void. There, she knits 30 little sweaters without anyone disturbing her. She puts the sweaters in her sack, drinks tea, and returns through another wormhole. Everything is where she left it, and she says nothing.

A grandmother has important knitting to finish before winter. She lives with a large family, and her grandchildren are curious about the ball of yarn. They ask many questions while she tries to work. At last, the old woman packs her belongings and leaves, shouting, “Leave me alone!” First, she knits beside a fire in a deep forest. Bears come to look at her and the light, but they do not understand her words. Next, she climbs the mountain and sits in a shelter. Mountain goats come for a visit and snacks, while the ghosts argue over red ones. The old woman keeps moving. She climbs onto the moon, where little green moon men scan her. They cannot hear her because they have no ears. She goes through a wormhole into a silent, dark void. Alone there, she finishes 30 little sweaters, packs them up, has tea, and travels home.

Before winter arrives, an old woman wants to complete her knitting. Her big family and curious grandchildren make it hard for her to work, so she tidies her bed, packs a big sack, and tells everyone to leave her alone. She tries knitting in a forest, but a bear family comes near her fire. Since the bears do not speak English, they do not listen, and she moves on. On a cold mountainside, mountain goats come because she has snacks. The ghosts become busy fighting over the red snacks, so she leaves again. The woman climbs higher and reaches the moon. Little green moon men study her with scanners, but they cannot hear her because they have no ears. She escapes through a wormhole and finds a very dark, quiet place. It is perfect for knitting. She uses all her yarn to make 30 little sweaters, puts them in her sack, drinks tea, and returns through another wormhole. Everything is back where it was.

video_title: INKY THE OCTOPUS, by Erin Guendelsberger | Children’s Picture Book Read Aloud | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Inky the octopus lives in a tank with clear walls and a lid. He gets lobster, shrimp, and squid every day, so he has a good life. Still, Inky wants to see the open sea. He misses the idea of new plants, rocks, and fish. One night, Inky notices that the tank lid is ajar. He tells his tank mate, Blotchy, about leaving, but Blotchy wants to stay in his comfortable home. Inky climbs out one arm at a time. The room feels dry, cool, strange, and exciting. He crosses the wood floor and wonders if he can leave his friends and old life behind. His heart says yes. Inky reaches the sea and falls toward the water. Then he plunges, swims, floats, spins, and glides. At last, Inky is free and travels far into the splendid sea.

Inky enjoys games in his aquarium, such as seaweed hide-and-seek, gravel hockey, and tentacle tag. He is fed well, but his curious heart wants more. Inky dreams of discovering a new world outside the tank. When the lid is left open, he sees a chance to escape. Blotchy, his tank mate, does not want to leave his cozy home, so Inky goes alone. He climbs up the tank and stretches all eight arms outside. His head follows, and he slides down onto the floor. Everything feels different: the floor is rough, the noises are odd, and the air smells new. Inky feels excited, but he thinks about his friends and everything he knows. He decides it is time to go. The sea is close. Inky falls into it, swims and glides through the water, and follows his heart toward a wide, free journey.

An octopus named Inky lives behind see-through aquarium walls. He eats three meals each day and plays fun games, but he still wishes to explore the ocean. Inky wants to discover plants, rocks, fish, and things he has never known. One night, the tank lid is ajar. Inky tells Blotchy that they could explore a new place together. Blotchy would rather remain in his comfortable tank, so Inky begins the adventure by himself. He carefully lifts one arm, then another, until all eight arms and his head are outside. He slides down and crosses the unfamiliar floor. The room smells and sounds different, and Inky feels free. He wonders about leaving his life and friends, but his hearts say yes. Soon he sees the sea and falls toward it. Inky plunges into the water, swims, floats, spins, and glides. He is finally free to travel far and wide.

video_title: Encanto - Family is Everything 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Mirabelle Madrigal lives with her family in the magical home called Casita. Her sisters have gifts: Louisa is strong, and Isabella makes beautiful flowers. Mirabelle has no magical gift, so she sometimes feels different, but she is still special. One night, she learns that Casita’s magic is dying. She listens to Louisa, who tells her to search Bruno’s tower for a missing vision. Mirabelle finds Bruno hiding inside Casita, and he finishes the vision. It shows Mirabelle and Isabella together. Mirabelle and Isabella talk about how hard it is to be perfect. Isabella makes a cactus and shows that she is more than pretty flowers. Casita cracks, and Abuela blames Mirabelle. Mirabelle says Abuela expects too much. Casita falls apart, but Abuela later says the trouble was her fault. The family rebuilds Casita, the magic returns, and the Madrigal family becomes closer than ever.

Mirabelle loves her family, even though she is the only Madrigal without a magical gift. Her family lives in Casita, where Abuela protects the family and its magic. Mirabelle’s sister Louisa is strong, while Isabella can make flowers. One night, Mirabelle overhears that Casita’s magic is dying. Bruno, her uncle who can see the future, had seen this happen. Mirabelle tries to understand the vision. She listens when Louisa shares her worries, and Louisa tells her to look in Bruno’s tower. Mirabelle finds pieces of the vision and then discovers Bruno hiding in Casita. Bruno completes the vision, which shows Mirabelle and Isabella. Mirabelle talks with Isabella, who says being perfect is difficult. Isabella makes a cactus, showing there is more to her than flowers. Casita cracks, and Abuela blames Mirabelle. Mirabelle says Abuela expects too much. After Casita falls, Abuela apologizes. The family rebuilds their home, and the magic comes back.

Mirabelle Madrigal is kind and funny, and she cares about her family. She lives in Casita with Abuela, her mother, and her sisters Louisa and Isabella. Louisa is strong, and Isabella makes flowers, but Mirabelle has no magical gift. Even so, Mirabelle is special. When Mirabelle hears that Casita’s magic is dying, she looks for answers. Bruno’s vision may explain what is happening. Mirabelle checks Bruno’s tower, finds the pieces of the vision, and finds Bruno hiding inside Casita. Bruno finishes the vision, and it shows Mirabelle with Isabella. Mirabelle learns that she needs to embrace her sister. Isabella explains that being perfect is hard. She makes a cactus instead of only making pretty flowers. Then Casita cracks. Abuela says Mirabelle is causing the magic to die, but Mirabelle says Abuela expects too much from everyone. Casita falls apart. By the river, Abuela says the fault is hers. The family rebuilds Casita, and its magic returns.

video_title: Ready..Set..Frog! | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

summaries.summary: Frog loved games, challenges, and building obstacle courses. When he heard that a neighborhood fair would have an obstacle course, he began practicing. He built a tall mountain of stones, but Mole called for help. Mole needed an apple for a pie, so Frog jumped into the tree and found one. The next day, Frog made a bridge and another rock mountain. Then Giraffe asked him to help put on her hat. Frog moved the hat until it was just right. Later, Kitten became stuck across the pond, so Frog hopped across the lily pads to help. Frog worried that he had not practiced at all. His mother explained that helping his friends was practice, too, and that he could also save time for his own plans. At the fair, Frog crossed logs, hay, and rocks. He won second place and felt proud and excited to try again next year.

Frog wanted to be ready for the fair's obstacle course. He first stacked stones in the backyard, but Mole startled him and the stones fell down. Mole needed an apple for an apple pie, so Frog climbed and hopped to the tallest branch to get one. The next morning, Frog built a bridge with sticks and chairs. When the bridge fell, Giraffe asked Frog to place her hat on her head because the sun was bright. Frog carefully moved it higher and lower until Giraffe said it was right. After school, Frog planned to practice again, but Kitten was stuck on lily pads across the pond. Frog crossed the pond to help Kitten. Frog thought he had lost all his practice time. His mother told him that helping others takes practice, while he should also make time for himself. At the fair, Frog finished the course and earned second place.

Frog enjoyed hopping and making obstacle courses with his neighbors. He was happy when he learned about the fair, because he wanted to practice for its obstacle course. His first stone mountain fell when Mole asked for an apple. Frog helped Mole by jumping into the tree and bringing down the brightest apple. Then Frog built a bridge, but it fell when he lost his balance. Giraffe needed help with her hat, so Frog balanced and moved it until she was comfortable. Later, Kitten was stuck on the other side of a pond. Frog stopped practicing and hopped across the lily pads to reach Kitten. Frog felt sad because he had no time for his own practice. His mother said that helping friends was good practice, but it was also fine to say no sometimes and save time for himself. Frog competed at the fair, came in second, and looked forward to next year.

The elves work very fast, and Santa is ready on time. Cookie becomes the Chief Inventor, and every elf may choose the job that brings the most joy.

Cookie comes from a family of maker elves. She is told to make toys, but her favorite thing is inventing new machines. Her ideas are not accepted because the elves must stay in their assigned jobs. One day, the sleigh loader makes a strange noise and breaks with a loud clunk. The elves try to repair it, but nothing works. They worry that Santa will not be ready for Christmas. Cookie says she has an idea. She makes a plan during the night, but the CEO puts it aside. Pudding sees the plan and takes it to the meeting for Santa. Santa thinks Cookie’s invention is brilliant. Cookie builds Lifter Gifts to carry presents and makes robots to clean up. The elves finish quickly, so Santa can leave on time. Cookie wants to invent, even though she is expected to make toys. She has many clever ideas, but the Chief Elf Officer says inventing is not her job. video_title: Two Bad Ants

summaries.summary: A scout finds a beautiful sparkling crystal and brings it to the ant queen. She loves its taste, so many ants travel through the dark woods and climb a huge mountain to find more. They reach a strange place filled with crystals. Most ants take one crystal and go home, but two ants stay because they want to eat crystals forever. Soon, a giant scoop lifts them into the air and drops them into a boiling brown lake. The ants struggle through waves, a whirlpool, heat, rushing water, spinning food, and a strange force in narrow holes. Exhausted, they sleep. At night, their fellow ants return. The two ants join the line, each take only one crystal, and follow their friends home. They hear their family below and feel happy because they understand that their true home is with their ant family and queen.

The ant queen tastes a sparkling crystal and wants more. The ants set out to gather crystals, crossing a forest, climbing a mountain, and entering a mysterious world with a sea of treasure. Two little ants decide not to return home. They eat crystal after crystal and fall asleep. In the morning, a giant silver scoop carries them high above the crystals and drops them into a hot, bitter lake. They are pushed through a whirlpool, pulled toward a dark cave, and trapped in several frightening places. They hide in a round disc, become very hot, fly through the air, and try to drink from a fountain. The water throws them into a spinning chamber full of soggy food. Later, a strange force blasts them from narrow holes. At last, they rest. When the other ants return, the two join them, take one crystal each, and happily go home to their queen and family.

After the queen enjoys a crystal, the ants travel far away to collect more for her. The journey is dangerous, with cold drops, darkness, wind, and a tall mountain. At the top, they find a shiny place filled with crystals. Two ants choose to stay behind because they think they can eat the treasure forever. Their choice brings trouble. A giant scoop drops them into a boiling lake, where waves and a whirlpool nearly pull them under. They escape but are lifted into hot darkness, thrown through the air, and swept into a wet chamber that spins with food and rain. They try to find safety in narrow holes, but a powerful force shoots them out. The tired ants sleep until their friends return. This time, they take just one crystal and go home. Hearing the happy nest, they realize that home, family, and being with the other ants make them happier than the crystals alone.

Aru has grown up in the Museum of Ancient Indian Art and Culture, where she knows almost everything, except the secret of a clay diya known as the Lamp of Destruction. The story begins by showing why Aru is comfortable around dangerous objects. She has lived in a museum all her life, but she has always obeyed the rule against lighting its mysterious diya. video_title: WHAT IF EVERYBODY THOUGHT THAT? Read Aloud by Mrs. K. | By Ellen Javernick | Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: People make quick guesses about others. They think a small boy cannot play basketball, but he gets the ball in the hoop and everyone cheers. The story gives many examples of people being judged before they have a chance to show what they can do. A boy is called too little for basketball, yet he makes the shot. A girl is told she cannot be in a relay race, but she runs and receives cheers. At the end, people think a boy cannot sing because he can barely say hello. He tries, and everyone applauds. The characters realize their guesses can be wrong and say that everyone is fantastic and people should be more thoughtful.

At first, different people look at others and decide what they can or cannot do. They say a little boy will not make the basketball team, but he gets the ball into the hoop.
