A surprise party shows him that he has wonderful friends, and he becomes happier than ever.

The story begins with a monster whose M goes missing. Every M is specially made, so he cannot replace it. Now called the onster, he is teased and sits alone at lunch. He searches Monster Wood for the letter, checking his sheets, bed, playground, shed, garbage cans, and engines. Nothing works. Without his M, he thinks he is not himself. He tries living like a human helper. He sweeps, keeps things tidy, organizes drawers, plays sports, and swims. He enjoys these activities, but other monsters laugh because he is not acting mean. He tries to change by thinking about pulling flowers from Mrs. Power's yard and throwing eggs at Mr. Lander's van. However, he is too kind: he waters the roses and cooks brunch for the Lander family. Feeling he does not fit in, he returns home. A party is waiting. His name and picture fill the room, and he learns that losing his M helped him find amazing friends.

video_title: GROUNDHUG DAY – Groundhog Day Read Aloud | Valentines Day Read Aloud | + FUN Kids Craft Activity

summaries.summary: Moose plans a big Valentine’s Day party with balloons, cards, and hugs. His friends want everyone to come, but Bunny explains that Groundhog may see his shadow on Groundhog Day and stay in his hole for six weeks. The friends make plans to stop Groundhog from seeing his shadow, but they argue until morning. Groundhog sees shadows and dives back inside. Moose learns that Groundhog is afraid of shadows. Instead of forcing him outside, the friends show him dancing leaf shadows, silhouettes, cloud shadows, and shadow puppets. Groundhog has fun, but he still wants to stay in his warm hole because winter is cold. The friends give him hugs and a nose kiss before he leaves. Six weeks later, Groundhog comes out wearing a green hat and starts planning a Saint Patrick’s Day party. Bunny is missing, because he is staying in his hole this time of year.

Moose is excited to have a Valentine’s Day party, and Squirrel, Bunny, and Porcupine help prepare. Then Bunny says Groundhog might see his shadow and sleep through the party. The friends try to keep Groundhog from seeing a shadow by changing his calendar, using a blindfold, putting up a tent, and blocking his hole. Their arguing takes so long that Groundhog comes out in the morning and sees shadows. He quickly returns underground. Moose asks if he is scared, and Groundhog says the shadows are everywhere outside. The friends decide to show him that shadows can be fun. They make dancing shadows, silhouettes, cloud shadows, and shadow puppets. Groundhog enjoys the day, but he still chooses his warm hole for six more weeks. Everyone shares hugs. Six weeks later, Groundhog comes out for a Saint Patrick’s Day party, while Bunny stays hidden in his hole.

A Valentine’s party is coming, and Moose wants all his friends there. Bunny worries that Groundhog will see his shadow and remain underground for six weeks. Squirrel, Porcupine, Bunny, and Moose think of ways to prevent Groundhog from seeing the shadow, but they argue all night and miss their chance. Groundhog sees shadows and hides. Moose discovers that Groundhog is afraid of them. The friends then help by showing him many kinds of shadows. Leaves make shadows that dance, clouds make shadows on hills, Bunny draws silhouettes, and Porcupine makes shadow puppets. Groundhog thinks everything sounds fun and spends the day with them. At night, he says he must return to his warm hole because winter is cold. The friends hug him and give him a special nose kiss. Six weeks later, Groundhog comes out wearing a green hat and calls for a Saint Patrick’s Day party. Bunny is still in his hole.

video_title: Huge Harold by Bill Peet

summaries.summary: Harold is a rabbit whose feet begin growing until he becomes huge. His worried parents send him away because hunters and dogs might find him. In a dark forest, foxes, weasels, and owls plan to eat him, so Harold runs away. He tries to rest near a cow and pig, but they chase him off. When he eats near a farm, a farmer shoots at him, and Harold races away. A storm drives him into an empty mansion, where two boys discover him and tell the neighborhood. Hunters search for him for weeks, but Harold hides in a treetop. Cold weather finally sends him to a barn. Orville protects him, feeds him, and cares for him. In spring, Harold pulls a buggy, enters a race, and becomes a champion trotter. Even after people bring him treats and praise him, Harold stays modest and humble, because rabbits are always the same no matter what happens.

Harold starts as a tiny rabbit, but his feet and whole body grow bigger every day. His parents fear that he cannot hide from hunters, so Harold leaves home and searches for a safe place. The forest seems empty, but hungry foxes, weasels, and owls are waiting for him. Harold escapes and later gets chased away by a cow and a pig. He finds lettuce and peas, but a farmer fires a shot, making him run in fear. During a storm, he hides in an abandoned house. Two boys see him and bring hunters, beginning a long hunt. Harold cleverly hides in a treetop, where the hunters and dogs do not look. Months later, snow and cold force him into Orville Boft's barn. Orville keeps the hunters out and takes good care of Harold. Harold eventually pulls a buggy and wins a trotting race. The crowd celebrates him, but he remains humble.

Harold's unusual size causes trouble from the beginning. His parents know he is too large to hide, so they sadly watch him leave for the woods. Harold is frightened by dangerous animals, chased from a pasture, and shot at while eating vegetables. He runs through the countryside until a storm sends him into an old mansion. After boys report seeing him, hunters follow his trail for many weeks. Harold uses his great size and cleverness to hide in a leafy treetop, but the search continues through autumn and winter. When the snow becomes too cold, Harold finds a warm barn. Orville Boft hears him snoring and refuses to let the hunters enter. Harold worries that Orville wants to fatten him for stew, but spring shows that he was wrong. Orville brushes him and hitches him to a buggy. At the fair, Harold enters a trotting race, wins easily, and becomes a champion. People bring him food and praise, yet he stays modest and humble.

video_title: Bambi Read Along Story book | Bambi Storybook | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids

summaries.summary: Bambi is born in the forest, and all the animals come to meet the new little prince. He learns words with Thumper and becomes friends with Flower. Bambi’s mother takes him to the meadow, where he plays with Felen. A loud noise makes the deer run away, but the great prince helps Bambi get back to his mother. In winter, Thumper teaches Bambi to slide on ice. Later, hunting sounds frighten Bambi and his mother. Bambi reaches safety, but his mother is gone. The great prince tells Bambi he will care for him. As Bambi grows, he loves Feline, protects her from a jealous deer, and lives happily with her. A forest fire comes, and Bambi saves Feline from hounds. His father helps him escape to the river. In spring, the forest heals, and Bambi and Feline welcome new twins.

On a bright spring morning, a fawn named Bambi is born. The forest animals celebrate, and Thumper helps Bambi learn about birds, butterflies, flowers, and a skunk named Flower. Bambi’s mother takes him to the meadow and warns him to be careful. Bambi plays with Felen, but a loud sound sends the deer running. The great prince brings Bambi back to his mother. During winter, Bambi learns to skate on a frozen pond, though he falls down. When food is scarce, Bambi and his mother find grass, but hunters make them run. Bambi reaches home alone, and the great prince tells him his mother cannot return. Bambi grows up and finds love with Feline. When fire and hounds threaten the forest, Bambi fights to save Feline, and his father leads him to safety. The forest grows green again, and Bambi becomes a proud father.

The animals welcome Bambi, a baby deer and forest prince. He explores with Thumper and Flower and learns the names of things around him. In the meadow, Bambi meets Felen and plays with her until a frightening noise makes everyone flee. The great prince helps Bambi return safely. Bambi enjoys winter by learning to slide on ice, but hunger and hunters bring danger. His mother helps him run to the thicket, yet Bambi cannot find her afterward. His father stays with him and takes care of him. When Bambi is older, he meets Feline again and falls in love. A jealous deer fights Bambi, but Bambi wins. Later, smoke and fire spread through the forest. Bambi rescues Feline from fierce hounds, then becomes too weak to run. His father helps him reach the river. The animals rebuild after the fire, and Bambi and Feline have twins.

video_title: Dog Loves Books

summaries.summary: Dog loved books. He loved their smell, their feel, and everything about them. Because he loved books so much, he opened a bookstore. Dog prepared the shop by unpacking and stacking the books. On opening day, he washed, dried, and prepared himself to greet customers. But nobody came. A lady entered and asked for tea with milk and two sugars, but Dog explained that his shop only sold books, so she left. Dog waited alone. A man came in to ask for directions, and then he left too. Dog felt downhearted, but he did not wait any longer. He chose a book and began to read. While reading, Dog forgot that he was waiting, alone, and inside the bookstore. When one adventure ended, he chose another book and began a new adventure. Later, a customer asked for a book, and Dog knew which books to recommend. Most of all, Dog loved sharing books.

Dog loved books in every way. He loved how books smelled and felt, so he decided to open a bookstore of his own. He unpacked the books, stacked them carefully, and got ready for the grand opening. Dog had a bath, dried his fur, blew his nose, and opened the door for customers. At first, no one came. A lady walked in, but she wanted tea with milk and two sugars. Dog told her that the shop was a bookstore and that he only sold books. She walked away, leaving Dog alone. Dog waited and waited. Then a man came to ask for directions, but he left too. Dog was downhearted. He chose not to wait any longer and took a book from the shelf. Reading helped Dog forget that he was waiting and alone. It also carried him away from the bookstore. Each time one adventure ended, he started another. When a customer finally wanted a book, Dog knew exactly what to recommend and loved sharing it.

Dog decided to open a bookstore because he loved books so much. He loved their smell, their feel, and everything about them. Before opening, he unpacked the books and stacked them in the shop. On the special day, Dog cleaned himself, dried his fur, blew his nose, and opened the door. He expected new customers, but nobody was there. A lady came inside and asked for tea with milk and two sugars. Dog said that he only sold books, so the lady left. Dog waited alone. A man came in to ask for directions, and he left as well. Dog felt downhearted, but then he took a book from the shelf and began to read. His book made him forget that he was waiting, forget that he was alone, and forget that he was in the bookstore. When one adventure finished, Dog picked another book and began a new adventure. Then a customer asked for a book. Dog knew which ones to recommend, and he especially loved sharing books.

video_title: The Butter Battle Book by Dr Seuss

summaries.summary: A grandfather tells a child about two groups living on opposite sides of a wall. The Yooks put butter on top of their bread, while the Zooks put it underneath. The grandfather says this difference makes the Zooks dangerous. Long ago, he watched the wall with a prickly switch, but Van Itch broke it. The Yook leader gave him bigger and stronger weapons. Each time, Van Itch returned with an even stronger Zook weapon. The Yook soldier brought a clever dog named Daniel and later flew a machine that sprayed blue goo, but the Zooks copied that machine too. Finally, the Yook leader gave him a powerful bomb and told everyone to hide underground. The child sees Grandfather climb onto the wall with the bomb. Van Itch arrives carrying another bomb. The child asks who will drop it, and Grandfather says they will see.

On the last day of summer, a grandfather brings his grandchild to a wall and explains the quarrel between the Yooks and the Zooks. The Yooks believe butter belongs on top of bread, and they believe Zooks are wrong for putting it underneath. When Van Itch breaks the guard's Snick-Berry switch, the Yook leader keeps giving the guard new weapons. First comes a triple sling. Then the Zooks answer with the Rock Snatch 'Em. The Yooks build the Kapoo Kid and train Daniel, a gun-toting spaniel, but the Zooks defeat them with the Eight-Nozzled Elephant-Toted Boom Blitz. The guard is promoted and receives the Utterly Sputter, which sprays blue goo. Van Itch has one too. Then the Yooks create the Bitsy Big-Boy Boomeroo. Everyone hides underground, but Grandfather climbs onto the wall with it. Van Itch appears with his own bomb, and the story ends before either one drops it.

The story begins with a wall separating Yooks from Zooks. A young guard watches the Zooks because they eat bread with the butter side down. After Van Itch breaks the guard's switch, the Yook chief supplies a triple sling. Van Itch quickly gets a machine that catches and throws the rocks back. The chief's helpers then invent bigger guns, including the Kapoo Kid, while Daniel the dog helps the Yooks. Van Itch's powerful Boom Blitz defeats them, so the guard returns sadly. The Yooks cheer him, promote him to general, and give him a flying machine called the Utterly Sputter. It sprays blue goo, but Van Itch has the same kind of machine. Back home, the chief gives the general the Bitsy Big-Boy Boomeroo, a bomb meant for the Zooks. The Yooks hide underground. Grandfather climbs onto the wall, and Van Itch arrives with another bomb. The child asks who will drop one first. Grandfather answers, "We'll see."

video_title: The Dark by Lemony Snicket

summaries.summary: Llo is afraid of the dark, which lives in the basement of his house. Every morning, Llo says hello to it, but he hopes it will stay away from his room. One night, the dark visits Llo and asks him to come downstairs. Llo follows it from the living room to the basement. The dark tells him that it is close by and explains that darkness is part of the house and the world. Without a roof, rain would fall on his bed. Without windows, he could not see outside. Without stairs, closets, or a shower curtain, the house would not work the same way. The dark says that without darkness, everything would be light. Then it asks Llo to open the bottom drawer. After that night, the dark does not bother Llo anymore. Llo visits the basement the next morning and says hello again. The open drawer looks as if something is smiling in the corner.

Llo is scared because the dark lives in his house. It hides in the closet, behind the shower curtain, and mostly in the basement. At night, it spreads over the windows and doors, but in the morning it returns downstairs. Llo often peeks at it and says, “Hi, dark.” One night, the dark comes to Llo’s room and tells him it wants to show him something. Llo follows it downstairs. In the basement, the dark asks him to come closer and says that the dark is not afraid of him. It explains that darkness is always nearby and that many things in the house are important, including the roof, windows, stairs, closet, and shower curtain. The dark then tells Llo to open the bottom drawer. Llo thanks it. Later, the dark is gone from his room, except when Llo closes his eyes. The next morning, Llo visits the basement, and the dark never bothers him again.

The dark lives with Llo in a large, creaky house. During the day, it waits in the basement beside old boxes and an unopened chest of drawers. At night, it spreads across the house’s windows and doors. Llo is afraid, but he tries to be friendly and says hello to the dark each morning. One night, the dark speaks to him and leads him downstairs. Llo looks at the darkness outside, then follows the dark into the basement. The dark tells Llo that people may be afraid of darkness, but darkness is not afraid of them. It says that darkness is near corners, doors, and the sky. It also explains how the roof, window, stairs, closet, and shower curtain help the house, and that darkness helps people know when they need a light bulb. Then the dark tells Llo to open the bottom drawer. After Llo goes back to bed, the dark is no longer in his room. The next morning, Llo says hello in the basement. The dark stays with him but never bothers him again.

video_title: Moana Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Moana lives on an island and loves the ocean, but her people never sail beyond the reef. Long ago, Maui took the heart of Taffy Tea, the Mother Island. Without her heart, Taffy Tea crumbled, darkness spread, and the lava monster Tikka attacked Maui. The ocean gives Moana the heart, and Grandma Tala keeps it safe. When Moana grows up, Grandma gives it back and tells her to find Maui. Moana sails across the ocean and meets him. Maui first refuses to help and sails away, but the ocean brings him back. Together, they find Maui’s magic fishhook in the world of monsters. Then they sail toward Tahiti, but Tocar attacks them. Moana offers the glowing heart. Taka accepts it, and plants and life return to the islands. Moana and Maui save the islands, say goodbye as friends, and Moana returns home as a great way finder and leader.

Moana’s island is surrounded by a reef, and the people are afraid to sail past it. In the past, Maui stole the heart of Taffy Tea, who gave life to the islands. Taffy Tea crumbled, darkness spread, and Maui lost his fishhook when Tikka struck him. The ocean gives Moana the heart, and Grandma Tala later tells Moana to take it back to Tahiti. Moana learns to sail and finds Maui. He does not want to help because he has lost his magic power, so he takes her boat and leaves. The ocean returns him to Moana, and they work together. They trick a crab monster and get Maui’s fishhook. On their journey, Tocar attacks from the sky. Moana keeps sailing and offers the heart. It glows, Taka accepts it, and life grows again. Moana and Maui save the islands and each other. Moana goes home, ready to lead her people.

Moana wants to help her island, even though her father says she must not go beyond the reef. Grandma Tala shows her old ships and explains that their people were once wayfinders. She gives Moana Taffy Tea’s heart and says Maui must return it to Tahiti. Moana sails into the open ocean, meets Maui, and asks him to help. Maui says he needs his fishhook, so Moana goes with him to the world of monsters. She tricks the crab monster with a shiny stone, and Maui gets his hook and powers back. Later, Tocar blocks their path and attacks Maui as he changes into a huge hawk. Moana does not give up. She sails quickly and offers the heart to Tocar. The heart glows, and Taka accepts it. Taffy Tea returns and blooms with plants. Life comes back to the islands. Moana and Maui become friends, and Moana returns home as a leader.

video_title: 😟 Ruby Finds a Worry | Big Bright Feelings

summaries.summary: Ruby loved swinging high and exploring the garden. She was happy until she found a tiny worry. At first, she hardly noticed it, but it grew bigger every day. The worry followed Ruby at breakfast, while she brushed her teeth, on the school bus, and at the movie theater. No one else could see it, so Ruby tried to pretend it was not there. Soon, worrying about the worry made it enormous, and Ruby could think of almost nothing else. One day at the park, Ruby saw a sad boy sitting alone. A worry was hovering beside him too. Ruby learned that other people had worries. She asked the boy what was on his mind, and his worry became smaller while he talked. Ruby talked about her own worry as well. Both worries disappeared, and Ruby felt like herself again. Worries came back sometimes, but they did not stay long when she talked about them.

Ruby enjoyed being Ruby. She liked swinging high, exploring faraway places, and going to the bottom of the garden. Then she discovered a small worry. It kept growing and followed her everywhere. It watched her over the cereal box and stayed while she brushed her teeth. Ruby tried to act as if everything was normal, but the worry stopped her from doing the things she loved. Soon it became so enormous that it filled parts of the kitchen, the school bus, and the movie theater. Ruby felt as if she would never be happy again. At the park, she saw a boy sitting alone and noticed that he had a worry too. Ruby asked him what was on his mind. As he spoke, his worry shrank. Ruby then talked about her own worry, and it shrank until it was almost gone. Both worries disappeared, and Ruby felt like herself again. Worries could return, but talking helped them leave quickly.

Ruby began with many happy adventures. She swung high, explored wild places, and visited the bottom of the garden. One day, a little worry appeared. Ruby ignored it, but it grew larger each day. It came to breakfast, stayed with her at bedtime, and stopped her from enjoying her favorite things. Because Ruby kept worrying about it, the worry became enormous. It filled the kitchen, part of the school bus, and rows at the movie theater. Then Ruby saw a boy alone in the park. He looked sad, and a worry hovered beside him. Ruby understood that she was not the only one who had a worry. She asked the boy what was troubling him. While he told her, his worry grew smaller. Ruby followed his example and talked about her own worry. Her worry shrank until it was barely there, and both worries went away. Ruby felt like herself again. Later worries might come, but they would not stay long.

video_title: This School Year Will Be the Best! | Irvington Public Library: Story Time With Ms. Charles

summaries.summary: On the first day of school, the children sit together on the rug. Their teacher asks what they hope will happen during the year. The children share many wishes. One child hopes for the best bus seat and hopes to remember homework. Other children want to look good in their school pictures, bring a pet snake for show and tell, eat lunch from a chocolate fountain, and score a goal. They also wish to squirt a fire-truck hose, take a very cool field trip, take the class pet home, and have a snow day. More children hope to make friends, grow tall, see butterflies hatch, have skateboard day, and keep their desks organized. They imagine a crazy principal, a pig kiss, and perfect report cards. At the end, the teacher shares her wish: to get to know every child. She says the year will be the best.

A new school year begins, and the children gather in a circle. Their teacher asks each child to name a hope for the year. The wishes are different and sometimes very silly. One child wants a great seat on the bus, remembered homework, and a good school picture. Another hopes to bring a pet snake and have a chocolate fountain at lunch. The children dream about kicking a ball into the right goal, spraying water from a fire truck, going on a wonderful field trip, and avoiding being a vegetable in the school play or festival. They hope for a birthday surprise, a snow day, new friends, tall measurements, hatching butterflies, and skateboard day. They also hope not to lose things, see the principal do something crazy, read 100 books, watch the principal kiss a pig, and earn perfect report cards. Finally, the teacher says she hopes to know each child, making the year the best.

The story starts on the first day of school. Everyone sits on the rug while the teacher asks what they hope will happen that year. The children answer one after another. They hope for good bus seats, remembered homework, nice school pictures, unusual show-and-tell pets, special lunches, successful soccer kicks, and a chance to use a fire hose. They hope their class will visit a cool place and that they will not play a vegetable in the school play or festival. They want to take home the class pet, receive a birthday surprise, and get a snow day. Other wishes include making friends, growing tall, seeing butterflies hatch, enjoying skateboard day, and keeping track of their things. The children also imagine a surprising principal, reading 100 books, a pig kiss, and perfect grades. Then the teacher tells her own wish: she will get to know every child, and this year will be the best.

video_title: It Came In The Mail by Ben Clanton

summaries.summary: Liam loved getting mail, but his mailbox was always empty. He checked it many times each day and found nothing. Then Liam had an idea. He wrote a letter to his mailbox and asked for something big. The mailbox shook and made funny sounds. When Liam looked inside, a fire-breathing dragon had arrived. Liam was delighted, so he asked the mailbox for more things. Soon it sent pickles, pigs, a whale with wings, a trombone, bones, and many other surprises. Liam asked for a gazillion more things, and oodles of mail poured out. Soon there was too much mail for one child. Liam had another idea. He wrote to the mailbox and asked for help sending the things to other children. He gave things away, including something Amelia might like. Liam discovered that sending things could be just as fun as receiving them.

Every day, Liam hoped to find mail, but his mailbox stayed empty. One day, he decided to send a letter to the mailbox itself. He asked for something big, and the mailbox answered by sending him a fire-breathing dragon. Liam loved his new dragon and quickly asked for more. The mailbox began sending many strange and wonderful things, including pickles, pigs, a flying whale, a trombone, and bones. Liam enjoyed everything, so he asked for a gazillion more items. Then the mailbox became full of mail, and too much of it flooded out. Liam wondered what he could do. He realized that other children probably wanted mail, too. Liam wrote another letter, asking the mailbox to help him share the things. Soon he was mailing gifts to children all over the place. Almost everything was gone, but Liam was happy. He learned through his actions that sending things to others could be very enjoyable.

Liam wanted mail more than anything, but he never received any. After checking his empty mailbox again and again, he thought that sending a letter might bring a letter back. He wrote to the mailbox and asked for something big. The mailbox shook, made strange sounds, and delivered a dragon that breathed fire. Liam was thrilled and asked for even more mail. The mailbox sent all kinds of unusual objects, such as pickles, pigs, a winged whale, a trombone, and dinosaur bones. Liam asked for a gazillion more things, and soon the mailbox overflowed with oodles of mail. At first he thought it was awesome, but then he saw there was too much for him. Liam decided to share. He asked the mailbox to help send the items to other children and began mailing things everywhere. When nearly everything was gone, Liam was still pleased. He could ask for more another time.

video_title: No Reading Allowed: The Worst Read Aloud Book Ever

summaries.summary: This book is a funny collection of sentences that sound alike but look different when written. First, the hair comes forth, and everyone is astonished by foul feet. A mummy prepares Pharaoh for dinner, while another sentence says that the mummy prepares Pharaoh for dinner again. People try to catch up, or perhaps catch ketchup, and someone has all the dough she needs. The sentences continue with cats and dogs, a long pole queue, tapered pants, and a New Deli clerk with a sorry store. There is Sir Francis Bacon, Orion’s Belt, a Navy father, and a mother who is well read or well red. Later come a B man, a Bard man, a hero with supervision, and a hero with super Vision. The book ends with miners, mermaids, and two sentences saying it is fun to read the book if it is not allowed.

A parade of playful sentences fills this book. At the beginning, hair comes forth, foul feet astonish everyone, and a mummy prepares Pharaoh for dinner. Some people mustered everything but could not catch up, while another sentence changes the ending to ketchup. Someone boldly writes in all caps, and someone else has all the dough she could need. The sentences then mention rain, cats and dogs, a pole queue, tapered pants, and a New Deli clerk. Names and phrases change in amusing ways: Sir Francis Bacon becomes Sir Fran is bacon, Orion’s Belt becomes Oh Ryan’s belt, and well read becomes well red. The middle includes a B man, a Bard man, a hero with supervision, and a hero with super Vision. Near the end are a barn, stew, Queensboro, a moose, a pitcher, a manatee, a fryer, miners, ores, and four mermaids. The final lines repeat that reading the book is fun if it is not allowed.

The story is made from many pairs of short, silly sentences. It starts with “The hair came forth” and “We were all astonished by the foul feet.” Next, a mummy prepares Pharaoh for dinner, and people try to catch up or catch ketchup. A woman has enough dough, rain falls with cats and dogs, and a pole queue is too long. The book visits a New Deli, Sir Francis Bacon, Orion’s Belt, a Navy father with blue jeans, and a mother who is well read or well red. Then a B man and a Bard man loot The Establishment. A hero has supervision, or super Vision, and people hear different versions of the same sounds. The Fearsome Predator prays, a barn is raised, and stew wears stew when it is time to eat. The sentences continue with Queensboro, an Aunt Hill, children scarfing a moose, a pitcher holding a batter, and a manate. Finally, a fryer sizzles, a key sounds beautiful, miners ride with ores, and mermaids jump over good news.

video_title: Duncan the Story Dragon by Amanda Driscoll

summaries.summary: Duncan the dragon loved reading, but whenever he opened a book, the story came alive and his imagination caught fire. Sadly, the book caught fire too, so Duncan could not discover how the story ended. He wondered whether pirates would find treasure, a captain would save a ship, or aliens would conquer Earth. Duncan tried to stay calm and decided to find a friend who could read the book to him. He asked a raccoon, a possum, and a bull, but none of them read it. Duncan returned home crying. A mouse saw his sadness and offered to help. The mouse loved books and read to Duncan. Together they battled sea monsters, dodged icebergs, discovered new lands, ate hot dogs and marshmallows, and sailed home. Then the mouse read, “the end.” But for Duncan, it was only the beginning of a wonderful book adventure.

Duncan the dragon wanted very much to finish his book. Each time he read, the story came alive, his imagination caught fire, and the book burned. He wished to know what happened to pirates, a captain, and aliens. Duncan tried everything to keep cool, then decided a friend could read the book aloud. He searched a neighborhood and asked a raccoon. He explored an evergreen forest and asked a possum. He traveled to a faraway farm and asked a bull. No one read the book, so Duncan went back to his cottage with a tear on his cheek. The tear ran across the floor and became a mouse. The mouse asked about the sad ending and listened to Duncan's problem. When Duncan asked whether the mouse liked books, the mouse said yes and agreed to read. They shared a grand adventure before reaching “the end,” which was actually just the beginning.

Duncan loved books, but reading made exciting stories spring to life and made his book catch fire. He wanted to finish one book and reach the two special words, “the end.” Since he could not read it safely, Duncan looked for someone to help. He greeted a raccoon, a possum, and a bull, asking each one to read the book. After searching the countryside, Duncan returned to his cottage and cried because he still did not know the ending. His tear turned into a mouse. The mouse noticed Duncan's trouble and said that books were wonderful. Duncan asked the mouse to read, and the mouse happily agreed. As the mouse read, Duncan and the mouse battled sea monsters, dodged icebergs, found new lands, ate roasted hot dogs and toasted marshmallows, and sailed home. The mouse finally said “the end,” but their book journey was only beginning.

video_title: Disney Up Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Carl lived alone in a little house and remembered his wife, Ellie. People wanted him to leave, so Carl tied many balloons to his house and flew toward Paradise Falls, a place Ellie wanted to visit. A boy named Russell came along. The house flew through a storm and landed. Carl and Russell pulled it toward the falls. They met Kevin, a big colorful bird, and Doug, a dog who could talk. Kevin had baby birds waiting at home, so Carl promised to protect her. Three fierce dogs took Carl and Russell to Charles Muntz, who wanted to capture Kevin. Muntz took Carl's house and set it on fire. Carl let Muntz take Kevin so he could save the house. Later, Carl felt lonely, so Russell and Doug helped him rescue Kevin. Carl lost his house, but he kept Ellie's memories and made friends.

Carl Fredricksen wanted to go to Paradise Falls because Ellie had always wanted to see it. He lifted his little house with hundreds of balloons and flew away. Russell, a young wilderness explorer, was on the porch, so he traveled with Carl. After storms and fog, the house landed, and they pulled it along with a garden hose. Russell found a strange bird and named her Kevin. Then they met Doug, a talking dog. Carl learned that Kevin was a mother with baby birds at home, and he promised to keep her safe. Some fierce dogs found them and brought them to Charles Muntz, who wanted Kevin for himself. Muntz caught them and burned Carl's house. Carl chose to save the house, but later he missed Kevin and went back with Russell and Doug. They rescued her. The house fell down, but Carl still had Ellie’s memories and his new friends.

Carl had a house full of memories of Ellie, but the world around him was changing. He used balloons to carry the house toward Paradise Falls. Russell came with him and held on during storms and fog. When they landed, Carl and Russell walked while pulling the house. They found Kevin, a huge colorful bird, and Doug, a dog who could talk. Doug wanted to take Kevin to his master, but Carl promised Russell that he would protect her. Kevin was a mother, and her babies were waiting at home. Charles Muntz and his dogs tried to capture her. Muntz caught Carl and set the house on fire. Carl let Muntz take Kevin to save the house. At Paradise Falls, Carl felt lonely. Russell and Doug helped him return for Kevin. This time the house was lost. Carl was still happy because he had Ellie's memories and friends.

video_title: 100th day worries kids book read along

summaries.summary: Jessica worries about many things, and then she worries about the 100th day of school. Her teacher, Mr. Martin, says every child must bring 100 small things. Jessica thinks of ice cubes, marshmallows, toothpicks, yo-yos, and lipsticks, but every idea seems wrong. At school, she sees other children bring peanuts, paper clips, and peppermints. Jessica still has nothing. On Friday, her family helps her collect ten ribbons, ten screws, ten erasers, ten beads, ten buttons, ten pennies, ten nickels, ten barrettes, and ten rocks. These make 90 things. At lunch, Jessica reads a loving note from Mom and gets an idea. She adds ten kisses from Mom. Her collection now has 100 things given by her family. Mr. Martin says it is special because Jessica has brought 100 bits of love.

Jessica is a girl who worries about everything. When Mr. Martin announces the 100th day collection, she worries even more because she cannot choose 100 things. She thinks ice cubes will melt, marshmallows will be sticky, and toothpicks will be pointy. Her family suggests ideas, but nothing feels right. Each day, Jessica watches classmates bring collections to school, while she still has none. On the last morning, Jessica tells her parents that everyone may make fun of her. Her family gives her many groups of ten: ribbons, screws, erasers, beads, buttons, pennies, nickels, barrettes, and rocks. Jessica counts 90 things and still needs ten. Then she finds Mom's note in her lunchbox. Jessica has an idea and brings ten kisses from Mom. Together, the gifts make 100 things. Mr. Martin says the collection is 100 bits of love.

Jessica's class is preparing for the 100th day of school. Mr. Martin asks everyone to bring 100 small objects. Jessica worries because she cannot find the right collection. She sees Bobby bring 100 peanuts, Sharon bring 100 paper clips, and Ashley bring peppermints. Jessica feels sick because the last day arrives and she has nothing. Her father and mother, brother Tom, and sister Laura help her gather different objects. Each group has ten pieces, but there are only 90 objects. Jessica feels worried again. At lunchtime, she reads that her mother will help her later and that Mr. Martin will understand. Jessica then thinks of ten kisses from Mom. In the hall, she explains that all 100 things came from her family. The children think the collection is pretty and cool. Mr. Martin says it is very special and calls it 100 bits of love.

video_title: Strictly No Elephants

summaries.summary: A child has a tiny elephant for a pet, but having an unusual pet can make it hard to fit in. Every day, the child takes the elephant for a walk. The elephant does not like cracks in the sidewalk, so the child goes back to help him over them. The child says that friends lift each other over cracks. One day, they go to number 17 for Pet Club day. A sign on the door says, “Strictly no elephants.” The elephant leads the child away, bravely crossing the sidewalk cracks. A girl says that her skunks are not allowed to play either. The child and the girl decide to start their own club. They invite their new friends to play, paint a sign that says, “All are welcome,” and make sure no one is left behind.

Every day, a child walks with a tiny elephant. The elephant walks thoughtfully because he does not like cracks in the sidewalk. His friend goes back and helps him over the cracks. Then the child takes him to a Pet Club meeting at number 17, where everyone is supposed to be. At the door, they see a sign saying, “Strictly no elephants.” The tiny elephant turns back, but he does not worry about the cracks anymore. A girl asks whether they also tried to join the club. She has skunks, and the club does not want to let them play either. She says the skunks do not stink, and the child agrees. The child suggests starting a new club. The elephant follows as they go to a place where they can play. New friends join them. Together, they paint a sign saying, “All are welcome.” The elephant can give directions, and the friends do not leave anyone behind.

A child and a tiny elephant are close friends. They walk together each day, and the child helps the elephant cross the cracks he dislikes. The child explains that friends lift each other over cracks. On Pet Club day, they walk to number 17 because everyone will be there. But a sign on the door says, “Strictly no elephants,” so they cannot go inside. The tiny elephant leads the child back to the sidewalk and bravely walks over the cracks. A girl asks about the meeting. She has skunks, and the club does not want to play with them either. The child says the skunks do not know any better and agrees that the elephant does not stink. Then the child asks, “What if we start our own club?” The girl, the elephant, and their new friends play together. They paint a sign saying, “All are welcome,” because friends never leave anyone behind.

video_title: Alexander and the Wind-Up Mouse

summaries.summary: Alexander was a little mouse who lived in a house. People often chased him with a broom, even though he only wanted a few crumbs. One day, he met Willie, a windup toy mouse who had wheels and a key. Willie was loved and cuddled, while Alexander felt lonely and wished he could be like Willie. Willie told Alexander about a magic lizard who could change animals. Alexander searched for a purple pebble for many days, but could not find one. Then he found Willie in a box of old toys. Willie said the toys might be thrown away. Alexander saw a purple pebble in the box and took it to the lizard under the full moon. Instead of changing himself, Alexander asked the lizard to change Willie into a real mouse. The lizard did so. Alexander and Willie hugged and danced together until dawn.

Alexander did not feel loved. He was a small mouse, and people screamed or chased him when they saw him. In Annie's room, he met Willie, a windup mouse with two wheels and a key. Willie told Alexander that people played with him and loved him. The two mice became friends, but Alexander wished he could be cuddled too. Willie told him about a magic lizard near the blackberry bush. The lizard said Alexander needed a purple pebble when the moon was round. Alexander looked everywhere, but found only yellow, blue, and green pebbles. Then he discovered Willie in a box with old toys. Willie might be thrown away. Alexander found a purple pebble there and hurried to the garden. Under the full moon, he asked the lizard to make Willie a real mouse. A bright light flashed, and Willie became a mouse. The friends hugged and danced until morning.

A mouse named Alexander lived in a house and searched for crumbs. The people were not kind to him, so he hid in a hole. Alexander met Willie, Annie's favorite windup mouse. Willie could move when someone turned his key, and people cuddled him. Alexander loved Willie but felt envious because everyone loved the toy mouse. Willie told him about a colorful lizard that could change one animal into another. Alexander wanted to become a windup mouse, but the lizard asked for a purple pebble. After searching for days, Alexander found the pebble in a box where old toys were being kept. Willie was in the box and was afraid that the toys would be thrown away. Alexander brought the pebble to the lizard during the full moon. He chose to help Willie instead of changing himself. The lizard changed Willie into a real mouse, and the two friends celebrated together.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime - 𝑇ℎ𝑒 𝑆𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑔𝑒 𝐶𝑎𝑠𝑒 𝑜𝑓 𝑂𝑟𝑖𝑔𝑎𝑚𝑖 𝑌𝑜𝑑𝑎 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Tommy goes to the school’s PTA fun night with his friends Kellen and Harvey. They sit on the edge of the stage because they do not dance, while other students move around the cafeteria. Tommy wants to ask Hannah to dance, even though he really likes Sarah and feels too nervous to ask her. Before Tommy can reach Hannah, Dwight stops him and places Origami Yoda on his finger. Dwight says Tommy should ask the paper puppet for advice. Origami Yoda says, “Russian fools do,” which Tommy thinks means “Fools are in a rush.” Tommy decides not to hurry. A moment later, Hannah runs to a taller student named Mark, and they kiss. Tommy realizes that asking Hannah to dance would have embarrassed him. He believes Origami Yoda saved him, so he starts listening to its advice. Harvey doubts the puppet has magic, but Tommy admits that its advice worked and says it later helped Kellen too.

At the April school dance, Tommy sits with several students who feel like social outcasts. His friend Dwight is especially embarrassing because, at the previous dance, he danced strangely, slipped on a spilled drink, and asked Jennifer to dance after she had already rejected him. This time, Kellen and Harvey encourage Tommy to ask Hannah to dance. Tommy is nervous but begins walking toward her. Dwight interrupts and tells him to ask Origami Yoda first. The paper puppet gives its confusing advice: “Russian fools do.” Tommy and Kellen decide it probably means that fools rush into things, so Tommy waits. Harvey argues that Tommy should go ahead, but Tommy still hesitates. Then Mark, a much taller seventh grader, arrives. Hannah runs to Mark, and they kiss in the cafeteria. Tommy is relieved because he would have looked foolish trying to dance with Hannah. He decides Origami Yoda helped him, although Harvey insists the puppet is only paper.

Tommy describes the students who gather near the stage during the school’s monthly dance. He explains that he, Kellen, and Harvey usually watch instead of dancing, and that Dwight often makes the group look even more awkward. Tommy remembers Dwight’s disastrous attempt to dance with Jennifer at the previous fun night. During the new dance, Kellen and Harvey try to persuade Tommy to ask Hannah to dance. Tommy thinks she might say yes, but he is frightened because he really likes Sarah. Just as he prepares to approach Hannah, Dwight brings out Origami Yoda. The puppet’s strange message seems to warn Tommy not to rush. Tommy pauses, and then Hannah chooses to kiss Mark, a taller student who has just arrived. Tommy is thankful that he avoided humiliation and says Origami Yoda saved him. Harvey gives a skeptical explanation, but Tommy remains unsure whether the puppet is magical. He does know that its advice was useful and that many other students begin listening to it.

video_title: Frozen Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Frozen - A Tale of two Sisters

summaries.summary: Elsa and Anna are sisters. Elsa has magic powers that can make ice, but one day her magic hits Anna and makes her very cold. Their parents worry. Elsa stays away from Anna to keep her safe, and this makes Elsa sad. When they grow up, Anna meets Hans, and Elsa becomes queen. Anna wants to marry Hans, but Elsa says no. Elsa's magic escapes, so she runs away and covers the land with snow. Anna searches for her with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf. Elsa accidentally blasts Anna with ice, and Anna begins turning to ice. A troll says true love can save her. Hans wants the kingdom, not Anna. When Hans tries to hurt Elsa, Anna freezes solid while protecting her sister. Elsa cries and hugs Anna. Anna melts, and the sisters become best friends again.

Princess Elsa and Princess Anna love each other, but Elsa keeps a secret. She can create ice with magic. When Elsa's magic hurts Anna, Elsa stays away so Anna will be safe. Later, Anna meets Hans and wants to marry him. Elsa becomes queen and says no, and the sisters argue. Elsa's magic shoots from her hand, so she runs away. Snow covers the kingdom, and Elsa builds an ice palace. Anna goes to find her. Kristoff and Sven help Anna, and Olaf leads them to Elsa. Elsa is afraid of hurting Anna, but she becomes angry and sends ice at her. Anna starts to freeze. A troll says an act of true love can save her. Hans only wants to rule the kingdom. When he attacks Elsa, Anna protects her sister and freezes solid. Elsa hugs Anna, and Anna melts because of her loving act. The sisters are best friends at last.

Elsa and Anna grow up as sisters. Elsa can make ice, but her magic once hits Anna and makes her very cold. To protect Anna, Elsa stays away from her. Anna is sad and later falls in love with Hans. When Elsa becomes queen, Anna asks to marry Hans, but Elsa refuses. Their argument makes Elsa's magic appear, and Elsa runs away. She covers the land with snow and makes an ice palace. Anna searches for Elsa with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf. Elsa accidentally hits Anna with ice, and Anna begins to turn to ice. An old troll explains that an act of true love may save Anna. Hans does not love Anna; he wants to rule the kingdom. He tries to hurt Elsa, but Anna gets in the way and freezes solid. Elsa is safe, and she hugs her sister. Anna melts because her loving act saves them. Elsa and Anna become best friends.

video_title: The Astonishing Secret of Awesome Man

summaries.summary: Awesome Man is a superhero with a red cape, a dark mask, flying powers, eye beams, and a very strong power grip. Because he is so strong, he worries that he might hurt someone or destroy a city. He flies to his quiet fortress under the Arctic Ocean and squeezes himself in his giant power grip. This helps him calm down and discover that he is almost out of positrons and is very tired. Mos the Awesome dog brings him a special protein orb and salt. After resting, Awesome Man follows the Flaming Eyeball to a wicked headquarters. He finds the villain with Sister Sinister and the Red Shark, uses his power grip and eye beams, and gets away. Awesome Man tells about his amazing superhero powers. He can fly very fast, shoot positronic rays, and use an awesome power grip strong enough to hug a runaway train. Awesome Man feels angry, but he knows his great strength could hurt people or damage a city. He goes home to the Fortress of Awesome beneath the Arctic Ocean. The quiet place helps him calm down. Awesome Man feels so angry that he must be careful not to hit or throw things and hurt somebody. He returns to his peaceful underwater fortress and gives himself a giant awesome power grip. Then he understands that he is tired because superhero fighting uses many positrons. Mos brings a protein orb from the fortress kitchen and a little salt. After he becomes calm and strong again, Awesome Man follows the Flaming Eyeball around the world and to the sun. He spies on the villain with Sister Sinister and the Red Shark, attacks them with his grip and eye beams, and returns home to his mother, who gives him food and receives a hug.

video_title: The Widows Broom | Read Aloud | Fall | Autumn | Witches | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: An old witch’s broom loses its flying magic and drops the witch beside Mina Shaw’s farmhouse. Mina is frightened, but she kindly helps the bruised witch into bed. During the night, the witch calls another witch with a blue fire and flies away, leaving the old broom behind. Mina discovers that the broom can sweep by itself. She teaches it many jobs, such as chopping wood, fetching water, feeding chickens, helping the cow, and playing simple piano tunes. Mina’s neighbors, the Spiveys, become afraid of the broom. When two Spivey boys bother it, the broom knocks them down, so Mr. Spivvy and other men burn it. The Spiveys soon see a white broom ghost and move away. Mina stays. That night, she learns the broom is not a ghost at all. It is her painted broom, and it bows before playing music for her.

One autumn night, a witch falls from the sky when her broom suddenly stops flying. Mina Shaw finds her in the garden and takes care of her. After healing, the witch leaves with another witch, but her powerless broom remains. Mina uses it as an ordinary broom until it begins sweeping on its own. The broom is eager to learn, and Mina teaches it to do many useful chores. The neighbors notice it. Mr. Spivvy thinks it is evil, even though it helps Mina and plays the piano. His boys tease the broom, throw stones in its path, and tap it with sticks. The broom hits the boys, and their father brings men to destroy it. They tie the broom to a stake and burn it. Later, the Spiveys find their dog safe in a tree, but a white broom carrying an axe frightens them away. Mina remains at home. She then discovers that the frightening ghost is really her broom covered in white paint.

Mina Shaw lives alone in a small farmhouse. She helps a witch who crashes in her garden, and the witch later flies away with a friend, leaving an old broom behind. The broom seems ordinary at first, but soon it sweeps without help. Mina is nervous, yet she sees that it works hard and learns quickly. It chops wood, carries water, cares for animals, and plays piano notes. Mina’s neighbors hear about it. The Spivey family’s father calls it wicked, while others notice that it is useful. Two Spivey boys cruelly disturb the broom, and it knocks them over. Their father and three farmers burn the broom. The family’s dog is found alive in a spruce tree. Soon a white broom ghost appears at the Spiveys’ house with an axe, so the family packs up and leaves. Mina chooses to stay. At home, she finds the broom safe, painted white, and happily playing music.

video_title: Cars Read Along Story Book | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids | Cars 3 Storybook

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen was a very fast race car with a wonderful coach named Doc Hudson. A new racer, Jackson Storm, raced faster, and Lightning crashed. Lightning kept trying and went to train at a special place with Cruz Ramirez. The training was hard and sometimes silly. Lightning broke a racing simulator, then tried racing at a beach and in a wild demolition derby. Lightning learned that Cruz had always dreamed of being a racer, but she had lost her confidence. In Thomasville, Smokey and Doc’s old friends helped Lightning train. Cruz became his training partner and even beat him in a race. At the big Florida race, Lightning realized Cruz needed a chance. Lightning McQueen wanted to keep racing after Jackson Storm caused him to crash. He went to a high-tech training center and met Cruz Ramirez, a young trainer. Cruz made Lightning do special exercises, but Lightning broke the racing simulator. They tried training at the beach, then went to Thunder Hollow Speedway in disguise. The race was a demolition derby, and Lightning helped Cruz when Miss Fritter chased her. After Cruz’s accident removed Lightning’s disguise, he felt the training was not working. Then he learned that Cruz had always wanted to race. Lightning and Cruz visited Doc Hudson’s hometown. Smokey, who had coached Doc, helped them meet Doc’s racing friends and trained them with tractors. Cruz beat Lightning before the Florida race. Lightning understood that Cruz deserved her dream. He gave her his race, and she wore number 95. Cruz passed the racers, flipped over Jackson Storm, and won. Lightning and Cruz continued racing as a team.

Lightning McQueen was a famous racer who loved racing because Doc Hudson had taught him to work hard. When young racer Jackson Storm became faster, Lightning crashed but did not quit. He trained with Cruz Ramirez, although the exercises, simulator, beach, and demolition derby did not go as planned. Lightning discovered that Cruz wanted to race, but she had become a trainer after losing confidence. In Thomasville, Smokey told stories about Doc and showed Lightning that Doc had been smart, not only fast. Smokey coached Lightning, and Cruz trained beside him. Cruz later beat Lightning on the track. At the Florida race, Lightning remembered how Cruz had trained and helped him. He decided she should have a chance to follow her dream. Ramone painted her car number 95. Cruz raced for Lightning, survived Storm’s push, used Doc’s flipping trick, and won. Cruz began her racing career, while Lightning continued racing with her.

video_title: 🐧 Lost and Found | Read Aloud for Kids | Oliver Jeffers Picture Book Storytime

summaries.summary: A boy finds a sad penguin at his door. The penguin follows him everywhere, so the boy thinks it is lost and tries to find its home. The lost-and-found office, some birds, and the boy’s duck cannot help. The boy learns that penguins come from the South Pole. He tries to get a big ship to take them, but nobody hears his small voice. Then he and the penguin use a little rowboat. They travel for many days over calm and rough water while the boy tells stories. At the South Pole, the boy leaves the penguin. But the penguin looks even sadder, and the boy understands that it was not lost. It was lonely. The boy turns around and searches for it. At last, he sees the penguin in the water. The boy and the penguin go home together, talking all the way.

One day, a boy opens his door and finds a penguin. The penguin looks unhappy and follows him, so the boy decides it must be lost. He asks many people and animals for help, but nobody knows where the penguin belongs. The boy discovers that penguins come from the South Pole. He tries to ask a large ship for a ride, but the ship’s horn is too loud. The boy and the penguin take a rowboat instead. They pack what they need and sail south through good weather and giant waves. When they arrive, the boy helps the penguin out of the boat and starts home. Then he looks back and sees that the penguin is very sad. The boy realizes the penguin was lonely and needed company. He quickly rows back, but the penguin is gone. On the way home, he spots the penguin in the water. They find each other and return home together.

A boy wants to help a penguin that comes to his door. He looks for the penguin’s home by asking the lost-and-found office, birds, and his duck, but no one can help. The boy learns that penguins live at the South Pole. Because a big ship cannot hear him, he chooses to row there with the penguin. They travel across the sea for many days and nights. The boy tells stories, and the penguin listens. At the South Pole, the boy thinks his job is finished. He lets the penguin out and rows away. Soon he notices that the penguin is sadder than before. The boy thinks carefully and sees his mistake: the penguin was lonely, not lost. He turns around and rows back quickly. He cannot find the penguin at first, so he begins going home sadly. Then he sees the penguin in the water. They go home together, talking about wonderful things.

video_title: If Your Best Friend is a Mermaid Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy

The story follows a child who has a mermaid for a best friend. They sing with an underwater choir instead of being squished by whales, admire pearls inside opening clams, and feed dolphins. The dolphins carry the child swimming and flying. Next, the friends ride to a castle in a golden carriage pulled by six seahorses. The mermaid serves salty water and seaweed for lunch, and a spilled drink simply washes away. After a wonderful day, the tired child goes home. The mermaid sings a bedtime song and becomes a doll to stay nearby.

Having a mermaid as a best friend brings many underwater adventures. The child can choose her name and use Mermaid Magic to swim without diving gear. While swimming into the dark ocean, the child sees a shark and feels afraid, but the shark belongs to the mermaid’s friends and only smiles with toothy grins. The child helps keep the seaweed neat with a giant comb. Huge whales are not dangerous, because the friends sing with an underwater choir instead. They discover mighty clams filled with beautiful pearls and gently feed dolphins. The dolphins take the child swimming and flying. For a meal, the friends ride in a golden carriage pulled by six seahorses to the mermaid’s castle. The meal is salty water and seaweed, and underwater spills clean themselves. After enjoying the water, the exhausted child goes home. The mermaid sings as the child sleeps, then changes into a doll and stays all night.

video_title: Bluey Camping kids book read along

summaries.summary: Bluey goes camping and wants to build a stick house with Bingo, but Bingo goes with Mom, so Bluey walks to the creek alone. There, Bluey meets John Luke. They build a stick house together and plant a seed that may grow fruit someday. They are hungry now, so they try to catch a wild pig, but it gets away. They are happy to play together, but John Luke must soon leave because his holiday is over. Bluey feels sad and asks Mom why special people have to go away. During a camping trip, Bluey goes to the creek to find sticks. She meets a boy named John Luke, even though she cannot understand all his words. A wild pig comes through the forest, and Bluey and John Luke try to catch it. Their first plan fails. The next morning, they try again. Bluey uses a trick her dad taught her, and John Luke jumps out when the pig appears. They catch the pig and celebrate. Soon, Bluey finds that their seed has started to grow into a little tree, but John Luke is gone. His holiday has ended. Bluey is sad, and Mom explains that special people sometimes stay only for a short time. The happy things they did together still matter.

Bluey wants a camping friend, and she finds one when she meets John Luke near the creek. Together, they make a stick house and plant a seed. They hope the seed will become a fruit tree, but they need food before it grows. A wild pig runs through the forest, so the children make a plan. The pig escapes at first, but Bluey remembers what her dad taught her. She scares the pig, and John Luke helps them catch it. The children are glad they worked together. The next morning, the seed is becoming a little tree, but John Luke is not at his campsite. Mom tells Bluey that John Luke has gone home because his holiday is over. Bluey feels sad because she liked her new friend. Mom says special people can come into our lives, stay for a while, and then leave. Bluey remembers catching the pig with John Luke and feels that their happy time was worth it.

video_title: Olive the other reindeer kids book read along

summaries.summary: Olive was a little dog who took walks every day. On Christmas Eve, she heard a song about the other reindeer and wondered if she might be a reindeer too. Olive was wrapping presents when she heard a Christmas song about reindeer. She sang along and decided she must be a reindeer, even though she thought she was a dog.
