On a winter holiday day, Olive heard people singing, “All of the other reindeer.” She sang too and thought, “I must be a reindeer.” She went to the North Pole, where Santa and the elves were preparing presents. Santa let Olive fly with the reindeer, and Comet tied her safely to the sleigh. The other reindeer looked at Olive and crashed into a tree. Olive could not fly up, but she climbed and chewed the sticks that held the sleigh. Then her nose helped again. She smelled gumdrops dropping from the sleigh, so Santa saved them. When flutes fell through a hole, Olive fetched every one while Santa repaired the sleigh. Near home, fog slowed the team and made them sleepy. Olive smelled Mrs. CLA's cookies and led the sleigh to the North Pole. Santa gave Olive antlers that fit perfectly.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑇ℎ𝑒 𝑆ℎ𝑎𝑑𝑜𝑤 𝐶𝑖𝑝ℎ𝑒𝑟 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: In 1855, William Covington Hanover follows Ava O’Neill through snowy New York. He wants to learn the secrets of Teresa and Theodore Morningstar, famous inventors who have disappeared after creating a mysterious treasure hunt called the Old York Cipher. William pretends to be a gentleman, but Ava knows he is a thief. When he threatens her and knocks away her book, Ava breaks his finger, hurts his knee, and calls the police. The coppers arrest William while Ava safely enters the Morningstar building. In the present day, Tess Biederman lives in that same building with her twin brother, Theo, and her unusual hybrid cat, Nine. Tess worries that developer Darnell Slant will buy their home and replace old buildings with new ones. She visits the post office for her grandfather and finds a strange letter sealed with gold wax and marked “Trust no one.” Although Tess tries not to worry, the Old York Cipher seems to be waking up and choosing her and other children for a new adventure.

The story begins on New Year’s Eve in old New York. William Covington Hanover is a thief wearing stolen fine clothes. He follows Ava O’Neill because she works for the missing Morningstar twins, Teresa and Theodore. The twins left behind a city trust and a series of clues leading to a hidden treasure. William believes Ava knows where the treasure is, so he tries to trick her into helping him. Ava is much stronger and cleverer than he expects. She breaks his pinky, knocks him down, and summons the coppers. Years later, Tess Biederman lives at Ava’s old address. Tess’s brother Theo has won a Lego contest, but Tess is more interested in the Morningstars, their inventions, and the Old York Cipher. She is afraid that Darnell Slant will buy the family’s building. At the post office, Tess discovers a carefully sealed letter saying, “Trust no one.” Nine keeps hold of it. Tess hopes for a peaceful summer, but the mysterious cipher appears ready to bring danger and change into her life.

Ava O’Neill protects the Morningstars’ secrets from William Covington Hanover, a thief who follows her through the snow. The Morningstar twins were famous for inventions that made New York bright, unusual, and full of machines. After they vanished, they left clues to a treasure in the Old York Cipher. William thinks Ava can lead him to the treasure, but she refuses to be frightened. She defeats him and lets the police take him away. In modern New York, Tess lives in the same Morningstar building with her family and Nine, a large spotted cat who is part Siamese and serval. Tess fears that Darnell Slant’s plans to replace old buildings will destroy her home. Her mother sends her to collect Grandpa Ben’s mail. Tess remembers that Grandpa once studied the cipher and believed it could almost solve people while they tried to solve it. In the mailbox, she finds a gold-sealed letter marked “Trust no one.” Nine will not release it. Tess decides to imagine good possibilities, but the cipher has already begun its next move.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse 📖 Read Along Storybook for Kids | Mickey's Mystery List

summaries.summary: Minnie, Goofy, Donald, and Daisy make a secret list for a surprise party. The list has rhyming clues. A gust of wind blows it away, so everyone looks for it. Mickey finds the list when Pluto brings back a piece of paper. Mickey thinks the surprise is for someone at the clubhouse, so he goes shopping. He solves the clues and gets hot dogs, flowers, a book, a bike, a bone for Pluto, and party hats. The last clue says to get a sweet dessert, but Mickey does not know what it means. When Mickey returns, his friends tell him the list was for his surprise birthday party. Minnie brings out a big birthday cake. Mickey solved the riddles and found most of the surprises, but the final surprise was the cake. Everyone is happy and surprised together.

Minnie opens her window and sees a sunny day. She plans a surprise party with her friends and writes a secret shopping list using rhyming riddles. The wind carries the list away. Minnie and her friends search for it, while Mickey finds it with Pluto. Mickey decides to collect the things on the list. He guesses that the first clue means hot dogs and buys hot dogs, buns, and mustard. Then he buys flower bouquets, a book, a bicycle, a big bone, and party hats. One last clue asks for a sweet dessert to share. Mickey cannot get that item. At the clubhouse, he learns the list was made for his birthday. Minnie and the others wanted to surprise him. Minnie brings out a magnificent cake, and everyone laughs and celebrates because Mickey solved the clues.

A secret party is being planned at the clubhouse. Minnie loses the shopping list when the wind blows it behind some trees. Her friends search, but they do not find it. Pluto finds the paper while playing fetch with Mickey. Mickey reads the rhyming clues and shops for the party. He gets tasty hot dogs, pretty flowers, a book called Mousechanics, a bike with a bow, a large dog bone, and hats for the guests. The final clue describes a dessert that must be baked and shared. Mickey returns without it and sees that his friends are sad. Then Minnie explains that the list was for Mickey's surprise birthday party. She brings out a birthday cake, which is the missing dessert. Mickey is pleased, and everyone is glad that the surprise worked.

video_title: One Witch

summaries.summary: A witch on a hill had an empty pot. One by one, spooky friends brought her strange things to fill it. Two cats brought a fish's tail. Scarecrows brought a blackbird's claw, goblins brought slimy slugs, and vampires brought fresh blood juice. Mummies, owls, ghosts, skeletons, and werewolves brought a moth, a rattlesnake, a hunk of hair, a finger bone, and spider soup. The witch planned a spooky bash. She emptied her bag and sent her trusty bats to call all her friends. Then she mixed and stirred her oozing stew and boiled and burned her gurgling goo. The werewolves, skeletons, ghosts, owls, mummies, vampires, goblins, scarecrows, and cats came. They ate the gruesome brew, everybody loved it, and they saved the last bowl just for you.

One witch needed to fill an empty pot. Many spooky creatures helped her. Cats gave her a fish's tail, scarecrows gave her a blackbird's claw, and goblins gave her slimy slugs. Vampires added fresh blood juice. Mummies brought a musty moth, owls brought a rattlesnake, ghosts brought a hunk of hair, skeletons brought a finger bone, and werewolves brought spider soup. With all these things, the witch planned a spooky party. She took her bag, emptied it, and sent her trusty bats to call the creatures. They came from their caves, graves, resting places, nests, tombs, rooms, holes, poles, and the cats' can. The witch mixed and stirred her stew. She boiled and burned the gurgling goo. Then her good friends ate the gruesome brew. Everybody loved it, and one last bowl was saved for you.

A witch lived on a hill with an empty pot. She received unusual gifts from her spooky friends: a fish's tail, a blackbird's claw, slimy slugs, fresh blood juice, a musty moth, a rattlesnake, a hunk of hair, a finger bone, and spider soup. After collecting the gifts, the witch planned her spooky bash. She took her bag and dumped her haul. Then she sent trusty bats to call the friends. The creatures came in a counting-down order, from ten werewolves to nine skeletons, eight ghosts, seven owls, six mummies, five vampires, four goblins, three scarecrows, two cats, and one witch. The witch mixed and stirred her oozing stew. She boiled and burned it until it was gurgling goo. The friends came and ate the gruesome brew. Everybody loved it, and they saved the last bowl just for you.

video_title: Toy Story Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Toy Story - Mixed Signals

summaries.summary: The toys were excited because Bonnie was going to the park. Jessie worried that Buzz had a loose wire. Bonnie asked Buzz to watch the toys while she was away. The peas began bouncing, and Buzz said it was dangerous. Slinky Dog fell, and many toys landed on Buzz. Buzz began speaking strangely and running around. He grabbed a curtain like a cape. Ham tried to stop him, but Ham slid into a bookshelf. A book fell on Buzz. After the fall, Buzz repeated what other toys said. The toys tried bouncing him on the bed, but Buzz flew off and would not move. When Bonnie came home, the toys tried to fix him. Jessie came out of Bonnie's backpack and tapped Buzz on the back. Buzz blinked and spoke normally again. The toys cleaned the room, and Bonnie found everything tidy. She thanked Buzz for taking care of things.

Bonnie left for the park and put Buzz in charge of the toys. Jessie told the others to watch him because he was acting funny. When the peas played, Buzz tried to stop them. Slinky Dog fell from the shelf, and toys tumbled onto Buzz. Buzz then spoke in a strange way. He ran away and used a dollhouse curtain like a cape. Ham chased him, but Ham slid into a bookshelf. A book fell on Buzz, and Buzz started repeating words. The toys tried to help him. They put him on the bed and bounced him, but he flew onto the floor and stopped moving. The toys heard a car. They hurried to fix Buzz before Bonnie returned. Rex looked at the wires, but the toys did not know which wires to use. Jessie returned with Woody and Dolly. Jessie hit Buzz gently on the back. Buzz started working normally. The toys cleaned the room before Bonnie came in.

The toys had a busy day in Bonnie's room. Bonnie asked Buzz to keep everyone under control while she went to the park. Buzz tried to stop the peas from bouncing, but Slinky Dog fell and many toys fell on Buzz. After that, Buzz spoke strangely, ran away, and carried a curtain like a cape. Ham tried to catch him and crashed into a bookshelf. A book landed on Buzz. Buzz was not hurt, but he repeated everything he heard. The toys tried tickling him and shouting, but he stayed still after flying off the bed. They opened his back panel and looked at his wires. Then Jessie came home with Woody and Dolly. Trixie stood Buzz up, but he fell down. Jessie shook her head and tapped Buzz on the back. Buzz blinked and asked if he had something on his face. The toys were happy because Buzz was himself again. They tidied the room, and Bonnie thanked Buzz.

video_title: Frozen Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Frozen - Olaf's Summer Day

summaries.summary: Olaf the snowman had never known summer, but he dreamed about it. He imagined wishing on dandelions, splashing in puddles, resting on a sunny beach, and drinking juice in sunglasses. He imagined dancing and having fun with friends on the sand. He wanted to wear a hat, swim in the blue sea, and make water angels. He also imagined lying in the grass and watching funny cloud shapes. At sunset, Olaf dreamed of sitting in a tub with hot chocolate. He loved summer in his imagination, but he wondered why the marshmallows melted. Then Olaf told Anna and Kristoff about his dream. Anna said she would be by his side in every season. Kristoff began to speak, but Olaf talked about puddles again. Anna and Kristoff nodded and let Olaf dream big.

Olaf wanted to know what summer was like. He imagined a warm day filled with happy things. He would wish on dandelions and splash in puddles. He would sit on a bright beach with sunglasses and juice, then dance on the sand with his friends. Olaf thought summer would be a perfect time to celebrate. He and his friends would wear hats so the Sun would not give them a tan. Olaf also imagined swimming in the clear sea and making water angels. In the grass, he would watch clouds make funny shapes. At night, he would relax in a tub with hot chocolate. Olaf said he loved summer, but he noticed his marshmallows were melting. He shared his dream with Anna and Kristoff. Anna promised to be by his side, and Kristoff started to answer. Olaf interrupted with his favorite thought about puddles, so his friends nodded and let him keep dreaming.

Olaf dreamed of a wonderful summer, even though he had never known one. In his dream, he found dandelions, splashed in puddles, and rested on a beach with sunglasses and juice. He danced on the sand with new friends and celebrated the sunny season. Everyone wore hats, because the Sun could give them a tan. Olaf went into the clear blue sea and made water angels. Then he lay in the grass and watched clouds move across the sky. Some clouds looked funny and made him smile. When the Sun went down, Olaf sat in a tub and drank hot chocolate. He said he loved summer, but his marshmallows were melting. Later, he told Anna and Kristoff about his summer dream. Anna said she would be by his side no matter the season. Kristoff began a sentence about summer turning Olaf into a..., but Olaf interrupted. He talked about splashing in puddles, and Anna and Kristoff nodded.

video_title: Muncha! Muncha! Muncha! by Candace Fleming

summaries.summary: Mr. McGrey wanted a garden with lettuce, carrots, peas, and tomatoes. He planted the seeds and watched the vegetables grow. Then three hungry bunnies came at night and munched on the garden. Mr. McGrey was angry. First, he made a small wire fence. The bunnies still ate the plants. Next, he built a tall wall, but the bunnies still got into the garden. Then he made a deep, wet trench. The bunnies kept coming. Finally, Mr. McGrey built a huge thing around the garden. The bunnies looked, smelled, and touched it, but then they hopped away. In the morning, Mr. McGrey saw that his vegetables were untouched. He danced because he thought he had won. Then he climbed over, jumped across, squeezed between, and crawled under his garden defenses. He picked his vegetables and reached for something yummy.

For a long time, Mr. McGrey dreamed about growing vegetables. One spring, he finally planted a garden. Soon, lettuce, carrots, peas, and tomatoes grew. Mr. McGrey was excited to eat them. But three bunnies came when the sun went down. They munched on the new sprouts. Mr. McGrey put a wire fence around the garden. The next night, the bunnies came again and nibbled the leaves. He built a tall wooden wall. Then the bunnies chewed the stems, so he dug a deep, wet trench. Still, he tried one more time. He made a huge, enormous thing around the garden. The bunnies looked at it and went away. Mr. McGrey found his vegetables safe the next morning. He celebrated with a funny dance. Then he went through all the fences, walls, and barriers to get to his garden. He picked the vegetables and reached inside his full basket for something yummy.

Mr. McGrey wanted to grow and eat fresh vegetables, so he planted a garden. His garden grew lettuce, carrots, peas, and tomatoes. At night, three hungry bunnies came to eat the plants. Mr. McGrey did not want them in his garden. He made a small wire fence, but the bunnies got past it. He made a tall wooden wall, but they came again. He dug a deep, wet trench, but the bunnies still visited. Mr. McGrey became furious and built a huge, enormous barrier. He said the bunnies could not get through, under, or over it. The bunnies looked, smelled, and touched the barrier, then hopped away. Mr. McGrey saw his vegetables were safe and did a jiggly victory dance. After that, he climbed over, jumped across, squeezed between, and crawled under his barriers. He reached his garden, picked the vegetables, and reached into his overflowing basket for something yummy.

video_title: Cars 🚗 Storybook 📚 Read Along Story books 📖 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen was a bright red race car who loved winning. His pit crews kept leaving because he thought he could do everything alone. One night, he hurried to a big race, and Mack the Truck drove for too long. Mack got tired, swerved, and Lightning fell out. Lightning ended up in Radiator Springs. He drove fast, knocked things down, and damaged Main Street. The sheriff took him to jail. Mater, a friendly tow truck, wanted to be his friend. Doc said Lightning could leave after fixing the road. Lightning rushed and made the road worse. He raced Doc, crashed into cactuses, and Mater helped him. Lightning learned that the town was special and that Doc had been a champion racer. Lightning fixed the road. The townspeople cleaned and repaired him. At the end, Lightning returned to racing with Doc, a new pit crew, and new best friends.

Lightning McQueen was a famous red race car with a lightning bolt. He liked races so much that he had no friends except Mack, who carried him to races. When Lightning made Mack drive too long, Mack became tired and Lightning fell from the truck. Lightning reached Radiator Springs and chased through the town. He damaged Main Street, so the sheriff took him to jail. Mater, a rusty tow truck, was kind to him. In court, Doc said Lightning had to fix the road before leaving. Lightning worked too quickly and made the road bumpy. Doc challenged him to a race, but Lightning crashed into a cactus patch. Mater helped him. Lightning then learned that the townspeople loved their home, Sally loved Radiator Springs, and Doc had once been a champion racer. Lightning fixed the road and let the town make him shiny and new. He left with Doc and a friendly new pit crew.

Lightning McQueen wanted to reach a very big race quickly. He was a flashy red race car, but he believed he did not need help. Mack the Truck became tired while driving, and Lightning fell out. He found the little town of Radiator Springs and made a big mess on Main Street while trying to get away from the sheriff. The sheriff took him to jail. Mater became Lightning's friend, and Sally helped make a deal with Doc. Lightning could go after fixing the road. He hurried, but the road became bumpier. Doc raced Lightning, and Lightning crashed into a cactus patch. Mater helped him, and Lightning began to learn about his new friends and their town. He learned that Doc had been a champion racer. Lightning fixed the road, and the townspeople cleaned him, gave him tires, paint, and oil. Then he went back to the racetrack with Doc and new best friends.

video_title: The Leaf Thief | Fall Read Aloud | Creative Read Alouds

summaries.summary: A squirrel is making its nest while enjoying the red, gold, and orange leaves. Then the squirrel sees that one leaf is missing and thinks someone stole it. The squirrel asks Bird and Mouse, but Mouse says the leaf belongs to Mouse. The next morning, the squirrel sees that more leaves are gone. Woodpecker says the leaves belong to Woodpecker, and Bird tells the squirrel that no one is stealing the leaves. The following morning, the squirrel asks Bird if Bird is the leaf thief. Bird shows the squirrel what is happening. The wind shakes the trees, rustles the leaves, and even takes the squirrel’s hat. Bird explains that the leaves change colors and the wind blows them away every autumn. They will grow back in spring. The squirrel understands that there is no leaf thief and goes to sleep. The next morning, the squirrel says someone has stolen the grass too.

The squirrel feels happy in its nest, with hazelnuts in its belly and sunshine above the leafy canopy. The leaves are beautiful red, gold, and orange. Suddenly, one leaf is missing. The squirrel asks Bird where it is and worries that someone stole it. Mouse has a leaf, but Mouse says it is Mouse’s leaf. Bird says it is normal to lose a leaf in this season. The next day, the squirrel finds more leaves missing and asks Woodpecker about them. Woodpecker says the leaves belong to Woodpecker. Bird tells the squirrel to relax. On the next morning, the squirrel asks Bird to find the leaf thief. Bird points all around. The wind shakes trees, rustles leaves, and takes the squirrel’s hat. The squirrel learns that the wind takes the leaves every autumn. The leaves change colors, blow away, and grow back in spring. The squirrel realizes that no thief took the leaves and plans to sleep well.

A squirrel notices a missing leaf and becomes worried. The squirrel asks Bird, Mouse, and then Woodpecker about the missing leaves. Mouse and Woodpecker each say that the leaves they have belong to them. Bird says that losing leaves is normal and tells the squirrel that this happened last year too. The squirrel tries to relax, but the next morning feels that it is a disaster because still more leaves are missing. The squirrel asks Bird if Bird is the leaf thief. Bird says no and shows the squirrel the real cause. The wind is all around them. It shakes the trees, rustles the leaves, and takes the squirrel’s hat. Bird explains that autumn comes every year. During autumn, leaves change colors and the wind blows them away. The leaves will grow back in spring. The squirrel understands that there is no leaf thief and says, “Silly me.” The squirrel goes to sleep, but the next morning says that someone has stolen the grass.

video_title: Kindergarten, Here I Come!

summaries.summary: A child gets ready for kindergarten by checking a backpack, glue, clothes, crayons, and scissors. The child also wants to bring a cuddle bear, a magic wand, and other special things, but Mom says they are not needed. At school, the teacher knows the child’s name and makes the day feel fun. The child learns to sit crisscross applesauce, listens to stories, eats a cupcake, and loses a tooth while eating an apple. At recess, the children pretend to be many exciting characters. They count classroom objects, visit the zoo, meet a guinea pig, plant seeds, and celebrate the 100th day. The child has changing best friends and makes a hand puppet for show and tell. The child notices growing clothes and shoes. On the last day, the child hugs the teacher and says the class is going to first grade.

Before school starts, a child checks a list of things needed for kindergarten. Mom says everything is ready, even though the child wants to take many toys and tools. The first school day brings a kind teacher, sitting lessons, story time, lunch, recess, and a nap. The child imagines being a fireman, monkey, climber, queen, raccoon, and rocket pilot during recess. In class, the child counts children, animals, crayons, cars, blocks, and cans. There is a loud and happy field trip to the zoo. The child tries several best friends, but friends change when someone talks too much, will not share blocks, or eats part of a cupcake. The child also talks with the classroom guinea pig, celebrates the 100th day, and makes a finger puppet for show and tell. Seeds grow, clothes become too small, and kindergarten ends as first grade begins.

The child says, “Kindergarten, here I come,” and prepares for school. The child packs school supplies but wants to bring a cuddle bear, magic wand, cape, flashlights, and a tool set too. At school, the teacher quickly learns the child’s name and sees that the child is nice, smart, and good at art. The child learns classroom routines, hears stories, opens a yellow lunchbox, and finds a favorite chocolate cupcake. During recess, everyone pretends and plays. The child counts many things, goes on a field trip to the zoo, and falls asleep during nap time. Friends change throughout the day, but a friend later asks to paint together. The child teaches George Washington, the class guinea pig, some lessons. The child shows a hand at show and tell, leads a line, watches a seedling grow, and realizes they have grown too. Finally, the child hugs the teacher and says they are going to first grade.

video_title: Delight in Your Hue | Let’s celebrate diversity

summaries.summary: Bo was a small blue fish who lived alone in a cave. One night, he woke up frightened and traveled to a place filled with colorful fish and bright lights. Some fish told him that he could not be alone and tried to cover his blue color. Bo felt nervous, homesick, and unseen, but he kept exploring. In a beautiful cove, the Creator told Bo that every fish was a work of art and that all colors were reflections of the Creator. Bo saw his own portrait and learned that every fish had a special light to share. When the fish joined together, their lights grew brighter. Bo then helped the fish listen to one another and work together. Fish of many colors gathered, placed rocks carefully, and made a stunning rainbow. They learned that love and teamwork can make the world more beautiful, and Bo understood that every color matters.

A little fish named Bo lived by himself deep inside a cave. He was used to being alone, but one night he was suddenly sent on a journey. He discovered red fish, green fish, and a wonderful cove glowing with many colors. At first, Bo was afraid to dance with the red fish, and he felt unseen. Then the Creator spoke to him and said, “I delight in your blue.” The Creator explained that every fish was made as a work of art, and that no single color could show all the beauty in the world. Bo saw his portrait and began to understand. He wanted the other fish to share in this joy. He encouraged fish of different colors and patterns to listen closely and help one another. Together, they placed rocks with care and created a beautiful rainbow. Bo and the fish discovered that friendship, service, and teamwork bring hope.

Bo, a blue fish, began his life alone in a cave. After a frightening journey, he met colorful fish. The red fish invited him to a party, but Bo felt nervous when they stared at him. He also saw green fish and a cove filled with colorful lights. There, the Creator told Bo that every fish was a reflection of the Creator and that all the different colors were important. Bo found his portrait displayed with many other bright fish. He realized that the fish were missing the joy planned for them because they were not connected. Bo decided to help. Fish that were purple, pink, green, blue, striped, or spotted came together in many shapes and sizes. By listening closely, they found hurts they could mend. They served one another and worked as a team, carefully placing rocks until a rainbow appeared. Bo learned that each fish has a light to show, and that love can help the whole world become more beautiful.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝐴 𝑇𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝐷𝑎𝑟𝑘 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐺𝑟𝑖𝑚𝑚 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: In the kingdom of Grimm, an old king is dying. He asks his faithful servant, Johannes, to care for his young son and show him everything he inherits except one locked room. The room contains a portrait of the Golden Princess, and the old king warns that seeing it will make his son fall in love and may cost him his life. After becoming king, the young prince insists on entering the room. He sees the beautiful princess and immediately wants to marry and save her, even after learning that she is cursed and that her husbands have died. Johannes gathers gold, disguises himself and the king as merchants, and visits the princess. She follows them to the ship because she loves the golden treasures. When she discovers she has been taken away, she protests, but learns that the merchant is a king who loves her. Johannes says she may return without the gold, so she chooses to marry the young king, and they live happily ever after.

Faithful Johannes has served several generations of kings when the old king gives him an important final task. Johannes must support the new king, but he must never show him the portrait of the Golden Princess because she is dangerous to love. The new king becomes curious about the single locked room in his castle and refuses to stop asking about it. Once Johannes opens the door, the king sees the princess's portrait and faints. He learns that she lives alone in a black marble palace, is cursed, and has lost husbands who tried to marry her. Still, he decides he must have her. Johannes uses the princess's love of gold to make a plan. He and the king sail to her land with beautiful golden objects. The princess follows Johannes to the ship to see more treasures. The king reveals that he is a king and loves her. Although she is angry about being carried away, she decides to marry him after learning she can keep the gold.

Before the young prince is born, his grandfather warns Johannes to protect him. The old king says that one room must remain hidden because its portrait shows the Golden Princess, whose curse has brought death to her husbands. After the old king dies, the prince becomes king and explores his inheritance with Johannes. His curiosity about the locked room grows until he demands that it be opened. The portrait makes him fall in love with the princess. Johannes explains that she is lonely in her golden-roofed palace and that her marriages have ended tragically. The young king asks Johannes to help him marry her, so Johannes collects gold and travels with him in disguise. He shows golden statuettes to a serving girl, who brings the princess to meet him. She is tempted by the gold and goes to the ship. The ship sails away, and the princess first protests. When she learns the young merchant is a king who loves her, she accepts his marriage proposal and stays with him.

video_title: Mickey Mouse Clubhouse - Music Is Everywhere 📖 Read Along Story books 📚 Read Aloud Stories for Kids

summaries.summary: An elephant makes music at the carnival. It stomps on the ground in a steady rhythm. Then it lifts its trunk, swings it around, and makes a toot-toot trumpet sound. At a busy carnival, many friends and animals make different sounds. First, an elephant stomps on the ground. The stomping makes a steady rhythm. The elephant swings its trunk and gives a toot-toot trumpet sound. Daisy taps her feet in a fun dance beat. Then the birds trill and toot. Their sounds are like a flute. Kofy hears a rum-pum-pum-pum, and a tennis ball sounds like a drum. There is lots to see and lots to hear at the carnival. Ferris wheel writers shout, “Wee!” while marimbas play joyfully. Finally, butterflies fly with very thin wings. Their wings make a fluttering sound like a violin. The sounds come one after another, making the carnival lively and full of music.

The story takes us through a carnival filled with sounds. An elephant begins by stomping on the ground. Its steady rhythm is followed by a trumpet-like toot from its swinging trunk. Daisy adds a dance beat when her feet move and tap. Nearby, cute birds make trills and toots that sound like a flute. Kofy hears a rum-pum-pum-pum, and the sound of a tennis ball is compared with a drum. The carnival has many things to see and hear. People on the Ferris wheel shout, “Wee!” Marimbas play joyfully as the carnival continues. Butterflies then fly with their thin wings. Their wings make a soft fluttering sound like a violin. Each part of the carnival brings another sound for everyone to hear.

video_title: Dasher by Matt Tavares read aloud – Kids Christmas Story read along | Kids Self-Esteem Picture Book

summaries.summary: Dasher lived with her reindeer family in a traveling circus. The animals stayed in a hot, crowded pen, but Mama told Dasher about a wonderful home with cold air, white snow, and the North Star shining above. Dasher wished to see that place. One windy night, the gate opened, so Dasher ran away. She followed the North Star but could not reach it. Then she heard bells and found Santa and his tired horse, Silverbell. Dasher offered to help pull the heavy sleigh. She flew through the sky, delivered toys, and discovered the North Star above the North Pole. Dasher loved her new home, but she missed her family. Santa helped her bring them to the North Pole. The whole family joined Santa's team, and Dasher finally had the snowy home she had always wished for.

A young reindeer named Dasher dreamed of living under the North Star. Her mother told stories about cold air and snow, but the family was kept at Mr. Finnegan's circus. Dasher enjoyed seeing kind children and eating carrots, yet she still wished to be free. One night, the pen gate opened, and Dasher followed the star into the woods. There she met Santa, whose sleigh was too heavy for his horse, Silverbell. Dasher pulled with all her strength and helped deliver toys to children. At the North Pole, she saw the North Star directly overhead and felt at home. But Dasher's family was still missing. She told Santa her wish, so they returned to the circus and brought the reindeer family to the North Pole. Soon Dasher and her family became Santa's team of eight reindeer.

Dasher's family lived in a circus, where they worked during the day and had little rest at night. Mama told Dasher about a snowy place beneath the North Star, and Dasher longed to go there. During a storm, the gate opened, and she escaped. After running for hours, Dasher met Santa and Silverbell. Santa needed help because his sleigh was heavy, so Dasher pulled it through the sky. She helped deliver toys and enjoyed many carrots. When they reached the North Pole, Dasher found the snow and the star from Mama's stories. Still, she missed her family. Santa listened to her wish and helped her bring everyone from the circus. Silverbell stayed behind while Dasher, her family, and the other reindeer pulled Santa's sleigh around the world. Dasher's wish came true: she had snow, family, and a happy home.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝐴𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑖 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑡ℎ𝑒 𝑁𝑖𝑔ℎ𝑡 𝐵𝑟𝑜𝑡ℎ𝑒𝑟𝑠 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Amari Peters is sent to the principal after shoving Emily Grant, who has bullied her and made cruel jokes about Amari’s missing brother, Quinton. Emily’s mother demands that Amari lose her scholarship, and Principal Merritt says school rules may cause Amari to be expelled. Amari feels angry and ashamed, but she still believes Quinton is alive. On the ride home, Amari remembers that Quinton was a brilliant student who worked at a secret job and sent money home. The police believe he may have been involved in something illegal, but Amari does not believe them. At home, Amari uses Quinton’s old laptop to post his missing-person notice online. She then sees hurtful comments about him and opens a surprising new email from Quinton’s delivery service. The message says a package has arrived and will disappear. Just then, someone knocks at the apartment door, leaving Amari wondering what Quinton has sent and whether it can help her find him.

Amari has been searching for Quinton since he disappeared six months earlier. At school, Emily and her friends treat Amari badly because she attends on scholarship, and Emily jokes that Quinton is dead. Amari shoves her, so Emily’s mother asks the principal to take away Amari’s scholarship. Mama explains that the scholarship could give Amari a better future, but Amari feels she never belonged at the school. Mama also worries because Amari spends hours using her laptop to search for Quinton. After Mama leaves for work, Amari gets the laptop working and posts Quinton’s missing-person poster on many websites. She looks at Emily’s social-media page and finds cruel comments about her family. Then an email arrives from Quinton’s account through Discreet Deliveries. It says a package has been delivered and that the message will self-destruct. Before Amari can understand what she is supposed to sign, a knock comes from the front door.

Amari is punished after fighting with Emily Grant, but she believes the fight happened because Emily mocked Quinton’s disappearance. Amari’s mother, Mama, is worried about both the lost scholarship and the way Amari is coping. Quinton had been an excellent student who rejected Ivy League scholarships for a mysterious job. The police say they cannot find proof that he ever worked, which makes Amari think they do not understand what happened. Back at their apartment, Mama tells Amari to give up her laptop, but Amari secretly keeps searching. The computer finally turns on, allowing her to share Quinton’s missing-person poster. Amari then reads Emily’s cruel online comments and becomes furious. Before she can answer them, she receives an unusual email from Quinton’s delivery service. It announces that a package has arrived and then deletes itself. A knock at the door follows, suggesting that Quinton’s secret may finally be reaching Amari.

video_title: Bluey My mum is the best kids book read along

summaries.summary: Bluey and Bingo tell why their mum is the best. Mum works hard, drives them to gymnastics, gets them ready, and does many things at once. She looks after them by helping them clean their teeth, brush their hair, and get into bed. She gives them kisses and reads bedtime stories. Mum is also fun. She takes them to the park, rides scooters, dances, rides the bus, and plays pretend games. Sometimes she makes them clean their toys and eat vegetables, but they turn her into a chicken with magic asparagus. Mum is very smart. She fixes a leaking toilet, helps with bad moods, and teaches the children many things. When they feel sad, Mum helps them have a cry, pick themselves up, dust themselves off, and keep going. Bluey and Bingo love their mum, and she loves them too.

Mum works hard and still makes time for Bluey and Bingo. She drives them to gymnastics, helps them get ready, and wishes sometimes that she could rest in a hammock. She keeps them clean, tucks them into bed, kisses them good night, and reads stories. Mum also plays with them. She goes to the park, rides scooters, dances, rides the bus, pretends to be a police lady, and becomes the GPS in their taxi game. Mum can be strict when she asks them to clean up and eat vegetables, but the children play a magic asparagus game and turn her into a chicken. Mum is clever too. She fixes the toilet, helps with sad feelings, and teaches the children about the world. She teaches Dad how to behave. When the children are sad, she helps them keep going. They say their mum is the best.

Bluey and Bingo share many things their mum does. She works hard, takes them places, and helps them do exciting activities. She gets them ready, cares for their teeth and hair, reads bedtime stories, and gives good-night kisses. Mum likes having fun with the children. She plays grannies, dances, rides the bus, chases them like a police lady, and joins their taxi game. She also gives them jobs and makes them eat vegetables, so they pretend to turn her into a chicken with magic asparagus. Mum is super smart because she fixes a leaking toilet and can help fix a bad mood. She teaches the children how to crawl, solve problems, and see that the world is magical. She teaches Dad not to tease them. When Bluey feels sad, Mum gives her a checklist for getting through it. The children love her very much.

video_title: Toy Story Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Andy loves playing with Buzz Lightyear and Woody. They are his favorite toys. At Christmas, Andy goes on a trip with his mom, but he cannot take his toys. Woody feels sad because he will miss Andy. Buzz, Rex, Bo Peep, and the other toys want to help Woody feel happy. They make a Christmas plan. They wrap presents, put them under the tree, and make ribbons, bows, a Santa hat, and a beard. They also turn RC into a sled. On Christmas Eve, Buzz tells Woody about the surprise. The toys make a Christmas tree, snowflakes, bows, and a light show. They sing carols and share presents. Bo Peep gives Woody a Christmas kiss. Woody is happy to spend Christmas with his friends. The toys sing together and wish each other a Merry Christmas. They look at the snow and enjoy being together on Christmas.

Andy has many favorite toys, including Woody and Buzz. Andy is happy when his mom says they are going on a Christmas trip, but Woody is sad because the toys cannot go with Andy. Buzz and the other toys decide to give Woody a special Christmas. They gather supplies and work together. Buzz, Jessie, and Bo Peep wrap presents. Rex and Ham place the presents under the tree. The green army men and the aliens decorate with ribbons, bows, buttons, and snowflakes. They make Rex look like Santa and make RC into a sled. On Christmas Eve, Slinky shows Woody a little tree made of cotton balls. The toys read a story, sing carols, and make a bright laser light show. Then they give presents and gather around the tree. Woody feels happy with his friends. He wishes everyone a Merry Christmas, and the toys look out at the snow.

Woody and Buzz are Andy's favorite toys. When Andy leaves for a Christmas trip without them, Woody misses him and feels sad. Buzz wants to cheer Woody up, so the toys prepare a Christmas surprise. They make a plan and collect supplies. Some toys wrap gifts, while others put gifts under the tree. The green army men and aliens decorate with ribbons, bows, buttons, and snowflakes. Jesse makes Rex a Santa hat, and Buzz makes him a beard. RC becomes a sled. On Christmas Eve, the friends show Woody their decorations. Slinky shows him a cotton-ball Christmas tree. Bo Peep reads a Christmas story. Buzz makes lights with his laser beam, and the toys cheer. Rex and RC help give out presents. Ham gives Jesse a doll's dress, and Bo Peep gives Woody a Christmas kiss. The toys sing carols. Woody is happy because he is with his friends on Christmas.

video_title: The Little Mermaid Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Ariel's Royal Wedding

summaries.summary: Ariel and Prince Eric love each other and are going to get married. Ariel is a mermaid, so she does not know what a human wedding is like. Grimsby teaches her how to dance, and Carlotta helps make a beautiful white wedding dress. Chef Lui plans a wonderful wedding cake. Ariel enjoys the plans, but then she feels sad because her family lives under the sea and may not come. Eric has a kind idea. The wedding can happen on a royal ship at sea, where both humans and merfolk can be together. Ariel asks her sisters to be bridesmaids, Sebastian to carry the ring, and King Triton to walk with her. Her family gives her special wedding treasures. At the wedding, the vows are spoken and the rings are exchanged. Sebastian calls for a kiss, and Ariel and Eric are married. They share cake and dance while family and friends celebrate on land and sea together.

Ariel is excited to marry Prince Eric, but she has never attended a human wedding. She asks Grimsby about the guest list and learns that weddings are for family too. Ariel practices a waltz because she does not know how to dance with legs. Carlotta makes her a soft, beautiful white dress, and Chef Lui prepares a special cake. Ariel likes everything, yet she wishes her family could see the wedding. When Eric finds her crying, he tells her that they will marry on the royal ship at sea. Ariel is happy because her human friends and mermaid family can both be there. Her sisters become bridesmaids, Sebastian becomes the ring bearer, and King Triton gives her away. Her family brings a hair clip, a pink pearl from her mother, and a blue starfish. At the celebration, Ariel and Eric exchange rings, eat cake, and dance together as husband and wife.

Prince Eric loves Ariel when he hears her sing, and Ariel loves him when she sees him. They plan a wedding, but Ariel does not know what to do at a human wedding. She learns about the guest list, practices dancing with Grimsby, chooses a beautiful dress with Carlotta, and helps Chef Lui plan a cake. The wedding preparations make Ariel think about her family under the sea. She becomes sad because they might miss her special day. Eric listens and makes a plan for a wedding on the royal ship. Ariel invites her sisters, Sebastian, and King Triton to help. Her family gives her special things, including a pearl that belonged to her mother. On the wedding day, people sit on the ship while merfolk watch from the sea. Triton brings Ariel and her sisters up. Ariel and Eric say their vows, exchange rings, share cake, and dance. Everyone celebrates together.

video_title: Rooster's Off to See the World

summaries.summary: One morning, a rooster wanted to travel and see the world. He met two cats, three frogs, four turtles, and five fish, and each group happily joined him. They walked together down the road. When night came, the animals needed dinner, a place to sleep, and warmth. The rooster had not made plans for food or shelter, so he did not know how to help. The fish swam home, the turtles crawled home, the frogs jumped away, and the cats went home for an unfinished meal. Soon the rooster was alone. He had not seen the world, and he was hungry, cold, and homesick. He told the moon how he felt, but the moon disappeared. Then the rooster turned around and went home. He ate grain, sat on his own perch, and dreamed a happy dream about traveling around the world.

A rooster set out to see the world because he wanted to travel. At first, he felt lonely, so he invited two cats to come with him. Along the road, three frogs, four turtles, and five fish joined the group. Everyone enjoyed walking together. But the rooster had not thought about what they would eat or where they would sleep. When the sun went down, the cats asked about dinner, the frogs asked about sleeping, the turtles said they were cold, and the fish were afraid. The fish decided to swim home. The turtles crawled back to their warm house. The frogs jumped away, one by one, and the cats returned for their unfinished meal. The rooster was left alone. He was hungry, cold, and homesick, and he had not seen the world. He went home, ate grain, rested on his perch, and dreamed about his trip.

A rooster wanted to take a trip around the world, so he started down the road. He invited cats, frogs, turtles, and fish to join him. The traveling group grew bigger as they walked. Then darkness came, and the animals discovered that no dinner or shelter had been planned. The cats were hungry, the frogs wondered where they would sleep, the turtles were cold, and the fish were afraid of the fireflies. One after another, the animals left. The fish swam home, the turtles crawled home, the frogs jumped away, and the cats went back to their unfinished meal. The rooster stayed by himself. He told the moon that he was hungry, cold, and homesick. When the moon disappeared, he knew he should return home too. He went back, ate a good meal of grain, sat on his own perch, and fell asleep. In his dream, he happily traveled around the world.

video_title: Part 1/3 of George's Marvellous Medicine by Roald Dahl. Read-aloud/audiobook with illustrations.

summaries.summary: George lives on a farm and feels lonely because there are no other children nearby. On Saturday, his mother goes shopping and tells him to give Grandma her medicine. Grandma is tiny, grumpy, and mean to George. She frightens him by talking about magic powers, strange creatures, and scary secrets. George runs to the kitchen, where he decides to make a new medicine to shock her. He gathers almost everything runny, powdery, or gooey that he can find, including shampoo, toothpaste, shaving foam, face cream, nail varnish, cleaning products, spices, gin, and shoe polish. He also takes animal medicines from the shed, even though the labels warn that they are for animals and must be used carefully. George stirs the mixture, then boils it. Blue smoke, strong smells, foam, and sparks appear. Finally, he adds brown paint so it looks like Grandma's real medicine, fills her bottle, and carries it toward her at medicine time.

George is bored while caring for his unpleasant Grandma. She orders him to make tea and complains about his growing. She tells him to eat cabbage with caterpillars, slugs, beetles, worms, and earwigs. Then she pretends to have frightening magic powers, and George becomes very scared. He escapes into the kitchen and decides to make a powerful medicine for her. George hopes it will cure her or create a huge shock. He chooses a large saucepan and begins collecting ingredients. He puts in bathroom items, bedroom cosmetics, laundry supplies, shoe polish, gin, curry powder, mustard, chili sauce, pepper, and horseradish. He then visits the shed and adds medicines meant for chickens, horses, cows, sheep, and pigs. The mixture becomes thick and colorful. George also adds engine oil, antifreeze, and grease. He cooks everything on the stove until it bubbles, foams, smokes blue, and smells magical. He adds dark brown paint, fills Grandma's medicine bottle, and gets ready to give her the strange mixture.

After George's mother leaves, George must look after Grandma and give her medicine at eleven o'clock. Grandma is demanding and cruel, and her talk about witches and magic makes George tremble. Wanting to frighten her back, George plans a fantastic new medicine. He decides to use every household substance he can find, but he stays away from the medicine cupboard because his parents told him it could kill someone. In the bathroom, he gathers shampoo, toothpaste, shaving foam, creams, nail varnish, hair remover, dandruff cure, false-teeth powder, deodorant, and liquid paraffin. He adds bedroom products, washing powder, floor polish, flea powder, canary seed, shoe polish, gin, and strong foods from the larder. In the shed, he pours in animal powders, liquids, and hundreds of pills. He stirs in garage products and cooks the mixture. It froths and produces blue smoke, sparks, and a powerful smell. George adds brown paint, replaces Grandma's medicine, and enters the room with the bottle and spoon.

video_title: The Mixed Up Chameleon

summaries.summary: A small green chameleon lives on a shiny leaf. When it moves to a brown tree, it turns brown. On a red flower, it turns red, and on yellow sand, it turns yellow. When it is warm and has food, it becomes sparkling green. When it is cold and hungry, it becomes gray and dull. The chameleon waits very still for a fly, then catches it with its long, sticky tongue. One day, it sees many animals at a zoo. It wishes to be big like a polar bear, then wishes to be like a flamingo, fox, fish, deer, giraffe, turtle, elephant, seal, and people. The chameleon becomes mixed up and cannot catch a fly. At last, it wishes to be itself. The wish comes true, and the chameleon catches the fly.

A little chameleon changes colors as it moves. It is brown on a tree, reddish on a flower, and yellowish on sand. When it is warm and has something to eat, it is sparkling green. When it is cold and hungry, it is gray and dull. The hungry chameleon waits with only its eyes moving until it sees a fly. Its long, sticky tongue catches the fly. Then the chameleon visits a zoo and sees beautiful animals. It wishes to be big and white like a polar bear. That wish comes true, but the chameleon is not happy. It wishes for many animal qualities, becoming a little of this and a little of that. When another fly flies by, the mixed-up chameleon cannot catch it. Finally, it wishes to be itself. Its wish comes true, and it catches the fly.

On a green leaf, a small chameleon begins its life. It changes color to match places around it: brown on a tree, red on a flower, and yellow on sand. It can be bright green when warm and fed, or gray and dull when cold and hungry. It waits quietly for food and catches a fly with its sticky tongue. At a zoo, the chameleon sees many beautiful animals and thinks it is small, slow, and weak. It wishes to be big like a polar bear, then wishes to be handsome, smart, fast, strong, funny, and able to do what other animals and people can do. The chameleon becomes mixed up and cannot catch a fly. Then it makes one more wish: to be itself. That wish comes true, and the chameleon catches the fly.

video_title: Toy Story Read Along Storybook, Read Aloud Story Books, Books Stories, Bedtime Stories

summaries.summary: Bonnie's toys are making a dinosaur play. Mr. Pricklepants directs it, Buzz and Woody build, and Trixie makes costumes. Rex wants to be the King of the Jungle, but his roar is only a tiny squeak. He feels sad and falls asleep in Bonnie's closet. Rex dreams he is in a jungle. A big dinosaur grabs a cave alien, so Buzz, Woody, Trixie, and Rex try to help. Rex tries to roar, but he squeaks again. Mr. Pricklepants tells Rex to believe in his roar. Rex takes a deep breath and roars louder and louder. He grows big and scares the dinosaur. Woody makes the dinosaur trip, and Buzz saves the alien. The dinosaur falls into the volcano. Rex wakes up and learns that he was roaring in his sleep. Mr. Pricklepants gives Rex the part of King of the Jungle.

The toys are putting on a dinosaur show. Rex hopes to be the biggest dinosaur, the King of the Jungle. Mr. Pricklepants asks for a loud roar, but Rex makes only a squeak. Rex feels like he cannot do the job, so he goes to sleep. In his dream, Rex sees a jungle, cave aliens, and a very big T-rex. The T-rex takes an alien and runs to a volcano. Buzz and Woody try to stop him, but they need help. Trixie asks Rex to use his roar. At first, Rex can only squeak. Mr. Pricklepants tells him to believe it can happen. Rex takes a deep breath. His roars become louder and stronger, and Rex becomes bigger too. He scares the T-rex. Woody trips the T-rex, and Buzz rescues the alien. Rex roars one more time, and the T-rex falls into the volcano. Rex wakes up as a hero and gets the role.

Rex thinks he is the only dinosaur who cannot roar. During a toy play, his little squeak keeps him from getting the part he wants. Then Rex dreams about a jungle adventure. A giant T-rex, called the King of the Jungle, troubles the cave aliens and carries one alien toward a volcano. Buzz flies, Woody uses a rope, and the friends chase the dinosaur. Mr. Pricklepants tells Rex that his roar can become big if he believes in it. Rex bravely helps his friends. He breathes deeply and roars again and again. Each roar is stronger. Rex grows tall over the T-rex, and his biggest roar shakes the trees and ground. The T-rex is frightened. Woody makes him trip with a rope, and Buzz takes the alien away. Rex roars once more, and the T-rex falls into the volcano. Rex wakes beside his friends. Mr. Pricklepants says it was his best roar and gives him the role.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝐶𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑜𝑓 𝐺ℎ𝑜𝑠𝑡𝑠 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Cassidy Blake can see ghosts and sense them even though most people cannot. During the last week of school, a tapping feeling draws her away from lunch and into the auditorium. Her best friend Jacob, who is dead but still spends time with her, follows. Cassidy discovers that the tapping comes from the veil, a boundary between the living world and the dead. She and Jacob cross into a ghostly version of the theater. There, Cassidy witnesses the memory of a boy performing in A Midsummer Night’s Dream. A loose sandbag causes a spark, and the stage quickly catches fire. The boy escapes beneath a trapdoor, but burning scenery seals him inside. Cassidy becomes trapped in the memory until Jacob pushes her back through the veil. She returns safely, though she understands that staying too long makes escaping harder. Jacob reminds her that friends do not leave each other behind.

Cassidy hopes summer will bring six peaceful weeks at her family’s beach house, where there are fewer ghosts. Instead, a persistent tap, tap, tap leads her and Jacob through the school to an auditorium with a frightening ghost story. Long ago, a boy died there during a school performance after a fire. Cassidy finds the trapdoor and sees the gray veil separating the living from the dead. She crosses it with Jacob and enters the past. The theater is filled with actors and an audience that are only memories. Cassidy identifies the dead boy and watches the accident happen: rigging comes loose, a sandbag knocks a fuse, and a spark ignites the paper forest. As flames spread, the boy hides beneath the trapdoor, which becomes pinned shut. Cassidy feels smoke and cannot leave until Jacob forces her out. Back in the present, she realizes the veil can trap people who stay too long.

Cassidy is different from other students because she has psychic abilities and can see her ghost friend Jacob. When the school day ends, she follows a ghostly signal instead of going to lunch. The signal takes them to the auditorium stage, where Cassidy investigates the legend of a boy who died in a theater fire. She finds a hidden entrance to the veil and crosses into a changed version of the auditorium. The past plays out around her like a living memory. A young actor’s cape catches on the rigging, and a falling sandbag causes a fuse to spark. The paper scenery catches fire, and the entire stage becomes dangerous. The boy crawls toward the trapdoor, but burning scenery falls and traps him. Cassidy is also trapped by the memory and begins to weaken. Jacob pulls and pushes her back to the living side. She returns exhausted, while the tapping remains as a reminder of the ghostly world.

video_title: Brave Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, Brave Storybook

summaries.summary: Merida is a princess whose mother, Queen Elinor, has many rules. Merida does not want to marry one of the young lords chosen for her, so she enters the Royal Games and wins for herself. Her mother becomes very angry, and Merida cuts the family tapestry before riding into the woods. There, glowing wisps lead her to a witch. Merida asks for a spell to change her mother’s mind, but the spell changes Elinor into a bear. Merida and her bear mother must escape from Fergus and the hunters. They learn to work together and discover that the witch’s clue means they must mend the torn tapestry. Merida fixes it, but her mother stays a bear. Merida hugs her and says she loves her. Then Elinor changes back into a queen, and mother and daughter learn to love each other as they are.

Princess Merida wants to make her own choices. Queen Elinor wants Merida to marry, so three young men come to compete in the Royal Games. Merida does not choose any of them. She wins the games herself, and this makes her mother angry. Merida rides away and follows blue wisps to a witch’s cottage. The witch gives her a spell cake. Merida gives it to Queen Elinor, hoping her mother will change her mind. Instead, Elinor becomes a bear. Fergus sees the bear and hunts for her, while Merida’s brothers help her mother get away. Merida reads the witch’s clue and understands that she must fix the family tapestry. At the castle, hunters catch the bear. Merida protects her mother, and the dangerous bear is crushed. Merida repairs the tapestry and tells her mother, “I love you.” Elinor becomes human again, and they learn to love each other just the way they are.

Merida feels unhappy because her mother gives her many princess rules and wants her to marry. At the Royal Games, Merida wins instead of letting one of the young lords win her hand. She and Queen Elinor argue, and Merida tears their family tapestry. In the forest, blue wisps guide Merida to a witch. Merida asks for help changing her mother’s mind. The magic cake changes Elinor into a bear, so Merida must help her mother before Fergus finds her. Merida’s brothers make a wild chase, and the Queen escapes. In the woods, Merida and Elinor work together and begin enjoying one another. Merida learns that repairing the torn tapestry may repair their bond. The hunters catch Elinor, but Merida stands between her mother and Fergus’s sword. After the dangerous bear is defeated, Merida hugs her mother and says she loves her. Elinor changes back, and they love each other as they are.

video_title: Chapter Book Storytime • 𝑀𝑎𝑐 𝐵, 𝑆𝑝𝑦 𝐾𝑖𝑑 • EVPL Digital Program

summaries.summary: Mac lives with his mother in Castro Valley and helps with many chores, including answering the phone. One afternoon, the Queen of England calls him. Someone has stolen the crown jewels, and she asks Mac to find them and return them. Mac wonders why a queen chose a child, but she says he is the smartest student in his class. She sends him a plane ticket, British money, and notes for his mother and school. Mac packs his Game Boy, books, clothes, and favorite pair of jeans. Before he leaves, the queen warns that the mission is extremely dangerous. On the plane to London, Mac thinks about spies and wonders whether the passengers around him work for the KGB. He plays his favorite spy video game until a flight attendant brings milk and dinner. After eating the pudding and ravioli, Mac becomes sleepy. His vision swirls, everything goes black, and he wakes to discover that someone has stolen his Game Boy.

Mac is an ordinary boy who lives with his mother and two rabbits, but his life changes when the Queen of England phones him. The crown jewels have been stolen, and the queen chooses Mac to recover them because he earns straight A's, except in handwriting. Mac receives a ticket to London and prepares for his secret mission. He brings his Game Boy, books, toothbrush, clothes, and favorite jeans, which are his only pair. On the flight, Mac thinks about how strange it is to become a spy while he is still a child. He watches a man with sunglasses, a woman with perfume, and a baby, imagining that they may be dangerous agents. He plays SpyMaster, a game about stealing plans from KGB headquarters. A flight attendant gives him milk and a meal. Mac eats the pudding and ravioli but leaves the green beans. Soon, he feels dizzy and blacks out. When he wakes up, his Game Boy is gone.

Mac answers the telephone because it is one of his jobs at home. One day, the caller is the Queen of England. She tells Mac that the crown jewels were stolen and asks him to bring them back. Mac asks why he should do it, since he is only a child living in California. The queen explains that he is the smartest child in his class and orders him to fly to London. She sends a plane ticket and money, so Mac packs quickly and leaves. Just before he goes, the queen calls again to warn him about the danger. During the overnight flight, Mac hopes he can return for a karate birthday party, even though he has not been invited. He studies the people nearby and suspects they could be spies. To relax, he plays SpyMaster on his Game Boy. A flight attendant brings food, and Mac eats the pudding and ravioli. Then he becomes sleepy and loses consciousness. When he wakes, his Game Boy has disappeared.

video_title: Cars Read Along Story Book | Read Aloud Story Books for Kids | Cars 2 Storybook

summaries.summary: Lightning McQueen goes to a big race with his best friend, Mater, and friends from Radiator Springs. There are races in Tokyo, Italy, and London. In Tokyo, Mater talks to a pretty purple car named Holly. She is really a spy, but Mater thinks she likes him. During the race, Mater gives Lightning silly directions because he is looking for Holly. Lightning loses to Francesco and feels upset. Mater leaves, but spies Holly and Finn save him and ask for help. In Italy, Lightning wins the race, but cars keep exploding. Mater learns Lightning is in danger. Bad cars capture Mater, Holly, and Finn in Big Bentley. Mater escapes during the London race. A bomb is under Mater's hood, so he drives away to protect Lightning. Lightning follows him and holds his hook. Mater uses spy tools and stops the bomb. Everyone is safe. Lightning learns that being a good friend matters more than being the fastest car.

Lightning McQueen wants to prove he is the fastest car in the world. His friend Mater comes with him to three races. At a party in Tokyo, Mater meets a purple car named Holly. Holly and Finn are spies, but Mater thinks Holly asked him on a date. During the first race, Mater gives Lightning strange directions while he looks for Holly. Lightning swerves and Francesco wins. Lightning is angry, so Mater tries to go home. Holly and Finn save Mater and ask him to help with a secret mission. In Italy, Lightning remembers that a friend is a treasure and plans to say sorry. He wins the race, but cars are exploding. Mater learns that Lightning is in danger. The bad cars capture Mater, Holly, and Finn. Mater escapes in London, but a bomb is under his hood. Lightning follows him. Mater turns off the bomb with his spy gadgets, and the cars are safe. Mater receives a medal, and Lightning is happy to have his best friend.

When the speaker and child are apart, the speaker is still delivering a piece of their heart. The poem shows love through familiar pizza words and a gentle promise to stay loving.

video_title: The Lion King Read Along Story book, Read Aloud Story Books, The Lion King Storybook 2

summaries.summary: Simba is a little lion whose father, Mufasa, is king. Mufasa shows Simba the kingdom and tells him not to visit the shadowy elephant graveyard. Scar, Simba’s uncle, wants to be king, so he tricks Simba into going there. Simba and Nala meet hyenas, but Mufasa saves them. Later, Scar causes a wildebeest stampede. Mufasa saves Simba, but Scar pushes Mufasa from a rock. Simba thinks his father is dead because of him and runs away. Timon and Pumbaa care for him and teach him “Hakuna Matata,” which means no worries. When Simba grows up, Nala tells him the pride lands are hungry. Rafiki helps Simba remember Mufasa’s words. Simba returns, fights Scar, and wins. Scar falls to the hyenas. Simba becomes king, and he and Nala have a cub who is welcomed into the circle of life.

The young lion Simba is next to become king after his father, Mufasa. Simba is curious about the place beyond the kingdom. His uncle Scar tells him about an elephant graveyard, hoping Simba will go there. Simba and Nala explore it and are chased by hyenas until Mufasa arrives. Scar later makes a dangerous plan. A herd of wildebeests rushes toward Simba, and Mufasa saves him. Scar pushes Mufasa from a cliff, then tells Simba to run away. Simba meets Timon and Pumbaa, who take him home and teach him to live with no worries. One day, Nala finds Simba and tells him that Scar has made the pride lands dry and hungry. Rafiki shows Simba his father’s face in the water. Mufasa tells Simba to be the true king. Simba returns, tells Scar the truth is known, and fights him. Scar is defeated, and Simba becomes king with Nala.

Mufasa and the queen have a baby lion named Simba. Simba is happy to learn about his future kingdom, but Scar wants the crown for himself. Scar sends Simba and Nala toward danger in the elephant graveyard. The hyenas chase them, and Mufasa rescues them. Scar then starts a wildebeest stampede. Mufasa saves Simba, but Scar causes Mufasa’s death and makes Simba leave. Simba is lonely in the desert until Timon and Pumbaa find him. They bring him to the jungle and teach him “Hakuna Matata,” or no worries. Simba grows up there. Nala tells him that the animals at home are starving under Scar. Rafiki reminds Simba that he is Mufasa’s son and the rightful king. Simba returns with Nala, Timon, and Pumbaa. He battles Scar and the hyenas. Simba sends Scar over the cliff, ends Scar’s rule, and becomes king. Later, Simba and Nala welcome their own cub.

video_title: A Beautiful Girl Like You | A story about being beautiful on the inside & out

summaries.summary: The story describes many beautiful girls. One girl has fair skin and shares what she has with others. Another has brown skin and uses encouraging words to help people soar. A girl with skin like desert sands uses her hands to hold and heal. A girl with freckles is gentle, softly spoken, and helps others feel at ease. A girl with black hair is thoughtful, clever, and good at solving problems. A girl with gold hair brings laughter and fun. A tall, gracious girl is honest and stays beside a friend. A small girl shares love through music and art. A girl with red hair does good deeds for people in need. Another girl gives hope and does not give up when life is hard. A courageous girl seeks justice and speaks the truth. In the end, the story says every girl is beautiful, valuable, and made to love and be loved.

This story shows that girls can look many different ways and still be beautiful. Some girls have fair, brown, or desert-colored skin. Some have freckles, black hair, gold hair, red hair, or a cool curly mop. Each girl also has special ways of caring. One shares gifts and thoughtful kindness. One uses encouraging words. One holds and heals with gentle hands. One brings peace. Others solve problems, make people laugh, catch a friend who falls, share love through music and art, and help people in need. A girl with hope keeps going when things are difficult. A strong and courageous girl stands up for justice and speaks the truth. The story then says beauty is not only on the outside. Any girl can bring beauty to the world by being herself. Every girl is worth more than rubies and is a valuable treasure.

A beautiful girl in the story may be gentle, clever, joyful, honest, artistic, compassionate, hopeful, or brave. She may have any kind of skin, hair, or size. A girl with fair skin shares her blessings and thinks of others. A girl with brown skin looks for inner beauty and encourages people. Other girls heal with hugs, bring peace, solve problems, spread laughter, stay with friends, and share their hearts through music and art. A girl with red hair helps people who have needs. A girl with a hopeful smile makes the most of each day and does not give up. A girl with curly hair seeks justice, stands up for the week, and speaks the truth. The story ends by saying that every girl is beautiful, not only because of how she looks. Every girl is valuable, precious from birth, and made to love and be loved.
